### [Subpart 1 --- Aerodromes]{.HTitleText2} {#h-988738 .Subheading}

#### [Application]{.HTitleText3} {#h-988739 .Subheading}

**[[301.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-301.01 .sectionLabel}** This Subpart
applies in respect of all aerodromes except airports, heliports and
military aerodromes.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 5
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-301.01-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 301.01"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Inspection]{.HTitleText3} {#h-988743 .Subheading}

**[[301.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-301.02 .sectionLabel}** The operator of
an aerodrome shall, without charge, at the request of a Department of
Transport inspector, allow the inspector access to aerodrome facilities
and provide the equipment necessary to conduct an inspection of the
aerodrome.

#### [Registration]{.HTitleText3} {#h-988745 .Subheading}

- **[[301.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-301.03
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), where the
  operator of an aerodrome provides the Minister with information
  respecting the location, markings, lighting, use and operation of the
  aerodrome, the Minister must register the aerodrome and submit the
  information to the provider of aeronautical information services for
  publication in the Canada Flight Supplement or the Water Aerodrome
  Supplement, as applicable.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may refuse to register an aerodrome if
  the operator of the aerodrome does not meet the requirements of
  sections 301.05 to 301.09 or if using the aerodrome is likely to be
  hazardous to aviation safety and, in such a case, must not submit the
  information with respect to that aerodrome to the provider of
  aeronautical information services for publication.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an aerodrome registered under
  subsection (1) must notify the Minister immediately after any change
  is made to the location, markings, lighting, use or operation of the
  aerodrome that is likely to affect the accuracy of the information
  published by the provider of aeronautical information services under
  subsection (1).

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An aerodrome that is listed in the Canada Flight
  Supplement or the Water Aerodrome Supplement on the coming into force
  of this Subpart is deemed to be registered pursuant to subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-26, s. 12](#1511683-1516206){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1511683-1516206.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-301.03-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 301.03"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Markers and Markings]{.HTitleText3} {#h-988751 .Subheading}

- **[[301.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-301.04
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} When an aerodrome is closed
  permanently, the operator of the aerodrome shall remove all of the
  markers and markings installed at the aerodrome.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an aerodrome, other than a water
  aerodrome, shall install red flags or red cones along the boundary of
  an unserviceable movement area.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subsections (4) to (8) do not apply in respect of any
  manoeuvring area or part thereof that is closed for 24 hours or less.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where a runway or part of a runway is closed, the
  operator of the aerodrome shall place closed markings, as set out in
  Schedule I to this Subpart, on the runway as follows:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where the runway is greater than 1 220 m (4,000
    feet) in length, a closed marking shall be located at each end of
    the closed runway or part thereof and additional closed markings
    shall be located on the closed runway or part thereof at intervals
    not exceeding 300 m (1,000 feet);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the runway is greater than 450 m (1,500 feet)
    but not greater than 1 220 m (4,000 feet) in length, a closed
    marking of not less than one-half the dimensions set out in that
    Schedule shall be located at each end of the closed runway or part
    thereof and an additional closed marking of the same dimensions
    shall be located on the closed runway or part thereof at a point
    equidistant from the two markings; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} where the runway is 450 m (1,500 feet) or less in
    length, a closed marking of not less than one-half the dimensions
    set out in that Schedule shall be located at each end of the closed
    runway or part thereof.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} Where a taxiway or part of a taxiway is closed, the
  operator of the aerodrome shall place on each end of the closed
  taxiway, or part thereof, a closed marking with the dimensions set out
  in Schedule I to this Subpart.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} Where a helicopter take-off and landing area at an
  aerodrome is closed, the operator of the aerodrome shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} place a closed marking over the letter "H", where
    the letter "H" identifies the helicopter take-off and landing area,
    or, where no letter identifies the helicopter take-off and landing
    area, over the centre of the area; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} comply with subsection (4), where the helicopter
    take-off and landing area is a runway.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} Where a manoeuvring area or part thereof is closed
  permanently, the operator of the aerodrome shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} obliterate all of the markings that indicate that
    the manoeuvring area or part thereof is open; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsection (8), paint on the manoeuvring
    area or part thereof the markings required pursuant to
    subsections (4) to (6).

- [(8)]{.lawlabel} Where the surface of a manoeuvring area or part
  thereof is snow-covered or otherwise unsuitable for painting or where
  the closure is not permanent, closed markings may be applied by means
  of a conspicuously coloured dye or may be constructed from a suitable
  conspicuously coloured material or product.

#### [Warning Notices]{.HTitleText3} {#h-988768 .Subheading}

**[[301.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-301.05 .sectionLabel}** Where low-flying
or taxiing aircraft at or in the vicinity of an aerodrome are likely to
be hazardous to pedestrian or vehicular traffic, the operator of the
aerodrome shall immediately

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} post notices warning of the hazard on any public way
  that is adjacent to the manoeuvring area; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} where such a public way is not owned or controlled by
  the operator, inform the authorities responsible for placing markings
  on the public way that there is a hazard.

#### [Wind Direction Indicator]{.HTitleText3} {#h-988772 .Subheading}

- **[[301.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-301.06
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except where the direction of the
  wind at an aerodrome can be determined by radio or other means such as
  smoke movement in the air or wind lines on water, the operator of the
  aerodrome shall install and maintain at the aerodrome a wind direction
  indicator that is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} of a conspicuous colour or colours;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the shape of a truncated cone;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} visible from an aircraft flying at an altitude of
    300 m (1,000 feet) above the wind direction indicator; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} illuminated when the aerodrome is used at night.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} When an aerodrome is closed permanently, the operator
  of the aerodrome shall immediately remove all of the wind direction
  indicators installed at the aerodrome.

#### [Lighting]{.HTitleText3} {#h-988780 .Subheading}

- **[[301.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-301.07
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), where a
  runway is used at night, the operator of the aerodrome shall indicate
  each side of the runway along its length with a line of fixed white
  lights that is visible in all directions from an aircraft in flight at
  a distance of not less than two nautical miles.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where it is not practical to provide at an aerodrome
  the fixed white lights referred to in subsection (1) for reasons such
  as the lack of an available electrical power source or insufficient
  air traffic, the operator of the aerodrome may, if a fixed white light
  is displayed at each end of the runway to indicate runway alignment,
  use white retro-reflective markers that are capable of reflecting
  aircraft lights and that are visible at a distance of not less than
  two nautical miles from an aircraft in flight that is aligned with the
  centre line of the runway.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The lines of lights or retro-reflective markers
  required by subsection (1) or (2) shall be arranged so that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the lines of lights or markers are parallel and of
    equal length and the transverse distance between the lines is equal
    to the runway width in use during the day;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the distance between adjacent lights or markers in
    each line is the same and is not more than 60 m (200 feet);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} each line of lights or markers is not less than 420
    m (1,377 feet) in length and contains no fewer than eight lights or
    markers; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} each light or marker in a line of lights or markers
    is situated opposite to a light or marker in the line of lights or
    markers on the other side of the runway, so that a line connecting
    them forms a right angle to the centre line of the runway.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Fixed white lights displayed at each end of a runway
  pursuant to subsection (2) shall be placed so that they are not likely
  to cause a hazard that could endanger persons or property.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} Where a taxiway is used at night, the operator of the
  aerodrome shall indicate each side of the taxiway with a line of fixed
  blue lights or blue retro-reflective markers placed so that the two
  lines of lights or markers are parallel and the distance between
  adjacent lights or markers in each line is not more than 60 m (200
  feet).

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} Where a manoeuvring area or part thereof or a
  heliport is closed, the operator of the aerodrome shall not operate
  the lights or keep the retro-reflective markers thereon, except as
  required for maintenance of the lights and markers.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} Where an aerodrome is used at night, the operator of
  the aerodrome shall indicate an unserviceable portion of the movement
  area with fixed red lights, red retro-reflective markers or
  floodlighting.

- [(8)]{.lawlabel} Where an aircraft parking area at an aerodrome is
  used at night, the operator of the aerodrome shall indicate the
  boundary of the area with fixed blue lights or blue retro-reflective
  markers, placed at intervals not exceeding 60 m (200 feet), or with
  floodlighting.

- [(9)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (10), where a heliport is used
  at night for the take-off or landing of helicopters, the operator of
  the heliport shall illuminate the entire take-off and landing area
  with floodlights or

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where the take-off and landing area is rectangular,
    shall indicate the boundary with no fewer than eight fixed yellow
    lights, including one light at each corner, placed so that adjacent
    lights are not more than 13 m (42.5 feet) apart; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the take-off and landing area is circular,
    shall indicate the boundary with no fewer than five fixed yellow
    lights placed so that adjacent lights are not more than 13 m (42.5
    feet) apart.

- [(10)]{.lawlabel} Where it is not practical to provide at a heliport
  the fixed yellow lights referred to in subsection (9) for reasons such
  as lack of an available electrical power source or insufficient air
  traffic, the operator of the heliport may use yellow retro-reflective
  markers that are capable of reflecting aircraft lights and that are
  visible at a distance of not less than two nautical miles from an
  aircraft in flight that is aligned with the approach path, if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a light source is provided to show the location of
    the heliport; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where there is only one path for approach and
    departure, two lights are used to show the approach orientation.

- [(11)]{.lawlabel} Where the lighting required by subsections (1),
  (2), (5) and (7) to (10) is operated by a radio-controlled system
  capable of activation from an aircraft, the system shall meet the
  requirements set out in Schedule II to this Subpart.

- [(12)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an aerodrome may display flare pots
  to provide temporary lighting for the landing or take-off of aircraft.

#### [Prohibitions]{.HTitleText3} {#h-988802 .Subheading}

**[[301.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-301.08 .sectionLabel}** No person shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} walk, stand, drive a vehicle, park a vehicle or
  aircraft or cause an obstruction on the movement area of an aerodrome,
  except in accordance with permission given

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} by the operator of the aerodrome, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where applicable, by the appropriate air traffic
    services unit;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} tow an aircraft on an active movement area at night
  unless the aircraft displays operating wingtip, tail and
  anti-collision lights or is illuminated by lights mounted on the
  towing vehicle and directed at the aircraft;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} park or otherwise leave an aircraft on an active
  manoeuvring area at night unless the aircraft displays operating
  wingtip, tail and anti-collision lights or is illuminated by lanterns
  suspended from the wingtips, tail and nose of the aircraft;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} operate any vessel, or cause any obstruction, on the
  surface of any part of a water area of an aerodrome that is to be kept
  clear of obstructions in the interest of aviation safety, when
  ordered, by signal or otherwise, to leave or not to approach that area
  by the appropriate air traffic services unit or by the operator of the
  aerodrome;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} knowingly remove, deface, extinguish or interfere
  with a marker, marking, light or signal that is used at an aerodrome
  for the purpose of air navigation, except in accordance with
  permission given

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} by the operator of the aerodrome, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where applicable, by the appropriate air traffic
    services unit;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} at a place other than an aerodrome, knowingly display
  a marker, marking, light or signal that is likely to cause a person to
  believe that the place is an aerodrome;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} knowingly display at or in the vicinity of an
  aerodrome a marker, marking, sign, light or signal that is likely to
  be hazardous to aviation safety by causing glare or by causing
  confusion with or preventing clear visual perception of a marker,
  marking, sign, light or signal that is required under this Subpart;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} allow a bird or other animal that is owned by the
  person or that is in the person's custody or control to be
  unrestrained within the boundaries of an aerodrome except for the
  purpose of controlling other birds or animals at the aerodrome as
  permitted by the operator; or

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} discharge a firearm within or into an aerodrome
  without the permission of the operator of the aerodrome.

#### [Fire Prevention]{.HTitleText3} {#h-988817 .Subheading}

- **[[301.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-301.09
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection 301.07(12) and
  subsections (2) and (3), no person shall, while at an aerodrome, smoke
  or display an open flame

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} on an apron;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} on an aircraft loading bridge or on a gallery or
    balcony that is contiguous to or that overhangs an apron; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in an area where smoking or the presence of an open
    flame is likely to create a fire hazard that could endanger persons
    or property.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an aerodrome may, in writing,
  authorize maintenance or servicing operations on an apron that involve
  the use, production or potential development of an open flame or that
  involve the production or potential development of a spark where the
  operations are conducted in a manner that is not likely to create a
  fire hazard that could endanger persons or property.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an aerodrome may permit smoking in an
  enclosed building or shelter located on an apron where such smoking is
  not likely to create a fire hazard that could endanger persons or
  property.

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-988843 .Subheading}

- **[[302.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.01
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), this
  Subpart applies in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an aerodrome that is located within the built-up
    area of a city or town;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a land aerodrome that is used by an air operator
    for the purpose of a scheduled service for the transport of
    passengers; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any other aerodrome, other than an aerodrome
    referred to in subsection (2), in respect of which the Minister is
    of the opinion that meeting the requirements necessary for the
    issuance of an airport certificate would be in the public interest
    and would further the safe operation of the aerodrome.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} This Subpart does not apply in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a military aerodrome;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a land aerodrome referred to in paragraph (1)(b)
    where the Minister has issued a written authorization for each air
    operator using the aerodrome to land at and take-off from the
    aerodrome; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} heliports.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall issue an authorization referred to
  in paragraph (2)(b) where it is possible to specify conditions in the
  authorization that will ensure a level of safety in respect of the use
  of the aerodrome that is equivalent to the level of safety established
  by this Subpart, and, in any such authorization, the Minister shall
  specify those conditions.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 7
:::

##### [Application for Airport Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-988856 .Subheading}

- **[[302.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.02
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for an airport
  certificate shall submit to the Minister for approval

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an application for an airport certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a copy of the proposed airport operations manual in
    respect of the airport.

- [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} The applicant shall include in the application
  proof that the applicant has consulted with the interested parties in
  accordance with the requirements of Subpart 7.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The application shall be signed by the applicant and
  shall be in the form set out in the aerodrome standards and
  recommended practices publications.

- SOR/2016-261, s. 2

##### [Issuance of Airport Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-988865 .Subheading}

- **[[302.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.03
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection 6.71(1) of the
  Act, the Minister shall issue an airport certificate to an applicant
  authorizing the applicant to operate an aerodrome as an airport if the
  proposed airport operations manual, submitted pursuant to paragraph
  302.02(1)(b), is approved by the Minister pursuant to subsection (2)
  and

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the standards set out in the aerodrome standards
    and recommended practices publications are met; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} on the basis of an aeronautical study, the Minister
    determines that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the level of safety at the aerodrome is
      equivalent to that provided for by the standards set out in the
      aerodrome standards and recommended practices publications, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the issuance of the airport certificate is in
      the public interest and not detrimental to aviation safety.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall approve a proposed airport
  operations manual if it

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} accurately describes the physical specifications of
    the aerodrome; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} conforms to the requirements set out in the
    aerodrome standards and recommended practices publications that
    apply in respect of an airport operations manual.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where an aerodrome does not meet a standard set out
  in the aerodrome standards and recommended practices publications, the
  Minister may specify in the airport certificate such conditions
  relating to the subject-matter of the standard as are necessary to
  ensure a level of safety equivalent to that established by the
  standard and as are necessary in the public interest and to ensure
  aviation safety.

##### [Transfer of Airport Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-988876 .Subheading}

- **[[302.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.04
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} When an airport certificate is
  transferred, it shall be transferred in accordance with this section.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall transfer an airport certificate to
  a transferee where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the current holder of the airport certificate, at
    least 14 days before ceasing to operate the airport, notifies the
    Minister in writing that the current holder will cease to operate
    the airport as of the date specified in the notice;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the current holder of the airport certificate
    notifies the Minister in writing of the name of the transferee;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the transferee applies in writing to the Minister,
    within 14 days before the current holder ceases to operate the
    airport, for the airport certificate to be transferred to the
    transferee; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the requirements set out in section 302.03 are met.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An application referred to in paragraph (2)(c) shall
  include a copy of the notice referred to in paragraph (2)(a).

##### [Interim Airport Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-988885 .Subheading}

- **[[302.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.05
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may, by mail, telex or
  facsimile machine, issue to an applicant referred to in section 302.03
  or a transferee referred to in section 302.04 an interim airport
  certificate authorizing the applicant or transferee to operate an
  aerodrome as an airport if the Minister is satisfied that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an airport certificate in respect of the aerodrome
    will be issued to the applicant or transferred to the transferee as
    soon as the application procedure in respect of the issuance or
    transfer is completed; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the issuance of the interim airport certificate is
    in the public interest and not detrimental to aviation safety.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An interim airport certificate issued pursuant to
  subsection (1) expires on the earlier of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the date on which the airport certificate is issued
    or transferred, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the date specified in the interim airport
    certificate on which it will expire.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Except for paragraph 302.02(1)(b), subsections
  302.03(1) and (2) and section 302.08, this Subpart applies in respect
  of an interim airport certificate in the same manner as it applies in
  respect of an airport certificate.

##### [Amendment and Cancellation of Airport Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-988894 .Subheading}

- **[[302.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.06
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may, if the
  requirements of section 302.03 and paragraph 302.08(1)(c) are met,
  amend an airport certificate where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} there is a change in the use or operation of the
    airport;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} there is a change in the boundaries of the airport;
    or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the holder of the airport certificate requests the
    amendment.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall cancel an airport certificate
  where this Subpart no longer applies in respect of the aerodrome
  referred to in the airport certificate, as determined in accordance
  with section 302.01.

##### [Obligations of Operator]{.HTitleText4} {#h-988901 .Subheading}

- **[[302.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.07
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} comply

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} subject to subparagraph (ii), with the standards
      set out in the aerodrome standards and recommended practices
      publications, as they read on the date on which the airport
      certificate was issued,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in respect of any part or facility of the
      airport that has been replaced or improved, with the standards set
      out in the aerodrome standards and recommended practices
      publications, as they read on the date on which the part or
      facility was returned to service, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} with any conditions specified in the airport
      certificate by the Minister pursuant to subsection 302.03(3);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} without charge, at the request of a Department of
    Transport inspector, allow access to airport facilities and provide
    the equipment necessary to conduct an inspection of the airport;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} review each issue of each aeronautical information
    publication on receipt thereof and, immediately after such review,
    notify the Minister of any inaccurate information contained therein
    that pertains to the airport;

  - [(c.1)]{.lawlabel} provide to the provider of aeronautical
    information services, in the manner specified in the processes and
    procedures established by the provider of aeronautical information
    services, information on the airport in accordance with the
    applicable requirements set out in the aerodrome standards and
    recommended practices publications;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} notify the provider of aeronautical information
    services before any planned change to the airport, the airport
    facilities or the level of service at the airport that has been
    planned in advance and that is likely to affect the accuracy of the
    information contained in an aeronautical information publication;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} as the circumstances require for the purpose of
    ensuring aviation safety, inspect the airport

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} as soon as practicable after any aviation
      occurrence, as that term is defined in section 2 of the [Canadian
      Transportation Accident Investigation and Safety Board
      Act](/eng/acts/C-23.4),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} during any period of construction or repair of
      the airport or of airport facilities that are designated in the
      airport certificate, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} at any other time when there are conditions at
      the airport that could be hazardous to aviation safety;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} notify the Minister in writing of any change in
    airport operations within 14 days after the date of the change; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} assign duties on the movement area and any other
    area set aside for the safe operation of aircraft, including
    obstacle limitation surfaces, at the airport, which are described in
    the airport operations manual, only to employees who have
    successfully completed a safety-related initial training course on
    human and organizational factors.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), the operator of an airport
  shall give to the Minister, and cause to be received at the
  appropriate air traffic services unit, immediate notice of any of the
  following circumstances of which the operator has knowledge:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any projection by an object through an obstacle
    limitation surface relating to the airport;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the existence of any obstruction or hazardous
    condition affecting aviation safety at or in the vicinity of the
    airport;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any reduction in the level of services at the
    airport that are set out in an aeronautical information publication;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the closure of any part of the manoeuvring area of
    the airport; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} any other conditions that could be hazardous to
    aviation safety at the airport and against which precautions are
    warranted.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where it is not feasible for an operator to cause
  notice of a circumstance referred to in subsection (2) to be received
  at the appropriate air traffic services unit, the operator shall give
  immediate notice directly to the pilots who may be affected by that
  circumstance.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport may remove from the
  surface of the airport any vehicle or other obstruction that is likely
  to be hazardous to aviation safety at or in the vicinity of the
  airport.

##### [Airport Operations Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-988927 .Subheading}

- **[[302.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.08
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} on the issuance of an airport certificate, provide
    the Minister with a copy of the airport operations manual, as
    approved by the Minister pursuant to subsection 302.03(2), and
    distribute copies of the applicable portions to the persons and
    institutions referred to in the airport operations manual;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} maintain the airport operations manual; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} submit to the Minister for approval any proposed
    amendment to the airport operations manual.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The provisions of this Subpart that apply in respect
  of the making of an airport operations manual also apply in respect of
  any amendment to an airport operations manual.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An airport operations manual shall set out the
  standards to be met and the services to be provided by an airport
  operator.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An airport operations manual shall contain

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a table of contents;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any information relating to the administration of
    the airport, including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a record of any amendments to the airport
      operations manual,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a list of holders of copies of the airport
      operations manual or of portions thereof,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a description of the procedure for amendment of
      the airport operations manual,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a description of the organizational structure
      and operational procedures of the airport management,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} an enumeration of the obligations of the operator
      referred to in section 302.07,

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} an undertaking, signed by the operator, in
      respect of the operator's obligations under paragraphs
      302.07(1)(c) and (d),

    - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} a statement, signed by the operator, certifying
      that the airport operations manual is complete and accurate, and
      that the operator agrees to comply with all of the conditions and
      specifications referred to therein,

    - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} a statement, signed by the Minister, that the
      Minister has approved the airport operations manual and any
      amendments thereto, and

    - [(ix)]{.lawlabel} a copy of any agreement or memorandum of
      understanding that affects the operation of the airport;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} all of the information necessary to verify that the
    airport meets the applicable standards set out in the aerodrome
    standards and recommended practices publications, as they read on
    the date on which the airport certificate was issued, and satisfies
    any conditions specified by the Minister pursuant to subsection
    302.03(3) in respect of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} physical characteristics,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} obstacle limitation surfaces,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} declared distances,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} lighting,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} markers,

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} markings,

    - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} signs,

    - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} emergency response measures,

    - [(ix)]{.lawlabel} airport safety measures,

    - [(x)]{.lawlabel} access to the movement area and control
      procedures, and

    - [(xi)]{.lawlabel} apron management plans and apron safety plans;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} an enumeration of the facilities and services
    provided and the measures in effect at the airport, including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} movement area maintenance services,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} measures for the removal of disabled aircraft,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} air traffic services and aeronautical
      information and communication services,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} navigation aids, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} aviation weather services;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a description of movement area services and
    facilities provided at the discretion of the operator; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} with respect to the safety management system
    required under section 107.02,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a description of the system's components
      specified in section 302.502, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a list of the titles, dates and locations of any
      documents that are not in the airport operations manual and that
      describe how the operator is meeting its obligations with respect
      to the safety management system.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall operate the airport
  in accordance with the airport operations manual.

##### [Warning Notices]{.HTitleText4} {#h-988972 .Subheading}

**[[302.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.09 .sectionLabel}** Where low-flying
or taxiing aircraft at or in the vicinity of an airport are likely to be
hazardous to pedestrian or vehicular traffic, the operator of the
airport shall immediately

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} post notices warning of the hazard on any public way
  that is adjacent to the manoeuvring area; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} where such a public way is not owned or controlled by
  the operator, inform the authorities responsible for posting notices
  on the public way that there is a hazard.

##### [Prohibitions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-988976 .Subheading}

**[[302.10]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.10 .sectionLabel}** No person shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} operate an aerodrome referred to in subsection
  302.01(1) unless an airport certificate is issued in respect of that
  aerodrome;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} knowingly use an airport in a manner contrary to a
  condition set out in the airport certificate;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} walk, stand, drive a vehicle, park a vehicle or
  aircraft or cause an obstruction on the movement area of an airport,
  except in accordance with permission given

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} by the operator of the airport, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where applicable, by the appropriate air traffic
    services unit;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} operate any vessel, or cause any obstruction, on the
  surface of any part of a water area of an airport that is to be kept
  clear of obstructions in the interest of aviation safety, when
  ordered, by signal or otherwise, to leave or not to approach that area
  by the appropriate air traffic services unit or by the operator of the
  airport;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} tow an aircraft on an active movement area at night
  unless the aircraft displays operating wingtip, tail and
  anti-collision lights or is illuminated by lights mounted on the
  towing vehicle and directed at the aircraft being towed;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} park or otherwise leave an aircraft on an active
  manoeuvring area at night unless the aircraft displays operating
  wingtip, tail and anti-collision lights or is illuminated by lanterns
  suspended from the wingtips, tail and nose of the aircraft;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} at an airport, knowingly remove, deface, extinguish
  or interfere with a marker, marking, light or signal that is used for
  the purpose of air navigation, except in accordance with permission
  given

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} by the operator of the airport, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where applicable, by the appropriate air traffic
    services unit;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} at or in the vicinity of an airport, knowingly
  display a marker, marking, sign, light or signal that is likely to be
  hazardous to aviation safety by causing glare or by causing confusion
  with or preventing clear visual perception of a marker, marking, sign,
  light or signal that is required under this Subpart;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} allow a bird or other animal that is owned by the
  person or that is in the person's custody or control to be
  unrestrained within the boundaries of an airport, except for the
  purpose of controlling other birds or animals at the airport as
  permitted by the operator; or

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} discharge a firearm within or into an airport without
  the permission of the operator of the airport.

##### [Fire Prevention]{.HTitleText4} {#h-988992 .Subheading}

- **[[302.11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.11
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) to (4),
  no person shall, at an airport, smoke or display an open flame

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} on an apron;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} on an aircraft loading bridge or on a gallery or
    balcony that is contiguous to or that overhangs an apron; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in an area where smoking or an open flame is likely
    to create a fire hazard that could endanger persons or property.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport may display flare pots to
  provide temporary lighting for the take-off or landing of aircraft.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport may, in writing, authorize
  maintenance or servicing operations on an apron that involve the use,
  production or potential development of an open flame or that involve
  the production or potential development of a spark where the
  operations are conducted in a manner that is not likely to create a
  fire hazard that could endanger persons or property.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport may permit smoking in an
  enclosed building or shelter located on an apron where such smoking is
  not likely to create a fire hazard that could endanger persons or
  property.

**\[302.12 to 302.200 reserved\]**

#### [Division II --- Airport Emergency Planning]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989002 .Subheading}

##### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989003 .Subheading}

**[[302.201]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.201 .sectionLabel}** The following
definitions apply in this Division.

[[community organization]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[community organization]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed,
    SOR/2022-267, s. 4\]]{.Repealed}

[[emergency coordination centre]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[emergency coordination centre]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a
    designated area to be used in supporting and coordinating emergency
    operations and whose location is specified under paragraph
    302.203(1)(r). ([centre de coordination des
    urgences]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[full emergency standby]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[full emergency standby]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means attendance at
    an emergency scene and preparedness to respond at the necessary
    level when an aircraft has, or may have, an operational problem that
    affects flight operations to the extent that there is a possibility
    of an accident. ([état d'alerte complet]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[on-scene controller]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[on-scene controller]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the person
    identified in an airport emergency plan as being responsible for the
    overall coordination of the response at an emergency scene.
    ([coordonnateur sur place]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[table top exercise]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[table top exercise]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an exercise
    requiring the participation of the organizations and other resources
    identified in an airport emergency plan to review and coordinate
    their respective roles, responsibilities and response actions
    without actually activating the plan. ([exercice en
    salle]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

##### [Airport Emergency Plan]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989012 .Subheading}

###### [General]{.HTitleText5} {#h-989013 .Subheading}

- **[[302.202]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.202
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} After consultation with a
  representative sample of the air operators that use the airport and
  with organizations that may be of assistance during emergency
  operations at the airport or in its vicinity, the operator of an
  airport shall have and maintain an emergency plan for the purpose of
  identifying

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the emergencies that are likely to occur at the
    airport or in its vicinity and that could be a threat to the safety
    of persons or the operation of the airport;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the measures to activate the emergency plan for
    each type of emergency;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the organizations capable of providing assistance
    in an emergency; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} any additional resources available at the airport
    and in the surrounding area.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall have and maintain a
  system of supervision and control that allows the operator to be able
  to manage the size and complexity of the emergencies referred to in
  paragraph (1)(a).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} keep at the airport, in the format of a manual, a
    copy of an updated version of the emergency plan; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} provide a copy to the Minister on request.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} review the emergency plan at least once a year
    after consultation with a representative sample of the air operators
    that use the airport and the organizations identified in the
    emergency plan; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} update the emergency plan as necessary to ensure
    its effectiveness in emergency operations.

::: HistoricalNote

###### [Content]{.HTitleText5} {#h-989029 .Subheading}

- **[[302.203]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.203
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In an emergency plan, the operator
  of an airport shall, at a minimum,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} identify the potential emergencies, including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft accident or incident

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} within the airport boundaries, and

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} within a critical rescue and fire-fighting
        access area that extends 1000 m beyond the ends of a runway and
        150 m at 90° outwards from the centreline of the runway,
        including any part of that area outside the airport boundaries,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft emergency declared by either air
      traffic services or a pilot,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a fuel spill that spreads at least 1.5 m in any
      direction or exceeds 12 mm in depth,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a medical emergency,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} a fire in which airport operations or passenger
      safety is threatened,

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} an emergency that is related to a special
      aviation event and that might have an impact on airport
      operations,

    - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} a natural disaster, and

    - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} any other emergency that is a threat or is
      likely to be a threat to the safety of persons or to the operation
      of the airport;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} identify the organizations capable of providing
    assistance during an emergency at an airport or in its vicinity,
    provide the telephone numbers and other contact information for each
    organization and describe the type of assistance each can provide;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} identify the other resources available at the
    airport and in the surrounding communities for use during emergency
    response or recovery operations and provide their telephone numbers
    and other contact information;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} describe for emergency situations the lines of
    authority and the relationships between the organizations identified
    in the emergency plan and describe how actions will be coordinated
    among all and within each of the organizations;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} identify, for emergency situations, the supervisors
    and describe the duties of each;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} specify the positions occupied by the airport
    personnel who will respond to an emergency and describe the specific
    emergency response duties of each;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} identify the on-scene controller and describe the
    controller's emergency response duties;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} provide authorization for a person to act as an
    on-scene controller or a supervisor if they are not airport
    personnel;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} set out the criteria to be used for positioning the
    on-scene controller within visual range of an emergency scene;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} set out the measures to be taken to make the
    on-scene controller easily identifiable and reachable at all times
    by all persons responding to an emergency;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} if initial on-scene control has been assumed by a
    person from a responding organization, describe the procedure for
    transferring control to the on-scene controller;

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} describe any training and qualifications required
    for the on-scene controller and the airport personnel identified in
    the emergency plan;

  - [(m)]{.lawlabel} describe the method for recording any training
    provided to the on-scene controller and airport personnel;

  - [(n)]{.lawlabel} describe the communication procedures and specify
    the radio frequencies to be used to link the operator of the airport
    with

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the on-scene controller, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the providers of ground traffic control services
      and air traffic control services at the airport;

  - [(o)]{.lawlabel} describe the communication procedures allowing the
    on-scene controller to communicate with the organizations identified
    in the emergency plan;

  - [(p)]{.lawlabel} identify the alerting procedures that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} activate the emergency plan,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} establish the necessary level of response,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} allow immediate communication with the
      organizations identified in the emergency plan in accordance with
      the required level of response,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, confirm the dispatch of each
      responding organization,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} establish the use of standard terminology in
      communications, and

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} establish the use of the appropriate radio
      frequencies as set out in the emergency plan;

  - [(q)]{.lawlabel} specify

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the airport communication equipment testing
      procedures,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a schedule for the testing, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the method of keeping records of the tests;

  - [(r)]{.lawlabel} for airports designated under Subpart 3, specify
    the location of the emergency coordination centre used to provide
    support to the on-scene controller;

  - [(s)]{.lawlabel} describe the measures for dealing with adverse
    climatic conditions and darkness for each potential emergency set
    out in paragraph (a);

  - [(t)]{.lawlabel} describe the procedures to assist persons who have
    been evacuated if their safety is threatened or airside operations
    are affected;

  - [(u)]{.lawlabel} describe the procedures respecting the review and
    confirmation of the following to permit the return of the airport to
    operational status after an emergency situation:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} emergency status reports,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} coordination with the coroner and the
      investigator designated by the Transportation Safety Board of
      Canada regarding the accident site conditions,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} disabled aircraft removal,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} airside inspection results,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} accident or incident site conditions, and

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} air traffic services and NOTAM coordination;

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} describe the procedures for controlling vehicular
    flow during an emergency to ensure the safety of vehicles, aircraft
    and persons;

  - [(w)]{.lawlabel} specify the procedures for issuing a NOTAM in the
    event of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} an emergency affecting the critical category for
      fire fighting required under section 303.07, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} changes or restrictions in facilities or
      services at the airport during and after an emergency;

  - [(x)]{.lawlabel} describe the procedures for preserving evidence as
    it relates to the removal of an aircraft or part of an aircraft;

  - [(y)]{.lawlabel} describe the procedures to be followed, after any
    exercise set out in section 302.208 or the activation of the plan
    for an emergency that requires a full emergency standby, in the
    following cases:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a post-emergency debriefing session with all
      participating organizations,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the recording of the minutes of the debriefing
      session,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} an evaluation of the effectiveness of the
      emergency plan to identify deficiencies,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} changes, if any, to be made in the emergency
      plan, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} partial testing subsequent to the modification of
      an emergency plan;

  - [(z)]{.lawlabel} describe

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the process for an annual review and update of
      the emergency plan, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the administrative procedure for the
      distribution of copies of an updated version of the emergency plan
      to the airport personnel who require them and to the organizations
      identified in the plan; and

  - [(z.1)]{.lawlabel} describe the procedures to assist in locating an
    aircraft when the airport receives notification that an ELT has been
    activated.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall include a copy of
  the following documents in the emergency plan:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the signed agreements, if any, between the airport
    operator and the resources referred to in paragraph (1)(c); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an airport grid map.

##### [On-scene Controller]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989102 .Subheading}

**[[302.204]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.204 .sectionLabel}** The on-scene
controller shall be at the emergency site and shall not have other
duties during an emergency, unless the life of a person is in danger
nearby and the on-scene controller is alone and has the ability to
assist the person.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-262, s. 2
:::

SOR/2022-267, s. 7\]]{.Repealed}

##### [Aircraft Crash Charts and Airport Grid Maps]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989109 .Subheading}

- **[[302.206]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.206
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For aircraft operating in a
  passenger or cargo configuration, the operator of an airport shall
  make available to the emergency coordination centre aircraft crash
  charts specific to the aircraft used by the air operators that use the
  airport, and shall provide copies of the charts to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the organizations responsible for fire-fighting
    services that are identified in the emergency plan; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the on-scene controller.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} In the case of aircraft that have or may have a
  seating configuration of not more than nine passenger seats, the
  operator of an airport may use, instead of the aircraft crash charts
  referred to in subsection (1), other documents containing equivalent
  information.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall have in their
  possession and review and update annually, if necessary, an airport
  grid map that includes a minimum of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an area covering at least one kilometre around each
    runway;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the airport access roads and gates; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the location of rendezvous points to which persons
    and vehicles that are responding to an emergency situation proceed
    in order to receive instructions.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall provide copies of
  the airport grid map to the airport personnel who must have one and
  the organizations identified in the emergency plan.

##### [Personnel and Training]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989122 .Subheading}

- **[[302.207]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.207
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall
  assign specific emergency response duties, other than those of an
  on-scene controller or a supervisor, only to those airport personnel
  who are identified in the emergency plan and who

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} are knowledgeable of their duties as described in
    the plan; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} have the skills to carry out their duties.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall assign to act as an
  on-scene controller or a supervisor only those airport personnel, or
  other persons authorized by the operator in the emergency plan, who
  are

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} knowledgeable about the procedures for the overall
    coordination of emergency operations at an emergency site; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} trained for the particular role that they perform.

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2022-267, s. 8\]]{.Repealed}

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} keep records of the training that was received by
    persons to meet the requirements of subsections (1) and (2);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} retain the training records for three years after
    the day on which the training was received; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} submit a copy of the training records to the
    Minister on request.

##### [Testing of the Emergency Plan]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989137 .Subheading}

- **[[302.208]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.208
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In this section, [[international
  service]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} has the same meaning as in subsection
  55(1) of the [Canada Transportation Act](/eng/acts/C-10.4).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall test the emergency
  plan by conducting a full-scale exercise

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} for the airports designated by the Minister in the
    *Canada Flight Supplement* to be used by international service, at
    intervals not exceeding two years; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} for other airports, at intervals not exceeding four
    years.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall conduct full-scale
  exercises based on scenarios that relate to a major aircraft accident
  and, at a minimum, the exercises shall include the assembly and
  deployment of fire-fighting, policing and medical services
  organizations.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall conduct a table top
  exercise each year in which no full-scale exercise is conducted.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport, when conducting a table
  top exercise, shall have

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an up-to-date list of the participants and their
    telephone numbers and the radio frequencies used to communicate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} fully operational communication equipment; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a copy of the airport grid map.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall base the table top
  exercises on scenarios that include an aircraft accident or incident.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall provide the Minister
  with a notice in writing of the date and time when a table top or
  full-scale exercise is to be carried out at least 60 days before the
  day of the exercise.

- [(8)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2022-267, s. 9\]]{.Repealed}

- [(9)]{.lawlabel} After each exercise, the operator of an airport shall
  conduct a debriefing with all the organizations identified in the plan
  and a representative of the airport personnel who participated to
  evaluate the effectiveness of the emergency plan and identify
  deficiencies.

- [(10)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall implement an action
  plan to correct any deficiencies in the emergency plan that were
  identified during a debriefing session.

- [(11)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall conduct partial
  exercises to assess proposed changes in the plan in order to correct
  deficiencies.

- [(12)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall record

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the date of an exercise;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the type of exercise;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the minutes of the debriefing session after the
    exercise; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} any action plans to correct deficiencies that were
    identified during a debriefing session.

- [(13)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall keep an exercise
  record for 10 years after the day on which the record is made.

- [(14)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall submit debriefing
  minutes and corrective action plans relating to an exercise to the
  Minister on request.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-262, s. 2
- [SOR/2022-267, s. 9](#1381613-1387796){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1381613-1387796.html"}

##### [Authorization]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989164 .Subheading}

**[[302.209]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.209 .sectionLabel}** The Minister
may, on application by the operator of an airport, provide to the
operator written authorization not to conduct the full-scale exercise
during an interval set out in paragraph 302.208(2)(a) or (b) if the
operator demonstrates that the testing requirements for a full-scale
exercise have been met through an activation of the emergency plan in
response to an emergency during that interval.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-262, s. 2
:::

**\[302.210 to 302.300 reserved\]**

#### [Division III --- Airport Wildlife Planning and Management]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989169 .Subheading}

##### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989170 .Subheading}

**[[302.301]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.301 .sectionLabel}** In this
Division,

[[waste disposal facility]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[waste disposal facility]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a landfill
    site, garbage dump, waste transfer and sorting facility, recycling
    and composting facility or commercial fish processing plant;
    ([installation d'élimination des déchets]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[wildlife strike]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[wildlife strike]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a collision between an
    aircraft and wildlife. ([impact faunique]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-85, s. 3
:::

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989176 .Subheading}

- **[[302.302]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.302
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), this
  Division applies to airports

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} that, within the preceding calendar year, had 2 800
    movements of commercial passenger-carrying aircraft operating under
    Subpart 4 or 5 of Part VII;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} that are located within a built-up area;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} that have a waste disposal facility within 15 km of
    the geometric centre of the airport;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} that had an incident where a turbine-powered
    aircraft collided with wildlife other than a bird and suffered
    damage, collided with more than one bird or ingested a bird through
    an engine; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} where the presence of wildlife hazards, including
    those referred to in section 322.302 of the Airport
    Standards-Airport Wildlife Planning and Management, has been
    observed in an airport flight pattern or movement area.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Section 302.303 applies to all airports.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-85, s. 3
- SOR/2015-160, s. 7(F)
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-302.302-20060505.html "Link to previous version of section 302.302"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Wildlife Strikes]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989187 .Subheading}

- **[[302.303]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.303
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall
  keep records of all wildlife strikes at the airport, including those
  reported by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} pilots;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} ground personnel; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} aircraft maintenance personnel when they identify
    damage to an aircraft as having been caused by a wildlife strike.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Wildlife remains that are found within 200 feet of a
  runway or an airside pavement area are presumed to be the result of a
  wildlife strike unless another cause of death is identified.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of the airport shall submit a written
  and dated report to the Minister

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} for each wildlife strike, within 30 days of its
    occurrence; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} for all wildlife strikes that occur in a calendar
    year, before March 1 of the following calendar year.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-85, s. 3
- SOR/2015-160, s. 8
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-302.303-20060505.html "Link to previous version of section 302.303"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Risk Analysis]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989199 .Subheading}

- **[[302.304]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.304
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall
  collect information in respect of the requirements set out in section
  322.304 of the Airport Standards-Airport Wildlife Planning and
  Management.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of the airport shall, after consultation
  with a representative sample of the operators in respect of an
  aircraft, air operators and private operators that use the airport,
  conduct a risk analysis that evaluates the collected information.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The risk analysis shall be in writing and include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an analysis of the risks associated with the
    wildlife hazards, including those referred to in section 322.302 of
    the Airport Standards-Airport Wildlife Planning and Management; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the measures that are necessary to manage or remove
    the hazards or to manage or mitigate the risks.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The operator of the airport shall, at the request of
  the Minister, make the risk analysis available for inspection.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-85, s. 3
:::

##### [Airport Wildlife Management Plan]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989209 .Subheading}

###### [General]{.HTitleText5} {#h-989210 .Subheading}

- **[[302.305]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.305
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall
  establish and maintain an airport wildlife management plan in
  accordance with section 322.305 of the Airport Standards --- Airport
  Wildlife Planning and Management.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of the airport shall submit the plan to
  the Minister in accordance with the requirements set out in subsection
  322.305(2) of the Airport Standards --- Airport Wildlife Planning and
  Management.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of the airport shall keep a copy of the
  plan at the airport and it shall, on request by the Minister, be made
  available to the Minister.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2019-295, s. 6\]]{.Repealed}

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The operator of the airport shall review the plan
  every two years.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} The operator of the airport shall amend the plan and
  submit the amended plan to the Minister within 30 days of the
  amendment if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the amendment is necessary as a result of the
    review conducted under subsection (5);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an incident has occurred in which a turbine-powered
    aircraft collided with wildlife other than a bird and suffered
    damage, collided with more than one bird or ingested a bird through
    an engine;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a variation in the presence of wildlife hazards,
    including those referred to in section 322.302 of the Airport
    Standards-Airport Wildlife Planning and Management, has been
    observed in an airport flight pattern or movement area; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} there has been a change

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in the wildlife management procedures or in the
      methods used to manage or mitigate wildlife hazards,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in the types of aircraft at the airport, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} in the types of aircraft operations at the
      airport.

::: HistoricalNote

  ajax-after="1194385-1195503.html"}

###### [Content]{.HTitleText5} {#h-989227 .Subheading}

**[[302.306]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.306 .sectionLabel}** An airport
wildlife management plan shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} identify and describe the risks associated with all
  wildlife hazards, including those referred to in section 322.302 of
  the Airport Standards-Airport Wildlife Planning and Management, at or
  near the airport that might affect the safe operation of aircraft,
  including the proximity of any waste disposal facility or migration
  route affecting wildlife populations near the airport;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} specify the particular measures that are used by the
  operator of the airport to manage or mitigate the risks;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} identify and describe the actions that are used by
  the operator of the airport to satisfy the requirements set out in
  section 322.306 of the Airport Standards-Airport Wildlife Planning and
  Management in respect of firearm certificates and permits, wildlife
  control permits, wildlife strikes, wildlife management logs, and
  evaluations of habitats, land uses and food sources at or near the
  airport;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} set out a policy for the management of airport
  habitats that might attract wildlife;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} set out a policy that prohibits the feeding of
  wildlife and the exposure of food wastes;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} set out a procedure to ensure that all endangered or
  protected wildlife at the airport are inventoried;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} identify the role of the personnel and agencies
  involved in wildlife management issues and provide the contact numbers
  for each; and

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} provide details of any wildlife hazard awareness
  program.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-85, s. 3
:::

###### [Training]{.HTitleText5} {#h-989239 .Subheading}

- **[[302.307]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.307
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} provide any person who has duties in respect of the
    airport wildlife management plan with training at least once every
    five years regarding their assigned duties and the matters set out
    in section 322.307 of the Airport Standards-Airport Wildlife
    Planning and Management; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} ensure that any person who has duties in respect of
    the airport wildlife management plan holds any required firearm
    permit.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of the airport shall maintain a record
  of each person's training for a period of five years and provide the
  Minister with a copy of any record, if requested.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-85, s. 3
- SOR/2015-160, s. 9
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-302.307-20061230.html "Link to previous version of section 302.307"){.PITLink}
:::

###### [Communication and Alerting Procedure]{.HTitleText5} {#h-989247 .Subheading}

**[[302.308]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.308 .sectionLabel}** The operator of
an airport shall establish a communication and alerting procedure for
wildlife management personnel in accordance with section 322.308 of the
Airport Standards-Airport Wildlife Planning and Management to alert
pilots as soon as possible of the wildlife hazards at the airport and
the risks associated with those hazards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-85, s. 3
:::

**\[302.309 to 302.400 reserved\]**

#### [Division IV --- Airport Winter Maintenance]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989252 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2007-290, s. 10

\]
:::

##### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1247222 .Subheading}

**[[302.401]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.401 .sectionLabel}** The following
definitions apply in this Division.

[[AMSCR]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[AMSCR]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} or [[Aircraft Movement Surface
    Condition Report]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a report that details
    the surface conditions of all movement areas at an airport,
    including runways and taxiways. ([AMSCR]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"}
    ou [compte rendu de l'état de la surface pour les mouvements
    d'aéronefs]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"} )

[[contaminant]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[contaminant]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means material that collects on
    a surface, including standing water, snow, slush, compacted snow,
    ice, frost, sand, and ice control
    chemicals. ([contaminant]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[CRFI]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[CRFI]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} or [[Canadian Runway Friction
    Index]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the average of the friction
    measurements taken on runway surfaces on which freezing or frozen
    contaminants are present. ([CRFI]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"} ou
    [coefficient canadien de frottement sur piste]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"} )

[[dry snow]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[dry snow]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means snow that does not contain
    sufficient water to allow the crystals to stick together or bond to
    a surface. ([neige sèche]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[ice control chemicals]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[ice control chemicals]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means chemicals used
    to prevent ice formation, to prevent ice from bonding to a surface,
    or to break up or melt ice on a surface. ([produits chimiques de
    déglaçage]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[priority 1 area]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[priority 1 area]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an airside area that,
    based on prevailing winds or operational requirements, is necessary
    to maintain the operational capability of an airport, and includes
    the features referred to in paragraph 322.411(1)(a) of the Airport
    Standards --- Airport Winter Maintenance. ([zone de priorité
    1]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[priority 2 area]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[priority 2 area]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an airside area that
    is necessary to provide additional runway availability should wind
    conditions or operational requirements change, and includes the
    features referred to in paragraph 322.411(1)(b) of the Airport
    Standards --- Airport Winter Maintenance. ([zone de priorité
    2]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[priority 3 area]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[priority 3 area]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an airside area that
    is not a priority 1 area or priority 2 area, and includes the
    features referred to in paragraph 322.411(1)(c) of the Airport
    Standards --- Airport Winter Maintenance. ([zone de priorité
    3]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[sand]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[sand]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means small particles of crushed
    angular mineral aggregates or natural sand material used to improve
    runway surface friction levels. ([sable]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[slush]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[slush]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means partially melted snow or ice,
    with a high water content, from which water readily flows. ([neige
    fondante]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[wet snow]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[wet snow]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means snow that will stick together
    when compressed but will not readily allow water to flow from it if
    squeezed. ([neige mouillée]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-118, s. 3](#1126507-1247236){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126507-1247236.html"}
:::

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1247237 .Subheading}

- **[[302.402]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.402
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to paragraph (2)(b),
  sections 302.406 and 302.407 apply in respect of an airport if
  aeroplanes at the airport are operated in an air transport service
  under Subpart 3 of Part VII.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Sections 302.410 to 302.419 apply in respect of an
  airport if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} aeroplanes at the airport are operated in an air
    transport service under Subpart 4 or 5 of Part VII; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} aeroplanes at the airport are operated in an air
    transport service under Subpart 3 of Part VII and the operator of
    the airport has decided to comply with those sections instead of
    sections 302.406 and 302.407.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-118, s. 3](#1126507-1247244){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126507-1247244.html"}
:::

##### [Notification]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1247245 .Subheading}

**[[302.403]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.403 .sectionLabel}** The operator of
an airport referred to in paragraph 302.402(2)(b) shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} provide the Minister, at least 60 days before
  implementing a decision to comply with sections 302.410 to 302.419
  instead of sections 302.406 and 302.407, with notice in writing of
  that decision;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} provide the Minister, at least 60 days before
  implementing a decision to resume complying with sections 302.406 and
  302.407, with notice in writing of that decision; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} notify the air operators that use the airport, and
  the air navigation services provider, of any change in the level of
  service provided at the airport as a result of a decision referred to
  in paragraph (a) or (b).
