##### [Winter Maintenance Measures]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1247253 .Subheading}

- **[[302.406]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.406
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Each year, before the start of
  winter maintenance operations, the operator of an airport shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} consult a representative sample of the air
    operators that use the airport about the intended level of winter
    maintenance and keep a record of the consultations;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} provide the aeronautical information publications
    provider with information, for publication in the Canada Flight
    Supplement, about the level of winter maintenance; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} include information in the airport operations
    manual about the level of winter maintenance.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of the airport shall use AMSCRs to
  report the surface conditions of all movement areas, and shall forward
  the AMSCRs to the air navigation services provider.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-118, s. 3](#1126507-1247261){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126507-1247261.html"}
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 28(F)](#1522598-1525714){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522598-1525714.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-302.406-20200515.html "Link to previous version of section 302.406"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Ice Control Chemicals and Sand]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1247262 .Subheading}

- **[[302.407]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.407
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall, on
  movement areas, use only

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the ice control chemicals specified in subsection
    322.415(1) of the Airport Standards --- Airport Winter Maintenance;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} sand that meets the requirements specified in
    subsection 322.415(2) of the Airport Standards --- Airport Winter
    Maintenance.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of the airport shall remove sand from
  movement areas, with the exception of gravel runways, as soon as

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the sand is no longer required to provide more
    friction for aircraft and service vehicles; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} there are no higher operational priorities.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-118, s. 3](#1126507-1247377){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126507-1247377.html"}
:::

**\[302.408 to 302.409 reserved\]**

##### [Airport Winter Maintenance Plan]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1247379 .Subheading}

- **[[302.410]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.410
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall
  have an airport winter maintenance plan that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} was developed by the operator after consultations
    with a representative sample of the air operators that use the
    airport; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} includes the items required under section 302.411.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of the airport shall review its airport
  winter maintenance plan at least once a year as well as each time the
  operator does not clear a priority area in accordance with the plan.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the operator of the airport determines, as a
  result of a review, that its airport winter maintenance plan should be
  amended, the operator shall consult a representative sample of the air
  operators that use the airport before amending the plan.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The operator of the airport shall keep at the airport

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an up-to-date copy of its airport winter
    maintenance plan;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a record of all consultations required under this
    section; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a record of each review required under this
    section.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-118, s. 3](#1126507-1247391){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126507-1247391.html"}
:::

##### [Content]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1247392 .Subheading}

**[[302.411]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.411 .sectionLabel}** An airport
winter maintenance plan shall include

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} procedures for identifying which airside areas are
  priority 1 areas, priority 2 areas or priority 3 areas during winter
  storm conditions;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a description of the winter maintenance operations to
  be carried out in an airside area once it is identified as a priority
  1 area, priority 2 area or priority 3 area;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} communication procedures that meet the requirements
  of subsection 322.411(2) of the Airport Standards --- Airport Winter
  Maintenance;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} procedures for publishing a NOTAM in the event of
  winter conditions that might be hazardous to aircraft operations or
  affect the use of movement areas and facilities used to provide
  services relating to aeronautics;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} safety procedures for controlling the flow of ground
  vehicles during winter maintenance operations to ensure the safety of
  persons, vehicles and aircraft;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} procedures for minimizing the risk of ice control
  chemicals --- other than the ice control chemicals specified in
  subsection 322.415(1) of the Airport Standards --- Airport Winter
  Maintenance --- being tracked onto an airside area;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} a description of the lines of authority and
  organizational relationships with respect to winter maintenance,
  including contact names and telephone numbers;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} a description of how actions undertaken as part of
  winter maintenance will be coordinated;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} a description of the arrangements for snow clearance;

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} a description of the process for reviewing and
  amending the plan;

- [(k)]{.lawlabel} a description of the administrative procedure for
  distributing the plan and its amendments; and

- [(l)]{.lawlabel} a list of all agreements respecting the provision of
  winter maintenance services for navigation aids at the airport, and
  signed copies of those agreements.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-118, s. 3](#1126507-1247407){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126507-1247407.html"}
:::

##### [Removal of Contaminants from Priority Areas]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1247408 .Subheading}

- **[[302.412]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.412
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport who
  decides to operate the airport during winter storm conditions shall
  remove contaminants

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} from priority 1 areas;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} from priority 2 areas to the extent that doing so
    does not compromise the operator's ability to keep priority 1 areas
    operational; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} from priority 3 areas after the winter storm
    conditions have ended.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the operator of the airport does not remove
  contaminants from a priority area in accordance with its airport
  winter maintenance plan, the operator shall make a record of that fact
  and the surrounding circumstances.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of the airport shall keep the record for
  two years after the day on which the operator was required to remove
  the contaminants.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-118, s. 3](#1126507-1247417){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126507-1247417.html"}
:::

##### [Snow Accumulation on or Adjacent to Threshold Areas]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1247418 .Subheading}

**[[302.413]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.413 .sectionLabel}** The operator of
an airport shall prevent snow that has accumulated on or adjacent to
threshold areas from interfering with the operation of aeroplanes by
clearing and banking the snow in a manner that meets or exceeds the
specifications set out in section 322.413 of the Airport Standards ---
Airport Winter Maintenance.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-118, s. 3](#1126507-1247421){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126507-1247421.html"}
:::

##### [Snow Accumulation Adjacent to Runways or Taxiways]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1247422 .Subheading}

**[[302.414]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.414 .sectionLabel}** The operator of
an airport shall prevent snow that has accumulated adjacent to runways
or taxiways from interfering with the operation of aeroplanes by
clearing and banking the snow in a manner that meets or exceeds the
specifications set out in section 322.414 of the Airport Standards ---
Airport Winter Maintenance.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-118, s. 3](#1126507-1247425){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126507-1247425.html"}
:::

##### [Ice Control Chemicals and Sand]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1247426 .Subheading}

- **[[302.415]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.415
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall, on
  movement areas, use only

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the ice control chemicals specified in subsection
    322.415(1) of the Airport Standards --- Airport Winter Maintenance;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} sand that meets the requirements specified in
    subsection 322.415(2) of the Airport Standards --- Airport Winter
    Maintenance.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of the airport shall remove sand from
  movement areas, with the exception of gravel runways, as soon as

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the sand is no longer required to provide more
    friction for aircraft and service vehicles; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} there are no higher operational priorities.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-118, s. 3](#1126507-1247329){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126507-1247329.html"}
:::

##### [Friction Measurement]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1247330 .Subheading}

- **[[302.416]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.416
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} carry out the measurements for the purposes of
    determining CRFIs in accordance with section 322.416 of the Airport
    Standards --- Airport Winter Maintenance;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} provide the CRFIs to the ground station in
    accordance with subsection 322.411(2) of those standards; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} maintain the accuracy of the equipment referred to
    in section 322.416 of those standards in accordance with that
    section.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the airport does not receive any aeroplanes
    operated in an air transport service under Subpart 5 of Part VII; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the airport runways are gravel and the airport does
    not receive turbo-jet-powered aeroplanes operated in an air
    transport service under Subpart 5 of Part VII.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-118, s. 3](#1126507-1247340){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126507-1247340.html"}
:::

##### [Movement Area Inspections and Reports]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1247341 .Subheading}

- **[[302.417]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.417
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} inspect movement areas and prepare AMSCRs in
    accordance with section 322.417 of the Airport Standards --- Airport
    Winter Maintenance;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} include a CRFI in each AMSCR if section 302.416
    applies to the operator;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} forward AMSCRs to the air navigation services
    provider in a manner that will permit its prompt dissemination to
    aircraft operators;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} provide the aeronautical information publications
    provider with information about the availability of CRFIs and AMSCRs
    for publication in the Canada Flight Supplement; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} include information in the airport operations
    manual about the availability of CRFIs and AMSCRs.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite paragraph (1)(b), the operator of the airport
  shall not include friction readings in an AMSCR if those friction
  readings are obtained from a runway surface using a decelerometer and
  if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the runway surface is wet but there is no
    contaminant;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} on the runway surface there is a layer of slush but
    no other contaminant;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} on the runway surface there is wet snow that, when
    stepped on or driven on, splatters, turns to slush or results in the
    presence of visible water; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} on the runway surface there is dry snow or wet snow
    that exceeds 2.5 cm (one inch) in depth.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-118, s. 3](#1126507-1247355){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126507-1247355.html"}
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 28(F)](#1522598-1525715){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522598-1525715.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-302.417-20200515.html "Link to previous version of section 302.417"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Training]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1247356 .Subheading}

- **[[302.418]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.418
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall not
  assign duties in respect of its airport winter maintenance plan to a
  person unless that person has received training from the operator on
  those duties and on the matters set out in section 322.418 of the
  Airport Standards --- Airport Winter Maintenance.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of the airport shall not assign
  supervisory duties in respect of its airport winter maintenance plan
  to a person unless that person has received training on those duties
  and on the content of the plan.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Each year, before the start of winter maintenance
  operations, the operator of the airport shall provide persons who will
  be assigned duties in respect of its airport winter maintenance plan
  with training on any amendments that have been made to the plan since
  the previous winter.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Training provided under this section shall be
  competency-based with an emphasis on performance, and shall include
  written or practical examinations.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-118, s. 3](#1126507-1247433){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126507-1247433.html"}
:::

##### [Training Records]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1247434 .Subheading}

**[[302.419]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.419 .sectionLabel}** The operator of
an airport shall keep a training record for each person who receives any
training under section 302.418, and shall keep the record for five years
after the day on which the latest training was received.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-118, s. 3](#1126507-1247437){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126507-1247437.html"}
:::

**\[302.420 to 302.499 reserved\]**

#### [Division V --- Safety Management System]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989256 .Subheading}

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989257 .Subheading}

- **[[302.500]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.500
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This Division applies to an
  applicant for, or a holder of, an airport certificate issued under
  section 302.03 in respect of the following airports:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Calgary International;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Edmonton International;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} Gander International;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} Halifax Robert L. Stanfield International;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} Montréal --- Pierre Elliott Trudeau International;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} Ottawa Macdonald-Cartier International;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} St. John's International;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} Toronto / Lester B. Pearson International;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} Vancouver International; and

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} Winnipeg James Armstrong Richardson International.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} On and after January 1, 2009, this Division applies
  to an applicant for, or a holder of, an airport certificate issued
  under section 302.03.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-290, s. 10
:::

##### [Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989273 .Subheading}

**[[302.501]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.501 .sectionLabel}** The safety
management system required under section 107.02 in respect of an
applicant for, or a holder of, an airport certificate shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} meet the requirements of Subpart 7 of Part I and
  section 302.502; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} be under the control of the accountable executive
  appointed under paragraph 106.02(1)(a).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-290, s. 10
:::

##### [Components of the Safety Management System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989279 .Subheading}

**[[302.502]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.502 .sectionLabel}** The safety
management system shall include, among others, the following components:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a safety management plan that includes

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a safety policy that the accountable executive has
    approved and communicated to all employees,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the roles and responsibilities of personnel
    assigned duties under the safety management system,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} performance goals and a means of measuring
    attainment of those goals,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a policy for the internal reporting of hazards,
    incidents and accidents, including the conditions under which
    immunity from disciplinary action will be granted, and

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} a process for reviewing the safety management
    system to determine its effectiveness;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} procedures for reporting hazards, incidents and
  accidents to the appropriate manager;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} procedures for the collection of data relating to
  hazards, incidents and accidents;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} procedures for the exchange of information in respect
  of hazards, incidents and accidents among the operators of aircraft
  and the provider of air traffic services at the airport and the
  airport operator;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} procedures for analysing data obtained under
  paragraph (c) and during an audit conducted under a quality assurance
  program required under paragraph 107.03(g) and for taking corrective
  actions;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} training requirements for the person managing the
  safety management system and for personnel assigned duties under the
  safety management system;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} procedures for making progress reports to the
  accountable executive at intervals determined by the accountable
  executive and other reports as needed in urgent cases; and

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} procedures for involving employees in the
  implementation and ongoing development of the safety management
  system.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-290, s. 10
:::

##### [Quality Assurance Program]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989296 .Subheading}

- **[[302.503]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.503
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The quality assurance program
  required under paragraph 107.03(g) in respect of an applicant for, or
  a holder of, an airport certificate shall include a process for
  quality assurance that includes periodic reviews or audits of the
  activities authorized under a certificate and reviews or audits, for
  cause, of those activities.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The holder of an airport certificate shall ensure
  that records relating to the findings resulting from the quality
  assurance program are distributed to the appropriate manager for
  corrective action and follow-up.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The holder of an airport certificate shall establish
  an audit system in respect of the quality assurance program that
  consists of the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an initial audit conducted within 12 months after

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an airport specified in subsection
      302.500(1), the later of January 1, 2008 and the day on which the
      airport certificate is issued, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of any other airport, the later of
      January 1, 2009 and the day on which the airport certificate is
      issued;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an audit of the entire quality assurance program
    carried out every three years, calculated from the initial audit, in
    one of the following ways:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a complete audit, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a series of audits conducted at intervals set
      out in the airport operations manual;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} checklists of all activities controlled by the
    airport operations manual;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a record of each occurrence of compliance or
    non-compliance with the airport operations manual found during an
    audit referred to in paragraph (a) or (b);

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} procedures for ensuring that each finding of an
    audit is communicated to the accountable executive;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} follow-up procedures for ensuring that corrective
    actions are effective; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a system for recording the findings of an audit
    referred to in paragraph (a) or (b), corrective actions and
    follow-ups.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The records resulting from a system required under
  paragraph (3)(g) shall be retained for the greater of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} two audit cycles, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} two years.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The duties related to the quality assurance program
  that involve specific tasks or activities among the activities of an
  airport shall be fulfilled by persons who are not responsible for
  carrying out those tasks or activities unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the size, nature and complexity of the operations
    and activities authorized under the airport certificate justify the
    fulfilling of those duties by the person responsible for carrying
    out those tasks or activities;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the holder of the airport certificate demonstrates
    to the Minister, by means of a risk analysis, that the fulfilling of
    those duties by the person responsible for carrying out those tasks
    or activities will not result in an unacceptable risk to aviation
    safety; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the holder of the airport certificate provides the
    Minister, in writing, with the information required under
    paragraphs (a) and (b).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-290, s. 10
- [SOR/2019-295, s. 7](#1194389-1195505){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1194389-1195505.html"}
:::

##### [Duties of the Certificate Holder]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989321 .Subheading}

**[[302.504]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.504 .sectionLabel}** The holder of
an airport certificate shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} ensure that corrective actions are taken in respect
  of any findings resulting from the safety management system referred
  to in section 302.501;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} appoint a person to manage the safety management
  system; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the person managing the safety management
  system performs the duties required under section 302.505.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-290, s. 10
:::

##### [Person Managing the Safety Management System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989328 .Subheading}

- **[[302.505]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.505
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The person managing the safety
  management system shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} implement a reporting system to ensure the timely
    collection of information related to hazards, incidents and
    accidents that may adversely affect safety;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} identify hazards and carry out risk management
    analyses of those hazards;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} investigate, analyze and identify the cause or
    probable cause of all hazards, incidents and accidents identified
    under the safety management system;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} implement a safety data system, by either
    electronic or other means, to monitor and analyze trends in hazards,
    incidents and accidents;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} monitor and evaluate the results of corrective
    actions with respect to hazards, incidents and accidents;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} monitor the concerns of the civil aviation industry
    in respect of safety and their perceived effect on the holder of the
    airport certificate; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} determine the adequacy of the training required by
    paragraph 302.502(f).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The person managing the safety management system
  shall, if a finding resulting from the safety management system
  referred to in section 302.501 is reported to them,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} determine what, if any, corrective actions are
    required and carry out those actions;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} keep a record of any determination made under
    paragraph (a) and the reason for it;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if management duties have been assigned to another
    person under subsection (3), communicate any determination regarding
    a corrective action to that person; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} notify the certificate holder of any systemic
    deficiency and of the corrective action taken.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The person managing the safety management system may
  assign the management functions for the safety management system
  referred to in section 302.501 to another person if the assignment and
  its scope are described in the airport operations manual.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The person to whom management functions have been
  assigned under subsection (3) shall notify the person managing the
  safety management system of any systemic deficiency and of the
  corrective action taken.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The responsibility and accountability of the
  accountable executive are not affected by the appointment of a person
  to manage the safety management system under paragraph 302.504(b) or
  the assignment of management functions to another person under
  subsection (3).

#### [Division VI --- Runway End Safety Area (RESA)]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1336337 .Subheading}

##### [RESA --- Obligations of Operator]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1336338 .Subheading}

- **[[302.600]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.600
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall
  ensure that a runway that is used for the take-off or landing of
  commercial aeroplanes engaged in a scheduled air service for the
  purpose of carrying passengers has a RESA that meets the requirements
  of section 302.602 if, according to the statistics referred to in
  subsection (2) or (3), the total of the number of passengers that are
  emplaned and the number of passengers that are deplaned at the airport
  is at least 325,000 per year during a period of two consecutive
  calendar years, the first period beginning the year in which this
  section comes into force.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The statistics in respect of the number of passengers
  are as published by Statistics Canada in the Airport Activity Survey.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the statistics in respect of the number of
  passengers are not published or are incomplete, the statistics are
  those provided by Statistics Canada to the Minister.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} In the case referred to in subsection (3), if the
  threshold in respect of the number of passengers referred to in
  subsection (1) has been reached, the Minister shall notify the
  operator of the airport.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall comply with the
  requirements of subsection (1)

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} within three years of the day on which the
    statistics referred to in subsection (2) are published in respect of
    the last year of a period referred to in subsection (1); or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} within three years of the day on which the Minister
    notifies the operator under subsection (4).

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (5), if a new runway is first in
  operation after the threshold in respect of the number of passengers
  referred to in subsection (1) has been reached, the operator of an
  airport shall comply with the requirements of subsection (1) beginning
  on the day on which the runway is first in operation.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} If the total of the number of passengers that are
  emplaned and the number of passengers that are deplaned at the airport
  falls below 325,000 per year during any period of three consecutive
  calendar years after the day on which this section comes into force,
  the operator of an airport referred to in subsection (1) is no longer
  required to comply with the requirements of that subsection until the
  total of the number of passengers that are emplaned and the number of
  passengers that are deplaned at the airport is at least 325,000 per
  year during a period of two consecutive calendar years.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2021-269, s. 4](#1335314-1336350){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1335314-1336350.html"}
:::

##### [RESA --- Obligations of Operator of a Listed Airport]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1336351 .Subheading}

- **[[302.601]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.601
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection 302.600(1), the
  operator of an airport referred to in the table to this section shall
  ensure that a runway that is used for the take-off or landing of
  commercial aeroplanes engaged in a scheduled air service for the
  purpose of carrying passengers has a RESA that meets the requirements
  of section 302.602.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport shall comply with the
  requirements of subsection (1) within three years of the day on which
  this section comes into force.

##### [RESA --- Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1336363 .Subheading}

- **[[302.602]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.602
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A RESA shall have a minimum length
  of 150 m and shall conform to the requirements respecting location,
  characteristics and objects in the runway end safety area set out in
  3.2 of Chapter 3 of the document entitled Aerodrome Standards and
  Recommended Practices, TP 312E, published by the Department of
  Transport.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport may reduce the length of
  the ASDA, LDA or TORA in order to obtain the minimum length referred
  to in subsection (1).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The minimum length referred to in subsection (1) does
  not apply if the operator of an airport installs an arresting system
  that is designed to stop an aeroplane in the event that the aeroplane
  overruns a runway and that conforms to the requirements regarding such
  a system set out in 3.2 of Chapter 3 of TP 312E.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} A RESA is not required before the starting point of
  the LDA if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the runway is equipped with a serviceable precision
    approach path indicator (PAPI) or abbreviated precision approach
    path indicator (APAPI); or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an instrument approach procedure with approved
    vertical guidance that is not restricted by a special authorization
    or an operations specification is available in respect of the
    runway.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of paragraph (4)(b), [[approved
  vertical guidance]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means glide slope deviation
  information provided to a pilot until the decision height is reached
  to assist in the carrying out of a three-dimensional instrument
  approach without a missed approach point, but in respect of a missed
  approach segment that begins at the decision height.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2021-269, s. 4](#1335314-1336373){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1335314-1336373.html"}
:::

##### [Notice to Minister]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1336374 .Subheading}

**[[302.603]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.603 .sectionLabel}** The operator of
an airport shall notify the Minister, no later than 90 days before the
end of the period referred to in paragraph 302.600(5)(a) or (b) or
subsection 302.601(2), as applicable, of the manner in which the
operator intends to comply with the requirements of subsection
302.600(1) or 302.601(1).

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2021-269, s. 4](#1335314-1336377){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1335314-1336377.html"}
:::

##### [Ministerial Order]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1336378 .Subheading}

**[[302.604]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-302.604 .sectionLabel}** If the operator
fails to comply with the requirements of subsection 302.600(1) or
302.601(1), the Minister is authorized to make an order requiring the
operator to reduce the length of the ASDA, LDA or TORA by the length
required to meet the minimum length of a RESA.

::: HistoricalNote
\[

#### [Division I --- General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989351 .Subheading}

##### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989352 .Subheading}

**[[303.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-303.01 .sectionLabel}** In this Subpart,

[[aircraft category for fire fighting]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[aircraft category for fire fighting]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an
    aircraft category, determined in accordance with section 303.05 for
    the purpose of fighting fires involving aircraft; ([catégorie
    d'aéronefs --- SLIA]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[aircraft emergency]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[aircraft emergency]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed,
    SOR/2002-226, s. 2\]]{.Repealed}

[[aircraft fire-fighting standards]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[aircraft fire-fighting standards]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the
    Aerodrome and Airport Standards respecting Aircraft Fire Fighting at
    Airports and Aerodromes published under the authority of the
    Minister; ([normes de lutte contre les incendies
    d'aéronefs]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[critical category for fire fighting]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[critical category for fire fighting]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means
    the aircraft category that

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in respect of a designated airport, is determined
      in accordance with section 303.07 for the purpose of establishing
      the required level of service for fighting fires involving
      aircraft at the airport, and

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in respect of a participating airport or
      aerodrome, is specified for the airport or aerodrome in the Canada
      Flight Supplement and corresponds to the level of service for
      fighting fires involving aircraft at that airport or aerodrome;
      ([catégorie critique --- SLIA]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[designated airport]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[designated airport]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed,
    SOR/2006-86, s. 2\]]{.Repealed}

[[in response posture]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[in response posture]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means, in respect of
    personnel, in a location at or near the airport or aerodrome that
    will permit an operator to obtain a satisfactory result in a
    response test referred to in subsection 303.18(4); ([en position
    d'intervention]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[participating airport or aerodrome]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[participating airport or aerodrome]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an
    airport, other than a designated airport, or an aerodrome, for which
    a critical category for fire fighting is specified in the Canada
    Flight Supplement. ([aéroport ou aérodrome
    participant]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[rescue]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[rescue]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the act of evacuating persons
    from an aircraft involved in an aircraft accident or incident at an
    airport by means of fire suppression and then, if circumstances
    permit, aircraft entry. ([sauvetage]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989366 .Subheading}

- **[[303.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-303.02
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This Subpart, except subsections
  303.03(2) and 303.04(4), applies in respect of a designated airport,
  which is an airport at which, according to the statistics referred to
  in subsection 303.06(1), the total of the number of passengers that
  are emplaned and the number of passengers that are deplaned is more
  than 180,000 per year.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} This Subpart, except subsections 303.03(1) and
  303.04(1) to (3), sections 303.06 and 303.07, subsection 303.10(2) and
  sections 303.11 and 303.12, applies in respect of a participating
  airport or aerodrome.

##### [General Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989372 .Subheading}

- **[[303.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-303.03
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a designated airport
  shall provide the aircraft fire-fighting vehicles and the personnel
  required under this Subpart to respond to an aircraft emergency at the
  airport

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an airport listed in the schedule to
    this Subpart, on the coming into force of these Regulations; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in any other case, twelve months after the
    statistics compiled in accordance with subsection 303.06(1) show
    that the airport meets the criteria for a designated airport set out
    in subsection 303.02(1).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a participating airport or aerodrome
  shall provide the aircraft fire-fighting vehicles and the personnel
  required pursuant to this Subpart that correspond to the critical
  category for fire-fighting published in the Canada Flight Supplement
  to respond to an aircraft emergency at the airport or aerodrome.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/97-518, s. 2
- SOR/2006-86, s. 4
:::

Version](section-303.03-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 303.03"){.PITLink}

##### [Hours of Operation of an Aircraft Fire-fighting Service]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989380 .Subheading}

- **[[303.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-303.04
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), the
  operator of a designated airport shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at the beginning of each month and after
    consultation with the air operators that use the airport, establish
    the hours of operation of an aircraft fire-fighting service for the
    month and ensure that those hours coincide with at least 90 per cent
    of the movements during that month by commercial passenger-carrying
    aircraft at the airport of which the operator receives notice at
    least 30 days in advance; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the critical category for fire fighting
    and the hours of operation of an aircraft fire fighting service are
    published in the Canada Flight Supplement and in a NOTAM, if the
    NOTAM is published earlier.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (5), the operator of a
  designated airport shall provide an aircraft fire-fighting service for
  the operation at the airport of aeroplanes in respect of which a type
  certificate has been issued authorizing the transport of 20 or more
  passengers if the aeroplanes are operated under

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Part VI, Subpart 4; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Part VII, Subpart 1 or 5.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a designated airport shall provide an
  aircraft fire-fighting service until an aircraft referred to in
  subsection (2) has taken off or landed or the flight has been
  cancelled.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a participating airport or aerodrome
  shall establish the hours during which an aircraft fire-fighting
  service is to be operated and shall ensure that the hours are
  published in the Canada Flight Supplement and in a NOTAM, if the NOTAM
  is published earlier.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (2) does not apply in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a cargo flight without passengers;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a ferry flight;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a positioning flight;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a training flight if no fare-paying passengers are
    on board;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the arrival of an aeroplane when the airport is
    being used for a diversion or as an alternate aerodrome; or

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the subsequent departure of an aeroplane referred
    to in paragraph (e), if it is conducted in accordance with paragraph
    602.96(7)(f).

##### [Aircraft Category for Fire Fighting]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989399 .Subheading}

- **[[303.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-303.05
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An aircraft category for fire
  fighting set out in column I of an item of the table to this
  subsection shall be established for an aircraft based on the aircraft
  overall length set out in column II of the item and the aircraft
  maximum fuselage width set out in column III of that item.

  fire fighting for the aircraft shall be one category higher than the
  category set out in column I of that item.

##### [Statistics on the Number of Passengers and Aircraft Movements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989411 .Subheading}

- **[[303.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-303.06
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an airport or
  aerodrome shall review, at least once every six months, the statistics
  in respect of the number of emplaned and deplaned passengers resulting
  from the Electronic Collection of Air Transportation Statistics
  project carried out jointly by the Department of Transport and
  Statistics Canada for the twelve months preceding the date of the
  review and determine whether the airport or aerodrome qualifies as a
  designated airport under subsection 303.02(1).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a designated airport shall compile
  monthly statistics setting out the number of movements by commercial
  passenger-carrying aircraft in each aircraft category for fire
  fighting.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a designated airport shall, at least
  once every six months, review the monthly statistics for the twelve
  months preceding the date of the review and determine the three
  consecutive months with the highest total number of movements by
  commercial passenger-carrying aircraft in all aircraft categories for
  fire fighting.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where the review shows more than one period of three
  consecutive months having the same total number of movements by
  commercial passenger-carrying aircraft, the period to be used for the
  purposes of section 303.07 is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the period involving the highest aircraft category
    for fire fighting; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where those periods involve the same highest
    aircraft category for fire fighting, the period involving the
    greatest number of movements in that category.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may, in writing, on application by the
  operator of a designated airport, authorize the operator to cease
  providing an aircraft fire-fighting service if the operator
  demonstrates by means of a risk analysis based on Standard
  CAN/CSA-Q850-97 entitled Risk Management: Guideline for
  Decision-makers as amended from time to time that the cessation of the
  aircraft fire-fighting service will not result in an unacceptable risk
  to aviation safety.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister issues an authorization under
  subsection (5), the operator of a designated airport shall submit the
  content of the authorization for publication in the Canada Flight
  Supplement and in a NOTAM, if the NOTAM is published earlier.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a designated airport shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} retain the monthly statistics referred to in
    subsection (2) for five years after the date of the review; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} provide them to the Minister at the Minister's
    request.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/97-518, s. 2
- SOR/2006-86, s. 6
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-303.06-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 303.06"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Critical Category for Fire Fighting]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989426 .Subheading}

- **[[303.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-303.07
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a designated airport
  shall determine a critical category for fire fighting for the airport
  based on the number of movements at the airport during the three-month
  period determined in accordance with subsection 303.06(3) or (4) by
  commercial passenger-carrying aircraft in the highest and the next
  highest aircraft categories for fire fighting.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where, during the period referred to in subsection
  (1), the number of movements at the designated airport by aircraft in
  the highest aircraft category for fire fighting is 700 or more, the
  critical category for fire fighting is equivalent to that highest
  aircraft category for fire fighting.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If, during the period referred to in subsection (1),
  the number of movements at the designated airport by aircraft in the
  highest aircraft category for fire fighting is less than 700, the
  critical category for fire fighting shall be determined by decreasing
  the highest aircraft category for fire fighting by one category.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the operator of a designated airport anticipates a
  period of one or more hours of movements of aircraft of a lower
  aircraft category for fire fighting only, the operator may reduce the
  critical category for fire fighting to the highest aircraft category
  for fire fighting anticipated for that period if the operator

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} documents the anticipated situation; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} notifies the appropriate air traffic services unit
    of the reduced critical category for fire fighting for publication
    in a NOTAM.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/97-518, s. 2
- SOR/2003-58, s. 5
- SOR/2003-42, s. 1
- SOR/2006-86, s. 7
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 27](#1522588-1525685){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522588-1525685.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-303.07-20060630.html "Link to previous version of section 303.07"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Division II --- Extinguishing Agents and Aircraft Fire-Fighting Vehicles]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989436 .Subheading}

##### [Extinguishing Agents and Equipment]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989437 .Subheading}

**[[303.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-303.08 .sectionLabel}** The operator of a
designated airport or of a participating airport or aerodrome shall
provide its aircraft fire-fighting service with both the principal and
the complementary extinguishing agents and the equipment delivering the
agents that meet the requirements set out in the aircraft fire-fighting
standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/97-518, s. 2
:::

##### [Extinguishing Agent and Aircraft Fire-fighting Vehicle Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989441 .Subheading}

**[[303.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-303.09 .sectionLabel}** Subject to
sections 303.10 and 303.11, the operator of a designated airport or of a
participating airport or aerodrome the critical category for fire
fighting of which is set out in column I of an item of the table to this
section shall provide to the aircraft fire-fighting service at the
airport or aerodrome the quantities of water and complementary
extinguishing agents set out in columns II and III of the item, and the
minimum number of aircraft fire-fighting vehicles set out in column IV
of that item necessary to provide the total discharge capacity set out
in column V of that item.

##### [Temporary Exemption]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989451 .Subheading}

- **[[303.10]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-303.10
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), the
  operator of a designated airport or of a participating airport or
  aerodrome does not have to meet the requirements referred to in
  section 303.09 where those requirements cannot be met because of a
  personnel shortage or unserviceable equipment at the airport or
  aerodrome caused by circumstances beyond the control of its operator
  and a notification of the reduced level of aircraft fire-fighting
  service at the airport or aerodrome has been given to the appropriate
  air traffic services unit for publication in a NOTAM.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} When the condition described in subsection (1)
  continues for seven days or more, the operator of a designated airport
  shall, no later than seven days after the onset of the condition,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} establish a plan specifying the corrective measures
    that are necessary to meet the requirements of section 303.09 and
    the dates by which those measures shall be taken, which dates shall
    be as early as practicable given the circumstances; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} submit the plan to the Minister.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a designated airport shall implement
  the submitted plan by the date specified in the plan.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/97-518, s. 2
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 27](#1522588-1525687){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522588-1525687.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-303.10-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 303.10"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Authorization Respecting Reduced Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989460 .Subheading}

- **[[303.11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-303.11
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may, in writing, on
  application by the operator of a designated airport, authorize the
  operator to meet the requirements set out in the table to section
  303.09 for a lower critical category for fire fighting than that
  established for the airport pursuant to section 303.07 where that
  operator demonstrates that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the critical category for fire fighting was the
    result of movements by unusually large commercial passenger-carrying
    aircraft or an unusually high number of movements by commercial
    passenger-carrying aircraft at the airport and either of these
    situations is unlikely to be repeated within the next year; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number of movements by, or the size of,
    commercial passenger-carrying aircraft at the airport is expected to
    be altered in a manner that would result in a lower critical
    category for fire fighting.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a written authorization has been issued
  pursuant to subsection (1), the operator of the designated airport
  shall meet the requirements set out in the table to section 303.09 for
  the lower critical category for fire fighting specified in the
  authorization and shall ensure that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} notification of the reduced level of aircraft
    fire-fighting service and the period during which the level is
    reduced is given to the appropriate air traffic services unit for
    publication in the Canada Flight Supplement and in a NOTAM, where
    the NOTAM is published earlier;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} procedures are established to restore the level of
    aircraft fire-fighting service to the previous higher level if the
    reduction in the number of movements by, or in the size of,
    commercial passenger-carrying aircraft at the airport is temporary;
    and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the procedures for a reduction in the level of
    aircraft fire-fighting service and the procedures referred to in
    paragraph (b) are set out in the airport operations manual.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/97-518, s. 2
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 27](#1522588-1525689){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522588-1525689.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-303.11-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 303.11"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Adjustment to Higher Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989471 .Subheading}

**[[303.12]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-303.12 .sectionLabel}** Where an increase
in the number of movements by, or in the size of, commercial
passenger-carrying aircraft at a designated airport results in the
establishment for the airport of a higher critical category for fire
fighting than the previous category, the operator of the airport shall
meet the requirements for that higher category as set out in the table
to section 303.09 within one year after the date of establishing the
higher critical category for fire fighting.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/97-518, s. 2
:::

#### [Division III --- Personnel Requirements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989475 .Subheading}

##### [Minimum Personnel]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989476 .Subheading}

**[[303.13]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-303.13 .sectionLabel}** During the hours
of operation of the aircraft fire-fighting service, the operator of a
designated airport or of a participating airport or aerodrome shall
ensure that trained aircraft fire-fighting personnel are in response
posture and in sufficient number to operate the aircraft fire-fighting
vehicles and apply the extinguishing agents required by section 303.09.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/97-518, s. 2
- SOR/2003-58, s. 6
:::

##### [Training of Personnel]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989480 .Subheading}

**[[303.14]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-303.14 .sectionLabel}** The operator of a
designated airport or of a participating airport or aerodrome shall
ensure that all personnel assigned to aircraft fire-fighting duties are
trained in accordance with the aircraft fire-fighting standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/97-518, s. 2
:::

##### [Equipment and Protective Clothing]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989484 .Subheading}

**[[303.15]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-303.15 .sectionLabel}** The operator of a
designated airport or of a participating airport or aerodrome shall
provide all personnel assigned to aircraft fire-fighting duties with the
equipment and protective clothing necessary to perform their duties.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/97-518, s. 2
:::

##### [Firefighter Qualifications]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989488 .Subheading}

- **[[303.16]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-303.16
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No operator of a designated airport
  or of a participating airport or aerodrome shall permit a person to
  act and no person shall act as an aircraft firefighter at the airport
  or aerodrome unless the person has, within the previous 12 months,
  successfully completed the training specified in the aircraft
  fire-fighting standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a designated airport or of a
  participating airport or aerodrome shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} maintain, for each aircraft firefighter, a training
    record containing the information specified in the aircraft
    fire-fighting standards;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} keep the training record for three years after the
    day on which the aircraft firefighter leaves the service of the
    airport or aerodrome; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} at the request of the Minister, provide the
    Minister with a copy of the training record.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/97-518, s. 2
- [SOR/2022-267, s. 10(E)](#1381614-1387798){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1381614-1387798.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-303.16-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 303.16"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Division IV --- Response Readiness]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989497 .Subheading}

##### [Personnel Readiness]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989498 .Subheading}

**[[303.17]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-303.17 .sectionLabel}** The operator of a
designated airport or of a participating airport or aerodrome shall
ensure that, during the hours of operation of its aircraft fire-fighting
service, of the fire-fighting personnel required to be available
pursuant to section 303.13, the number of personnel capable of immediate
response is sufficient to meet the requirements of the response test
referred to in section 303.18.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/97-518, s. 2
:::

##### [Response Test]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989502 .Subheading}

- **[[303.18]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-303.18
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a designated airport
  or of a participating airport or aerodrome shall carry out a response
  test to evaluate the response time and effectiveness of the aircraft
  fire-fighting service required to be maintained during the hours of
  operation specified in section 303.04

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} every 12 months; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} at any time at the request of the Minister, where
    the Minister has reasonable grounds to believe that the aircraft
    fire-fighting service at the airport or aerodrome does not meet the
    requirements of this Subpart.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a designated airport or of a
  participating airport or aerodrome shall give the Minister at least
  four weeks written notice of the date on which a response test is to
  be carried out.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a designated airport or of a
  participating airport or aerodrome shall provide the Minister with a
  copy of the results of a response test within 14 days after the date
  of the test.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} A response test at a designated airport or at a
  participating airport or aerodrome has a satisfactory result if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} within three minutes after an alarm is sounded,
    aircraft fire-fighting vehicles in a number sufficient for applying
    the principal extinguishing agent at 50 per cent of the total
    discharge capacity required by section 303.09 are dispatched from
    their assigned position and, under optimum surface and visibility
    conditions at the airport or aerodrome, reach the midpoint of the
    farthest runway serving commercial passenger-carrying aircraft, or
    another predetermined point of comparable distance and terrain; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} within four minutes after the alarm is sounded, any
    other aircraft fire-fighting vehicle required by section 303.09
    reaches the location referred to in paragraph (a).

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a designated airport or of a
  participating airport or aerodrome shall record the results of a
  response test and keep the record for two years after the date of the
  test.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} If a response test does not have a satisfactory
  result, the operator of a designated airport or of a participating
  airport or aerodrome shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} within six hours after the test, identify the
    deficiencies that caused the result and notify the appropriate air
    traffic services unit of the critical category for fire fighting
    that corresponds to the level of service that can be provided, for
    publication in a NOTAM; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} within seven days after the test, if any deficiency
    is not corrected, submit a plan to the Minister specifying the
    measures necessary to obtain a satisfactory result and the dates by
    which they must be taken, which shall be as early as practicable
    given the circumstances.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a designated airport or of a
  participating airport or aerodrome shall implement the submitted plan
  by the dates specified in the plan.

#### [Division V --- Communication and Alerting System]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989519 .Subheading}

##### [Requirement]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989520 .Subheading}

**[[303.19]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-303.19 .sectionLabel}** The operator of a
designated airport or of a participating airport or aerodrome shall
provide a communication and alerting system that meets the aircraft
fire-fighting standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/97-518, s. 2
:::

##### [Transitional Provisions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989524 .Subheading}

- **[[303.20]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-303.20
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a designated airport
  shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} until November 30, 1998, except in respect of
    aircraft referred to in subsection 303.04(2), maintain the aircraft
    fire-fighting service that was provided on November 30, 1997; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} effective December 1, 1998, meet the requirements
    for an aircraft fire-fighting service prescribed in subsections
    303.03(1) and 303.04(1) and sections 303.07 to 303.19.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a participating airport or aerodrome
  shall, effective December 1, 1998, meet the requirements for an
  aircraft fire-fighting service prescribed in subsections 303.03(2) and
  303.04(4), sections 303.08 and 303.09, subsection 303.10(1) and
  sections 303.13 to 303.19.

### [Subpart 4 -- \[Reserved\]]{.HTitleText2} {#h-989535 .Subheading}

### [Subpart 5 -- Heliports]{.HTitleText2} {#h-989536 .Subheading}

#### [Division I --- General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989537 .Subheading}

##### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989538 .Subheading}

**[[305.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.01 .sectionLabel}** The following
definitions apply in this Subpart.

[[applicable heliport standard]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[applicable heliport standard]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the
    standard that is applicable to a heliport or to a part of it, or to
    its administration and operation, as determined under subsection
    305.17(1). ([norme sur les héliports applicable]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[FATO]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[FATO]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a final approach and take-off
    area, which consists of a defined area over which the final phase of
    a helicopter approach manoeuvre to hover or land is completed and
    from which the take-off manoeuvre is commenced.
    ([FATO]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[heliport certificate]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[heliport certificate]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a certificate
    issued under section 305.08, 305.11 or 305.12. ([certificat
    d'héliport]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[heliport closed marking]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[heliport closed marking]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a marking that
    meets the requirements of subsection 305.41(1). ([marque de zone
    fermée d'héliport]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[heliport operations manual]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[heliport operations manual]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} or
    [[HOM]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed, SOR/2022-267, s.
    12\]]{.Repealed}

[[standard 621.19]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[standard 621.19]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed, SOR/2011-285, s.
    4\]]{.Repealed}

[[TLOF]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[TLOF]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a touchdown and lift off area,
    which consists of a load-bearing area on which a helicopter may
    touch down or lift off. ([TLOF]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
- SOR/2011-285, s. 4
- [SOR/2019-122, s. 2](#1126313-1130985){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126313-1130985.html"}
- [SOR/2022-267, s. 12](#1381618-1387822){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1381618-1387822.html"}
:::

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989549 .Subheading}

- **[[305.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.02
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), this
  Subpart applies in respect of the operation of a heliport

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} that is located within a built-up area of a city or
    town;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} that is used by an air operator providing a
    scheduled air service for the purpose of transporting persons;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} for which an instrument approach procedure to
    precision limits is established in accordance with the applicable
    heliport standard; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} that is any other heliport in respect of which the
    issuance of a heliport certificate would be in the public interest
    and would further the safe operation of the heliport.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} This Subpart does not apply in respect of a military
  heliport.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
:::

##### [Requirement to Hold a Heliport Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989559 .Subheading}

**[[305.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.03 .sectionLabel}** A person shall
not operate a heliport referred to in subsection 305.02(1) unless a
heliport certificate is issued in respect of the heliport.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
- [SOR/2019-295, s. 8](#1194391-1195507){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1194391-1195507.html"}
:::

Version](section-305.03-20070630.html "Link to previous version of section 305.03"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Eligibility to Hold a Heliport Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989563 .Subheading}

**[[305.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.04 .sectionLabel}** A person is
eligible to hold a heliport certificate if they are

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a citizen of Canada;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a permanent resident of Canada;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a corporation incorporated under the territorial,
  provincial or federal laws of Canada; or

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a municipal, provincial or federal entity.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
:::

##### [Management Agreement]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989571 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2015-160, s. 10(F)

\]
:::

**[[305.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.05 .sectionLabel}** No heliport
operator shall manage another heliport operator's heliport unless they
are authorized to do so in the heliport operations manual of the other
operator's heliport.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
:::

**\[305.06 and 305.07 reserved\]**

#### [Division II --- Certification]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989578 .Subheading}

##### [Application and Issuance of a Heliport Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989579 .Subheading}

- **[[305.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.08
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for a heliport
  certificate shall, with their application, submit to the Minister for
  approval a copy of a proposed heliport emergency response plan and a
  copy of a proposed heliport operations manual that describes

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the manner in which the heliport meets the
    certification requirements set out in these Regulations; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the physical characteristics of the heliport.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The applicant shall include in the application

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the heliport classification; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} proof that the applicant has consulted with the
    relevant local government authority relating to the proposed
    heliport and adjacent land.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall issue a heliport certificate to
  the applicant authorizing them to operate an aerodrome as a heliport
  if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the proposed heliport operations manual is approved
    by the Minister in accordance with subsection (5) and the applicant
    demonstrates to the Minister the ability to

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} maintain an organizational structure in
      accordance with the requirements of the heliport operations
      manual, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} meet the operational requirements set out in
      their heliport operations manual; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the proposed heliport emergency response plan meets
    the applicable requirements of section 305.45.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (3), the applicant
  shall have

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an organization capable of exercising heliport
    operational management; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} operational support services and equipment that
    meet the requirements set out in their heliport operations manual.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall approve the proposed heliport
  operations manual if it

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} accurately describes the physical characteristics
    of the heliport; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} meets the certification requirements set out in
    these Regulations.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} If a heliport does not meet a certification
  requirement set out in these Regulations, the Minister may specify
  replacement conditions to be included in the heliport operations
  manual that relate to the same subject matter as the unmet requirement
  and that are necessary to ensure an equivalent level of safety.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
- SOR/2015-160, s. 11(F)
- [SOR/2022-267, s. 13](#1381619-1387821){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1381619-1387821.html"}
:::

::: PITLink

Version](section-305.08-20150831.html "Link to previous version of section 305.08"){.PITLink}

##### [Contents of a Heliport Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989596 .Subheading}

**[[305.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.09 .sectionLabel}** A heliport
certificate shall contain the following information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the certificate number;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name of the heliport;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the name of the heliport operator;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the signature of the Minister; and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the date of issue.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
:::

##### [General Conditions of a Heliport Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989605 .Subheading}

- **[[305.10]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.10
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a heliport certificate
  shall ensure that the heliport meets the applicable requirements set
  out in these Regulations and in the applicable heliport standard.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a heliport certificate shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} maintain the organizational structure referred to
    in subparagraph 305.08(3)(a)(i); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} notify the Minister within 10 working days after
    any change in its legal name, trade name or managerial personnel.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8

:::

Version](section-305.10-20221207.html "Link to previous version of section 305.10"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Transfer of a Heliport Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989614 .Subheading}

**[[305.11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.11 .sectionLabel}** The Minister
shall approve the transfer of a heliport certificate to a transferee and
issue an amended heliport certificate only if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the current holder of the heliport certificate
  notifies the Minister in writing at least 14 days before ceasing to
  operate the heliport that they will cease to operate the heliport as
  of the date specified in the notice and of the name of the transferee;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the transferee applies in writing to the Minister for
  the issuance of a new heliport certificate and includes a copy of the
  transfer notice referred to in paragraph (a) within 14 days before the
  current holder ceases to operate the heliport; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the requirements set out in section 305.10 are met on
  the day of transfer and there are no indications that they will not
  continue to be met.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
:::

##### [Interim Heliport Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989621 .Subheading}

- **[[305.12]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.12
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may issue an interim
  heliport certificate in writing to the following persons authorizing
  them to operate a heliport:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an applicant referred to in section 305.08, until
    the day of issuance of the heliport certificate that will be issued
    to the applicant as soon as the application procedure in respect of
    the issuance is completed; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a transferee referred to in section 305.11, until
    the day of issuance of an amended heliport certificate in respect of
    the heliport that will be issued to the transferee as soon as the
    application procedure in respect of the transfer is completed.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An interim heliport certificate expires on the
  earlier of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the day on which the heliport certificate or the
    amended heliport certificate is issued, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the day specified in the interim heliport
    certificate as the day on which it will expire.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Except for sections 305.08 and 305.09, this Subpart
  applies in respect of an interim heliport certificate in the same
  manner as it applies in respect of a heliport certificate.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
:::

**\[305.13 to 305.16 reserved\]**

#### [Division III --- Operator of a Heliport]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989633 .Subheading}

##### [Obligations of an Operator]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989634 .Subheading}

- **[[305.17]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.17
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall
  comply with the requirements

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} with respect to the heliport as a whole, the
    following heliport standards as identified in their heliport
    operations manual:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} unless the operator has voluntarily adopted the
      standard referred to in subparagraph (ii), for heliports in
      respect of which a heliport certificate was issued before the
      coming into force of these Regulations, the Heliport and Helideck
      Standards and Recommended Practices, TP 2586E, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} for any other heliport, standard 325 ---
      Heliport Standards, as they read on the day on which the heliport
      certificate was issued;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} with respect to any procedure pertaining to the
    administration, heliport traffic management, safety and security,
    emergency response and heliport maintenance, standard 325 ---
    Heliport Standards; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} with respect to any replacement or improvement to
    the heliport since the day on which the heliport certificate was
    issued, the following heliport standards:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} for parts or facilities of the heliport that
      returned to service before the coming into force of these
      Regulations, the most recent applicable heliport standard for the
      heliport as identified in their heliport operations manual, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} for parts or facilities of the heliport returned
      to service on or after the day of coming into force of these
      Regulations, standard 325 --- Heliport Standards, as they read on
      the day on which the part or facility was returned to service.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} review each aeronautical information publication as
    soon as possible after its issuance and immediately after the review
    notify the Minister and the provider of aeronautical information
    services of any inaccurate information contained in the publication
    that pertains to the heliport that they operate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} notify the provider of an aeronautical information
    publication before any planned change to the heliport, the heliport
    facilities or the level of service at the heliport that would affect
    the accuracy of information contained in the publication;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the notification is in accordance with
    the processes and procedures established by the provider of the
    aeronautical information services to meet the standards referred to
    in Part VIII;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} notify the provider of aeronautical information
    services of all changes to operational information published in the
    aeronautical information publications; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} notify the Minister in writing of any change in
    heliport operations within 14 days after the day of the change and
    take the following measures, as applicable:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} if a hazardous condition has been identified,
      have a NOTAM issued identifying the hazard, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if a change in heliport operations constitutes a
      change to the provisions identified in the heliport certificate,
      ensure that the change has been approved by the Minister.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), the operator of a heliport
  shall give to the Minister, and cause to be received at the
  appropriate air traffic services unit, immediate notice of any of the
  following circumstances of which the operator has knowledge:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any projection by an object through an obstacle
    limitation surface relating to the heliport;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the existence of any obstruction or hazardous
    condition affecting aviation safety at or in the vicinity of the
    heliport;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any reduction in the level of services at the
    heliport that are set out in an aeronautical information publication
    as being provided at the heliport;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the closure of any part of the manoeuvring area of
    the heliport; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} any other conditions that could be hazardous to
    aviation safety at the heliport and against which precautions are
    warranted.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where it is not feasible for the operator of a
  heliport to cause notice of a circumstance referred to in
  subsection (3) to be received at the appropriate air traffic services
  unit, the operator of the heliport shall give immediate notice
  directly to the pilots who may be affected by that circumstance.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} Prior to the use of a heliport for helicopter
  operations, the operator of the heliport shall remove from the surface
  of the heliport, or from the surrounding ground over which the
  operator has control, any vehicle or other obstruction that is likely
  to be hazardous to aviation safety.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
- SOR/2015-160, s. 12
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 26](#1522575-1525662){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522575-1525662.html"}
:::

##### [Heliport Operations Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989662 .Subheading}

- **[[305.18]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.18
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall, as
  soon as possible after the issuance of the heliport certificate,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} provide the Minister with a copy of the heliport
    operations manual as approved under subsection 305.08(5) and any
    amendments to the manual approved under subsection (3); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} distribute copies of the applicable portions and
    amendments to the applicable persons and institutions referred to in
    the manual.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of the heliport shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} keep their heliport operations manual up to date;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} submit to the Minister for approval any proposed
    amendment to their heliport operations manual.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall approve the amended heliport
  operations manual if it meets the requirements of subsection
  305.08(5).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
- SOR/2015-160, s. 13
- [SOR/2022-267, s. 15](#1381623-1387831){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1381623-1387831.html"}
:::
