[Previous
Version](section-305.18-20150831.html "Link to previous version of section 305.18"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Division IV --- General Certification Requirements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989672 .Subheading}

##### [Heliport Classification]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989673 .Subheading}

- **[[305.19]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.19
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall
  determine the heliport classification in accordance with standard 325
  --- Heliport Standards in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the classification of non-instrument heliports; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} performance requirements of helicopters that are
    expected to use the heliport.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall review the heliport
  classification if there are changes to the obstacles at or in the
  vicinity of the heliport.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
- [SOR/2022-267, s. 16](#1381628-1387840){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1381628-1387840.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-305.19-20070630.html "Link to previous version of section 305.19"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Operational Limits]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989679 .Subheading}

**[[305.20]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.20 .sectionLabel}** The operator of a
heliport shall determine, and record in their heliport operations
manual, the heliport operational limitations in accordance with the
applicable heliport standard with respect to

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} load bearing strength of the TLOF when required by
  the applicable heliport standard;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the maximum helicopter overall length for which each
  operational area at a heliport is certified; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the heliport classification as specified in paragraph
  305.19(a) and category as determined in accordance with the applicable
  heliport standard.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
:::

##### [Units of Measurement]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989686 .Subheading}

**[[305.21]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.21 .sectionLabel}** Unless otherwise
specified in the applicable heliport standard, units of measurement used
in this Division and in the heliport operations manual shall use the
following rounding rules and specified measurement units:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} elevations to the nearest foot;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} linear dimensions to the nearest metre;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} geographic coordinates in latitude and longitude to
  the nearest second;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} geographic coordinates measured in accordance with
  North American Datum 1983;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} bearings to the nearest degree;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} water depths, measured in the specified unit
  expressed, to the nearest foot or metre; and

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} range of tides or water levels, measured in the
  specified unit expressed, to the nearest foot or metre.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
:::

**\[305.22 to 305.24 reserved\]**

#### [Division V --- Physical Characteristics]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989698 .Subheading}

- **[[305.25]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.25
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall
  ensure that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the heliport has at least one FATO; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} no FATO is used to accommodate the manoeuvres of
    more than one helicopter at a time.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (3) to (6), the operator of a
  heliport shall ensure that the heliport meets the requirements set out
  in the applicable heliport standard in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} FATOs;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} safety areas;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} rejected take-off areas, if applicable;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} helicopter clearways, if applicable;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} TLOFs, if applicable;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} taxiways as follows, if applicable:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} air taxiways,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} helicopter ground taxiways,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} helicopter ground taxiway shoulders, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} helicopter ground taxiway strips;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} aprons, if applicable; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} helicopter parking positions, if applicable.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a surface-level heliport shall ensure
  that the heliport meets the special requirements for a surface-level
  heliport set out in the applicable heliport standard in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} TLOFs;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} taxiways; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} aprons.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an elevated or rooftop heliport shall
  ensure that the heliport meets the special requirements for an
  elevated or rooftop heliport set out in the applicable heliport
  standard in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} TLOFs;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} safety nets; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} helicopter parking positions.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport located on an aerodrome
  primarily designed to serve aeroplanes shall ensure that the heliport
  meets the special requirements for a heliport located on an aerodrome
  set out in the applicable heliport standard in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} application of additional standards regarding
    aerodromes;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} FATOs;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} ground taxiway separation distances;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} taxi-holding positions;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} aprons; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} helicopter parking positions.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an H1 heliport shall ensure that the
  heliport meets the special requirements for an H1 heliport set out in
  the applicable heliport standard in respect of FATOs and TLOFs.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
:::

**\[305.26 to 305.28 reserved\]**

#### [Division VI --- Obstacle Limitation Surfaces]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989735 .Subheading}

- **[[305.29]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.29
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) to (4),
  the operator of a heliport shall establish the following obstacle
  limitation surfaces in accordance with the applicable heliport
  standard for a non-instrument, non-precision or precision FATO and
  meet the special requirements for the surfaces and any obstacles that
  may affect them, set out in the applicable heliport standard:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} approach surfaces;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} take-off surfaces; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} transitional surfaces.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an H1 heliport shall ensure that the
  heliport meets the special requirements for obstacle limitation
  surfaces for non-instrument FATOs set out in the applicable heliport
  standard for an H1 heliport in respect of approach or take-off
  surfaces.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an H1 heliport shall conduct a survey
  of the approach and take-off surface to determine obstacle information
  and submit a copy to the Minister at the time of the initial heliport
  certification and after that at least once every five years, unless no
  new obstacle has been established in the approach and take-off surface
  during the five-year period and a report to that effect is made to the
  Minister.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an H2 heliport shall ensure that the
  heliport meets the special requirements for obstacle limitation
  surfaces for non-instrument FATOs set out in the applicable heliport
  standard for an H2 heliport in respect of approach or take-off
  surfaces.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport equipped with an
  instrument FATO shall ensure that the heliport meets the special
  requirements for obstacle limitation surfaces for instrument FATOs set
  out in the applicable heliport standard.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
:::

**\[305.30 reserved\]**

#### [Division VII --- Visual Aids for Air Navigation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989748 .Subheading}

- **[[305.31]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.31
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall
  equip the heliport with at least one wind direction indicator and meet
  the requirements for wind direction indicators set out in the
  applicable heliport standard.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall meet the
  requirements for heliport markings set out in the applicable heliport
  standard in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} heliport identification marking;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a hospital heliport, hospital
    heliport identification marking;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} an aiming point marking for each FATO;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} FATO edge marking;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a FATO designation marking for each FATO;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a FATO centre line marking for each FATO;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} approach and take-off direction indicator marking;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} a TLOF edge marking for each TLOF;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the maximum allowable helicopter weight marking for
    each TLOF;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} the following taxiway markings:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} taxiway centre line marking,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} taxiway holding position marking, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} taxiway edge marking;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} where the apron edge is not easily identifiable, an
    apron edge marking;

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} where a helicopter parking position is provided, a
    helicopter parking position marking;

  - [(m)]{.lawlabel} where a helicopter parking position is provided and
    helicopters are required to have a specific alignment on the parking
    position, an alignment marking;

  - [(n)]{.lawlabel} where a helicopter parking position is not large
    enough for the largest helicopter for which the heliport is designed
    or where the size of the parking position is limited by the minimum
    separation requirement to an obstacle or an adjacent parking
    position, a helicopter parking position information marking; and

  - [(o)]{.lawlabel} where passengers are required to walk on a specific
    path on an apron between a helicopter parking position and the
    passenger terminal, an apron passenger path marking.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
- SOR/2015-160, s. 14(F)
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-305.31-20070630.html "Link to previous version of section 305.31"){.PITLink}
:::

**\[305.32 reserved\]**

#### [Division VIII --- Lights]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989773 .Subheading}

- **[[305.33]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.33
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall
  extinguish, screen or otherwise modify a ground light, other than an
  aeronautical ground light, that may cause confusion to heliport users
  within the heliport boundary or other spaces within the boundaries of
  the control of the heliport operator.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall meet the
  requirements set out in the applicable heliport standard in respect of
  the installation of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} elevated approach lights;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} elevated lights for operational areas;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} inset lights;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} light intensity and control; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a heliport beacon.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport equipped with a
  non-instrument FATO that is certified to be available for use at night
  shall provide an approach and take-off direction light that meets the
  requirements set out in the applicable heliport standard where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at least one approach and departure path is
    required to be indicated to pilots; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} obstacle clearance, noise abatement or air traffic
    control procedures require that a specific direction be flown.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall provide a visual
  approach slope indicator system that meets the requirements set out in
  the applicable heliport standard where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} there are inadequate visual references;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} obstacle clearance, noise abatement or air traffic
    control procedures require that a particular slope be flown; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the surrounding terrain may produce misleading
    information.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} Where a heliport approach path indicator or an
  abbreviated heliport approach path indicator is provided at a
  heliport, the visual approach slope indicator system shall meet the
  general design requirements and specific requirements set out in the
  applicable heliport standard.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall monitor the visual
  approach slope indicator system provided at a heliport in accordance
  with the requirements of the applicable heliport standard.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} Where a visual approach slope indicator system is
  provided, the operator of a heliport shall provide an obstacle
  protection surface (OPS) in accordance with the applicable heliport
  standard.

- [(8)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall provide FATO lights
  that meet the requirements of the applicable heliport standard for

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a surface-level heliport unless the FATO and the
    TLOF are coincidental or the extent of the FATO is conspicuous;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an instrument FATO; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} where an illuminated TLOF is not provided, a FATO
    that is certified to be available for use at night unless the FATO
    edge marking is clearly visible to heliport users by means of
    external floodlighting.

- [(9)]{.lawlabel} Where a TLOF is not located within a FATO that is
  certified to be available for use at night, the operator of a heliport
  shall ensure the aiming point is illuminated in accordance with the
  applicable heliport standard.

- [(10)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall provide TLOF lights
  consisting of perimeter lights, floodlights or luminescent panels for
  a TLOF that is certified to be available for use at night and, if the
  perimeter of the TLOF is not coincidental with that of the FATO, in
  accordance with the requirements of the applicable heliport standard.

- [(11)]{.lawlabel} Where a rejected take-off area is established for a
  surface-level heliport that is certified to be available for use at
  night, the operator of a heliport shall provide in that area rejected
  take-off area lights in accordance with the requirements of the
  applicable heliport standard.

- [(12)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall provide taxiway
  centre line lights in accordance with the requirements of the
  applicable heliport standard for a taxiway that is used in runway
  visual range conditions of less than 1200 feet or in conditions of
  ground visibility of less than one-quarter statute mile.

- [(13)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall provide taxiway
  edge lights in accordance with the requirements of the applicable
  heliport standard for a taxiway that is available at a heliport that
  is certified to be available for use at night and that is not provided
  with taxiway centre line lights.

- [(14)]{.lawlabel} Where an apron is available at a heliport that is
  certified to be available for use at night, the operator of the
  heliport shall provide apron edge lights, retro-reflective edge
  markers or apron floodlighting in accordance with the requirements of
  the applicable heliport standard.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
- SOR/2015-160, s. 15
- [SOR/2019-119, s. 10](#1126705-1144141){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126705-1144141.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-305.33-20150831.html "Link to previous version of section 305.33"){.PITLink}
:::

**\[305.34 reserved\]**

#### [Division IX --- Markers]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989805 .Subheading}

- **[[305.35]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.35
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall
  ensure that the markers installed at the heliport are either flush
  mounted or lightweight and frangibly mounted and in accordance with
  the requirements of the applicable heliport standard.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall provide FATO markers
  where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a FATO edge marking is not provided; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the extent of the FATO and the adjacent ground is
    not conspicuous.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall provide ground
  taxiway edge markers in accordance with the requirements of the
  applicable heliport standard if the helicopters must travel along a
  ground taxiway to or from a FATO to an apron, unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the edges of the taxiway are conspicuous;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} taxiway centre line lights are provided;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} taxiway edge lights are provided; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} taxiway centre line markers are provided.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall provide air taxiway
  markers if the helicopters must travel by air to or from a FATO to an
  apron via a specific corridor in accordance with the applicable
  heliport standard.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
- SOR/2015-160, s. 16
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-305.35-20070630.html "Link to previous version of section 305.35"){.PITLink}
:::

**\[305.36 reserved\]**

#### [Division X --- Visual Aids for Denoting Obstacles]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989820 .Subheading}

##### [Requirements for Marking or Lighting Obstacles]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989821 .Subheading}

- **[[305.37]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.37
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), the
  operator of a heliport shall ensure that obstacles, other than
  aircraft, on the movement, manoeuvring and safety areas of the
  heliport are marked and lighted as follows:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} vehicles and other mobile obstacles on the movement
    area shall be marked so as to be visible to pilots during aircraft
    operations;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the heliport is used at night or in
    conditions of low visibility, vehicles and other mobile obstacles on
    the manoeuvring area shall be lighted;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} elevated aeronautical ground lights on the movement
    area shall be marked so as to be conspicuous by day; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in accordance with the applicable heliport
    standard, a fixed obstacle located on the safety area shall be

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} marked, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where the heliport is certified to be available
      for use at night, lighted.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall mark and, if the
  heliport is certified to be available for use at night, light fixed
  obstacles located within the area identified in the applicable
  heliport standard, except where the obstacle is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} shielded by another fixed obstacle that is marked
    in accordance with Standard 621;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} conspicuous by reason of its shape, dimensions or
    colour;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} identified in an aeronautical evaluation as being
    sufficiently lit by ambient light at night; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} not more than 150 m above the adjacent ground and
    lighted in accordance with Standard 621.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport where a fixed obstacle
  that is more than 150 m above the surrounding ground is located within
  the area identified in the applicable heliport standard shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} light the obstacle by high-intensity obstacle
    lights by day in accordance with Standard 621; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} mark the obstacle in accordance with the applicable
    heliport standard.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall mark an elevated
  obstacle on the helicopter ground taxiway strips and, where the
  heliport is certified to be available for use at night, light the
  obstacle.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall mark and, if
  applicable, light an obstacle referred to in subsection (2) unless an
  aeronautical evaluation determines that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the obstacle is conspicuous by reason of its shape,
    dimensions or colour; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} retro-reflective tape or markers are sufficiently
    conspicuous to be used instead of lights.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
- SOR/2011-285, s. 7
- SOR/2015-160, s. 17
- [SOR/2019-119, s. 11(E)](#1126707-1144143){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126707-1144143.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-305.37-20150831.html "Link to previous version of section 305.37"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Marking Obstacles]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989844 .Subheading}

- **[[305.38]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.38
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall
  ensure that a fixed obstacle or a mobile obstacle on the heliport is
  marked in accordance with the requirements of the applicable heliport
  standard.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Obstacles required to be marked shall, in accordance
  with Standard 621, be

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} coloured;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} marked by markers; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} marked by flags.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
- SOR/2011-285, s. 7
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-305.38-20070630.html "Link to previous version of section 305.38"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Lighting Obstacles]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989853 .Subheading}

- **[[305.39]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.39
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall
  light a fixed obstacle in accordance with Standard 621.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall ensure that
  maintenance and service vehicles in use display lights in accordance
  with the requirements of the applicable heliport standard.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall ensure that
  emergency vehicles in use that are required to be lighted display the
  lights specified in the applicable heliport standard.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
- SOR/2011-285, s. 7
:::

[Previous
Version](section-305.39-20070630.html "Link to previous version of section 305.39"){.PITLink}
:::

**\[305.40 reserved\]**

#### [Division XI --- Visual Aids for Denoting Restricted Use Areas]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989861 .Subheading}

- **[[305.41]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.41
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} When a FATO, helicopter parking
  position, taxiway, or any part of those areas is permanently closed,
  the operator of a heliport shall display a closed marking on the area
  that meets the requirements of the applicable heliport standard.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} When an area of a heliport is temporarily closed or
  an area is snow-covered, the heliport operator shall ensure that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} notice of the closure is

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} included in the Canada Flight Supplement, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} reported in a NOTAM; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a closed marking referred to in subsection (1) is
    displayed on the affected area.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall ensure that
  non-load-bearing surfaces adjacent to a FATO, helicopter parking
  position or taxiway that cannot be visually distinguished from
  load-bearing surfaces are marked as set out in the applicable heliport
  standard.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall ensure that
  unserviceability markers consisting of flags, cones or marker boards
  that meet the requirements of the applicable heliport standard and are
  positioned in conformity with that standard are displayed on any part
  of a taxiway or apron that is unfit for the movement of aircraft.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall ensure that
  unserviceability lights that meet the requirements of the applicable
  heliport standard are displayed in conformity with that standard
  wherever any portion of a taxiway or apron at a heliport that is
  certified to be available for use at night is unfit for the movement
  of aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
:::

**\[305.42 reserved\]**

#### [Division XII --- Equipment and Installations]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989875 .Subheading}

- **[[305.43]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.43
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall
  ensure that the lights of a visual approach slope indicator system,
  when required and installed as specified in subsection 305.33(4), are
  aligned by means of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a daily inspection of alignment and, if necessary,
    a correction of any misalignment of more than 3 minutes of arc; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an automatic shut-off switch installed in the
    system.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall ensure that a fence
  or other barrier is installed on the heliport and that the fence or
  other barrier meets the requirements of the applicable heliport
  standard.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport or a person under the
  operator's authority shall direct any vehicle that is operated on an
  apron or manoeuvring area of the heliport or, in the case of a vehicle
  in a manoeuvring area, shall ensure that the vehicle's operation is
  under the direction of the air traffic services unit or the heliport
  operator or a person working under their authority, in accordance with
  the requirements of the applicable heliport standard.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The operator of the heliport shall ensure that the
  drivers of vehicles on an apron or manoeuvring area are trained for
  the tasks to be performed and that they know they must comply with
  instructions issued by the air traffic services unit or the heliport
  operator or a person working under their authority.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall ensure that
  equipment required for air navigation purposes that is located on a
  safety area, a taxiway strip or within the separation distances
  specified in the applicable heliport standard is located, constructed
  and installed in accordance with that standard.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall ensure that visual
  aids, precision approach FATO lights and centre line lights on a
  taxiway are maintained in accordance with the applicable heliport
  standard.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
:::

**\[305.44 reserved\]**

#### [Division XIII --- Emergency and Other Services]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989888 .Subheading}

##### [Emergency Response Plan]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989889 .Subheading}

- **[[305.45]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.45
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall
  have a heliport emergency response plan available at the heliport.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall identify in the
  emergency response plan those organizations that are capable of
  providing assistance in responding to an emergency at the heliport or
  in its vicinity.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall specify in the
  emergency response plan the procedures to be followed for

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft crash or other accident within the
    heliport perimeter;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft crash outside the heliport perimeter;
    and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any medical emergency.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where an approach and departure path at a heliport is
  located over water, the operator of the heliport shall specify in the
  emergency response plan

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the organization that is responsible for
    co-ordinating rescue in the event of an aircraft ditching; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} how to contact that organization.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall include in the
  emergency response plan the information required in accordance with
  standard 325 --- Heliport Standards.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall consult with all
  organizations identified in the emergency response plan concerning
  their role in it.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall annually review the
  emergency response plan and update the information.

- [(8)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport that provides a scheduled
  service for the transport of passengers shall carry out a test of the
  emergency response plan at intervals not exceeding three years.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
- [SOR/2022-267, s. 17](#1381630-1387842){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1381630-1387842.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-305.45-20070630.html "Link to previous version of section 305.45"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Fire Protection Services]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989906 .Subheading}

- **[[305.46]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.46
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a surface-level
  heliport or of a heliport over a parking garage or on an elevated
  structure that is not an occupied building shall ensure that fire
  protection services are provided at the heliport and that those
  services and the fire resistance of the structure meets the
  requirements of the applicable heliport standard.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a rooftop heliport shall ensure that
  fire protection services are provided at the heliport and that those
  services and the fire resistance of the structure meets the
  requirements of the applicable heliport standard.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
:::

##### [Extinguishing Agents and Equipment]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989912 .Subheading}

**[[305.47]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.47 .sectionLabel}** The operator of a
heliport shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} determine the requirements for extinguishing agents
  and equipment used for fire protection at the heliport based on the
  longest dimension helicopter for which the heliport has been
  certified;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the agents and equipment are in
  accordance with the applicable heliport standard; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} provide a fire extinguisher or fire fighting system
  that is protected from freezing.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
:::

##### [Safety Personnel for Rooftop Heliport]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989919 .Subheading}

**[[305.48]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.48 .sectionLabel}** The operator of a
rooftop heliport shall ensure that a minimum of one trained safety
person is in attendance during helicopter operations.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
:::

##### [Training for Safety Personnel]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989923 .Subheading}

**[[305.49]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.49 .sectionLabel}** The operator of a
heliport shall provide initial and refresher training to safety
personnel provided at the heliport in accordance with the applicable
heliport standard.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
:::

**\[305.50 to 305.52 reserved\]**

#### [Division XIV --- Heliport Operations Manual]{.HTitleText3} {#h-989928 .Subheading}

##### [General]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989929 .Subheading}

- **[[305.53]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.53
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The provisions of this Subpart that
  specify the procedures for making a heliport operations manual also
  apply in respect of any amendment to the manual.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall set out in the
  heliport operations manual

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the heliport certification standards that were met
    for issuance of the heliport certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the level and types of services to be provided by
    the operator of the heliport.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2019-295, s. 9\]]{.Repealed}

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
- [SOR/2019-295, s. 9](#1194393-1195509){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1194393-1195509.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-305.53-20070630.html "Link to previous version of section 305.53"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Heliport Data]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989938 .Subheading}

- **[[305.54]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.54
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall
  determine and record in the heliport operations manual, the following
  data in respect of the heliport in accordance with the applicable
  heliport standard:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} geographic coordinates for

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the heliport reference point if

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} the heliport is not located on an aerodrome
        that already has a reference point, and

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} the heliport operator intends to submit to the
        Minister a request that a zoning regulation be made under the
        [Aeronautics Act](/eng/acts/A-2),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the heliport geometric centre,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the FATO coordinates,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the heliport elevation,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the heliport magnetic variation, and

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} where installed, the electronic navigation aids;
      and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} information in respect of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the heliport type,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the dimensions, slope and surface type of all
      TLOFs,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the length, width, slope, category, surface
      type and designation number of all FATOs,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the length, width and surface type of all safety
      areas,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the designation, width and surface type of
      helicopter ground and air taxiways,

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} the apron surface type and description of
      helicopter parking positions, and

    - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} the declared distances for

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} take-off distance available,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} rejected take-off distance available, and

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} landing distance available.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall ensure that a
  heliport geometric centre is redetermined and recorded in the manual
  if the physical characteristics of the heliport change because

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an existing FATO is closed;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the boundaries of an existing FATO are altered; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a new FATO is constructed.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operator of a heliport shall report the heliport
  data specified in paragraph (1)(a) to the Aeronautical Information
  Services of NAV Canada within 14 days after the Minister's approval of
  certification.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
- [SOR/2022-267, s. 18](#1381632-1387844){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1381632-1387844.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-305.54-20070630.html "Link to previous version of section 305.54"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Administration]{.HTitleText4} {#h-989968 .Subheading}

**[[305.55]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.55 .sectionLabel}** The operator of a
heliport shall ensure that the heliport operations manual contains

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a table of contents; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the following information relating to the
  administration of the heliport:

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a record of any amendments to the manual,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a list of holders of copies of the manual or of
    portions of it,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a description of a procedure for amending the
    manual,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a description of the organizational structure of
    the heliport management,

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} a description of the operational procedures of the
    heliport,

  - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} a declaration, signed and dated by the operator,
    in which they agree to fulfill the obligations of the operator
    referred to in section 305.17,

  - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} a statement, signed and dated by the operator,
    certifying that their heliport operations manual is complete and
    accurate, and that the operator agrees to comply with all of the
    conditions and specifications set out in it,

  - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} a statement, signed by the Minister, that the
    heliport operations manual and any amendments to it have been
    approved,

  - [(ix)]{.lawlabel} a copy of any agreement or memorandum of
    understanding that affects the operation of the heliport, including
    the provision of emergency services at the heliport, and

  - [(x)]{.lawlabel} the information necessary to verify that the
    heliport meets the applicable heliport standard.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
- SOR/2015-160, s. 18(F)
- [SOR/2022-267, s. 19](#1381634-1387847){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1381634-1387847.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-305.55-20150831.html "Link to previous version of section 305.55"){.PITLink}
:::

**[[305.56]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.56 .sectionLabel}** The operator of a
heliport shall ensure that their heliport operations manual sets out the
information specified in subsection 305.25(1).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
:::

**[[305.57]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-305.57 .sectionLabel}** The operator of a
heliport shall ensure that the following are provided in accordance with
the applicable heliport standard and recorded in their heliport
operations manual:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the applicable physical characteristics set out in
  section 305.25;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the obstacle limitation surfaces set out in section
  305.29;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the visual aids for navigation set out in section
  305.31;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the lighting or marking of obstacles set out in
  section 305.37;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the visual aids utilized for denoting restricted use
  areas set out in section 305.41;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the equipment and installations set out in section
  305.43; and

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the emergency response plan set out in section
  305.45.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 8
:::

**\[305.58 to 305.67 reserved\]**

### [Subpart 6 -- \[Reserved\]]{.HTitleText2} {#h-989998 .Subheading}

### [Subpart 7 --- Aerodromes --- Consultations]{.HTitleText2} {#h-989999 .Subheading}

#### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-990000 .Subheading}

**[[307.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-307.01 .sectionLabel}** The following
definitions apply in this Subpart.

[[aerodrome work]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[aerodrome work]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means work, other than work
    necessary to comply with a new requirement imposed by or under the
    Act, carried out for any of the following purposes:

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} building a new aerodrome; or

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} at an existing aerodrome,

      - [(i)]{.lawlabel} building a new runway for aeroplanes, or

      - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} increasing the length of an existing runway
        for aeroplanes by more than 100 m or 10%, whichever is
        greater. ([travaux d'aérodrome]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[proponent]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[proponent]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person who proposes to
    carry out aerodrome work. ([promoteur]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[protected area]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[protected area]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a natural area or
    habitat that is protected by or under federal legislation. ([aire
    protégée]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-261, s. 3
- [SOR/2019-119, s. 12](#1126709-1144145){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126709-1144145.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-307.01-20170101.html "Link to previous version of section 307.01"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Application]{.HTitleText3} {#h-990011 .Subheading}

**[[307.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-307.02 .sectionLabel}** This Subpart
applies to existing and proposed aerodromes that are not

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} military aerodromes;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} water aerodromes;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} aerodromes that are used primarily for agricultural
  operations;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} aerodromes, including heliports, that are used
  primarily for helicopter operations; and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} aerodromes that are used as temporary installations
  for the purpose of providing emergency services, such as forest fire
  suppression, law enforcement activities, and search and rescue
  operations, and responding to a medical emergency.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-261, s. 3
:::

#### [Requirement --- Consultations]{.HTitleText3} {#h-990020 .Subheading}

**[[307.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-307.03 .sectionLabel}** The proponent
shall consult with the interested parties in accordance with the
requirements of this Subpart.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-261, s. 3
:::

#### [Interested Parties]{.HTitleText3} {#h-990024 .Subheading}

- **[[307.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-307.04
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Subpart,
  the interested parties are the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if a built-up area of a city or town is located
    within a radius of 4 000 m from the location of the proposed
    aerodrome work,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the Minister,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the providers of air navigation services,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the operator of a certified or registered
      aerodrome located within a radius of 30 nautical miles from the
      location of the proposed aerodrome work,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the authority responsible for a protected area
      located within the radius of 4 000 m from the location of the
      proposed aerodrome work,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} any local land use authority where the proposed
      aerodrome work is to be carried out, and

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} members of the public who are within the radius
      of 4 000 m from the location of the proposed aerodrome work; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in any other case,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the Minister,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the providers of air navigation services,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the operator of a certified or registered
      aerodrome located within a radius of 30 nautical miles from the
      location of the proposed aerodrome work,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the authority responsible for a protected area
      located within a radius of 4 000 m from the location of the
      proposed aerodrome work,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} any local land use authority where the proposed
      aerodrome work is to be carried out, and

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} the owner of any land bordering the land on
      which the proposed aerodrome work is to be carried out.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), the radius of
  4 000 m from the location of the proposed aerodrome work shall be
  measured from the outer perimeter of the site of that location.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-261, s. 3
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 28(F)](#1522598-1525716){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522598-1525716.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-307.04-20170101.html "Link to previous version of section 307.04"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Notice and Sign]{.HTitleText3} {#h-990044 .Subheading}

**[[307.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-307.05 .sectionLabel}** The proponent
shall, at least 75 days before the expected start date of the proposed
aerodrome work,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} provide a notice of the proposed aerodrome work to
  the interested parties referred to in subparagraphs 307.04(1)(a)(i)
  to (v) or paragraph 307.04(1)(b), as applicable; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case referred to in paragraph 307.04(1)(a),
  place a sign, in plain view of the public, at the location where the
  proposed aerodrome work is to be carried out.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-261, s. 3
:::

#### [Content of Notice and Sign]{.HTitleText3} {#h-990050 .Subheading}

**[[307.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-307.06 .sectionLabel}** The proponent
shall include the following information on the notice and the sign:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a drawing showing the location of the proposed
  aerodrome work;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a description of the proposed aerodrome work and its
  purpose;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the expected start date and completion date of the
  proposed aerodrome work;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a statement that the interested parties may provide
  their comments or objections to the proponent with respect to the
  proposed aerodrome work;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} contact information, including the mailing address,
  phone number and email address, for the contact persons to whom the
  interested parties may provide their comments or objections; and

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the period, which shall be at least 45 days, during
  which the interested parties may provide their comments or objections.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-261, s. 3
:::

#### [Summary Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-990060 .Subheading}

**[[307.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-307.07 .sectionLabel}** At the end of the
period referred to in paragraph 307.06(f), the proponent shall prepare a
summary report that includes the following:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a description of the proposed aerodrome work;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a description of the measures taken by the proponent
  to comply with the requirements of this Subpart;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the interested parties who were notified of the
  proposed aerodrome work; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a summary of the comments and objections received,
  the actions that the proponent proposes to take to address those
  comments and objections, and any objections that were not addressed,
  if applicable.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-261, s. 3
:::

#### [Communication of Summary Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-990068 .Subheading}

**[[307.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-307.08 .sectionLabel}** The proponent
shall, as soon as practicable after the end of the period referred to in
paragraph 307.06(f), provide the summary report to the Minister and make
it available to the interested parties.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-261, s. 3
:::

#### [Availability of Summary Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-990072 .Subheading}

**[[307.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-307.09 .sectionLabel}** The proponent
shall ensure that the summary report is available to the interested
parties for at least five years after the date on which it is made
available to them.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-261, s. 3
:::

#### [Start of Aerodrome Work]{.HTitleText3} {#h-990076 .Subheading}

- **[[307.10]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-307.10
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The proponent shall not start the
  proposed aerodrome work before the end of 30 days after the date on
  which the summary report is provided to the Minister.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the proponent does not start the proposed
  aerodrome work within five years after the date on which the summary
  report is provided to the Minister, the proponent shall once again
  comply with the requirements of this Subpart.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2016-261, s. 3
:::

## [Part IV --- Personnel Licensing and Training]{.HTitleText1} {#h-990099 .Part}

### [Division I --- General]{.HTitleText2} {#h-990100 .Subheading}

#### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-990101 .Subheading}

- **[[400.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-400.01
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In this Part,

  [[aerobatic manoeuvre]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[aerobatic manoeuvre]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed,
      SOR/2001-49, s. 1\]]{.Repealed}

  [[aeroplane]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[aeroplane]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} does not include an ultra-light
      aeroplane; ([avion]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[aviation document booklet]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[aviation document booklet]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a booklet
      issued by the Minister in which certain documents issued under
      this Part can be affixed. ([carnet de documents
      d'aviation]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[balloon]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[balloon]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes any lighter-than-air
      aircraft; ([ballon]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[booklet label]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[booklet label]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a label that is
      intended to be affixed in an aviation document booklet.
      ([étiquette de carnet]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[complex aeroplane]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[complex aeroplane]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an aeroplane that
      has flaps and a constant-speed propeller and, except in the case
      of a seaplane, retractable landing gear; ([avion
      complexe]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[dual instruction flight time]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[dual instruction flight time]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the
      flight time during which a person is receiving flight instruction
      from a person qualified in accordance with section 425.21 of
      Standard 425 --- Flight Training; ([temps d'instruction de vol en
      double commande]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[employed on a full-time basis]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[employed on a full-time basis]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means
      working for a flight training unit on a continuous basis for at
      least the number of hours required to carry out the duties of the
      position intended to ensure the safe operation of the flight
      training service; ([employé à temps plein]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[examination]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[examination]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means any written examination
      or written practical qualifications examination required by the
      personnel licensing standards for the issuance of a permit or
      licence or for the endorsement of a permit or licence with a
      rating; ([examen]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[flight following]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[flight following]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed,
      SOR/2014-131, s. 8\]]{.Repealed}

  [[flight instructor experience]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[flight instructor experience]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} with respect
      to the experience requirements for a flight instructor rating for
      an aeroplane or helicopter, means the flight time accumulated in
      an aeroplane or helicopter

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} by a holder of a flight instructor rating while
        providing dual flight instruction to applicants for

        - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a pilot permit --- recreational,

        - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a private or commercial pilot licence, or

        - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a night rating, VFR OTT rating, flight
          instructor rating --- aeroplane, flight instructor rating ---
          helicopter or flight instructor rating --- aeroplane ---
          aerobatic,

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} by a holder of a foreign flight instructor
        rating issued by a contracting state, while providing dual
        flight instruction to an applicant for a permit, licence or
        rating equivalent to one of those referred to in paragraph (a),
        and

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} by a Canadian Armed Forces qualified flying
        instructor while providing dual flight instruction to persons
        undergoing initial flight training in the Canadian Armed Forces;
        ([expérience d'instructeur de vol]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[flight watch]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[flight watch]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed, SOR/2014-131, s.
      8\]]{.Repealed}

  [[foreign licence validation certificate]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[foreign licence validation certificate]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
      means a certificate issued by the Minister pursuant to subsection
      401.07(1); ([certificat de validation de licence
      étrangère]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[glider]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[glider]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes a powered glider;
      ([planeur]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[ground school instruction]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[ground school instruction]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means
      classroom-type instruction generally given to one or more persons
      and covering an organized program of lectures, homework or
      self-paced study that complies with an approved training
      program; ([instruction théorique au sol]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[high-performance aeroplane]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[high-performance aeroplane]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, with respect
      to a rating, means

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an aeroplane that is specified in the minimum
        flight crew document as requiring only one pilot and that has a
        maximum speed (V~ne~) of 250 KIAS or greater or a stall speed
        (V~so~) of 80 KIAS or greater, or

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an amateur-built aeroplane that has a wing
        loading greater than that specified in section 549.103 of the
        Airworthiness Manual; ([avion à hautes
        performances]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[instrument time]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[instrument time]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed,
      SOR/2014-131, s. 8\]]{.Repealed}

  [[integrated course]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[integrated course]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a course of pilot
      training developed using the principles of instructional systems
      design, in which all instructional stages are completed as one
      continuous course and the flight training elements are
      interrelated and sequenced to provide for the efficient
      achievement of the learning objectives; ([cours
      intégré]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[invigilator]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[invigilator]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person who is
      designated by the Minister to supervise a written examination;
      ([surveillant]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[main base]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[main base]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a location at which a
      flight training unit has personnel, aircraft and facilities for
      the operation of a flight training service and that is established
      as the principal place of business of the flight training unit;
      ([base principale]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[minimum flight crew document]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[minimum flight crew document]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a
      document, issued by the Minister, a contracting state or an
      aircraft manufacturer, that relates to an aircraft and that
      specifies the number of pilots required to operate the
      aircraft; ([document relatif à l'équipage de conduite
      minimal]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[operational control]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[operational control]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the exercise of
      authority over the initiation, continuation, diversion or
      termination of a flight in the interest of the safety of the
      aircraft and the regularity and efficiency of the flight;
      ([contrôle d'exploitation]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[operations specifications]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[operations specifications]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, in respect of a
      flight training unit, means the operations specifications set out
      in a flight training unit operator certificate, and includes any
      amendment to the conditions of operation; ([spécifications
      d'exploitation]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[pilot's self-dispatch]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[pilot's self-dispatch]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed,
      SOR/2014-131, s. 8\]]{.Repealed}

  [[pre-flight briefing]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[pre-flight briefing]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a one-to-one
      practical briefing that is conducted just prior to a training
      flight for the purpose of ensuring that the trainee understands
      exactly what will take place during the flight; ([exposé avant
      vol]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[preparatory ground instruction]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[preparatory ground instruction]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means
      classroom-type instruction, generally on a one-to-one basis but
      not excluding group instruction, that is based on lesson plans
      contained in or developed from the applicable flight instructor
      guide; ([instruction au sol avant vol]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[satellite base]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[satellite base]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a location at which a
      flight training unit has personnel, aircraft and facilities for
      the operation of a flight training service on a temporary basis;
      ([base satellite]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[solo flight time]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[solo flight time]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means, with respect to
      the flight time necessary to acquire a permit, licence or rating,

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a pilot, the flight time during
        which the pilot is the sole flight crew member, and

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a student pilot permit holder,
        the flight time during which the holder is the sole occupant of
        an aircraft while under the direction and supervision of the
        holder of an instructor rating for the appropriate category of
        aircraft; ([temps de vol en solo]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[sub-base]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[sub-base]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a location at which a
      flight training unit positions aircraft and personnel and from
      which operational control is exercised in accordance with the
      flight training operations manual and operational control system;
      ([base secondaire]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[training flight]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[training flight]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a dual instruction
      flight or a solo practice flight that is conducted under the
      direction and supervision of a flight instructor; ([vol
      d'entraînement]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[ultra-light aeroplane]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[ultra-light aeroplane]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes a powered
      parachute and a powered para-glider. ([avion
      ultra-léger]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Any reference in this Part to a permit, licence,
  rating or foreign licence validation certificate is a reference to a
  valid Canadian permit, licence, rating or foreign licence validation
  certificate.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Any reference in this Part to "military" is a
  reference to the Canadian Armed Forces.

does not apply in respect of the issuance of a Canadian aviation
document in respect of the operation of remotely piloted aircraft

### [Division II --- Examinations]{.HTitleText2} {#h-990149 .Subheading}

#### [Examination Rules]{.HTitleText3} {#h-990150 .Subheading}

- **[[400.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-400.02
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except as authorized by an
  invigilator, no person shall, or shall attempt to, in respect of an
  examination,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} copy or remove from any place all or any portion of
    the text of the examination;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} give to or accept from any person a copy of all or
    any portion of the text of the examination;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} give help to or accept help from any person during
    the examination;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} complete all or any portion of the examination on
    behalf of any other person; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} use any aid or written material during the
    examination.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who commits an act prohibited under
  subsection (1) fails the examination and may not take any other
  examination for a period of one year.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A person who uses a hand-held calculator during an
  examination shall use a hand-held calculator whose memory is cleared
  before and after the examination in the presence of the invigilator.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} A person who uses a hand-held electronic computer
  during an examination shall use a hand-held electronic computer

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} that has been specifically designed for flight
    operations;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} that has been approved by the Minister for
    examination purposes; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} whose memory is cleared before and after the
    examination in the presence of the invigilator.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-320, s. 2
- [SOR/2020-151, s. 5](#1252583-1257154){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1252583-1257154.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-400.02-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 400.02"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Time Limits]{.HTitleText3} {#h-990166 .Subheading}

- **[[400.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-400.03
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), written
  examinations, including all sections of a sectionalized examination,
  that are required for the issuance of a permit or licence or for the
  endorsement of a permit or licence with a rating shall be completed
  during the 24-month period preceding the date of the application for
  the permit, licence or rating.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of
  examinations that are required for the issuance of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a student pilot permit; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an airline transport pilot licence if examinations
    were previously written

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} for the endorsement of a type rating, a mark of
      70 per cent or higher was obtained on the examination and the type
      rating was issued;

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} for the issuance of the former senior commercial
      pilot licence, a mark of 70 per cent or higher was obtained on the
      examination and the senior commercial pilot licence was issued; or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} for the issuance of an airline transport pilot
      licence --- aeroplane, an airline transport pilot licence ---
      aeroplane integrated course was successfully completed during the
      5-year period preceding the date of the application for the
      licence and a course completion certificate was issued.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The regulatory requirements examination referred to
  in subsection 566.03(5) of Standard 566 --- Aircraft Maintenance
  Engineer Licensing and Training that is required for the issuance of
  an aircraft maintenance engineer (AME) licence shall be completed
  during the 12-month period immediately following the date on which the
  application for the licence is accepted by the Minister.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2001-49, s. 2
- SOR/2003-154, s. 2
- SOR/2006-352, s. 5
- SOR/2011-284, s. 2
:::

#### [Rewriting of Examinations]{.HTitleText3} {#h-990178 .Subheading}

- **[[400.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-400.04
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) and (6),
  a person who fails an examination or a section of a sectionalized
  examination required for the issuance of a flight crew permit,
  licence, rating or foreign licence validation certificate is
  ineligible to rewrite the examination or the failed section for a
  period of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a first failure, 14 days;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a second failure, 30 days; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a third or subsequent failure, 30
    days plus an additional 30 days for each failure in excess of two
    failures, up to a maximum of 180 days.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who fails the Student Pilot Permit or
  Private Pilot Licence for Foreign and Military Applicants, Aviation
  Regulations (PSTAR) examination is eligible to rewrite the examination
  at any time after the person has received notice of the failure and
  has reviewed their weak knowledge areas.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A person who fails an examination required for the
  issuance of an aircraft maintenance engineer (AME) licence or rating
  is eligible to rewrite the examination in accordance with the criteria
  specified in Chapter 566 of the Airworthiness Manual.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} A person who passes a sectionalized examination but
  fails one or more sections of that examination shall rewrite the
  failed section or sections in one sitting.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} Where a person requests to rewrite an examination,
  the Minister shall inform the person in writing of the date on which
  the person may rewrite the examination and whether the person is
  required to provide evidence of further study or instruction before
  rewriting the examination.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} If a person submits a request to the Minister to
  shorten the period between examination attempts, the Minister shall
  grant the request on receipt of confirmation that the person has
  reviewed their weak knowledge areas.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2001-49, s. 3
:::

### [Division III --- Flight Training Service]{.HTitleText2} {#h-990191 .Subheading}

#### [Authorization to Operate Flight Training Service Under CUSMA]{.HTitleText3} {#h-990192 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2020-150, s. 2

\]
:::

- **[[400.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-400.05
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A person who is a citizen, permanent
  resident or corporation of the United States of America or Mexico and
  who is eligible to operate a flight training service in Canada in
  accordance with Chapter 15 and Annex I --- Schedule of Canada of CUSMA
  shall, prior to operating the service, obtain from the Minister an
  authorization to operate the service. The request for the
  authorization shall be in the form and shall contain the information
  specified in the Personnel Licensing and Training Standards respecting
  Flight Training Units.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 6.71 of the Act, the Minister
  shall, on receipt of a request referred to in subsection (1) and where
  the requirements of the Personnel Licensing and Training Standards
  respecting Flight Training Units are met, issue an authorization
  containing the conditions under which the flight training service may
  be operated.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An authorization referred to in subsection (1) is
  required in addition to a flight training unit operator certificate
  for those persons who are required to hold a flight training unit
  operator certificate pursuant to Subpart 6.

### [Subpart 1 --- Flight Crew Permits, Licences and Ratings]{.HTitleText2} {#h-990205 .Subheading}

#### [Division I --- General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-990206 .Subheading}

##### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-990207 .Subheading}

**[[401.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-401.01 .sectionLabel}** Any reference in
this Subpart to the personnel licensing standards is a reference to the
Personnel Licensing and Training Standards respecting Flight Crew
Permits, Licences and Ratings.

**[[401.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-401.02 .sectionLabel}** \[Reserved,
SOR/2014-15, s. 1\]

##### [Requirement to Hold a Flight Crew Permit, Licence or Rating or a Foreign Licence Validation Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-990210 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2003-129, s. 3

\]
:::

- **[[401.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-401.03
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no person
  shall act as a flight crew member or exercise the privileges of a
  flight crew permit, licence or rating unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person holds the appropriate permit, licence or
    rating;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the permit, licence or rating is valid;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the person holds the appropriate medical
    certificate; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the person can produce the permit, licence or
    rating, and the certificate, when exercising those privileges.

- [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall exercise the privileges of a
  foreign licence validation certificate unless the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} holds the appropriate foreign licence validation
    certificate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} has signed the certificate; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} can produce the certificate when exercising those
    privileges.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who holds a military flight crew permit,
  licence or rating or a flight crew permit, licence or rating issued by
  a contracting state other than Canada may act as a flight crew member
  or exercise the privileges of a flight crew permit, licence or rating
  for the sole purpose of the person's flight test where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the test is conducted in accordance with section
    401.15; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} no passenger is carried on board the aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2003-129, s. 4
- SOR/2005-320, s. 3
- SOR/2010-26, s. 3
- SOR/2014-15, s. 2
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-401.03-20100202.html "Link to previous version of section 401.03"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Flight Crew Members of Aircraft Registered in Contracting States Other Than Canada]{.HTitleText4} {#h-990228 .Subheading}

**[[401.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-401.04 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
act as a flight crew member or exercise the privileges of a flight crew
licence in Canada in an aircraft registered in a contracting state other
than Canada, unless the person holds, and can produce while so acting or
while exercising such privileges,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a flight crew permit or licence issued under this
  Subpart; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a flight crew licence, or a document equivalent to a
  foreign licence validation certificate, that is issued under the laws
  of the contracting state.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2003-129, s. 5
:::

##### [Recency Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-990234 .Subheading}

- **[[401.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-401.05
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite any other provision of this
  Subpart, no holder of a flight crew permit, licence or rating, other
  than the holder of a flight engineer licence, shall exercise the
  privileges of the permit, licence or rating unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the holder has acted as pilot-in-command or
    co-pilot of an aircraft within the five years preceding the flight;
    or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} within the 12 months preceding the flight

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the holder has completed a flight review, in
      accordance with the personnel licensing standards, conducted by
      the holder of a flight instructor rating for the same category of
      aircraft,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the flight instructor who conducted the flight
      review has certified in the holder's personal log that the holder
      meets the skill requirements for the issuance of the permit or
      licence set out in the personnel licensing standards, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the holder has successfully completed the
      appropriate examination specified in the personnel licensing
      standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite any other provision of this Subpart, no
  holder of a flight crew permit or licence, other than the holder of a
  flight engineer licence, shall exercise the privileges of the permit
  or licence in an aircraft unless the holder

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} has successfully completed a recurrent training
    program in accordance with the personnel licensing standards within
    the 24 months preceding the flight; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where a passenger other than a flight test examiner
    designated by the Minister is carried on board the aircraft, has
    completed, within the six months preceding the flight,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft other than a glider or
      a balloon, in the same category and class of aircraft as the
      aircraft, or in a Level B, C or D simulator of the same category
      and class as the aircraft, at least

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} five night or day take-offs and five night or
        day landings, if the flight is conducted wholly by day, or

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} five night take-offs and five night landings,
        if the flight is conducted wholly or partly by night,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a glider, at least

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} five take-offs and five landings in a glider,
        or

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} two take-offs and two landings in a glider with
        the holder of a flight instructor rating --- glider and obtained
        a certification of competence to carry passengers on board a
        glider from that holder in accordance with the personnel
        licensing standards, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a balloon, at least

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} five landings in a balloon by day and five
        take-offs in a balloon by day or night, if the flight is
        conducted by day, or

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} five landings in a balloon by day and five
        take-offs in a balloon by night, if the flight is conducted
        partly by night.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No holder of a Canadian pilot licence endorsed with
  an instrument rating or to which is attached instrument rating
  privileges shall exercise the privileges of the instrument rating
  unless the holder has successfully completed, within the 24 months
  preceding the flight, one of the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an instrument rating flight test in an aircraft or
    in a Level B, C or D simulator of the same group as the aircraft;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a Canadian Armed Forces instrument rating flight
    test;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} an instrument proficiency check that complies with
    the applicable requirements of subsection 421.05(1) of Standard 421
    -- Flight Crew Permits, Licences and Ratings and that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} consisted of tasks representative of those
      required by sections 1 to 4 of section 5 of Schedule 8 of Standard
      428 -- Conduct of Flight Tests,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} was conducted in

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft of the same group as set out in
        subsection 421.46(1) of Standard 421 that met the requirements
        of section 605.18, or

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} a flight simulation training device that was
        approved for instrument rating flight tests and configured for
        aircraft of the same group as set out in subsection 421.46(1) of
        Standard 421, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} was conducted by any of the following persons
      who hold a valid instrument rating for aircraft of the same group
      as set out in subsection 421.46(1) of Standard 421:

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} a pilot examiner authorized by the Minister to
        conduct instrument rating flight tests,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} an approved check pilot authorized by the
        Minister to conduct an instrument proficiency check for the
        specific type of aircraft on which the instrument proficiency
        check was conducted,

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} a person who holds an authorization, issued by
        a contracting state having a reciprocal licensing agreement with
        Canada, that is equivalent to the authorization referred to in
        clause (A) or (B), or

      - [(D)]{.lawlabel} a Canadian Armed Forces instrument check pilot,
        if the holder of a Canadian pilot licence being tested is a
        member of the Canadian Armed Forces; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} one of the following competency checks or pilot
    proficiency checks for which the validity period has not expired and
    that includes a portion on instrument procedures:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a competency check conducted in accordance with
      the Flight Test Guide --- Competency Check (Private Operators),
      published by the Minister, in the case of aircraft operated under
      Subpart 4 of Part VI,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a line operational evaluation from an approved
      advanced qualification program conducted by a Canadian Advanced
      Qualification Program Evaluator,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a foreign pilot proficiency or competency check
      that is approved by a contracting state and conducted by a foreign
      check pilot who is authorized to conduct instrument proficiency
      checks for commercial and private air operators of that state, if
      the holder is working for hire or reward for a foreign commercial
      or private air operator, or

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a competency check or pilot proficiency check
      conducted in compliance with one of the following schedules to the
      Commercial Air Services Standards:

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} Schedule I to section 722.65 of Standard 722
        --- Aerial Work, in the case of aeroplanes operated under
        Subpart 2 of Part VII,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} Schedule II to section 722.65 of Standard 722
        --- Aerial Work, in the case of helicopters operated under
        Subpart 2 of Part VII,

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} Schedule I to section 723.88 of Standard 723
        --- Air Taxi --- Aeroplanes, in the case of aeroplanes operated
        under Subpart 3 of Part VII,

      - [(D)]{.lawlabel} the schedule to section 723.88 of Standard 723
        --- Air Taxi --- Helicopters, in the case of helicopters
        operated under Subpart 3 of Part VII,

      - [(E)]{.lawlabel} Schedule I or II to section 724.108 of Standard
        724 --- Commuter Operations --- Aeroplanes, in the case of
        aeroplanes operated under Subpart 4 of Part VII,

      - [(F)]{.lawlabel} the schedule to section 724.108 of Standard 724
        --- Commuter Operations --- Helicopters, in the case of
        helicopters operated under Subpart 4 of Part VII, or

      - [(G)]{.lawlabel} Schedule I, II or III to section 725.106 of
        Standard 725 --- Airline Operations --- Aeroplanes, in the case
        of aeroplanes operated under Subpart 5 of Part VII.

- [(3.1)]{.lawlabel} No holder of a Canadian pilot licence endorsed with
  an instrument rating or to which is attached instrument rating
  privileges shall exercise the privileges of the instrument rating
  unless, following the first day of the 13th month after the completion
  date of a test referred to in subsection (3) and within six months
  before the flight, the holder has

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} acquired six hours of instrument time; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} completed six instrument approaches in an aircraft
    in actual or simulated instrument meteorological conditions, or in a
    Level B, C or D simulator or an approved flight training device
    configured for the same category as the aircraft

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} under the supervision of a person who holds the
      qualifications referred to in subsection 425.21(9) of Standard 425
      --- Flight Training, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} while acting as a flight instructor conducting
      training in respect of the endorsement of a flight crew licence or
      permit with an instrument rating.

- [(3.2)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a Canadian pilot licence endorsed
  with an instrument rating or to which is attached instrument rating
  privileges shall retain a record of having met the applicable recency
  requirement set out in subsection (3) or (3.1) for three years.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} No holder of a Canadian flight engineer licence shall
  exercise the privileges set out in section 401.37 unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the holder has acted as flight engineer on board an
    aircraft within the five years preceding the flight or has met the
    written examination requirements for the licence within the 12
    months preceding the flight; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where a passenger or a trainee is carried on board
    the aircraft, the holder has, within the six months preceding the
    flight, acted as flight engineer

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in an aircraft of the same type, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in a synthetic flight trainer for an aircraft of
      the same type.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} No holder of a Canadian pilot licence endorsed with a
  second officer rating shall exercise the privileges set out in section
  401.53 unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the holder has acted as a second officer on board
    an aircraft within the five years preceding the flight; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where a passenger or a trainee is carried on board
    the aircraft, the holder has, within the six months preceding the
    flight, acted as a second officer in

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft of the same type, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a synthetic flight trainer for an aircraft of
      the same type.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} No holder of a Canadian pilot licence endorsed with a
  flight instructor rating --- ultra-light aeroplane shall exercise the
  privileges set out in section 401.88 unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the holder has

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} acted as pilot-in-command or co-pilot of an
      aircraft within the five years preceding the flight, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} met the written examination requirements for the
      rating within the 12 months preceding the flight;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the holder has successfully completed a recurrent
    training program in accordance with the personnel licensing
    standards within the 24 months preceding the flight; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the holder has, where a student is carried on board
    the aeroplane, completed at least five take-offs and five landings
    in an ultra-light aeroplane of the same control configuration within
    the six months preceding the flight.
