- [(2)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a flight test conducted in accordance
  with Schedules 9 to 18 to the flight testing standards, a candidate
  successfully completes the flight test if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the candidate completes all of the items set out in
    section 5 of those schedules; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the candidate successfully completes each item of
    the flight test and does not fail the test for any of the reasons
    set out in section 408.19.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2011-284, s. 16
:::

#### [Conduct of a Flight Test]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991731 .Subheading}

- **[[408.15]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-408.15
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The examiner shall conduct a flight
  test in accordance with section 3 of Schedules 1 to 18 to the flight
  testing standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The examiner shall evaluate the performance of a
  candidate in accordance with section 4 of Schedules 1 to 18 to the
  flight testing standards by verifying, during the flight test, the
  candidate's knowledge and skills when performing the items set out in
  section 4 of those schedules, taking into account the general
  tolerances specified in that section. The examiner shall record the
  results on the form entitled Flight Test Report in the manner
  specified by the Minister.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a flight test conducted in accordance
  with Schedules 1 to 8 to the flight testing standards, the examiner
  shall not take part in the pilotage of the aeroplane or helicopter
  during the flight test except in the cases set out in paragraph 3(b)
  of those schedules.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2011-284, s. 16
:::

**[[408.16]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-408.16 .sectionLabel}** In the case of a
flight test conducted in accordance with Schedules 1 to 8 to the flight
testing standards, the examiner may have the candidate repeat an item if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the item is discontinued for safety reasons;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the examiner intervened on the flight controls to
  avoid a collision with another aircraft that the candidate could not
  see;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the candidate understood the specific nature of the
  item but did not understand the examiner's request to perform it; or

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the examiner was distracted to the point of not being
  able to adequately observe the candidate's performance of the item.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2011-284, s. 16
:::

#### [Incomplete Flight Test]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991745 .Subheading}

**[[408.17]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-408.17 .sectionLabel}** If the candidate
has successfully completed some of the items during a flight test but
the flight test cannot be completed for reasons beyond the candidate's
control, the subsequent flight test shall meet the following
requirements:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} only the items that the candidate could not perform
  during the initial flight test shall be performed;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the candidate shall take the subsequent flight test
  within

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} 60 days after the date of the incomplete flight
    test, in the case of a flight test described in Schedule 1 to the
    flight testing standards, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} 30 days after the date of the incomplete flight
    test, in the case of a flight test described in Schedules 2 to 18 to
    the flight testing standards; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a flight test conducted in accordance
  with Schedule 8 to the flight testing standards, the subsequent flight
  test shall be conducted using an aircraft in the same instrument
  rating group as the aircraft used in the initial flight test.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2011-284, s. 16
- SOR/2015-160, s. 24(F)
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-408.17-20120219.html "Link to previous version of section 408.17"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Failure and Re-test --- Schedules 1 to 8 to Flight Testing Standards]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991754 .Subheading}

- **[[408.18]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-408.18
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a flight test
  conducted in accordance with Schedules 1 to 8 to the flight testing
  standards, a candidate fails the flight test if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the candidate's performance of an item includes
    deviations that are repeated or that the candidate either does not
    recognize or does not correct in a timely manner;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the candidate's handling of the aircraft is rough
    or includes uncorrected or excessive deviations from specified
    tolerances;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the candidate, as a result of a pilot error or
    faulty handling of the aircraft, exceeds by more than double the
    deviation tolerances specified in the table to section 4 of
    Schedules 1 to 8 of those standards, even if a correction is made;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the candidate does not demonstrate the level of
    technical proficiency or knowledge necessary to carry out the
    functions of a holder of a licence, permit or rating;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the candidate has lapses in situational awareness
    that are not identified or corrected;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the candidate's flight management skills are
    ineffective; or

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the safety of the flight is compromised.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A candidate who fails not more than two air flight
  test items described in Schedules 1 to 7 to the flight testing
  standards may take a re-test of each failed item within:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 60 days after the date of the failed test, in the
    case of a flight test described in Schedule 1 to those standards; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 30 days after the date of the failed test, in the
    case of a flight test described in Schedules 2 to 7 to those
    standards.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A candidate who fails not more than one air flight
  test item described in Schedule 8 to the flight testing standards may
  take a re-test of the failed item within 30 days after the date of the
  failed test.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} A candidate must take a complete re-test for a
  licence, permit or rating referred to in Schedules 1 to 8 to the
  flight testing standards if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} during a flight test, the candidate displays unsafe
    airmanship or dangerous flying resulting in the flight test being
    assessed as a failure;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the candidate repeatedly fails to use appropriate
    and effective visual scanning techniques to ensure that the area is
    cleared before or while performing an item that involves visual
    manoeuvres;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} during a complete flight test, the candidate fails
    any ground flight test item;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} during a complete flight test, the candidate fails
    more than two air flight test items in the case of a flight test
    described in Schedules 1 to 7 to the flight testing standards or
    more than one air flight test item in the case of a flight test
    described in Schedule 8 to those standards;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the candidate fails an item during a partial
    re-test; or

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the candidate does not complete a partial re-test
    within a period specified in subsection (2).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2011-284, s. 16
:::

#### [Failure of a Flight Test --- Schedules 9 to 18 to Flight Testing Standards]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991777 .Subheading}

**[[408.19]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-408.19 .sectionLabel}** In the case of a
flight test conducted in accordance with Schedules 9 to 18 to the flight
testing standards, a candidate fails the flight test if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the candidate performs an air flight test item using
  unsafe airmanship or completes the item with major deviations from the
  level of competency required for the issuance of a commercial pilot
  licence --- aeroplane or a commercial pilot licence --- helicopter;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the candidate fails to use appropriate and effective
  visual scanning techniques to ensure that the area is cleared before
  or while performing an item that involves visual manoeuvres;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the candidate acts or fails to act in such a manner
  that the examiner is required to take corrective action to maintain
  safe flight;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the candidate instructs, on the ground or in the air,
  in a manner that the examiner determines would result in a lack of
  understanding or in a misunderstanding that could lead to a dangerous
  flight situation;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the candidate fails to accomplish the aim of one or
  more of the items of the flight test;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the candidate does not demonstrate the level of
  technical proficiency or knowledge necessary to carry out the
  functions of a holder of a flight instructor rating; or

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the candidate displays an ineffective instructional
  technique.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2011-284, s. 16
:::

## [Part V --- Airworthiness]{.HTitleText1} {#h-991788 .Part}

### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText2} {#h-991789 .Subheading}

**[[500.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-500.01 .sectionLabel}** In this Part,
[[rotorcraft]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a gyroplane or a helicopter.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/98-526, s. 2
- SOR/2009-280, s. 23
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-500.01-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 500.01"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Subpart 1 --- Annual Airworthiness Information Report]{.HTitleText2} {#h-991793 .Subheading}

#### [Requirement to Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991794 .Subheading}

- **[[501.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-501.01
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), the owner
  of a Canadian aircraft --- other than a remotely piloted aircraft that
  is an element of a remotely piloted aircraft system in respect of
  which a design approval document has not been issued or applied for
  under Subpart 21 of this Part or an ultra-light aeroplane --- shall
  submit to the Minister an Annual Airworthiness Information Report in
  respect of the aircraft, in the form and manner specified in Chapter
  501 of the Airworthiness Manual, either as

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an individual report; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where approved in conformity with Chapter 501 of
    the Airworthiness Manual, a consolidated fleet report.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The submission of the Annual Airworthiness
  Information Report is not required where the aircraft is out of
  service and its owner

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} reports, in the form and manner specified in
    Chapter 501 of the Airworthiness Manual, that the aircraft is out of
    service and is expected to remain out of service for one or more of
    the reporting periods for which an Annual Airworthiness Information
    Report would otherwise be required; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} notifies the Minister forthwith when that aircraft
    is brought back into service.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-11, s. 11](#1045395-1110467){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045395-1110467.html"}
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 37](#1516894-1527482){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1516894-1527482.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-501.01-20190109.html "Link to previous version of section 501.01"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Information to Be Reported]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991802 .Subheading}

**[[501.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-501.02 .sectionLabel}** The owner of a
Canadian aircraft shall provide in the Annual Airworthiness Information
Report the information on the characteristics of the aircraft and on the
maintenance of its airworthiness that is specified in Chapter 501 of the
Airworthiness Manual.

#### [Reporting Schedule]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991804 .Subheading}

**[[501.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-501.03 .sectionLabel}** The owner of a
Canadian aircraft shall submit the Annual Airworthiness Information
Report to the Minister each year by not later than March 30 following
the calendar year for which the Report was prepared or another date
agreed on, beforehand, by the owner and the Minister.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-119, s. 18](#1126728-1215045){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126728-1215045.html"}
- [SOR/2021-152, s. 7(F)](#1302010-1308388){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1302010-1308388.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-501.03-20200101.html "Link to previous version of section 501.03"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Subpart 7 --- Flight Authority and Certificate of Noise Compliance]{.HTitleText2} {#h-991806 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2000-404, s. 1

\]
:::

#### [Application]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991809 .Subheading}

**[[507.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-507.01 .sectionLabel}** This Subpart
applies in respect of aircraft --- other than remotely piloted aircraft
that are an element of a remotely piloted aircraft system in respect of
which a design approval document has not been issued or applied for
under Subpart 21 of this Part, ultra-light aeroplanes and hang gliders
--- that are

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} Canadian aircraft; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} operated in Canadian airspace.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-11, s. 12](#1045397-1110471){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045397-1110471.html"}
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 38](#1516896-1527486){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1516896-1527486.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-507.01-20190109.html "Link to previous version of section 507.01"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Certificate of Airworthiness]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991813 .Subheading}

**[[507.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-507.02 .sectionLabel}** Where an
application for a flight authority is made pursuant to section 507.06,
the Minister shall issue a certificate of airworthiness in respect of an
aircraft

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} for which an aircraft type design has been certified
  by the Minister and the certification is not in respect of a
  restricted category aircraft;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} that conforms to its certified type design; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} that is safe for flight.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 24
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-507.02-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 507.02"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Special Certificate of Airworthiness]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991820 .Subheading}

**[[507.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-507.03 .sectionLabel}** Where an
application for a flight authority is made pursuant to section 507.06,
the Minister shall issue a special certificate of airworthiness in
respect of an aircraft that

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} meets the criteria for one of the classifications of
  a special certificate of airworthiness specified in Chapter 507 of the
  Airworthiness Manual;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} conforms to the applicable type design or, in the
  case of an amateur-built aircraft, is designed and constructed in a
  way that ensures its airworthiness, in conformity with the
  requirements of Chapter 549 of the Airworthiness Manual; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} is safe for flight.

#### [Flight Permit]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991825 .Subheading}

**[[507.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-507.04 .sectionLabel}** Where an
application for a flight authority is made pursuant to section 507.06,
the Minister shall issue a flight permit in respect of an aircraft that
meets the criteria for one of the classifications of a flight permit
specified in Chapter 507 of the Airworthiness Manual and that is safe
for flight.

#### [Validation of Foreign Flight Authority]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991827 .Subheading}

**[[507.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-507.05 .sectionLabel}** Where an aircraft
is operating under a foreign flight authority that is issued in respect
of the aircraft or the fleet of which it is a part and that does not
conform to Article 31 of the Convention, and the Minister determines
that the aircraft is safe for flight, the Minister shall validate the
foreign flight authority, thereby authorizing the operation of the
aircraft in Canadian airspace.

#### [Application for Flight Authority]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991829 .Subheading}

- **[[507.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-507.06
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An application for a flight
  authority shall be signed by the owner of the aircraft in respect of
  which it is submitted, or by a representative of the owner as defined
  in Chapter 507 of the Airworthiness Manual.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who applies for a flight authority shall do
  so in the form and manner specified in Chapter 507 of the
  Airworthiness Manual.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for a flight authority shall include
  with the application a declaration, made by a person authorized to do
  so pursuant to section 507.10, attesting that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an application for a certificate of
    airworthiness, the aircraft meets the requirements of section
    507.02;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an application for a special
    certificate of airworthiness, the aircraft meets the requirements of
    section 507.03; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an application for a flight permit,
    the aircraft meets the requirements of section 507.04.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} In the case of an application to validate a foreign
  flight authority, the applicant shall submit a copy of the foreign
  flight authority, including any operational limitation imposed in
  respect of that flight authority.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may inspect, or may cause to be
  inspected, any aircraft for which an application for flight authority
  has been made, for the purposes of determining conformity with its
  type design and compliance with the applicable requirements of these
  Regulations.

#### [Flight Authority for an Imported Aircraft]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991839 .Subheading}

**[[507.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-507.07 .sectionLabel}** Where an
application for a flight authority is made in respect of an aircraft
being imported, the applicant must comply with the importation
requirements specified in Chapter 507 of the Airworthiness Manual.

#### [Issuance of Additional Flight Authority]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991841 .Subheading}

- **[[507.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-507.08
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where the owner of an aircraft
  requests an additional flight authority in accordance with section
  507.06 and demonstrates compliance with the applicable standards
  contained in Standard 507 --- Flight Authority and Certificate of
  Noise Compliance and if the aircraft is safe for flight, the Minister
  shall issue

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft that has been damaged or
    has inoperative systems such that it no longer conforms to the
    conditions of the existing flight authority, an additional flight
    authority to allow the aircraft to be flown to a location where the
    required maintenance can be performed; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft that has been modified
    to allow multiple configurations one of which results in the
    aircraft no longer meeting the conditions of issue of the existing
    flight authority, an additional flight authority in respect of the
    new configuration.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where an additional flight authority is issued in
  respect of an aircraft pursuant to this section,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the additional flight authority takes effect when
    an entry indicating that it is in effect, is made in the aircraft
    journey log; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} except where provided for by technical dispatch
    procedures required by subsection 706.06(1), the flight authority
    specified in the most recent journey log entry made pursuant to
    paragraph 571.06(3)(a) remains in effect until a new flight
    authority is specified.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2003-154, s. 4
:::

#### [Operating Conditions]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991851 .Subheading}

**[[507.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-507.09 .sectionLabel}** Where an aircraft
does not meet the requirements for the issue of a flight authority that
conforms to Article 31 of the Convention, the Minister shall make the
flight authority subject to operating conditions where the conditions
are required to ensure the safety of the aircraft, other aircraft,
persons, animals or property.

#### [Persons Who May Attest to Condition and Conformity]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991853 .Subheading}

**[[507.10]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-507.10 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
make a declaration of an aircraft's condition or conformity to its
certified type design for the purpose of obtaining a flight authority
other than the holder of an aircraft maintenance engineer (AME) licence
issued pursuant to Part IV or

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a new aircraft, an authorized
  representative of the manufacturer; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft that is operated under a
  special certificate of airworthiness in the owner-maintenance or
  amateur-built classification, the owner of the aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-112, s. 2
:::

#### [Duration of a Flight Authority]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991859 .Subheading}

**[[507.11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-507.11 .sectionLabel}** Unless
surrendered, suspended or cancelled, a flight authority issued pursuant
to this Subpart remains in force during the period or for the number of
flights specified in it or, where no limit is specified, indefinitely,
if the aircraft continues to meet the conditions subject to which the
flight authority was issued.

#### [Alteration of Document]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991861 .Subheading}

**[[507.12]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-507.12 .sectionLabel}** No person other
than the Minister shall amend a flight authority issued pursuant to this
Subpart.

#### [Replacing a Lost or Destroyed Flight Authority]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991863 .Subheading}

**[[507.13]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-507.13 .sectionLabel}** The Minister
shall replace a lost or destroyed flight authority of a Canadian
aircraft on receipt of a written application from the registered owner,
or from a representative of the owner as specified in Standard 507 ---
Flight Authority and Certificate of Noise Compliance, if the aircraft
continues to meet the requirements for the issue of the flight
authority.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2003-154, s. 5
:::

**\[507.14 to 507.19 reserved\]**

#### [Certificate of Noise Compliance]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991868 .Subheading}

**[[507.20]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-507.20 .sectionLabel}** If an application
for a certificate of noise compliance is made in respect of an aircraft
under section 507.21 and the aircraft meets the applicable noise
emission levels specified in Chapter 516 of the Airworthiness Manual,
the Minister shall issue the certificate.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2000-404, s. 2
:::

#### [Application for a Certificate of Noise Compliance]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991872 .Subheading}

- **[[507.21]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-507.21
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An application for a certificate of
  noise compliance shall be signed by the owner or operator of the
  aircraft in respect of which it is submitted or by a representative of
  the owner within the meaning of Chapter 507 of the Airworthiness
  Manual.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who applies for a certificate of noise
  compliance shall do so in the form and manner specified in Chapter 507
  of the Airworthiness Manual.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for a certificate of noise compliance
  shall include with the application evidence that the aircraft meets
  the noise emission levels referred to in section 507.20.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2000-404, s. 2
:::

#### [Suspension of a Certificate of Noise Compliance]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991879 .Subheading}

**[[507.22]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-507.22 .sectionLabel}** A certificate of
noise compliance is suspended and shall be surrendered to the Minister
on request if the aircraft in respect of which it was issued no longer
meets the noise emission levels referred to in section 507.20.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2000-404, s. 2
:::

#### [Validation of a Foreign Certificate of Noise Compliance]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991883 .Subheading}

**[[507.23]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-507.23 .sectionLabel}** In the process of
validating a foreign flight authority in respect of an aircraft under
section 507.05, if a foreign certificate of noise compliance is in
effect in respect of the aircraft, the Minister shall validate the
foreign certificate of noise compliance in the form and manner specified
for the validation of the flight authority.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2000-404, s. 2
:::

### [Subpart 9 --- Export Airworthiness Certificates]{.HTitleText2} {#h-991887 .Subheading}

#### [Application]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991888 .Subheading}

**[[509.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-509.01 .sectionLabel}** This Subpart
applies in respect of the following aircraft if they meet the export
requirements specified in Chapter 509 of the Airworthiness Manual,
except for aircraft that are operated under a special certificate of
airworthiness in the owner-maintenance or amateur-built classification,
remotely piloted aircraft that are an element of a remotely piloted
aircraft system in respect of which a design approval document has not
been issued or applied for under Subpart 21 of this Part, ultra-light
aeroplanes and hang gliders:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} new aircraft manufactured in Canada;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} Canadian aircraft in respect of which a Certificate
  of Airworthiness has been issued pursuant to Subpart 7; or

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} aircraft that were last registered in Canada but are
  no longer registered in any state.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-112, s. 3
- [SOR/2019-11, s. 13](#1045399-1110473){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045399-1110473.html"}
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 39](#1516898-1527487){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1516898-1527487.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-509.01-20190109.html "Link to previous version of section 509.01"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Application for an Export Airworthiness Certificate]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991895 .Subheading}

- **[[509.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-509.02
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A person who applies for an Export
  Airworthiness Certificate shall do so in the form and manner specified
  in Chapter 509 of the Airworthiness Manual.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for an Export Airworthiness Certificate
  shall include with the application a declaration made by a person
  authorized to do so pursuant to section 509.04, attesting that the
  aircraft conforms to the certified type design specified in the
  application.

#### [Authority for Export]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991899 .Subheading}

- **[[509.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-509.03
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), the
  Minister shall issue an Export Airworthiness Certificate where the
  aircraft in respect of which the application is made conforms to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the type design specified in a type certificate; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} another type design specified in the application,
    where the aircraft is being exported to a state with which Canada
    has entered into an agreement that provides for the acceptance of
    Export Airworthiness Certificates and the aircraft conforms to any
    special requirements specified by that state.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where an aircraft does not meet the requirements of
  subsection (1), the Minister may issue an Export Airworthiness
  Certificate that specifies the non-conformity to the applicable type
  design or any special requirement and the acceptance of that
  non-conformity by the state to which the aircraft is being exported.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 25
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-509.03-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 509.03"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Persons Who May Attest to Condition and Conformity]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991907 .Subheading}

**[[509.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-509.04 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
make a declaration of an aircraft's condition or conformity to its
certified type design for the purpose of obtaining an Export
Airworthiness Certificate in respect of the aircraft, other than

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the holder of an aircraft maintenance engineer (AME)
  licence issued pursuant to Part IV that is applicable to that aircraft
  type; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a new aircraft manufactured in Canada,
  an authorized representative of the manufacturer.

#### [Responsibilities of the Exporter]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991911 .Subheading}

**[[509.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-509.05 .sectionLabel}** Where an Export
Airworthiness Certificate has been issued in respect of an aircraft, the
owner of the aircraft shall, on transfer of its title,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} forward to the new owner all of the documents and
  information required by Chapter 509 of the Airworthiness Manual;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the exported aircraft is disassembled, forward
  to the new owner the manufacturer's assembly instructions and the
  other documents relating to the aircraft specified in Chapter 509 of
  the Airworthiness Manual; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the temporary equipment, if any,
  incorporated into the aircraft for the purpose of the export delivery
  flight is removed and the aircraft is restored to the configuration
  approved in the type certificate.

### [Subpart 21 --- Approval of the Type Design or a Change to the Type Design of an Aeronautical Product]{.HTitleText2} {#h-991963 .Subheading}

#### [Division I --- General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991964 .Subheading}

##### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-991965 .Subheading}

**[[521.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.01 .sectionLabel}** The following
definitions apply in this Subpart.

[[aeronautical product]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[aeronautical product]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an aircraft,
    aircraft engine, aircraft propeller or aircraft appliance or part,
    or a component part of any of those things. ([produit
    aéronautique]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[applicant]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[applicant]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an individual or
    organization responsible for the design of an aeronautical product,
    or a representative of such an individual or organization, that
    makes an application for the issuance of or a change to a design
    approval document in respect of an aeronautical product.
    ([demandeur]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[design approval document]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[design approval document]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a type
    certificate, a supplemental type certificate, a repair design
    approval, a part design approval or a Canadian Technical Standard
    Order (CAN-TSO) design approval. ([document d'approbation de la
    conception]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[foreign aeronautical product]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[foreign aeronautical product]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an
    aeronautical product for which the state of design is a state other
    than Canada. ([produit aéronautique étranger]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[VLA]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[VLA]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} or [[very light
    aeroplane]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an aeroplane that has a single
    engine with a spark or compression ignition, has no more than two
    seats and is designed and manufactured to have

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a maximum certificated take-off weight not
      exceeding 750 kg; and

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a stall speed in the landing configuration (Vso)
      of 45 knots (52 mph) calibrated air speed (CAS), or less. ([VLA
      ou]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"}[avion très léger]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-991976 .Subheading}

**[[521.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.02 .sectionLabel}** This Subpart
applies to applicants for and holders of the following documents and
applicants for a change to one of those documents:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a type certificate issued under section 521.57 in
  respect of an aeronautical product;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a Canadian Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO) design
  approval issued under section 521.109 in respect of an appliance or a
  part;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a supplemental type certificate issued under section
  521.206 in respect of an aeronautical product;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a repair design approval issued under section 521.256
  in respect of an aeronautical product; and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} a part design approval issued under section 521.306
  in respect of a replacement part for an aeronautical product.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Appliances and Parts]{.HTitleText4} {#h-991985 .Subheading}

**[[521.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.03 .sectionLabel}** An appliance or a
part, other than a standard part, may be approved by the issuance of any
one of the following:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a Canadian Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO) design
  approval;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a type certificate, in the case of an appliance or
  part that is part of an aeronautical product on which it is installed;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a supplemental type certificate, in the case of an
  appliance or part that is part of a change to the type design of an
  aeronautical product; or

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a part design approval, in the case of a part that is
  a replacement part.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

**\[521.04 to 521.24 reserved\]**

#### [Division II --- Type Certificates]{.HTitleText3} {#h-991994 .Subheading}

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-991995 .Subheading}

**[[521.25]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.25 .sectionLabel}** This Division
applies

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in respect of the issuance of a type certificate for
  an aeronautical product; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} to applicants for and holders of a type certificate
  in respect of an aeronautical product.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Eligibility Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992001 .Subheading}

**[[521.26]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.26 .sectionLabel}** An applicant for
a type certificate in respect of an aeronautical product shall have, or
have access to, the technical capability to conduct the design analyses
and tests required to demonstrate the conformity of the aeronautical
product with its certification basis.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Aircraft Categories]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992005 .Subheading}

- **[[521.27]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.27
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An applicant may, in the case of an
  aircraft, request a type certificate in respect of the following
  aircraft categories or any combination of them:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} normal category;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} utility category;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} aerobatic category;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} commuter category;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} transport category; or

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} restricted category.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An applicant may, in the case of an aircraft for
  which no standards of airworthiness are listed in subsection
  521.31(1), request a type certificate in respect of an aircraft
  category that is not listed in subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Application for a Type Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992017 .Subheading}

**[[521.28]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.28 .sectionLabel}** An applicant for
a type certificate in respect of an aeronautical product shall submit to
the Minister

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} an application that contains the information
  specified on the form published by the Minister entitled Type
  Certificate Application;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a description of the aeronautical product that
  contains, in addition to its principal design features and its
  specifications,

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft, a three-view drawing,
    the preliminary data respecting the design and performance, and the
    proposed operating characteristics and limitations, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft engine or propeller, a
    general arrangement drawing, and the proposed operating
    characteristics and limitations;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a proposed certification basis; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a certification plan that identifies

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the means to be used to demonstrate that the
    aeronautical product conforms to the applicable certification basis,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the documentation that demonstrates the conformity
    of the aeronautical product with the applicable certification basis,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the resources necessary for carrying out the
    demonstration of conformity referred to in subparagraph (i), and

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the schedule for carrying out the demonstration of
    conformity referred to in subparagraph (i).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Effective Period of an Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992031 .Subheading}

- **[[521.29]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.29
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Unless an applicant demonstrates, at
  the time of submitting an application for a type certificate in
  respect of an aeronautical product, that a longer period is required
  for the design, development and testing of the product, and for that
  reason the Minister approves a longer period, the application is
  effective during one of the following periods, beginning on the date
  of the application:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} five years, in the case of a transport category
    aeroplane or a transport category rotorcraft; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} three years, in the case of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft other than an aircraft referred to in
      paragraph (a),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft engine, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft propeller.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a type certificate is not issued within the
  applicable effective period referred to in subsection (1), the
  applicant may

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} submit a new application for a type certificate; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} apply for an extension of the effective period of
    the original application.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the effective period of an application for a type
  certificate is extended under paragraph (2)(b), the standards of
  airworthiness applicable to the aeronautical product are those in
  force on the date that precedes, by one of the periods referred to in
  subsection (1), the date of the issuance of the type certificate.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Certification Basis]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992045 .Subheading}

- **[[521.30]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.30
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall establish, in
  respect of an aeronautical product, a certification basis consisting
  of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsections (2) to (5), the applicable
    standards of airworthiness referred to in section 521.31 that are in
    force on the date of application for the type certificate, unless
    the applicant

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} elects to include in the certification basis
      later amendments to those standards of airworthiness, in
      accordance with subsection (5), or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} is required to comply with later amendments to
      the standards of airworthiness in accordance with subsection
      521.29(3);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the applicable aircraft emissions standards
    referred to in section 521.32;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any special conditions that are necessary to ensure
    that the type design of an aeronautical product having a novel or
    unusual design feature provides a level of safety equivalent to that
    provided by the standards of airworthiness in force on the date of
    application for the type certificate;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} any finding of equivalent safety based on any
    factors or design features that provide for an alternate means of
    compliance with the standards of airworthiness in force on the date
    of application for the type certificate; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} any exemptions.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} In the case of an aeronautical product to which no
  complete standards of airworthiness referred to in section 521.31
  apply, the applicable standards of airworthiness are the portions of
  the standards of airworthiness referred to in section 521.31 that are
  in force on the date of application for the type certificate.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} In the case of an aircraft, including its engine and
  propeller, that is designed in accordance with the requirements of,
  and accepted for use by, the Department of National Defence, other
  than an aircraft referred to in paragraph (4)(b), the applicable
  standards of airworthiness are those referred to in section 521.31

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} that are appropriate to the type of aircraft, the
    number and type of its engines and propellers, and its MCTOW; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} that provide a level of safety equivalent to that
    provided by the standards of airworthiness in force on the date that
    the aircraft was accepted for use by that Department.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} In the case of an aircraft for which a type
  certificate in the restricted category is requested, the applicable
  standards of airworthiness are

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the standards of airworthiness referred to in
    section 521.31 that are in force on the date of application for the
    type certificate, except for those that are inappropriate for the
    use specified on the application for the type certificate; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the design and performance requirements established
    by the Department of National Defence in respect of the aircraft on
    the date that the aircraft was accepted for use by that Department.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} An applicant may elect to include in the
  certification basis later amendments to the applicable standards of
  airworthiness referred to in subsections (1) to (4), if the applicant
  complies with any other amendment that is directly related to those
  standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Standards of Airworthiness]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992065 .Subheading}

- **[[521.31]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.31
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For the issuance of a type
  certificate in respect of an aeronautical product, the standards of
  airworthiness, including the aircraft categories set out in subsection
  521.27(1), are those specified in the following chapters of the
  Airworthiness Manual, as applicable:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Chapter 522 --- Gliders and Powered Gliders;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Chapter 523 --- Normal, Utility, Aerobatic and
    Commuter Category Aeroplanes;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} Chapter 523 -- VLA --- Very Light Aeroplanes;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} Chapter 525 --- Transport Category Aeroplanes;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} Chapter 527 --- Normal Category Rotorcraft;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} Chapter 529 --- Transport Category Rotorcraft;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} Chapter 531 --- Manned Free Balloons;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} Chapter 533 --- Aircraft Engines;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} Chapter 535 --- Propellers; and

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} Chapter 541 --- *Airships*.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The standards of airworthiness for the design and
  installation of an item of aircraft equipment required by Part VI or
  VII are

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} those specified in Chapter 551 --- Aircraft
    Equipment and Installation of the Airworthiness Manual; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if no standards of airworthiness for the design and
    installation of the item of aircraft equipment are specified in
    Chapter 551 --- Aircraft Equipment and Installation of the
    Airworthiness Manual, those specified in the certification basis of
    the aircraft on which the equipment is installed.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
- [SOR/2019-119, s. 19(F)](#1126730-1144202){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126730-1144202.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-521.31-20091201.html "Link to previous version of section 521.31"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Aircraft Emissions Standards]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992083 .Subheading}

**[[521.32]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.32 .sectionLabel}** The aircraft
emissions standards applicable to the issuance of a type certificate are
the following:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft other than an aircraft for
  which certification is requested in the restricted category for use in
  agricultural operations or fire prevention and suppression, the noise
  standards specified in Subchapter A of Chapter 516 --- Aircraft
  Emissions of the Airworthiness Manual;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a turbine-powered aircraft, the
  standards respecting the prevention of intentional fuel venting
  specified in Subchapter B of Chapter 516 --- Aircraft Emissions of the
  Airworthiness Manual;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft engine, the smoke and
  gaseous aircraft emissions standards specified in Subchapter B of
  Chapter 516 --- Aircraft Emissions of the Airworthiness Manual; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft, the carbon dioxide
  (CO~2~) emissions standards specified in Subchapter C of Chapter 516
  --- Aircraft Emissions of the Airworthiness Manual.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
- [SOR/2020-251, s. 1](#1274599-1276793){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1274599-1276793.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-521.32-20091201.html "Link to previous version of section 521.32"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Conformity with Certification Basis]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992090 .Subheading}

**[[521.33]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.33 .sectionLabel}** An applicant for
a type certificate in respect of an aeronautical product shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} demonstrate to the Minister that the aeronautical
  product conforms to the certification basis established by the
  Minister under section 521.30;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} submit to the Minister a declaration attesting to the
  demonstration of conformity of the aeronautical product with its
  certification basis;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} make available to the Minister the means by which
  conformity is established;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft, record the noise levels
  in its flight manual or in a supplement to that manual using the
  Guidelines for the Administration of Noise Certification Documentation
  set out in Attachment G of Annex 16, Volume I to the Convention; and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} submit to the Minister for approval any manuals,
  instructions and limitations that are required by the certification
  basis established in respect of the aeronautical product.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

**\[521.34 to 521.43 reserved\]**

##### [Inspections and Tests]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992100 .Subheading}

**[[521.44]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.44 .sectionLabel}** An applicant for
a type certificate in respect of an aeronautical product shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} ensure, before conducting a test, that the item to be
  tested conforms to the drawings, specifications and manufacturing
  processes proposed for the type design of the aeronautical product and
  that the measuring device and test equipment to be used are
  appropriate and calibrated for the test;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the equipment and procedures used for
  conducting a test flight meet the requirements set out in sections
  521.45 and 521.46;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} conduct all the inspections, analyses and tests
  necessary to demonstrate to the Minister that the type design of the
  aeronautical product conforms to its certification basis;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} in accordance with the certification plan, submit to
  the Minister for review the data and reports resulting from the
  inspections, analyses and tests conducted under paragraph (c); and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} provide the Minister with access to the aeronautical
  product for the purpose of making any inspection, making any
  engineering assessment, or conducting or witnessing any test,

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} required to verify the applicant's declaration
    attesting to the demonstration of conformity of the aeronautical
    product with its certification basis, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} required to make a determination of the conformity
    of the aeronautical product with its certification basis.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Test Flights]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992111 .Subheading}

- **[[521.45]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.45
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for a type certificate
  in respect of an aeronautical product who conducts a test flight shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} make provisions for emergency situations and
    provide the emergency equipment required for the safety of the test
    flight personnel;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} conduct the inspections, analyses, structural
    tests, wind tunnel tests and functional tests of the critical
    systems and components of the aircraft used for the test flight ---
    including an evaluation of the effect of their failure --- to ensure
    that the aircraft will operate safely within the operating
    limitations and restrictions specified by the applicant;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} provide a pilot who holds a licence endorsed with a
    rating appropriate for conducting the test flight; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} conduct the test flight in accordance with the
    conditions specified by the Minister in a flight authority issued in
    respect of that flight.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The applicant shall, before conducting the first test
  flight of an aircraft type, submit

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a written airworthiness declaration attesting that
    the aircraft being used for the test flight satisfies the conditions
    referred to in paragraph (1)(b); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a written declaration attesting to the condition of
    the aircraft and its conformity with the configuration specified for
    the purposes of the test flight, made by a person authorized to do
    so by the manufacturer of the aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Test Flight Operations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992123 .Subheading}

- **[[521.46]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.46
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for a type certificate
  in respect of an aeronautical product who intends to conduct a test
  flight and who has the resources, personnel and facilities for
  conducting a test flight shall establish and maintain a test flight
  operations manual that is appropriate to the size, nature and
  complexity of the test flight operations and that contains

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a statement signed by the person responsible for
    the test flight operations certifying that the test flight
    operations are being carried out in accordance with the policies and
    procedures set out in the manual and in any document incorporated
    into that manual;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a description of the system used by the applicant
    to supervise the test flight operations;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a description of the system used by the applicant
    to manage matters relating to safety and risk during the conduct of
    a test flight;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a description of record-keeping practices and
    procedures;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a description of how the configuration of an
    aircraft used in a test flight is defined and how a change to that
    configuration is documented;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a description of the qualification, training and
    currency requirements of the test flight crew members;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a description of the test flight planning
    procedures; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} duty time limitations for test flight crew members.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The person responsible for test flight operations
  shall submit the test flight operations manual and any amendment to
  the manual to the Minister for approval.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall approve the test flight operations
  manual and any amendment to the manual if they meet the requirements
  set out in this section.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Function and Reliability Test Flights]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992138 .Subheading}

- **[[521.47]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.47
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), an
  applicant for a type certificate in respect of an aircraft shall
  conduct one or more function and reliability test flights in order to
  demonstrate to the Minister that the aircraft, its components and its
  equipment are reliable and function properly.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A function and reliability test flight shall consist
  of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft that uses a turbine
    engine of a type not previously used in an aircraft for which a type
    certificate has been issued, at least 300 hours of operation of the
    aircraft with a full complement of engines that conform to a type
    certificate or to an equivalent certificate issued by the
    airworthiness authority of a foreign state with which Canada has an
    airworthiness agreement or similar arrangement; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of every other aircraft, at least 150
    hours of operation of the aircraft.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the following aircraft:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} aeroplanes having a MCTOW of 2 720 kg (6,000
      pounds) or less,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} gliders,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} airships having a seating configuration,
      excluding pilot seats, of nine or less,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} manned free balloons, or

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} restricted category aircraft; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a change to a type design, unless otherwise
    determined by the Minister taking into consideration the
    certification plan submitted under paragraph 521.28(d).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

**\[521.48 to 521.56 reserved\]**

##### [Issuance of a Type Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992155 .Subheading}

- **[[521.57]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.57
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 6.71 of the Act,
  the Minister shall issue a type certificate in respect of an
  aeronautical product if the applicant

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} submits the declaration required under paragraph
    521.33(b);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} submits a signed undertaking to carry out the
    responsibilities specified in Division VIII; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements set out in subsection (2)
    or (3) in respect of the category of the aeronautical product.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for a type certificate in respect of an
  aeronautical product other than a restricted category aircraft shall
  demonstrate to the Minister that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the type design of the aeronautical product
    conforms to its certification basis;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft, no feature or
    characteristic makes the aircraft unsafe, taking into account the
    category in which certification is requested;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} subject to paragraph (d), any test flights required
    under paragraph 521.44(c) and section 521.47 have been conducted;
    and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} if the function and reliability test flights
    required under section 521.47 have not been completed, a program
    exists to ensure their completion before the later of the delivery
    of the first aircraft and the issuance of the certificate of
    airworthiness.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for a type certificate in respect of a
  restricted category aircraft shall demonstrate to the Minister that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} no feature or characteristic makes the aircraft
    unsafe when that aircraft is operated within the limitations
    specified for its intended use; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} has a type design that conforms to its
      certification basis, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} is of a type manufactured in accordance with the
      requirements of, and accepted for use by, the Department of
      National Defence and has been modified for its intended use.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Change to the Type Design Approved in a Type Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992173 .Subheading}

**[[521.58]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.58 .sectionLabel}** The holder of a
type certificate in respect of an aeronautical product who proposes to
make a change to the type design approved in the type certificate shall
meet the requirements set out in section 521.152.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

**\[521.59 to 521.100 reserved\]**

#### [Division III --- Canadian Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO) Design Approvals]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992178 .Subheading}

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992179 .Subheading}

**[[521.101]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.101 .sectionLabel}** This Division
applies

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in respect of the issuance of a Canadian Technical
  Standard Order (CAN-TSO) design approval for an appliance or a part;
  and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} to applicants for and holders of a Canadian Technical
  Standard Order (CAN-TSO) design approval in respect of an appliance or
  a part.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Eligibility Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992185 .Subheading}

**[[521.102]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.102 .sectionLabel}** An applicant
for a Canadian Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO) design approval in
respect of an appliance or a part shall have, or have access to, the
technical capability to conduct the design analyses and tests required
to demonstrate the conformity of the appliance or part with its
certification basis.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Application for a Canadian Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO) Design Approval]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992189 .Subheading}

**[[521.103]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.103 .sectionLabel}** An applicant
for a Canadian Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO) design approval in
respect of an appliance or a part shall submit to the Minister

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} an application that contains the information
  specified on the form published by the Minister entitled Canadian
  Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO) Design Approval Application;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a description of the appliance or part that contains
  its principal design features and its specifications;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a proposed certification basis;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a certification plan that identifies

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the means to be used to demonstrate that the
    appliance or part conforms to the applicable certification basis,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the documentation that demonstrates the conformity
    of the appliance or part with the applicable certification basis,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the resources necessary for carrying out the
    demonstration of conformity referred to in subparagraph (i), and

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the schedule for carrying out the demonstration of
    conformity referred to in subparagraph (i);

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} a draft of the declaration of design and performance
  referred to in paragraph 521.107(b); and

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the means to be used to identify the model number of
  an appliance or a part and the part number of each component of the
  appliance or part and how changes to the appliance or part will be
  identified.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Effective Period of an Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992203 .Subheading}

- **[[521.104]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.104
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Unless an applicant demonstrates, at
  the time of submitting an application for a Canadian Technical
  Standard Order (CAN-TSO) design approval in respect of an appliance or
  a part, that a longer period is required for the design, development
  and testing of the appliance or part, and for that reason the Minister
  approves a longer period, the application is effective during one of
  the following periods, beginning on the date of the application:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} two years, in the case of an appliance or a part
    other than a turbine-powered APU; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} three years, in the case of a turbine-powered APU.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a Canadian Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO)
  design approval is not issued within the applicable effective period
  referred to in subsection (1), the applicant may

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} submit a new application for a Canadian Technical
    Standard Order (CAN-TSO) design approval; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} apply for an extension of the effective period of
    the original application.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the effective period of an application for a
  Canadian Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO) design approval is
  extended under paragraph (2)(b), the standards of airworthiness
  applicable to the appliance or part are those in force on the date
  that precedes, by one of the periods referred to in subsection (1),
  the date of the issuance of the Canadian Technical Standard Order
  (CAN-TSO) design approval.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Certification Basis]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992214 .Subheading}

**[[521.105]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.105 .sectionLabel}** The Minister
shall establish, in respect of an appliance or a part, a certification
basis consisting of

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the applicable standards of airworthiness referred to
  in section 521.106 that are in force on the date of application for
  the Canadian Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO) design approval; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} any finding of equivalent safety based on any factors
  or design features that provide for an alternate means of compliance
  with the standards of airworthiness in force on the date of
  application for the Canadian Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Standards of Airworthiness]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992220 .Subheading}

**[[521.106]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.106 .sectionLabel}** The standards
of airworthiness for the issuance of or a change to a Canadian Technical
Standard Order (CAN-TSO) design approval in respect of an appliance or a
part are

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} those specified in Chapter 537 --- Appliances and
  Parts of the Airworthiness Manual; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} if no standards of airworthiness for the issuance of
  or a change to a Canadian Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO) design
  approval in respect of the appliance or part are specified in Chapter
  537 --- Appliances and Parts of the Airworthiness Manual, the minimum
  performance standards specified by the Minister.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Conformity with Certification Basis]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992226 .Subheading}

**[[521.107]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.107 .sectionLabel}** An applicant
for a Canadian Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO) design approval in
respect of an appliance or a part shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} demonstrate to the Minister that the appliance or
  part conforms to the certification basis established by the Minister
  under section 521.105;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} submit to the Minister a declaration of design and
  performance that contains

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the content of the certification basis,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a declaration attesting to the demonstration of
    conformity of the appliance or part with its certification basis,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} information identifying the components of the
    type design of the appliance or part,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the rated performance of the appliance or part,

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} a reference to the record documenting the means of
    demonstrating conformity with the certification basis, and

  - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} a reference to the maintenance, overhaul and
    repair manuals;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} make available to the Minister the means by which
  conformity is established; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} submit to the Minister for approval any manuals,
  instructions and limitations that are required by the certification
  basis established in respect of the appliance or part.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Inspections and Tests]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992240 .Subheading}

**[[521.108]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.108 .sectionLabel}** An applicant
for a Canadian Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO) design approval in
respect of an appliance or a part shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} ensure, before conducting a test, that the item to be
  tested conforms to the drawings, specifications and manufacturing
  processes proposed for the type design of the appliance or part and
  that the measuring device and test equipment to be used are
  appropriate and calibrated for the test;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} conduct all the inspections, analyses and tests
  necessary to demonstrate to the Minister that the type design of the
  appliance or part conforms to its certification basis;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} in accordance with the certification plan, submit to
  the Minister for review the data and reports resulting from the
  inspections, analyses and tests conducted under paragraph (b); and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} provide the Minister with access to the appliance or
  part for the purpose of making any inspection, making any engineering
  assessment, or conducting or witnessing any test,

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} required to verify the applicant's declaration
    attesting to the demonstration of conformity of the appliance or
    part with its certification basis, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} required to make a determination of the conformity
    of the appliance or part with its certification basis.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Issuance of a Canadian Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO) Design Approval]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992250 .Subheading}

**[[521.109]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.109 .sectionLabel}** Subject to
section 6.71 of the Act, the Minister shall issue a Canadian Technical
Standard Order (CAN-TSO) design approval in respect of an appliance or a
part if the applicant

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements set out in section 521.107;
  and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} submits a signed undertaking to carry out the
  responsibilities specified in Division VIII.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Change to a Type Design Approved in a Canadian Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO) Design Approval]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992256 .Subheading}

- **[[521.110]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.110
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a Canadian Technical
  Standard Order (CAN-TSO) design approval in respect of an appliance or
  a part who proposes to make a change to the appliance or part shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a change to the type design, apply
    for a new Canadian Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO) design
    approval under section 521.103; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in any other case, establish procedures to ensure
    that the changed appliance or part continues to conform to its
    certification basis and make the change after the Minister accepts
    the procedures.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An individual or organization, other than the holder
  of a Canadian Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO) design approval in
  respect of an appliance or a part, who proposes to make a change or
  repair to the appliance or part shall make an application in respect
  of that appliance or part for the issuance of a Canadian Technical
  Standard Order (CAN-TSO) design approval, a supplemental type
  certificate, or a repair design approval.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

**\[521.111 to 521.150 reserved\]**

#### [Division IV --- Changes to a Type Design]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992265 .Subheading}

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992266 .Subheading}

**[[521.151]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.151 .sectionLabel}** This Division
applies

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in respect of the approval of a change to the type
  design of an aeronautical product; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} to applicants for an approval of a change to the type
  design of an aeronautical product.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Change to a Type Design]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992272 .Subheading}

- **[[521.152]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.152
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 521.153, no
  person shall undertake a change to the type design of an aeronautical
  product that has other than a negligible effect on the weight and
  centre-of-gravity limits, structural strength, performance, power
  plant operation, flight characteristics or other qualities affecting
  its airworthiness or environmental characteristics except in
  accordance with sections 521.155 to 521.160.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} In any other case, no person shall undertake a change
  to the type design of an aeronautical product except in accordance
  with section 521.154.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Change to a Type Design Requiring a New Type Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992278 .Subheading}

**[[521.153]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.153 .sectionLabel}** An applicant
for the approval of a change to the type design of an aeronautical
product shall submit an application for a new type certificate under
section 521.28 if the Minister determines that the change is so
extensive in relation to the design, configuration, power or weight of
the product --- including, in the case of an engine, its power
limitations --- that a substantially complete investigation by the
applicant is necessary to determine conformity with the applicable
certification basis.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Change Other than a Change to the Type Design]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992282 .Subheading}

**[[521.154]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.154 .sectionLabel}** The holder of a
design approval document who proposes to make a change to an
aeronautical product, other than a change to the type design referred to
in subsection 521.152(1), shall establish procedures to ensure that the
changed aeronautical product continues to conform to its certification
basis and make the change after the Minister accepts the procedures.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Application for Approval of a Change to the Type Design]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992286 .Subheading}

**[[521.155]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.155 .sectionLabel}** An applicant
for the approval of a change to the type design of an aeronautical
product shall submit to the Minister

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} an application that contains the information
  specified on the form published by the Minister entitled Design Change
  Approval Application;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a description of the change to the type design that
  identifies

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} all parts of the type design, including all parts
    of the approved manuals, that are affected by the change, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} any re-investigations necessary to demonstrate the
    continued conformity of the aeronautical product with the applicable
    certification basis, by listing the standards of airworthiness that
    must be met and the means to be used to demonstrate conformity;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a proposed certification basis; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a certification plan that identifies

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the means to be used to demonstrate that the change
    to the type design of the aeronautical product conforms to the
    applicable certification basis,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the documentation that demonstrates that the
    change to the type design of the aeronautical product conforms to
    the applicable certification basis, and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the resources necessary for carrying out the
    demonstration of conformity referred to in subparagraph (i), and

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the schedule for carrying out the demonstration of
    conformity referred to in subparagraph (i).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Effective Period of an Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992300 .Subheading}

- **[[521.156]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.156
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Unless an applicant demonstrates, at
  the time of submitting an application for the approval of a change to
  the type design of an aeronautical product, that a longer period is
  required for the design, development and testing of the product, and
  for that reason the Minister approves a longer period, the application
  is effective during one of the following periods, beginning on the
  date of the application:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} five years, in the case of a transport category
    aeroplane or a transport category rotorcraft; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} three years, in the case of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft other than an aircraft referred to in
      paragraph (a),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft engine, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft propeller.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a change to the type design of an aeronautical
  product is not approved within the applicable effective period
  referred to in subsection (1), the applicant may

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} submit a new application for the approval of a
    change to the type design of the aeronautical product; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} apply for an extension of the effective period of
    the original application.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the effective period of an application for the
  approval of a change to the type design of an aeronautical product is
  extended under paragraph (2)(b), the standards of airworthiness
  applicable to the change are those in force on the date that precedes,
  by one of the periods referred to in subsection (1), the date of the
  approval of the change to the type design.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Certification Basis]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992314 .Subheading}

**[[521.157]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.157 .sectionLabel}** The Minister
shall establish, in respect of a change to the type design of an
aeronautical product, a certification basis consisting of the applicable
standards referred to in sections 521.158 and 521.159.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Standards of Airworthiness]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992318 .Subheading}

- **[[521.158]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.158
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) to (9),
  an applicant for the approval of a change to the type design of an
  aeronautical product shall demonstrate that the product meets the
  standards of airworthiness recorded in the type certificate data
  sheets and in force on the date of the application for the change.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The certification basis for the issuance of a repair
  design approval or a part design approval is that recorded in the type
  certificate data sheets, and includes any special conditions referred
  to in subsection (7).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A change to the type design of an aeronautical
  product may conform to an earlier amendment to a standard referred to
  in subsection (1) if the Minister determines that the change is not
  significant in the context of all previous relevant design changes and
  of all related amendments to the applicable standards recorded in the
  type certificate data sheets. The change is significant if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the general configuration or principles of
    construction are not retained; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the assumptions used in obtaining the type
    certificate for the aeronautical product do not remain valid.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} A change to the type design of an aeronautical
  product may conform to an earlier amendment to a standard referred to
  in subsection (1) in respect of an area, system, component, item of
  equipment or appliance if the Minister determines that the area,
  system, component, item of equipment or appliance

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is not affected by the change; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is affected by the change, but conformity with a
    standard referred to in subsection (1) would not contribute
    materially to the level of safety or would not be practical.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} In respect of an area, system, component, item of
  equipment or appliance that is affected by a change, a standard
  referred to in subsection (3) or (4) may not predate a standard that
  is recorded in the type certificate data sheets or

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a normal, utility, aerobatic and
    commuter category aeroplane, the standards set out in section 523.2
    of Chapter 523 --- Normal, Utility, Aerobatic and Commuter Category
    Aeroplanes of the Airworthiness Manual;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a transport category aeroplane, the
    standards set out in section 525.2 of Chapter 525 --- Transport
    Category Aeroplanes of the Airworthiness Manual;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a normal category rotorcraft, the
    standards set out in section 527.2 of Chapter 527 --- Normal
    Category Rotorcraft of the Airworthiness Manual; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a transport category rotorcraft, the
    standards set out in section 529.2 of Chapter 529 --- Transport
    Category Rotorcraft of the Airworthiness Manual.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} The standards of airworthiness that apply in respect
  of a change to the type design of an aircraft, other than a
  rotorcraft, having a MCTOW of 2 720 kg (6,000 pounds) or less, or of a
  non-turbine rotorcraft having a MCTOW of 1 360 kg (3,000 pounds) or
  less, are those recorded in the type certificate data sheets, unless
  the Minister determines that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the change is significant and requires compliance
    with an amendment to the standards that are recorded in the type
    certificate data sheets and that apply in respect of the change and
    with any other standards that are directly related to the change;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} compliance with the amendment referred to in
    paragraph (a) would contribute materially to the level of safety and
    would be practical.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for the approval of a change to the type
  design of an aeronautical product having a novel or unusual design
  feature shall comply with any special conditions that are necessary to
  ensure that the change provides a level of safety equivalent to that
  provided by the applicable certification basis determined under
  subsections (1) to (6), (8) and (9).

- [(8)]{.lawlabel} If a change is made to the type design of a
  restricted category aircraft, or if a change to the type design of an
  aircraft results in the aircraft being reclassified as a restricted
  category aircraft, that aircraft must meet

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the standards of airworthiness referred to in
    section 521.31 applicable to that category of aircraft that are in
    force on the date of the application for the change; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the standards of airworthiness recorded in the type
    certificate data sheets, or an earlier amendment to a standard
    referred to in paragraph (a), if the standards or the amendment
    provide a level of safety appropriate for the intended use of that
    aircraft.

- [(9)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for the approval of a change to the type
  design of an aeronautical product may elect to include in the
  certification basis a later amendment to the standards of
  airworthiness specified in subsection (1), on the condition that the
  applicant comply with any other amendment that is directly related to
  those standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
- [SOR/2019-119, s. 20(F)](#1126732-1144203){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126732-1144203.html"}
:::
