:::

##### [Aircraft Emissions Standards]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992343 .Subheading}

- **[[521.159]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.159
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), an
  applicant for the approval of a change to the type design of an
  aeronautical product that results in a change in the noise levels of
  an aircraft shall demonstrate

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} that the aircraft meets the noise standards
    specified in Subchapter A of Chapter 516 --- Aircraft Emissions of
    the Airworthiness Manual; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} that the aircraft continues to meet the noise
    standards that applied before the change was undertaken and that are
    recorded in the type certificate data sheets or in a document that
    has been accepted by the Minister as being equivalent to a type
    certificate for that aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a restricted category aircraft for use in
    agricultural operations or fire prevention and suppression;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the installation or removal of floats or skis;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the installation or removal of external equipment
    on a rotorcraft; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft whose certification basis does not
    contain noise standards, if the change to the type design does not
    involve

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a change in the number or type of propellers,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a change in the number of engines or in the
      principle of propulsion of the engines, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a rotorcraft, a change in the
      number of rotors or in the principle of operation of the rotors.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for the approval of a change to the type
  design of a turbine-powered aircraft shall demonstrate that the
  aircraft meets the standards respecting the prevention of intentional
  fuel venting specified in Subchapter B of Chapter 516 --- Aircraft
  Emissions of the Airworthiness Manual.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for the approval of a change to the type
  design of an aircraft engine shall demonstrate that the aircraft
  engine meets the smoke and gaseous aircraft emissions standards
  specified in Subchapter B of Chapter 516 --- Aircraft Emissions of the
  Airworthiness Manual.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for the approval of a change to the type
  design of an aircraft shall demonstrate that the aircraft meets the
  carbon dioxide (CO~2~) emissions standards specified in Subchapter C
  of Chapter 516 --- Aircraft Emissions of the Airworthiness Manual.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26

##### [Conformity with Certification Basis]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992360 .Subheading}

- **[[521.160]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.160
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for the approval of a
  change to the type design of an aeronautical product shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} demonstrate to the Minister that the product
    conforms to the certification basis established by the Minister
    under section 521.157 by conducting the inspections and tests
    referred to in section 521.44;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} submit to the Minister a declaration attesting to
    the demonstration of conformity of the product with its
    certification basis;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} make available to the Minister the means by which
    conformity is established;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft, record the noise levels
    in its flight manual or in a supplement to that manual using the
    Guidelines for the Administration of Noise Certification
    Documentation set out in Attachment G of Annex 16, Volume I to the
    Convention;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} submit a signed undertaking to carry out the
    responsibilities specified in Division VIII; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} submit to the Minister for approval any manual,
    instructions and limitations that are required by the certification
    basis established in respect of the product.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for the approval of a change to the type
  design of an aeronautical product other than a restricted category
  aircraft shall demonstrate to the Minister that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft, no feature or
    characteristic makes the aircraft unsafe, taking into account the
    category in which certification is requested; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the type design of the product provides a level of
    safety at least equivalent to that provided by the certification
    basis that applied before the change was undertaken.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for the approval of a change to the type
  design of a restricted category aircraft shall demonstrate to the
  Minister that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} no feature or characteristic makes the aircraft
    unsafe when that aircraft is operated within the limitations
    specified for its intended use; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft has a type design that conforms to its
    certification basis.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
- [SOR/2019-119, s. 22(F)](#1126743-1144205){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126743-1144205.html"}
:::

##### [Issuance of Approval of a Change to the Type Design]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992377 .Subheading}

**[[521.161]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.161 .sectionLabel}** Subject to
section 6.71 of the Act, the Minister shall approve a change to the type
design of an aeronautical product if the applicant meets the
requirements set out in section 521.160.

::: HistoricalNote

#### [Division V --- Supplemental Type Certificates]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992382 .Subheading}

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992383 .Subheading}

**[[521.201]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.201 .sectionLabel}** This Division
applies

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in respect of the issuance of a supplemental type
  certificate as a result of a change to the type design of an
  aeronautical product; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} to applicants for and holders of a supplemental type
  certificate in respect of an aeronautical product.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Eligibility Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992389 .Subheading}

for a supplemental type certificate in respect of a change to the type
design of an aeronautical product shall have, or have access to, the
technical capability to conduct the design analyses and tests required
to demonstrate the conformity of the aeronautical product with its
certification basis.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Application for a Supplemental Type Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992393 .Subheading}

**[[521.203]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.203 .sectionLabel}** Subject to
section 521.153, an applicant for a supplemental type certificate in
respect of a change to the type design of an aeronautical product for
which the Minister has issued or accepted a type certificate shall
submit an application to the Minister as specified in section 521.155.

##### [Certification Basis]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992397 .Subheading}

**[[521.204]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.204 .sectionLabel}** The Minister
shall establish, in respect of a change to the type design of an
aeronautical product, a certification basis consisting of the applicable
standards referred to in section 521.157.

- SOR/2009-280, s. 26

#### [Division VI --- Repair Design Approvals]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992414 .Subheading}

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992415 .Subheading}

**[[521.251]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.251 .sectionLabel}** This Division
applies

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in respect of the issuance of a repair design
  approval as a result of a repair to an aeronautical product; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} to applicants for and holders of a repair design
  approval in respect of an aeronautical product.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Eligibility Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992421 .Subheading}

**[[521.252]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.252 .sectionLabel}** An applicant
for a repair design approval in respect of an aeronautical product shall
have, or have access to, the technical capability to conduct the design
analyses and tests required to demonstrate the conformity of the
aeronautical product with its certification basis.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Application for a Repair Design Approval]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992425 .Subheading}

**[[521.253]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.253 .sectionLabel}** An applicant
for a repair design approval in respect of an aeronautical product shall
submit an application to the Minister as specified in section 521.155 if
the repair is in respect of

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} an aeronautical product for which the Minister has
  issued or accepted a type certificate; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft registered in a foreign state, or an
  aeronautical product intended for installation on an aircraft
  registered in a foreign state, with which Canada has an airworthiness

  technical data used to repair the aeronautical product.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Certification Basis]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992431 .Subheading}

**[[521.254]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.254 .sectionLabel}** The Minister
shall establish a certification basis, in respect of a repair design
approval for an aeronautical product, consisting of the applicable
standards referred to in section 521.157.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

**[[521.255]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.255 .sectionLabel}** An applicant

#### [Division VII --- Part Design Approvals]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992448 .Subheading}

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992449 .Subheading}

**[[521.301]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.301 .sectionLabel}** This Division
applies

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in respect of the issuance of a part design approval
  for a replacement part that is intended to be installed on an
  aeronautical product; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} to applicants for and holders of a part design
  approval in respect of a replacement part.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Eligibility Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992455 .Subheading}

**[[521.302]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.302 .sectionLabel}** An applicant
for a part design approval in respect of a replacement part shall have,
or have access to, the technical capability to conduct the design
analyses and tests required to demonstrate the conformity of the
replacement part with its certification basis.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Application for a Part Design Approval]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992459 .Subheading}

- **[[521.303]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.303
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for a part design
  approval in respect of a replacement part for an aeronautical product
  for which the Minister has issued or accepted a type certificate shall
  submit an application to the Minister as specified in section 521.155.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A part design approval shall not be issued if the
  replacement part

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is subject to an airworthiness limitation;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is a standard part or a commercial part;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} constitutes a change to the type design of the
    aeronautical product; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} creates an airworthiness limitation.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Certification Basis]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992469 .Subheading}

**[[521.304]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.304 .sectionLabel}** The Minister
shall establish, in respect of a part design approval for a replacement
part, a certification basis consisting of the applicable standards
referred to in section 521.157.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Conformity with Certification Basis]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992473 .Subheading}

**[[521.305]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.305 .sectionLabel}** An applicant
for a part design approval in respect of a replacement part shall comply
with the requirements set out in section 521.160 within the effective
period referred to in section 521.156.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Issuance of a Part Design Approval]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992477 .Subheading}

**[[521.306]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.306 .sectionLabel}** Subject to
section 6.71 of the Act, the Minister shall issue a part design approval
in respect of a replacement part if the applicant complies with the
requirements set out in section 521.305.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Change to a Part Design Approved in a Part Design Approval]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992481 .Subheading}

**[[521.307]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.307 .sectionLabel}** The holder of a
part design approval in respect of a replacement part who proposes to
make a change to the part design approved in the part design approval
shall comply with

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a change to the type design, the
  requirements set out in Division V; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in any other case, the requirements set out in
  section 521.154.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

**\[521.308 to 521.350 reserved\]**

#### [Division VIII --- Responsibilities of a Design Approval Document Holder]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992488 .Subheading}

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992489 .Subheading}

**[[521.351]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.351 .sectionLabel}** This Division
applies to holders of a design approval document.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Technical Capability]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992493 .Subheading}

**[[521.352]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.352 .sectionLabel}** The holder of a
design approval document in respect of an aeronautical product shall
have, or have access to, the technical capability

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} to conduct design analyses and tests in order to
  develop the data required to maintain the aeronautical product in an
  airworthy condition; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} to carry out the responsibilities specified this
  Division.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Service Difficulty Reporting]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992499 .Subheading}

**[[521.353]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.353 .sectionLabel}** The holder of a
design approval document in respect of an aeronautical product shall
report to the Minister, in accordance with Division IX, any reportable
service difficulty related to the aeronautical product.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Establishing a Service Difficulty Reporting System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992503 .Subheading}

**[[521.354]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.354 .sectionLabel}** The holder of a
design approval document in respect of an aeronautical product shall
establish and maintain a service difficulty reporting system for the
purpose of receiving, recording, analyzing and investigating reports and
information concerning a reportable service difficulty related to the
aeronautical product.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Investigation of Service Difficulty Reports]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992507 .Subheading}

- **[[521.355]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.355
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} When the holder of a design approval
  document in respect of an aeronautical product receives notice that a
  service difficulty report has been submitted to the Transport Canada
  web service difficulty reporting system in relation to the
  aeronautical product, the holder shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} investigate the service difficulty and, if it
    results from a deficiency in the aeronautical product, develop a
    corrective action to rectify the deficiency; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} report to the Minister the progress of the
    investigation and any proposed corrective action.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 521.356, if the Minister
  determines that a corrective action is required to rectify the
  deficiency, the holder of the design approval document in respect of
  the aeronautical product shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} submit the technical data in support of the
    proposed corrective action to the Minister; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} undertake any corrective action that the Minister
    determines is necessary to rectify the deficiency.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
- [SOR/2019-119, s. 24(F)](#1126747-1144207){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126747-1144207.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-521.355-20091201.html "Link to previous version of section 521.355"){.PITLink}

##### [Mandatory Changes]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992517 .Subheading}

**[[521.356]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.356 .sectionLabel}** If the Minister
determines that a corrective action is required to rectify an unsafe
condition in an aeronautical product, the holder of the design approval
document in respect of the aeronautical product shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} submit to the Minister for approval the corrective
  action required to rectify the unsafe condition; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} on approval of the corrective action, make available
  to each owner and each operator of the aeronautical product the
  information needed to rectify the unsafe condition.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Transfer]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992523 .Subheading}

- **[[521.357]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.357
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), the
  Minister shall approve the transfer of a design approval document in
  respect of an aeronautical product from the holder of the design
  approval document to a transferee if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the holder

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} notifies the Minister in writing of the intention
      to transfer the design approval document,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} provides the Minister with the legal name,
      address and telephone number of the transferee,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} provides the Minister with the number of the
      design approval document, the legal name of the manufacturer and
      the model designation of the aeronautical product that is the
      subject of the transfer,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} returns to the Minister the original design
      approval document signed by the holder, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} provides the transferee with the type design of
      the aeronautical product that is the subject of the transfer and
      the information recorded under paragraph 521.365(a); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the transferee

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} applies for the issuance of an amended design
      approval document,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} complies with the requirements set out in
      section 521.352, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} submits a signed undertaking to carry out the
      responsibilities specified in this Division.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the transfer involves a foreign state, the holder
  of the design approval document and the transferee shall comply with
  the provisions of any airworthiness agreement or similar arrangement
  that exists between Canada and the foreign state involved in the
  transfer.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26

**\[521.358 to 521.364 reserved\]**

##### [Record Keeping]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992540 .Subheading}

**[[521.365]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.365 .sectionLabel}** The holder of a
design approval document in respect of an aeronautical product shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} establish and maintain a system for recording

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the type design of the aeronautical product,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the analyses, tests and inspections that were
    conducted to demonstrate the conformity of the aeronautical product
    with its certification basis,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the certification plan and record and the
    declaration attesting to the demonstration of conformity of the
    aeronautical product with its certification basis,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the data developed by the holder and required to
    maintain the aeronautical product in an airworthy condition, and

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the distribution or initial sale of the
    aeronautical product;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} at the request of the Minister, make available to the
  Minister the design approval document, the type design and any of the
  information recorded under paragraph (a); and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} notify the Minister in writing if the holder no
  longer intends to make the information recorded under paragraph (a)
  available for the purpose of manufacture, modification, repair or
  installation of the aeronautical product or for maintaining the
  airworthiness of the aeronautical product.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
- [SOR/2019-119, s. 26](#1126751-1144211){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126751-1144211.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-521.365-20091201.html "Link to previous version of section 521.365"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Loss or Disposal of Records]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992552 .Subheading}

- **[[521.366]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.366
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall dispose of or
  destroy the records containing the information recorded under
  paragraph 521.365(a) without the written authorization of the
  Minister.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a design approval document in respect
  of an aeronautical product shall notify the Minister in writing if the
  records containing the information recorded under paragraph 521.365(a)
  are lost or destroyed.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Manuals]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992558 .Subheading}

- **[[521.367]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.367
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a design approval
  document in respect of an aeronautical product shall develop and
  maintain the manuals and their supplements that are required by the
  certification basis of the aeronautical product and are required to
  support the operation of the product in service, including

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an installation manual;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an operating manual;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a maintenance manual;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} an overhaul manual;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} servicing instructions;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} instructions for continued airworthiness;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} an illustrated parts manual; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} service bulletins or equivalent documents.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a design approval document other than a
  Canadian Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO) Design Approval in respect
  of an appliance or a part shall develop and maintain the manuals and
  their supplements that are required by the certification basis of the
  aeronautical product and are required to support the operation of the
  product in service, including

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft flight manual;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a structural repair manual;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} supplemental integrity instructions;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a master minimum equipment list; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a maintenance review board report.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a design approval document in respect
  of an aeronautical product shall, on request, provide the Minister
  with up to six copies of the manuals and their supplements referred to
  in subsections (1) and (2), at no cost, in a format agreed to by the
  Minister.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Instructions for Continued Airworthiness]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992578 .Subheading}

**[[521.368]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.368 .sectionLabel}** If the
certification basis of an aeronautical product requires that
instructions for continued airworthiness be developed, the holder of a
design approval document in respect of the aeronautical product shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} provide the instructions for continued airworthiness

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aeronautical product other than
    an aircraft, to each owner of the aeronautical product on the date
    of its delivery, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft, to each owner of the
    aeronautical product on the later of the date of its delivery and
    the date of the issuance of its first certificate of airworthiness;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} provide any change to the instructions for continued
  airworthiness

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aeronautical product other than
    an aircraft, to each of its owners, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft, to each of its
    operators;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} make available to any person referred to in
  subsection 571.02(1) the instructions for continued airworthiness and
  any changes to those instructions; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} submit to the Minister a plan that identifies how
  changes to the instructions for continued airworthiness will be made
  available and distributed to any person referred to in paragraph
  (a), (b) or (c).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Supplemental Integrity Instructions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992590 .Subheading}

- **[[521.369]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.369
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This section applies in respect of
  an aeroplane for which a type certificate has been issued and that is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a commuter category aeroplane operated under
    Subpart 4 of Part VII; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a transport category aeroplane operated under
    Subpart 4 or 5 of Part VII.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Before an aeroplane referred to in subsection (1)
  meets the applicable in-service criterion specified in subsection (3),
  the holder of the type certificate in respect of the aeroplane shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} develop supplemental integrity instructions in
    accordance with subsection (4) and submit them to the Minister for
    approval in accordance with subsection (5); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} on their approval, make the supplemental integrity
    instructions available to each owner and each operator of an
    aeroplane of that type.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The in-service criterion that determines whether
  supplemental integrity instructions are required in respect of the
  aeroplane is that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane reaches the design life goal ---
    which is the expected period of operational service of the aeroplane
    --- as established by the type certificate holder, and a corrosion
    protection and control program is in place; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane completes 20 years of service and

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} no corrosion protection and control program is in
      place, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} no design life goal has been established.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The supplemental integrity instructions required
  under subsection (2) shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} specify a method for maintaining the conformity of
    the aeroplane with its certification basis;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} incorporate any recommendation resulting from a
    detailed engineering assessment of the primary airframe structure of
    the aeroplane and from the service history of that aeroplane;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} identify, for periodic review, all principal
    structural elements whose failure could result in the loss of the
    aeroplane or significantly reduce the overall structural strength of
    its airframe;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} contain a supplemental structural integrity
    document that consists of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a description of each principal structural
      element that has been selected for supplementary inspection,
      modification or replacement, and its structural location,
      component or damage site,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a description of the type of damage expected ---
      such as fatigue, corrosion, delamination, disbondment, accidental
      damage or multiple-site damage --- for each structural location
      identified, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a reference to any existing maintenance manual
      or service bulletin intended for the aeroplane;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} recommend, for each principal structural element
    that has been selected for supplementary inspection under paragraph
    (d),

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} an initial or threshold inspection and the
      intervals for repeat inspections, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} inspection methods and inspection procedures
      appropriate for the type of damage referred to in subparagraph
      (d)(ii), including any alternatives to the intervals for
      inspections and to the methods and procedures used;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} specify any modifications, replacements or
    corrosion control measures, optional or mandatory, that could change
    or terminate the inspection requirements set out in paragraph (e);
    and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} provide guidance for reporting to the Minister the
    findings from any inspection conducted using the supplemental
    structural integrity document.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall approve the supplemental integrity
  instructions submitted in respect of an aeroplane if the Minister
  determines that the instructions provide a level of safety equivalent
  to that provided by the standards of airworthiness in force at the
  time the type certificate was issued in respect of the aeroplane.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a type certificate in respect of an
  aeroplane who proposes to make a change to the supplemental integrity
  instructions for the aeroplane shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} submit the change to the Minister for approval; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} on approval of the change, make the changed
    instructions available to each owner and each operator of an
    aeroplane of that type.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

**\[521.370 to 521.400 reserved\]**

#### [Division IX --- Service Difficulty Reporting]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992623 .Subheading}

##### [Form and Submission]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992624 .Subheading}

- **[[521.401]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.401
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A person who is required to report a
  service difficulty shall submit to the Minister, for each reportable
  service difficulty, a separate service difficulty report that contains
  the information specified in the form published by the Minister
  entitled Service Difficulty Report.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A service difficulty report shall be submitted

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} by electronic means, such as the Transport Canada
    web service difficulty reporting system; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} by mail or courier.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Time Limits]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992632 .Subheading}

- **[[521.402]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.402
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), a person
  who is required to report a service difficulty shall submit a service
  difficulty report to the Minister within three working days after the
  day on which the reportable service difficulty is discovered.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If all of the information required under subsection
  521.401(1) is not available within the period specified in subsection
  (1), an interim service difficulty report containing the following
  elements may be submitted to the Minister in a manner specified in
  subsection 521.401(2) within three working days after the day on which
  the reportable service difficulty is discovered:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft registration, if applicable;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the date of the occurrence of the reportable
    service difficulty;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a description of the reportable service difficulty;
    and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the name, mailing address, and telephone and fax
    numbers of the person submitting the report.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The person submitting the interim service difficulty
  report shall submit a complete service difficulty report that complies
  with the requirements set out in subsection 521.401(1) within 14 days
  after the day on which the reportable service difficulty is
  discovered.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Service Difficulty Report Not Required]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992643 .Subheading}

**[[521.403]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.403 .sectionLabel}** A service
difficulty report is not required for a reportable service difficulty
that has been reported by another person or organization.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

**\[521.404 to 521.425 reserved\]**

#### [Division X --- Airworthiness Directives]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992648 .Subheading}

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992649 .Subheading}

**[[521.426]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.426 .sectionLabel}** This Division
applies in respect of aeronautical products for which a design approval
document has been issued or accepted by the Minister.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Conditions for Issuance]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992653 .Subheading}

- **[[521.427]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.427
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall issue an
  airworthiness directive in respect of an aeronautical product if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an unsafe condition exists in the aeronautical
    product and the condition is likely to exist or develop in other
    aeronautical products;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} it is necessary to modify or cancel the
    requirements of an airworthiness directive issued by the foreign
    airworthiness authority having jurisdiction over the type design of
    the aeronautical product because the Minister considers the
    airworthiness directive inappropriate for reasons related to the
    environment, safety, the delayed receipt of an instruction issued by
    the foreign airworthiness authority or reliance on foreign
    legislation; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} it is necessary to modify or cancel a Canadian
    airworthiness directive that is in force, because a condition for
    issuance referred to in paragraph (a) or (b) has changed or ceased
    to exist.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The airworthiness directive shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} identify the unsafe condition;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} identify the affected aeronautical products;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} specify the corrective actions required;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} specify the schedule for completion of the required
    corrective actions; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} specify its effective date.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} This section does not apply if the unsafe condition
  referred to in paragraph 521.427(1)(a) is rectified by a corrective
  action taken under section 521.356.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Distribution]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992668 .Subheading}

**[[521.428]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.428 .sectionLabel}** The Minister
shall distribute an airworthiness directive to

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the registered owner of a Canadian aircraft affected
  by the airworthiness directive;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the manufacturer of an aeronautical product and the
  holder of the design approval document in respect of the aeronautical
  product; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the airworthiness authority of all known states of
  registry of the aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

**\[521.429 to 521.450 reserved\]**

#### [Division XI --- Foreign Aeronautical Products]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992676 .Subheading}

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992677 .Subheading}

**[[521.451]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.451 .sectionLabel}** This Division
applies

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in respect of the issuance of a design approval
  document for a foreign aeronautical product; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} to applicants for and holders of a design approval
  document in respect of a foreign aeronautical product.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Eligibility Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992683 .Subheading}

**[[521.452]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.452 .sectionLabel}** An applicant
for a design approval document in respect of a foreign aeronautical
product shall demonstrate to the Minister that the foreign airworthiness
authority having jurisdiction over the type design of the foreign
aeronautical product has issued or will issue a document equivalent to a
design approval document in respect of that foreign aeronautical
product.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Application for a Design Approval Document]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992687 .Subheading}

- **[[521.453]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.453
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), an
  applicant for a design approval document in respect of a foreign
  aeronautical product shall submit an application to the Minister as
  specified in

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} section 521.28, in the case of a type certificate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} section 521.103, in the case of a Canadian
    Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO) design approval;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} section 521.203, in the case of a supplemental type
    certificate;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} section 521.253, in the case of a repair design
    approval; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} section 521.303, in the case of a part design
    approval.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for a design approval document in
  respect of a foreign aeronautical product shall submit an application
  in accordance with the provisions of any airworthiness agreement or
  similar arrangement that exists between Canada and the state of design
  of the foreign aeronautical product.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Exceptions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992698 .Subheading}

**[[521.454]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.454 .sectionLabel}** Paragraphs
521.44(a) and (b), section 521.47 and paragraph 521.108(a) do not apply
in respect of a foreign aeronautical product.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Issuance of a Design Approval Document]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992702 .Subheading}

- **[[521.455]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.455
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), if the
  foreign airworthiness authority having jurisdiction over the type
  design of a foreign aeronautical product has issued or will issue a
  document equivalent to a design approval document in respect of the
  foreign aeronautical product, the Minister shall issue a design
  approval document if the applicant

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} complies with the requirements set out in the
    division applicable to the design approval document that is the
    subject of the application; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} demonstrates that the foreign aeronautical product
    conforms to the standards of airworthiness and the aircraft
    emissions standards referred to in the division applicable to the
    design approval document that is the subject of the application and
    that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} are in force on the date on which the application
      for the document equivalent to the design approval document was
      submitted to the foreign airworthiness authority having
      jurisdiction over the type design of the foreign aeronautical
      product, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} are recorded by the foreign airworthiness
      authority in the type certificate data sheets in respect of that
      foreign aeronautical product.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the airworthiness authority of a foreign state has
  entered into an airworthiness agreement or similar arrangement with
  Canada, the Minister shall conduct a type design examination of the
  foreign aeronautical product that is the subject of the application to
  determine if the type design of that foreign aeronautical product
  provides a level of safety equivalent to that specified in this
  Subpart.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister determines that the type design of
  the foreign aeronautical product provides a level of safety equivalent
  to that specified in this Subpart, the Minister shall, in accordance
  with the provisions of the airworthiness agreement or similar
  arrangement referred to in subsection (2), issue a design approval
  document or accept the design approval document issued by the foreign
  airworthiness authority in respect of the foreign aeronautical
  product.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

##### [Changes to a Type Design]{.HTitleText4} {#h-992713 .Subheading}

- **[[521.456]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-521.456
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If the holder of a design approval
  document issued under section 521.455 makes a change to the type
  design of a foreign aeronautical product that alters a condition or
  limitation prescribed for the foreign aeronautical product by the
  foreign airworthiness authority having jurisdiction over the type
  design of the foreign aeronautical product, the change shall be
  approved by that airworthiness authority and is subject to a type
  design examination by the Minister.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister determines that the change to the
  type design of the foreign aeronautical product provides a level of
  safety equivalent to that specified in this Subpart, the Minister
  shall, in accordance with the provisions of the airworthiness
  agreement or similar arrangement referred to in subsection 521.455(2),
  issue an amended design approval document or accept the design
  approval document issued by the foreign airworthiness authority in
  respect of the change to the type design of the foreign aeronautical
  product.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 26
:::

### [Subpart 49 --- Amateur-Built Aircraft]{.HTitleText2} {#h-992739 .Subheading}

#### [Requirements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992740 .Subheading}

**[[549.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-549.01 .sectionLabel}** A person who
intends to construct an aircraft and obtain, under paragraph 507.03(b),
a special certificate of airworthiness in the amateur-built category in
respect of the aircraft must

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} before starting construction,

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} inform the Minister of the intention to construct
    the aircraft,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} show that the aircraft design meets the standards
    specified in Chapter 549 of the Airworthiness Manual, and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} show that the major portion of the aircraft will
    be constructed from raw material and assembled on a non-commercial,
    non-production basis for educational or recreational purposes; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} during construction and again before the first
  flight, make the aircraft available to the Minister for inspection.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/98-526, s. 3
:::

### [SUBPART 51]{.HLabel2}[[\[Repealed, SOR/2009-280, s. 27\]]{.Repealed}]{.HTitleText2} {#h-992749 .Subheading}

**[[551.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-551.01 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed,
SOR/2009-280, s. 27\]]{.Repealed}

### [Subpart 61 --- Manufacture of Aeronautical Products]{.HTitleText2} {#h-992751 .Subheading}

#### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992752 .Subheading}

**[[561.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-561.01 .sectionLabel}** In this Subpart,

[[design approval]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[design approval]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a type certificate, a
    supplemental type certificate, a part design approval, a Canadian
    Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO) design approval or a document
    equivalent to any of those documents that is issued by the
    airworthiness authority of a foreign state; ([approbation de
    conception]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[manual]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[manual]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the manual established under
    section 561.07; ([manuel]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[Standard 561]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[Standard 561]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means Standard 561 --- Standard
    for Approved Manufacturers. ([norme 561]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-348, s. 4
- SOR/2009-280, s. 28
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-561.01-20071201.html "Link to previous version of section 561.01"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Application]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992759 .Subheading}

**[[561.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-561.02 .sectionLabel}** This Subpart
applies in respect of the manufacture of an aeronautical product in
respect of which a design approval has been issued but does not apply in
respect of

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} maintenance;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the manufacture of standard parts;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the manufacture of commercial parts; or

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the manufacture of parts during a repair or
  modification under subsection 571.06(4).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-348, s. 4
:::

#### [Manufacturer Certificate --- Application, Issuance and Amendment]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992767 .Subheading}

- **[[561.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-561.03
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for the issuance or
  amendment of a manufacturer certificate respecting an aeronautical
  product shall submit an application to the Minister that includes the
  documents specified in section 561.03 of Standard 561.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for the issuance or amendment of a
  manufacturer certificate respecting an aeronautical product shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} be the holder of, or applicant for, a design
    approval for that aeronautical product; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} have written authorization from the holder of a
    design approval to manufacture that aeronautical product.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for the issuance or amendment of a
  manufacturer certificate respecting an aeronautical product shall
  demonstrate that they have access to all present and future design
  data, process specifications and other related information necessary
  for the continuing airworthiness of the aeronautical product.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall issue or amend a manufacturer
  certificate authorizing an applicant to manufacture the aeronautical
  products set out in the manufacturer certificate if the applicant
  meets the requirements of this Subpart.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} A manufacturer certificate may authorize the
  manufacture of a limited number of an aeronautical product where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an applicant has made an application for a design
    approval for that aeronautical product but it has not yet been
    issued; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an applicant is about to enter into a license
    agreement with the holder of the design approval for that
    aeronautical product.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} Unless an expiry date is specified in the
  manufacturer certificate issued under subsection (4), the certificate
  shall remain in effect until it is surrendered by the manufacturer or
  suspended or cancelled.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} A manufacturer certificate is not transferable.

- [(8)]{.lawlabel} Except as provided in section 561.06, the final
  assembly facilities for an aeronautical product specified in a
  manufacturer certificate shall be located in Canada.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-348, s. 4
:::

#### [Management Personnel]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992783 .Subheading}

- **[[561.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-561.04
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a manufacturer
  certificate shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} appoint a person to be responsible for all the
    activities performed under this Subpart and specified in the manual;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the person appointed has acquired
    experience in the areas of responsibility set out in subsection
    561.04(1) of Standard 561.

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2022-246, s. 12\]]{.Repealed}

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2022-246, s. 12\]]{.Repealed}

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2022-246, s. 12\]]{.Repealed}

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2022-246, s. 12\]]{.Repealed}

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a manufacturer certificate shall
  provide the person appointed with the authority and the financial and
  human resources necessary to ensure that the requirements of this
  Subpart are met.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} The person appointed may assign responsibility for
  the management of specific activities, systems or programs required by
  this Subpart to other persons, provided that the assignments and the
  scope of the assigned responsibilities are specified in the manual.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a manufacturer certificate shall ensure
  that no person is appointed under paragraph (1)(a) or remains
  responsible for the activities referred to in that paragraph if, at
  the time of their appointment or during their tenure, they have a
  record of conviction for

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an offence under section 7.3 of the Act; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} two or more offences in respect of section 561.10
    of these Regulations, not arising from a single occurrence.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-348, s. 4
- [SOR/2019-119, s. 27(F)](#1126753-1144212){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126753-1144212.html"}
- [SOR/2022-246, s. 12](#1380136-1380767){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1380136-1380767.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-561.04-20190614.html "Link to previous version of section 561.04"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Resources]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992799 .Subheading}

**[[561.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-561.05 .sectionLabel}** The holder of a
manufacturer certificate shall have, and ensure that any supplier
referred to in section 561.13 has, the financial and human resources
necessary for the manufacture and inspection of any aeronautical product
specified in the manufacturer certificate, including those specified in
section 561.05 of Standard 561.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-348, s. 4
:::

#### [Facilities Located in a Foreign State]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992803 .Subheading}

**[[561.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-561.06 .sectionLabel}** If an arrangement
exists between Canada and a foreign state concerning the manufacture of
an aeronautical product, the holder of a manufacturer certificate may be
authorized to perform their activities under the certificate in
facilities located in that foreign state if the holder

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} submits a written application to that effect to the
  Minister;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} gives, by a written agreement, an undertaking to the
  Minister to ensure that the Minister has access to those facilities to
  verify that the performance of the activities complies with the
  requirements of the Act and these Regulations, as if those facilities
  were located in Canada; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} undertakes to pay the expenses referred to in
  paragraphs 104.04(1)(a) and (b) incurred by the Department of
  Transport under paragraph (b).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-348, s. 4
:::

#### [Manual]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992810 .Subheading}

- **[[561.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-561.07
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a manufacturer
  certificate shall establish, maintain and require the use of a manual
  that must include the information set out in section 561.07 of
  Standard 561 and that sets out policies and procedures respecting the
  construction and inspection of the aeronautical products specified in
  the manufacturer certificate.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), the person appointed under
  paragraph 561.04(1)(a) shall ensure that any person who performs work
  under a manufacturer certificate complies with the manual.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2019-295, s. 10\]]{.Repealed}

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subject to the following conditions, the holder of a
  manufacturer certificate and any person who performs work under a
  manufacturer certificate may temporarily be authorized to use
  alternative policies and procedures to comply with subsections (2) and
  (3):

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} they have determined that, as a result of
    unforeseen or temporary circumstances, compliance with the manual
    would be impossible or unreasonable;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} they believe on reasonable grounds that the safety
    of the aeronautical product can be achieved by complying with the
    alternative policies and procedures;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} they have notified the Minister in writing; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the Minister has notified them in writing that they
    can use those alternative policies and procedures.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a manufacturer certificate shall submit
  the manual and any subsequent amendment to the Minister for approval.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall approve the manual and any
  subsequent amendment if they meet the requirements of this Subpart and
  Standard 561.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} If the manual no longer meets the requirements of
  this Subpart or Standard 561, the holder of a manufacturer certificate
  shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} submit an amendment to the manual for the
    Minister's approval; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} amend the manual immediately if instructed to do so
    by the Minister.

- [(8)]{.lawlabel} The person who has been assigned the responsibility
  under subsection 561.04(6) shall amend each copy of the manual within
  30 days after receiving the Minister's approval of an amendment to it.

- [(9)]{.lawlabel} A manual may incorporate other documents by reference
  if it includes policies and procedures to control the incorporated
  material.

- [(10)]{.lawlabel} The person appointed under paragraph 561.04(1)(a)
  shall ensure that any part of the manual or incorporated document that
  is relevant to the work to be performed is made available to each
  person who performs that work.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-348, s. 4
- SOR/2015-160, s. 25(F)
- [SOR/2019-295, s. 10](#1194394-1195511){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1194394-1195511.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-561.07-20150831.html "Link to previous version of section 561.07"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Production Control System]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992830 .Subheading}

- **[[561.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-561.08
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a manufacturer
  certificate shall establish and maintain a production control system
  that consists of systems and procedures set out in section 561.08 of
  Standard 561 to ensure that aeronautical products comply with these
  Regulations throughout the manufacturing process.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The production control system shall be under the
  control of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person appointed under paragraph 561.04(1)(a);
    or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a person assigned the responsibility for the
    management of the production control system under subsection
    561.04(6).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The person referred to in subsection (2) who has
  control of the production control system shall ensure that the
  activities carried out under the manufacturer certificate for which
  they have been assigned responsibility are in compliance with this
  Subpart.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-348, s. 4
:::

#### [Quality Assurance Program]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992839 .Subheading}

- **[[561.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-561.09
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a manufacturer
  certificate shall, in order to ensure that all aspects of the
  activities carried out under the manufacturer certificate continue to
  comply with these Regulations, establish and maintain a quality
  assurance program, independent of the production control system, that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is under the sole control of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the person appointed under paragraph
      561.04(1)(a), or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a person assigned the responsibility for the
      management of the quality assurance program under subsection
      561.04(6); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements specified in section 561.09
    of Standard 561.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The person referred to in paragraph (1)(a) shall
  ensure that records related to the findings from the quality assurance
  program are distributed to the appropriate manager for corrective
  action and follow-up in accordance with the procedures specified in
  the manual.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The person referred to in paragraph (1)(a) shall
  establish and maintain an audit system that consists of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an initial audit, within 12 months after the day on
    which the manufacturer certificate is issued, that covers all
    aspects of the manufacturer's activities;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} subsequent audits conducted at the intervals set
    out in the manual;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a record of each occurrence of compliance or
    non-compliance found during an audit referred to in paragraph (a) or
    (b);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} procedures for ensuring that each finding of an
    audit is communicated to them;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} follow-up procedures for ensuring that corrective
    actions are effective; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a system for recording the findings of initial and
    periodic audits, corrective actions and follow-ups.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The records required under paragraph (3)(f) shall be
  retained for the greater of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} two audit cycles; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} two years.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The quality assurance program duties related to
  specific tasks or activities shall be performed by persons who are not
  responsible for and have not been involved in the performance of the
  tasks or activities being audited.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-348, s. 4
:::

#### [Statement of Conformity]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992860 .Subheading}

- **[[561.10]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-561.10
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall sign a statement of
  conformity in respect of an aeronautical product unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the statement contains the elements referred to in
    section 561.10 of Standard 561;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person has been authorized to do so by the
    person in control of the production control system;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the aeronautical product is specified in the
    manufacturer certificate; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the aeronautical product has been manufactured in
    accordance with this Subpart.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall authorize a person to sign, on behalf
  of the holder of a manufacturer certificate, a statement of conformity
  unless the person being authorized has complied with the policies and
  procedures set out in the manual and has successfully completed the
  training required under section 561.11.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-348, s. 4
:::

#### [Training Program]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992870 .Subheading}

**[[561.11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-561.11 .sectionLabel}** The holder of a
manufacturer certificate shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} establish and maintain a training program that
  includes the initial training, updating and any other training set out
  in section 561.11 of Standard 561 to ensure continued qualification
  that is appropriate to the function to be performed or supervised; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} ensure that persons who are authorized to perform or
  supervise the performance of any function required under this Subpart
  are trained in respect of the parts of the policies and procedures of
  the holder of the manufacturer certificate and the parts of these
  Regulations applicable to that function.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-348, s. 4
:::

#### [Personnel Records]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992876 .Subheading}

- **[[561.12]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-561.12
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a manufacturer
  certificate shall establish and maintain a personnel record for each
  employee of the manufacturer and retain each record for at least three
  years after the end of their employment.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A personnel record may be in paper or electronic form
  and shall include all of the employee's qualifications, all
  authorizations to sign a statement of conformity pursuant to section
  561.10 and a description of the training referred to in section
  561.11.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a manufacturer certificate shall ensure
  that a copy of any record required by this section is provided to the
  employee referred to in the record on the completion of each training
  activity or the granting of an authorization to sign a statement of
  conformity under section 561.10.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-348, s. 4
:::

#### [Control of Suppliers]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992883 .Subheading}

- **[[561.13]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-561.13
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a manufacturer
  certificate who contracts work to a supplier shall ensure that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a written agreement with the supplier specifies the
    work to be performed by the supplier and provides that the Minister
    may have access to and inspect the supplier's facilities and records
    to ensure compliance with this Subpart;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} work is contracted only to suppliers that have been
    evaluated in accordance with the policies and procedures set out in
    the manual;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} work is done under the holder's supervision and is
    subject to the quality assurance program set out in section 561.09;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the supplier's capability to perform the contracted
    work is evaluated and monitored; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the aeronautical product conforms to its approved
    design.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a supplier holds, in respect of an aeronautical
  product, a manufacturer certificate or an equivalent document issued
  by a foreign state with which Canada has an airworthiness agreement or
  similar arrangement, the issuance of the supplier's own statement of
  conformity in respect of that product is considered as meeting the
  requirements of paragraphs (1)(c) to (e).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No supplier who performs work for a holder of a
  manufacturer certificate under this Subpart shall subcontract the work
  to another supplier without having first obtained the written consent
  of the holder of a manufacturer certificate.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-348, s. 4
:::

#### [Aeronautical Product Records]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992895 .Subheading}

- **[[561.14]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-561.14
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a manufacturer
  certificate shall establish and maintain records for each aeronautical
  product manufactured under a manufacturer certificate, including those
  specified in section 561.14 of Standard 561.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a manufacturer certificate shall ensure
  that product records are kept for at least three years after the day
  on which the statement of conformity was signed.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-348, s. 4
:::

#### [Service Difficulty Reporting]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992901 .Subheading}

**[[561.15]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-561.15 .sectionLabel}** The holder of a
manufacturer certificate shall report to the Minister, in accordance
with Division IX of Subpart 21 of Part V, any reportable service
difficulty related to an aeronautical product being manufactured.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-348, s. 4
- SOR/2009-280, s. 29
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-561.15-20071201.html "Link to previous version of section 561.15"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Cessation of Manufacturing]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992905 .Subheading}

**[[561.16]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-561.16 .sectionLabel}** The holder of a
manufacturer certificate shall notify the Minister in writing of the
permanent cessation of the manufacture of an aeronautical product
specified in the manufacturer certificate within 30 days after
cessation.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-348, s. 4
:::

### [Subpart 71 --- Aircraft Maintenance Requirements]{.HTitleText2} {#h-992909 .Subheading}

#### [Application]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992910 .Subheading}

**[[571.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-571.01 .sectionLabel}** This Subpart
applies in respect of maintenance and elementary work performed on the
following aircraft, except for remotely piloted aircraft that are an
element of a remotely piloted aircraft system in respect of which a
design approval document has not been issued or applied for under
Subpart 21 of this Part, ultra-light aeroplanes and hang gliders:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} Canadian aircraft;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} foreign aircraft operated under Part IV or VII;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} foreign aircraft, other than aircraft referred to in
  paragraph (b), if the maintenance or elementary work is performed
  under the terms of an agreement or technical arrangement between
  Canada and the state of registry of the aircraft; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} parts intended for installation on aircraft referred
  to in paragraphs (a) to (c).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2000-404, s. 3
- [SOR/2019-11, s. 14](#1045401-1110476){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045401-1110476.html"}
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 40](#1516900-1527488){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1516900-1527488.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-571.01-20190109.html "Link to previous version of section 571.01"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Maintenance and Elementary Work Performance Rules]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992918 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2000-404, s. 4

\]
:::

- **[[571.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-571.02
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), a person
  who performs maintenance or elementary work on an aeronautical product
  shall use the most recent methods, techniques, practices, parts,
  materials, tools, equipment and test apparatuses that are

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} specified for the aeronautical product in the most
    recent maintenance manual or instructions for continued
    airworthiness developed by the manufacturer of that aeronautical
    product;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} equivalent to those specified by the manufacturer
    of that aeronautical product in the most recent maintenance manual
    or instructions for continued airworthiness; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in accordance with recognized industry practices at
    the time the maintenance or elementary work is performed.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who performs maintenance or elementary work
  pursuant to subsection (1) shall ensure that any measuring device or
  test equipment used

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} meets the specifications of the manufacturer of the
    aeronautical product with respect to accuracy, taking into account
    the intended use; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if calibration requirements are published by the
    manufacturer of the measuring device or test equipment, is
    calibrated by means traceable to a national standard.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Except if the work is performed in respect of an
  aircraft that is operated under a special certificate of airworthiness
  in the owner-maintenance or amateur-built classification, no person
  shall supervise, or perform without supervision, an inspection using a
  method set out in column I of an item of Schedule I to this Subpart
  unless the person holds the personnel certification set out in column
  II of that item.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-112, s. 4
- SOR/2003-122, s. 1
:::

#### [Recording of Maintenance and Elementary Work]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992932 .Subheading}

**[[571.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-571.03 .sectionLabel}** A person who
performs maintenance or elementary work on an aeronautical product shall
ensure that

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the details required by Standard 571 --- Maintenance
  are entered in the technical record for the aeronautical product, in
  respect of the task performed; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the technical record is accurate with respect to any
  outstanding elements of the work performed, in particular, the need to
  secure any fastening device that was disturbed to facilitate the work.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-122, s. 21](#1126379-1131018){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126379-1131018.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-571.03-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 571.03"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Specialized Maintenance]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992936 .Subheading}

**[[571.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-571.04 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
perform the specialized maintenance set out in Schedule II to this
Subpart on an aeronautical product other than an aircraft operated under
a special certificate of airworthiness in the owner-maintenance or
amateur-built classification, except in accordance with

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a maintenance policy manual (MPM) established by the
  holder of an approved maintenance organization (AMO) certificate
  issued pursuant to section 573.02 with a rating of a category
  appropriate to the work to be performed; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a foreign document equivalent to an MPM established
  by a maintenance organization approved under the laws of a state that
  is party to an agreement with Canada, and the agreement provides for
  recognition of the work to be performed.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-112, s. 5
:::

#### [Maintenance of Aircraft Operated under Part IV or VII]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992942 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2000-404, s. 5

\]
:::

**[[571.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-571.05 .sectionLabel}** Except in the
case of a balloon, no person shall perform maintenance on an aircraft
operated under Part IV or VII, or install on one of the foregoing a part
that has undergone maintenance, unless the maintenance on that aircraft
or part has been performed in accordance with

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a maintenance policy manual (MPM) established by the
  holder of an approved maintenance organization (AMO) certificate
  issued pursuant to section 573.02 with a rating of a category
  appropriate to the work to be performed; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a foreign document equivalent to an MPM established
  by a maintenance organization approved under the laws of a state that
  is party to an agreement with Canada and the agreement provides for
  recognition of the work to be performed.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2000-404, s. 6
:::

#### [Repairs and Modifications]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992950 .Subheading}

- **[[571.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-571.06
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except as provided in subsection (5)
  and in the case of aircraft that are operated under a special
  certificate of airworthiness in the owner-maintenance classification,
  a person who signs a maintenance release in respect of a major repair
  or major modification on an aeronautical product shall ensure that the
  major repair or major modification conforms to the requirements of the
  relevant technical data

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} that have been approved or the use of which has
    been approved within the meaning of the term [[approved
    data]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} in section 571.06 of the Airworthiness
    Manual; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} that have been established within the meaning of
    the term [[specified data]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} in section 571.06 of
    the Airworthiness Manual.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Except as provided in subsection (5), a person who
  signs a maintenance release in respect of a repair or modification,
  other than a major repair or major modification, shall ensure that the
  repair or modification conforms to the requirements of the relevant
  technical data within the meaning of the term [[acceptable
  data]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} in section 571.06 of the Airworthiness
  Manual.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where an additional flight authority has been issued
  under paragraph 507.08(1)(b) in respect of an aircraft, no person
  shall change the configuration of the aircraft in such a manner that
  the aircraft no longer meets the conditions subject to which the
  flight authority applicable to the aircraft prior to the modification
  was issued, unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person makes an entry in the aircraft journey
    log required by section 605.94 indicating the flight authority that
    is in effect for the modified aircraft; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the change is made in accordance with technical
    dispatch procedures required by section 706.06.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Repairing or modifying an aeronautical product may
  include the making of a part in conformity with the standards
  specified in section 571.06 of the Airworthiness Manual, if no part
  made is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} marked with the part number specified in the type
    design; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} installed by a person or organization other than
    the person or organization that made the part.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} A person who signs a maintenance release in respect
  of a repair or modification performed on a foreign aeronautical
  product under the terms of an agreement or a technical arrangement
  between Canada and the aircraft's state of registry shall ensure that
  the repair or modification conforms to the requirements of the
  relevant technical data that are specified in the agreement or
  technical arrangement.

::: HistoricalNote

#### [Installation of New Parts]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992965 .Subheading}

- **[[571.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-571.07
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall install a new part
  on an aeronautical product unless the part meets the standards of
  airworthiness applicable to the installation of new parts and, subject
  to subsections (2) and (3), has been certified under Subpart 61.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No certification referred to in subsection (1) is
  required where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a new part is a foreign-manufactured part that is
    certified pursuant to an agreement with Canada, which agreement
    provides for the acceptance of export airworthiness certification;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a new part is a foreign-manufactured part that is
    obtained from a manufacturer holding a type design recognized in
    Canada and the part is certified in accordance with the laws of the
    state of manufacture;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a new part, whose accompanying documentation has
    been verified, has been inspected in accordance with the
    requirements of Standard 571 --- Maintenance;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a new part is installed on an aircraft that is
    operated under a special certificate of airworthiness in the
    owner-maintenance or amateur-built classification; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a part is made in accordance with subsection
    571.06(4).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No certification referred to in subsection (1) is
  required in respect of a new part that bears markings identifying it
  as a part specified in the type design and that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is a standard part;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is a commercial part; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} is a part that was not originally designed and
    manufactured for aeronautical use but has been approved for use on
    the aeronautical product in the type design.

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2009-280, s. 30\]]{.Repealed}

#### [Installation of Used Parts]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992981 .Subheading}

- **[[571.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-571.08
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall install a used part
  on an aeronautical product, other than aircraft that are operated
  under a special certificate of airworthiness in the owner-maintenance
  or amateur-built classification, unless the part meets the standards
  of airworthiness that are applicable to the installation of used parts
  and are set out in Standard 571 --- Maintenance and

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is an airworthy part that has been removed from an
    aircraft for immediate installation on another aircraft;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is an airworthy part that has undergone maintenance
    for which a maintenance release has been signed pursuant to
    paragraph 571.11(2)(c); or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} has been inspected and tested to ensure that the
    part conforms to its type design and is in a safe condition, and a
    maintenance release has been signed to that effect.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If, under the terms of a loan agreement or an air
  operator parts pooling agreement, a used part has been obtained from a
  source not subject to these Regulations, no person shall permit the
  part to remain in service for longer than 90 days unless specifically
  authorized by the Minister on receipt of documentation demonstrating
  that the part conforms to the applicable type design.

#### [Installation and Disposal of Life-limited Parts]{.HTitleText3} {#h-992990 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2002-112, s. 9

\]
:::

- **[[571.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-571.09
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall install a used
  life-limited part on an aeronautical product unless the part meets the
  standards of airworthiness applicable to the installation of
  life-limited parts and

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the technical history of the part within the
    meaning of section 571.09 of the Airworthiness Manual is available
    to show that the time in service authorized for that part in the
    type certificate governing the installation has not been exceeded;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the history referred to in paragraph (a) is
    incorporated into the technical record for the aeronautical product
    on which the part is installed.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall install a used life-limited part in a
  place other than that from which it was removed unless the part is
  installed

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the same or in an identical position on another
    aeronautical product bearing the same part number as that from which
    the part was removed; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in conformity with the requirements in respect of
    technical data that have been approved or the use of which has been
    approved within the meaning of section 571.09 of the Airworthiness
    Manual.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} When a life-limited part has reached the time in
  service authorized in its type design, the part shall be

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} rendered unusable; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} identified as not airworthy and kept segregated
    from airworthy parts.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-112, s. 10
:::

#### [Maintenance Release]{.HTitleText3} {#h-993005 .Subheading}

- **[[571.10]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-571.10
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall sign a maintenance
  release required pursuant to section 605.85 or permit anyone whom the
  person supervises to sign a maintenance release, unless the standards
  of airworthiness applicable to the maintenance performed and stated in
  Standard 571 --- Maintenance have been complied with and the
  maintenance release meets the applicable requirements specified in
  section 571.10 of the Airworthiness Manual.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Except as provided in subsection (4), a maintenance
  release shall include the following, or a similarly worded, statement:

  "The described maintenance has been performed in accordance with the
  applicable airworthiness requirements."

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No maintenance release is required in respect of any
  task designated as elementary work in the Aircraft Equipment and
  Maintenance Standards that is performed by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a glider, a balloon or an
    unpressurized small aircraft that is powered by a piston engine and
    not operated pursuant to Part IV or VII, the pilot of the aircraft;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft operated under Part IV
    or VII, a person who has been trained and authorized in accordance
    with the flight training unit's or the air operator's maintenance
    control manual (MCM), approved under Subpart 6 of Part IV or of Part
    VII, respectively; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft operated pursuant to
    Subpart 4 of Part VI, a person who has been trained in accordance
    with those sections of a private operator's operations manual that
    contain details of the operator's maintenance control system.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where a person signs a maintenance release in respect
  of maintenance performed on an aircraft, the satisfactory completion
  of which cannot be verified by inspection or testing of the aircraft
  on the ground, the maintenance release shall be made conditional on
  the satisfactory completion of a test flight carried out pursuant to
  subsections 605.85(2) and (3), by the inclusion of the phrase "subject
  to satisfactory test flight".

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} No person shall sign a maintenance release in respect
  of specialized maintenance unless the requirements of section 571.04
  have been met.
