#### [Persons Who May Sign a Maintenance Release]{.HTitleText3} {#h-993018 .Subheading}

- **[[571.11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-571.11
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except as provided in
  subsections (2) and (7), no person other than the holder of an
  aircraft maintenance engineer (AME) licence issued under Part IV,
  specifying a rating appropriate to the aeronautical product being
  maintained, shall sign a maintenance release as required by section
  571.10.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person other than a person described in
  subsection (1) may sign a maintenance release if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of maintenance performed outside
    Canada,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the person is authorized to sign under the laws
      of a state that is party to an agreement or a technical
      arrangement with Canada and the agreement or technical arrangement
      provides for such certification, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if no agreement or technical arrangement
      provides for such certification, the person holds qualifications
      that the Minister determines to be equivalent to those of a person
      described in subsection (1);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of maintenance performed on an aircraft
    that is operated under a special certificate of airworthiness in the
    amateur-built classification, the person is an owner of the
    aircraft;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of maintenance performed on a part that
    is intended for installation on an aircraft, the person has been
    authorized to sign by the holder of an approved maintenance
    organization (AMO) certificate issued under section 573.02; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of maintenance performed on an aircraft
    that is operated under a special certificate of airworthiness in the
    owner-maintenance classification, the person is a licensed pilot and
    an owner of the aircraft.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Except as provided in subsection (7), no person shall
  sign a maintenance release in respect of maintenance performed on an
  aircraft operated under Part IV or VII, or on parts intended to be
  installed on the aircraft, unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person is authorized to sign in accordance with
    a maintenance policy manual (MPM) established by the holder of an
    AMO certificate issued under section 573.02 with a rating of a
    category appropriate to the work performed; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the maintenance is performed outside Canada, the
    person is authorized to sign in accordance with a foreign document
    equivalent to an MPM, established by a maintenance organization
    approved under the laws of a state that is party to an agreement or
    technical arrangement with Canada and the agreement or technical
    arrangement provides for such certification.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Except as provided in subsections (5) and (7), no
  person shall sign a maintenance release in respect of maintenance
  performed on a transport category aeroplane or a turbine-powered
  helicopter, unless the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} has successfully completed a course of maintenance
    training that has been approved by the Minister and that is
    applicable to the type of aircraft, engine or system on which the
    maintenance is performed, in accordance with Appendix M of Standard
    571 --- Maintenance; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} held a type rating applicable to the type of
    aircraft, engine or system on which the maintenance is performed,
    issued by the Minister before August 1, 1999.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The holder of an applicable AME licence may sign a
  maintenance release in respect of maintenance performed on a transport
  category aeroplane or a turbine-powered helicopter that consists of
  any of the types of work set out in Schedule III without having
  successfully completed the course required by paragraph (4)(a) and
  without having held the type rating required by paragraph (4)(b).

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} If a maintenance release is signed by a person in
  respect of work performed by another person, the person signing the
  maintenance release must personally observe the work to the extent
  necessary to ensure that it is performed in accordance with the
  requirements of any applicable standards of airworthiness and,
  specifically, the requirements of sections 571.02 and 571.10.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} A person who is not the holder of an AME licence
  specifying a rating appropriate to the aeronautical product being
  maintained may sign a maintenance release if the person holds a
  restricted certification authority issued in accordance with
  subsection (8), in respect of a particular case specified on the
  restricted certification authority.

- [(8)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall issue a restricted certification
  authority and specify therein its validity period and the scope of the
  work that may be performed, if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an application is made in accordance with section
    571.11 of the Airworthiness Manual;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the applicant demonstrates to the Minister that
    there is no holder of an AME licence specifying a rating appropriate
    to the aeronautical product being maintained available within a
    geographical area accessible within one hour by surface
    transportation;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the person to whom the restricted certification
    authority is to be issued has received the training and has the
    knowledge equivalent to that of a holder of an AME licence
    specifying a rating appropriate to the aeronautical product being
    maintained; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the level of aviation safety is not affected by the
    issuance of the restricted certification authority.

#### [Reporting Major Repairs and Major Modifications]{.HTitleText3} {#h-993044 .Subheading}

**[[571.12]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-571.12 .sectionLabel}** A person who
performs a major repair or major modification on an aeronautical product
or installs on an aircraft a part that has undergone a major repair or
major modification shall report the action to the Minister in accordance
with the procedures specified in section 571.12 of the Airworthiness
Manual.

#### [Installation of Parts (General)]{.HTitleText3} {#h-993046 .Subheading}

- **[[571.13]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-571.13
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to sections 571.07 to
  571.09, no person shall install a part on an aeronautical product
  unless the part is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} inspected and its accompanying documentation
    verified in accordance with a procedure that ensures that the part
    conforms to its type design, as is indicated by the maintenance
    release; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} installed in accordance with the requirements of
    section 571.13 of the Airworthiness Manual.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a part is obtained from an aeronautical product
  that was damaged or permanently withdrawn from service, the part shall
  not be installed unless it

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} can be traced to the manufacturer certificate
    holder; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is inspected in conformity with the instructions
    for continued airworthiness or, if the part has been repaired or
    modified, it can be ascertained that the work was performed in
    accordance with approved data within the meaning of section 571.06
    of the Airworthiness Manual.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-112, s. 12
:::

## [SCHEDULE II]{.scheduleLabel}[(Section 571.04)]{.OriginatingRef}[Specialized Maintenance]{.scheduleTitleText}  {#h-993067 .scheduleLabel}
:::

The following tasks constitute the specialized maintenance referred to
in section 571.04 of these Regulations.

#### [Airframe]{.HTitleText2} {#airframe .SchedHeadL2}

- 1
  - [(1)]{.lawlabel} The modification, repair or replacement by
    riveting, bonding or laminating, or the making of any of the
    following airframe parts is structural specialized maintenance:

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a box beam;

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a wing stringer or chord member;

    - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a spar;

    - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a spar flange;

    - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a member of a truss-type beam;

    - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the web of a beam;

    - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a keel or chine member of a flying boat hull or a
      float;

    - [(h)]{.lawlabel} a corrugated sheet compression member in a wing
      or tail surface;

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a wing main rib;

    - [(j)]{.lawlabel} a wing or tail surface brace strut;

    - [(k)]{.lawlabel} an engine mount;

    - [(l)]{.lawlabel} a fuselage longeron or frame;

    - [(m)]{.lawlabel} a member of a side truss, horizontal truss or
      bulkhead;

    - [(n)]{.lawlabel} a seat support brace or bracket, excluding the
      replacement of seat rails;

    - [(o)]{.lawlabel} a seat rail replacement for transport category
      aircraft;

    - [(p)]{.lawlabel} a landing gear strut or brace strut;

    - [(q)]{.lawlabel} an axle;

    - [(r)]{.lawlabel} a wheel; and

    - [(s)]{.lawlabel} a ski or ski pedestal, excluding the replacement
      of a low-friction coating.

  - [(2)]{.lawlabel} The modification or repair of any of the following
    parts of an airframe is structural specialized maintenance:

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} aircraft skin, or the skin of an aircraft float,
      if the work requires the use of a support, jig or fixture;

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} aircraft skin that is subject to pressurization
      loads, if the damage to the skin measures more than 15 cm (6
      inches) in any direction;

    - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a load-bearing part of a control system,
      including a control column, pedal, shaft, quadrant, bellcrank,
      torque tube, control horn and forged or cast bracket, but
      excluding

      - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the swaging of a repair splice or cable
        fitting, and

      - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the replacement of a push-pull tube end
        fitting that is attached by riveting; and

    - [(d)]{.lawlabel} any other structure that a manufacturer has
      identified as a primary structure in its maintenance manual,
      structural repair manual or any instructions for continuing
      airworthiness.

#### [Engine]{.HTitleText2} {#engine .SchedHeadL2}

- [2]{.lawlabel} Any of the following types of tasks is engine
  specialized maintenance:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the reassembly of a multi-part engine crankshaft or
    a crankshaft equipped with a dynamic counterweight system;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the reassembly of the crankcase of a reciprocating
    engine that is equipped with an integral supercharger or a propeller
    reduction gear;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the overhaul of a reciprocating engine that is
    equipped with an integral or turbo supercharger; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the overhaul of a turbine engine or turbine engine
    module.

#### [Propeller]{.HTitleText2} {#propeller .SchedHeadL2}

- [3]{.lawlabel} Any of the following types of propeller repair, if the
  work is beyond the limits recommended in the manufacturer's
  maintenance manual or service instructions for service in the field is
  propeller specialized maintenance:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the re-contouring, twisting, shortening or
    straightening of a propeller blade or the blending of damage
    thereto;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the repair or machining of a propeller hub,
    excluding the removal of surface corrosion or application of a
    protective coating;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the reinstallation of a metal leading edge sheath
    or tip of a wooden blade;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the replacement of the outer protective coating on
    a wooden blade, excluding the restoration of varnish;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the repair of an elongated propeller attachment or
    propeller blade attachment bolt hole;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the inlaying of a repair patch on a wooden blade;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the repair of a composite blade; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} an overhaul or repair involving the reassembly of a
    controllable-pitch propeller, excluding the reassembly of a
    propeller that has been disassembled for shipping purposes, or the
    replacement of seals.

#### [Avionics]{.HTitleText2} {#avionics .SchedHeadL2}

- 4
  - [(1)]{.lawlabel} The repair of avionics components and systems is
    avionics specialized maintenance, except for:

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} repairs of wiring and connectors;

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} replacement of connectors and electrical
      components with identical or equivalent items;

    - [(c)]{.lawlabel} replacement of antennas with identical or
      equivalent items;

    - [(d)]{.lawlabel} replacement of integral fuses and lighting
      components when the line replaceable unit (LRU) is designed for
      flight-line replacement of these components;

    - [(e)]{.lawlabel} replacement of an avionics LRU provided that any
      testing required can be done using standard test equipment,
      built-in test equipment (BITE) or equipment specified in the
      aircraft manufacturer's instructions for continuing airworthiness;

    - [(f)]{.lawlabel} on-site maintenance of passenger entertainment
      systems performed in accordance with the applicable instructions
      in the maintenance manual of the aircraft or systems manufacturer
      or the manufacturer's instructions for continuing airworthiness;
      and

    - [(g)]{.lawlabel} routine maintenance that is described in the
      aircraft manufacturer's maintenance manual or instructions for
      continuing airworthiness or performed in accordance with currently
      recognized industry practices for service in the field.

  - [(2)]{.lawlabel} Any avionics system installation or modification is
    avionics specialized maintenance except for:

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} installation of ELT systems conforming to the
      CAN-TSO as set out in section 551.104 of Chapter 551 --- Aircraft
      Equipment and Installation of the Airworthiness Manual, if the ELT
      systems are not interfaced with any other systems;

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} installation of single VHF communication or
      single integrated navigation/communication systems that are not
      interfaced with any other system, other than an intercom system;

    - [(c)]{.lawlabel} installation of VFR long-range navigation systems
      which are not interfaced with any other systems;

    - [(d)]{.lawlabel} modifications to existing avionics installations,
      where no additional test requirements are imposed on the affected
      system other than those which would be required following routine
      maintenance of that system;

    - [(e)]{.lawlabel} installation of instruments which are not
      interfaced with any other systems; and

    - [(f)]{.lawlabel} replacement of an avionics LRU where equivalency
      is maintained, and where no additional test requirements are
      imposed on the affected system other than those which would be
      required following routine maintenance of that system.

#### [Instrument]{.HTitleText2} {#instrument .SchedHeadL2}

- [5]{.lawlabel} Maintenance of instruments, other than display devices
  whose operation is integrated with an appliance to which another
  category of specialized maintenance applies, if the work is beyond the
  limits recommended in the manufacturer's maintenance manual or service
  instructions for service in the field, is instrument specialized
  maintenance.

#### [Component]{.HTitleText2} {#component .SchedHeadL2}

- [6]{.lawlabel} Any of the following types of maintenance of an
  appliance or component, where the work is beyond the limits
  recommended in the manufacturer's maintenance manual or service
  instructions for service in the field, is component specialized
  maintenance:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the reassembling of valves that are activated
    electrically or through the use of controlled fluid pressure;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the calibrating or flow checking of any fuel
    metering or air metering component, other than a float-type
    carburettor;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the overhaul of any pressure-type fuel, oil,
    pneumatic or hydraulic pump;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a repair involving the disassembly of
    speed-regulating devices, including an engine or propeller governor
    or a constant-speed drive;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the overhaul of a rotor head, transmission or any
    mechanism used to transmit power to the rotors of a tilt-wing
    aircraft or helicopter;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the repair of a helicopter rotor blade;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the rewinding of the field coil or armature of an
    electrical accessory;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the overhaul of an aircraft magneto; and

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the patch repair of a bladder-type fuel tank.

#### [Welding]{.HTitleText2} {#welding .SchedHeadL2}

- [7]{.lawlabel} The welding of the following parts is welding
  specialized maintenance:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any part of the primary structure, including a
    wheel, an axle and a passenger restraint or cargo restraint system;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any part of an aircraft system, including a fuel
    tank, an oil tank and a pneumatic or hydraulic container; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any structural or dynamic engine part.

#### [Non-destructive Testing (NDT)]{.HTitleText2} {#non-destructive-testing-ndt .SchedHeadL2}

- [8]{.lawlabel} Any required inspection of an aeronautical product that
  uses liquid penetrant, magnetic particle, radiographic, ultrasonic or
  eddy current methods, unless the inspection is performed under
  Appendix K to Standard 571 --- Maintenance, is Non-Destructive Testing
  (NDT) Specialized Maintenance.

### [Subpart 73 --- Approved Maintenance Organizations]{.HTitleText2} {#h-993181 .Subheading}

#### [Division I --- General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-993182 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2005-173, s. 14

\]
:::

##### [Application for Approval]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993185 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2005-173, s. 29

\]
:::

- **[[573.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-573.01
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for an approved
  maintenance organization (AMO) certificate or for an amendment of an
  AMO certificate that is in effect shall make an application in the
  form and manner specified in Standard 573 ---Approved Maintenance
  Organizations.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An applicant referred to in subsection (1) shall
  submit to the Minister with the application a copy of its maintenance
  policy manual (MPM) required pursuant to subsection 573.10(1).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-173, s. 28
:::

##### [Entitlement to and Scope of Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993193 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2005-173, s. 29

\]
:::

- **[[573.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-573.02
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall issue to a
  maintenance organization that demonstrates that it meets the
  requirements of this Subpart an approved maintenance organization
  (AMO) certificate authorizing the maintenance of specified
  aeronautical products or the provision of specified maintenance
  services.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The AMO certificate shall specify, in accordance with
  the criteria specified in section 573.02 of Standard 573 --- Approved
  Maintenance Organizations, any category in which ratings have been
  issued and shall list the aeronautical products that the AMO is
  authorized to maintain or the maintenance services that the AMO is
  authorized to perform.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The scope of the work that may be performed under
  each rating specified on the AMO certificate is determined by
  limitations that are set out in the certificate.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Unless an expiry date is specified in an AMO
  certificate issued pursuant to subsection (1), the certificate remains
  in effect until it is surrendered, suspended or cancelled.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-173, s. 15
:::

##### [Duties of Certificate Holder]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993203 .Subheading}

- **[[573.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-573.03
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The holder of an approved
  maintenance organization (AMO) certificate shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} appoint a person responsible for maintenance;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the person responsible for maintenance
    meets the requirement set out in subsection 573.04(1);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsection (4), ensure that the person
    responsible for maintenance

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} has achieved a grade of 70% or more in an
      open-book examination that demonstrates knowledge of the
      provisions of the [Canadian Aviation
      Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-96-433), and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} meets the experience requirement set out in
      subsection 573.04(1) of Standard 573 --- Approved Maintenance
      Organizations;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2022-246, s. 13\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the person responsible for maintenance
    performs the duties referred to in subsections 573.04(3) and
    573.09(2) and (3);

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} provide the person responsible for maintenance with
    the financial and human resources necessary to ensure that the
    holder of the AMO certificate meets the requirements of these
    Regulations;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} ensure that corrective actions are taken in respect
    of any findings resulting from a quality assurance program
    established under subsection 573.09(1) or a safety management system
    referred to in section 573.30; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} conduct reviews of the safety management system to
    determine its effectiveness.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2022-246, s. 13\]]{.Repealed}

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2022-246, s. 13\]]{.Repealed}

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The knowledge requirement set out in subparagraph
  (1)(c)(i) does not apply in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a person responsible for maintenance who held that
    position on January 1, 1997; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the holder of an aircraft maintenance engineer
    (AME) licence.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The experience requirement set out in subsection
  573.04(1) of Standard 573 --- Approved Maintenance Organizations does
  not apply in the case of an AMO certificate in respect of which no
  rating in the aircraft, avionics, instrument, engine or propeller
  category has been issued if the accountable executive can demonstrate
  to the Minister by means of a risk assessment that the lesser
  experience is appropriate to the scope of work performed by the AMO
  and will not affect aviation safety or the safety of the public.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} The holder of an AMO certificate shall ensure that no
  person is appointed to be responsible for maintenance or remains
  responsible for maintenance if, at the time of their appointment or
  during their tenure, they have a record of conviction for

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an offence under section 7.3 of the Act; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} two or more offences under any of sections 571.10
    and 571.11 not arising from a single occurrence.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} The holder of a certificate referred to in
  subsection (1) shall ensure that the person managing the safety
  management system who is referred to in section 573.32 performs the
  duties set out in that section.

##### [Person Responsible for Maintenance]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993228 .Subheading}

- **[[573.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-573.04
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The person responsible for
  maintenance shall, within 30 days after their appointment under
  paragraph 573.03(1)(a), submit to the Minister a signed statement that
  they accept the responsibilities of their position.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2019-295, s. 12\]]{.Repealed}

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The person responsible for maintenance shall, where a
  finding resulting from a quality assurance program established under
  subsection 573.09(1) or a safety management system referred to in
  section 573.30 is reported to them,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} determine what, if any, corrective actions are
    required and carry out those actions;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} keep a record of any determination made under
    paragraph (a) and the reason for it;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if management functions have been assigned to
    another person under subsection (4) or (5), communicate any
    determination regarding a corrective action to that person; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} notify the accountable executive of any systemic
    deficiency and of the corrective action taken.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The person responsible for maintenance may assign the
  management functions for the entire quality assurance program
  established under subsection 573.09(1) or for the safety management
  system referred to in 573.30 to another person if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} that person meets the requirements set out in
    paragraph 573.03(1)(c) and subsection 573.03(6); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the assignment and its scope are described in the
    AMO's MPM.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The person responsible for maintenance may assign the
  management functions for specific maintenance activities to another
  person if the assignment and its scope are described in the AMO's MPM.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} The responsibility of the person responsible for
  maintenance is not affected by the assignment to another person of
  management functions under subsection (4) or (5).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-173, s. 16
- [SOR/2019-295, s. 12](#1194397-1195547){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1194397-1195547.html"}
- [SOR/2022-246, s. 14](#1380142-1380773){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1380142-1380773.html"}
:::

##### [Authorization to Sign a Maintenance Release]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993244 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2005-173, s. 29

\]
:::

- **[[573.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-573.05
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No approved maintenance organization
  (AMO) certificate holder shall authorize a person to sign a
  maintenance release unless the person meets the applicable
  requirements of section 571.11 and has successfully completed the
  training required by section 573.06.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No AMO certificate holder shall authorize a person to
  sign a maintenance release under paragraph 571.11(2)(c) unless the
  person has, in respect of the work being certified, demonstrated to
  the certificate holder levels of knowledge and experience that are
  appropriate and that meet the applicable criteria set out in section
  573.05 of Standard 573 --- Approved Maintenance Organizations.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-173, s. 17
:::

##### [Training Program]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993252 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2005-173, s. 29

\]
:::

- **[[573.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-573.06
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An approved maintenance organization
  (AMO) certificate holder shall implement a training program to ensure
  that persons authorized to perform or supervise the performance of any
  function under this Subpart are trained in respect of the regulations,
  the standards and the AMO procedures applicable to that function.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The program required by subsection (1) shall include
  initial training, updating and any other training necessary, within
  the meaning assigned to those terms in section 573.06 of Standard 573
  --- Approved Maintenance Organizations, to ensure continued
  qualification that is appropriate to the function to be performed or
  supervised.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-173, s. 18
:::

##### [Personnel Records]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993260 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2005-173, s. 29

\]
:::

- **[[573.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-573.07
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An approved maintenance organization
  (AMO) certificate holder shall establish, maintain and retain for at
  least two years after an entry is made, for each affected person, a
  record of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} all personal qualifications in respect of
    appointments made pursuant to section 573.03 and in respect of
    assignments of functions made pursuant to section 573.04;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} all of the authorizations to sign a maintenance
    release pursuant to section 573.05; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} all of the training conducted pursuant to section
    573.06.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An AMO certificate holder shall provide a copy of a
  record required by this section to the person to whom the record
  refers on the completion of each training activity or the granting of
  an authorization referred to in paragraph (1)(b).

##### [Facilities, Equipment, Standards and Procedures]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993269 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2005-173, s. 29

\]
:::

- **[[573.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-573.08
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An approved maintenance organization
  (AMO) certificate holder shall provide the facilities and equipment
  specified in Standard 573 ---Approved Maintenance Organizations that
  are necessary for the work to be performed.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Except in cases provided for in a maintenance policy
  manual (MPM), work performed by an AMO certificate holder shall be
  performed in the facilities required by subsection (1), unless
  unforeseen circumstances do not permit the work to be performed in
  those facilities and the safety of the aircraft is not affected by the
  fact that the work is performed elsewhere.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where an AMO uses standards equivalent to those of
  the manufacturer of an aeronautical product for the performance of
  work pursuant to paragraph 571.02(1)(b), those standards shall be
  identified in accordance with section 573.10.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where a task undertaken by an AMO is divided into
  sub-tasks, the person appointed pursuant to section 573.03 shall
  establish a system of task control to ensure that all of the sub-tasks
  are completed prior to the signing of a maintenance release in respect
  of the completion of that task.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-173, s. 28
:::

##### [Quality Assurance Program]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993279 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2005-173, s. 29

\]
:::

- **[[573.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-573.09
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The holder of an approved
  maintenance organization (AMO) certificate shall establish and
  maintain a quality assurance program consisting of provisions for
  sampling maintenance processes to evaluate the AMO's ability to
  perform its maintenance in a safe manner.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The person responsible for maintenance shall ensure
  that records relating to the findings resulting from the quality
  assurance program are distributed to the appropriate manager for
  corrective action and follow-up in accordance with the policies and
  procedures specified in the maintenance policy manual (MPM).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The person responsible for maintenance shall
  establish an audit system in respect of the quality assurance program
  that consists of the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an initial audit within 12 months after the date on
    which the AMO certificate is issued;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} subsequent audits conducted at intervals set out in
    the MPM;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} checklists of all activities controlled by the MPM;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a record of each occurrence of compliance or
    non-compliance with the MPM found during an audit referred to in
    paragraph (a) or (b);

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} procedures for ensuring that each finding of an
    audit is communicated to them and, if management functions have been
    assigned to another person under subsection 573.04(4) or (5), to
    that person;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} follow-up procedures for ensuring that corrective
    actions are effective; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a system for recording the findings of initial and
    periodic audits, corrective actions and follow-ups.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The records required under paragraph (3)(g) shall be
  retained for the greater of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} two audit cycles; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} two years.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The duties related to the quality assurance program
  that involve specific tasks or activities within an AMO's activities
  shall be fulfilled by persons who are not responsible for carrying out
  those tasks or activities.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-173, s. 19
:::

##### [Maintenance Policy Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993299 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2005-173, s. 29

\]
:::

- **[[573.10]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-573.10
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An approved maintenance organization
  (AMO) certificate holder shall establish, maintain and authorize the
  use of a maintenance policy manual (MPM) that contains information to
  ensure the efficiency of the AMO's maintenance policies, dealing with
  the subjects set out in Standard 573 ---Approved Maintenance
  Organizations.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may authorize the incorporation by
  reference in an MPM of detailed procedures manuals and lists prepared
  by the AMO certificate holder, dealing with the subjects set out in
  Standard 573 ---Approved Maintenance Organizations, where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the policy affecting those detailed procedures and
    the composition of the lists is set out in the MPM;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} each incorporation is clearly indicated in the MPM;
    and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the AMO certificate holder ensures that the
    incorporated procedures manuals and lists meet the requirements of
    this section.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where detailed procedures manuals or lists are being
  incorporated by reference in an MPM, the person appointed pursuant to
  section 573.03 or another person to whom that management function is
  assigned pursuant to section 573.04 shall certify in writing that the
  incorporated documents and every amendment thereto meet the
  requirements of the policy established in the MPM with respect to
  those documents.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An AMO certificate holder need not conform to the
  policy and procedures contained in its MPM, where the Minister has
  authorized the non-conformity in writing, after it has been
  demonstrated that such non-conformity would not affect the safety of
  the aeronautical product to be maintained or the maintenance service
  to be offered.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} An AMO certificate holder shall submit each page of
  its MPM to the Minister for approval, either individually or in
  accordance with a procedure that ensures compliance with the
  requirements of Standard 573 ---Approved Maintenance Organizations.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} An AMO certificate holder shall amend its MPM when
  instructed to do so by the Minister, where the MPM does not

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} meet the requirements of this Subpart; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} contain policies or procedures that are
    sufficiently detailed to demonstrate that the AMO's quality
    assurance program meets the requirements of these Regulations.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} An AMO certificate holder shall take steps to ensure
  that a current copy of its MPM, or the portions thereof that are
  relevant to the task to be performed, is made available to each person
  who performs or certifies that task.

- [(8)]{.lawlabel} An AMO certificate holder shall amend each copy of
  its MPM within 30 days after receiving an approval issued pursuant to
  subsection (5).

- [(9)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall, if the standards set out in
  Standard 573 ---Approved Maintenance Organizations are met, approve an
  MPM and any amendments to that manual.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2000-404, s. 12
- SOR/2005-173, s. 28
:::

##### [Maintenance Arrangements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993319 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2005-173, s. 29

\]
:::

- **[[573.11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-573.11
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except as provided in subsection
  (2), no approved maintenance organization (AMO) certificate holder
  shall permit an external agent to perform maintenance on its behalf
  unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the external agent holds an AMO certificate with a
    rating of a category specified pursuant to section 573.02 that is
    appropriate to the type of work to be performed or the aeronautical
    product to be maintained;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the work is to be performed outside Canada,
    the external agent has been authorized to do the type of work to be
    performed or to perform maintenance on the type of aeronautical
    product to be maintained under the laws of a state that is party to
    an agreement with Canada and the agreement provides for the
    recognition of maintenance functions; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in all other cases, the performance of the
    maintenance by the person or organization has been approved by the
    Minister as being in conformity with these Regulations.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), an AMO certificate holder
  may permit work to be performed by an external agent other than an
  agent described in subsection (1) where the work is performed in
  accordance with an arrangement that provides for it, under the direct
  supervision of the person appointed pursuant to section 573.03 or
  573.04 and certified by persons authorized to do so in accordance with
  the approved procedures set out in the AMO's maintenance policy manual
  (MPM).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Arrangements respecting work to be performed by
  external agents pursuant to subsection (2) shall be made in accordance
  with procedures governing maintenance arrangements set out in the MPM
  or, if no such procedures are set out in the MPM, shall be approved by
  the Minister as ensuring conformity with the requirements of this
  Subpart.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An AMO certificate holder that requests an external
  agent to perform work shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where the work is to be performed pursuant to
    subsection (1) or (2), be responsible for specifying the tasks to be
    performed by the agent and ensuring completion of the work; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the work is to be performed pursuant to
    subsection (2), be responsible for ensuring the conformity of that
    work with the requirements of Subpart 71.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} A maintenance arrangement that is made by a foreign
  air operator to have its maintenance done in Canada by a person or
  organization that holds an AMO certificate issued pursuant to section
  573.02 shall be authorized by a maintenance specification issued to
  the AMO in accordance with the requirements of Standard 573 ---
  Approved Maintenance Organizations, where the air operator is from a
  state that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is party to an agreement with Canada that provides
    for recognition of the work performed and the issuance of a
    maintenance specification is specified in the agreement; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is not party to an agreement with Canada that
    provides for recognition of the work performed and the issuance of a
    maintenance specification is requested by that state.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-173, s.28
:::

##### [Service Difficulty Reporting]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993337 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote

- SOR/2005-173, s. 29

\]
:::

**[[573.12]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-573.12 .sectionLabel}** The holder of an
approved maintenance organization (AMO) certificate shall report to the
Minister, in accordance with Division IX of Subpart 21 of Part V, any
reportable service difficulty related to an aeronautical product being
maintained.

::: HistoricalNote

##### [Foreign Approvals]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993343 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2005-173, s. 29

\]
:::

**[[573.13]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-573.13 .sectionLabel}** An application
submitted by a maintenance organization for the issuance or amendment of
an approved maintenance organization (AMO) certificate authorizing the
performance of work in facilities located outside Canada is granted if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the applicant has demonstrated that the issuance of
  the approval in respect of those facilities is in the public interest
  as provided for in subsection 6.71(1) of the Act;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the applicant has recognized by advance agreement the
  Minister's right to enter and inspect those facilities and seize
  anything found in those facilities, under the same conditions as would
  govern the exercise of the Minister's powers pursuant to subsection
  8.7(1) of the Act if the facilities were located in Canada;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the AMO has agreed to reimburse the Minister for any
  expenses incurred by Department of Transport personnel in carrying out
  the activities provided for in paragraph (b) in respect of those
  facilities; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an AMO whose facilities are located
  outside Canada, the Minister specifies on the AMO certificate the date
  on which the certificate expires.

##### [Identification of an AMO]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993351 .Subheading}

- **[[573.14]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-573.14
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person, other than the holder of
  an approved maintenance organization (AMO) certificate issued in
  accordance with this Subpart, shall identify oneself as an AMO
  certificate holder.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who holds an AMO certificate issued in
  accordance with this Subpart shall not include, in a list of approved
  maintenance services offered for aeronautical products, a service that
  is outside the scope of the person's AMO certificate.

##### [Technical Records]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993355 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2005-173, s. 29

\]
:::

**[[573.15]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-573.15 .sectionLabel}** An approved
maintenance organization (AMO) certificate holder shall maintain records
in accordance with section 573.15 of Standard 573 --- Approved
Maintenance Organizations for work performed on all aeronautical
products maintained and keep those records for at least two years
beginning on the date that the maintenance release was signed.

#### [Division II --- Safety Management System]{.HTitleText3} {#h-993362 .Subheading}

##### [Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993363 .Subheading}

**[[573.30]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-573.30 .sectionLabel}** The safety
management system required under section 107.02 in respect of an
applicant for, or a holder of, an approved maintenance organization
(AMO) certificate authorizing the holder to perform maintenance on an
aircraft operated under Subpart 5 of Part VII shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} meet the requirements of Subpart 7 of Part I and
  section 573.31; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} be under the control of the person responsible for
  maintenance appointed under paragraph 573.03(1)(a).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-173, s. 20
:::

##### [Components of the Safety Management System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993369 .Subheading}

- **[[573.31]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-573.31
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The safety management system shall
  include, among others, the following components:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a safety management plan that includes

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a safety policy that the accountable executive
      has approved and communicated to all employees,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the roles and responsibilities of personnel
      assigned duties under the quality assurance program established
      under subsection 573.09(1) or the safety management system,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} performance goals and a means of measuring
      attainment of those goals,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a policy for the internal reporting of a hazard,
      an incident or an accident, including the conditions under which
      immunity from disciplinary action will be granted, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} a review of the safety management system to
      determine its effectiveness;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} procedures for reporting a hazard, an incident or
    an accident to the appropriate manager;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} procedures for the collection of data relating to
    hazards, incidents and accidents;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} procedures for analysing data obtained under
    paragraph (c) and during an audit conducted under subsection
    573.09(3) and for taking corrective actions;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} an audit system referred to in subsection
    573.09(3);

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} training requirements for the person responsible
    for maintenance and for personnel assigned duties under the safety
    management system; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} procedures for making progress reports to the
    accountable executive at intervals determined by the accountable
    executive and other reports as needed in urgent cases.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The components specified in subsection (1) shall be
  set out in the approved maintenance organization (AMO) certificate
  holder's maintenance policy manual (MPM).

  ::: HistoricalNote
  - SOR/2005-173, s. 20
  :::

##### [Person Managing the Safety Management System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993387 .Subheading}

**[[573.32]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-573.32 .sectionLabel}** The person
managing the safety management system in respect of an approved
maintenance organization (AMO) shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} establish and maintain a reporting system to ensure
  the timely collection of information related to hazards, incidents and
  accidents that may adversely affect safety;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} identify hazards and carry out risk management
  analyses of those hazards;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} investigate, analyze and identify the cause or
  probable cause of all hazards, incidents and accidents identified
  under the safety management system;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} establish and maintain a safety data system, by
  either electronic or other means, to monitor and analyze trends in
  hazards, incidents and accidents;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} monitor and evaluate the results of corrective
  actions with respect to hazards, incidents and accidents;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} monitor the concerns of the civil aviation industry
  in respect of safety and their perceived effect on the AMO;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} determine the adequacy of the training required by
  paragraph 573.31(1)(f); and

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} where the person responsible for maintenance has
  assigned the management functions for the safety management system
  under subsection 573.04(4) to another person, report to the person
  responsible for maintenance the hazards, incidents and accidents
  identified under the safety management system required under section
  573.30 or as a result of an audit required under paragraph
  573.31(1)(e).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-173, s. 20
:::

## [Part VI --- General Operating and Flight Rules]{.HTitleText1} {#h-993404 .Part}

### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText2} {#h-993405 .Subheading}

**[[600.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-600.01 .sectionLabel}** In this Part,

[[ADIZ]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[ADIZ]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} or [[Air Defence Identification
    Zone]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the airspace that extends upward
    from the surface in those areas of Canada and off the coasts of
    Canada, the boundaries of which are specified in the Designated
    Airspace Handbook; ([ADIZ]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"}ou[zone
    d'identification de défense aérienne]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[aerial application]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[aerial application]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the seeding from an
    aircraft or the spraying or dusting of chemicals from an aircraft,
    or any other operation of a similar nature; ([traitement
    aérien]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[aerial inspection]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[aerial inspection]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the inspection from
    an aircraft of crops, forests, livestock or wildlife, the patrolling
    of pipelines or power lines, a flight inspection or any other
    operation of a similar nature; ([inspection
    aérienne]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[appropriate ATS unit]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[appropriate ATS unit]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} with respect to aircraft operations within a
      control zone or on the movement area of an aerodrome,

      - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the ATC unit identified for the aerodrome in
        the Canada Air Pilot or Canada Flight Supplement, or

      - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if the ATC unit is not in operation or an ATC
        unit is not identified, the FS unit identified in the Canada Air
        Pilot or Canada Flight Supplement as providing air traffic
        services to the aerodrome;

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} with respect to aircraft operations within an MF
      area or on the movement area of an aerodrome, the FS unit
      identified in the Canada Air Pilot or Canada Flight Supplement as
      providing air traffic services to the aerodrome; and

    - [(c)]{.lawlabel} with respect to any other situation, the ATS unit
      identified in an aeronautical publication as providing air traffic
      services in the airspace concerned; ([unité ATS
      compétente]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[AX class]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[AX class]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed, SOR/2006-77, s.
    4\]]{.Repealed}

[[fly-in]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[fly-in]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an activity during which
    aircraft are gathered at an aerodrome before an invited assembly of
    persons, during which no competitive flights between aircraft or
    aerial demonstrations take place; ([rassemblement
    d'aéronefs]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[large aircraft]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[large aircraft]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an aeroplane having a
    maximum permissible take-off weight in excess of 5 700 kg (12,566
    pounds) or a rotorcraft having a maximum permissible take-off weight
    in excess of 2 730 kg (6,018 pounds); ([gros
    aéronef]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[police authority]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[police authority]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the Royal Canadian
    Mounted Police, Ontario Provincial Police, Sûreté du Québec or
    Canadian Coast Guard, or any municipal or regional police force
    established pursuant to provincial legislation. ([corps
    policier]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[visual approach]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[visual approach]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an approach in which
    the pilot-in-command of an IFR aircraft operating in VMC proceeds to
    the destination aerodrome by using visual reference to the surface
    and, as applicable, by maintaining visual separation from, and
    avoiding the wake turbulence of, a preceding aircraft. ([approche
    visuelle]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-77, s. 4
- [SOR/2020-151, s. 7](#1252587-1257159){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1252587-1257159.html"}
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 6](#1522530-1525166){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522530-1525166.html"}
:::

### [Subpart 1 --- Airspace]{.HTitleText2} {#h-993415 .Subheading}

#### [Division I --- Airspace Structure, Classification and Use]{.HTitleText3} {#h-993416 .Subheading}

##### [Airspace Structure]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993417 .Subheading}

- **[[601.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.01
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Controlled airspace consists of the
  following types of airspace:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the Arctic Control Area, Northern Control Area and
    Southern Control Area;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} high level airspace;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} high level airways;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} low level airspace;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} low level airways;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} fixed RNAV routes;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} terminal control areas;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} military terminal control areas;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} control area extensions;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} transition areas;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} control zones;

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} restricted airspace;

  - [(m)]{.lawlabel} advisory airspace;

  - [(n)]{.lawlabel} military operations areas; and

  - [(o)]{.lawlabel} danger areas.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Uncontrolled airspace consists of the following types
  of airspace:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} high level airspace;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} low level airspace;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} high level air routes;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} low level air routes;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} fixed RNAV routes;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} restricted airspace;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} advisory airspace;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} military operations areas; and

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} danger areas.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The horizontal and vertical limits of any type of
  airspace referred to in subsection (1) or (2) are

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a high level air route, a low level
    air route and an uncontrolled fixed RNAV route, those specified on
    an aeronautical chart; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in any other case, those specified in the
    Designated Airspace Handbook.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The geographical location and the horizontal and
  vertical limits of the following items are those specified in the
  Designated Airspace Handbook:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Canadian Domestic Airspace;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Canadian minimum navigation performance
    specifications (CMNPS) airspace;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the CMNPS transition area;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} reduced vertical separation minimum (RVSM)
    airspace;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} required navigation performance capability (RNPC)
    airspace;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} transponder airspace;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the air defence identification zone (ADIZ);

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} flight information regions (FIR);

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} standard pressure regions;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} altimeter setting regions;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} mountainous regions; and

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} any other areas, zones, regions and points.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-77, s. 5
- SOR/2015-160, s. 26
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-601.01-20060630.html "Link to previous version of section 601.01"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Airspace Classification]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993463 .Subheading}

- **[[601.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.02
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The class of any controlled airspace
  of a type referred to in subsection 601.01(1) is one of the following,
  as specified in the Designated Airspace Handbook:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Class A;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Class B;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} Class C;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} Class D;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} Class E;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} Class F Special Use Restricted; or

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} Class F Special Use Advisory.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The class of any uncontrolled airspace of a type
  referred to in subsection 601.01(2) is one of the following, as
  specified in the Designated Airspace Handbook:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Class G;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Class F Special Use Restricted; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} Class F Special Use Advisory.

##### [Transponder Airspace]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993477 .Subheading}

**[[601.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.03 .sectionLabel}** Transponder
airspace consists of

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} all Class A, B and C airspace as specified in the
  Designated Airspace Handbook; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} any Class D or E airspace specified as transponder
  airspace in the Designated Airspace Handbook.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-77, s. 6
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-601.03-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 601.03"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Flight in Class F Special Use Restricted Airspace or Class F Special Use Advisory Airspace]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993483 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2025-70, s. 41

\]
:::

- **[[601.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.04
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The procedures for the operation of
  aircraft in Class F Special Use Restricted airspace and Class F
  Special Use Advisory airspace are those specified in the Designated
  Airspace Handbook.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aircraft in Class F
  Special Use Restricted airspace unless authorized to do so by the
  person specified for that purpose in the Designated Airspace Handbook.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (2), a person
  specified in the Designated Airspace Handbook may authorize the
  operation of an aircraft where activities on the ground or in the
  airspace are not hazardous to aircraft operating in that airspace and
  access by aircraft to that airspace does not jeopardize national
  security interests.

##### [IFR Flight in Class A, B, C, D or E Airspace or Class F Special Use Restricted or Class F Special Use Advisory Controlled Airspace]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993488 .Subheading}

- **[[601.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.05
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an IFR
  aircraft in Class A, B, C, D or E airspace or in Class F Special Use
  Restricted or Class F Special Use Advisory controlled airspace unless
  the aircraft is operated in accordance with an air traffic control
  clearance or an authorization issued by the Minister.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may issue an authorization referred to
  in subsection (1) where the operation of the aircraft is in the public
  interest and is not likely to affect aviation safety.

##### [VFR Flight in Class A Airspace]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993492 .Subheading}

- **[[601.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.06
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate a VFR
  aircraft in Class A airspace unless the aircraft is operated in
  accordance with an authorization issued by the Minister.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may issue an authorization referred to
  in subsection (1) where the operation of the aircraft is in the public
  interest and is not likely to affect aviation safety.

##### [VFR Flight in Class B Airspace]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993496 .Subheading}

- **[[601.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.07
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate a VFR
  aircraft in Class B airspace unless the aircraft is operated in
  accordance with an air traffic control clearance or an authorization
  issued by the Minister.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may issue an authorization referred to
  in subsection (1) where the operation of the aircraft is in the public
  interest and is not likely to affect aviation safety.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of a VFR aircraft operating in
  Class B airspace in accordance with an air traffic control clearance
  shall, when it becomes evident that it will not be possible to operate
  the aircraft in VMC at the altitude or along the route specified in
  the air traffic control clearance,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where the airspace is a control zone, request
    authorization to operate the aircraft in special VFR flight; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in any other case,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} request an amended air traffic control clearance
      that will enable the aircraft to be operated in VMC to the
      destination specified in the flight plan or to an alternate
      aerodrome, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} request an air traffic control clearance to
      operate the aircraft in IFR flight.

##### [VFR Flight in Class C Airspace]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993505 .Subheading}

- **[[601.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.08
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no person
  operating a VFR aircraft shall enter Class C airspace unless the
  person receives a clearance to enter from the appropriate air traffic
  control unit before entering the airspace.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of a VFR aircraft that is not
  equipped with radiocommunication equipment capable of two-way
  communication with the appropriate air traffic control unit may,
  during daylight in VMC, enter Class C airspace if the pilot-in-command
  receives authorization to enter from the appropriate air traffic
  control unit before entering the airspace.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Class C airspace becomes Class E airspace when the
  appropriate air traffic control unit is not in operation.

##### [VFR Flight in Class D Airspace]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993510 .Subheading}

- **[[601.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.09
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no person
  operating a VFR aircraft shall enter Class D airspace unless the
  person establishes two-way radio contact with the appropriate air
  traffic control unit before entering the airspace.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of a VFR aircraft that is not
  equipped with radiocommunication equipment capable of two-way
  communication with the appropriate air traffic control unit may,
  during daylight in VMC, enter Class D airspace if the pilot-in-command
  receives authorization to enter from the appropriate air traffic
  control unit before entering the airspace.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Class D airspace becomes Class E airspace when the
  appropriate air traffic control unit is not in operation.

**\[601.10 to 601.13 reserved\]**

#### [Division II --- Aircraft Operating Restrictions and Hazards to Aviation Safety]{.HTitleText3} {#h-993516 .Subheading}

##### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993517 .Subheading}

**[[601.14]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.14 .sectionLabel}** In this Division,

[[directed bright light source]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[directed bright light source]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means any
    directed light source (coherent or non-coherent), including lasers,
    that may create a hazard to aviation safety or cause damage to an
    aircraft or injury to persons on board the aircraft; ([source
    lumineuse dirigée de forte intensité]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[fire control authority]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[fire control authority]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an official of
    a government forestry service or other fire control agency that is
    responsible for the protection of persons and property against fire;
    ([responsable de la lutte contre l'incendie]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[forest fire area]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[forest fire area]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an area on the
    surface of the earth on which standing timber, grass or any other
    vegetation or buildings are burning. ([zone d'incendie de
    forêt]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-182, s. 1
- [SOR/2020-151, s. 8(F)](#1252589-1257161){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1252589-1257161.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-601.14-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 601.14"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Forest Fire Aircraft Operating Restrictions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993524 .Subheading}

**[[601.15]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.15 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} over a forest fire area, or over any area that is
  located within five nautical miles of a forest fire area, at an
  altitude of less than 3,000 feet AGL; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in any airspace that is described in a NOTAM issued
  pursuant to section 601.16.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-151, s. 9(F)](#1252593-1257163){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1252593-1257163.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-601.15-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 601.15"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Issuance of NOTAM for Forest Fire Aircraft Operating Restrictions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993528 .Subheading}

**[[601.16]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.16 .sectionLabel}** The Minister may
issue a NOTAM that relates to restrictions on the operation of aircraft
in the case of a forest fire and that describes

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the location and dimensions of the forest fire area;
  and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the airspace in which forest fire control operations
  are being conducted.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-151, s. 10(F)](#1252595-1257165){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1252595-1257165.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-601.16-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 601.16"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Exceptions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993532 .Subheading}

- **[[601.17]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.17
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Section 601.15 does not apply to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} persons who are operating an aircraft at the
    request of, or with the authorization of, an appropriate fire
    control authority for the purpose of assisting the fire control
    authority in the conduct of its operations;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} persons who are operating an aircraft with the
    authorization of the Minister issued under subsection (2); or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} Department of Transport personnel who are operating
    an aircraft in the performance of duties related to surveillance and
    the enforcement of aviation legislation.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} On receipt of an application in writing, the Minister
  shall issue a written authorization permitting the applicant to
  operate an aircraft if the Minister is of the opinion that operating
  the aircraft is necessary for the safety of the public or to support
  the operation of an aerodrome that is in or adjacent to the forest
  fire area.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may specify conditions in the
  authorization governing the operation of the aircraft as are necessary
  for its safe and proper operation.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aircraft under the
  authorization unless the authorization is on board and the aircraft is
  operated in accordance with any conditions specified in the
  authorization.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2022-267, s. 20](#1381636-1387857){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1381636-1387857.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-601.17-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 601.17"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Orders Prohibiting or Restricting Aircraft Operation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993536 .Subheading}

**[[601.18]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.18 .sectionLabel}** The Minister may
make orders prohibiting or restricting the operation of aircraft over
such areas as are specified by the Minister, either absolutely or
subject to such exceptions or conditions as may be specified by the
Minister.
