##### [Projection of Directed Bright Light Source at an Aircraft]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993539 .Subheading}

**[[601.20]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.20 .sectionLabel}** Subject to
section 601.21, no person shall project or cause to be projected a
directed bright light source into navigable airspace in such a manner as
to create a hazard to aviation safety or cause damage to an aircraft or
injury to persons on board the aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-182, s. 2
:::

##### [Requirement for Notification]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993543 .Subheading}

- **[[601.21]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.21
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Any person planning to project or
  cause to be projected a directed bright light source into navigable
  airspace shall, before the projection,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} submit a written request to the Minister for an
    authorization to project the directed bright light source into
    navigable airspace; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} obtain a written authorization from the Minister to
    do so.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} On receipt of the request for authorization, the
  Minister shall issue a written authorization if the projection is not
  likely to create a hazard to aviation safety or to cause damage to an
  aircraft or injury to persons on board the aircraft.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may specify in the authorization any
  conditions necessary to ensure that the projection is not likely to
  create a hazard to aviation safety or to cause damage to an aircraft
  or injury to persons on board the aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-182, s. 2
- SOR/2014-286, s. 3
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-601.21-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 601.21"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Requirement for Pilot-in-command]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993552 .Subheading}

- **[[601.22]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.22
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No pilot-in-command shall
  intentionally operate an aircraft into a beam from a directed bright
  light source or into an area where a directed bright light source is
  projected, unless the aircraft is operated in accordance with an
  authorization issued by the Minister.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may issue the authorization if the
  operation of the aircraft is not likely to create a hazard to aviation
  safety.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-182, s. 2
:::

#### [Division III --- Marking and Lighting of Obstacles to Air Navigation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-993558 .Subheading}

##### [Obstacles to Air Navigation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993559 .Subheading}

- **[[601.23]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.23
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Division,
  any building, structure or object, including any addition to it,
  constitutes an obstacle to air navigation if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} it penetrates an airport obstacle limitation
    surface as calculated in accordance with Chapter 4 of the document
    entitled Aerodrome Standards and Recommended Practices, TP 312E,
    published by the Department of Transport;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} it is higher than 90 m AGL and is located within
    6 km of the geographical centre of an aerodrome;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} it is higher than 90 m AGL and is located within
    3.7 km of the centreline of a recognized VFR route, including, but
    not limited to, a valley, a railway track, a transmission line, a
    pipeline, a river and a highway;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} it is higher than 150 m AGL; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} in the case of any catenary wires crossing over a
    river, any portion of the wires or supporting structures is higher
    than 90 m AGL.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), an addition to a
  building, structure or object includes any vertical mast, pole, tower
  or other object erected on top of the building, structure or object
  and adding to its height.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2011-285, s. 6
- [SOR/2021-269, s. 7](#1335319-1336383){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1335319-1336383.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-601.23-20111231.html "Link to previous version of section 601.23"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Marking and Lighting of Obstacles to Air Navigation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993570 .Subheading}

- **[[601.24]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.24
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Any person who plans to construct or
  modify a building, structure or object, or launch a tethered object
  shall notify the Minister of the proposed construction, modification
  or launch in accordance with the requirements of Standard 621 if the
  building, structure or object, or tethered object, will constitute an
  obstacle to air navigation.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who has responsibility for or control over a
  building, structure or object that constitutes an obstacle to air
  navigation shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} mark and light the building, structure or object in
    accordance with the requirements of Standard 621; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} use the equivalent marking and lighting approved by
    the Minister under subsection 601.27(2).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2011-285, s. 6
:::

##### [Other Obstacles to Air Navigation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993578 .Subheading}

- **[[601.25]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.25
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister determines that a
  building, structure or object, other than a building, structure or
  object described in section 601.23, is hazardous to air navigation
  because of its height or location, the Minister shall require the
  person who has responsibility for or control over the building,
  structure or object to mark and light it in accordance with the
  requirements of Standard 621.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who is required by the Minister to mark and
  light a building, structure or object under subsection (1) shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} do so within six months; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} cause to be received at the appropriate air traffic
    services unit a notice identifying the nature, location and height
    of the building, structure or object.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2011-285, s. 6
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 26](#1522575-1525664){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522575-1525664.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-601.25-20111231.html "Link to previous version of section 601.25"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Upgrading of Marking and Lighting]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993586 .Subheading}

**[[601.26]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.26 .sectionLabel}** A person who has
responsibility for or control over an obstacle to air navigation shall
upgrade the markings and lights of the whole obstacle to the most recent
requirements set out in Standard 621 if any change occurs in

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the location of the obstacle with respect to any
  other marked or lighted obstacle; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the surrounding conditions of the obstacle that can
  affect aviation safety.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2011-285, s. 6
:::

##### [Equivalent Marking and Lighting]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993592 .Subheading}

- **[[601.27]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.27
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A person who proposes to use
  equivalent marking and lighting on an obstacle to air navigation for
  which the person has responsibility or over which the person has
  control shall apply to the Minister for approval.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall approve the equivalent marking and
  lighting if the applicant

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} submits a risk assessment that identifies the risks
    to air navigation associated with the obstacle and the methods for
    eliminating or reducing those risks; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} demonstrates that the equivalent marking and
    lighting provides a level of safety at least equivalent to the level
    provided by the requirements of Standard 621.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} In determining whether the equivalent marking and
  lighting provides the level of safety required by paragraph (2)(b),
  the Minister shall consider the following factors:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the location of the obstacle;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the surrounding terrain, buildings, structures and
    objects;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the VFR air traffic volume; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the proximity of the obstacle to an aerodrome.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2011-285, s. 6
:::

##### [Notification of Deterioration, Failure or Malfunction]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993605 .Subheading}

**[[601.28]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.28 .sectionLabel}** A person who has
responsibility for or control over an obstacle to air navigation shall
report immediately any deterioration of a marking or any failure or
malfunction of a light required under this Division to the appropriate
ATS unit.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2011-285, s. 6
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 7](#1522532-1524943){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522532-1524943.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-601.28-20111231.html "Link to previous version of section 601.28"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Prohibition]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993609 .Subheading}

**[[601.29]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-601.29 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
deface, alter or otherwise damage a marking or a light required, under
this Division, to be displayed on an obstacle to air navigation.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2011-285, s. 6
:::

### [Subpart 2 --- Operating and Flight Rules]{.HTitleText2} {#h-993613 .Subheading}

#### [Division I --- General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-993614 .Subheading}

##### [Application --- Remotely Piloted Aircraft]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993615 .Subheading}

**[[602.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.01 .sectionLabel}** This Subpart does
not apply in respect of remotely piloted aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-11, s. 15](#1045403-1138153){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045403-1138153.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-602.01-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 602.01"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Reckless or Negligent Operation of Aircraft]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1138154 .Subheading}

**[[602.01.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.01.1 .sectionLabel}** No person
shall operate an aircraft in such a reckless or negligent manner as to
endanger or be likely to endanger the life or property of any person.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-11, s. 15](#1045403-1138160){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045403-1138160.html"}
:::

##### [Fitness of Flight Crew Members]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993617 .Subheading}

**[[602.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.02 .sectionLabel}** An operator of an
aircraft shall not require any person to act as a flight crew member or
to carry out a preflight duty, and a person shall not act as a flight
crew member or carry out that duty, if the operator or the person has
reason to believe that the person is not, or is not likely to be, fit
for duty.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-269, s. 4
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-602.02-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 602.02"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Alcohol or Drugs --- Crew Members]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993621 .Subheading}

**[[602.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.03 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
act as a crew member of an aircraft

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} within 12 hours after consuming an alcoholic
  beverage;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} while under the influence of alcohol; or

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} while using any drug that impairs the person's
  faculties to the extent that the safety of the aircraft or of persons
  on board the aircraft is endangered in any way.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-269, s. 5
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-602.03-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 602.03"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Alcohol or Drugs --- Passengers]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993628 .Subheading}

- **[[602.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.04
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In this section, [[intoxicating
  liquor]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a beverage that contains more than
  2.5 per cent proof spirits.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall consume on board an aircraft an
  intoxicating liquor unless the intoxicating liquor

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} has been served to that person by the operator of
    the aircraft; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where no flight attendant is on board, has been
    provided by the operator of the aircraft.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No operator of an aircraft shall provide or serve any
  intoxicating liquor to a person on board the aircraft, where there are
  reasonable grounds to believe that the person's faculties are impaired
  by alcohol or a drug to an extent that may present a hazard to the
  aircraft or to persons on board the aircraft.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (5), no operator of an aircraft
  shall allow a person to board the aircraft, where there are reasonable
  grounds to believe that the person's faculties are impaired by alcohol
  or a drug to an extent that may present a hazard to the aircraft or to
  persons on board the aircraft.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The operator of an aircraft may allow a person whose
  faculties are impaired by a drug to board an aircraft, where the drug
  was administered in accordance with a medical authorization and the
  person is under the supervision of an attendant.

##### [Compliance with Instructions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993637 .Subheading}

- **[[602.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.05
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every passenger on board an aircraft
  shall comply with instructions given by any crew member respecting the
  safety of the aircraft or of persons on board the aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Every crew member on board an aircraft shall, during
  flight time, comply with the instructions of the pilot-in-command or
  of any person whom the pilot-in-command has authorized to act on
  behalf of the pilot-in-command.

##### [Prohibition Against Smoking]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993641 .Subheading}

- **[[602.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.06
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall smoke on board an
  aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2025-26, s. 23\]]{.Repealed}

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No person shall tamper with or disable a smoke
  detector installed in an aircraft lavatory without permission from a
  crew member or the operator of the aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-26, s. 23](#1511715-1516250){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1511715-1516250.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-602.06-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 602.06"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Aircraft Operating Limitations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993646 .Subheading}

**[[602.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.07 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft unless it is operated in accordance with the
operating limitations

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} set out in the aircraft flight manual, where an
  aircraft flight manual is required by the applicable standards of
  airworthiness;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} set out in a document other than the aircraft flight
  manual, where use of that document is authorized pursuant to Part VII;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} indicated by markings or placards required pursuant
  to section 605.05; or

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} prescribed by the competent authority of the state of
  registry of the aircraft.

##### [Portable Electronic Devices]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993652 .Subheading}

- **[[602.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.08
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No operator of an aircraft shall
  permit the use of a PED on board an aircraft if the use of the PED
  could adversely affect the operation of the aircraft or the
  functioning of the aircraft's systems or equipment.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall use a portable electronic device on
  board an aircraft except with the permission of the operator of the
  aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-296, s. 6](#1194430-1195818){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1194430-1195818.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-602.08-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 602.08"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Fuelling with Engines Running]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993656 .Subheading}

**[[602.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.09 .sectionLabel}** No person
operating an aircraft shall permit the fuelling of the aircraft while an
engine used for the propulsion of the aircraft is running and passengers
are on board the aircraft or are embarking or disembarking, unless
subsection 604.84(1), 704.33(4) or 705.40(3), as applicable, is complied
with.

##### [Starting and Ground Running of Aircraft Engines]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993660 .Subheading}

- **[[602.10]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.10
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall start an engine of
  an aircraft unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a pilot's seat is occupied by a person who is
    competent to control the aircraft;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} precautions have been taken to prevent the aircraft
    from moving; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a seaplane, the aircraft is in a
    location from which any movement of the aircraft will not endanger
    persons or property.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall leave an engine of an aircraft
  running unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a pilot's seat is occupied by a person who is
    competent to control the aircraft; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where no persons are on board the aircraft,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} precautions have been taken to prevent the
      aircraft from moving, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is not left unattended.

##### [Aircraft Icing]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993671 .Subheading}

- **[[602.11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.11
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In this section, [[critical
  surfaces]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the wings, control surfaces,
  rotors, propellers, horizontal stabilizers, vertical stabilizers or
  any other stabilizing surfaces of an aircraft, as well as any other
  surfaces identified as critical surfaces in the aircraft flight
  manual.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct or attempt to conduct a
  take-off in an aircraft that has frost, ice or snow adhering to any of
  its critical surfaces.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (2), a person may conduct a
  take-off in an aircraft that has frost caused by cold-soaked fuel
  adhering to the underside or upper side, or both, of its wings if the
  take-off is conducted in accordance with the aircraft manufacturer's
  instructions for take-off under those conditions.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where conditions are such that frost, ice or snow may
  reasonably be expected to adhere to the aircraft, no person shall
  conduct or attempt to conduct a take-off in an aircraft unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} for aircraft that are not operated under Subpart 5
    of Part VII,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft has been inspected immediately prior
      to take-off to determine whether any frost, ice or snow is
      adhering to any of its critical surfaces, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the operator has established an aircraft
      inspection program in accordance with the Operating and Flight
      Rules Standards, and the dispatch and take-off of the aircraft are
      in accordance with that program; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} for aircraft that are operated under Subpart 5 of
    Part VII, the operator has established an aircraft inspection
    program in accordance with the Operating and Flight Rules Standards,
    and the dispatch and take-off of the aircraft are in accordance with
    that program.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The inspection referred to in subparagraph (4)(a)(i)
  shall be performed by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a flight crew member of the aircraft who is
    designated by the pilot-in-command; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a person, other than a person referred to in
    paragraph (a) or (b), who

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} is designated by the operator of the aircraft,
      and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} has successfully completed training relating to
      ground and airborne icing operations under Subpart 4 or relating
      to aircraft surface contamination under Part VII.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} Where, before commencing take-off, a crew member of
  an aircraft observes that there is frost, ice or snow adhering to the
  wings of the aircraft, the crew member shall immediately report that
  observation to the pilot-in-command, and the pilot-in-command or a
  flight crew member designated by the pilot-in-command shall inspect
  the wings of the aircraft before take-off.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} Before an aircraft is de-iced or anti-iced, the
  pilot-in-command of the aircraft shall ensure that the crew members
  and passengers are informed of the decision to do so.

::: HistoricalNote

  ajax-after="1274641-1276811.html"}

##### [Overflight of Built-up Areas or Open-air Assemblies of Persons during Take-offs, Approaches and Landings]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993691 .Subheading}

- **[[602.12]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.12
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section and
  sections 602.14 and 602.15, an aircraft shall be deemed to be operated
  over a built-up area or over an open-air assembly of persons if the
  built-up area or open-air assembly of persons is within a horizontal
  distance of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 500 feet from a helicopter or balloon; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 2,000 feet from an aircraft other than a helicopter
    or balloon.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Except at an airport, heliport or military aerodrome,
  no person shall conduct a take-off, approach or landing in an aircraft
  over a built-up area or over an open-air assembly of persons, in a
  manner that is likely to create a hazard to persons or property.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Except at an airport, heliport or military aerodrome,
  no person shall conduct a take-off, approach or landing in an aircraft
  over a built-up area or over an open-air assembly of persons unless
  that aircraft will be operated at an altitude from which, in the event
  of an engine failure or any other emergency necessitating an immediate
  landing, the aircraft can land without creating a hazard to persons or
  property.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-447, s. 1
- SOR/2007-87, s. 9
:::

Version](section-602.12-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 602.12"){.PITLink}

##### [Take-offs, Approaches and Landings within Built-up Areas of Cities and Towns]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993700 .Subheading}

- **[[602.13]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.13
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except if otherwise permitted under
  this section, section 603.66 or Part VII, no person shall conduct a
  take-off, approach or landing in an aircraft within a built-up area of
  a city or town, unless that take-off, approach or landing is conducted
  at an airport, heliport or a military aerodrome.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person may conduct a take-off or landing in an
  aircraft within a built-up area of a city or town at a place that is
  not located at an airport, heliport or a military aerodrome where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the place is not set apart for the operation of
    aircraft;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the flight is conducted without creating a hazard
    to persons or property on the surface; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is operated

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} for the purpose of a police operation that is
      conducted in the service of a police authority, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} for the purpose of saving human life.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A person may conduct a take-off in a balloon within a
  built-up area of a city or town from a place that is not located at an
  airport, heliport or a military aerodrome, where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} permission to use the place as a launch site has
    been obtained from the land owner;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a special aviation event is not being held at that
    place at the time of take-off;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} no written objection in respect of the use of the
    place as a launch site has been received by the Minister from a
    competent land use authority;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the diameter of the launch site is no less than the
    greater of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} 100 feet, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the greatest dimension of the balloon, be it the
      length, width or height, plus 25 per cent; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the take-off point within the launch site is upwind
    of the highest obstacle in the take-off path by a horizontal
    distance equal to the height of that obstacle, and the take-off is
    conducted

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} using a positive rate of climb to a minimum
      altitude of 500 feet above the highest obstacle located within a
      horizontal distance of 500 feet from the balloon, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where the flight path of the balloon is directly
      over residential or commercial buildings or over an open-air
      assembly of persons, using the maximum rate of climb possible,
      considering operational and passenger safety.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} A person may conduct a landing in a balloon within a
  built-up area of a city or town at a place that is not located at an
  airport, heliport or military aerodrome, where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the landing is necessary to avoid endangering the
    safety of the persons on board; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command contacts the appropriate air
    traffic services unit, either prior to landing or as soon as
    possible after landing, and provides

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the balloon's nationality mark and registration
      mark,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the estimated or actual, as applicable, time and
      location of the landing, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the reasons why it is believed that the safety
      of the persons on board is or was endangered.

##### [Minimum Altitudes and Distances]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993727 .Subheading}

- **[[602.14]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.14
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2002-447, s.
  2\]]{.Repealed}

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Except where conducting a take-off, approach or
  landing or where permitted under section 602.15, no person shall
  operate an aircraft

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} over a built-up area or over an open-air assembly
    of persons unless the aircraft is operated at an altitude from
    which, in the event of an emergency necessitating an immediate
    landing, it would be possible to land the aircraft without creating
    a hazard to persons or property on the surface, and, in any case, at
    an altitude that is not lower than

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} for aeroplanes, 1,000 feet above the highest
      obstacle located within a horizontal distance of 2,000 feet from
      the aeroplane,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} for balloons, 500 feet above the highest
      obstacle located within a horizontal distance of 500 feet from the
      balloon, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} for an aircraft other than an aeroplane or a
      balloon, 1,000 feet above the highest obstacle located within a
      horizontal distance of 500 feet from the aircraft; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in circumstances other than those referred to in
    paragraph (a), at a distance less than 500 feet from any person,
    vessel, vehicle or structure.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-447, s. 2
:::

##### [Permissible Low Altitude Flight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993738 .Subheading}

- **[[602.15]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.15
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A person may operate an aircraft at
  altitudes and distances less than those specified in subsection
  602.14(2) where the aircraft is operated at altitudes and distances
  that are no less than necessary for the purposes of the operation in
  which the aircraft is engaged, the aircraft is operated without
  creating a hazard to persons or property on the surface and the
  aircraft is operated

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} for the purpose of a police operation that is
    conducted in the service of a police authority;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} for the purpose of saving human life;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} for fire-fighting or air ambulance operations;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} for the purpose of the administration of the
    [Fisheries Act](/eng/acts/F-14) or the [Coastal Fisheries Protection
    Act](/eng/acts/C-33);

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} for the purpose of the administration of the
    national or provincial parks; or

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} for the purpose of flight inspection.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person may operate an aircraft, to the extent
  necessary for the purpose of the operation in which the aircraft is
  engaged, at altitudes and distances less than those set out in

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 602.14(2)(a), where operation of the
    aircraft is authorized under Subpart 3 or section 702.22; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 602.14(2)(b), where the aircraft is
    operated without creating a hazard to persons or property on the
    surface and the aircraft is operated for the purpose of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} aerial application or aerial inspection,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} aerial photography conducted by the holder of an
      air operator certificate,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} helicopter external load operations, or

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} flight training conducted by or under the
      supervision of a qualified flight instructor.

##### [Flights over Open-Air Assemblies of Persons or Built-up Areas --- Helicopters with External Loads]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993754 .Subheading}

- **[[602.16]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.16
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate a helicopter
  that is carrying a Class B, C or D external load over an open-air
  assembly of persons.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Except where authorized under section 603.66 or
  702.22, no person shall operate a helicopter that is carrying a Class
  B, C or D external load over a built-up area.

##### [Carriage of Persons during Low Altitude Flight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993758 .Subheading}

**[[602.17]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.17 .sectionLabel}** No person
operating an aircraft shall conduct helicopter Class B, C or D external
load operations or engage in aerial application or aerial inspection at
altitudes less than 500 feet AGL while carrying on board any person
other than a flight crew member, unless that person's presence on board
is essential to the purposes of the flight.

##### [Flights over Built-up Areas --- Balloons]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993760 .Subheading}

- **[[602.18]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.18
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate a balloon
  over a built-up area without carrying on board sufficient fuel to
  permit the balloon to fly clear of the built-up area, taking into
  consideration the take-off weight of the balloon, the ambient
  temperature and actual and forecast winds, and possible variations of
  those factors.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate a balloon on a flight that is
  planned to enter Class C airspace while over a built-up area unless
  the clearance to enter that airspace that is required pursuant to
  section 601.08 has been obtained from the appropriate air traffic
  control unit prior to take-off.

##### [Right of Way --- General]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993764 .Subheading}

- **[[602.19]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.19
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite any other provision of this
  section,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command of an aircraft that has the
    right of way shall, if there is any risk of collision, take such
    action as is necessary to avoid collision; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the pilot-in-command of an aircraft is aware
    that another aircraft is in an emergency situation, the
    pilot-in-command shall give way to that other aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} When two aircraft are converging at approximately the
  same altitude, the pilot-in-command of the aircraft that has the other
  on its right shall give way, except as follows:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a power-driven, heavier-than-air aircraft shall
    give way to airships, gliders and balloons;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an airship shall give way to gliders and balloons;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a glider shall give way to balloons; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a power-driven aircraft shall give way to aircraft
    that are seen to be towing gliders or other objects or carrying a
    slung load.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} When two balloons operating at different altitudes
  are converging, the pilot-in-command of the balloon at the higher
  altitude shall give way to the balloon at the lower altitude.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where an aircraft is required to give way to another
  aircraft, the pilot-in-command of the first-mentioned aircraft shall
  not pass over or under, or cross ahead of, the other aircraft unless
  passing or crossing at such a distance as will not create a risk of
  collision.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} Where two aircraft are approaching head-on or
  approximately so and there is a risk of collision, the
  pilot-in-command of each aircraft shall alter its heading to the
  right.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} An aircraft that is being overtaken has the right of
  way and the pilot-in-command of the overtaking aircraft, whether
  climbing, descending or in level flight, shall give way to the other
  aircraft by altering the heading of the overtaking aircraft to the
  right, and no subsequent change in the relative positions of the two
  aircraft shall absolve the pilot-in-command of the overtaking aircraft
  from this obligation until that aircraft has entirely passed and is
  clear of the other aircraft.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} Where an aircraft is in flight or manoeuvring on the
  surface, the pilot-in-command of the aircraft shall give way to an
  aircraft that is landing or about to land.

- [(8)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft that is
  approaching an aerodrome for the purpose of landing shall give way to
  any aircraft at a lower altitude that is also approaching the
  aerodrome for the purpose of landing.

- [(9)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft at a lower
  altitude, as described in subsection (8), shall not overtake or cut in
  front of an aircraft at a higher altitude that is in the final stages
  of an approach to land.

- [(10)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct or attempt to conduct a
  take-off or landing in an aircraft until there is no apparent risk of
  collision with any aircraft, person, vessel, vehicle or structure in
  the take-off or landing path.

- [SOR/2021-152, s. 19(E)](#1302038-1308419){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1302038-1308419.html"}
:::

##### [Right of Way --- Aircraft Manoeuvring on Water]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993782 .Subheading}

- **[[602.20]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.20
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where an aircraft on the water has
  another aircraft or a vessel on its right, the pilot-in-command of the
  first-mentioned aircraft shall give way.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where an aircraft on the water is approaching another
  aircraft or a vessel head-on, or approximately so, the
  pilot-in-command of the first-mentioned aircraft shall alter its
  heading to the right.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft that is
  overtaking another aircraft or a vessel on the water shall alter its
  heading to keep well clear of the other aircraft or the vessel.

##### [Avoidance of Collision]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993787 .Subheading}

**[[602.21]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.21 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft in such proximity to another aircraft as to create a
risk of collision.

##### [Towing]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993789 .Subheading}

**[[602.22]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.22 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aeroplane that is towing an object unless the aeroplane is
equipped with a tow hook and release control mechanism.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-77, s. 7
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-602.22-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 602.22"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Dropping of Objects]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993793 .Subheading}

**[[602.23]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.23 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
create a hazard to persons or property on the surface by dropping an
object from an aircraft in flight.

##### [Formation Flight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993795 .Subheading}

**[[602.24]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.24 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft in formation with other aircraft except by
pre-arrangement between

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the pilots-in-command of the aircraft; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the flight is conducted within a control zone,
  the pilots-in-command and the appropriate air traffic control unit.

##### [Entering or Leaving an Aircraft in Flight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993799 .Subheading}

- **[[602.25]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.25
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall enter or leave an
  aircraft in flight except with the permission of the pilot-in-command
  of the aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No pilot-in-command of an aircraft shall permit a
  person to enter or leave the aircraft during flight unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person leaves for the purpose of making a
    parachute descent;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the entering or leaving is permitted under section
    702.19; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the flight is conducted in accordance with

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a special flight operations certificate-special
      aviation event issued under section 603.02, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a special flight operations certificate issued
      under section 603.67.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-77, s. 8
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-602.25-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 602.25"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Parachute Descents]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993810 .Subheading}

**[[602.26]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.26 .sectionLabel}** Except where
permitted in accordance with section 603.37, no pilot-in-command of an
aircraft shall permit, and no person shall conduct, a parachute descent
from the aircraft

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in or into controlled airspace or an air route; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} over or into a built-up area or an open-air assembly
  of persons.

##### [Aerobatic Manoeuvres --- Prohibited Areas and Flight Conditions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993814 .Subheading}

**[[602.27]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.27 .sectionLabel}** No person
operating an aircraft shall conduct aerobatic manoeuvres

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} over a built-up area or an open-air assembly of
  persons;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2019-119, s. 28\]]{.Repealed}

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} when flight visibility is less than three miles;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} below 2,000 feet AGL, except in accordance with a
  special flight operations certificate issued pursuant to section
  603.02 or 603.67;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} in any class of airspace that requires radio contact
  with air traffic services unless the appropriate unit that provides
  air traffic services is advised that aerobatic manoeuvres will be
  conducted; or

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} in Class A, B or C airspace or Class D Control Zones
  without prior co-ordination between the pilot-in-command and the air
  traffic control unit that provides air traffic control service in that
  airspace.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-119, s. 28](#1126758-1144219){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126758-1144219.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-602.27-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 602.27"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Aerobatic Manoeuvres with Passengers]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993820 .Subheading}

**[[602.28]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.28 .sectionLabel}** No person
operating an aircraft with a passenger on board shall conduct an
aerobatic manoeuvre unless the pilot-in-command of the aircraft has
engaged in

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} at least 10 hours dual flight instruction in the
  conducting of aerobatic manoeuvres or 20 hours conducting aerobatic
  manoeuvres; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} at least one hour of conducting aerobatic manoeuvres
  in the preceding six months.

##### [Hang Glider and Ultra-light Aeroplane Operation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993824 .Subheading}

- **[[602.29]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.29
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate a hang
  glider or an ultra-light aeroplane

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at night;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in IFR flight;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsections (2) and (3), in controlled
    airspace;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} unless the aircraft is equipped with

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a suitable means of restraint that is attached to
      the primary structure of the aircraft,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a radiocommunication system adequate to permit
      two-way communication on the appropriate frequency when the
      aircraft is operated within

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} Class D airspace,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} the ADIZ, or

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} an MF area, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is an ultra-light aeroplane,
      a placard that is affixed to a surface in plain view of any
      occupant seated at the flight controls and that states, "THIS
      AEROPLANE IS OPERATING WITHOUT A CERTIFICATE OF AIRWORTHINESS/CET
      AVION EST UTILISÉ SANS CERTIFICAT DE NAVIGABILITÉ";

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsections (4) and (5), while carrying
    another person on board; or

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} unless each person on board

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} is secured by a means of restraint referred to in
      subparagraph (d)(i), and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is not an advanced
      ultra-light aeroplane, is wearing a protective helmet.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person may operate a hang glider or an ultra-light
  aeroplane in controlled airspace

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} within five nautical miles from the centre of an
    airport or heliport or within a control zone of an uncontrolled
    airport where the person has obtained permission from the airport or
    heliport operator;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} within a control zone of a controlled airport where
    the person has obtained an air traffic control clearance by two-way
    radio voice communication from the air traffic control unit of the
    airport; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is a basic ultra-light
    aeroplane, in Class E airspace other than the airspace that is
    described in paragraph (a) or (b), if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane is equipped with a portable or
      fixed altimeter, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a cross-country flight, the
      aeroplane is equipped with a portable or fixed magnetic compass or
      global navigation satellite system (GNSS) receiver; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is an advanced ultra-light
    aeroplane, if the aeroplane is equipped in accordance with section
    605.14.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A person may operate a hang glider in Class E
  airspace where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the pilot

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} is at least 16 years of age,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} is in possession of a Category 1, 3 or 4 medical
      certificate, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} has obtained a grade of not less than 60 per
      cent on a Department of Transport written examination pertaining
      to the [Canadian Aviation
      Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-96-433), air traffic procedures,
      flight instruments, navigation, flight operations and human
      factors respecting hang glider operations in Class E airspace;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the hang glider is equipped with a magnetic compass
    and altimeter;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the flight is a cross-country flight; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the pilot informs the nearest air traffic services
    unit of the time of departure and estimated duration of the flight
    in Class E airspace.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} A person may operate

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a hang glider with one other person on board if the
    flight is conducted for the purpose of providing dual flight
    instruction; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an ultra-light aeroplane with one other person on
    board if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the flight is conducted for the purpose of
      providing dual flight instruction,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the pilot is a holder of a pilot permit ---
      ultra-light aeroplane endorsed with a passenger-carrying rating
      and the aeroplane has no restrictions against carrying another
      person, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the other person is a holder of a pilot licence
      or permit, other than a student pilot permit, that allows them to
      act as pilot-in-command of an ultra-light aeroplane.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} A person may operate an advanced ultra-light
  aeroplane with another person on board where the pilot holds a permit
  or licence issued pursuant to Subpart 1 of Part IV that is appropriate
  to the functions or privileges being exercised.

##### [Fuel Dumping]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993862 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2025-98, s. 8(F)

\]
:::

**[[602.30]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.30 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
jettison fuel from an aircraft in flight unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} it is necessary to do so in order to ensure aviation
  safety; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} all appropriate measures are taken to minimize danger
  to human life and damage to the environment, insofar as the
  circumstances permit.

##### [Compliance with Air Traffic Control Instructions and Clearances]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993866 .Subheading}

- **[[602.31]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.31
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), the
  pilot-in command of an aircraft shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} comply with and acknowledge, to the appropriate air
    traffic control unit, all of the air traffic control instructions
    directed to and received by the pilot-in-command; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} comply with all of the air traffic control
    clearances received and accepted by the pilot-in-command and

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsection (2), in the case of an IFR
      flight, read back to the appropriate air traffic control unit the
      text of any air traffic control clearance received, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a VFR flight, read back to the
      appropriate air traffic control unit the text of any air traffic
      control clearance received, when so requested by the air traffic
      control unit.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Except if requested to do so by an air traffic
  control unit, the pilot-in-command of an IFR aircraft is not required
  to read back the text of an air traffic control clearance pursuant to
  paragraph (1)(b)(i) where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air traffic control clearance is received on
    the ground by the pilot-in-command before departing from a
    controlled aerodrome in respect of which a standard instrument
    departure procedure is specified in the Canada Air Pilot; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the receipt of the air traffic control clearance is
    acknowledged by the pilot-in-command by electronic means.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft may deviate from
  an air traffic control clearance or an air traffic control instruction
  to the extent necessary to carry out a collision avoidance manoeuvre,
  if the manoeuvre is carried out

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in accordance with a resolution advisory generated
    by an ACAS; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in response to an alert from a TAWS or a Ground
    Proximity Warning System (GPWS).

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} as soon as possible after initiating the collision
    avoidance manoeuvre referred to in subsection (3), inform the
    appropriate air traffic control unit of the deviation; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} immediately after completing the collision
    avoidance manoeuvre referred to in subsection (3), comply with the
    last air traffic control clearance received and accepted by, or the
    last air traffic control instruction received and acknowledged by,
    the pilot-in-command.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2012-136, s. 7
:::

##### [Airspeed Limitations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993884 .Subheading}

- **[[602.32]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.32
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no person
  shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} operate an aircraft at an indicated airspeed of
    more than 250 knots if the aircraft is below 10,000 feet ASL; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} operate an aircraft at an indicated airspeed of
    more than 200 knots if the aircraft is below 3,000 feet AGL within
    10 nautical miles of a controlled aerodrome unless authorized to do
    so in an air traffic control clearance.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person may operate an aircraft at an indicated
  airspeed greater than the airspeeds referred to in subsection (1) if
  the aircraft is being operated in accordance with a special flight
  operations certificate -- special aviation event issued pursuant to
  section 603.02.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the minimum safe airspeed for the flight
  configuration of an aircraft is greater than the airspeed referred to
  in subsection (1), the aircraft shall be operated at the minimum safe
  airspeed.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2010-219, s. 2
:::

##### [Supersonic Flight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993893 .Subheading}

**[[602.33]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.33 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft at a true Mach number of 1 or greater.

##### [Cruising Altitudes and Cruising Flight Levels]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993895 .Subheading}

- **[[602.34]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.34
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The appropriate cruising altitude or
  cruising flight level for an aircraft in level cruising flight is
  determined in accordance with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the magnetic track, in the Southern Domestic
    Airspace; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the true track, in the Northern Domestic Airspace.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), the pilot-in-command of an
  aircraft shall ensure that the aircraft is operated at a cruising
  altitude or cruising flight level appropriate to the track, as set out
  in the table to this section, unless the pilot-in-command is assigned
  another altitude or flight level by an air traffic control unit and
  the aircraft is operated in level cruising flight

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at more than 3,000 feet AGL, in VFR flight; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in IFR flight.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (2) does not apply where an aircraft is
  operated for the purpose of aerial survey or mapping and the following
  conditions are met:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command of the aircraft contacts the
    appropriate air traffic control unit as far in advance as possible
    of the proposed flight;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command of the aircraft provides, as
    far in advance as possible of the proposed take-off time of the
    aircraft, to any air traffic control unit that so requests, a
    topographical map at either a 1:500 000 or a 1:1 000 000 scale of
    the area to be surveyed or mapped, with proposed tracks and planned
    entry and exit points clearly delineated on the map;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command of the aircraft files a flight
    plan or flight itinerary with an air traffic control unit as far in
    advance as possible of the proposed take-off time of the aircraft;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the flight plan or flight itinerary referred to in
    paragraph (c) specifies the area to be surveyed or mapped

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} by reference to the relevant maps of the National
      Topographic System,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} by reference to the geographic co-ordinates of
      the area, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} where required by an air traffic control unit,
      by reference to the air photograph block reference grid map
      provided by the air traffic control unit; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is operated in controlled
    airspace, it is operated in accordance with an air traffic control
    clearance.

##### [Altimeter-setting and Operating Procedures in the Altimeter-setting Region]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993919 .Subheading}

**[[602.35]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.35 .sectionLabel}** When an aircraft
is operated in the altimeter-setting region, each flight crew member who
occupies a flight crew member position that is equipped with an
altimeter shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} immediately before conducting a take-off from an
  aerodrome, set the altimeter to the altimeter setting of the aerodrome
  or, if that altimeter setting is not obtainable, to the elevation of
  the aerodrome;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} while in flight, set the altimeter to the altimeter
  setting of the nearest station along the route of flight or, where the
  nearest stations along the route of flight are separated by more than
  150 nautical miles, to the altimeter setting of a station near the
  route of flight; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} immediately before commencing a descent for the
  purpose of landing at an aerodrome, set the altimeter to the altimeter
  setting of the aerodrome, if that altimeter setting is obtainable.

##### [Altimeter-setting and Operating Procedures in the Standard Pressure Region]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993924 .Subheading}

- **[[602.36]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.36
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} When an aircraft is operated in the
  standard pressure region, each flight crew member who occupies a
  flight crew member position that is equipped with an altimeter shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} immediately before conducting a take-off from an
    aerodrome, set the altimeter to the altimeter setting of the
    aerodrome or, if that altimeter setting is not obtainable, to the
    elevation of the aerodrome;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} before reaching the flight level at which the
    flight is to be conducted, set the altimeter to 29.92 inches of
    mercury or 1,013.2 millibars; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} immediately before commencing a descent for the
    purpose of landing at an aerodrome, set the altimeter to the
    altimeter setting of the aerodrome, if that altimeter setting is
    obtainable.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite paragraph (1)(c), when a holding procedure is
  being conducted before landing at an aerodrome located in the standard
  pressure region, each flight crew member who occupies a flight crew
  member position that is equipped with an altimeter shall set the
  altimeter to the altimeter setting of the aerodrome immediately before
  descending below the lowest flight level at which the holding
  procedure is conducted.

##### [Altimeter-setting and Operating Procedures in Transition between Regions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993931 .Subheading}

**[[602.37]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.37 .sectionLabel}** Except where
otherwise authorized by an air traffic control unit, each flight crew
member who occupies a flight crew member position that is equipped with
an altimeter shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} when flying from the altimeter-setting region into
  the standard pressure region, set the altimeter to 29.92 inches of
  mercury or 1,013.2 millibars immediately after the aircraft's entry
  into the standard pressure region; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} when flying from the standard pressure region into
  the altimeter-setting region, set the altimeter to the altimeter
  setting of the nearest station along the route of flight or, where the
  nearest stations along the route of flight are separated by more than
  150 nautical miles, the altimeter setting of a station near the route
  of flight immediately before the aircraft's entry into the
  altimeter-setting region.

##### [Flight over the High Seas]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993935 .Subheading}

**[[602.38]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.38 .sectionLabel}** The
pilot-in-command of a Canadian aircraft that is in flight over the high
seas shall comply with the applicable Rules of the Air set out in Annex
2 to the Convention and the applicable Regional Supplementary Procedures
set out in Document 7030/4 of the International Civil Aviation
Organization (ICAO).

##### [Transoceanic Flight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993937 .Subheading}

**[[602.39]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.39 .sectionLabel}** No
pilot-in-command of a single-engined aircraft, or of a multi-engined
aircraft that would be unable to maintain flight in the event of the
failure of any engine, shall commence a flight that will leave Canadian
Domestic Airspace and enter airspace over the high seas unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command holds a pilot licence endorsed
  with an instrument rating;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is equipped with

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the equipment referred to in section 605.18,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a high frequency radio capable of transmitting and
    receiving on a minimum of two appropriate international air-ground
    general purpose frequencies, and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} hypothermia protection for each person on board;
    and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft carries sufficient fuel to meet the
  requirements of section 602.88 and, in addition, carries contingency
  fuel equal to at least 10 per cent of the fuel required pursuant to
  section 602.88 to complete the flight to the aerodrome of destination.

##### [Landing at or Take-off from an Aerodrome at Night]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993945 .Subheading}

- **[[602.40]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.40
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no person
  shall conduct a landing or a take-off in a heavier-than-air aircraft
  at night at an aerodrome unless the aerodrome is lighted in accordance
  with the aerodrome lighting requirements specified in Part III.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person may conduct a landing or a take-off in a
  heavier-than-air aircraft at night at an aerodrome that is not lighted
  in accordance with the requirements referred to in subsection (1)
  where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the flight is conducted without creating a hazard
    to persons or property on the surface; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is operated

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} for the purpose of a police operation that is
      conducted in the service of a police authority, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} for the purpose of saving human life.

**[[602.41]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.41 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed,
SOR/2019-11, s. 16\]]{.Repealed}

##### [Large Unoccupied Free Balloons]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993957 .Subheading}

**[[602.42]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.42 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
release an unoccupied free balloon having a gas-carrying capacity of
more than 115 cubic feet (3.256 m^3^) except in accordance with an
authorization issued by the Minister pursuant to section 602.44.

##### [Rockets]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993959 .Subheading}

**[[602.43]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.43 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
launch a rocket, other than a model rocket or a rocket of a type used in
a fireworks display, except in accordance with an authorization issued
by the Minister pursuant to section 602.44.

##### [Authorization by the Minister]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993961 .Subheading}

**[[602.44]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.44 .sectionLabel}** The Minister may
issue an authorization referred to in section 602.42 or 602.43 where the
release of the balloon or the launch of the rocket is in the public
interest and is not likely to affect aviation safety.

##### [Kites and Model Rockets]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993963 .Subheading}

**[[602.45]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.45 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
fly a kite or launch a model rocket or a rocket of a type used in a
fireworks display into cloud or in a manner that is or is likely to be
hazardous to aviation safety.

##### [Refusal to Transport]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993965 .Subheading}

**[[602.46]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.46 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
or private operator shall transport a person if at the time of check-in
or at boarding the actions or statements of the person indicate that the
person may present a risk to the safety of the aircraft, persons or
property.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-90, s. 3
:::

##### [Suitable Accommodation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993969 .Subheading}

**[[602.47]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.47 .sectionLabel}** A private
operator or an air operator, as the case may be, shall provide a flight
crew member with suitable accommodation for rest periods away from home
base.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-269, s. 6
:::

**\[602.48 to 602.56 reserved\]**

#### [Division II --- Operational and Emergency Equipment Requirements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-993974 .Subheading}

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993975 .Subheading}

**[[602.57]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.57 .sectionLabel}** This Division
applies to persons operating

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} Canadian aircraft; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} foreign aircraft in Canada where those persons are
  Canadian citizens, permanent residents or corporations incorporated by
  or under the laws of Canada or a province.

##### [Prohibition]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993979 .Subheading}

**[[602.58]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.58 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft referred to in section 602.57 unless the operational
and emergency equipment required by these Regulations is carried on
board.

##### [Equipment Standards]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993981 .Subheading}

- **[[602.59]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.59
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no person
  shall operate an aircraft unless the operational and emergency
  equipment carried on board the aircraft

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} meets the applicable standards specified in the
    Airworthiness Manual; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is functional.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Paragraph (1)(a) does not apply in respect of the
  following operational and emergency equipment:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} survival equipment;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2019-49, s. 3\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a hand-held fire extinguisher, except if carried on
    board an aircraft operated under Subpart 4 or Part VII, where the
    extinguisher meets the applicable standards published by the
    Canadian Standards Association;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a first aid kit;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} aeronautical charts and publications;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a timepiece; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a flashlight.

##### [Requirements for Power-driven Aircraft]{.HTitleText4} {#h-993994 .Subheading}

- **[[602.60]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.60
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off
  in a power-driven aircraft, other than an ultra-light aeroplane,
  unless the following operational and emergency equipment is carried on
  board:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a checklist or placards that enable the aircraft to
    be operated in accordance with limitations specified in the aircraft
    flight manual, aircraft operating manual, pilot operating handbook
    or any equivalent document provided by the manufacturer;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} all of the necessary current aeronautical charts
    and publications covering the route of the proposed flight and any
    probable diversionary route, if the aircraft is operated in VFR OTT,
    night VFR flight or IFR flight;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a current database, if the aircraft is operated in
    IFR flight, in VFR OTT flight or in night VFR flight under Subpart 4
    of Part VI or Subpart 2, 3, 4 or 5 of Part VII and
    database-dependent navigation equipment is used;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} current data covering the route of the proposed
    flight and any probable diversionary route, if the aircraft is
    operated in VFR OTT flight other than VFR OTT flight referred to in
    paragraph (c) and database-dependent navigation equipment is used;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a hand-held fire extinguisher in the cockpit that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} is of a type suitable for extinguishing fires
      that are likely to occur,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} is designed to minimize the hazard of toxic gas
      concentrations, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} is readily available to each flight crew
      member;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a timepiece that is readily available to each
    flight crew member and that displays the time in hours, minutes and
    seconds;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a flashlight that is readily available to each crew
    member, if the aircraft is operated at night; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} a first aid kit.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A checklist or placards referred to in paragraph
  (1)(a) shall enable the aircraft to be operated in normal, abnormal
  and emergency conditions and shall include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a pre-start check;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a pre-take-off check;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a post-take-off check;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a pre-landing check; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} emergency procedures.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Emergency procedures referred to in paragraph (2)(e)
  shall include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} emergency operation of fuel, hydraulic, electrical
    and mechanical systems, where applicable;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} emergency operation of instruments and controls,
    where applicable;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} engine inoperative procedures; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} any other procedure that is necessary for aviation
    safety.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Checks and emergency procedures referred to in
  subsections (2) and (3) shall be performed and followed where they are
  applicable.

##### [Survival Equipment --- Flights over Land]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994022 .Subheading}

- **[[602.61]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.61
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no person
  shall operate an aircraft over land unless there is carried on board
  survival equipment, sufficient for the survival on the ground of each
  person on board, given the geographical area, the season of the year
  and anticipated seasonal climatic variations, that provides the means
  for

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} starting a fire;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} providing shelter;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} providing or purifying water; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} visually signalling distress.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a balloon, a glider, a hang glider, a gyroplane or
    an ultra-light aeroplane;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft that is operated within 25 nautical
    miles of the aerodrome of departure and that has the capability of
    radiocommunication with a surface-based radio station for the
    duration of the flight;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a multi-engined aircraft that is operated south of
    66° 30' north latitude

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in IFR flight within controlled airspace, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} along designated air routes;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft that is operated by an air operator,
    where the aircraft is equipped with equipment specified in the air
    operator's company operations manual, but not with the equipment
    required by subsection (1); or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft that is operated in a geographical area
    where and at a time of year when the survival of the persons on
    board is not jeopardized.

##### [Life Preservers and Flotation Devices]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994037 .Subheading}

- **[[602.62]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.62
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off
  or a landing on water in an aircraft or operate an aircraft over water
  beyond a point where the aircraft could reach shore in the event of an
  engine failure, unless a life preserver, individual flotation device
  or personal flotation device is carried for each person on board.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate a land aeroplane, gyroplane,
  helicopter or airship at more than 50 nautical miles from shore unless
  a life preserver is carried for each person on board.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate a balloon at more than two
  nautical miles from shore unless a life preserver, individual
  flotation device or personal flotation device is carried for each
  person on board.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (5), for aircraft other than
  balloons, every life preserver, individual flotation device and
  personal flotation device referred to in this section shall be stowed
  in a position that is easily accessible to the person for whose use it
  is provided, when that person is seated.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} In cases where infant life preservers are carried on
  board an aircraft operated with flight attendants on board, the infant
  life preservers may be stowed in bulk in a location that is easily
  accessible to the flight attendants if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the location is adjacent to a ditching emergency
    exit and is clearly marked as the stowage location for infant life
    preservers; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the operator has established procedures that
    require flight attendants to distribute an infant life preserver to
    each passenger responsible for an infant when preparing for a
    ditching.

:::

##### [Life Rafts and Survival Equipment --- Flights over Water]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994043 .Subheading}

- **[[602.63]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.63
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate over water a
  single-engined aeroplane, or a multi-engined aeroplane that is unable
  to maintain flight with any engine failed, at more than 100 nautical
  miles, or the distance that can be covered in 30 minutes of flight at
  the cruising speed filed in the flight plan or flight itinerary,
  whichever distance is the lesser, from a suitable emergency landing
  site unless life rafts are carried on board and are sufficient in
  total rated capacity to accommodate all of the persons on board.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), no person shall operate
  over water a multi-engined aeroplane that is able to maintain flight
  with any engine failed at more than 200 nautical miles, or the
  distance that can be covered in 60 minutes of flight at the cruising
  speed filed in the flight plan or flight itinerary, whichever distance
  is the lesser, from a suitable emergency landing site unless life
  rafts are carried on board and are sufficient in total rated capacity
  to accommodate all of the persons on board.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A person may operate over water a transport category
  aircraft that is an aeroplane, at up to 400 nautical miles, or the
  distance that can be covered in 120 minutes of flight at the cruising
  speed filed in the flight plan or flight itinerary, whichever distance
  is the lesser, from a suitable emergency landing site without the life
  rafts referred to in subsection (2) being carried on board.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate over water a single-engined
  helicopter, or a multi-engined helicopter that is unable to maintain
  flight with any engine failed, at more than 25 nautical miles, or the
  distance that can be covered in 15 minutes of flight at the cruising
  speed filed in the flight plan or flight itinerary, whichever distance
  is the lesser, from a suitable emergency landing site unless life
  rafts are carried on board and are sufficient in total rated capacity
  to accommodate all of the persons on board.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate over water a multi-engined
  helicopter that is able to maintain flight with any engine failed at
  more than 50 nautical miles, or the distance that can be covered in 30
  minutes of flight at the cruising speed filed in the flight plan or
  flight itinerary, whichever distance is the lesser, from a suitable
  emergency landing site unless life rafts are carried on board and are
  sufficient in total rated capacity to accommodate all of the persons
  on board.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} The life rafts referred to in this section shall be

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} stowed so that they are easily accessible for use
    in the event of a ditching;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} installed in conspicuously marked locations near an
    exit; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} equipped with an attached survival kit, sufficient
    for the survival on water of each person on board the aircraft,
    given the geographical area, the season of the year and anticipated
    seasonal climatic variations, that provides a means for

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} providing shelter,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} providing or purifying water, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} visually signalling distress.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} Where a helicopter is required to carry life rafts
  pursuant to subsection (4) or (5), no person shall operate the
  helicopter over water having a temperature of less than 10^o^C unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a helicopter passenger transportation suit system
    that conforms to paragraph 551.407(c) of the Airworthiness Manual is
    provided for each passenger on board;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a helicopter crew member transportation suit system
    is provided for each crew member on board; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command directs all persons on board
    to wear their helicopter transportation suit system.

- [(8)]{.lawlabel} Every person who has been directed to wear a
  helicopter transportation suit system pursuant to paragraph (7)(c)
  shall wear that suit system.

- [(9)]{.lawlabel} Paragraph (7)(a) does not apply if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the flight is necessary in order to respond to a
    medical emergency or any other emergency that is a threat to the
    safety of persons and

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the helicopter is a transport category
      rotorcraft, in respect of which a type certificate has been
      issued, that meets the requirements of Chapter 529 --- Transport
      Category Rotorcraft of the Airworthiness Manual that are
      applicable to Category A rotorcraft,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} there is insufficient time before the flight to
      acquire a helicopter passenger transportation suit system of the
      appropriate size for each passenger, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} there is a crew member in the cabin for the
      duration of the flight who is trained to assist passengers in an
      emergency evacuation in the event of a landing in water and who is
      able to come to the assistance of passengers; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} there is a medical reason that prevents a passenger
    from wearing a helicopter passenger transportation suit system.

- [(10)]{.lawlabel} A passenger who is not wearing a helicopter
  passenger transportation suit system for a reason referred to in
  subparagraph (9)(a)(ii) or paragraph (9)(b) shall be provided with a
  life preserver and the pilot-in-command shall direct the passenger to
  wear the life preserver for the duration of the flight if they are
  physically and medically able to do so.

##### [Offshore Operations Flight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994064 .Subheading}

- **[[602.64]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.64
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 602.65, no person
  shall dispatch or conduct a take-off in a helicopter to conduct an
  offshore operations flight if the pilot-in-command or the air operator
  is aware that the sea state at any point along the planned route
  exceeds the sea state for which the helicopter is able to conduct a
  ditching, according to the type certificate issued for its type
  design.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator who uses a helicopter to conduct an
  offshore operations flight shall notify the pilot-in-command if, at
  take-off or during the flight, the air operator is or becomes aware
  that the sea state at any point along the planned route between the
  position of the helicopter and the destination exceeds the sea state
  for which the helicopter is certified, as part of its type design, to
  conduct a ditching.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the pilot-in-command of a helicopter who is
  conducting an offshore operations flight is or becomes aware that the
  sea state at any point along the planned route between the position of
  the helicopter and the destination exceeds the sea state for which the
  helicopter is certified, as part of its type design, to conduct a
  ditching, the pilot-in-command shall, subject to section 602.65,
  proceed directly to a land base.

##### [Emergency Exception]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994071 .Subheading}

**[[602.65]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.65 .sectionLabel}** Subsections
602.64(1) and (3) do not apply in respect of an offshore operations
flight conducted for the purpose of responding to an emergency.
