##### [Emergency Underwater Breathing Apparatus (EUBA)]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994075 .Subheading}

- **[[602.66]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.66
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate a helicopter
  to conduct an offshore operations flight over Canadian waters unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a EUBA is provided for each person on board;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} each EUBA

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} is readily accessible for immediate use in the
      event of a ditching,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} can be donned quickly,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} provides a supplemental air supply that is
      effective to a depth of at least 3.6 m, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} is not likely to pose a snagging risk during an
      evacuation of the helicopter; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} each person on board has, in the 36-month period
    preceding the flight, received EUBA training that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} is specific to the type of EUBA provided,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} includes classroom theory training on the use of
      the EUBA and its limits and hazards, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} includes practical pool training that simulates
      the evacuation of a helicopter that has overturned or is sinking
      after a ditching.

- [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the flight is necessary in order to respond to a
    medical emergency or any other emergency that is a threat to the
    safety of persons and

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the helicopter is a transport category
      rotorcraft, in respect of which a type certificate has been
      issued, that meets the requirements of Chapter 529 --- Transport
      Category Rotorcraft of the Airworthiness Manual that are
      applicable to Category A rotorcraft and in respect of which a type
      certificate has been issued,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} before the flight,

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} there is insufficient time to acquire a EUBA
        for all passengers, or

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} the passengers have not received the training
        referred to in paragraph (1)(c), and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} there is a crew member in the cabin for the
      duration of the flight who is trained to assist passengers in an
      emergency evacuation in the event of a landing in water and who is
      able to come to the assistance of passengers; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} there is a medical reason that prevents a passenger
    from wearing a EUBA.

- [(1.2)]{.lawlabel} A passenger who is not wearing a EUBA for a reason
  referred to in subparagraph (1.1)(a)(ii) or paragraph (1.1)(b) shall
  be provided with a life preserver and the pilot-in-command shall
  direct the passenger to wear the life preserver for the duration of
  the flight if they are physically and medically able to do so.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate a helicopter to conduct an
  offshore operations flight over Canadian waters that have a
  temperature of 10°C or more unless the EUBA that is provided for a
  person under subsection (1) is attached to the life preserver,
  individual flotation device or personal flotation device that is
  carried on board the helicopter for that person.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate a helicopter to conduct an
  offshore operations flight over Canadian waters that have a
  temperature of less than 10°C unless the EUBA that is provided for a
  person under subsection (1)

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is in a pocket or pouch that is part of the
    person's helicopter passenger transportation suit system or
    helicopter crew member transportation suit system;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is in a pouch that is worn with the person's
    helicopter passenger transportation suit system or helicopter crew
    member transportation suit system; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} is attached to the person's helicopter passenger
    transportation suit system or helicopter crew member transportation
    suit system.

#### [Division III --- Flight Preparation, Flight Plans and Flight Itineraries]{.HTitleText3} {#h-994096 .Subheading}

##### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994097 .Subheading}

**[[602.70]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.70 .sectionLabel}** In this Division,

[[overdue]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[overdue]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, in respect of an aircraft, means an
    aircraft for which an arrival report has not been filed

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where a flight plan has been filed in respect of
      the aircraft,

      - [(i)]{.lawlabel} if a search and rescue notification time is
        specified in the flight plan, immediately after the last
        reported such time, or

      - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in all other cases, within one hour after the
        last reported estimated time of arrival, or

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where a flight itinerary has been filed in
      respect of the aircraft,

      - [(i)]{.lawlabel} if a search and rescue notification time is
        specified in the flight itinerary, immediately after the last
        reported such time, or

      - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in all other cases, within 24 hours after the
        last reported estimated time of arrival; ([en
        retard]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[responsible person]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[responsible person]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an individual who
    has agreed with the person who has filed a flight itinerary to
    ensure that the following are notified in the manner prescribed in
    this Division, if the aircraft is overdue, namely,

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an air traffic services unit or a community
      aerodrome radio station, or

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a Rescue Co-ordination Centre. ([personne de
      confiance]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 26](#1522575-1525669){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522575-1525669.html"}
:::

##### [Pre-flight Information]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994109 .Subheading}

**[[602.71]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.71 .sectionLabel}** The
pilot-in-command of an aircraft shall, before commencing a flight, be
familiar with the available information that is appropriate to the
intended flight.

##### [Weather Information]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994111 .Subheading}

**[[602.72]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.72 .sectionLabel}** The
pilot-in-command of an aircraft shall, before commencing a flight, be
familiar with the available weather information that is appropriate to
the intended flight.

##### [Requirement to File a Flight Plan or a Flight Itinerary]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994113 .Subheading}

- **[[602.73]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.73
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), no
  pilot-in-command shall operate an aircraft in IFR flight unless an IFR
  flight plan has been filed.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No pilot-in-command shall operate an aircraft in VFR
  flight unless a VFR flight plan or a VFR flight itinerary has been
  filed, except where the flight is conducted within 25 nautical miles
  of the departure aerodrome.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A pilot-in-command may file an IFR flight itinerary
  instead of an IFR flight plan where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the flight is conducted in part or in whole outside
    controlled airspace; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} facilities are inadequate to permit the
    communication of flight plan information to an air traffic services
    unit or a community aerodrome radio station.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Despite anything in this Division, no
  pilot-in-command shall, unless a flight plan has been filed, operate
  an aircraft between Canada and a foreign state.

##### [Contents of a Flight Plan or a Flight Itinerary]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994121 .Subheading}

**[[602.74]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.74 .sectionLabel}** A flight plan or
flight itinerary shall contain such information as is specified by the
Minister in the Canada Flight Supplement.

##### [Filing of a Flight Plan or a Flight Itinerary]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994123 .Subheading}

- **[[602.75]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.75
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A flight plan shall be filed with an
  air traffic services unit or a community aerodrome radio station.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A flight itinerary shall be filed with a responsible
  person, an air traffic services unit or a community aerodrome radio
  station.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A flight plan or flight itinerary shall be filed by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} sending, delivering or otherwise communicating the
    flight plan or flight itinerary or the information contained
    therein; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} receiving acknowledgement that the flight plan or
    flight itinerary or the information contained therein has been
    received.

##### [Changes in the Flight Plan]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994130 .Subheading}

- **[[602.76]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.76
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft
  for which an IFR flight plan or an IFR flight itinerary has been filed
  shall follow the procedure set out in subsection (2) where the
  pilot-in-command intends to make any change in the plan or itinerary
  in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the cruising altitude or cruising flight level;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the route of flight;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the destination aerodrome;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a flight plan, the true airspeed at
    the cruising altitude or cruising flight level, where the change
    intended is five per cent or more of the true airspeed specified in
    the IFR flight plan; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the Mach number, where the change intended is .01
    or more of the Mach number that has been included in the air traffic
    control clearance.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A pilot-in-command of an aircraft who intends to make
  any of the changes in the IFR flight plan or the IFR flight itinerary
  that are referred to in subsection (1) shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} notify as soon as practicable an air traffic
    control unit or the responsible person, as the case may be, of the
    intended change; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the flight is being conducted in controlled
    airspace, receive an air traffic control clearance before making the
    intended change.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft for which a VFR
  flight plan or a VFR flight itinerary has been filed shall follow the
  procedure set out in subsection (4) where the pilot-in-command intends
  to make a change in the plan or itinerary in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the route of flight;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the duration of the flight; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the destination aerodrome.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} A pilot-in-command of an aircraft who intends to make
  any of the changes in the VFR flight plan or the VFR flight itinerary
  that are referred to in subsection (3) shall notify as soon as
  practicable an air traffic services unit, a community aerodrome radio
  station or the responsible person, of the intended change.

##### [Requirement to File an Arrival Report]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994146 .Subheading}

- **[[602.77]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.77
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (3) and (4),
  a pilot-in-command of an aircraft who terminates a flight in respect
  of which a flight plan has been filed under subsection 602.75(1) shall
  ensure that an arrival report is filed with an air traffic services
  unit or a community aerodrome radio station as soon as practicable
  after landing but not later than

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the search and rescue action initiation time
    specified in the flight plan; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where no search and rescue action initiation time
    is specified in the flight plan, one hour after the last reported
    estimated time of arrival.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), a pilot-in-command of an
  aircraft who terminates a flight in respect of which a flight
  itinerary has been filed under subsection 602.75(2) shall ensure that
  an arrival report is filed with an air traffic services unit, a
  community aerodrome radio station or, if the flight itinerary was
  filed with a responsible person, the responsible person, as soon as
  practicable after landing but not later than

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the search and rescue action initiation time
    specified in the flight itinerary; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where no search and rescue action initiation time
    is specified in the flight itinerary, 24 hours after the last
    reported estimated time of arrival.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A pilot-in-command who terminates an IFR flight at an
  aerodrome where there is an operating air traffic services unit is not
  required to file an arrival report unless requested to do so by the
  appropriate air traffic control unit.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} A pilot-in-command of an aircraft who conducts a
  flight in respect of which a flight plan or flight itinerary has been
  filed with an air traffic services unit or community aerodrome radio
  station may file an arrival report by closing the flight plan or
  flight itinerary with an air traffic services unit or community
  aerodrome radio station prior to landing.

##### [Contents of an Arrival Report]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994158 .Subheading}

**[[602.78]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.78 .sectionLabel}** An arrival report
shall contain such information as is specified by the Minister in the
Canada Flight Supplement.

##### [Overdue Aircraft Report]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994160 .Subheading}

**[[602.79]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.79 .sectionLabel}** Any person who
assumes responsibilities with respect to an aircraft and who has reason
to believe that the aircraft is overdue, or any other person who has
been directed by that person to do so, shall immediately, by the
quickest means available,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} notify an air traffic services unit, a community
  aerodrome radio station or a Rescue Co-ordination Centre; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} provide, to the best of the person's knowledge, all
  of the available information concerning the overdue aircraft that may
  be requested by the air traffic services unit, the community aerodrome
  radio station or the Rescue Co-ordination Centre.

#### [Division IV --- Pre-Flight and Fuel Requirements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-994165 .Subheading}

##### [Carry-on Baggage, Equipment and Cargo]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994166 .Subheading}

- **[[602.86]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.86
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aircraft
  with carry-on baggage, equipment or cargo on board, unless the
  carry-on baggage, equipment and cargo are

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} stowed in a bin, compartment, rack or other
    location that is certified in accordance with the aircraft type
    certificate in respect of the stowage of carry-on baggage, equipment
    or cargo; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} restrained so as to prevent them from shifting
    during movement of the aircraft on the surface and during take-off,
    landing and in-flight turbulence.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aircraft with carry-on
  baggage, equipment or cargo on board unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the safety equipment, the normal and emergency
    exits that are accessible to passengers and the aisles between the
    flight deck and a passenger compartment are not wholly or partially
    blocked by carry-on baggage, equipment or cargo;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} all of the equipment and cargo that are stowed in a
    passenger compartment are packaged or covered to avoid possible
    injury to persons on board;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is type-certificated to carry 10
    or more passengers and passengers are carried on board,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} no passenger's view of any "seat belt" sign, "no
      smoking" sign or exit sign is obscured by carry-on baggage,
      equipment or cargo except if an auxiliary sign is visible to the
      passenger or another means of notification of the passenger is
      available,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} all of the passenger service carts and trolleys
      are securely restrained during movement of the aircraft on the
      surface, take-off and landing, and during in-flight turbulence
      where the pilot-in-command or in-charge flight attendant has
      directed that the cabin be secured pursuant to subsection
      605.25(3) or (4), and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} all of the video monitors that are suspended
      from the ceiling of the aircraft and extend into an aisle are
      stowed and securely restrained during take-off and landing; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} all of the cargo that is stowed in a compartment to
    which crew members have access is stowed in such a manner as to
    allow a crew member to effectively reach all parts of the
    compartment with a hand-held fire extinguisher.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-353, s. 1(F)
:::

##### [Crew Member Instructions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994181 .Subheading}

**[[602.87]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.87 .sectionLabel}** The
pilot-in-command of an aircraft shall ensure that each crew member,
before acting as a crew member on board the aircraft, has been
instructed with respect to

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the duties that the crew member is to perform; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the location and use of all of the normal and
  emergency exits and of all of the emergency equipment that is carried
  on board the aircraft.

##### [Fuel Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994185 .Subheading}

- **[[602.88]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.88
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This section does not apply in
  respect of any glider, balloon or ultra-light aeroplane.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No pilot-in-command of an aircraft shall commence a
  flight or, during flight, change the destination aerodrome set out in
  the flight plan or flight itinerary, unless the aircraft carries
  sufficient fuel to ensure compliance with subsections (3) to (5).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An aircraft operated in VFR flight shall carry an
  amount of fuel that is sufficient to allow the aircraft

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft other than a helicopter,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} when operated during the day, to fly to the
      destination aerodrome and then to fly for a period of 30 minutes
      at normal cruising speed, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} when operated at night, to fly to the
      destination aerodrome and then to fly for a period of 45 minutes
      at normal cruising speed; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a helicopter, to fly to the
    destination aerodrome and then to fly for a period of 20 minutes at
    normal cruising speed.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An aircraft operated in IFR flight shall carry an
  amount of fuel that is sufficient to allow the aircraft

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a propeller-driven aeroplane,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} where an alternate aerodrome is specified in the
      flight plan or flight itinerary, to fly to and execute an approach
      and a missed approach at the destination aerodrome, to fly to and
      land at the alternate aerodrome and then to fly for a period of 45
      minutes, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where an alternate aerodrome is not specified in
      the flight plan or flight itinerary, to fly to and execute an
      approach and a missed approach at the destination aerodrome and
      then to fly for a period of 45 minutes; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a turbo-jet-powered aeroplane or a
    helicopter,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} where an alternate aerodrome is specified in the
      flight plan or flight itinerary, to fly to and execute an approach
      and a missed approach at the destination aerodrome, to fly to and
      land at the alternate aerodrome and then to fly for a period of 30
      minutes, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where an alternate aerodrome is not specified in
      the flight plan or flight itinerary, to fly to and execute an
      approach and a missed approach at the destination aerodrome and
      then to fly for a period of 30 minutes.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} Every aircraft shall carry an amount of fuel that is
  sufficient to provide for

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} taxiing and foreseeable delays prior to take-off;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} meteorological conditions;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} foreseeable air traffic routings and traffic
    delays;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} landing at a suitable aerodrome in the event of
    loss of cabin pressurization or, in the case of a multi-engined
    aircraft, failure of any engine, at the most critical point during
    the flight; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} any other foreseeable conditions that could delay
    the landing of the aircraft.

##### [Passenger Briefings]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994207 .Subheading}

- **[[602.89]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.89
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft
  shall ensure that all of the passengers on board the aircraft are
  briefed before take-off with respect to the following, where
  applicable:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the location and means of operation of emergency
    and normal exits;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the location and means of operation of safety
    belts, shoulder harnesses and restraint devices;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the positioning of seats and the securing of seat
    backs and chair tables;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the stowage of carry-on baggage;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is unpressurized and it is
    possible that the flight will require the use of oxygen by the
    passengers, the location and means of operation of oxygen equipment;
    and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} any prohibition against smoking.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft shall ensure that
  all of the passengers on board the aircraft are briefed

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an over-water flight where the
    carriage of life preservers, individual flotation devices or
    personal flotation devices is required pursuant to section 602.62,
    before commencement of the over-water portion of the flight, with
    respect to the location and use of those items; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a pressurized aircraft that is to be
    operated at an altitude above FL 250, before the aircraft reaches FL
    250, with respect to the location and means of operation of oxygen
    equipment.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft shall, before
  take-off, ensure that all of the passengers on board the aircraft are
  provided with information respecting the location and use of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} first aid kits and survival equipment;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is a helicopter or a small
    aircraft that is an aeroplane, any ELT that is required to be
    carried on board pursuant to section 605.38; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any life raft that is required to be carried on
    board pursuant to section 602.63.

**\[602.90 to 602.95 reserved\]**

#### [Division V --- Operations at or in the Vicinity of an Aerodrome]{.HTitleText3} {#h-994224 .Subheading}

##### [General]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994225 .Subheading}

- **[[602.96]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.96
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This section applies to persons
  operating VFR or IFR aircraft at or in the vicinity of an uncontrolled
  or controlled aerodrome.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Before taking off from, landing at or otherwise
  operating an aircraft at an aerodrome, the pilot-in-command of the
  aircraft shall be satisfied that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} there is no likelihood of collision with another
    aircraft or a vehicle; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aerodrome is suitable for the intended
    operation.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft operating at or
  in the vicinity of an aerodrome shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} observe aerodrome traffic for the purpose of
    avoiding a collision;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} conform to or avoid the pattern of traffic formed
    by other aircraft in operation;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} make all turns to the left when operating within
    the aerodrome traffic circuit, except where right turns are
    specified by the Minister in the Canada Flight Supplement or where
    otherwise authorized by the appropriate air traffic control unit;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} if the aerodrome is an airport or heliport, comply
    with any airport or heliport operating restrictions specified by the
    Minister in the Canada Flight Supplement or in a NOTAM;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} where practicable, land and take off into the wind
    unless otherwise authorized by the appropriate air traffic control
    unit;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} maintain a continuous listening watch on the
    appropriate frequency for aerodrome control communications or, if
    this is not possible and an air traffic control unit is in operation
    at the aerodrome, keep a watch for such instructions as may be
    issued by visual means by the air traffic control unit; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} where the aerodrome is a controlled aerodrome,
    obtain from the appropriate air traffic control unit, either by
    radio communication or by visual signal, clearance to taxi, take off
    from or land at the aerodrome.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Unless otherwise authorized by the appropriate air
  traffic control unit, no pilot-in-command shall operate an aircraft at
  an altitude of less than 2,000 feet over an aerodrome except for the
  purpose of landing or taking off or if the aircraft is operated
  pursuant to subsection (5).

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} Where it is necessary for the purposes of the
  operation in which the aircraft is engaged, a pilot-in-command may
  operate an aircraft at an altitude of less than 2,000 feet over an
  aerodrome, where it is being operated

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the service of a police authority;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} for the purpose of saving human life;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} for fire-fighting or air ambulance operations;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} for the purpose of the administration of the
    [Fisheries Act](/eng/acts/F-14) or the [Coastal Fisheries Protection
    Act](/eng/acts/C-33);

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} for the purpose of the administration of the
    national or provincial parks;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} for the purpose of flight inspection;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} for the purpose of aerial application or aerial
    inspection;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} for the purpose of highway or city traffic patrol;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} for the purpose of aerial photography conducted by
    the holder of an air operator certificate;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} for the purpose of helicopter external load
    operations; or

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} for the purpose of flight training conducted by the
    holder of a flight training unit operator certificate.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off or landing at a
  designated airport without an aircraft fire-fighting service in an
  aeroplane in respect of which a type certificate has been issued
  authorizing the transport of 20 or more passengers if the aeroplane is
  operated under

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Part VI, Subpart 4; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Part VII, Subpart 1 or 5.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (6) does not apply in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a cargo flight without passengers;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a ferry flight;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a positioning flight;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a training flight if no fare-paying passengers are
    on board;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the arrival of an aeroplane when the airport is
    being used for a diversion or as an alternate aerodrome; or

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the subsequent departure of an aeroplane referred
    to in paragraph (e) if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the air operator or private operator has notified
      the operator of the designated airport of the intended time of
      departure,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the operator of the designated airport has
      advised the air operator or private operator that aircraft
      fire-fighting services cannot be made available within one hour
      after the later of the time that notification was given under
      subparagraph (i) and the time of landing, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command and the operations manager
      of the air operator or private operator have agreed that the
      aeroplane will depart without aircraft fire-fighting services
      being available.

##### [VFR and IFR Aircraft Operations at Uncontrolled Aerodromes within an MF Area]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994267 .Subheading}

- **[[602.97]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.97
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), no
  pilot-in-command shall operate a VFR or IFR aircraft within an MF area
  unless the aircraft is equipped with radiocommunication equipment
  pursuant to Subpart 5.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of a VFR or IFR aircraft
  operating within an MF area shall maintain a listening watch on the
  mandatory frequency specified for use in the MF area.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of a VFR aircraft that is not
  equipped with the radiocommunication equipment referred to in
  subsection (1) may operate the aircraft to or from an uncontrolled
  aerodrome that lies within an MF area if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a ground station is in operation at the aerodrome;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} prior notice of the pilot-in-command's intention to
    operate the aircraft at the aerodrome has been given to the ground
    station;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} when conducting a take-off, the pilot-in-command
    ascertains by visual observation that there is no likelihood of
    collision with another aircraft or a vehicle during take-off; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} when approaching for a landing, the aircraft enters
    the aerodrome traffic circuit from a position that will require it
    to complete two sides of a rectangular circuit before turning onto
    the final approach path.

##### [General MF Reporting Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994276 .Subheading}

- **[[602.98]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.98
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every report made pursuant to this
  Division shall be made on the mandatory frequency that has been
  specified for use in the applicable MF area.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Every report referred to in subsection (1) shall be

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} directed to the ground station associated with the
    MF area, if a ground station exists and is in operation; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} broadcast, if a ground station does not exist or is
    not in operation.

##### [MF Reporting Procedures before Entering Manoeuvring Area]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994282 .Subheading}

**[[602.99]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.99 .sectionLabel}** The
pilot-in-command of a VFR or IFR aircraft that is operated at an
uncontrolled aerodrome that lies within an MF area shall report the
pilot-in-command's intentions before entering the manoeuvring area of
the aerodrome.

##### [MF Reporting Procedures on Departure]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994284 .Subheading}

**[[602.100]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.100 .sectionLabel}** The
pilot-in-command of a VFR or IFR aircraft that is departing from an
uncontrolled aerodrome that lies within an MF area shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} before moving onto the take-off surface, report the
  pilot-in-command's departure procedure intentions;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} before take-off, ascertain by radiocommunication and
  by visual observation that there is no likelihood of collision with
  another aircraft or a vehicle during take-off; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} after take-off, report departing from the aerodrome
  traffic circuit.

##### [MF Reporting Procedures on Arrival]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994289 .Subheading}

**[[602.101]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.101 .sectionLabel}** The
pilot-in-command of a VFR aircraft arriving at an uncontrolled aerodrome
that lies within an MF area shall report

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} before entering the MF area and, where circumstances
  permit, shall do so at least five minutes before entering the area,
  giving the aircraft's position, altitude and estimated time of landing
  and the pilot-in-command's arrival procedure intentions;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} when joining the aerodrome traffic circuit, giving
  the aircraft's position in the circuit;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} when on the downwind leg, if applicable;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} when on final approach; and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} when clear of the surface on which the aircraft has
  landed.

##### [MF Reporting Procedures When Flying Continuous Circuits]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994296 .Subheading}

**[[602.102]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.102 .sectionLabel}** The
pilot-in-command of a VFR aircraft carrying out continuous circuits at
an uncontrolled aerodrome that lies within an MF area shall report

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} when joining the downwind leg of the circuit;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} when on final approach, stating the
  pilot-in-command's intentions; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} when clear of the surface on which the aircraft has
  landed.

##### [Reporting Procedures When Flying through an MF Area]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994301 .Subheading}

**[[602.103]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.103 .sectionLabel}** The
pilot-in-command of an aircraft flying through an MF area shall report

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} before entering the MF area and, where circumstances
  permit, shall do so at least five minutes before entering the area,
  giving the aircraft's position and altitude and the pilot-in-command's
  intentions; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} when clear of the MF area.

##### [Reporting Procedures for IFR Aircraft When Approaching or Landing at an Uncontrolled Aerodrome]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994305 .Subheading}

- **[[602.104]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.104
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This section applies to persons
  operating IFR aircraft when approaching or landing at an uncontrolled
  aerodrome, whether or not the aerodrome lies within an MF area.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an IFR aircraft who intends
  to conduct an approach to or a landing at an uncontrolled aerodrome
  shall report

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command's intentions regarding the
    operation of the aircraft

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} five minutes before the estimated time of
      commencing the approach procedure, stating the estimated time of
      landing,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} when commencing a circling manoeuvre, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} as soon as practicable after initiating a
      missed approach procedure; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft's position

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} when passing the fix outbound, where the
      pilot-in-command intends to conduct a procedure turn or, if no
      procedure turn is intended, when the aircraft first intercepts the
      final approach course,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} when passing the final approach fix or three
      minutes before the estimated time of landing where no final
      approach fix exists, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} on final approach.

##### [Noise Operating Criteria]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994317 .Subheading}

**[[602.105]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.105 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft at or in the vicinity of an aerodrome except in
accordance with the applicable noise abatement procedures and noise
control requirements specified by the Minister in the Canada Air Pilot
or Canada Flight Supplement, including the procedures and requirements
relating to

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} preferential runways;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} minimum noise routes;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} hours when aircraft operations are prohibited or
  restricted;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} arrival procedures;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} departure procedures;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} duration of flights;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the prohibition or restriction of training flights;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} VFR or visual approaches;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} simulated approach procedures; and

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} the minimum altitude for the operation of aircraft in
  the vicinity of the aerodrome.

##### [Noise-restricted Runways]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994329 .Subheading}

- **[[602.106]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.106
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no person
  shall operate a subsonic turbo-jet aeroplane that has a maximum
  certificated take-off weight of more than 34 000 kg (74,956 pounds) on
  take-off at a noise-restricted runway set out in column II of an item
  of the table to this section at an aerodrome set out in column I of
  that item, unless there is on board

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a certificate of noise compliance issued in respect
    of the aeroplane under section 507.20; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the aeroplane is not a Canadian aircraft, a
    foreign certificate of noise compliance issued by the state of
    registry that has been validated by the Minister under section
    507.23.

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2020-151, s. 14\]]{.Repealed}

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} to the extent that it is inconsistent with any
    obligation assumed by Canada in respect of a foreign state in a
    treaty, convention or agreement;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the pilot-in-command of an aircraft has
    declared an emergency; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} where an aircraft is operated on

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} an air evacuation operation,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} any other emergency air operation , or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a departure from an aerodrome at which it was
      required to land because of an emergency.

#### [Division VI --- Visual Flight Rules]{.HTitleText3} {#h-994351 .Subheading}

##### [Minimum Visual Meteorological Conditions for VFR Flight in Controlled Airspace]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994352 .Subheading}

**[[602.114]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.114 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft in VFR flight within controlled airspace unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is operated with visual reference to the
  surface;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} flight visibility is not less than three miles;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the distance of the aircraft from cloud is not less
  than 500 feet vertically and one mile horizontally; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is operated within a control zone,

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} when reported, ground visibility is not less than
    three miles, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} except when taking off or landing, the distance of
    the aircraft from the surface is not less than 500 feet.

##### [Minimum Visual Meteorological Conditions for VFR Flight in Uncontrolled Airspace]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994360 .Subheading}

**[[602.115]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.115 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft in VFR flight within uncontrolled airspace unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is operated with visual reference to the
  surface;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is operated at or above 1,000 feet
  AGL

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} during the day, flight visibility is not less than
    one mile,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} during the night, flight visibility is not less
    than three miles, and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} in either case, the distance of the aircraft from
    cloud is not less than 500 feet vertically and 2,000 feet
    horizontally;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is not a helicopter and is
  operated at less than 1,000 feet AGL

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} during the day, flight visibility is not less than
    two miles, except if otherwise authorized in an air operator
    certificate,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} during the night, flight visibility is not less
    than three miles, and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} in either case, the aircraft is operated clear of
    cloud; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is a helicopter and is operated at
  less than 1,000 feet AGL

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} during the day, flight visibility is not less than
    one mile, except if otherwise authorized in an air operator
    certificate or a flight training unit operator certificate ---
    helicopter,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} during the night, flight visibility is not less
    than three miles, and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} in either case, the aircraft is operated clear of
    cloud.

##### [VFR Over-the-Top]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994377 .Subheading}

**[[602.116]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.116 .sectionLabel}** Despite
paragraphs 602.114(a) and 602.115(a), an aircraft may be operated in VFR
OTT flight during the cruise portion of the flight during the day if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is operated at a vertical distance from
  cloud of at least 1,000 feet;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is operated between two cloud
  layers, the vertical distance between the layers is at least 5,000
  feet;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} flight visibility at the cruising altitude of the
  aircraft is at least five miles; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the weather at the aerodrome of destination is
  forecast to have no broken, overcast or obscured layer lower than
  3,000 feet above the planned flight altitude and the ground visibility
  is forecast to be five miles or greater with no thunderstorms or
  precipitation

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} where the forecast is an aerodrome forecast (TAF),
    for the period from one hour before to two hours after the estimated
    time of arrival, using the worst forecast condition together with
    any of the references TEMPO (temporary fluctuation), BECMG
    (becoming) or PROB (probability), and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where an aerodrome forecast (TAF) is not available
    and the forecast is an area forecast (FA), for the period from one
    hour before to three hours after the estimated time of arrival.

##### [Special VFR Flight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994385 .Subheading}

- **[[602.117]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.117
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite paragraph 602.114(b), an
  aircraft may be operated in special VFR flight within a control zone
  if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} weather conditions preclude compliance with
    paragraph 602.114(b);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} flight visibility is not less than

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} one mile, where the aircraft is not a helicopter,
      or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} one-half mile, where the aircraft is a
      helicopter;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is operated clear of cloud and with
    visual reference to the surface at all times; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} authorization to do so has been requested and
    obtained from the appropriate air traffic control unit.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where aerodrome traffic permits, an air traffic
  control unit shall authorize a pilot-in-command to operate an aircraft
  in special VFR flight within a control zone if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command requests authorization to
    operate the aircraft in special VFR flight;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} when reported, ground visibility within the control
    zone is not less than

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} one mile, where the aircraft is not a helicopter,
      or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} one-half mile, where the aircraft is a
      helicopter;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is equipped with radiocommunication
    equipment capable of maintaining communication with the appropriate
    air traffic control unit; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is not a helicopter and is operated
    during the night, and the authorization is for the purpose of
    allowing the aircraft to land at the destination aerodrome.

#### [Division VII --- Instrument Flight Rules]{.HTitleText3} {#h-994404 .Subheading}

##### [General Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994405 .Subheading}

- **[[602.121]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.121
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No pilot-in-command shall operate an
  aircraft in IMC in any class of airspace, except in accordance with
  IFR.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No pilot-in-command of an aircraft shall conduct an
  IFR flight within controlled airspace unless the aircraft is operated
  in accordance with an air traffic control clearance pursuant to
  section 602.31.

##### [Alternate Aerodrome Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994409 .Subheading}

**[[602.122]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.122 .sectionLabel}** Except as
otherwise authorized by the Minister in an air operator certificate or
in a special authorization issued under subsection 604.05(2), no
pilot-in-command shall operate an aircraft in IFR flight unless the IFR
flight plan or IFR flight itinerary that has been filed for the flight
under section 602.73 includes an alternate aerodrome having a landing
area suitable for use by that aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 15
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-602.122-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 602.122"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Alternate Aerodrome Weather Minima]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994413 .Subheading}

**[[602.123]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.123 .sectionLabel}** No
pilot-in-command of an aircraft shall include an alternate aerodrome in
an IFR flight plan or IFR flight itinerary unless available weather
information indicates that the ceiling and visibility at the alternate
aerodrome will, at the expected time of arrival, be at or above the
alternate aerodrome weather minima specified in the Canada Air Pilot.

##### [Minimum Altitudes to Ensure Obstacle Clearance]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994415 .Subheading}

- **[[602.124]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.124
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) and (3),
  the pilot-in-command of an IFR aircraft shall, except when taking off
  or landing, or when being vectored by an ATC unit, ensure that the
  aircraft is operated at or above

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the MOCA, when the aircraft is on an airway or air
    route; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the minimum altitude established by the Minister to
    ensure obstacle clearance and specified on an IFR chart, when the
    aircraft is within airspace in respect of which such a minimum
    altitude has been established.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} When an aircraft referred to in subsection (1) is not
  being operated on an airway or air route or within airspace in respect
  of which a minimum altitude referred to in paragraph (1)(b) has been
  established, the pilot-in-command shall ensure that the aircraft is
  operated at or above

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an altitude of 1,000 feet above the highest
    obstacle located within a horizontal distance of five nautical miles
    from the estimated position of the aircraft in flight;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in a region designated as a mountainous region in
    the Designated Airspace Handbook and identified therein as area 1 or
    5, an altitude of 2,000 feet above the highest obstacle within a
    horizontal distance of five nautical miles from the estimated
    position of the aircraft in flight; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in a region designated as a mountainous region in
    the Designated Airspace Handbook and identified therein as area 2, 3
    or 4, an altitude of 1,500 feet above the highest obstacle within a
    horizontal distance of five nautical miles from the estimated
    position of the aircraft in flight.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If aviation safety would be at risk as a result of
  the presence of obstacles to air navigation, the Minister may issue a
  NOTAM that establishes a higher minimum altitude requirement than that
  referred to in subsection (1) or (2).

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 11](#1522540-1525171){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522540-1525171.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-602.124-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 602.124"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Enroute IFR Position Reports]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994425 .Subheading}

- **[[602.125]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.125
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an IFR
  aircraft shall transmit position reports over compulsory reporting
  points specified on an IFR chart unless advised by the appropriate ATC
  unit that the aircraft is an identified aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A position report transmitted pursuant to
  subsection (1) shall contain the information specified by the Minister
  in the Canada Flight Supplement.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-77, s. 12
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 12](#1522542-1525173){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522542-1525173.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-602.125-20060630.html "Link to previous version of section 602.125"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Take-off Minima]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994431 .Subheading}

- **[[602.126]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.126
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No pilot-in-command of an aircraft
  shall conduct a take-off if the take-off visibility, as determined in
  accordance with subsection (2), is below the minimum take-off
  visibility specified in

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator certificate where the aircraft is
    operated in accordance with Part VII;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a special authorization issued under subsection
    604.05(2); or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the Canada Air Pilot in any case other than a case
    described in paragraph (a) or (b).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), the take-off
  visibility is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the RVR of the runway, if the RVR is reported to be
    at or above the minimum take-off visibility specified in a document
    or the manual referred to in subsection (1);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the ground visibility of the aerodrome for the
    runway, if the RVR

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} is reported to be less than the minimum take-off
      visibility specified in a document or the manual referred to in
      subsection (1),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} is reported to vary between distances less than
      and greater than the minimum take-off visibility specified in the
      Canada Air Pilot or a certificate referred to in subsection (1),
      or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} is not reported; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the runway visibility as observed by the
    pilot-in-command, if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the RVR is not reported, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the ground visibility of the aerodrome is not
      reported.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-199, s. 11
- SOR/2014-131, s. 16
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-602.126-20061201.html "Link to previous version of section 602.126"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Instrument Approaches]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994448 .Subheading}

- **[[602.127]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.127
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Unless otherwise authorized by the
  appropriate air traffic control unit, the pilot-in-command of an IFR
  aircraft shall, when conducting an approach to an aerodrome or a
  runway, ensure that the approach is made in accordance with the
  instrument approach procedure.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No pilot-in-command of an IFR aircraft shall commence
  an instrument approach procedure unless the aircraft altimeter is set
  to an altimeter setting that is usable at the aerodrome where the
  approach is to be conducted.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No pilot-in-command of an IFR aircraft shall conduct
  a landing following an instrument approach unless, immediately before
  landing, the pilot-in-command ascertains, by means of
  radiocommunication or visual inspection,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the condition of the runway or surface of intended
    landing; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the wind direction and speed.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-26, s. 24](#1511719-1516263){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1511719-1516263.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-602.127-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 602.127"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Contact Approach --- Authorization]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525174 .Subheading}

**[[602.127.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.127.1 .sectionLabel}** A
pilot-in-command shall not conduct a contact approach unless authorized
by the appropriate ATC unit.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 13](#1522544-1525177){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522544-1525177.html"}
:::

##### [Contact Approach --- Conditions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525178 .Subheading}

- **[[602.127.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.127.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Before requesting authorization to
  conduct a contact approach, the pilot-in-command of an IFR aircraft
  shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the aircraft is being operated clear of
    cloud and that flight visibility is not less than one mile;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} establish visual contact with the surface of the
    earth; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} determine that they are able to proceed to the
    aerodrome of intended landing while complying with the requirements
    of paragraphs (a) and (b).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} When conducting the contact approach, the
  pilot-in-command shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} avoid entering any restricted airspace;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} comply with the requirements of paragraphs (1)(a)
    and (b); and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} immediately advise the appropriate ATC unit if they
    are unable to complete the contact approach.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 13](#1522544-1525189){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522544-1525189.html"}
:::

##### [Visual Approach --- Authorization]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525190 .Subheading}

**[[602.127.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.127.3 .sectionLabel}** A
pilot-in-command shall not conduct a visual approach unless authorized
by the appropriate ATC unit.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 13](#1522544-1525193){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522544-1525193.html"}
:::

##### [Visual Approach --- Conditions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525194 .Subheading}

- **[[602.127.4]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.127.4
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Before requesting authorization to
  conduct a visual approach, the pilot-in-command of an IFR aircraft
  shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} ensure that they are operating the aircraft in VMC;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} establish visual contact with the aerodrome of
    intended landing; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} determine that they are able to proceed to the
    aerodrome of intended landing while complying with the requirements
    of paragraphs (a) and (b).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Before accepting authorization to conduct a visual
  approach, the pilot-in-command shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} ensure that they are operating the aircraft in VMC;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} establish visual contact with the aerodrome of
    intended landing or with the aircraft from which they must maintain
    visual separation; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} determine that they are able to

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} proceed to the aerodrome of intended landing in
      VMC,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} maintain visual separation from, and avoid the
      wake turbulence of, a preceding aircraft, if instructed to do so,
      and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} conduct the approach in accordance with any
      instructions issued with the authorization.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} When conducting the visual approach, the
  pilot-in-command shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} ensure that they are operating the aircraft in VMC;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} avoid entering any restricted airspace; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} immediately advise the appropriate ATC unit if they
    are unable to complete the visual approach.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 13](#1522544-1525212){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522544-1525212.html"}
:::

##### [Landing Minima]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994452 .Subheading}

- **[[602.128]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.128
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No pilot-in-command of an IFR
  aircraft shall conduct an instrument approach procedure except in
  accordance with the minima specified in the Canada Air Pilot or the
  Restricted Canada Air Pilot.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No pilot-in-command of an IFR aircraft shall, unless
  the required visual reference necessary to continue the approach to
  land has been established,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a CAT I or CAT II precision
    approach, continue the final approach descent below the decision
    height; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a non-precision approach, descend
    below the minimum descent altitude.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where the pilot-in-command of an IFR aircraft
  conducting an instrument approach does not establish the required
  visual reference referred to in subsection (2), the pilot-in-command
  shall initiate a missed approach procedure

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a CAT I or CAT II precision
    approach, at decision height; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a non-precision approach, at the
    missed approach point.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Despite anything in this Division, no
  pilot-in-command of an IFR aircraft shall conduct a precision approach
  to CAT II or CAT III minima unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the flight crew has received the training specified
    in the Manual of All Weather Operations (Categories II and III); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is operated in accordance with the
    procedures, the equipment requirements and the limitations specified
    in the manual referred to in paragraph (a).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-199, s. 12
- SOR/2014-131, s. 17
- [SOR/2021-152, s. 19(E)](#1302038-1308431){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1302038-1308431.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-602.128-20140529.html "Link to previous version of section 602.128"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Approach Ban --- General]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994466 .Subheading}

- **[[602.129]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.129
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This section does not apply in
  respect of aircraft operated under Part VII.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (4), the RVR with
  respect to an aeroplane is less than the minimum RVR if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where the RVR is measured by RVR "A" and RVR "B",
    the RVR measured by RVR "A" for the runway of intended approach is
    less than 1,200 feet or the RVR measured by RVR "B" for the runway
    of intended approach is less than 600 feet; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the RVR is measured by only one of RVR "A"
    and RVR "B", the RVR for the runway of intended approach is less
    than 1,200 feet.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (4), the RVR with
  respect to a helicopter is less than the minimum RVR if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where the RVR is measured by RVR "A" and RVR "B",
    the RVR measured by RVR "A" for the surface of intended approach is
    less than 1,200 feet; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the RVR is measured by only one of RVR "A"
    and RVR "B", the RVR for the surface of intended approach is less
    than 1,200 feet.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where the RVR is reported to be less than the minimum
  RVR set out in subsection (2) or (3), as applicable, no person shall
  continue an instrument approach in an IFR aircraft unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at the time the RVR report is received, the
    aircraft has passed the FAF inbound or, where there is no FAF, the
    point where the final approach course is intercepted;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is on a training flight where a
    landing is not intended and the appropriate air traffic control unit
    is informed that a missed approach procedure will be initiated at or
    above the decision height or minimum descent altitude, as
    appropriate;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the RVR is varying between distances less than and
    greater than the minimum RVR;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the RVR is less than the minimum RVR, and the
    ground visibility at the aerodrome where the runway is located is
    reported to be at least one quarter of a mile; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command of the aircraft is conducting
    a precision approach to CAT III minima.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} No pilot-in-command of an IFR aircraft shall commence
  a non-precision approach, an APV or a CAT I or CAT II precision
  approach to an airport where low-visibility procedures are in effect.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-199, s. 13
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-602.129-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 602.129"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Approach Ban --- CAT III Precision]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994484 .Subheading}

- **[[602.130]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.130
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This section does not apply in
  respect of aircraft operated under Part VII.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall continue a CAT III precision approach
  in an IFR aircraft beyond the FAF inbound or, where there is no FAF,
  the point where the final approach course is intercepted, unless the
  RVR reported is equal to or greater than the minimum RVR specified in
  the Canada Air Pilot in respect of the runway or surface of intended
  approach for the instrument approach procedure conducted.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-199, s. 13
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-602.130-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 602.130"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Runway Visibility]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994490 .Subheading}

- **[[602.131]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.131
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} When no reading from RVR "A" or RVR
  "B" for the runway of intended approach is available, runway
  visibility is assessed

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} by a pilot holding an instrument rating and in the
    manner set out in section 622.131 of Standard 622 --- Pilot
    Assessment of Runway Visibility Standards of the General Operating
    and Flight Rules Standards; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} by a person qualified in accordance with section
    804.26 and in the manner set out in section 804.25.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The assessment of runway visibility is valid only for
  a period of 20 minutes after it is established.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-199, s. 14
- SOR/2015-160, s. 28(F)
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-602.131-20061201.html "Link to previous version of section 602.131"){.PITLink}
:::

**\[602.132 reserved\]**

#### [Division VIII --- Radiocommunications]{.HTitleText3} {#h-994499 .Subheading}

##### [Language Used in Aeronautical Radiocommunications]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994500 .Subheading}

**[[602.133]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.133 .sectionLabel}** English and
French are the languages of aeronautical radiocommunication in Canada.

##### [Request for Air Traffic Services]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994502 .Subheading}

**[[602.134]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.134 .sectionLabel}** Any person
operating an aircraft who wishes to receive air traffic services
referred to in section 801.24 in English or French shall make their
request known to the appropriate ATS unit by means of an initial
radiocommunication in English or French.

::: HistoricalNote

:::

**[[602.135]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.135 .sectionLabel}** \[Reserved,
SOR/2019-119, s. 35\]

**\[602.135 Reserved\]**

##### [Continuous Listening Watch]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994568 .Subheading}

**[[602.136]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.136 .sectionLabel}** Subject to
sections 602.137 and 602.138, where an aircraft is equipped with
radiocommunication equipment, the pilot-in-command shall ensure that

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a listening watch is maintained on the appropriate
  frequency; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} where communications are required, communication is
  established with an air traffic services unit or community aerodrome
  radio station, as applicable, on that appropriate frequency.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 26](#1522575-1525681){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522575-1525681.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-602.136-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 602.136"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Two-way Radiocommunication Failure in IFR Flight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994572 .Subheading}

- **[[602.137]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.137
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where there is a two-way
  radiocommunication failure between the controlling air traffic control
  unit and an IFR aircraft that is in or has received a clearance to
  enter controlled airspace, the pilot-in-command shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} maintain a listening watch on the appropriate
    frequency for control messages or further clearance and acknowledge
    receipt of any such messages, if possible, by any means available;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} set the transponder to code 7600; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} attempt to establish communications with any air
    traffic services facility or other aircraft, inform the facility or
    aircraft of the difficulty and request it to relay the information
    to the last air traffic control unit with which communications had
    been established.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where communications cannot be established with any
  air traffic services facility, either directly or by relay through an
  intermediary, the pilot-in-command shall, except where specific
  instructions to cover an anticipated communications failure have been
  received from an air traffic control unit, comply with the procedures
  specified by the Minister in the Canada Air Pilot and the Canada
  Flight Supplement.

##### [Two-way Radiocommunication Failure in VFR Flight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994579 .Subheading}

**[[602.138]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.138 .sectionLabel}** Where there is
a two-way radiocommunication failure between the controlling air traffic
control unit and a VFR aircraft while operating in Class B, Class C or
Class D airspace, the pilot-in-command shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} leave the airspace

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} where the airspace is a control zone, by landing at
    the aerodrome for which the control zone is established, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in any other case, by the shortest route;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is equipped with a transponder,
  set the transponder to code 7600; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} inform an air traffic control unit as soon as
  possible of the actions taken pursuant to paragraph (a).

**\[602.139 to 602.142 reserved\]**

#### [Division IX --- Emergency Communications and Security]{.HTitleText3} {#h-994587 .Subheading}

##### [Emergency Radio Frequency Capability]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994588 .Subheading}

**[[602.143]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.143 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft equipped with two-way VHF radiocommunication
equipment unless the equipment is capable of providing communication on
VHF frequency 121.5 MHz.

##### [Interception Signals, Interception of Aircraft and Instructions to Land]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994590 .Subheading}

- **[[602.144]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.144
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall give an interception
  signal or an instruction to land except

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a peace officer, an officer of a police authority
    or an officer of the Canadian Armed Forces acting within the scope
    of their duties; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a person authorized to do so by the Minister
    pursuant to subsection (2).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may authorize a person to give an
  interception signal or an instruction to land if such authorization is
  in the public interest and is not likely to affect aviation safety.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft who receives an
  instruction to land from a person referred to in subsection (1) shall,
  subject to any direction received from an air traffic control unit,
  comply with the instruction.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an intercepting aircraft and
  the pilot-in-command of an intercepted aircraft shall comply with the
  rules of interception set out in the Canada Flight Supplement.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2021-152, s. 18](#1302032-1308411){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1302032-1308411.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-602.144-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 602.144"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [ADIZ]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994598 .Subheading}

- **[[602.145]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.145
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This section applies in respect of
  aircraft before entering into and while operating within the ADIZ, the
  dimensions of which are specified in the Designated Airspace Handbook.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Every flight plan or flight itinerary required to be
  filed pursuant to this section shall be filed with an air traffic
  services unit or a community aerodrome radio station.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft whose point of
  departure within the ADIZ or last point of departure before entering
  the ADIZ has facilities for the transmission of flight plan or flight
  itinerary information shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} before take-off, file a flight plan or flight
    itinerary;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a VFR aircraft where the point of
    departure is outside the ADIZ,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} indicate in the flight plan or flight itinerary
      the estimated time and point of ADIZ entry, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} as soon as possible after take-off, communicate
      by radio to an air traffic control unit, a flight service station
      or a community aerodrome radio station a position report of the
      aircraft's location, altitude, aerodrome of departure and
      estimated time and point of ADIZ entry; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a VFR aircraft where the point of
    departure is within the ADIZ, as soon as possible after take-off,
    communicate by radio to an air traffic control unit, a flight
    service station or a community aerodrome radio station a position
    report of the aircraft's location, altitude and aerodrome of
    departure.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft whose point of
  departure within the ADIZ or last point of departure before entering
  the ADIZ does not have facilities for the transmission of flight plan
  or flight itinerary information shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} as soon as possible after take-off, file by
    radiocommunication a flight plan or flight itinerary; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a VFR aircraft, indicate in the
    flight plan or flight itinerary the estimated time and point of ADIZ
    entry, if applicable.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of a VFR aircraft shall revise
  the estimated time and point of ADIZ entry and inform an air traffic
  control unit, a flight service station or a community aerodrome radio
  station, when the aircraft is not expected to arrive

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} within plus or minus five minutes of the estimated
    time at

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a reporting point,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the point of ADIZ entry, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the point of destination within the ADIZ; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} within 20 nautical miles of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the estimated point of ADIZ entry, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the centre line of the route of flight indicated
      in the flight plan or flight itinerary.

##### [ESCAT Plan]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994619 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote

\]
:::

- **[[602.146]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.146
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This section applies in respect of
  aircraft before entering into and while operating within Canadian
  domestic airspace or the ADIZ.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft referred to in
  subsection (1) who is notified by an air traffic control unit of the
  implementation of the ESCAT Plan shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} before take-off, obtain approval for the flight
    from the appropriate air traffic services unit;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} comply with any instruction to land or to change
    course or altitude that is received from the appropriate air traffic
    services unit; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} provide the appropriate air traffic services unit
    with position reports

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} when operating within controlled airspace, as
      required pursuant to section 602.125, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} when operating outside controlled airspace, at
      least every 30 minutes.

#### [Division X --- Noise Emission Levels for Subsonic Turbo-Jet Aeroplanes]{.HTitleText3} {#h-994633 .Subheading}

##### [Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994634 .Subheading}

- **[[602.150]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-602.150
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate a subsonic
  turbo-jet aeroplane that has a maximum certificated take-off weight of
  34 000 kg (74,956 pounds) or more to or from an aerodrome other than
  Gander International Airport unless the aeroplane meets the noise
  emission standards set out in Chapter 3 or 4 of Volume I, Aircraft
  Noise, of Annex 16 to the Convention.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of subsection (1), the following
  expressions, used in Annex 16 to the Convention, have the following
  meanings:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} [[aeroplane]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} has the same
    meaning as in subsection 101.01(1);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} [[maximum certificated take-off
    mass]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} has the same meaning as [[maximum
    certificated take-off weight]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} in subsection
    101.01(1); and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} [[subsonic jet]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} has the same
    meaning as [[subsonic turbo-jet aeroplane]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} in
    subsection (1).
