### [Subpart 3 --- Special Flight Operations]{.HTitleText2} {#h-994655 .Subheading}

#### [Division I --- Special Aviation Events]{.HTitleText3} {#h-994656 .Subheading}

##### [Certification Requirements for Special Aviation Events]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994657 .Subheading}

**[[603.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.01 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
conduct a special aviation event, other than a fly-in, unless the person
complies with the provisions of a special flight operations certificate
--- special aviation event issued by the Minister under section 603.02.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-151, s. 15](#1252605-1257182){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1252605-1257182.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-603.01-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 603.01"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Issuance of Special Flight Operations Certificate --- Special Aviation Event]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994659 .Subheading}

**[[603.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.02 .sectionLabel}** Subject to
section 6.71 of the Act, the Minister shall, on receipt of an
application submitted in the form and manner required by and within the
time limits specified in the Special Flight Operations Standards, issue
a special flight operations certificate-special aviation event to an
applicant who demonstrates to the Minister the ability to conduct a
special aviation event in accordance with the Special Flight Operations
Standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-77, s. 13
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-603.02-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 603.02"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Contents of Special Flight Operations Certificate --- Special Aviation Event]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994663 .Subheading}

**[[603.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.03 .sectionLabel}** A special flight
operations certificate --- special aviation event shall contain the
following information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the certificate holder;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number of the certificate;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the date of issue of the certificate;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the validity period of the certificate;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the general conditions identified in section 603.04;
  and

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} specific conditions with respect to

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the types of aircraft authorized to operate at the
    special aviation event and, if applicable, their registration,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the names and, if applicable, the qualifications
    of the flight crew members authorized to participate in the special
    aviation event, and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} any other condition pertaining to the special
    aviation event that the Minister deems necessary for aviation
    safety.

##### [General Conditions of Special Flight Operations Certificate --- Special Aviation Event]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994674 .Subheading}

**[[603.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.04 .sectionLabel}** A special flight
operations certificate --- special aviation event shall contain the
following general conditions:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the certificate holder shall maintain an adequate
  management organization;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the certificate holder shall ensure that participants
  are

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} qualified for the type of demonstration to be
    flown, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} provided with a briefing that meets the Special
    Flight Operations Standards; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the certificate holder shall conduct the special
  aviation event in a safe manner.

##### [Event Management]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994681 .Subheading}

**[[603.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.05 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
conduct a special aviation event unless the person has a management
organization that

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} is capable of exercising supervision and operational
  control over

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} persons attending the special aviation event,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} any flight that is to be operated at the special
    aviation event; and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} personnel involved in the conduct of the special
    aviation event whose duties and responsibilities are specified in
    the Special Flight Operations Standards; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} meets the Special Flight Operations Standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-77, s. 14
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-603.05-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 603.05"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Participant and Aircraft Eligibility]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994690 .Subheading}

**[[603.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.06 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft or permit an aircraft to be operated in a special
aviation event unless the person operating the aircraft and the aircraft

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} meet the eligibility requirements specified in
  section 623.06 of the Special Flight Operations Standards; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} are authorized to do so in a special flight
  operations certificate-special aviation event.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-77, s. 15
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-603.06-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 603.06"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Minimum Safety Distances and Altitudes]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994696 .Subheading}

**[[603.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.07 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft in a special aviation event at a distance from, or
at an altitude above, a spectator area, a built-up area or an occupied
building if that distance or altitude is less than the minimum specified
in section 623.07 of the Special Flight Operations Standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-77, s. 15
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-603.07-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 603.07"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Weather Conditions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994700 .Subheading}

**[[603.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.08 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft in a special aviation event in weather conditions
that are below the minimum conditions specified in the Special Flight
Operations Standards.

##### [Participant Briefing]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994702 .Subheading}

**[[603.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.09 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft in a special aviation event unless the person has
received a participant briefing that meets the Special Flight Operations
Standards.

**\[603.10 to 603.15 reserved\]**

#### [Division II --- Balloons with Fare-paying Passengers]{.HTitleText3} {#h-994705 .Subheading}

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994706 .Subheading}

**[[603.16]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.16 .sectionLabel}** This Division
applies in respect of the operation of a balloon where fare-paying
passengers are carried on board.

##### [Certification Requirements for Balloon Operations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994708 .Subheading}

**[[603.17]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.17 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate a balloon under this Division unless the person complies with
the provisions of a special flight operations certificate --- balloons
issued by the Minister pursuant to section 603.18.

##### [Issuance of Special Flight Operations Certificate --- Balloons]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994710 .Subheading}

**[[603.18]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.18 .sectionLabel}** Subject to
section 6.71 of the Act, the Minister shall, on receipt of an
application submitted in the form and manner required by the Special
Flight Operations Standards, issue a special flight operations
certificate --- balloons to an applicant who demonstrates to the
Minister the ability to conduct the flight operation in accordance with
the Special Flight Operations Standards.

##### [Contents of Special Flight Operations Certificate --- Balloons]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994712 .Subheading}

**[[603.19]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.19 .sectionLabel}** A special flight
operations certificate --- balloons shall contain the following
information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the balloon operator;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number of the certificate;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the date of issue of the certificate;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the general conditions identified in section 603.20;
  and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} specific conditions with respect to

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the types and AX class of balloons authorized and,
    where the balloon is of a special shape or is a foreign-registered
    balloon, its registration,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the external carriage of passengers, and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} any other condition pertaining to the operation
    that the Minister deems necessary for aviation safety.

##### [General Conditions of Special Flight Operations Certificate --- Balloons]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994722 .Subheading}

**[[603.20]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.20 .sectionLabel}** A special flight
operations certificate --- balloons shall contain the following general
conditions:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the balloon operator shall maintain balloons that are
  properly equipped for the area of operation and the type of operation;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the balloon operator shall maintain its balloons in
  accordance with the requirements of Subpart 5;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the balloon operator shall employ flight crew members
  who meet the Special Flight Operations Standards; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the balloon operator shall conduct a safe operation.

##### [Crew Member Qualifications]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994728 .Subheading}

**[[603.21]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.21 .sectionLabel}** No balloon
operator shall permit a person to act and no person shall act as the
pilot-in-command of a balloon unless the person meets the qualification
and currency requirements set out in the Special Flight Operations
Standards.

##### [Briefing of Passengers]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994730 .Subheading}

**[[603.22]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.22 .sectionLabel}** The
pilot-in-command of a balloon shall ensure that passengers are given a
safety briefing that meets the Special Flight Operations Standards.

##### [Operations at Night]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994732 .Subheading}

**[[603.23]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.23 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate a balloon in free flight at night unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the balloon is equipped in accordance with section
  605.19; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} landings are conducted during the day.

##### [Tethered Flight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994736 .Subheading}

- **[[603.24]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.24
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate a balloon in
  tethered flight with passengers on board unless the pilot-in-command
  is on board.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command shall record all time spent in
  tethered flight as air time for the purpose of maintenance.

##### [Carriage of Passengers]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994740 .Subheading}

**[[603.25]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.25 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate a balloon with passengers on board unless each passenger is
carried in the basket.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-77, s. 16
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-603.25-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 603.25"){.PITLink}
:::

**[[603.26]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.26 .sectionLabel}** [\[Repealed,
SOR/2006-77, s. 16\]]{.Repealed}

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-603.26-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 603.26"){.PITLink}
:::

**\[603.26 to 603.35 reserved\]**

#### [Division III --- Parachuting]{.HTitleText3} {#h-994746 .Subheading}

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994747 .Subheading}

**[[603.36]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.36 .sectionLabel}** This Division
applies in respect of the conduct of parachute descents

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in or into controlled airspace or an air route; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} over or into a built-up area or open-air assembly of
  persons.

##### [Certification Requirements for Parachute Operations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994751 .Subheading}

**[[603.37]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.37 .sectionLabel}** For the purposes
of section 602.26, a pilot-in-command may permit and a person may
conduct a parachute descent under this Division if the person complies
with the provisions of a special flight operations certificate ---
parachuting issued by the Minister pursuant to section 603.38.

##### [Issuance of Special Flight Operations Certificate --- Parachuting]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994753 .Subheading}

**[[603.38]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.38 .sectionLabel}** Subject to
section 6.71 of the Act, the Minister shall, on receipt of an
application submitted in the form and manner required by the Special
Flight Operations Standards, issue a special flight operations
certificate --- parachuting to an applicant who demonstrates to the
Minister the ability to conduct the flight operation in accordance with
the Special Flight Operations Standards.

##### [Contents of Special Flight Operations Certificate --- Parachuting]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994755 .Subheading}

**[[603.39]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.39 .sectionLabel}** A special flight
operations certificate --- parachuting shall contain the following
information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the certificate holder;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number of the certificate;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the date of issue of the certificate;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the validity period of the certificate;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the type of flight operation authorized; and

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} any condition pertaining to the operation that the
  Minister deems necessary for aviation safety.

**\[603.40 to 603.64 reserved\]**

#### [Division IV --- Miscellaneous Special Flight Operations]{.HTitleText3} {#h-994764 .Subheading}

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994765 .Subheading}

**[[603.65]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.65 .sectionLabel}** This Division
applies in respect of the following flight operations when not conducted
under Part VII:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the operation of an aircraft, other than a balloon,
  for the purpose of conducting a take-off or landing within a built-up
  area of a city or town at a place other than an airport, heliport or
  military aerodrome;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the operation of an aircraft for the purpose of
  conducting aerial application, aerial inspection or aerial photography
  at altitudes and distances less than those specified in paragraph
  602.14(2)(a);

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the operation of a helicopter while conducting Class
  B, C or D external load operations over a built-up area or open-air
  assembly of persons, including flight at altitudes and distances less
  than those specified in paragraph 602.14(2)(a);

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2019-11, s. 18\]]{.Repealed}

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the operation of a powered aircraft while persons
  enter or, except for parachute descents, leave the aircraft in flight;
  and

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the operation of an aircraft while conducting
  aerobatic manoeuvres below 2,000 feet AGL.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2003-271, s. 7
- SOR/2007-87, s. 12
- [SOR/2019-11, s. 18](#1045408-1138167){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045408-1138167.html"}
- [SOR/2019-119, s. 36](#1126776-1144246){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126776-1144246.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-603.65-20190601.html "Link to previous version of section 603.65"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Certification Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994777 .Subheading}

**[[603.66]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.66 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
conduct a flight operation referred to in section 603.65 unless the
person complies with the provisions of a special flight operations
certificate issued by the Minister pursuant to section 603.67.

##### [Issuance of Special Flight Operations Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994779 .Subheading}

**[[603.67]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.67 .sectionLabel}** Subject to
section 6.71 of the Act, the Minister shall, on receipt of an
application submitted in the form and manner required by the Special
Flight Operations Standards, issue a special flight operations
certificate to an applicant who demonstrates to the Minister the ability
to conduct the flight operation in accordance with the Special Flight
Operations Standards.

##### [Contents of Special Flight Operations Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994781 .Subheading}

**[[603.68]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-603.68 .sectionLabel}** A special flight
operations certificate shall contain the following information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the certificate holder;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number of the certificate;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the date of issue of the certificate;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the validity period of the certificate;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the type of flight operation authorized; and

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} any condition pertaining to the operation that the
  Minister deems necessary for aviation safety.

**\[603.69 to 603.75 reserved\]**

### [Subpart 4 --- Private Operators]{.HTitleText2} {#h-994790 .Subheading}

#### [Division I --- General Provisions]{.HTitleText3} {#h-994791 .Subheading}

##### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994792 .Subheading}

- **[[604.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.01
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The following definitions apply in
  this Subpart.

  [[flight deck duty time]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[flight deck duty time]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the period
      spent by a flight crew member at a flight crew member position in
      an aeroplane during flight time. ([temps de service au poste de
      pilotage]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[main base]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[main base]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a location where a private
      operator has personnel, aircraft and facilities for its operations
      and that is established as the principal place of business of the
      private operator. ([base principale]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[PBN Manual]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[PBN Manual]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means ICAO Document 9613,
      entitled Performance-based Navigation (PBN) Manual. ([manuel
      PBN]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[special authorization]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[special authorization]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an
      authorization issued by the Minister under subsection 604.05(2)
      that permits the carrying out of an activity referred to in
      Division IV or an activity in respect of which the Minister has
      established requirements under subsection
      604.74(1). ([autorisation spéciale]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[sub-base]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[sub-base]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a location where a private
      operator has personnel and aircraft and from which operational
      control is exercised in accordance with the private operator's
      operational control system. ([base secondaire]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of interpreting a document
  incorporated by reference into this Subpart, unless the context
  requires otherwise,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} "should" and "must" shall be read as "shall";

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} "operator" and "aircraft operator" shall be read as
    "private operator"; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} "authority", "competent aviation authority" and
    "operating authority" shall be read as "Minister".

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-341, s. 5
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
- SOR/2018-269, s. 7
:::

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994806 .Subheading}

**[[604.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.02 .sectionLabel}** This Subpart
applies to the following Canadian aircraft:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} large aeroplanes;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} turbine-powered aircraft;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} pressurized aircraft; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} multi-engined aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-341, s. 5
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-604.02-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 604.02"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Prohibition]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994814 .Subheading}

- **[[604.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.03
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no person
  shall operate any of the following Canadian aircraft for the purpose
  of transporting passengers or goods unless the person is the holder of
  a private operator registration document:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a large aeroplane;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a turbo-jet-powered aeroplane; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a turbine-powered pressurized aeroplane
    certificated for more than six passenger seats.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply to the operation of an
  aircraft referred to in paragraphs (1)(a) to (c) by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an air operator who operates the aircraft in
    accordance with the requirements of Part VII; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a person who operates the aircraft under a flight
    permit issued under section 507.04.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-341, s. 5
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

[Previous
Version](section-604.03-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 604.03"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Issuance of a Private Operator Registration Document]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994825 .Subheading}

- **[[604.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.04
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The applicant for a private operator
  registration document shall submit to the Minister an application
  containing the following information:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the applicant's legal name and, if any, trade name;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the applicant's contact information;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the names of the operations manager, chief pilot
    and maintenance manager;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a description of the proposed area of operation,
    using the chart depicted in the Index to Application of
    Supplementary Procedures in ICAO Document 7030, entitled Regional
    Supplementary Procedures;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the location of the applicant's main base and, if
    any, sub-bases; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} for each aircraft that will be operated, the
    aircraft type, the nationality mark and the registration mark.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall, on receipt of the application
  referred to in subsection (1), issue a private operator registration
  document to the applicant if the applicant is the registered owner of
  all the aircraft that will be operated under this Subpart or is
  permitted to use those aircraft under section 203.03.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-341, s. 5
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
- [SOR/2022-246, s. 15(F)](#1380144-1380774){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1380144-1380774.html"}
:::

:::

##### [Issuance of Special Authorization]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994837 .Subheading}

- **[[604.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.05
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A private operator who wishes to
  operate an aircraft under a special authorization shall submit to the
  Minister an application that

  - [a)]{.lawlabel} identifies the activity referred to in Division IV
    that the applicant wishes to carry out; and

  - [b)]{.lawlabel} includes a copy of the part of the private
    operator's operations manual that sets out the processes, practices
    and procedures relating to the special authorization requested.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall, on receipt of the application
  referred to in subsection (1), issue a special authorization to the
  applicant if the applicant

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} holds a private operator registration document;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is able to meet the requirements of Division IV
    relating to the special authorization requested; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} has an operations manual that sets out the
    processes, practices and procedures that are necessary to meet the
    requirements of Division IV relating to the special authorization
    requested.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-341, s. 5
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Notice to the Minister]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994848 .Subheading}

**[[604.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.06 .sectionLabel}** A private
operator shall notify the Minister if a change is made to the
information contained in an application submitted under subsection
604.04(1) within ten days after the day on which the change is made.

##### [Amendment of Private Operator's Operations Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994852 .Subheading}

**[[604.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.07 .sectionLabel}** A private
operator who has been issued a special authorization, and who amends the
part of the private operator's operations manual that sets out the
processes, practices and procedures relating to the special
authorization, shall submit to the Minister a copy of that part of the
operations manual within ten days after the day on which the amendment
is made.

##### [Duties of a Private Operator]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994856 .Subheading}

**[[604.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.08 .sectionLabel}** A private
operator shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} ensure that no person is appointed operations manager
  or chief pilot or continues to serve as operations manager or chief
  pilot if, at the time of the person's appointment or during the
  person's tenure, the person has a record of conviction for

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} an offence under section 7.3 of the Act, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} two or more offences under these Regulations that
    did not arise from a single incident;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} ensure that no person is appointed maintenance
  manager or continues to serve as maintenance manager if, at the time
  of the person's appointment or during the person's tenure, the person
  has a record of conviction for an offence under section 7.3 of the
  Act;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the operations manager performs the
  duties set out in section 604.204;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} perform the duties set out in section 604.208; and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} provide the operations manager and the maintenance
  manager with the financial and human resources necessary to ensure
  that the private operator meets the requirements of these Regulations.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Accountability]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994867 .Subheading}

- **[[604.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.09
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No operations manager, no chief
  pilot and no maintenance manager shall assign to another person a
  management function for which he or she is responsible and accountable
  unless the private operator's operations manual

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} identifies the functions that may be assigned;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} identifies either by name or by position the
    persons to whom those functions may be assigned; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} describes the scope of the assignment.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The responsibility and accountability of an
  operations manager, a chief pilot and a maintenance manager are not
  affected by the assignment of a management function to another person
  under subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

#### [Division II --- Flight Operations]{.HTitleText3} {#h-994881 .Subheading}

##### [Operational Control System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994882 .Subheading}

- **[[604.25]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.25
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A private operator shall have an
  operational control system that is adapted to the complexity of the
  private operator's operations and to the private operator's area of
  operation, and that meets the requirements of subsections (2) and (3).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operational control system shall include
  procedures for ensuring that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} all the operational requirements specified in this
    Subpart are met;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} each aircraft is operated within the weight and
    balance limits specified in the aircraft flight manual;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the names of the persons on board an aircraft are
    recorded by the private operator before each flight; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} search and rescue authorities are notified in a
    timely manner if a flight is overdue or missing.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operational control system shall include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} pilot self-dispatch procedures that set out the
    following elements:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} flight planning requirements,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the timing within which a flight crew member
      must inform the private operator of an aircraft's departure and
      arrival, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a method of confirming that an aircraft has
      arrived safely at an unattended aerodrome during a VFR flight or
      that an IFR flight plan has been cancelled prior to landing; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} co-authority dispatch procedures that set out the
    following elements:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} flight planning requirements,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} flight following requirements,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} flight watch requirements,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a method of confirming that an aircraft has
      arrived safely at an unattended aerodrome during a VFR flight or
      that an IFR flight plan has been cancelled prior to landing,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the method by which the operational flight plan
      is approved and recorded by the pilot-in-command and the flight
      dispatcher,

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} if operational flight plans are prepared and
      accepted for a series of flights, the method by which any changes
      to those plans are approved and recorded by the pilot-in-command
      and the flight dispatcher,

    - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} if flight planning and flight watch are two
      separate functions, the method of switching from one to the other,
      and

    - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} a means to ensure that, at each location where
      a flight originates, the pilot-in-command will

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} receive meteorological information related to
        the flight,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} receive a copy of the operational flight plan,
        and

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} can contact the responsible flight dispatcher
        prior to take-off.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Documentation related to the operational control of a
  flight shall be retained by the private operator for at least 180 days
  after the day on which the flight is completed.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-341, s. 5
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-604.25-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 604.25"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Designation of Pilot-in-command and Second-in-command]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994910 .Subheading}

- **[[604.26]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.26
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A private operator shall designate,
  for each flight, a pilot-in-command or, if the crew includes two or
  more flight crew members, a pilot-in-command and a second-in-command.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The private operator shall record the name of the
  pilot-in-command and, if applicable, second-in-command designated for
  each flight under subsection (1) and shall retain the record for at
  least 180 days after the day on which the flight is completed.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-341, s. 5
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-604.26-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 604.26"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Flight Dispatchers and Flight Followers]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994916 .Subheading}

**[[604.27]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.27 .sectionLabel}** A flight
dispatcher and a flight follower shall, in respect of a flight conducted
by a private operator,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} perform flight following and flight watch;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} provide any operational information requested by a
  flight crew member; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} notify search and rescue authorities in a timely
  manner if a flight is overdue or missing.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-341, s. 5
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-604.27-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 604.27"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Instrument Approaches --- Landing]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994923 .Subheading}

**[[604.28]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.28 .sectionLabel}** No person shall,
in an aircraft operated by a private operator, conduct a landing
following an instrument approach unless, immediately before landing, the
pilot-in-command ascertains, by means of radiocommunication or visual
inspection,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the condition of the runway or surface of intended
  landing; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the wind direction and speed.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 34
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-604.28-20091201.html "Link to previous version of section 604.28"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Division III --- Flight Operations --- Documents]{.HTitleText3} {#h-994931 .Subheading}

##### [Checklist]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994932 .Subheading}

- **[[604.36]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.36
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A private operator shall provide
  every crew member with the checklist referred to in paragraph
  602.60(1)(a) or with the part of the checklist that is necessary for
  the performance of the crew member's duties.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Every crew member shall follow, in the performance of
  his or her duties, the checklist or part of the checklist referred to
  in subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Aircraft Operating Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994938 .Subheading}

- **[[604.37]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.37
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A private operator may establish an
  aircraft operating manual for the operation of its aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An aircraft operating manual shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} contain aircraft operating procedures that are
    consistent with those contained in the aircraft flight manual;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} contain, if the aircraft flight manual is not
    carried on board the aircraft, the aircraft performance data and
    limitations specified in that manual, and clearly identify them as
    aircraft flight manual requirements;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} contain the private operator's standard operating
    procedures, if any; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} identify the aircraft to which it relates.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Operational Flight Data Sheet]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994948 .Subheading}

- **[[604.38]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.38
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off
  in an aircraft operated by a private operator unless an operational
  flight data sheet has been prepared and contains the following
  information:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the date of the flight;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft's nationality mark and registration
    mark;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the name of the pilot-in-command;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the departure aerodrome;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the destination aerodrome;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the alternate aerodrome, if any;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the estimated flight time;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the fuel endurance;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the weight of the fuel on board the aircraft;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} the zero fuel weight of the aircraft;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} the take-off weight and centre of gravity of the
    aircraft;

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} the number of persons on board the aircraft;

  - [(m)]{.lawlabel} the proposed time of departure; and

  - [(n)]{.lawlabel} the estimated time of arrival.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft referred to in
  subsection (1) shall, on the completion of each flight, record on the
  operational flight data sheet the flight time, time of departure, time
  of arrival and aerodrome of arrival.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The private operator shall retain a copy of the
  operational flight data sheet for at least 180 days after the day on
  which the flight is completed.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

**\[604.39 to 604.45 reserved\]**

#### [Division IV --- Flight Operations --- Special Authorizations]{.HTitleText3} {#h-994970 .Subheading}

##### [Minimum Performance Capability of Long-range Navigation Systems]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994971 .Subheading}

- **[[604.46]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.46
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Division, a
  long-range navigation system shall have the following performance
  capability:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the standard deviation of the lateral track
    deviations is less than 6.3 nautical miles;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the proportion of the total flight time that is
    spent by the aircraft at a distance of 30 or more nautical miles
    from the cleared track is less than 5.3 x 10^-4^; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the proportion of the total flight time that is
    spent by the aircraft at a distance of 50 to 70 nautical miles from
    the cleared track is less than 1.3 x 10^-4^.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Division, a global
  navigation satellite system (GNSS) receiver is considered to be a
  long-range navigation system if it is installed in accordance with the
  requirements of Advisory Circular 20-138B, entitled Airworthiness
  Approval of Positioning and Navigation Systems, dated September 27,
  2010 and published by the Federal Aviation Administration of the
  United States, as amended from time to time.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [General Prohibition --- Special Authorizations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994980 .Subheading}

- **[[604.47]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.47
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no person
  shall carry out any activity referred to in this Division or in
  respect of which the Minister has established requirements under
  subsection 604.74(1) unless that person is a private operator.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person other than a private operator may conduct an
  instrument approach using a GNSS receiver to the following minima:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} lateral navigation (LNAV);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} lateral navigation/vertical navigation (LNAV/VNAV);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} localizer performance without vertical guidance
    (LP); and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} localizer performance with vertical guidance (LPV).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [No Alternate Aerodrome --- IFR Flight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-994990 .Subheading}

- **[[604.48]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.48
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of section 602.122,
  a pilot-in-command may conduct an IFR flight in an aircraft operated
  by a private operator when an alternate aerodrome has not been
  designated in the IFR flight plan or in the IFR flight itinerary if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the private operator is authorized to do so under a
    special authorization;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the estimated flight time is not more than six
    hours and the departure aerodrome is located in North America,
    Bermuda or the Caribbean islands;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the forecast or reported weather at the destination
    aerodrome, from one hour before until one hour after the estimated
    time of arrival, does not include

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} conditions, including fog or precipitation, that
      restrict flight visibility to less than three miles,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a thunderstorm,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a ceiling of less than 1,000 feet above the FAF
      altitude and a ground visibility of less than three miles,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a ceiling of less than 1,500 feet above the
      minimum descent altitude and a ground visibility of less than six
      miles, or

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} freezing rain, freezing drizzle or sleet;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the destination aerodrome

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} has at least two runways that are

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} operational,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} separate and not reciprocal directions of the
        same runway, and

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} suitable for the aircraft on the basis of the
        aircraft operating procedures, the aircraft performance data and
        limitations specified in the aircraft flight manual, and the
        factors that affect the performance of the aircraft, such as
        atmospheric and surface conditions, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} is equipped with an emergency electrical power
      supply to operate the equipment and facilities that are essential
      for a safe landing of the aircraft in the event of a failure of
      the main electrical power supply; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} every flight crew member has received training, for
    which the validity period has not expired, in the conduct of an IFR
    flight when an alternate aerodrome has not been designated in the
    IFR flight plan or in the IFR flight itinerary.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the requirements of paragraphs (1)(a) to (e) are
  met, and regardless of the departure aerodrome, the pilot-in-command
  of an aircraft that is operated by a private operator, and that is on
  a flight to a destination aerodrome in Canada, may file a new IFR
  flight plan or a new IFR flight itinerary that does not include an
  alternate aerodrome when the aircraft is within six hours' flight time
  of the destination aerodrome.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Take-off Minima]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995011 .Subheading}

**[[604.49]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.49 .sectionLabel}** Despite paragraph
602.126(1)(b),

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a pilot-in-command may conduct a take-off in an
  aircraft operated by a private operator when the reported RVR is at
  least 1,200 feet or the reported ground visibility is at least one
  quarter of a statute mile if

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the private operator is authorized to do so under a
    special authorization,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is operated by at least two flight
    crew members,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the flight plan filed for the flight specifies a
    take-off alternate aerodrome that

    - [(A)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a twin-engined aircraft, is within
      the distance that can be flown in 60 minutes at normal cruising
      speed, or

    - [(B)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft with three or more
      engines, is within the distance that can be flown in 120 minutes
      at normal cruising speed,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command and, if the operations manual
    provides that the second-in-command may conduct the take-off, the
    second-in-command have received the following training for which the
    validity period has not expired:

    - [(A)]{.lawlabel} take-off alternate aerodrome requirements,

    - [(B)]{.lawlabel} pilot-in-command experience requirements,

    - [(C)]{.lawlabel} pilot-in-command responsibility for visibility
      and obstacle clearance requirements, and

    - [(D)]{.lawlabel} minimum aircraft and runway equipment
      requirements,

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command

    - [(A)]{.lawlabel} identifies any obstructions that may be in the
      take-off path,

    - [(B)]{.lawlabel} determines --- using the aircraft performance
      data and limitations specified in the aircraft flight manual ---
      that the aircraft is, with the critical engine inoperative, able
      to

      - [(I)]{.lawlabel} safely clear those obstructions, and

      - [(II)]{.lawlabel} maintain at least the minimum enroute altitude
        to the take-off alternate aerodrome, and

    - [(C)]{.lawlabel} verifies that the RVR is at least 1,200 feet or
      the ground visibility is at least one quarter of a statute mile,

  - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} the runway is equipped with high-intensity runway
    lights, or runway centre line lights, that are serviceable and
    functioning and that are visible to the pilot throughout the
    take-off run, or with runway centre line markings that are visible
    to the pilot throughout the take-off run,

  - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command and second-in-command
    attitude indicators provide a clear depiction of total aircraft
    attitude that includes the incorporation of pitch attitude index
    lines in appropriate increments up to 15° above and 15° below the
    reference line,

  - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} failure warning systems to immediately detect
    failures and malfunctions in attitude indicators, directional gyros
    and horizontal situation indicators are operative, and

  - [(ix)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command and, if the operations manual
    provides that the second-in-command may conduct the take-off, the
    second-in-command have demonstrated to the private operator the
    ability to operate the aircraft in accordance with this paragraph;
    and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a pilot-in-command may conduct a take-off in an
  aircraft operated by a private operator when the reported RVR is at
  least 600 feet if

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the private operator is authorized to do so under a
    special authorization,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is operated by at least two flight
    crew members,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the flight plan filed for the flight specifies a
    take-off alternate aerodrome that

    - [(A)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a twin-engined aircraft, is within
      the distance that can be flown in 60 minutes at normal cruising
      speed, or

    - [(B)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft with three or more
      engines, is within the distance that can be flown in 120 minutes
      at normal cruising speed,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command and, if the operations manual
    provides that the second-in-command may conduct the take-off, the
    second-in-command have received the following training for which the
    validity period has not expired:

    - [(A)]{.lawlabel} ground training in

      - [(I)]{.lawlabel} take-off alternate aerodrome requirements,

      - [(II)]{.lawlabel} pilot-in-command experience requirements,

      - [(III)]{.lawlabel} pilot-in-command responsibility for
        visibility and obstacle clearance requirements, and

      - [(IV)]{.lawlabel} minimum aircraft and runway equipment
        requirements, and

    - [(B)]{.lawlabel} level C or D flight simulator training that
      includes

      - [(I)]{.lawlabel} one completed take-off at an RVR of 600 feet,
        and

      - [(II)]{.lawlabel} one rejected take-off, at an RVR of 600 feet,
        that includes an engine failure,

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command

    - [(A)]{.lawlabel} identifies any obstructions that may be in the
      take-off path,

    - [(B)]{.lawlabel} determines --- using the aircraft performance
      data and limitations specified in the aircraft flight manual ---
      that the aircraft is, with the critical engine inoperative, able
      to

      - [(I)]{.lawlabel} safely clear those obstructions, and

      - [(II)]{.lawlabel} maintain at least the minimum enroute altitude
        to the take-off alternate aerodrome, and

    - [(C)]{.lawlabel} verifies that the RVR is at least 600 feet,

  - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} the runway is equipped

    - [(A)]{.lawlabel} with high-intensity runway lights, and runway
      centre line lights, that are serviceable and functioning and that
      are visible to the pilot throughout the take-off run, and with
      runway centre line markings that are visible to the pilot
      throughout the take-off run, and

    - [(B)]{.lawlabel} with two RVR sensors that each show an RVR of at
      least 600 feet, one sensor being situated at the approach end of
      the runway and the other at

      - [(I)]{.lawlabel} the mid-point of the runway, or

      - [(II)]{.lawlabel} the departure end of the runway, if the runway
        is equipped with three RVR sensors and the sensor situated at
        the mid-point is not serviceable,

  - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command and second-in-command
    attitude indicators provide a clear depiction of total aircraft
    attitude that includes the incorporation of pitch attitude index
    lines in appropriate increments up to 15° above and 15° below the
    reference line,

  - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} failure warning systems to immediately detect
    failures and malfunctions in attitude indicators, directional gyros
    and horizontal situation indicators are operative, and

  - [(ix)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command and, if the operations manual
    provides that the second-in-command may conduct the take-off, the
    second-in-command have demonstrated to the private operator the
    ability to operate the aircraft in accordance with this paragraph.

##### [Instrument Procedures --- GNSS]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995065 .Subheading}

**[[604.50]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.50 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
conduct an instrument procedure using a GNSS receiver in an aircraft
operated by a private operator unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the private operator is authorized to do so under a
  special authorization;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} every flight crew member has received the following
  training for which the validity period has not expired:

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} ground training in

    - [(A)]{.lawlabel} the GNSS and its theory of operation,

    - [(B)]{.lawlabel} the operation of the model of GNSS receiver that
      will be used, and

    - [(C)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken in response to GNSS
      receiver warnings and messages, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in-flight training

    - [(A)]{.lawlabel} in the operation of the model of GNSS receiver
      that will be used,

    - [(B)]{.lawlabel} in the actions to be taken in response to GNSS
      receiver warnings and messages,

    - [(C)]{.lawlabel} in the use of the GNSS receiver for instrument
      procedures and other associated duties for each crew position that
      the flight crew member will occupy,

    - [(D)]{.lawlabel} provided

      - [(I)]{.lawlabel} on board an aircraft, or

      - [(II)]{.lawlabel} using a Level C or D flight simulator equipped
        with the same model of GNSS receiver as is installed in the
        private operator's aircraft or with a model with a user
        interface comparable to the user interface of that GNSS
        receiver, and

    - [(E)]{.lawlabel} provided by a pilot who has received training on
      the same model of GNSS receiver as is installed in the private
      operator's aircraft or on a model with a user interface comparable
      to the user interface of that GNSS receiver;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} every flight crew member has demonstrated to the
  private operator the ability to conduct an instrument approach using a
  GNSS receiver in accordance with this section;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the coverage area of the GNSS receiver database is
  compatible with the area of operation in which the aircraft will be
  operated;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the private operator has established procedures to
  ensure that

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the GNSS receiver database is updated so that it
    remains current,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} flight crew members who identify GNSS receiver
    database errors communicate those errors to the private operator,
    and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the GNSS receiver database errors identified are
    communicated to the private operator's other personnel and to the
    GNSS receiver database provider;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} if the aircraft is designed to be operated by one
  flight crew member, the GNSS course deviation and distance displays
  are located at the pilot station normally occupied by the
  pilot-in-command and within the primary field of vision of the flight
  crew member who occupies the pilot station;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} if the aircraft is designed to be operated by two
  flight crew members, the GNSS course deviation and distance displays
  are located at each pilot station and within the primary field of
  vision of the flight crew member who occupies the pilot station;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} if the aircraft is designed to be operated by one
  flight crew member, but can be operated by two flight crew members,

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the control display unit that is linked to the GNSS
    receiver is centrally located in relation to the two pilot stations
    and provides navigation information that is visible to the pilot not
    flying, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the GNSS course deviation and distance displays
    are located at each pilot station and within the primary field of
    vision of the flight crew members who occupy those pilot stations;
    and

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} the private operator has established GNSS approach
  procedures in order to prevent confusion between GNSS distance
  information and distance measuring equipment (DME) information.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Precision Approaches --- CAT II and CAT III]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995095 .Subheading}

**[[604.51]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.51 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
conduct a CAT II or a CAT III precision approach in an aircraft operated
by a private operator unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the private operator is authorized to do so under a
  special authorization;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the requirements of section 602.128 are met;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} every flight crew member has received, in respect of
  CAT II and CAT III precision approaches, ground training for which the
  validity period has not expired that includes the following elements:

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the characteristics, capabilities and limitations
    of the instrument landing system (ILS), including how its
    performance is affected by interference from other airborne or
    taxiing aircraft and from ground vehicles,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the characteristics of the visual aids and the
    limitations on their use in reduced visibility at the various glide
    path angles and cockpit cut-off angles, and the height at which
    visual cues are expected to appear in actual operating conditions,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the operation, capabilities and limitations of
    the airborne systems,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the procedures and techniques for an approach, a
    missed approach and a rejected landing, and a description of the
    factors affecting height loss during a missed approach in normal and
    abnormal aircraft configurations,

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the use and limitations of RVR, including the
    applicability of RVR readings from different positions along the
    runway,

  - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} obstacle limitation surfaces, obstacle-free zones,
    missed approach design criteria, obstacle clearance for a CAT II or
    CAT III precision approach, and obstacle clearance for a go-around
    and a rejected landing,

  - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} the effects of turbulence, precipitation and low
    level windshear,

  - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} the procedures and techniques for making the
    transition from instrument flight to visual flight in low RVR
    conditions, including the geometry of eye, wheel and antenna
    positions in relation to ILS reference datum height,

  - [(ix)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken if the required visual
    reference becomes inadequate when the aircraft is below the decision
    height, and the technique to be used for making the transition from
    visual flight to instrument flight if a go-around is necessary,

  - [(x)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken in the event of a failure
    of the approach and landing equipment above and below the decision
    height or alert height,

  - [(xi)]{.lawlabel} the recognition of a failure of the ground
    equipment, and the actions to be taken in the event of such a
    failure,

  - [(xii)]{.lawlabel} the factors to be taken into account in the
    determination of the decision height or alert height,

  - [(xiii)]{.lawlabel} the effect of aircraft malfunctions, including
    engine failure, on auto-throttle and auto-pilot performance,

  - [(xiv)]{.lawlabel} the procedures to be followed and the precautions
    to be taken while taxiing in reduced visibility, and

  - [(xv)]{.lawlabel} the standard operating procedures to be followed
    by flight crew members in normal, abnormal and emergency conditions;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} every flight crew member has received, in respect of
  CAT II and CAT III precision approaches, training on a synthetic
  flight training device that includes the following elements:

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} two approaches, at least one of which is in an
    engine-out configuration if the aircraft is certified under Part V
    to perform in that configuration,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a missed approach from the lowest minima specified
    in the special authorization, or a rejected landing, as applicable,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} an automatic landing or a manual landing from one
    of the approaches, as applicable, at the maximum crosswind
    authorized for the aircraft, and

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} for CAT III approaches based on the use of a
    fail-passive rollout control system, a manual rollout using visual
    references or a combination of visual and instrument references;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} every flight crew member has received, in respect of
  CAT II and CAT III precision approaches, training on a synthetic
  flight training device for which the validity period has not expired
  that includes the following elements:

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} one precision approach resulting in a landing, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a missed approach from the lowest minima specified
    in the special authorization, or a rejected landing, as applicable;
    and

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} every flight crew member has demonstrated to the
  private operator the ability to operate the aircraft in accordance
  with this section.

::: HistoricalNote

##### [Instrument Procedures --- Restricted Canada Air Pilot]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995126 .Subheading}

**[[604.52]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.52 .sectionLabel}** No person shall,
in an aircraft operated by a private operator, conduct an instrument
procedure that is specified in the Restricted Canada Air Pilot for an
aerodrome unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the private operator is authorized to do so under a
  special authorization;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person conducts the procedure in accordance with
  the requirements set out in the Restricted Canada Air Pilot in respect
  of the procedure; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} every flight crew member has received the training
  necessary to mitigate the risks or hazards associated with that
  procedure with respect to the safety of the aircraft, persons or
  property, and the validity period for that training has not expired.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [CMNPS and RNPC Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995133 .Subheading}

**[[604.53]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.53 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
file a flight plan indicating that an aircraft operated by a private
operator can be operated in accordance with Canadian minimum navigation
performance specifications (CMNPS) or required navigation performance
capability (RNPC) unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the private operator is authorized under a special
  authorization to operate the aircraft in accordance with CMNPS or
  RNPC;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} every flight crew member has received CMNPS or RNPC
  training, for which the validity period has not expired, in

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} normal operating procedures, including long-range
    navigation system pre-flight data entry and periodic cross-checking
    of the system position display against the aircraft position,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the method of monitoring and cross-checking the
    long-range navigation system that is coupled to the auto-pilot,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken in the event of a
    discrepancy among long-range navigation systems, and the method of
    determining which is the most accurate or reliable system,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} contingency procedures,

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken in the event of a failure
    of one or more long-range navigation systems,

  - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} the procedure for manually updating long-range
    navigation systems,

  - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} airborne emergency procedures, including
    realignment, if applicable,

  - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} the procedure for regaining track after a
    deliberate or accidental deviation from the cleared track, and

  - [(ix)]{.lawlabel} RNAV systems; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is equipped with at least two
  independent long-range navigation systems or is operated as follows:

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft equipped only with the
    radio navigation equipment referred to in paragraph 605.18(j), the
    aircraft is operated only on high level airways, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft equipped with at least
    two independent navigation systems, one of which is a long-range
    navigation system, the aircraft is operated only in RNPC airspace

    - [(A)]{.lawlabel} on high level fixed RNAV routes,

    - [(B)]{.lawlabel} on direct routes that begin and end within the
      reception range of ground-based navigation aids, or

    - [(C)]{.lawlabel} on high level airways.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18

  ajax-after="1126323-1130994.html"}

##### [RNPC Requirements --- High Level Fixed RNAV Routes]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995154 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[SOR/2019-122, s. 8(F)\]
:::

**[[604.54]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.54 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
file a flight plan indicating that an aircraft operated by a private
operator can be operated on a high level fixed RNAV route in accordance
with required navigation performance capability (RNPC) unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the private operator is authorized under a special
  authorization to operate the aircraft in accordance with RNPC;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} every flight crew member has received RNPC training,
  for which the validity period has not expired, in

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} normal operating procedures, including navigation
    system pre-flight data entry and periodic cross-checking of the
    system position display against the aircraft position,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the method of monitoring and cross-checking the
    navigation system that is coupled to the auto-pilot,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken in the event of a
    discrepancy among navigation systems, and the method of determining
    which is the most accurate or reliable system,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} contingency procedures,

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken in the event of a failure
    of one or more navigation systems,

  - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} the procedure for manually updating navigation
    systems,

  - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} airborne emergency procedures, including
    realignment, if applicable,

  - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} the procedure for regaining track after a
    deliberate or accidental deviation from the cleared track, and

  - [(ix)]{.lawlabel} RNAV systems; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is equipped with at least two
  independent navigation systems, one of which is a long-range
  navigation system.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [NAT-MNPS Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995170 .Subheading}

- **[[604.55]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.55
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall file a flight plan
  indicating that an aircraft operated by a private operator can be
  operated in accordance with North Atlantic minimum navigation
  performance specifications (NAT-MNPS) unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the private operator is authorized under a special
    authorization to operate the aircraft in accordance with NAT-MNPS;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} every flight crew member has received NAT-MNPS
    training, for which the validity period has not expired, in

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} normal operating procedures, including long-range
      navigation system pre-flight data entry and periodic
      cross-checking of the system position display against the aircraft
      position,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the method of monitoring and cross-checking the
      long-range navigation system that is coupled to the auto-pilot,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken in the event of a
      discrepancy among long-range navigation systems, and the method of
      determining which is the most accurate or reliable system,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} contingency procedures,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken in the event of a failure
      of one or more long-range navigation systems,

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} the procedure for manually updating long-range
      navigation systems,

    - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} airborne emergency procedures, including
      realignment, if applicable,

    - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} the procedure for regaining track after a
      deliberate or accidental deviation from the cleared track, and

    - [(ix)]{.lawlabel} RNAV systems; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsections (2) and (4), the aircraft is
    equipped with at least two independent long-range navigation
    systems.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate, in NAT-MNPS airspace, an
  aircraft operated by a private operator that is equipped with only one
  long-range navigation system, or that has only one functioning
  long-range navigation system, except on routes that are specified by
  the civil aviation authority of a contracting state as routes for
  aircraft equipped with only one long-range navigation system.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the long-range navigation system referred to in
  subsection (2) is a GNSS receiver, it may be used if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a Canadian Technical Standard Order (CAN-TSO)
    design approval has been issued in respect of the GNSS receiver; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the GNSS receiver meets the performance
    requirements of Technical Standard Order TSO-C196a, Airborne
    Supplemental Navigation Sensors for Global Positioning System
    Equipment Using Aircraft-Based Augmentation, published by the
    Federal Aviation Administration of the United States.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate, in NAT-MNPS airspace, an
  aircraft operated by a private operator that is equipped only with
  short-range navigation equipment (VOR, DME, ADF), except on routes G3
  or G11.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [RVSM Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995192 .Subheading}

**[[604.56]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.56 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
file a flight plan indicating that an aircraft operated by a private
operator can be operated in accordance with reduced vertical separation
minima (RVSM) unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the private operator is authorized under a special
  authorization to operate the aircraft in accordance with RVSM;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} every flight crew member has received RVSM training,
  for which the validity period has not expired, in

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the floor, ceiling and horizontal boundaries of
    RVSM airspace,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} rules on the exclusion of non-RVSM-compliant
    aircraft from the airspace,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the procedures to be followed by flight crew
    members with respect to

    - [(A)]{.lawlabel} pre-flight and in-flight altimeter checks,

    - [(B)]{.lawlabel} use of the automatic altitude control system,

    - [(C)]{.lawlabel} items on the minimum equipment list,

    - [(D)]{.lawlabel} in-flight contingencies,

    - [(E)]{.lawlabel} weather deviation procedures,

    - [(F)]{.lawlabel} track offset procedures for wake turbulence,

    - [(G)]{.lawlabel} inconsequential collision-avoidance systems
      alerts, and

    - [(H)]{.lawlabel} pilot level-off call,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} procedures relating to non-RVSM-compliant aircraft
    required to carry out ferry flights, humanitarian flights or
    delivery flights, and

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the use of an Airborne Collision Avoidance System
    (ACAS) and a Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (TCAS);

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft meets the eligibility requirements set
  out in section 624.56 of Standard 624 --- RVSM Eligibility
  Requirements, with respect to aircraft performance and aircraft
  equipment; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the private operator meets the aircraft continued
  airworthiness maintenance requirements set out in section 624.56 of
  Standard 624 --- RVSM Eligibility Requirements.

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2025-26, s. 25\]]{.Repealed}

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18

  ajax-after="1511721-1516267.html"}
:::

##### [RNP 10 Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995216 .Subheading}

**[[604.57]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.57 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
file a flight plan indicating that an aircraft operated by a private
operator can be operated in accordance with required navigation
performance 10 (RNP 10) requirements unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the private operator is authorized under a special
  authorization to operate the aircraft in accordance with RNP 10
  requirements;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} every flight crew member has received RNP 10
  training, for which the validity period has not expired, in

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} flight planning requirements,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} navigation performance requirements,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} enroute procedures, and

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} contingency procedures;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft meets one of the following eligibility
  requirements:

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft flight manual or the pilot operating
    handbook, or any equivalent document provided by the manufacturer of
    the avionics equipment or by the aircraft manufacturer, specifies
    that the aircraft can be operated in accordance with RNP 10
    requirements,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft can be operated in accordance with
    another navigation standard with performance criteria that are
    equivalent to RNP 10 requirements, or

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the private operator has demonstrated to the
    Minister, using one of the data collection methods set out in
    section 1.3.3.1.4.2 of Chapter 1 of Part B of Volume II of the PBN
    Manual, that the aircraft meets the navigational accuracy
    requirements for RNP 10;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is equipped with the navigation
  equipment referred to in sections 1.3.4 and 1.3.6.1 of Chapter 1 of
  Part B of Volume II of the PBN Manual;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the equipment referred to in paragraph (d) meets the
  standards, criteria and performance requirements set out in sections
  1.3.4.1, 1.3.4.2, 1.3.6.1 and 1.3.11 of Chapter 1 of Part B of Volume
  II of the PBN Manual; and

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the private operator applies the processes, practices
  and procedures relating to the duties and practices set out in
  sections 1.3.7, 1.3.8 and 1.3.9.2 to 1.3.9.9 of Chapter 1 of Part B of
  Volume II of the PBN Manual.

::: HistoricalNote

  ajax-after="1126327-1130997.html"}
:::

##### [RNP 4 Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995233 .Subheading}

**[[604.58]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.58 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
file a flight plan indicating that an aircraft operated by a private
operator can be operated in accordance with required navigation
performance 4 (RNP 4) requirements unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the private operator is authorized under a special
  authorization to operate the aircraft in accordance with RNP 4
  requirements;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} every flight crew member has received the training
  referred to in paragraph 604.60(b), and the validity period for that
  training has not expired;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft meets one of the following eligibility
  requirements:

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft flight manual or the pilot operating
    handbook, or any equivalent document provided by the manufacturer of
    the avionics equipment or by the aircraft manufacturer, specifies
    that the aircraft can be operated in accordance with RNP 4
    requirements,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft can be operated in accordance with
    another navigation standard with performance criteria that are
    equivalent to RNP 4 requirements, or

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the private operator has demonstrated to the
    Minister that the aircraft meets the navigational accuracy
    requirements for RNP 4;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is equipped with the navigation
  equipment referred to in sections 1.3.3.1 and 1.3.3.2 of Chapter 1 of
  Part C of Volume II of the PBN Manual;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the equipment referred to in paragraph (d) meets the
  standards, criteria and functional requirements set out in sections
  1.3.3.4 to 1.3.3.7 of Chapter 1 of Part C of Volume II of the PBN
  Manual; and

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the private operator applies the processes, practices
  and procedures relating to the duties and practices set out in
  sections 1.3.4.2.1 to 1.3.4.4.4 and 1.3.6 of Chapter 1 of Part C of
  Volume II of the PBN Manual.

##### [RNAV 5 Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995246 .Subheading}

**[[604.59]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.59 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
file a flight plan indicating that an aircraft operated by a private
operator can be operated in accordance with area navigation 5 (RNAV 5)
requirements unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the private operator is authorized under a special
  authorization to operate the aircraft in accordance with RNAV 5
  requirements;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} every flight crew member has received the training
  referred to in paragraph 604.60(b) and the validity period for that
  training has not expired;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft meets one of the following eligibility
  requirements:

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft flight manual or the pilot operating
    handbook, or any equivalent document provided by the manufacturer of
    the avionics equipment or by the aircraft manufacturer, specifies
    that the aircraft can be operated in accordance with RNAV 5
    requirements,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft can be operated in accordance with
    another navigation standard with performance criteria that are
    equivalent to RNAV 5 requirements, or

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the private operator has demonstrated to the
    Minister that the aircraft meets the navigational accuracy
    requirements for RNAV 5;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is equipped with at least one of the
  position sensors referred to in section 2.3.3 of Chapter 2 of Part B
  of Volume II of the PBN Manual;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the position sensors referred to in paragraph (d)
  meet the performance requirements, criteria and functional
  requirements set out in sections 2.3.3.1 to 2.3.3.3 of Chapter 2 of
  Part B of Volume II of the PBN Manual; and

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the private operator applies the processes, practices
  and procedures relating to the duties and practices set out in section
  2.3.4 of Chapter 2 of Part B of Volume II of the PBN Manual.

##### [RNAV 1 and RNAV 2 Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995259 .Subheading}

**[[604.60]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.60 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
file a flight plan indicating that an aircraft operated by a private
operator can be operated in accordance with area navigation 1 (RNAV 1)
or area navigation 2 (RNAV 2) requirements unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the private operator is authorized under a special
  authorization to operate the aircraft in accordance with RNAV 1 or
  RNAV 2 requirements;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} every flight crew member has received RNAV 1 or RNAV
  2 training, for which the validity period has not expired, in

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} pre-flight procedures for initialization, loading
    and verification of the area navigation system,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the normal operation of the area navigation
    system,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the procedure for manually updating the position
    of the area navigation system,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the method of monitoring and cross-checking the
    area navigation system,

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the operation of the area navigation system in a
    compass unreliability area,

  - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} malfunction procedures,

  - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} terminal area procedures,

  - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} waypoint symbology, plotting procedures and
    record-keeping duties and practices,

  - [(ix)]{.lawlabel} timekeeping procedures,

  - [(x)]{.lawlabel} post-flight performance checks,

  - [(xi)]{.lawlabel} flight planning,

  - [(xii)]{.lawlabel} navigation performance requirements,

  - [(xiii)]{.lawlabel} enroute procedures, and

  - [(xiv)]{.lawlabel} contingency procedures;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft meets one of the following eligibility
  requirements:

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft can be operated in accordance with
    precision area navigation (P-RNAV) requirements based on GNSS
    capability under an authorization issued by the competent authority
    of a contracting state,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft can be operated in accordance with
    area navigation (RNAV) requirements based on DME/DME or DME/DME/IRU
    capability under an authorization issued by the Federal Aviation
    Administration of the United States, or

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft flight manual or the pilot operating
    handbook, or any equivalent document provided by the manufacturer of
    the avionics equipment or by the aircraft manufacturer, specifies
    that the aircraft can be operated in accordance with RNAV 1 or RNAV
    2 requirements;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is equipped with at least one of the
  pieces of equipment referred to in section 3.3.3 of Chapter 3 of Part
  B of Volume II of the PBN Manual;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the equipment referred to in paragraph (d) meets the
  performance requirements, criteria and functional requirements set out
  in sections 3.3.3.1 to 3.3.3.2.1.1 and 3.3.3.2.1.3 to 3.3.3.3 of
  Chapter 3 of Part B of Volume II of the PBN Manual;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} every flight crew member has demonstrated to the
  Minister the ability to operate the aircraft in accordance with this
  section; and

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the private operator applies the processes, practices
  and procedures relating to the duties and practices set out in
  sections 3.3.3.2.1.2, 3.3.4.2 to 3.3.4.6 and 3.3.6 of Chapter 3 of
  Part B of Volume II of the PBN Manual.
