**\[604.61 to 604.73 reserved\]**

##### [Other Activities Approved by the Minister]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995288 .Subheading}

- **[[604.74]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.74
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall establish
  requirements in respect of an activity that is not set out in sections
  604.48 to 604.60 and in respect of which a special authorization may
  be issued if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the activity is subject to

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} operational and technical requirements
      established by ICAO or by the civil aviation authority of a
      foreign state, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a submission to the Minister, by a private
      operator, an air operator or a third party, that establishes
      operational and technical requirements and risk mitigation
      measures based on an analysis of aviation-safety-related hazards;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case referred to in subparagraph (a)(i), the
    operational and technical requirements are necessary for the conduct
    of flights abroad or in Canada by private operators, and those
    flights can be conducted in a safe manner; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case referred to in subparagraph (a)(ii),
    the operational and technical requirements and risk mitigation
    measures ensure the safety of the flights conducted by private
    operators and will not have an adverse effect on aviation safety.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister establishes requirements in respect
  of an activity referred to in subsection (1), no person shall, in an
  aircraft operated by a private operator, carry out the activity unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the private operator is authorized to carry out the
    activity under a special authorization;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} every flight crew member has received, if
    applicable, the training specified by the Minister under
    subsection (3) in respect of the activity, and the validity period
    for that training has not expired; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} every flight crew member has demonstrated to the
    Minister the ability to carry out the activity in accordance with
    the operational and technical requirements referred to in
    subparagraph (1)(a)(i) or (ii), as applicable, and to take the
    measures that are necessary to manage or mitigate the risks
    associated with that activity.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall specify training in respect of an
  activity referred to in subsection (1) taking into account

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any training that is recommended by the civil
    aviation authority of a foreign state or by ICAO in respect of the
    activity;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the risks and hazards associated with the activity
    with respect to the safety of the aircraft, persons or property; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the level of safety required by the activity.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

#### [Division V --- Flight Operations --- Passengers]{.HTitleText3} {#h-995307 .Subheading}

**[[604.81]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.81 .sectionLabel}** \[Reserved,
SOR/2015-127, s. 11\]

##### [Cabin Safety]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995309 .Subheading}

- **[[604.82]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.82
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off
  in an aircraft that is operated by a private operator and that has
  passengers on board, move the aircraft on the surface or direct that
  the aircraft be moved unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} safety belts are adjusted and fastened in
    accordance with paragraph 605.26(1)(a), infants are held in
    accordance with paragraph 605.26(1)(b), and persons using child
    restraint systems are secured in accordance with paragraph
    605.26(1)(c);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsection (5), seat backs are secured
    in the upright position;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} chair tables are stowed;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} carry-on baggage is stowed; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} no seat located at an emergency exit is occupied by
    a passenger --- including a passenger who has not been informed as
    to how that exit operates --- whose presence in that seat could
    adversely affect the safety of passengers or crew members during an
    evacuation.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a landing in an aircraft
  operated by a private operator unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} passengers have been directed to

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} adjust and fasten their safety belts in
      accordance with paragraph 605.26(1)(a), hold infants in accordance
      with paragraph 605.26(1)(b), and secure persons using child
      restraint systems in accordance with paragraph 605.26(1)(c),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsection (5), secure their seat
      backs in the upright position,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} stow their chair tables, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} stow their carry-on baggage; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if a seat located at an emergency exit is occupied
    by a passenger whose presence in that seat could adversely affect
    the safety of passengers or crew members during an evacuation, the
    passenger has been directed to move to another seat.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft operated by a
  private operator shall, in the event of an emergency and if time and
  circumstances permit,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} direct passengers to

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} adjust and fasten their safety belts in
      accordance with paragraph 605.26(1)(a), hold infants in accordance
      with paragraph 605.26(1)(b), and secure persons using child
      restraint systems in accordance with paragraph 605.26(1)(c),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsection (5), secure their seat
      backs in the upright position,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} stow their chair tables,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} stow their carry-on baggage,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} review the safety features card and assume the
      brace position until the aircraft stops moving, and

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} in the event of an emergency over water, don
      their life preservers; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if a seat located at an emergency exit is occupied
    by a passenger whose presence in that seat could adversely affect
    the safety of passengers or crew members during an evacuation,
    direct the passenger to move to another seat.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft operated by a
  private operator shall, if the "fasten safety belt" sign is turned on
  during the flight, direct passengers to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} adjust and fasten their safety belts in accordance
    with paragraph 605.26(1)(a), hold infants in accordance with
    paragraph 605.26(1)(b), and secure persons using child restraint
    systems in accordance with paragraph 605.26(1)(c); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} stow their carry-on baggage.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The seat of a passenger who is certified by a
  physician as unable to sit upright may remain in the reclining
  position during movement on the surface, take-off and landing if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the passenger is not seated in a location that
    would restrict the evacuation of the aircraft;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the passenger is not seated in a row that is next
    to or immediately in front of an emergency exit; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the seat immediately behind the passenger's seat is
    vacant.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Fuelling with Passengers on Board]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995342 .Subheading}

- **[[604.83]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.83
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person operating an aircraft
  operated by a private operator shall permit the fuelling of the
  aircraft while passengers are on board or are embarking or
  disembarking, unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in order for persons on board the aircraft to be
    notified promptly of a situation that could threaten their safety,
    two-way communication is maintained between the ground personnel
    supervising the fuelling and a person on board the aircraft who has
    received training in emergency evacuation procedures for that
    aircraft type;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} no ground power generator or other electrical
    ground power supply is being connected to or disconnected from the
    aircraft;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} no combustion heater installed on the aircraft is
    being used;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} every combustion heater used in the vicinity of the
    aircraft has a marking, applied by the manufacturer, indicating that
    the heater is manufactured to Canadian Standards Association (CSA)
    or Underwriters Laboratories of Canada (ULC) standards;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} no high-energy-emitting equipment, including
    high-frequency radios and airborne weather radar, is being operated
    unless the aircraft flight manual contains procedures for its use
    during fuelling and those procedures are followed;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} no aircraft battery is being removed or being
    installed;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} no external battery charger is being operated or is
    being connected to or disconnected from an aircraft battery;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} no auxiliary power unit having an efflux that
    discharges into the fuelling safety zone is started after filler
    caps are removed or fuelling connections are made;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} no auxiliary power unit that is stopped is
    restarted until the flow of fuel has ceased, unless the aircraft
    flight manual establishes procedures for restarting the unit during
    fuelling and those procedures are followed;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} no tool that is likely to produce a spark or
    electric arc is being used;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} no photographic equipment is being used within the
    fuelling safety zone;

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} the fuelling is suspended if there is a lightning
    discharge within eight kilometres of the aerodrome;

  - [(m)]{.lawlabel} the fuelling is carried out in accordance with the
    aircraft manufacturer's instructions;

  - [(n)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft emergency lighting system, if any, is
    armed or on;

  - [(o)]{.lawlabel} "no smoking" signs, if any, on board the aircraft
    are illuminated;

  - [(p)]{.lawlabel} no passenger is smoking or otherwise producing a
    source of ignition;

  - [(q)]{.lawlabel} two exits, one of which is the door through which
    passengers embarked, are free of obstruction and are available for
    immediate use by passengers and crew members in the event of an
    evacuation;

  - [(r)]{.lawlabel} the escape route from each of the exits referred to
    in paragraph (q) is free of obstruction and is available for
    immediate use by passengers and crew members in the event of an
    evacuation;

  - [(s)]{.lawlabel} a person who is authorized by the private operator
    to suspend fuelling is on board the aircraft and is ready to direct
    the suspension of fuelling if a requirement of this subsection
    ceases to be met;

  - [(t)]{.lawlabel} a means of evacuation is in place at the door used
    for the embarkation or disembarkation of passengers, is free of
    obstruction and is available for immediate use by passengers and
    crew members;

  - [(u)]{.lawlabel} the person on board the aircraft who has received
    the training referred to in paragraph (a) is ready to initiate and
    oversee an evacuation and is at or near the door referred to in
    paragraph (v); and

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the embarkation door is open, unless

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a crew member determines that, for climatic
      reasons, it is desirable to close it,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a crew member is on board the aircraft, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the door

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} opens inward or can be fully opened to the
        exterior without the need to reposition the loading stairs or
        stand,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} is latched, if that is necessary in order to
        keep it closed, and

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} is not locked.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The person who is authorized by the private operator
  to suspend fuelling shall direct the suspension of fuelling if a
  requirement of subsection (1) ceases to be met.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), [[fuelling safety
  zone]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an area that extends three metres (10
  feet) radially from the filling and venting points on the aircraft and
  from the fuelling equipment.

##### [Fuelling with Passengers on Board and an Engine Running]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995377 .Subheading}

- **[[604.84]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.84
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite section 602.09, a person
  operating an aircraft operated by a private operator may permit the
  fuelling of the aircraft while an engine used for the propulsion of
  the aircraft is running and passengers are on board or are embarking
  or disembarking, if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the requirements set out in subsection 604.83(1)
    are met;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft flight manual indicates that the
    engine that is running may be used as an auxiliary power unit; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the engine that is running has a propeller brake
    and that brake is set.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The person who is authorized by the private operator
  to suspend fuelling shall direct the suspension of fuelling if a
  requirement of subsection (1) ceases to be met.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Briefing of Passengers]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995386 .Subheading}

- **[[604.85]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.85
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite section 602.89, no person
  shall conduct a take-off in an aircraft operated by a private operator
  unless passengers are given a safety briefing --- orally by a crew
  member, or by audio or audiovisual means --- that contains the
  following information:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} when and where carry-on baggage is to be stowed;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} when and how to fasten, adjust and release safety
    belts and, if any, shoulder harnesses;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} when seat backs are to be secured in the upright
    position and chair tables are to be stowed;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the location of emergency exits and, in the case of
    a passenger seated next to such an exit, how that exit operates;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the requirement to comply with the instructions
    given by crew members and with the "fasten safety belt" and "no
    smoking" signs, and the location of those signs;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the location and operation of the passenger oxygen
    system, if any, including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be performed by a passenger in
      order to

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} obtain a mask,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} activate the flow of oxygen, and

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} don and secure the mask, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the recommendation that a passenger don and
      secure the passenger's own mask before assisting another passenger
      with his or her mask;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the use of life preservers, including how to remove
    them from their packaging, how to don them and when to inflate them;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} when and where smoking is prohibited;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the location of the emergency equipment required
    under sections 602.62, 602.63, 604.116 and 604.117, and how to
    access that equipment;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} the portable electronic devices that may be used,
    and when they may be used; and

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} the location and purpose of the safety features
    card.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), a person may conduct a
  take-off in an aircraft operated by a private operator without a
  safety briefing being given to the passengers if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the flight is the second or subsequent flight in a
    series of flights;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} no additional passengers have embarked on board the
    aircraft; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a crew member has verified that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} carry-on baggage is stowed,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} safety belts and, if any, shoulder harnesses are
      properly adjusted and securely fastened,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} seat backs are secured in the upright position,
      and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} chair tables are stowed.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), a person may conduct a
  take-off in an aircraft operated by a private operator without a
  safety briefing being given to the passengers if each passenger on
  board the aircraft has, within the 12 months preceding the date of the
  take-off, received the information referred to in subsection (1) and
  training in the performance of the following actions:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} fastening, adjusting and releasing safety belts
    and, if any, shoulder harnesses;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} operating each type of floor-level exit and window
    emergency exit;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} identifying the location of the passenger oxygen
    system, if any, and performing the actions necessary in order to

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} obtain a mask,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} activate the flow of oxygen, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} don and secure the mask;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} identifying the location of life preservers, if
    any, removing them from their packaging, donning them and inflating
    them; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} identifying the location of the emergency equipment
    required by sections 602.62, 602.63, 604.116 and 604.117 and
    accessing that equipment.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} A private operator shall record the name of every
  passenger who receives the training referred to in subsection (3) and
  the date on which the training is received. The private operator shall
  retain the record for two years after the day on which the most recent
  entry was made.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} If the safety briefing referred to in subsection (1)
  is insufficient for a passenger because of that passenger's physical,
  sensory or comprehension limitations or because the passenger is
  responsible for another person on board the aircraft, the passenger
  shall, subject to subsection (6), be given a safety briefing that
  consists of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} communication of the elements of the safety
    briefing referred to in subsection (1) that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the passenger is not able to receive either
      during that briefing or by referring to the safety features card,
      and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} are necessary for the safety of the persons on
      board the aircraft;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} communication of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the most appropriate brace position for the
      passenger, given the passenger's condition, injury or stature and
      the orientation and pitch of his or her seat, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where the passenger's service animal, if any, is
      to be located;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a mobility-impaired passenger who
    would require assistance in order to move to an exit in the event of
    an emergency, communication of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the most appropriate exit for the passenger,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the assistance that the passenger would require
      to reach that exit,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the most appropriate means of providing that
      assistance,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the most appropriate route to that exit, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the most appropriate time to begin to move to
      that exit;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a visually impaired passenger,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a tactile familiarization with

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} the equipment that the passenger may be
        required to use in the event of an emergency, and

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} if requested, the exits, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} communication of

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} where the passenger's cane, if any, is to be
        stored,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} the number of rows of seats separating the
        passenger's seat from the closest exit and from the alternate
        exit, and

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} the features of those exits;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a passenger who is responsible for
    another person on board the aircraft, communication of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} if the passenger is responsible for an infant,

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} the requirement to fasten the passenger's
        safety belt and, if any, the passenger's shoulder harness and
        not to secure the infant in that safety belt or shoulder
        harness,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} how to hold the infant during take-off and
        landing,

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} how to use the child restraint system, if any,

      - [(D)]{.lawlabel} how to place and secure the oxygen mask on the
        infant's face,

      - [(E)]{.lawlabel} the most appropriate brace position for the
        passenger, and

      - [(F)]{.lawlabel} the location of the infant's life preserver,
        how to remove it from its location and its packaging, how to
        assist the infant with donning it and when to inflate it, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if the passenger is responsible for a person,
      other than an infant,

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} how to assist that person with donning and
        securing his or her oxygen mask, and

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} how to use that person's personal restraint
        system, if any, on board the aircraft; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an unaccompanied minor,
    communication of the need to pay close attention to the safety
    briefing.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} A passenger may decline the safety briefing referred
  to in subsection (5).

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} No person shall permit passengers to disembark from
  an aircraft operated by a private operator unless the passengers are
  given a safety briefing --- orally by a crew member, or by audio or
  audiovisual means --- that contains the following information:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the safest route for passengers to take in order to
    move away from the aircraft; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the hazards, if any, associated with the aircraft,
    including the location of Pitot tubes, propellers, rotors and engine
    intakes.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
- [SOR/2019-122, s. 14](#1126349-1131003){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126349-1131003.html"}
:::

##### [Safety Features Card]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995462 .Subheading}

- **[[604.86]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.86
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), a private
  operator shall, before passengers on board an aircraft are given the
  safety briefing referred to in subsection 604.85(1), provide each
  passenger at his or her seat with a safety features card that shows
  the aircraft type and that contains safety information only in respect
  of the aircraft, including

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft configured for 19 or
    fewer passenger seats,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} when and how to fasten, adjust and release safety
      belts and, if any, shoulder harnesses,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the passenger brace position

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} for each type of seat and passenger restraint
        system, and

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} for a passenger who is holding an infant, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the location, operation and use of each
      emergency exit, including whether it is unusable in a ditching
      because of the aircraft configuration,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the location and operation of the passenger
      oxygen system, if any, including

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} a description of the masks and their use,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be performed by a passenger in
        order to

        - [(I)]{.lawlabel} obtain a mask,

        - [(II)]{.lawlabel} activate the flow of oxygen, and

        - [(III)]{.lawlabel} don and secure the mask, and

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} the recommendation that a passenger don and
        secure the passenger's own mask before assisting another
        passenger with his or her mask,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the location of life preservers, how they are to
      be removed from their packaging, how they are to be donned by
      adults, by children aged two years or older and by infants, and
      when they are to be inflated,

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} when and where smoking is prohibited, and

    - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} the location, removal and use of flotation
      devices and, if any, life rafts; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft configured for more than
    19 passenger seats,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the information set out in subparagraphs (a)(i)
      to (vii),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} when and where carry-on baggage is to be stowed,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the positioning of seats, securing of seat
      backs in the upright position and stowage of chair tables for
      take-off and landing,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the form, function, colour and location of the
      floor proximity emergency escape path markings, if any,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the safest route for passengers to take in order
      to move away from the aircraft in the event of an emergency, and

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} the attitude of the aircraft while floating, as
      determined by the aircraft manufacturer.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a flight attendant is not required on board an
  aircraft, the safety features card referred to in subsection (1) shall
  also contain the information on the location of the emergency
  equipment required under sections 604.116, 604.117 and 604.119 and how
  to access that equipment.

  ajax-after="1126352-1131005.html"}
:::

#### [Division VI --- Flight Time and Flight Duty Period]{.HTitleText3} {#h-995492 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2018-269, s. 18

\]
:::

##### [Flight Time Limits]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995495 .Subheading}

- **[[604.98]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.98
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No private operator shall assign
  flight time to a flight crew member, and no flight crew member shall
  accept such an assignment, if the flight crew member's total flight
  time in all flights conducted under this Subpart, Part IV or Part VII
  would, as a result, exceed

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 1,200 hours in a period of 12 consecutive months;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 300 hours in a period of 90 consecutive days;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} 120 hours in a period of 30 consecutive days; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} 8 hours in a period of 24 consecutive hours, if the
    assignment is for a single-pilot IFR flight.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a flight crew's flight duty period is extended
  under section 604.101, each flight crew member accumulates, for the
  purposes of subsection (1), the total flight time for the flight or
  the total flight time for the series of flights, as the case may be.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
- SOR/2018-269, s. 18
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-604.98-20140529.html "Link to previous version of section 604.98"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Flight Duty Period Limits and Rest Periods]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995505 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2018-269, s. 18

\]
:::

- **[[604.99]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.99
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to sections 604.100 to
  604.102, no private operator shall assign flight duty period to a
  flight crew member, and no flight crew member shall accept such an
  assignment, if the flight crew member's flight duty period would, as a
  result, exceed

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 14 consecutive hours in a period of 24 consecutive
    hours; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 15 consecutive hours in a period of 24 consecutive
    hours, if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the flight crew member's total flight duty period
      in the previous 30 consecutive days does not exceed 70 hours, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the rest period before the flight is at least 24
      hours.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A private operator shall ensure that, prior to
  reporting for flight duty, a flight crew member is provided with the
  minimum rest period and with any additional rest period required by
  this Division.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A flight crew member shall use the following periods
  to be adequately rested prior to reporting for flight duty:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the minimum rest period provided under subsection
    (2);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any additional rest period required by this
    Division; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any period with no assigned duties provided under
    section 604.104.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
- SOR/2018-269, s. 18
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-604.99-20140529.html "Link to previous version of section 604.99"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Split Flight Duty Period]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995521 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2018-269, s. 18

\]
:::

**[[604.100]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.100 .sectionLabel}** Flight duty
period may be extended by one half of the length of the rest period, to
a maximum of four hours, if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} before a flight crew member reports for the first
  flight or reports as a flight crew member on standby, as the case may
  be, the private operator provides the flight crew member with notice
  of the extension of the flight duty period;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the private operator provides the flight crew member
  with a rest period of at least four consecutive hours in suitable
  accommodation; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the flight crew member's next minimum rest period is
  increased by an amount of time at least equal to the length of the
  extension of the flight duty period.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
- SOR/2018-269, ss. 8(F), 18
:::

Version](section-604.100-20140529.html "Link to previous version of section 604.100"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Extension of Flight Duty Period]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995530 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2018-269, s. 18

\]
:::

**[[604.101]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.101 .sectionLabel}** If a flight
crew is augmented by at least one flight crew member, if there is a
balanced distribution of flight deck duty time and rest periods among
the flight crew members, and if the next minimum rest period is at least
equal to the length of the preceding flight duty period, the flight
crew's flight duty period may be extended

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} to 17 hours with a maximum flight deck duty time of
  12 hours, if a flight relief facility --- seat is provided; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} to 20 hours with a maximum flight deck duty time of
  14 hours, if a flight relief facility --- bunk is provided.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
- SOR/2018-269, s. 18
:::

Version](section-604.101-20140529.html "Link to previous version of section 604.101"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Unforeseen Operational Circumstances]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995538 .Subheading}

- **[[604.102]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.102
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Flight duty period may be extended
  by up to three hours if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command, after consultation with the
    other flight crew members, considers it safe to do so;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the flight duty period is extended as a result of
    an unforeseen operational circumstance that occurs after the
    beginning of the flight duty period;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the next minimum rest period is extended by an
    amount of time that is at least equal to the length of the extension
    of the flight duty period; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command notifies the private operator
    of the unforeseen operational circumstances and of the length of the
    extension of the flight duty period.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The private operator shall retain a copy of the
  notification for five years.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
- SOR/2018-269, ss. 9, 18
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-604.102-20140529.html "Link to previous version of section 604.102"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Delayed Reporting Time]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995548 .Subheading}

**[[604.103]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.103 .sectionLabel}** When a private
operator delays a flight crew member's reporting time by more than three
hours, the flight crew member's flight duty period is considered to
start three hours after the original reporting time if the private
operator notifies the flight crew member of the delay

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} within 12 hours before the original reporting time;
  and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} at least one hour before the flight crew member
  leaves a rest facility.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
- SOR/2018-269, s. 18
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-604.103-20140529.html "Link to previous version of section 604.103"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Time with no Assigned Duties]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995554 .Subheading}

**[[604.104]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.104 .sectionLabel}** No private
operator shall assign duties to a flight crew member, and no flight crew
member shall accept those duties, unless the private operator provides
the flight crew member with one of the following periods with no
assigned duties:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} at least 36 consecutive hours in a period of seven
  consecutive days; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} at least three consecutive calendar days in a period
  of 17 consecutive days.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Rest Period --- Flight Crew Member Positioning]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995560 .Subheading}

**[[604.105]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.105 .sectionLabel}** If a flight
crew member is required by a private operator to travel for the purpose
of positioning after the completion of flight duty period, the private
operator shall provide the flight crew member with an additional rest
period that is at least equal to one half of the time spent for that
purpose that is in excess of the flight duty period referred to in
paragraphs 604.99(1)(a) and (b).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
- SOR/2018-269, s. 18
:::

Version](section-604.105-20140529.html "Link to previous version of section 604.105"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Controlled Rest on the Flight Deck]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995564 .Subheading}

- **[[604.106]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.106
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No private operator shall allow a
  flight crew member to take a controlled rest on the flight deck of an
  aircraft operated by the private operator unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the private operator has a
    controlled-rest-on-the-flight-deck program that includes the
    following elements:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} guidelines on the use of controlled rest,
      including the factors allowing or preventing its use,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the general principles relating to fatigue and
      fatigue countermeasures, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the procedures to be followed by participating
      crew members before, during and after a controlled rest; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} every participating crew member has received
    training relating to the elements of the
    controlled-rest-on-the-flight-deck program.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft operated by a
  private operator shall determine whether the flight conditions, the
  duration of the flight and the physiological condition of the crew
  members allow a controlled rest on the flight deck to be taken by a
  flight crew member.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft operated by a
  private operator shall give participating crew members a briefing that
  includes the following elements:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the order in which the periods of controlled rest
    are to be taken by the flight crew members;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the planned duration of each period of controlled
    rest;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the circumstances under which a resting flight crew
    member is to be woken;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the procedures for the transfer of flight controls
    and duties; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} flight attendant duties in relation to a controlled
    rest.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The flight crew members on board an aircraft operated
  by a private operator shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} prior to each controlled rest on the flight deck,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} participate in an operational briefing,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} carry out the transfer of duties, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} inform the flight attendants of the controlled
      rest; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} remain on the flight deck during the controlled
    rest.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The flight crew member who supervises a controlled
  rest on the flight deck of an aircraft operated by a private operator
  shall, during the controlled rest,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} perform the duties of the resting flight crew
    member;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the controlled rest is taken only
    during the cruise portion of the flight and is completed at least 30
    minutes before top of descent;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the period of controlled rest is of no
    more than 45 minutes in duration;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the resting flight crew member is awake
    for at least 15 minutes before the resumption of duties, except in
    abnormal or emergency conditions; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} after the completion of the controlled rest, give
    an operational briefing to the flight crew member who has taken the
    controlled rest.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section, [[participating
  crew member]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the resting flight crew member
  and the flight crew member who supervises the controlled rest on the
  flight deck.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
- [SOR/2019-122, s. 16(F)](#1126354-1131006){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126354-1131006.html"}
:::

#### [Division VII --- Emergency Equipment]{.HTitleText3} {#h-995595 .Subheading}

##### [Survival Equipment]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995596 .Subheading}

- **[[604.116]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.116
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aircraft
  operated by a private operator, other than an aircraft referred to in
  subsection 602.61(2), unless a survival manual is carried on board
  that contains information about how to use the survival equipment that
  is carried on board to meet the requirements of subsection 602.61(1).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aircraft operated by a
  private operator on board of which life rafts are required to be
  carried in accordance with section 602.63 unless the survival kit
  referred to in paragraph 602.63(6)(c) contains

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a life raft repair kit;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a bailing bucket and a sponge;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a whistle;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a waterproof flashlight;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a supply of potable water --- based on 500 mL per
    person and calculated using the rated capacity of the life raft ---
    or a means of desalting or distilling salt water that can provide
    500 mL of potable water per person;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a waterproof survival manual that contains
    information about how to use the survival equipment;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a first aid kit that contains antiseptic swabs,
    burn dressing compresses, bandages and motion sickness pills; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} a pyrotechnic signalling device, or an aviation
    visual distress signal that has a marking applied by the
    manufacturer indicating that the signal meets the requirements of
    CAN-TSO-C168, a signalling mirror and a dye marker for visually
    signalling distress.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (2), if there is insufficient
  space in the attached survival kit, a supplemental survival kit shall
  be stowed adjacent to each required life raft and contain

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a supply of potable water --- based on 500 mL per
    person and calculated using the rated capacity of the life raft ---
    or a means of desalting or distilling salt water that can provide
    500 mL of potable water per person; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} motion sickness pills.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
- [SOR/2020-253, s. 5](#1274648-1276832){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1274648-1276832.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-604.116-20140529.html "Link to previous version of section 604.116"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [First Aid Kits]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995611 .Subheading}

- **[[604.117]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.117
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off
  in an aircraft operated by a private operator that is configured as
  follows unless, for the purposes of paragraph 602.60(1)(h), the
  corresponding number of first aid kits is carried on board and each
  kit contains the supplies and equipment set out in the [Aviation
  Occupational Health and Safety
  Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-2011-87):

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} configured for 0 to 50 passenger seats, one kit;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} configured for 51 to 150 passenger seats, two kits;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} configured for 151 to 250 passenger seats, three
    kits; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} configured for 251 or more passenger seats, four
    kits.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off in an aircraft
  operated by a private operator unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the first aid kits referred to in subsection (1)
    are distributed throughout the cabin and are readily available to
    crew members and passengers;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} each first aid kit is clearly identified; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if a first aid kit is stowed in a bin or
    compartment, the bin or compartment is clearly marked as containing
    a first aid kit.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
- [SOR/2020-253, s. 6](#1274650-1276838){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1274650-1276838.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-604.117-20140529.html "Link to previous version of section 604.117"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Protective Breathing Equipment]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995624 .Subheading}

- **[[604.118]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.118
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off
  in a pressurized aircraft operated by a private operator that has
  flight attendants on board unless one unit of protective breathing
  equipment with a 15-minute portable supply of breathing gas at a
  pressure-altitude of 8,000 feet is available

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at the entry into each Class A, B, E and F cargo
    compartment accessible to crew members during flight;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} at the site of each hand-held fire extinguisher
    that is located in an isolated galley;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} on the flight deck; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} at the site of each hand-held fire extinguisher
    that is required under section 604.119.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the breathing gas in the protective breathing
  equipment referred to in subsection (1) is oxygen, each unit of that
  equipment reduces by 15 minutes the crew member oxygen requirements
  specified in subsection 605.31(2).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Hand-held Fire Extinguishers]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995634 .Subheading}

**[[604.119]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.119 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
conduct a take-off in an aircraft operated by a private operator unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} hand-held fire extinguishers are available as
  follows:

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} extinguishers are distributed, in every passenger
    compartment configured as follows, in the numbers indicated:

    - [(A)]{.lawlabel} in a passenger compartment configured for fewer
      than 20 passenger seats, one extinguisher,

    - [(B)]{.lawlabel} in a passenger compartment configured for 20 to
      60 passenger seats, two extinguishers,

    - [(C)]{.lawlabel} in a passenger compartment configured for 61 to
      200 passenger seats, three extinguishers, and

    - [(D)]{.lawlabel} in a passenger compartment configured for 201 or
      more passenger seats, one additional extinguisher for each
      additional unit of 100 passenger seats,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} one extinguisher is located at the entrance to
    each Class E cargo compartment that is accessible to crew members
    during flight, and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} one extinguisher is located in each isolated
    galley; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} if a hand-held fire extinguisher is stowed in a bin
  or compartment, the bin or compartment is clearly marked as containing
  a fire extinguisher.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

**\[604.120 to 604.125 reserved\]**

#### [Division VIII --- Maintenance]{.HTitleText3} {#h-995648 .Subheading}

##### [Maintenance Manager]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995649 .Subheading}

**[[604.126]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.126 .sectionLabel}** The maintenance
manager is responsible and accountable for the maintenance control
system.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Maintenance Control System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995653 .Subheading}

**[[604.127]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.127 .sectionLabel}** A private
operator shall have, in respect of its aircraft, a maintenance control
system that includes

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a private operator who provides the
  parts and materials that will be used in the performance of
  maintenance or elementary work, procedures to ensure that only parts
  and materials that meet the requirements of Subpart 71 of Part V are
  used, including

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the details of part pooling arrangements, if any,
    that have been entered into by the private operator, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} procedures used for the inspection and storage of
    incoming parts and materials;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the private operator authorizes, for the
  performance of elementary work, the use of methods, techniques,
  practices, parts, materials, tools, equipment or test apparatuses
  referred to in paragraph 571.02(1)(b) or (c), the source of those
  methods, techniques, practices, parts, materials, tools, equipment or
  test apparatuses and a general description of the elementary work;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} procedures to ensure that the persons who perform
  maintenance, elementary work or servicing are authorized to do so
  under section 604.128;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} procedures to ensure that an aircraft is not returned
  to service unless it is

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} airworthy, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} equipped, configured and maintained for its
    intended use;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} a description of the defect reporting and control
  procedures required by section 604.129;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft service information review procedures
  required by section 604.131;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} procedures to ensure that the records referred to in
  section 604.132 are established and retained in accordance with that
  section;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} procedures to ensure that the tasks required by a
  maintenance schedule or by an airworthiness directive are completed in
  accordance with Subpart 5 of Part VI;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} procedures to ensure that the particulars relating to
  aircraft empty weight and empty centre of gravity are entered in
  accordance with the requirements of Item 2 of Schedule I to Subpart 5
  of Part VI;

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} a general description of the maintenance schedule
  required under paragraph 605.86(1)(a) and, in the case of a
  turbine-powered pressurized aeroplane or a large aeroplane, the
  approval number of the maintenance schedule approved under subsection
  605.86(2); and

- [(k)]{.lawlabel} details of the methods used to record the
  maintenance, elementary work or servicing performed and to ensure that
  any defects are recorded in the technical records that are required to
  be kept under subsection 605.92(1).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
- [SOR/2019-122, s. 17](#1126359-1131008){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126359-1131008.html"}
:::

##### [Maintenance, Elementary Work and Servicing]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995672 .Subheading}

- **[[604.128]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.128
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No private operator shall authorize
  a person to perform maintenance or elementary work on any of its
  aircraft unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} has received the training referred to in
      subsection 604.182(1), and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of elementary work, has performed
      that work at least once under the supervision of the holder of an
      aircraft maintenance engineer (AME) licence or the holder of an
      approved training organization certificate; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person is authorized to do so under a written
    agreement that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} describes the maintenance or elementary work to
      be performed, including the specific tasks and activities and the
      conditions under which they are to be performed, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} provides that the private operator is
      responsible for ensuring that the maintenance or elementary work
      is performed.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a member of the private operator's personnel
  performs servicing on any of the private operator's aircraft, the
  private operator shall ensure that the member meets the training
  requirements set out in subsection 604.182(2).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A private operator shall retain a copy of the written
  agreement referred to in paragraph (1)(b) for two years after the day
  on which the agreement comes into force.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Defect Reporting and Control Procedures]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995685 .Subheading}

**[[604.129]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.129 .sectionLabel}** A private
operator shall have procedures to ensure that

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} aircraft defects are recorded in accordance with
  subsection 605.94(1);

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} aircraft defects are rectified in accordance with the
  requirements of Subpart 5 of Part VI;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft defect that occurs three times within 15
  flights is identified and is reported as a recurring defect to the
  flight crew and maintenance personnel in order to avoid the repetition
  of unsuccessful attempts at rectification; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft defect, the rectification of which has
  been deferred, is scheduled for rectification.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Service Difficulty Reporting]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995693 .Subheading}

**[[604.130]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.130 .sectionLabel}** A private
operator shall report to the Minister, in accordance with Division IX of
Subpart 21 of Part V, any service difficulty related to the aircraft
that it operates under this Subpart.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Aircraft Service Information Review]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995697 .Subheading}

**[[604.131]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.131 .sectionLabel}** A private
operator shall have procedures to ensure that

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} it is aware of the aircraft service information that
  the holder of a design approval document produces in respect of the
  aeronautical products used by the private operator;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft service information is assessed, and the
  results of the assessment are signed and dated by the maintenance
  manager and retained for six years; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the maintenance schedule or any other procedure is,
  if necessary, amended in response to the assessment.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Personnel Records]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995704 .Subheading}

- **[[604.132]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.132
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A private operator shall have for
  its personnel a record that includes the following information:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name of any person authorized under section
    571.11 to sign a maintenance release under section 571.10; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name of any person who has performed elementary
    work in accordance with subparagraph 604.128(1)(a)(ii).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The private operator shall retain the record for two
  years after the day on which it was last updated.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

**\[604.133 to 604.138 reserved\]**

#### [Division IX --- Personnel Requirements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-995713 .Subheading}

##### [Validity Periods]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995714 .Subheading}

- **[[604.139]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.139
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) and (3),
  for the purposes of this Division and Division IV, the validity period
  of any training, any competency check or any pilot proficiency check
  expires on

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of training in the performance of the
    emergency procedures referred to in subsection 604.169(2) and in
    subparagraphs 604.179(z)(viii) and (ix), and the high altitude
    indoctrination training referred to in section 604.176, the first
    day of the thirty-seventh month after the month in which the
    training was completed;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of all other training, the first day of
    the thirteenth month after the month in which the training was
    completed; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a competency check or pilot
    proficiency check, the first day of the twenty-fifth month after the
    month in which the competency check or pilot proficiency check was
    successfully completed.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If any training, competency check or pilot
  proficiency check is renewed within the last 90 days of its validity
  period, its validity period is extended by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 36 months, in the case of training in the
    performance of the emergency procedures referred to in subsection
    604.169(2) and in subparagraphs 604.179(z)(viii) and (ix), and the
    high altitude indoctrination training referred to in section
    604.176;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 12 months, in the case of all other training; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} 24 months, in the case of a competency check or
    pilot proficiency check.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall extend the validity period of any
  training, competency check or pilot proficiency check for a period of
  not more than 60 days beginning on the day after the day on which the
  validity period expires, if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the application for extension is made during the
    validity period; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the applicant demonstrates that there has been no
    reasonable opportunity to renew the training, competency check or
    pilot proficiency check within the 90 days before the day on which
    the training, competency check or pilot proficiency check would
    otherwise expire.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Equivalencies]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995729 .Subheading}

- **[[604.140]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.140
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A person who will act as a crew
  member for a private operator, and who has received crew member
  training under the ground and flight training program of an air
  operator or under the training program of another private operator,
  may use that training to meet an equivalent training requirement set
  out in this Subpart if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the training received by the person is in respect
    of the aircraft type that the person will operate and the private
    operator's area of operation;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the validity period, if any, of that training has
    not expired; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the private operator provides the person with
    training in

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the processes, practices and procedures set out
      in the private operator's operations manual, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the private operator's emergency procedures for
      the aircraft in respect of which the person will be assigned
      duties.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who will act as a flight crew member for a
  private operator, and who has successfully completed a pilot
  proficiency check with an air operator or a competency check with
  another private operator, meets the requirements of paragraph
  604.143(1)(e) if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the pilot proficiency check or competency check was
    conducted using an aircraft of the same type that the person will
    operate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the validity period of the pilot proficiency check
    or competency check has not expired; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the private operator provides the person with
    training in respect of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the processes, practices and procedures set out
      in the private operator's operations manual,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} any differences between the equipment that is
      installed on the aircraft operated by the private operator and the
      equipment that is installed on the aircraft operated by the air
      operator or the other private operator, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} any differences between the private operator's
      operational procedures and those of the air operator or the other
      private operator.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Operations Manager Qualifications and Responsibilities]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995746 .Subheading}

- **[[604.141]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.141
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No private operator shall permit a
  person to act --- and no person shall act --- as the operations
  manager unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} holds, or has held, the licence and ratings
      required by Part IV to act as a pilot-in-command on an aircraft
      operated by the private operator, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} has acquired at least three years of supervisory
      experience with a private operator or air operator whose
      operations and activities are of a size, nature and complexity
      that correspond to the size, nature and complexity of the
      operations and activities of the private operator; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person has demonstrated to the private operator
    knowledge of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the content of the private operator's operations
      manual, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the provisions of this Subpart and of any other
      applicable laws, regulations or standards that ensure the safety
      of the private operator's operations or affect the person's
      responsibilities.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operations manager is responsible for the
  operational control of the private operator's operations and shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} coordinate the activities that affect operational
    control, including activities relating to

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} maintenance,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} crew members' schedules,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} load control, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} aircraft operation schedules;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} implement the private operator's policies and
    procedures to ensure that the private operator's operations meet the
    requirements of this Subpart;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the operations manager receives aeronautical
    information that indicates a risk to the safety of a flight, ensure
    that corrective actions are taken to manage or mitigate the risk;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} ensure the dissemination of aircraft safety
    information to the private operator's personnel; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} implement the emergency response procedures
    referred to in paragraph 604.203(1)(e).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
- [SOR/2019-122, s. 18(F)](#1126366-1131009){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126366-1131009.html"}
:::

##### [Chief Pilot Qualifications, Training and Responsibilities]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995767 .Subheading}

- **[[604.142]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.142
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No private operator shall permit a
  person to act --- and no person shall act --- as a chief pilot unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person meets the requirements of paragraphs
    604.143(1)(a), (b), (d) and (*e*) for acting as pilot-in-command on
    an aircraft operated by the private operator; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person has demonstrated to the private operator
    knowledge of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the content of the private operator's operations
      manual, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the provisions of this Subpart and of any other
      applicable laws, regulations or standards that ensure the safety
      of the private operator's operations or affect the person's
      responsibilities.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The chief pilot is responsible for the flight crew
  members involved in the private operator's operations and shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} develop standard operating procedures in respect of
    aircraft operated by the private operator;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} verify whether the aerodromes and routes for
    aircraft used by the private operator are suitable for aircraft
    operated by the private operator;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the operational requirements of the
    aerodromes and routes used by the private operator are met; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} process any flight crew member reports and take any
    necessary follow-up action.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Flight Crew Member Qualifications and Training]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995781 .Subheading}

- **[[604.143]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.143
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No private operator shall permit a
  person to act --- and no person shall act --- as a pilot-in-command or
  second-in-command unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person holds the licence, ratings and medical
    certificate required by Part IV;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a pilot-in-command,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the person has received, in respect of the
      aircraft type that the person will operate, the training set out
      in subsections 604.169(1) and 604.170(1) and, if applicable, the
      training set out in subsection 604.169(3) and sections 604.177 and
      604.178, or equivalent training that meets the requirements of
      subsection 604.140(1), as the case may be, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the validity period of the training has not
      expired;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a second-in-command,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the person has received, in respect of the
      aircraft type that the person will operate, the training set out
      in subsections 604.169(1) and 604.170(1) and, if applicable, the
      training set out in subsection 604.169(3) and section 604.177, or
      equivalent training that meets the requirements of subsection
      604.140(1), as the case may be, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the validity period of the training has not
      expired;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the person has received, in respect of the aircraft
    type that the person will operate, training in the performance of
    the emergency procedures referred to in subsection 604.169(2) or
    equivalent training that meets the requirements of subsection
    604.140(1), and the validity period of the training has not expired;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the person has successfully completed, in respect
    of the aircraft type that the person will operate, a competency
    check that meets the requirements of this section or a competency
    check or pilot proficiency check that meets the requirements of
    subsection 604.140(2), and the validity period of the competency
    check or pilot proficiency check has not expired; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} if the person is required to operate an aircraft
    above 13,000 feet ASL, the person has received the training set out
    in section 604.176 or equivalent training that meets the
    requirements of subsection 604.140(1).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who undergoes a competency check referred to
  in paragraph (1)(e)

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} shall have completed, within 30 days before the day
    on which the competency check is conducted, the training set out in
    subsection 604.170(1) or equivalent training that meets the
    requirements of subsection 604.140(1);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} shall have been recommended for the competency
    check by an instructor who provided the person with the training or
    equivalent training referred to in paragraph (a); and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} shall meet the following requirements:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the person holds the licence required by Part IV
      in respect of the aircraft that will be used for the competency
      check,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the person holds a type rating required by Part
      IV in respect of the aircraft that will be used for the competency
      check, or meets the knowledge and experience requirements set out
      in paragraph 421.40(3)(a) of Standard 421 --- Flight Crew Permits,
      Licences and Ratings, and the knowledge requirement was met within
      24 months before the day on which the competency check is
      conducted, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the person holds an instrument rating required
      by Part IV in respect of the aircraft that will be used for the
      competency check, or meets the knowledge and experience
      requirements set out in subsection 421.46(2) of Standard 421 ---
      Flight Crew Permits, Licences and Ratings, and the knowledge
      requirement was met within 24 months before the day on which the
      competency check is conducted.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The competency check referred to in paragraph (1)(e)

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} shall be based on the processes, practices and
    procedures set out in the private operator's operations manual;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} shall consist of the exercises set out in chapters
    2 or 3, as the case may be, of the standard entitled Flight Test
    Guide --- Competency Check (Private Operators), published by the
    Minister;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} shall assess the exercises referred to in
    paragraph (b) in accordance with the marking scale set out in
    section 1.3 of that standard;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} shall assess the competency as satisfactory or
    unsatisfactory in accordance with sections 1.4 and 1.5 of that
    standard; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} shall be subject to the retest procedures referred
    to in section 1.6 of that standard.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (5), the competency check
  referred to in paragraph (1)(e) shall be conducted by a person who

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} holds the licence and ratings required by Part IV
    to act as pilot-in-command of the aircraft used for the competency
    check;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} holds an instrument rating required by Part IV in
    respect of the aircraft used for the competency check;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} meets one of the following requirements:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} is a pilot examiner authorized by the Minister to
      conduct instrument rating flight tests under Part IV,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} is an approved check pilot authorized by the
      Minister to conduct a pilot proficiency check under Part VII in
      respect of the aircraft type used for the competency check, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} holds an authorization issued by the competent
      authority of a contracting state to conduct flight tests that are
      equivalent to competency checks, in which case the person shall
      have demonstrated to the private operator knowledge of the
      standard referred to in paragraph (3)(b); and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} is not the instructor who made the recommendation
    referred to in paragraph 2(b) in respect of the person undergoing
    the competency check.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The competency check referred to in paragraph (1)(e)
  may be conducted by a person who is not referred to in paragraph 4(c)
  if the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} has been assigned to conduct the competency check
    by the private operator;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements set out in paragraphs (4)(a)
    and (b);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} does not have a record of conviction for

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} an offence under section 7.3 of the Act, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} two or more offences under these Regulations not
      arising from a single occurrence;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} is at least 21 years old;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} has at least 3,000 hours of flight time in an
    aircraft of the same category as the aircraft that will be used for
    the competency check, including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} at least 2,000 hours as pilot-in-command,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} at least 500 hours in a multi-engined aircraft,
      and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} at least 500 hours of instrument time,
      including at least 100 hours as pilot-in-command; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} has successfully completed, within 24 months before
    the day on which the person conducts the competency check, training
    provided by a pilot examiner or by an approved check pilot that
    includes the following elements:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the responsibilities of a person conducting a
      competency check,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} evaluation principles,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the conduct of a competency check,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the content of the standard referred to in
      paragraph (3)(b), and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the record-keeping requirements set out in
      section 604.149.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Instructor Qualifications and Training]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995834 .Subheading}

- **[[604.144]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.144
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No private operator shall permit a
  person to act --- and no person shall act --- as a flight instructor
  or a flight simulator instructor unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a flight instructor, the person
    holds, in respect of the aircraft type used for the training, the
    licence and ratings required by Part IV or, in the case of a flight
    instructor licensed by a contracting state, a licence and ratings
    equivalent to those required by Part IV;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a flight simulator instructor, the
    person holds, or has held, in respect of the aircraft type used for
    the training, the licence and ratings required by Part IV or, in the
    case of an flight simulator instructor licensed by a contracting
    state, a licence and ratings equivalent to those required by Part
    IV;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the private operator is authorized under a
    special authorization to operate an aircraft in IFR flight, the
    person holds a valid instrument rating in respect of the aircraft
    type used for the training;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the person has received, in respect of the aircraft
    type used for the training, training that includes the elements set
    out in subsection 604.170(1), and the validity period of the
    training has not expired; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the person has demonstrated to the private operator
    knowledge of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the content of the private operator's operations
      manual, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the provisions of this Subpart that relate to
      the training of flight crew members.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No private operator shall permit a person to act ---
  and no person shall act --- as a ground instructor unless the person
  has received, before the day on which the person begins to act as
  ground instructor, training that includes the following elements:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the teaching and learning processes;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} instructional techniques; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the student-instructor relationship.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Flight Attendant Training]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995850 .Subheading}

**[[604.145]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.145 .sectionLabel}** No private
operator shall permit a person to act --- and no person shall act --- as
a flight attendant unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person has received the training set out in
  section 604.179 or equivalent training that meets the requirements of
  subsection 604.140(1), and the validity period of the training has not
  expired; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person has demonstrated to the private operator
  knowledge of

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the provisions of these Regulations and of
    standards that affect the responsibilities of a flight attendant,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} aeronautical terminology,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the physiological effects of flight, and

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the theory of flight.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Flight Dispatcher and Flight Follower Training]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995860 .Subheading}

- **[[604.146]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.146
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No private operator shall permit a
  person to act --- and no person shall act --- as a flight dispatcher
  unless the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} holds a flight dispatcher certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} has received the training set out in subsection
    604.180(1) and the validity period of the training has not expired.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No private operator shall permit a person to act ---
  and no person shall act --- as a flight follower unless the person has
  received the training set out in subsection 604.180(2) and the
  validity period of the training has not expired.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Ground and Airborne Icing Operations Training]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995868 .Subheading}

**[[604.147]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.147 .sectionLabel}** No private
operator shall permit a person to perform --- and no person shall
perform --- duties relating to ground and airborne icing operations
unless the person has received the training set out in section 604.181
and the validity period of the training has not expired.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Safety Management System Training]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995872 .Subheading}

**[[604.148]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.148 .sectionLabel}** A private
operator shall ensure that the operations manager, the maintenance
manager and all other personnel receive the training set out in section
604.183.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Training and Qualifications Records]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995876 .Subheading}

- **[[604.149]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.149
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A private operator shall have for
  its personnel a training and qualifications record that includes the
  following information:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} each person's name;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the dates on which the person received training and
    the name of the instructor who provided the training;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of the operations manager, information
    on how the operations manager has demonstrated to the private
    operator knowledge of the elements referred to in paragraph
    604.141(1)(b) and the date of that demonstration;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of the chief pilot, information on how
    the chief pilot has demonstrated to the private operator knowledge
    of the elements referred to in paragraph 604.142(1)(b) and the date
    of that demonstration;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a flight instructor, information on
    how the flight instructor has demonstrated to the private operator
    knowledge of the elements referred to in paragraph 604.144(1)(e) and
    the date of that demonstration;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a flight crew member,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the flight crew member licence number, the
      category and expiry date of the flight crew member's medical
      certificate, a list of the flight crew member's ratings and, if
      applicable, the expiry date of those ratings,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in respect of the training referred to in
      subsection 604.170(1) and sections 604.177 and 604.178,
      information indicating whether the training was completed using an
      aircraft or a flight simulation training device, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} in respect of the competency check referred to
      in paragraph 604.143(1)(e),

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} the name of the person who conducted the
        competency check and the date on which it was conducted,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} the name of the instructor who made the
        recommendation referred to in paragraph 604.143(2)(b) and the
        date on which it was made,

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} the date of each attempt by the flight crew
        member to complete a competency check and the result of each
        attempt,

      - [(D)]{.lawlabel} information indicating whether the competency
        check was conducted using an aircraft or a flight simulation
        training device, and

      - [(E)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a competency check conducted by
        the person referred to in subparagraph 604.143(4)(c)(iii),
        information indicating how the person has demonstrated to the
        private operator knowledge of the standard referred to in that
        subparagraph and the date of that demonstration,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} in respect of a pilot proficiency check
      conducted under Part VII, the name of the air operator for which
      the check was conducted and the date on which the check was
      conducted, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the dates on which the flight crew member
      demonstrated the ability to operate an aircraft in accordance with
      paragraphs 604.50(c), 604.51(f), 604.60(f) and 604.74(2)(c); and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft maintenance engineer
    (AME), the aircraft maintenance engineer licence number.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the training referred to in Divisions IV or X
  includes a written examination, the private operator shall retain a
  master copy of each examination.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The private operator shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} retain the records referred to in subsections (1)
    and (2) for two years after the day on which the records were last
    updated; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} retain the written examination referred to in
    subsection (2) for two years after the day on which the examination
    was given.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
- [SOR/2019-119, s. 37(E)](#1126778-1144248){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126778-1144248.html"}
:::
