[Previous
Version](section-604.149-20140529.html "Link to previous version of section 604.149"){.PITLink}
:::

**\[604.150 to 604.165 reserved\]**

#### [Division X --- Training Program]{.HTitleText3} {#h-995903 .Subheading}

##### [Training Program]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995904 .Subheading}

- **[[604.166]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.166
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), a private
  operator shall have a training program that covers the subject matter
  set out in Division IV and in this Division, and the competency check
  referred to in paragraph 604.143(1)(e), and that takes into account

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft types operated by the private
    operator; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the private operator's area of operation.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A private operator who is also an air operator shall
  have a training program that covers the subject matter set out in this
  Division and that takes into account

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft types operated by the private operator
    that are not specified in the air operator certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the differences, if any, between the areas in which
    operations are conducted.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Acquiring and Maintaining Competency]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995914 .Subheading}

**[[604.167]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.167 .sectionLabel}** A private
operator shall design its training program so that a person who receives
training required under this Subpart

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} will, if the person is receiving the training for the
  first time, acquire the competency necessary to perform his or her
  duties; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} will, if the person is receiving subsequent training,
  maintain the competency referred to in paragraph (a) and acquire any
  new competency necessary to perform his or her duties.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Training Program Content and Training Facilities]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995920 .Subheading}

**[[604.168]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.168 .sectionLabel}** A private
operator shall ensure that any training provided to meet the
requirements of this Subpart is

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} based on the content of the private operator's
  training program; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} provided in facilities that are equipped with the
  appropriate furnishings, audiovisual equipment and training aids.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Flight Crew Members --- Ground Instruction]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995926 .Subheading}

- **[[604.169]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.169
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The ground instruction component of
  the training program for flight crew members shall include the
  following elements:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the content of the private operator's operations
    manual;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft systems operation and limitations
    specified in the aircraft flight manual and, if the private operator
    has established an aircraft operating manual and standard operating
    procedures, those specified in that manual and in those procedures;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the operation of the aircraft equipment;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the differences, if any, between the equipment,
    operation and layout of aircraft of the same type;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the standard operating procedures, if any were
    established by the private operator;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft performance and limitations;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} weight and balance control procedures;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} aircraft servicing and ground handling;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the location and operation of emergency equipment;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken in the event of aircraft
    fire on the ground or in the air;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken in the event of a
    security-related event;

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} procedures to avoid Controlled Flight into Terrain
    (CFIT);

  - [(m)]{.lawlabel} if the flight crew members will be assigned to
    medical evacuation flights (MEDEVAC), emergency procedures specific
    to medical evacuations, including the evacuation of patients from
    aircraft; and

  - [(n)]{.lawlabel} the private operator's operational control system.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The ground instruction component of the training
  program for flight crew members shall include training in the
  performance of the following emergency procedures:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the use of fire extinguishers;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the operation and use of emergency exits;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} passenger preparation for an emergency landing or
    ditching;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} emergency evacuation procedures;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} if the flight crew members will be assigned to
    aircraft equipped with life preservers, the donning and inflation of
    life preservers;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} if the flight crew members will be assigned to
    aircraft equipped with life rafts, the removal of life rafts from
    the stowage compartment, and the deployment, inflation and boarding
    of life rafts; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} procedures for dealing with pilot incapacitation.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a private operator operates a turbo-jet-powered
  aeroplane, the ground instruction component of the training program
  for flight crew members who will operate that aeroplane shall include
  the following elements:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the low-energy landing regime for that type of
    aeroplane;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the performance and handling characteristics of the
    aeroplane and engine in the low-energy regime; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} balked landing procedures for the aeroplane.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Flight Crew Members --- Aircraft Operation Training]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995957 .Subheading}

- **[[604.170]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.170
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The aircraft operation component of
  the training program for flight crew members shall include procedures
  for the normal, abnormal and emergency operation of an aircraft and
  its systems and components, including the following elements:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} aircraft performance during take-off, climb,
    cruise, holding, descent, landing and diversion;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} calculations of the aircraft's take-off and landing
    distances and speeds, and the aircraft's fuel consumption, weight
    and centre of gravity;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the flight characteristics of the aircraft,
    including any abnormal characteristics that are applicable to the
    aircraft, such as dutch roll, buffet boundary onset and aircraft
    upset;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the effects of airframe and engine icing and the
    use of de-icing and anti-icing equipment;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} flight planning and instrument flight procedures,
    including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} departure, enroute, holding, arrival and
      diversion procedures,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} precision, non-precision and missed approaches
      in minimum visibility conditions, with the flight director in
      automatic mode and in degraded states of operation, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} circling approaches, if applicable;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} pre-flight checks of the interior and exterior of
    the aircraft;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the use of aircraft checklists;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} aircraft manoeuvres on the ground;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} normal, crosswind, noise abatement and maximum
    performance take-offs and landings;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} take-offs and landings on contaminated runways;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} rejected take-offs and landings;

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} steep turns;

  - [(m)]{.lawlabel} approach to a stall and recovery from a stall;

  - [(n)]{.lawlabel} the operation of the Flight Management Computer
    System (FMCS), Ground Proximity Warning System (GPWS), Terrain
    Awareness and Warning System (TAWS), Traffic Alert and Collision
    Avoidance System (TCAS), Airborne Collision Avoidance System (ACAS)
    and any other specialized equipment installed in the private
    operator's aircraft;

  - [(o)]{.lawlabel} the execution in VMC of one collision avoidance
    manoeuvre in response to a GPWS or a TAWS warning, if the aircraft
    is equipped with a GPWS or a TAWS;

  - [(p)]{.lawlabel} the operation of navigation and communication
    equipment;

  - [(q)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken in the event of hydraulic,
    electrical and other system failures;

  - [(r)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken in the event of flight
    control failures and, in the case of an aircraft with split control
    capability, briefings on degraded states of operation while in
    flight and during take-off and landing;

  - [(s)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken in the event of aircraft
    fire on the ground or in the air;

  - [(t)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken in the event of engine fire
    and engine failure while in flight;

  - [(u)]{.lawlabel} the recognition of and recovery from turbulence and
    windshear during an approach, landing and take-off;

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken in the event of an
    emergency evacuation of passengers and crew;

  - [(w)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken in the event of pilot
    incapacitation while in flight and during take-off and landing;

  - [(x)]{.lawlabel} crew resource management;

  - [(y)]{.lawlabel} if the private operator provides the training using
    a flight simulator, the performance of one balked landing initiated
    in the low-energy regime using the same simulator;

  - [(z)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a pressurized aircraft, the actions
    to be taken in the event of loss of pressurization and emergency
    descent;

  - [(z.1)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a three-engine or four-engine
    aircraft, take-off, landing and flight with the critical engine
    inoperative or with two other engines inoperative, including
    driftdown and engine-inoperative performance capabilities; and

  - [(z.2)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a helicopter,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} hovering manoeuvres, slope landings and confined
      areas,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} autorotations,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} transmission and main gear box faults and
      failures, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} tail rotor, tail rotor drive and tail rotor gear
      box faults and failures.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} When the training referred to in subsection (1) is
  provided on board an aircraft in flight, the private operator shall
  have procedures to ensure that situations are simulated or presented,
  and actions are simulated or performed, so as to not adversely affect
  the safety of the aircraft, its occupants or any other person.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Flight Crew Members --- Level B, C or D Flight Simulator]{.HTitleText4} {#h-995998 .Subheading}

**[[604.171]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.171 .sectionLabel}** Subject to
sections 604.172 to 604.174, a private operator may provide the training
referred to in subsection 604.170(1) and sections 604.177 and 604.178 to
a flight crew member either on board an aircraft or using a level B, C
or D flight simulator. However, if the private operator provides the
training using a level B flight simulator, the private operator shall
provide training in respect of the following activities on board an
aircraft:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} pre-flight checks of the interior and exterior of the
  aircraft;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} aircraft manoeuvres on the ground;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} normal take-offs and landings;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} crosswind take-offs and landings;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} a visual circuit, if the flight is conducted in VMC;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} approaches and landings with an engine simulated
  inoperative;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} simulated engine failure procedures during a take-off
  and a missed approach;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} approaches and landings without electronic glide
  slope indication;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} a circling approach, if applicable; and

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} any other approach for which a level B flight
  simulator lacks the capability.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Flight Crew Members --- Level C or D Flight Simulator]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996012 .Subheading}

**[[604.172]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.172 .sectionLabel}** A private
operator may provide the training referred to in subsection 604.170(1)
and sections 604.177 and 604.178 to a flight crew member using only a
level C or D flight simulator if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the flight crew member has acquired flight time on an
  aircraft certificated in the same category, and with engines using the
  same principle of propulsion, as the aircraft on which the flight crew
  member is to be trained; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the private operator provides to the flight crew
  member, using the same flight simulator, training in respect of the
  following activities under variable visual meteorological conditions
  of dusk and night, or day and night:

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} aircraft manoeuvres on the ground,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} normal take-offs and landings and crosswind
    take-offs and landings, up to 100% of the crosswind component
    specified by the aircraft manufacturer,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} encounters with moderate to severe in-flight
    icing conditions,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} simulated line flights that include at least one
    sector in which the flight crew member acts as pilot flying and at
    least one sector in which the flight crew member acts as pilot not
    flying or pilot monitoring,

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} visual circuits and landings with variable wind,
    runway illusion and runway surface conditions,

  - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} approaches and landings with an engine simulated
    inoperative,

  - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} approaches and landings without electronic glide
    slope indication,

  - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} approaches and landings with flight control
    failures and abnormalities, if applicable, and

  - [(ix)]{.lawlabel} engine failure procedures during a take-off and a
    missed approach.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Flight Crew Members --- Level D Flight Simulator]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996027 .Subheading}

**[[604.173]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.173 .sectionLabel}** A private
operator may provide the training referred to in subsection 604.170(1)
and sections 604.177 and 604.178 to a flight crew member using only a
level D flight simulator if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the flight crew member has at least 1,000 hours of
  flight time as a flight crew member;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of training provided on an aircraft that
  requires a minimum flight crew of two pilots, the flight crew member
  holds an individual type rating for an aircraft that requires a
  minimum flight crew of two pilots; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the private operator provides the training referred
  to in paragraph 604.172(b) to the flight crew member using that
  simulator.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Flight Crew Members --- Turbo-jet-powered Aeroplane or Transport Category Aircraft --- Level C or D Flight Simulator]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996034 .Subheading}

**[[604.174]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.174 .sectionLabel}** A private
operator who operates a turbo-jet-powered aeroplane or transport
category aircraft shall provide the training referred to in subsection
604.170(1) and sections 604.177 and 604.178 to a flight crew member
using a level C or D flight simulator if a level C or D flight simulator
is used for that aircraft type in Canada, the United States or Mexico.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Flight Crew Members --- Compatibility of Flight Simulators]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996038 .Subheading}

**[[604.175]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.175 .sectionLabel}** A flight
simulator that differs from the private operator's aircraft with respect
to installed equipment, systems, cockpit configuration, engine type or
performance may be used for the training referred to in subsection
604.170(1) and sections 604.177 and 604.178 if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the flight simulator has performance and handling
  characteristics equivalent to those of the private operator's
  aircraft; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the private operator's training program takes into
  account the differences between the flight simulator and the aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Flight Crew Members --- High Altitude Indoctrination Training]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996044 .Subheading}

**[[604.176]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.176 .sectionLabel}** The component
of the training program for flight crew members who will operate an
aircraft above 13,000 feet ASL shall include the following elements:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} physiological phenomena in a low pressure
  environment, including

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the effects on respiration,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the symptoms and effects of hypoxia,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the duration of consciousness at various
    altitudes without supplemental oxygen, and

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the effects of gas expansion and gas bubble
    formation; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the factors associated with rapid or explosive loss
  of pressurization, including

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the most likely causes of the loss of
    pressurization,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the increased level of noise, the change in cabin
    temperature and cabin fogging,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the effects on objects located near a point of
    fuselage failure, and

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken by flight crew members
    immediately after the loss of pressurization and the aircraft
    attitude likely to result from those actions.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Flight Crew Members --- One-engine Inoperative Ferry Flights]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996058 .Subheading}

**[[604.177]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.177 .sectionLabel}** The component
of the training program for flight crew members who will operate an
aircraft during a one-engine inoperative ferry flight under a flight
permit issued under section 507.04 shall include training in the
operational procedures and limits specified in the aircraft flight
manual.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Flight Crew Members --- Upgrade to Pilot-in-Command]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996062 .Subheading}

**[[604.178]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.178 .sectionLabel}** The component
of the training program for flight crew members who have served as
second-in-command and who are to be upgraded to pilot-in-command shall
include the following elements:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the elements of the training referred to in
  subsection 604.170(1) that are related to the duties of a
  pilot-in-command;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} training on the responsibilities of a
  pilot-in-command in relation to the use and operation of an aircraft;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a flight crew member who will conduct
  an operation under a special authorization, the training required to
  conduct that operation as pilot-in-command; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} crew resource management.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Flight Attendants]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996070 .Subheading}

**[[604.179]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.179 .sectionLabel}** The component
of the training program for flight attendants shall include the
following elements:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the roles and responsibilities of the private
  operator and crew members;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the coordination of crew member duties and crew
  resource management;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} aircraft communications systems and communication
  procedures in normal, abnormal and emergency conditions;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the content of the briefings given to passengers and
  crew members;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} cabin and passenger safety checks;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} aircraft surface contamination procedures;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} procedures relating to passengers requiring special
  treatment;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} requirements and procedures relating to seats and
  restraint systems for passengers and crew members;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} procedures for accepting and stowing carry-on
  baggage, and any applicable restrictions;

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} policies and procedures relating to the use of
  portable electronic devices;

- [(k)]{.lawlabel} procedures for fuelling with passengers on board;

- [(l)]{.lawlabel} procedures relating to passenger service when the
  aircraft is on the ground;

- [(m)]{.lawlabel} safety procedures relating to take-offs, landings and
  aircraft movements on the surface;

- [(n)]{.lawlabel} safety procedures relating to the embarkation and
  disembarkation of passengers and their movement on the apron;

- [(o)]{.lawlabel} procedures relating to passenger and crew member
  safety during periods of in-flight turbulence;

- [(p)]{.lawlabel} procedures for entering the flight deck and for
  serving beverages and meals to flight crew members;

- [(q)]{.lawlabel} procedures for dealing with the incapacitation of a
  crew member;

- [(r)]{.lawlabel} the location and operation of, and any safety
  instructions relating to, the various types of cabin exits and the
  flight deck escape routes;

- [(s)]{.lawlabel} the operation of cabin systems and of safety and
  emergency equipment by flight attendants in normal and abnormal
  conditions;

- [(t)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken with respect to the equipment
  identified on the minimum equipment list and intended for use by
  flight attendants;

- [(u)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken in the event of fumes or
  smoke in the cabin and to prevent fumes or smoke in the vicinity of
  the aircraft from entering the cabin;

- [(v)]{.lawlabel} fire detection, fire-fighting systems and
  fire-fighting procedures;

- [(w)]{.lawlabel} procedures in the event of loss of cabin
  pressurization;

- [(x)]{.lawlabel} how to identify the need for administering
  supplemental oxygen, and procedures for administering the oxygen;

- [(y)]{.lawlabel} procedures for the evacuation of passengers and crew
  members; and

- [(z)]{.lawlabel} training that includes the performance of the
  following emergency procedures:

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the use of the public address and interphone
    systems,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the briefing of passengers,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the operation and use of the emergency exits on
    each type of aircraft to which the flight attendant will be
    assigned,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} emergency evacuation procedures,

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} if the flight attendants will be assigned to an
    aircraft equipped with life preservers, the donning and inflation of
    life preservers,

  - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} if the flight attendants will be assigned to an
    aircraft equipped with an evacuation slide, the identification of
    the location of the manual inflation handle and the disconnect
    handle, and an evacuation using the slide,

  - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} if the flight attendants will be assigned to an
    aircraft equipped with either first aid oxygen equipment or portable
    oxygen equipment, the operation and use of that equipment,

  - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} if the flight attendants will be assigned to an
    aircraft equipped with life rafts, the removal of life rafts from
    the stowage compartment and the deployment, inflation and boarding
    of life rafts, and

  - [(ix)]{.lawlabel} fire fighting, including the use of a fire
    extinguisher on an actual fire.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Flight Dispatchers and Flight Followers]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996109 .Subheading}

- **[[604.180]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.180
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The component of the training
  program for flight dispatchers shall include the following elements:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the content of the private operator's operations
    manual;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the provisions of these Regulations, and of related
    standards, that affect the responsibilities of a flight dispatcher;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} flight planning and the private operator's standard
    operating procedures;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} radiocommunication procedures;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} aircraft fuelling procedures;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} aircraft surface contamination procedures;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the use of minimum equipment lists;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} meteorological conditions, including windshear and
    aircraft icing, in the private operator's area of operation;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the private operator's navigation and instrument
    approach procedures;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} accident and incident reporting;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} emergency procedures;

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} weight and balance control procedures;

  - [(m)]{.lawlabel} pre-flight crew member briefings;

  - [(n)]{.lawlabel} the differences between pilot self-dispatch
    procedures and co-authority dispatch procedures;

  - [(o)]{.lawlabel} the provision of meteorological information to the
    flight crew without analysis or interpretation;

  - [(p)]{.lawlabel} foreign regulations, if applicable;

  - [(q)]{.lawlabel} aeronautical information publications applicable to
    the private operator's area of operation;

  - [(r)]{.lawlabel} meteorological conditions and their effect on the
    flight and operation of an aircraft;

  - [(s)]{.lawlabel} the interpretation of meteorological information;

  - [(t)]{.lawlabel} the performance and limitations of the private
    operator's aircraft;

  - [(u)]{.lawlabel} air traffic control procedures; and

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} flight dispatch procedures.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The component of the training program for flight
  followers shall include the elements referred to in paragraphs (1)(a)
  to (q).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Ground and Airborne Icing Operations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996137 .Subheading}

**[[604.181]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.181 .sectionLabel}** The component
of the training program for flight crew members and ground personnel
that relates to ground and airborne icing operations shall include the
following elements:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the responsibilities of the pilot-in-command and
  other operations personnel in respect of aircraft de-icing and
  anti-icing procedures;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the provisions of these Regulations, and of related
  standards, that relate to ground and airborne icing operations;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the meteorological conditions that are conducive to
  ice, frost and snow contamination;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} procedures relating to pre-flight inspections and to
  the removal of contamination;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the hazards associated with the contamination of
  critical surfaces by ice, frost and snow;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} airborne icing recognition; and

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} in the case of training provided to flight crew
  members,

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the basis of the certification of the aircraft for
    flight into known icing conditions,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} airborne icing definitions and terminology,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the aerodynamic effects of airborne icing,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the weather patterns associated with airborne
    icing, including both classical and non-classical mechanisms that
    produce freezing precipitation,

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} flight planning and airborne icing information,

  - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} information specific to the private operator's
    aircraft fleet that relates to the operation of de-icing and
    anti-icing equipment, and operational procedures relating to that
    equipment, and

  - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} the private operator's directives concerning
    operations in airborne icing conditions set out in the private
    operator's operations manual and, if established by the private
    operator, in the private operator's standard operating procedures.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Maintenance, Elementary Work and Servicing]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996155 .Subheading}

- **[[604.182]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.182
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The component of the training
  program for persons who performs maintenance or elementary work shall
  include the following elements:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the performance rules set out in section 571.02,
    and the recording requirements set out in section 571.03 and
    subsection 605.92(1); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the private operator's maintenance control system.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The component of the training program for persons who
  perform servicing shall include the following elements:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the procedures that are set out in instructions for
    continued airworthiness provided by the holder of the design
    approval document, and that are applicable to the types of aircraft
    operated by the private operator; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} details of the methods used by the private operator
    to record servicing under paragraph 604.127(k).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Safety Management System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996165 .Subheading}

**[[604.183]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.183 .sectionLabel}** The component
of the training program in respect of the private operator's safety
management system shall include the following elements:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} training in the concepts and principles of safety
  management systems;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} training in the organization and operation of the
  private operator's safety management system;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} competency-based training for persons who have been
  assigned duties in respect of the safety management system;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} appropriate objectives for each person; and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} means of measuring the level of competency attained
  by each person who receives the training.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Amendments to Training Program]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1339513 .Subheading}

- **[[604.184]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.184
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister determines that a
  private operator's training program required under section 604.166
  does not include the competencies required for each person who
  receives training to perform their assigned duties, the Minister shall
  notify the private operator of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the corrective actions that the private operator is
    required to implement to its training program; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the date by which the private operator is required
    to implement the corrective actions to its training program.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The private operator referred to in subsection (1)
  shall implement the corrective actions on or before the date specified
  by the Minister under paragraph (1)(b).

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2022-17, s. 2](#1339255-1339520){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1339255-1339520.html"}
:::

**\[604.185 to 604.196 reserved\]**

#### [Division XI --- Operations Manual]{.HTitleText3} {#h-996175 .Subheading}

##### [General Requirement]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996176 .Subheading}

- **[[604.197]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.197
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A private operator shall have an
  operations manual that sets out the processes, practices and
  procedures applied in the course of its operations. The operations
  manual shall include a table of contents and shall deal with the
  following topics:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the duties and responsibilities of all operational
    and maintenance personnel, and the hierarchy and chain of command
    within management;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the organization and operation of the safety
    management system;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} personnel training and qualifications;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} record keeping;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the organization and operation of the maintenance
    control system;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} procedures for conducting an operation under a
    special authorization, if applicable;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the organization and operation of the operational
    control system;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} procedures, if any, relating to minimum equipment
    lists;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the procedures to follow in normal, abnormal and
    emergency conditions;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} the private operator's standard operating
    procedures, if any;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} weather restrictions;

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} flight time limits and flight duty period limits;

  - [(m)]{.lawlabel} controlled rest on the flight deck;

  - [(n)]{.lawlabel} accident and incident response considerations;

  - [(o)]{.lawlabel} procedures for dealing with security events;

  - [(p)]{.lawlabel} aircraft performance limitations; and

  - [(q)]{.lawlabel} the use and protection of records, if any, obtained
    from flight data recorders and cockpit voice recorders.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The private operator shall ensure that it is possible
  to verify the currency and validity of each part of its operations
  manual.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
- SOR/2018-269, s. 18
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-604.197-20140529.html "Link to previous version of section 604.197"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Distribution]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996199 .Subheading}

- **[[604.198]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.198
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A private operator shall provide a
  copy of its operations manual and a copy of every amendment to that
  manual to every member of its personnel who is involved in the private
  operator's operations.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Every person who has been provided with a copy of an
  operations manual under subsection (1) shall keep it up to date by
  inserting in it the amendments provided and shall ensure that the
  appropriate parts are accessible when the person is performing
  assigned duties.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), instead of providing every
  crew member with a copy of its operations manual and a copy of every
  amendment to that manual, a private operator may keep an up-to-date
  copy of the appropriate parts of that manual in each aircraft that it
  operates.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

**\[604.199 to 604.201 reserved\]**

#### [Division XII --- Safety Management System]{.HTitleText3} {#h-996207 .Subheading}

##### [Prohibition]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996208 .Subheading}

**[[604.202]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.202 .sectionLabel}** No private
operator shall conduct flight operations unless it has a safety
management system that meets the requirements of section 604.203.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Components of the Safety Management System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996212 .Subheading}

- **[[604.203]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.203
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), the
  private operator's safety management system shall include the
  following components:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a statement of the overall objectives that are to
    be achieved by the safety management system;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a safety management plan that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} specifies the duties that are assigned to the
      private operator's personnel in respect of the safety management
      system,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} sets out performance goals for the safety
      management system and a means of measuring the attainment of those
      goals,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} sets out a policy for the internal reporting of
      aviation-safety-related hazards, incidents and accidents,
      including the conditions, if any, under which personnel will be
      protected from disciplinary action,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} describes the relationship between the
      components of the safety management system, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} sets out procedures for involving personnel in
      the establishment of the safety management system;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a safety oversight program that includes

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} procedures for managing aviation-safety-related
      incidents, including their investigation and analysis,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} procedures for identifying and managing
      aviation-safety-related hazards, including the monitoring and risk
      profiling of those hazards,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a reporting and data collection system for
      collecting and communicating information relating to
      aviation-safety-related hazards and incidents that

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} uses a record-keeping system to monitor and
        analyze aviation safety trends,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} includes a means of communicating with persons
        who report issues relating to the safety management system or
        aviation safety,

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} is capable of generating progress reports for
        the person responsible for the functional area at intervals that
        the person determines, and

      - [(D)]{.lawlabel} is capable of generating other reports in
        urgent cases,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} procedures for investigating and analyzing
      aviation-safety-related hazards, incidents and accidents that

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} take into account human, environmental and
        supervisory factors and organizational elements,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} make it possible to make findings as to root
        causes and contributing factors, and

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} make it possible to communicate the findings to
        the operations manager,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} risk management analysis procedures that include

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} an analysis of aviation-safety-related hazards,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} a risk assessment based on risk criteria, and

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} a risk control strategy,

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} corrective action procedures

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} for determining what corrective actions are
        necessary, if any, and for carrying out those actions,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} for keeping a record of any determination made
        under clause (A) and the reason for that determination, and

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} for monitoring and evaluating, in accordance
        with the quality assurance program referred to in section
        604.206, the effectiveness of any corrective action carried out
        under clause (A),

    - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} procedures for disseminating to personnel, with
      the approval of the private operator, the following
      aviation-safety-related information:

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} information relating to an incident,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} information relating to a hazard analysis, and

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} information relating to the results of a review
        or audit, and

    - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} procedures for sharing, with any person with
      whom the private operator exchanges services, any information
      relating to aviation safety;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} procedures for

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} ensuring that all procedures relating to the
      safety management system are recorded and disseminated to
      personnel,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} managing and keeping all records and documents
      resulting from the safety management system,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} ensuring that records and reports relating to
      the safety management system are retained for at least two years,
      and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} reviewing all documents relating to the safety
      management system and keeping those documents up to date;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} emergency response procedures that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} cover all of the activities carried out by the
      private operator, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the duties relating to those
      procedures are assigned to the appropriate personnel;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the quality assurance program referred to in
    section 604.206; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the process for conducting a review of the safety
    management system under section 604.207.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The safety management system of a private operator
  who has no employees is not required to include the components
  referred to in the following provisions:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} subparagraphs (1)(b)(iii) and (v);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} clause (1)(c)(iii)(B);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} subparagraph (1)(c)(vii);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} subparagraph (1)(d)(i); and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} subparagraph (1)(e)(ii).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Duties of Operations Manager]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996265 .Subheading}

- **[[604.204]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.204
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The operations manager shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} manage the safety management system;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} implement the safety management plan referred to in
    paragraph 604.203(1)(b);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} implement the safety oversight program referred to
    in paragraph 604.203(1)(c);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} implement the procedures referred to in paragraph
    604.203(1)(d) in respect of all documents relating to the safety
    management system;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} implement the emergency response procedures
    referred to in paragraph 604.203(1)(e);

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} implement the quality assurance program referred to
    in section 604.206;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} ensure that any deficiency identified by the
    quality assurance program is analyzed to determine its root cause
    and contributing factors;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} communicate to the private operator any finding
    produced by the safety management system in respect of a hazard to
    aviation safety;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} share, with any person with whom the private
    operator exchanges services, any finding produced by the safety
    management system that is likely to have an adverse effect on
    aviation safety; and

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} analyze any information relating to aviation safety
    that is received from any person with whom the private operator
    exchanges services and take appropriate action to mitigate any
    hazard to aviation safety.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} When a finding produced by the safety management
  system is reported to the operations manager, the operations manager
  shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} determine what corrective actions are necessary to
    address that finding, if any, and carry out those actions;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} keep a record of any determination made under
    paragraph (a) and the reason for that determination;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the operations manager has assigned management
    functions to another person, communicate any determination made
    under paragraph (a) to that person; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} notify the private operator of any deficiency that
    reduces the effectiveness of all or part of the safety management
    system, and of the corrective action carried out.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Duties of Personnel]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996285 .Subheading}

**[[604.205]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.205 .sectionLabel}** The personnel
of a private operator shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} report to the operations manager any issue relating
  to the safety management system, including

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} deficiencies, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} aviation-safety-related hazards, incidents or
    accidents; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} share, with any person with whom the private operator
  exchanges services, any information relating to aviation safety.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Quality Assurance Program]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996293 .Subheading}

- **[[604.206]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.206
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The quality assurance program shall
  make provision for sampling the private operator's processes in order
  to measure

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the private operator's effectiveness in conducting
    an audit under subsection (2); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the private operator's ability to carry out its
    activities effectively and safely.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An audit required by the quality assurance program
  shall be conducted

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} within 12 months after the day on which the private
    operator registration document was issued;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} subject to paragraph (c), within 12 months after
    the day on which the previous audit was completed;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} within 36 months after the day on which the
    previous audit was completed, if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the private operator submits to the Minister a
      risk assessment establishing that the private operator is capable
      of managing the aviation-safety-related risks that may occur
      during that 36-month period, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} none of the following events have occurred since
      the day on which the previous audit was completed:

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} a major incident,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} a major change in the private operator's
        activities, and

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} a finding resulting from a review of the safety
        management system and indicating that the quality assurance
        program is not achieving its objectives;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} following an accident, or incident, that affects
    aviation safety; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} following the identification, as a result of a
    review of the safety management system, of a deficiency that reduces
    the effectiveness of all or part of the safety management system.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A quality assurance program shall include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} checklists of all of the activities carried out by
    the private operator;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} procedures for determining what corrective actions
    are necessary to eliminate the root cause and contributing factors
    of each finding of non-compliance with these Regulations;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} procedures for monitoring corrective actions to
    ensure that they are effective;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a system for recording the following information:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the findings resulting from an audit, and any
      supporting documentation,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} an analysis of the root cause and contributing
      factors of any deficiency identified by the quality assurance
      program,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} any corrective action, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} any follow-up action; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} procedures for ensuring that each finding resulting
    from an audit is communicated to the operations manager and to any
    person who has been assigned management functions respecting the
    safety management system, and is made available to the private
    operator.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An audit conducted under paragraph (2)(d) or (e)
  shall be a complete audit.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} No private operator shall assign a duty relating to
  the quality assurance program to a person who is responsible for
  carrying out a task or an activity evaluated by that program unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} owing to the size, nature and complexity of the
    private operator's operations and activities, it is impractical to
    assign the duty to a person who is not responsible for carrying out
    the task or activity;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} based on a risk analysis, assigning the duty to a
    person responsible for carrying out the task or activity will not
    result in an increased risk to aviation safety; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the operation of the audit system in relation to
    the quality assurance program will not be compromised.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Review of the Safety Management System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996326 .Subheading}

- **[[604.207]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.207
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A periodic review of the safety
  management system shall measure the effectiveness of the system in the
  attainment of the performance goals referred to in subparagraph
  604.203(1)(b)(ii).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A review of the safety management system shall be
  conducted

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} within 12 months after the day on which the private
    operator registration document was issued;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} within 12 months after the day on which the
    previous review was completed; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} following an accident, or incident, that affects
    aviation safety.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A review of the safety management system shall
  include procedures for

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} identifying any deficiency in the operation of the
    safety management system;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} investigating and analyzing the root cause and
    contributing factors of any deficiency identified by the review; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} ensuring that corrective actions are effective and
    are used on an ongoing basis to improve the safety management
    system.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} A review conducted under paragraph (2)(c) shall be a
  complete review.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} No private operator shall assign a duty relating to a
  review of the safety management system to a person who is responsible
  for carrying out a task or an activity that is the subject of the
  review unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} owing to the size, nature and complexity of the
    private operator's operations and activities, it is impracticable to
    assign the duty to a person who is not responsible for carrying out
    the task or activity;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} based on a risk analysis, assigning the duty to a
    person responsible for carrying out the task or activity will not
    result in an increased risk to aviation safety; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the integrity of the review of the safety
    management system will not be compromised.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

##### [Duties of Private Operator --- Review]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996344 .Subheading}

**[[604.208]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.208 .sectionLabel}** The private
operator shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} conduct the review of the safety management system
  under section 604.207;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} determine what corrective actions are necessary to
  address any deficiency identified by the review, and carry out those
  actions;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} keep a record of any determination made under
  paragraph (b) and the reason for it; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} if the private operator has assigned management
  functions to another person, provide that person with a copy of that
  record.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 18
:::

**\[604.209 to 604.219 reserved\]**

#### [Division XIII --- Flight Attendants and Emergency Evacuation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-996353 .Subheading}

##### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996354 .Subheading}

- **[[604.220]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.220
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Division
  and subject to subsection (2), [[model]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means
  [[aircraft master series]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} as described in section
  3.7 of version 1.3 of the document entitled International Standard for
  Aircraft Make, Model, and Series Groupings, dated October 2012 and
  published by the Common Taxonomy Team of the International Civil
  Aviation Organization (ICAO) and the Commercial Aviation Safety Team
  (CAST).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If no aircraft master series is assigned to an
  aeroplane, [[model]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} in respect of that aeroplane
  means [[aircraft model]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} as described in section
  3.6 of version 1.3 of the document entitled International Standard for
  Aircraft Make, Model, and Series Groupings, dated October 2012 and
  published by the Common Taxonomy Team of the International Civil
  Aviation Organization (ICAO) and the Commercial Aviation Safety Team
  (CAST).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 12
:::

##### [Minimum Number of Flight Attendants]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996360 .Subheading}

- **[[604.221]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.221
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off
  in an aeroplane that is operated by a private operator and is carrying
  more than 12 passengers unless the take-off is conducted with the
  minimum number of flight attendants required on each deck.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (3) to (5), the minimum number
  of flight attendants required on each deck is one flight attendant for
  each unit of 50 passengers or for each portion of such a unit.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No flight attendants are required if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane has 13 to 19 passengers on board;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane is operated by a pilot-in-command and
    a second-in-command;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the passenger cabin is readily accessible from the
    flight deck; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the flight crew members are able to exercise
    supervision over the passengers during flight by visual and aural
    means.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a private operator has carried out a successful
  demonstration of its emergency evacuation procedures for a model of
  aeroplane using more flight attendants than would have been required
  in accordance with the ratio set out in subsection (2), the minimum
  number of flight attendants required on each deck of an aeroplane of
  that model that is operated by the private operator is the number of
  flight attendants used in the demonstration.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} If the emergency evacuation demonstration required
  for the certification of a model of aeroplane was carried out using
  more flight attendants than would have been required in accordance
  with the ratio set out in subsection (2), the minimum number of flight
  attendants required on each deck of an aeroplane of that model is the
  number of flight attendants required in accordance with the ratio set
  out in subsection (2) plus an additional number of flight attendants
  that is equal to the difference between

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the number of flight attendants used in the
    demonstration, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number of flight attendants that would have
    been required in accordance with the ratio set out in subsection (2)
    at the time of the demonstration.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} If there is a conflict between subsection (3) and
  subsection (4) or (5), subsection (3) prevails to the extent of the
  conflict.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 12
:::

##### [Emergency Features]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996376 .Subheading}

**[[604.222]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.222 .sectionLabel}** No private
operator shall operate an aeroplane that is configured for 20 or more
passenger seats unless the features that facilitate emergency
evacuations meet the requirements set out in section 624.222 of Standard
624 --- Emergency Features of the General Operating and Flight Rules
Standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 12
:::

##### [Demonstration of Emergency Evacuation Procedures]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996380 .Subheading}

- **[[604.223]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.223
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A private operator who decides to
  introduce a model of aeroplane into its fleet for the purpose of
  carrying passengers shall carry out a successful demonstration of its
  emergency evacuation procedures for that model of aeroplane before
  operating an aeroplane of that model to carry passengers.

- [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), the demonstration of
  emergency evacuation procedures is not required if the private
  operator has

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} carried out a successful demonstration of its
    emergency evacuation procedures for another model of aeroplane in
    its fleet;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} conducted a comparative analysis to ensure that
    there is no difference in any of the following items between the
    model of aeroplane for which a successful demonstration has been
    carried out and the model of aeroplane being introduced:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the location of the flight attendants and their
      emergency evacuation duties and procedures,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the number, location and type of emergency
      exits, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the number, location and type of opening
      mechanisms for the emergency exits;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} verified that no changes have been made to any of
    the items listed in subparagraphs (b)(i) to (iii), in respect of the
    model of aeroplane for which a successful demonstration has been
    carried out, between the time of the successful demonstration and
    the time the comparative analysis is conducted; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} before operating an aeroplane of the model being
    introduced to carry passengers, made a record --- that it keeps for
    at least five years after the day on which the record is made --- of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} its decision to use the results of a successful
      demonstration of its emergency evacuation procedures for another
      model of aeroplane instead of carrying out a demonstration for the
      model of aeroplane it has decided to introduce, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the model of aeroplane for which a successful
      demonstration has been carried out and the model of aeroplane it
      has decided to introduce.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a private operator decides to introduce an
  aeroplane into its fleet and there is a difference in any of the
  following items between that aeroplane and other aeroplanes of the
  same model that are already in the fleet, the private operator shall
  treat the aeroplane as if it were a different model of aeroplane and
  carry out a successful demonstration of its emergency evacuation
  procedures for that model before operating the aeroplane to carry
  passengers:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the location of the flight attendants or their
    emergency evacuation duties or procedures;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number, location or type of emergency exits; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the number, location or type of opening mechanisms
    for the emergency exits.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A private operator who decides to change any of the
  following items in respect of an aeroplane shall carry out a
  successful demonstration of its emergency evacuation procedures for
  the model of that aeroplane, as changed, before operating the
  aeroplane to carry passengers:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the location of the flight attendants or their
    emergency evacuation duties or procedures;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number, location or type of emergency exits; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the number, location or type of opening mechanisms
    for the emergency exits.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subsections (1) to (3) do not apply in respect of a
  model of aeroplane that is configured to carry fewer than 44
  passengers.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 12
- [SOR/2020-253, s. 7](#1274655-1276839){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1274655-1276839.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-604.223-20150802.html "Link to previous version of section 604.223"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Carrying Out a Demonstration of Emergency Evacuation Procedures]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996394 .Subheading}

- **[[604.224]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.224
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A private operator who carries out a
  demonstration of its emergency evacuation procedures for a model of
  aeroplane shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} do so without passengers;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} do so with flight attendants who have completed the
    private operator's training program for that model of aeroplane; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} begin the demonstration using the private
    operator's normal procedures, then transition to its emergency
    procedures.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The demonstration is successful if the flight
  attendants can, within 15 seconds after the transition from the
  private operator's normal procedures to its emergency procedures,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} open 50% of the floor-level emergency exits that
    are required by the certification basis established in respect of
    the model of aeroplane;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} open 50% of the non-floor-level emergency exits the
    opening of which is set out as an emergency evacuation duty in the
    private operator's operations manual; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} deploy 50% of the escape slides.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The private operator shall record the demonstration
  using time-encoded video and keep the recording for at least five
  years after the day on which the demonstration is carried out.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 12
:::

##### [Extended Over-water Operations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996407 .Subheading}

- **[[604.225]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.225
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a private operator decides to
  operate an aeroplane to carry passengers in extended over-water
  operations and the aeroplane is required to have survival equipment
  under section 602.63, the private operator shall carry out a
  demonstration of its ditching emergency evacuation procedures for the
  model of that aeroplane before starting the extended over-water
  operations.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of an
  aeroplane that is configured for fewer than 20 passenger seats.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 13
:::

##### [Carrying Out a Demonstration of Emergency Evacuation Procedures --- Ditching]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996413 .Subheading}

- **[[604.226]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.226
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A private operator who carries out a
  demonstration of its ditching emergency evacuation procedures for a
  model of aeroplane shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} use an aeroplane of that model, a life-sized
    mock-up of that model of aeroplane or a floating device;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} assume that the ditching occurs during daylight
    hours and that all required crew members are available;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} ensure that passengers are on board and participate
    in the demonstration if the private operator's operations manual
    requires passengers to assist in the launching of life rafts;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} ensure that, after the ditching signal has been
    received, each evacuee dons a life preserver;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} ensure that each life raft is removed from its
    stowage compartment;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} ensure that, as applicable, one life raft or one
    slide raft is inflated; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} ensure that each evacuee boards the life raft or
    slide raft and that a crew member assigned to the life raft or slide
    raft indicates the location of the required survival equipment and
    describes the use of that equipment.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A life-sized mock-up of a model of aeroplane or a
  floating device must

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} be representative of the passenger cabin of the
    model of aeroplane;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} contain seats for all of the evacuees participating
    in the demonstration;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} be equipped with the same survival equipment that
    is installed on the model of aeroplane, including a life preserver
    for each evacuee participating in the demonstration;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} have emergency exits and doors that simulate those
    on the model of aeroplane; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} have enough wing area installed outside the window
    emergency exits to simulate the portions of the wings of the model
    of aeroplane that would be used in a ditching situation.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The private operator shall record the demonstration
  using time-encoded video and keep the recording for at least five
  years after the day on which the demonstration is carried out.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 13
:::

**\[604.227 to 604.239 reserved\]**

##### [Embarking and Disembarking of Passengers]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996433 .Subheading}

- **[[604.240]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.240
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) and (3),
  a private operator who operates an aeroplane to carry passengers shall
  ensure that all flight attendants assigned to a flight using that
  aeroplane are on board during passenger embarkation and
  disembarkation.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a flight to which more than one flight
  attendant is assigned, the private operator may reduce the number of
  flight attendants by one during passenger embarkation if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the flight attendant who leaves the aeroplane
    remains within the immediate vicinity of the door through which
    passengers are embarking and carries out safety-related duties for
    the flight;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the engines used for the propulsion of the
    aeroplane are not running; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} at least one floor-level exit remains open to
    provide for passenger egress.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a flight to which more than one flight
  attendant is assigned, the private operator may reduce the number of
  flight attendants during passenger disembarkation if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the engines used for the propulsion of the
    aeroplane are not running;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} at least one floor-level exit remains open to
    provide for passenger egress; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} half of the required number of flight attendants
    --- rounded down to the next lower number in the case of fractions,
    but never less than one --- remain on board.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Paragraphs (2)(b) and (3)(a) do not apply in respect
  of an engine on a propeller-driven aeroplane if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the engine has a propeller brake;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the propeller brake is set; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane flight manual indicates that the
    engine may be used as an auxiliary power unit.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The private operator shall ensure that, during
  passenger embarkation and disembarkation,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if only one flight attendant is on board, he or she
    remains in the vicinity of the door through which passengers are
    embarking or disembarking; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if more than one flight attendant is on board, they
    are evenly distributed in the passenger cabin and are in the
    vicinity of the floor-level exits.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 12
:::

##### [Emergency Evacuation --- Before and During Surface Movement]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996453 .Subheading}

**[[604.241]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.241 .sectionLabel}** A private
operator shall, for each aeroplane in its fleet that is configured to
carry 20 or more passengers, have procedures to ensure that

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} at least one floor-level exit provides for passenger
  egress before the movement of the aeroplane on the surface; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} every automatically deployable means of emergency
  passenger evacuation is ready for immediate use during the movement of
  the aeroplane on the surface.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 12
:::

##### [Single-aisle Aeroplane]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996459 .Subheading}

**[[604.242]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.242 .sectionLabel}** Despite section
605.09, no person shall conduct a take-off in a single-aisle aeroplane
that is carrying passengers unless all emergency exits and escape slides
are operative.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 12
:::

##### [Standardization]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996463 .Subheading}

**[[604.243]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-604.243 .sectionLabel}** No private
operator shall operate an aeroplane that is configured to carry 20 or
more passengers unless the emergency equipment, the stowage locations
for emergency equipment and the emergency procedures are standardized
for all aeroplanes in the private operator's fleet that are configured
to carry 20 or more passengers.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 14
:::

### [Subpart 5 --- Aircraft Requirements]{.HTitleText2} {#h-996467 .Subheading}

#### [Application]{.HTitleText3} {#h-996468 .Subheading}

- **[[605.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.01
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This Subpart applies to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} persons operating Canadian aircraft other than
    ultra-light aeroplanes, hang gliders or remotely piloted aircraft;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} persons operating foreign aircraft in Canada, other
    than remotely piloted aircraft, if those persons are Canadian
    citizens, permanent residents or corporations incorporated by or
    under the laws of Canada or a province.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The following requirements apply to persons operating
  foreign aircraft, other than persons referred to in paragraph (1)(b),
  while those aircraft are operated in Canada:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the requirement to carry a flight authority on
    board the aircraft in accordance with section 605.03;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the requirement that an aircraft be equipped with
    transponder and automatic pressure-altitude reporting equipment in
    accordance with section 605.35;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the requirement that an aircraft be equipped with
    one or more ELTs in accordance with section 605.38; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} radiocommunication and radio navigation equipment
    requirements that are specific to the aircraft and types of flight
    referred to in sections 605.14 to 605.21.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-11, s. 19](#1045409-1110480){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045409-1110480.html"}
:::
