**\[605.02 reserved\]**

#### [Division I --- Aircraft Requirements --- General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-996479 .Subheading}

##### [Flight Authority]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996480 .Subheading}

- **[[605.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.03
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aircraft
  in flight unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a flight authority is in effect in respect of the
    aircraft;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is operated in accordance with the
    conditions set out in the flight authority; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsections (2) and (3), the flight
    authority is carried on board the aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a specific-purpose flight permit has been
  issued pursuant to section 507.04, an aircraft may be operated without
  the flight authority carried on board where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the flight is conducted in Canadian airspace; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an entry is made into the journey log indicating

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} that the aircraft is operating under a
      specific-purpose flight permit, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where applicable, any operational conditions
      that pertain to flight operations under the specific-purpose
      flight permit.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A balloon may be operated without the flight
  authority carried on board where the flight authority is immediately
  available to the pilot-in-command

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} prior to commencing a flight; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} on completion of the flight.

##### [Availability of Aircraft Flight Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996494 .Subheading}

- **[[605.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.04
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off
  in an aircraft, for which an aircraft flight manual is required by the
  applicable standards of airworthiness, unless the aircraft flight
  manual or, if an aircraft operating manual has been established under
  section 604.37 or Part VII, the aircraft operating manual is available
  to the flight crew members at their duty stations.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The aircraft flight manual or, if an aircraft
  operating manual has been established under section 604.37 or Part
  VII, those parts of the aircraft flight manual that are incorporated
  into the aircraft operating manual shall include all the amendments
  and supplementary material that are applicable to the aircraft type.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-341, s. 6
- SOR/2014-131, s. 19
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-605.04-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 605.04"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Markings and Placards]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996500 .Subheading}

**[[605.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.05 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
conduct a take-off in an aircraft in respect of which markings or
placards are required by the applicable standards of airworthiness
unless the markings or placards are affixed to the aircraft or attached
to a component of the aircraft in accordance with those standards.

##### [Aircraft Equipment Standards and Serviceability]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996502 .Subheading}

**[[605.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.06 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
conduct a take-off in an aircraft, or permit another person to conduct a
take-off in an aircraft in their custody and control, unless the
aircraft equipment required by these Regulations

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} meets the applicable standards of airworthiness; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} is serviceable and, where required by operational
  circumstances, functioning, except if otherwise provided in section
  605.08, 605.09 or 605.10.

##### [Minimum Equipment Lists]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996506 .Subheading}

- **[[605.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.07
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may, in accordance with
  the MMEL/MEL Policy and Procedures Manual, establish a master minimum
  equipment list for each type of aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may supplement a master minimum
  equipment list that has been issued by the competent authority of a
  foreign state in respect of a type of aircraft where necessary to
  ensure compliance with the MMEL/MEL Policy and Procedures Manual.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where a master minimum equipment list has been
  established for an aircraft type pursuant to subsection (1) or
  supplemented pursuant to subsection (2), the Minister shall approve a
  minimum equipment list in respect of each operator of that type of
  aircraft, if the requirements set out in the MMEL/MEL Policy and
  Procedures Manual are met.

##### [Unserviceable and Removed Equipment --- General]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996511 .Subheading}

- **[[605.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.08
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (2) and sections
  605.09 and 605.10, no person shall conduct a take-off in an aircraft
  that has equipment that is not serviceable or from which equipment has
  been removed if, in the opinion of the pilot-in-command, aviation
  safety is affected.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite sections 605.09 and 605.10, a person may
  conduct a take-off in an aircraft that has equipment that is not
  serviceable or from which equipment has been removed where the
  aircraft is operated in accordance with the conditions of a flight
  permit that has been issued specifically for that purpose.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2021-152, s. 19(E)](#1302038-1308435){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1302038-1308435.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-605.08-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 605.08"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Unserviceable and Removed Equipment --- Aircraft with a Minimum Equipment List]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996515 .Subheading}

- **[[605.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.09
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), where a
  minimum equipment list has been approved in respect of the operator of
  an aircraft pursuant to subsection 605.07(3), no person shall conduct
  a take-off in the aircraft with equipment that is not serviceable or
  that has been removed unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is operated in accordance with any
    conditions or limitations specified in the minimum equipment list;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a copy of the minimum equipment list is carried on
    board.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where the conditions or limitations specified in a
  minimum equipment list are in conflict with the requirements of an
  airworthiness directive, the airworthiness directive prevails.

##### [Unserviceable and Removed Equipment --- Aircraft without a Minimum Equipment List]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996521 .Subheading}

- **[[605.10]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.10
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where a minimum equipment list has
  not been approved in respect of the operator of an aircraft, no person
  shall conduct a take-off in the aircraft with equipment that is not
  serviceable or that has been removed, where that equipment is required
  by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the standards of airworthiness that apply to day or
    night VFR or IFR flight, as applicable;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any equipment list published by the aircraft
    manufacturer respecting aircraft equipment that is required for the
    intended flight;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} an air operator certificate, a special
    authorization issued under subsection 604.05(2), a special flight
    operations certificate or a flight training unit operating
    certificate;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} an airworthiness directive; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} these Regulations.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a minimum equipment list has not been approved
  in respect of the operator of an aircraft and the aircraft has
  equipment, other than the equipment required by subsection (1), that
  is not serviceable or that has been removed, no person shall conduct a
  take-off in the aircraft unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where the unserviceable equipment is not removed
    from the aircraft, it is isolated or secured so as not to constitute
    a hazard to any other aircraft system or to any person on board the
    aircraft;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the appropriate placards are installed as required
    by the Aircraft Equipment and Maintenance Standards; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} an entry recording the actions referred to in
    paragraphs (a) and (b) is made in the journey log, as applicable.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2014-131, s. 20
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-605.10-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 605.10"){.PITLink}
:::

**\[605.11 to 605.13 reserved\]**

#### [Division II --- Aircraft Equipment Requirements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-996536 .Subheading}

##### [Power-driven Aircraft --- Day VFR]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996537 .Subheading}

**[[605.14]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.14 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
conduct a take-off in a power-driven aircraft for the purpose of day VFR
flight unless it is equipped with

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is operated in uncontrolled
  airspace, an altimeter;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is operated in controlled
  airspace, a sensitive altimeter adjustable for barometric pressure;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} an airspeed indicator;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a magnetic compass or a magnetic direction indicator
  that operates independently of the aircraft electrical generating
  system;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} a tachometer for each engine and for each propeller
  or rotor that has limiting speeds established by the manufacturer;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} an oil pressure indicator for each engine employing
  an oil pressure system;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} a coolant temperature indicator for each
  liquid-cooled engine;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} an oil temperature indicator for each air-cooled
  engine having a separate oil system;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} a manifold pressure gauge for each

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} reciprocating engine equipped with a variable-pitch
    propeller,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} reciprocating engine used to power a helicopter,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} supercharged engine, and

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} turbocharged engine;

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} a means for the flight crew, when seated at the
  flight controls to determine

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the fuel quantity in each main fuel tank, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if the aircraft employs retractable landing gear,
    the position of the landing gear;

- [(k)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsections 601.08(2) and 601.09(2), a
  radiocommunication system adequate to permit two-way communication on
  the appropriate frequency when the aircraft is operated within

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} Class B, Class C or Class D airspace,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} an MF area, unless the aircraft is operated
    pursuant to subsection 602.97(3), or

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the ADIZ;

- [(l)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is operated under Subpart 4 of
  this Part, or under Subpart 3, 4 or 5 of Part VII, radiocommunication
  equipment adequate to permit two-way communication on the appropriate
  frequency;

- [(m)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is operated in Class B airspace,
  radio navigation equipment that will enable it to be operated in
  accordance with a flight plan; and

- [(n)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is operated under Subpart 4 of
  this Part or under Subpart 5 of Part VII, radio navigation equipment
  that is adequate to receive radio signals from a transmitting
  facility.

##### [Power-driven Aircraft --- VFR OTT]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996562 .Subheading}

- **[[605.15]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.15
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off
  in a power-driven aircraft for the purpose of VFR OTT flight unless it
  is equipped with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the equipment referred to in paragraphs 605.14(c)
    to (j);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a sensitive altimeter adjustable for barometric
    pressure;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a means of preventing malfunction caused by icing
    for each airspeed indicating system;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a gyroscopic direction indicator or a stabilized
    magnetic direction indicator;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} an attitude indicator;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsection (2), a turn and slip
    indicator or turn coordinator;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is to be operated within the
    Northern Domestic Airspace, a means of establishing direction that
    is not dependent on a magnetic source;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} radiocommunication equipment adequate to permit
    two-way communication on the appropriate frequency; and

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} radio navigation equipment adequate to permit the
    aircraft to be navigated safely.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where the aircraft is equipped with a third attitude
  indicator that is usable through flight attitudes of 360° of pitch and
  roll for an aeroplane, or ± 80° of pitch and ± 120° of roll for a
  helicopter, the aircraft may be equipped with a slip-skid indicator in
  lieu of a turn and slip indicator or a turn coordinator.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-77, s. 18
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-605.15-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 605.15"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Power-driven Aircraft --- Night VFR]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996577 .Subheading}

- **[[605.16]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.16
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off
  in a power-driven aircraft for the purpose of night VFR flight, unless
  it is equipped with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the equipment referred to in paragraphs 605.14(c)
    to (n);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a sensitive altimeter adjustable for barometric
    pressure;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsection (2), a turn and slip
    indicator or turn coordinator;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} an adequate source of electrical energy for all of
    the electrical and radio equipment;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} in respect of every set of fuses of a particular
    rating that is installed on the aircraft and accessible to the
    pilot-in-command during flight, a number of spare fuses that is
    equal to at least 50 per cent of the total number of installed fuses
    of that rating;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is operated so that an aerodrome
    is not visible from the aircraft, a stabilized magnetic direction
    indicator or a gyroscopic direction indicator;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is to be operated within the
    Northern Domestic Airspace, a means of establishing direction that
    is not dependent on a magnetic source;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is an airship operated within
    controlled airspace, radar reflectors attached in such a manner as
    to be capable of a 360-degree reflection;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a means of illumination for all of the instruments
    used to operate the aircraft;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} when carrying passengers, a landing light; and

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} position and anti-collision lights that conform to
    the Aircraft Equipment and Maintenance Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where the aircraft is equipped with a third attitude
  indicator that is usable through flight attitudes of 360° of pitch and
  roll for an aeroplane, or ± 80° of pitch and ± 120° of roll for a
  helicopter, the aircraft may be equipped with a slip-skid indicator in
  lieu of a turn and slip indicator or a turn coordinator.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aircraft that is equipped
  with any light that may be mistaken for, or downgrade the conspicuity
  of, a light in the navigation light system, unless the aircraft is
  being operated for the purpose of aerial advertising.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} In addition to the equipment requirements specified
  in subsection (1), no person shall operate an aircraft in night VFR
  flight under Subpart 4 of this Part or Subparts 2 to 5 of Part VII,
  unless the aircraft is equipped with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an attitude indicator;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a vertical speed indicator;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a means of preventing malfunction caused by icing
    for each airspeed indicating system; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} an outside air temperature gauge.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-77, s. 19

##### [Use of Position and Anti-collision Lights]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996600 .Subheading}

- **[[605.17]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.17
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no person
  shall operate an aircraft in the air or on the ground at night, or on
  water between sunset and sunrise, unless the aircraft position lights
  and anti-collision lights are turned on.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Anti-collision lights may be turned off where the
  pilot-in-command determines that, because of operating conditions,
  doing so would be in the interests of aviation safety.

##### [Power-driven Aircraft --- IFR]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996604 .Subheading}

**[[605.18]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.18 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
conduct a take-off in a power-driven aircraft for the purpose of IFR
flight unless it is equipped with

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} when it is operated by day, the equipment required
  pursuant to paragraphs 605.16(1)(a) to (h);

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} when it is operated by night, the equipment required
  pursuant to paragraphs 605.16(1)(a) to (k);

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} an attitude indicator;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a vertical speed indicator;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} an outside air temperature gauge;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} a means of preventing malfunction caused by icing for
  each airspeed indicating system;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} a power failure warning device or vacuum indicator
  that shows the power available to gyroscopic instruments from each
  power source;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} an alternative source of static pressure for the
  altimeter, airspeed indicator and vertical speed indicator;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} sufficient radiocommunication equipment to permit the
  pilot to conduct two-way communications on the appropriate frequency;
  and

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} sufficient radio navigation equipment to permit the
  pilot, in the event of the failure at any stage of the flight of any
  item of that equipment, including any associated flight instrument
  display,

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} to proceed to the destination aerodrome or proceed
    to another aerodrome that is suitable for landing, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is operated in IMC, to complete
    an instrument approach and, if necessary, conduct a missed approach
    procedure.

##### [Balloons --- Day VFR]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996618 .Subheading}

**[[605.19]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.19 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
conduct a take-off in a balloon for the purpose of day VFR flight unless
it is equipped with

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} an altimeter;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a vertical speed indicator;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a hot air balloon,

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a fuel quantity gauge, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} an envelope temperature indicator;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a captive gas balloon, a magnetic
  direction indicator; and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsections 601.08(2) and 601.09(2), a
  radiocommunication system adequate to permit two-way communication on
  the appropriate frequency when the balloon is operated within

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} Class C or Class D airspace,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} an MF area, unless the aircraft is operated
    pursuant to subsection 602.97(3), or

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the ADIZ.

##### [Balloons --- Night VFR]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996630 .Subheading}

**[[605.20]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.20 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
conduct a take-off in a balloon for the purpose of night VFR flight
unless it is equipped with

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} equipment required pursuant to section 605.19;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} position lights;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a means of illuminating all of the instruments used
  by the flight crew, including a flashlight; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a hot air balloon, two independent
  fuel systems.

##### [Gliders --- Day VFR]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996636 .Subheading}

**[[605.21]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.21 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate a glider in day VFR flight unless it is equipped with

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} an altimeter;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} an airspeed indicator;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a magnetic compass or a magnetic direction indicator;
  and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsections 601.08(2) and 601.09(2), a
  radiocommunication system adequate to permit two-way communication on
  the appropriate frequency when the glider is operated within

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} Class C or Class D airspace,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} an MF area, unless the aircraft is operated
    pursuant to subsection 602.97(3), or

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the ADIZ.

##### [Seat and Safety Belt Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996645 .Subheading}

- **[[605.22]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.22
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection 605.23, no
  person shall operate an aircraft other than a balloon unless it is
  equipped with a seat and safety belt for each person on board the
  aircraft other than an infant.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply to a person operating
  an aircraft that was type-certificated with a safety belt designed for
  two persons.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A safety belt referred to in subsection (1) shall
  include a latching device of the metal-to-metal type.

##### [Restraint System Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996650 .Subheading}

**[[605.23]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.23 .sectionLabel}** An aircraft may
be operated without being equipped in accordance with section 605.22 in
respect of the following persons if a restraint system that is secured
to the primary structure of the aircraft is provided for each person who
is

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} carried on a stretcher or in an incubator or other
  similar device;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} carried for the purpose of parachuting from the
  aircraft; or

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} required to work in the vicinity of an opening in the
  aircraft structure.

##### [Shoulder Harness Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996655 .Subheading}

- **[[605.24]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.24
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an
  aeroplane, other than a small aeroplane manufactured before July 18,
  1978, unless each front seat or, if the aeroplane has a flight deck,
  each seat on the flight deck is equipped with a safety belt that
  includes a shoulder harness.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Except as provided in section 705.75, no person shall
  operate a transport category aeroplane unless each flight attendant
  seat is equipped with a safety belt that includes a shoulder harness.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate a small aeroplane
  manufactured after December 12, 1986, the initial type certificate of
  which provides for not more than nine passenger seats, excluding any
  pilot seats, unless each forward- or aft-facing seat is equipped with
  a safety belt that includes a shoulder harness.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate a helicopter manufactured
  after September 16, 1992, the initial type certificate of which
  specifies that the helicopter is certified as belonging to the normal
  or transport category, unless each seat is equipped with a safety belt
  that includes a shoulder harness.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} No person operating an aircraft shall conduct any of
  the following flight operations unless the aircraft is equipped with a
  seat and a safety belt that includes a shoulder harness for each
  person on board the aircraft:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} aerobatic manoeuvres;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} class B, C or D external load operations conducted
    by a helicopter; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} aerial application, or aerial inspection other than
    flight inspection for the purpose of calibrating electronic
    navigation aids, conducted at altitudes below 500 feet AGL.

##### [General Use of Safety Belts and Restraint Systems]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996665 .Subheading}

- **[[605.25]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.25
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft
  shall direct all of the persons on board the aircraft to fasten safety
  belts, including any shoulder harness,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} during movement of the aircraft on the surface;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} during take-off and landing; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} at any time during flight that the pilot-in-command
    considers it necessary that safety belts be fastened.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The directions referred to in subsection (1) also
  apply to the use of the following restraint systems:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a child restraint system;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a restraint system used by a person who is engaged
    in parachute descents; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a restraint system used by a person when working in
    the vicinity of an opening in the aircraft structure.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where an aircraft crew includes flight attendants and
  the pilot-in-command anticipates that the level of turbulence will
  exceed light turbulence, the pilot-in-command shall immediately direct
  each flight attendant to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} discontinue duties relating to service;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} secure the cabin; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} occupy a seat and fasten the safety belt provided,
    including any shoulder harness.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where an aircraft is experiencing turbulence and the
  in-charge flight attendant considers it necessary, the in-charge
  flight attendant shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} direct all of the passengers to fasten their safety
    belts; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} direct all flight attendants to discontinue duties
    relating to service, to secure the cabin, to occupy the assigned
    seats and to fasten the safety belts provided, including any
    shoulder harness, and to do so oneself.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} Where the in-charge flight attendant has given
  directions in accordance with subsection (4), the in-charge flight
  attendant shall so inform the pilot-in-command.

##### [Use of Passenger Safety Belts and Restraint Systems]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996685 .Subheading}

- **[[605.26]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.26
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where the pilot-in-command or the
  in-charge flight attendant directs that safety belts be fastened,
  every passenger who is not an infant shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the passenger's safety belt, including
    any shoulder harness, or restraint system is properly adjusted and
    securely fastened;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if responsible for an infant for which no child
    restraint system is provided, hold the infant securely in the
    passenger's arms; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if responsible for a person who is using a child
    restraint system, ensure that the person is properly secured.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No passenger shall be responsible for more than one
  infant.

##### [Use of Crew Member Safety Belts]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996692 .Subheading}

- **[[605.27]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.27
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), the crew
  members on an aircraft shall be seated at their stations with their
  safety belts, including any shoulder harness, fastened

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} during take-off and landing;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} at any time that the pilot-in-command directs; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of crew members who are flight
    attendants, at any time that the in-charge flight attendant so
    directs pursuant to paragraph 605.25(4)(b).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where the pilot-in-command directs that safety belts
  be fastened by illuminating the safety belt sign, a crew member is not
  required to comply with paragraph (1)(b)

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} during movement of the aircraft on the surface or
    during flight, if the crew member is performing duties relating to
    the safety of the aircraft or of the passengers on board;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is experiencing light
    turbulence, if the crew member is a flight attendant and is
    performing duties relating to the passengers on board; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the crew member is occupying a crew rest
    facility during cruise flight and the restraint system for that
    facility is properly adjusted and securely fastened.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command shall ensure that at least one
  pilot is seated at the flight controls with safety belt, including any
  shoulder harness, fastened during flight time, except when an air
  operator operating an aircraft under Subpart 4 of Part VI or Subpart
  2, 3, 4 or 5 of Part VII establishes procedures that allow flight crew
  members, while in cruise flight, to remove their shoulder harnesses at
  flight altitudes at or above 10,000 feet ASL.

##### [Child Restraint System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996703 .Subheading}

- **[[605.28]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.28
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No operator of an aircraft shall
  permit the use of a child restraint system on board the aircraft
  unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person using the child restraint system is
    accompanied by a parent or guardian who will attend to the safety of
    the person during the flight;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the weight and height of the person using the child
    restraint system are within the range specified by the manufacturer;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the child restraint system bears a legible label
    indicating the applicable design standards and date of manufacture;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the child restraint system is properly secured by
    the safety belt of a forward-facing seat that is not located in an
    emergency exit row and does not block access to an aisle; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the tether strap is used according to the
    manufacturer's instructions or, where subsection (2) applies,
    secured so as not to pose a hazard to the person using the child
    restraint system or to any other person.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a seat incorporates design features to reduce
  occupant loads, such as the crushing or separation of certain
  components, and the seat is in compliance with the applicable design
  standards, no person shall use the tether strap on the child restraint
  system to secure the system.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Every passenger who is responsible for a person who
  is using a child restraint system on board an aircraft shall be

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} seated in a seat adjacent to the seat to which the
    child restraint system is secured;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} familiar with the manufacturer's installation
    instructions for the child restraint system; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} familiar with the method of securing the person in
    the child restraint system and of releasing the person from it.

##### [Flight Control Locks]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996716 .Subheading}

**[[605.29]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.29 .sectionLabel}** No operator of an
aircraft shall permit the use of a flight control lock in respect of the
aircraft unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the flight control lock is incapable of becoming
  engaged when the aircraft is being operated; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} an unmistakable warning is provided to the person
  operating the aircraft whenever the flight control lock is engaged.

##### [De-icing or Anti-icing Equipment]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996720 .Subheading}

**[[605.30]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.30 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
conduct a take-off or continue a flight in an aircraft where icing
conditions are reported to exist or are forecast to be encountered along
the route of flight unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command determines that the aircraft is
  adequately equipped to operate in icing conditions in accordance with
  the standards of airworthiness under which the type certificate for
  that aircraft was issued; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} current weather reports or pilot reports indicate
  that icing conditions no longer exist.

##### [Oxygen Equipment and Supply]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996724 .Subheading}

- **[[605.31]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.31
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an
  unpressurized aircraft unless it is equipped with sufficient oxygen
  dispensing units and oxygen supply to comply with the requirements set
  out in the table to this subsection.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate a pressurized aircraft unless
  it is equipped with sufficient oxygen dispensing units and oxygen
  supply to provide, in the event of cabin pressurization failure at the
  most critical point during the flight, sufficient oxygen to continue
  the flight to an aerodrome suitable for landing while complying with
  the requirements of the table to this subsection.

  <p>Note 3: The minimum supply is that quantity of oxygen necessary for a

##### [Use of Oxygen]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996742 .Subheading}

- **[[605.32]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.32
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where an aircraft is operated at
  cabin-pressure-altitudes above 10,000 feet ASL but not exceeding
  13,000 feet ASL, each crew member shall wear an oxygen mask and use
  supplemental oxygen for any part of the flight at those altitudes that
  is more than 30 minutes in duration.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where an aircraft is operated at
  cabin-pressure-altitudes above 13,000 feet ASL, each person on board
  the aircraft shall wear an oxygen mask and use supplemental oxygen for
  the duration of the flight at those altitudes.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The pilot at the flight controls of an aircraft shall
  use an oxygen mask if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is not equipped with quick-donning
    oxygen masks and is operated at or above flight level 250; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is equipped with quick-donning oxygen
    masks and is operated above flight level 410.

##### [Flight Data Recorder]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996749 .Subheading}

- **[[605.33]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.33
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This section applies in respect of
  the following multi-engined turbine-powered aircraft:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft in respect of which a type certificate
    has been issued authorizing the transport of 30 or fewer passengers,
    configured for 10 or more passenger seats and manufactured after
    October 11, 1991;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an aeroplane in respect of which a type certificate
    has been issued authorizing the transport of 30 or fewer passengers
    and configured for 20 to 30 passenger seats;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft in respect of which a type certificate
    has been issued authorizing the transport of more than 30
    passengers; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} an aircraft in respect of which a type certificate
    has been issued authorizing the transport of cargo only and operated
    under Subpart 5 of Part VII.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), no person shall dispatch
  or conduct a take-off in an aircraft unless it is equipped with a
  flight data recorder that conforms to section 551.100 of Chapter 551
  of the Airworthiness Manual and section 625.33 of Standard 625 ---
  Aircraft Equipment and Maintenance of the General Operating and Flight
  Rules Standards.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), no person shall operate an
  aircraft unless the flight data recorder is operated continuously from
  the start of the take-off until the completion of the landing.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subsections (2) and (3) do not apply in respect of an
  aircraft without a serviceable flight data recorder if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a minimum equipment list has been approved by the
    Minister in respect of the operator of the aircraft under subsection
    605.07(3) and the aircraft is operated in accordance with the
    minimum equipment list; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a minimum equipment list has not been approved by
    the Minister in respect of the operator of the aircraft and the
    following conditions are met:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the period during which the aircraft is operated
      without a serviceable flight data recorder does not exceed 90 days
      from the day on which the flight data recorder ceased to be
      serviceable,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} aircraft technical records that indicate the
      date on which the flight data recorder ceased to be serviceable
      are carried on board the aircraft,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is required to be equipped with a
      cockpit voice recorder under section 605.34, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the cockpit voice recorder is serviceable.

##### [Underwater Locating Device for Flight Data Recorder]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1137542 .Subheading}

**[[605.33.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.33.1 .sectionLabel}** No person
shall operate an aircraft that is required to be equipped with a flight
data recorder under section 605.33 unless the aircraft is equipped with
a serviceable underwater locating device for its flight data recorder
that conforms to section 551.100 of Chapter 551 of the Airworthiness
Manual.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-130, s. 4](#1129295-1137545){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1129295-1137545.html"}
:::

##### [Cockpit Voice Recorder]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996759 .Subheading}

- **[[605.34]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.34
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This section applies in respect of
  the following aircraft:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a multi-engined turbine-powered aircraft that is
    configured for six or more passenger seats and is operated by two
    flight crew members, regardless of the minimum crew requirements set
    out in the aircraft type certificate or the subpart under which the
    aircraft is operated;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a turbine-powered aeroplane that was
    type-certificated on or after January 1, 2016 and for which more
    than one flight crew member is required by the aircraft type
    certificate or by the subpart under which the aeroplane is operated;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a turbine-powered aeroplane with an MCTOW of more
    than 27 000 kg (59,525 pounds) that was type-certificated after
    September 30, 1969 and was manufactured before January 1, 1987;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a large aeroplane that was manufactured on or after
    January 1, 1987; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a transport category helicopter with an MCTOW of
    more than 7 000 kg (15,400 pounds).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), no person shall dispatch
  or conduct a take-off in an aircraft unless the aircraft is equipped
  with a cockpit voice recorder that conforms to section 551.101 of
  Chapter 551 of the Airworthiness Manual and section 625.34 of Standard
  625 --- Aircraft Equipment and Maintenance of the General Operating
  and Flight Rules Standards.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), no person shall operate an
  aircraft unless the cockpit voice recorder is operated continuously
  from the time at which electrical power is first provided to the
  recorder before the flight to the time at which electrical power is
  removed from the recorder after the flight.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subsections (2) and (3) do not apply in respect of an
  aircraft without a serviceable cockpit voice recorder if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a minimum equipment list has been approved by the
    Minister in respect of the operator of the aircraft under subsection
    605.07(3) and the aircraft is operated in accordance with the
    minimum equipment list;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a minimum equipment list has not been approved by
    the Minister in respect of the operator of the aircraft and the
    following conditions are met:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the period during which the aircraft is operated
      without a serviceable cockpit voice recorder does not exceed 90
      days from the day on which the cockpit voice recorder ceased to be
      serviceable,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} aircraft technical records that indicate the
      date on which the cockpit voice recorder ceased to be serviceable
      are carried on board the aircraft,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is required to be equipped with a
      flight data recorder under section 605.33, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the flight data recorder is serviceable; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is described in paragraph (1)(a), its
    operator is authorized to conduct single-pilot operations in an air
    operator certificate issued under Subpart 3 of Part VII and the
    following conditions are met:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the period during which the aircraft is operated
      without a serviceable cockpit voice recorder does not exceed 45
      days from the day on which the cockpit voice recorder ceased to be
      serviceable,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the requirements of paragraph 703.66(a) cannot
      be met because the auto-pilot is not serviceable,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is operated by two pilots who meet
      the requirements of section 703.88, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} aircraft technical records that indicate the
      dates on which the cockpit voice recorder and the auto-pilot
      ceased to be serviceable are carried on board the aircraft.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} No person shall erase any communications that have
  been recorded by a cockpit voice recorder.

##### [Underwater Locating Device for Cockpit Voice Recorder]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1137550 .Subheading}

- **[[605.34.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.34.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no person
  shall operate an aircraft in respect of which a type certificate has
  been issued authorizing the transport of more than 30 passengers
  unless the aircraft is equipped with a serviceable underwater locating
  device for its cockpit voice recorder that conforms to section 551.101
  of Chapter 551 of the Airworthiness Manual and subsection 625.34(5) of
  Standard 625 --- Aircraft Equipment and Maintenance of the General
  Operating and Flight Rules Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of an
  aircraft that is equipped with a flight data recorder and cockpit
  voice recorder that are installed adjacent to each other and are not
  likely to be separated during a crash impact.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-130, s. 4](#1129295-1137594){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1129295-1137594.html"}
:::

##### [Use of Microphones]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1137643 .Subheading}

**[[605.34.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.34.2 .sectionLabel}** If an
aircraft is equipped to continuously record audio signals by means of a
boom microphone or mask microphones, each flight crew member shall use
the boom microphone or his or her mask microphone while the aircraft is
operated below 10,000 feet ASL.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-130, s. 4](#1129295-1137646){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1129295-1137646.html"}
:::

##### [Data Link Communications]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1398530 .Subheading}

**[[605.34.3]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.34.3 .sectionLabel}** If an
aircraft is equipped with a cockpit voice recorder and data-link
communications equipment, no person shall dispatch or conduct a take-off
in the aircraft unless the aircraft is equipped with a data-link
recorder that conforms to section 551.101 of Chapter 551 of the
Airworthiness Manual and section 625.34 of Standard 625 --- Aircraft
Equipment and Maintenance of the General Operating and Flight Rules
Standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-130, s. 6](#1129302-1398533){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1129302-1398533.html"}
:::

##### [Transponder and Automatic Pressure-Altitude Reporting Equipment]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996772 .Subheading}

- **[[605.35]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.35
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aircraft,
  other than a balloon or glider, in transponder airspace, unless the
  aircraft is equipped with a transponder and automatic
  pressure-altitude reporting equipment.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of an
  aircraft without a serviceable transponder and automatic
  pressure-altitude reporting equipment if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a minimum equipment list has been approved by the
    Minister in respect of the operator of the aircraft under subsection
    605.07(3) and the aircraft is operated in accordance with the
    minimum equipment list; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a minimum equipment list has not been approved by
    the Minister in respect of the operator of the aircraft and the
    aircraft is operated

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} to the next aerodrome of intended landing, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} after that landing, in accordance with an air
      traffic control clearance, to complete a planned flight schedule
      or to proceed to a maintenance facility.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of an
  aircraft without a serviceable transponder and automatic
  pressure-altitude reporting equipment if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is within airspace referred to in
    section 601.03;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an air traffic control unit provides an air traffic
    control service in respect of that airspace;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the air traffic control unit received a request
    from a person to operate the aircraft within that airspace before
    the aircraft entered the airspace;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the air traffic control unit authorized the person
    to operate the aircraft; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} aviation safety is not likely to be affected.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of an
  aircraft that is operated as part of a special aviation event without
  a serviceable transponder and automatic pressure-altitude reporting
  equipment if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is within class A, B, C, D or E
    airspace; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an air traffic control unit provides an air traffic
    control service in respect of that airspace.

##### [Altitude Alerting System or Device]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996786 .Subheading}

- **[[605.36]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.36
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no person
  shall conduct a take-off in a turbo-jet-powered aeroplane unless it is
  equipped with an altitude alerting system or device that conforms to
  the Aircraft Equipment and Maintenance Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of an
  aeroplane without a serviceable altitude alerting system or device if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a minimum equipment list has been approved by the
    Minister in respect of the operator of the aeroplane pursuant to
    subsection 605.07(3) and the aeroplane is operated in accordance
    with the minimum equipment list; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a minimum equipment list has not been approved by
    the Minister in respect of the operator of the aeroplane and the
    aeroplane is operated

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} from the place where the operator or
      pilot-in-command takes possession of the aeroplane to a place
      where the aeroplane can be equipped with such a system or device,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} for the sole purpose of conducting a flight
      test, a competency check, a pilot proficiency check or flight crew
      member training, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} where the system or device becomes
      unserviceable after take-off, until it reaches an aerodrome at
      which the system or device can be repaired or replaced.

##### [GPWS]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996797 .Subheading}

- **[[605.37]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.37
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) and (3),
  no person operating under Subpart 4 or 5 of Part VII shall conduct a
  take-off in a turbo-jet-powered aeroplane that has a MCTOW of more
  than 15 000 kg (33,069 pounds) and for which a type certificate has
  been issued authorizing the transport of 10 or more passengers, unless
  the aeroplane is equipped with a GPWS.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An aeroplane referred to in subsection (1) may be
  operated without a serviceable GPWS if a minimum equipment list has
  been approved by the Minister in respect of the operator of the
  aeroplane pursuant to subsection 605.07(3) and the aeroplane is
  operated in accordance with the minimum equipment list.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where, in the interests of aviation safety, it is
  necessary during a flight to deactivate any mode of a GPWS, the
  pilot-in-command of the aeroplane may deactivate that mode if the
  deactivation is performed in accordance with the aircraft flight
  manual, aircraft operating manual, flight manual supplement or minimum
  equipment list.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} This section

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} applies only in respect of aeroplanes manufactured
    on or before the day on which this subsection comes into force; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} shall cease to apply on the expiry of two years
    after that day.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2012-136, s. 9
:::

##### [ELT]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996807 .Subheading}

- **[[605.38]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.38
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), no person
  shall operate an aircraft unless it is equipped with one or more ELTs
  in accordance with subsection (2).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An aircraft set out in column I of an item of the
  table to this subsection shall, for the area of operation set out in
  column II of the item, be equipped with the quantity and type of ELTs
  referred to in column III of that item, which ELTs shall be armed, if
  so specified in the aircraft flight manual, aircraft operating manual,
  pilot operating handbook or equivalent document provided by the
  manufacturer.

  <figure id="1328342">

  class="table table-hover table-striped tablePointsize8 topdouble topbot">

  </tr>

  to in section 551.104 of Chapter 551 — Aircraft Equipment and

  </tr>

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An aircraft may be operated without an ELT on board
  if the aircraft

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is a glider, balloon, airship, ultra-light
    aeroplane or gyroplane;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is registered under the laws of a contracting state
    or a state that is a party to an agreement entered into with Canada
    relating to interstate flying, is equipped with a serviceable
    emergency beacon that transmits on the 406 MHz frequency with a
    tested life of at least 24 hours and

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} has a Class 1 or Class 2 Type Approval
      Certificate issued by the international search and rescue
      Cospas-Sarsat Council, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} is registered with the appropriate authority of
      the country identified in the coded message transmitted by the
      emergency beacon;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} is operated by the holder of a flight training unit
    operating certificate, engaged in flight training and operated
    within 25 nautical miles of the aerodrome of departure;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} is engaged in a flight test;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} is a new aircraft engaged in flight operations
    related to manufacture, preparation or delivery of the aircraft;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} is operated for the purpose of permitting a person
    to conduct a parachute descent within 25 nautical miles of the
    aerodrome of departure; or

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} is operated in accordance with section 605.39.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} If an aircraft is equipped with one or more ELTs that
  transmit on the 406 MHz frequency, the owner shall register each ELT
  with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the Canadian Beacon Registry; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the appropriate authority of the country identified
    in the coded message transmitted by the ELT.

##### [ELT --- Frequencies]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1328177 .Subheading}

- **[[605.38.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.38.1
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aircraft
  under a private operator registration document or in a commercial air
  service unless the aircraft is equipped with one or more ELTs that
  transmit simultaneously on the 406 MHz and 121.5 MHz frequencies.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person may operate an aircraft, other than an
  aircraft referred to in subsection (1), if it is equipped with one or
  more ELTs that transmit on one or both of the following frequencies:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 121.5 MHz; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 406 MHz.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-238, s. 6](#1273538-1328184){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1273538-1328184.html"}
:::

##### [Use of ELTs]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996834 .Subheading}

- **[[605.39]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.39
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An aircraft that is required to be
  equipped with one or more ELTs under section 605.38 may be operated
  without a serviceable ELT if the operator

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} repairs the ELT or removes it from the aircraft at
    the first aerodrome at which repairs or removal can be accomplished;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} on removal of the ELT, sends the ELT to a
    maintenance facility; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} displays on a readily visible placard within the
    aircraft cockpit, until the ELT is replaced, a notice stating that
    the ELT has been removed and setting out the date of its removal.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If an aircraft is required to have one ELT under
  section 605.38, the operator shall re-equip the aircraft with a
  serviceable ELT within

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 10 days after the date of removal, if the aircraft
    is operated under Subpart 4 or 5 of Part VII; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 30 days after the date of removal in the case of
    any other aircraft.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If an aircraft is required to have two ELTs under
  section 605.38, the operator shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if one of the ELTs is unserviceable, repair or
    replace it within 10 days after the date of removal; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if both ELTs are unserviceable, repair or replace

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} one ELT at the first aerodrome at which a repair
      or replacement can be accomplished, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the second ELT within 10 days after the date of
      removal.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-345, s. 3
:::

##### [ELT Activation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996850 .Subheading}

- **[[605.40]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.40
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no person
  shall activate an ELT except in an emergency.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person may activate an ELT, in accordance with the
  manufacturer's instructions, for the purpose of testing the ELT for a
  duration of not more than five seconds during the first five minutes
  of any hour UTC in the case of an ELT that transmits on the 121.5 MHz
  frequency or an ELT that transmits on both the 406 MHz and the 121.5
  MHz frequencies.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If an ELT has been inadvertently activated during
  flight, the pilot-in-command of the aircraft shall ensure, as soon as
  feasible, that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the nearest air traffic services unit or community
    aerodrome radio station is so informed; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the ELT is deactivated.

##### [Third Attitude Indicator]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996859 .Subheading}

- **[[605.41]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.41
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off
  in a turbo-jet-powered aeroplane that is operated under Part VII
  without a third attitude indicator that meets the requirements of
  section 625.41 of the Aircraft Equipment and Maintenance Standards
  unless the aeroplane

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} has a MCTOW of less than 5 700 kg (12,566 pounds);
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} was operated in Canada in a commercial air service
    on October 10, 1996.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off in a transport
  category aircraft without a third attitude indicator that meets the
  requirements of section 625.41 of the Aircraft Equipment and
  Maintenance Standards unless the aircraft

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is a transport category helicopter not operated in
    IFR flight;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is a transport category aeroplane powered by
    reciprocating engines that was manufactured before January 1, 1998;
    or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} is not operated pursuant to Part VII.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off in a
  turbo-propeller powered aeroplane that is operated under Part VII
  without a third attitude indicator that meets the requirements of
  section 625.41 of the Aircraft Equipment and Maintenance Standards
  unless the aeroplane

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} has a passenger seating configuration, excluding
    pilot seats, of 30 or fewer;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} has a payload capacity of 3 402 kg (7,500 pounds)
    or less; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} was manufactured prior to March 20, 1997.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} After December 20, 2010, no person shall conduct a
  take-off in a turbo-propeller powered aeroplane having a passenger
  seating configuration, excluding pilot seats, of 10 or more, and
  operated under Part VII, unless the aeroplane is equipped with a third
  attitude indicator that meets the requirements of section 625.41 of
  the Aircraft Equipment and Maintenance Standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-77, s. 22
- SOR/2015-160, s. 29(F)
:::

##### [TAWS]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996875 .Subheading}

- **[[605.42]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.42
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no
  operator shall operate a turbine-powered aeroplane that has a seating
  configuration, excluding pilot seats, of six or more, unless the
  aeroplane is equipped with an operative TAWS that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements for Class A or Class B
    equipment set out in CAN-TSO-C151a or a more recent version of it;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} meets the altitude accuracy requirements set out in
    section 551.102 of Chapter 551 of the Airworthiness Manual; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} has a terrain and airport database compatible with
    the area of operation.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operator may operate the aeroplane without its
  being equipped with an operative TAWS if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane is operated in day VFR only;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the event that a minimum equipment list has not
    been approved by the Minister and subject to subsection 605.08(1),
    the operation takes place within the three days after the day on
    which the failure of the TAWS occurs; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} it is necessary for the pilot-in-command to
    deactivate, in the interests of aviation safety, the TAWS or any of
    its modes and the pilot-in-command does so in accordance with the
    aircraft flight manual, aircraft operating manual, flight manual
    supplement or minimum equipment list.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} This section does not apply in respect of aeroplanes
  manufactured on or before the day on which this section comes into
  force until the day that is two years after that day.

**\[605.43 to 605.83 reserved\]**

#### [Division III --- Aircraft Maintenance Requirements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-996889 .Subheading}

##### [Aircraft Maintenance --- General]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996890 .Subheading}

- **[[605.84]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.84
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (3) and (4),
  no person shall conduct a take-off or permit a take-off to be
  conducted in an aircraft that is in the legal custody and control of
  the person, other than an aircraft operated under a special
  certificate of airworthiness in the owner-maintenance or amateur-built
  classification, unless the aircraft

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is maintained in accordance with any airworthiness
    limitations applicable to the aircraft type design;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements of any airworthiness
    directive issued under section 521.427; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} except as provided in subsection (2), meets the
    requirements of any notices that are equivalent to airworthiness
    directives and that are issued by

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the competent authority of the foreign state
      that, at the time the notice was issued, is responsible for the
      type certification of the aircraft, engine, propeller or
      appliance, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} for an aeronautical product in respect of which
      no type certificate has been issued, the competent authority of
      the foreign state that manufactured the aeronautical product.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a conflict between an airworthiness
  directive issued by the Minister under section 521.427 and a foreign
  notice, the airworthiness directive prevails.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall exempt the owner of a Canadian
  aircraft from the requirement to comply with all or part of an
  airworthiness directive, subject to appropriate conditions relating to
  aviation safety, as specified in Appendix H of the Aircraft Equipment
  and Maintenance Standards, where the owner demonstrates to the
  Minister that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} under circumstances specified in the exemption
    request, compliance is impractical or unnecessary; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the exemption will provide a level of safety that
    is equivalent to that required by the airworthiness directive.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall approve an alternative means of
  compliance with an airworthiness directive, for reasons set out in the
  approval, where the Minister is satisfied that the proposed
  alternative will maintain the level of safety that is provided for by
  the compliance time, the modification, the restriction, the
  replacement, the special inspection or the procedure set out in the
  airworthiness directive.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2000-389, s. 1
- SOR/2002-112, s. 13
- SOR/2009-280, s. 35
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-605.84-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 605.84"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Maintenance Release and Elementary Work]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996905 .Subheading}

- **[[605.85]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.85
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) and (3),
  no person shall conduct a take-off in an aircraft, or permit a
  take-off to be conducted in an aircraft that is in the legal custody
  and control of the person, where that aircraft has undergone
  maintenance, unless the maintenance has been certified by the signing
  of a maintenance release pursuant to section 571.10.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a maintenance release is conditional on the
  satisfactory completion of a test flight pursuant to subsection
  571.10(4), the aircraft may be operated for the purpose of the test
  flight if no person is carried on board other than flight crew members
  and persons necessary for the purpose of making observations that are
  essential to the test flight.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Following a test flight conducted pursuant to
  subsection (2), the pilot-in-command shall enter the results of the
  test flight in the journey log and, where the entry indicates that the
  results of the test flight are satisfactory, that entry completes the
  maintenance release required by subsection (1).

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} No maintenance release is required in respect of
  tasks identified as elementary work in the Aircraft Equipment and
  Maintenance Standards.

##### [Maintenance Schedule]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996911 .Subheading}

- **[[605.86]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.86
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), no person
  shall conduct a take-off in an aircraft, or permit a take-off to be
  conducted in an aircraft that is in the person's legal custody and
  control, unless the aircraft is maintained in accordance with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a maintenance schedule that conforms to the
    Aircraft Equipment and Maintenance Standards; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is operated under Subpart 6 of
    Part IV or under Part VII, or is a large aircraft, a turbine-powered
    pressurized aircraft or an airship, a maintenance schedule approved
    by the Minister in respect of the aircraft operator pursuant to
    subsection (2).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall approve a maintenance schedule in
  respect of an aircraft if the schedule conforms to the Aircraft
  Equipment and Maintenance Standards.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall authorize an operator to deviate
  from the requirements of the applicable maintenance schedule where the
  operator

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} submits a request in writing to the Minister in
    accordance with the Aircraft Equipment and Maintenance Standards;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} demonstrates that the deviation will not affect
    aviation safety.

##### [Transfer of Aeronautical Products between Maintenance Schedules]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996920 .Subheading}

**[[605.87]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.87 .sectionLabel}** No aeronautical
product shall be maintained in accordance with a maintenance schedule
that is different from the one under which it was previously maintained
unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aeronautical product has been subjected to an
  inspection that establishes it on the new maintenance schedule; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the times remaining until each action on the new
  maintenance schedule is to be taken have been established in
  accordance with the Aircraft Equipment and Maintenance Standards.

##### [Inspection after Abnormal Occurrences]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996924 .Subheading}

- **[[605.88]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.88
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off
  in an aircraft that has been subjected to any abnormal occurrence
  unless the aircraft has been inspected for damage in accordance with
  Appendix G of the Aircraft Equipment and Maintenance Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where the inspection referred to in subsection (1)
  does not involve disassembly, it may be performed by the
  pilot-in-command.

**\[605.89 to 605.91 reserved\]**

#### [Division IV --- Technical Records]{.HTitleText3} {#h-996929 .Subheading}

##### [Requirement to Keep Technical Records]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996930 .Subheading}

- **[[605.92]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.92
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every owner of an aircraft shall
  keep the following technical records in respect of the aircraft:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a journey log;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsections (2) and (3), a separate
    technical record for the airframe, each installed engine and each
    variable-pitch propeller; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} except where otherwise provided under the terms of
    a fleet empty weight and balance program referred to in subsection
    706.06(3), an empty weight and balance report that meets the
    applicable standards set out in Standard 571 --- Maintenance.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The technical records required by paragraph (1)(b)
  may consist of separate technical records for each component installed
  in the airframe, engine or propeller.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a balloon or glider, or an aircraft
  operated under a special certificate of airworthiness in the
  owner-maintenance or amateur-built classification, all entries in
  respect of the technical records referred to in paragraphs (1)(b)
  and (c) may be kept in the journey log.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-112, s. 14

  ajax-after="1126379-1131031.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-605.92-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 605.92"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Technical Records --- General]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996940 .Subheading}

- **[[605.93]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.93
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every person who makes an entry in a
  technical record shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} make the entry accurately, legibly and in a
    permanent manner;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} enter the person's name and signature or employee
    identifier or, where the record is kept as electronic data, enter
    the person's user code or an equivalent security designation; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} date the entry.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where the owner of an aircraft keeps the technical
  records for the aircraft as electronic data, the owner shall ensure
  that the electronic data system that is used complies with section
  103.04 and the Aircraft Equipment and Maintenance Standards.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The owner of an aircraft shall ensure that all of the
  necessary measures are taken to protect the technical records for the
  aircraft from damage and loss.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Every person who brings into use a new volume of an
  existing technical record shall make the entries relating to the
  preceding volume that are necessary to ensure that an unbroken
  chronological record is maintained.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (6), where a person alters an
  entry on a technical record for the purpose of correcting the entry,
  the person shall do so by striking out the incorrect entry in such a
  manner that the underlying information remains legible, and inserting
  the correct entry together with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the date of the alteration;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the reason for the alteration, if it is necessary
    to clarify why the alteration was made; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the person's name and signature or employee
    identifier or, where the record is kept as electronic data, the
    person's user code or equivalent security designation.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} Where a correction referred to in subsection (5) is
  being made to a technical record that is maintained as electronic
  data, the correction shall be made in a manner that does not render
  the original data inaccessible.

##### [Journey Log Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996954 .Subheading}

- **[[605.94]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.94
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The particulars set out in column I
  of an item in Schedule I to this Division shall be recorded in the
  journey log at the time set out in column II of the item and by the
  person responsible for making entries set out in column III of that
  item.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall make a single entry in a journey log
  in respect of a series of flights unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is operated by the same
    pilot-in-command throughout the series; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a daily flight record is used pursuant to section
    406.56.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The owner of an aircraft shall retain every entry in
  a journey log for a period of not less than one year.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Unless recorded in the operational flight plan or
  operational flight data sheet, the pilot-in-command of an aircraft
  engaged in a commercial air service and operating in international
  flight shall record in the journey log the following particulars in
  respect of each flight:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the names of all of the crew members and their duty
    assignments;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the places and times of departure and arrival;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the flight time;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the nature of the flight, such as private, aerial
    work, scheduled or non-scheduled; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} any incidents or observations relating to the
    flight.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-77, s. 23
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-605.94-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 605.94"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Journey Log --- Carrying on Board]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996969 .Subheading}

- **[[605.95]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.95
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no person
  shall conduct a take-off in an aircraft unless the journey log is on
  board the aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person may conduct a take-off in an aircraft
  without carrying the journey log on board where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} it is not planned that the aircraft will land and
    shut down at any location other than the point of departure; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is a balloon and the journey log is
    immediately available to the pilot-in-command

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} prior to commencing a flight, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} on completion of the flight.

##### [Requirements for Technical Records Other Than the Journey Log]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996977 .Subheading}

- **[[605.96]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.96
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The particulars set out in column I
  of an item in Schedule II to this Division shall be recorded in the
  appropriate technical record at the time set out in column II of the
  item and by the person responsible for making entries set out in
  column III of that item.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where particulars of any maintenance performed on an
  aircraft are transferred from the journey log at the time set out in
  column II of item 4 of Schedule II to this Division, the person
  responsible for the entry shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} transcribe the particulars and include the name and
    identification number of the person who made the original entry; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the pages of the journey log have detachable
    copies, attach the copy of the page containing these particulars to
    the applicable technical record.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where a component is installed on a higher assembly,
  the technical record for that component shall become a part of the
  technical record for the higher assembly.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Except in the case of the journey log, the owner of
  an aircraft shall retain each technical record for the applicable
  period set out in the Aircraft Equipment and Maintenance Standards.

##### [Transfer of Records]{.HTitleText4} {#h-996985 .Subheading}

**[[605.97]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-605.97 .sectionLabel}** Every owner of an
aircraft who transfers title of an aircraft, airframe, engine, propeller
or appliance to another person shall, at the time of transfer, also
deliver to that person all of the technical records that relate to that
aeronautical product.

**\[605.98 to 605.110 reserved\]**
