### [Subpart 6 --- Miscellaneous]{.HTitleText2} {#h-997008 .Subheading}

#### [Munitions of War]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997009 .Subheading}

**[[606.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-606.01 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
carry weapons, ammunition or other equipment designed for use in war on
board an aircraft unless the aircraft is a Canadian aircraft or the
Minister has authorized the carriage of such equipment.

#### [Liability Insurance]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997011 .Subheading}

- **[[606.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-606.02
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This section applies to every owner
  of an aircraft, other than a remotely piloted aircraft, that is
  registered in Canada or registered under the laws of a foreign state
  and operated in Canada, if the owner is not required to subscribe to
  liability insurance in respect of the aircraft under section 7 of the
  [Air Transportation Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-88-58).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), none of the following
  aircraft owners shall operate an aircraft unless, in respect of every
  incident related to the operation of the aircraft, the owner has
  subscribed for liability insurance covering risks of injury to or
  death of passengers in an amount that is not less than the amount
  determined by multiplying \$300,000 by the number of passengers on
  board the aircraft:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an air operator;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the holder of a flight training unit operator
    certificate; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the operator of a balloon in which fare-paying
    passengers are carried on board pursuant to Subpart 3.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The insurance coverage referred to in subsection (2)
  need not extend to any passenger who

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is an employee of an owner referred to in paragraph
    (2)(a), (b) or (c), if workers' compensation legislation governing a
    claim for damages against the owner by the employee is applicable;
    or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is carried on board the aircraft for the purpose of
    conducting a parachute descent, where the air operator has posted a
    readily visible notice to inform passengers, before embarking, that
    there is no insurance coverage for parachutists.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} No aircraft owner not referred to in paragraph
  (2)(a), (b) or (c) shall operate an aircraft of more than 2 268 kg
  (5,000 pounds) maximum permissible take-off weight unless the owner
  has, in respect of the aircraft, subscribed for liability insurance
  covering risks of injury to or death of passengers, other than
  passengers carried on board that aircraft for the purpose of
  conducting a parachute descent, in an amount not less than the amount
  determined by multiplying \$300,000 by the number of passengers on
  board the aircraft.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} No aircraft owner referred to in paragraph
  (2)(a), (b) or (c) shall operate an aircraft unless, in respect of
  every incident related to the operation of the aircraft, the owner has
  subscribed for liability insurance covering risks of public liability
  in an amount that is not less than

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} \$1,000,000, where the maximum permissible take-off
    weight of the aircraft is not greater than 3 402 kg (7,500 pounds);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} \$2,000,000, where the maximum permissible take-off
    weight of the aircraft is greater than 3 402 kg (7,500 pounds) but
    not greater than 8 165 kg (18,000 pounds); and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} where the maximum permissible take-off weight of
    the aircraft is greater than 8 165 kg (18,000 pounds), \$2,000,000
    plus an amount determined by multiplying \$150 by the number of
    pounds by which the maximum permissible take-off weight of the
    aircraft exceeds 8 165 kg (18,000 pounds).

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} No aircraft owner referred to in paragraph
  (2)(a), (b) or (c) shall, in order to comply with subsections (2), (4)
  and (5), subscribe for any liability insurance that contains an
  exclusion or waiver provision that reduces the insurance coverage for
  any incident below the applicable minimum determined pursuant to those
  subsections, unless that provision

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is a standard exclusion clause adopted by the
    international aviation insurance industry that applies in respect of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} war, hijacking and other perils,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} noise, pollution and other perils, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} radioactive contamination;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is in respect of a chemical drift;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} includes a statement that the insurance does not
    apply in respect of liability assumed by the owner under any
    contract or agreement unless the liability would have attached to
    the owner even in the absence of such a contract or agreement; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} includes a statement that the policy is void if the
    owner has concealed or misrepresented any material fact or
    circumstance concerning the insurance or the subject thereof or if
    there is any fraud, attempted fraud or false statement by the owner
    touching any matter relating to the insurance or the subject
    thereof, either before or after an incident.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} An aircraft owner referred to in paragraph
  (2)(a), (b) or (c) may comply with subsections (2), (4) and (5) by
  subscribing for comprehensive single limit liability insurance that
  consists of a single policy or a combination of primary and
  supplementary policies.

- [(8)]{.lawlabel} No aircraft owner not referred to in paragraph
  (2)(a), (b) or (c) shall operate an aircraft unless, in respect of
  every incident related to the operation of the aircraft, the owner has
  subscribed for liability insurance covering risks of public liability
  in an amount that is not less than

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} \$100,000, where the maximum permissible take-off
    weight of the aircraft is 1 043 kg (2,300 pounds) or less;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} \$500,000, where the maximum permissible take-off
    weight of the aircraft is greater than 1 043 kg (2,300 pounds) but
    not greater than 2 268 kg (5,000 pounds);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} \$1,000,000, where the maximum permissible take-off
    weight of the aircraft is greater than 2 268 kg (5,000 pounds) but
    not greater than 5 670 kg (12,500 pounds);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} \$2,000,000, where the maximum permissible take-off
    weight of the aircraft is greater than 5 670 kg (12,500 pounds) but
    not greater than 34 020 kg (75,000 pounds); and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} \$3,000,000, where the maximum permissible take-off
    weight of the aircraft is greater than 34 020 kg (75,000 pounds).

- [(9)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (10), no owner or operator of
  an aircraft shall operate the aircraft unless there is carried on
  board the aircraft proof that liability insurance is subscribed for in
  accordance with this section.

- [(10)]{.lawlabel} A balloon may be operated without the proof of
  insurance referred to in subsection (9) being carried on board if that
  proof is immediately available to the pilot-in-command

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} prior to commencing a flight; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} on completion of a flight.

#### [Synthetic Flight Training Equipment]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997045 .Subheading}

- **[[606.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-606.03
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Except in the case of a remotely
  piloted aircraft system, no person shall use synthetic flight training
  equipment to provide training or to conduct a skills assessment
  required under Part IV, this Part or Part VII, unless there is in
  force in respect of that equipment a flight simulator certificate or
  flight training device certificate issued under subsection (2) or an
  equivalent approval or certificate issued under the laws of a foreign
  state with which Canada has an agreement respecting such equipment.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall, where it is determined that the
  synthetic flight training equipment meets the standards set out for
  that equipment in the Aeroplane and Rotorcraft Simulator Manual, issue
  to the operator of that equipment a flight simulator certificate or
  flight training device certificate.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A certificate issued pursuant to subsection (2) shall
  set out the following information:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name of the operator of the synthetic flight
    training equipment;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the type, model or series number of aircraft
    represented;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the qualification level of the synthetic flight
    training equipment; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the date of issuance of the certificate.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} No certificate issued pursuant to subsection (2)
  remains in force unless the synthetic flight training equipment in
  respect of which the certificate has been issued

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} maintains the performance, function and other
    characteristics that are required for the issuance of the
    certificate, except in the cases set out in the Simulator Component
    Inoperative Guide (SCIG);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is maintained in accordance with the procedures set
    out in the Aeroplane and Rotorcraft Simulator Manual; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} is changed as required, where the aircraft type,
    model or series number represented by the synthetic flight training
    equipment undergoes a change as a result of the issuance of an
    airworthiness directive or an amendment to this Part or Part VII
    that affects the training being conducted.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} A certificate issued pursuant to subsection (2)
  remains in force where the synthetic flight training equipment in
  respect of which the certificate has been issued is re-evaluated

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a flight simulator, at least every
    six months; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a flight training device, at least
    every 12 months.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (7), the certificate referred
  to in subsection (5) remains in force

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a flight simulator, until the first
    day of the seventh month following the month in which the flight
    simulator was evaluated; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a flight training device, until the
    first day of the thirteenth month following the month in which the
    flight training device was evaluated.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may extend the period in respect of
  which a flight simulator certificate or a flight training device
  certificate is in force by up to 60 days where the Minister is of the
  opinion that aviation safety is not likely to be affected.

## [Part VII --- Commercial Air Services]{.HTitleText1} {#h-997067 .Part}

### [Division I --- General]{.HTitleText2} {#h-997068 .Subheading}

#### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997069 .Subheading}

**[[700.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.01 .sectionLabel}** In this Part,

[[acclimatized]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[acclimatized]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} describes a flight crew member
    whose biorhythm is aligned with local
    time; ([acclimaté]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[all-cargo aeroplane]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[all-cargo aeroplane]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an aeroplane that
    is equipped and used mainly for the carriage of goods; ([avion
    tout-cargo]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[areas of operation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[areas of operation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means areas in which
    operations are conducted between points in Canada, between points in
    Canada and points abroad, and between points abroad; ([régions
    d'exploitation]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[class 1 rest facility]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[class 1 rest facility]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a bunk or other
    horizontal surface located in an area that

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is separated from the flight deck and passenger
      cabin;

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} has devices to control the temperature and light;
      and

    - [(c)]{.lawlabel} is subject to a minimal level of noise and other
      disturbances; ([poste de repos de classe 1]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

[[class 2 rest facility]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[class 2 rest facility]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a seat that
    allows for a horizontal sleeping position in an area that

    - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is separated from passengers by a curtain or
      other means of separation that reduces light and sound;

    - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is equipped with portable oxygen equipment; and

    - [(c)]{.lawlabel} minimizes disturbances by passengers and crew
      members; ([poste de repos de classe 2]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

[[class 3 rest facility]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[class 3 rest facility]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a seat that
    reclines at least 40° from vertical and that has leg and foot
    support; ([poste de repos de classe 3]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[early duty]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[early duty]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means hours of work that begin
    between 02:00 and 06:59 at the location where the flight crew member
    is acclimatized; ([service de début de journée]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[employed on a full-time basis]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[employed on a full-time basis]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means working
    for an air operator on a continuous basis for at least the number of
    hours required to carry out the duties of the position for the safe
    operation of the commercial air service; ([employé à temps
    plein]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[extended charter]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[extended charter]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the charter of a
    Canadian commercial aircraft to a Canadian or foreign air operator
    for a period of 21 days or more in order to supplement the fleet of
    the charterer; ([affrètement de durée prolongée]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[farmer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[farmer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a person whose primary source
    of income is derived from the tillage of the soil, the raising of
    livestock or poultry, dairy farming, the growing of grain, fruit,
    vegetables or tobacco, or any other operation of a similar nature;
    ([agriculteur]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[flight crew member on reserve]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[flight crew member on reserve]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a flight
    crew member who has been designated by an air operator to be
    available to report for flight duty on notice of more than one hour;
    ([membre d'équipage de conduite en réserve]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[late duty]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[late duty]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means hours of work that end
    between midnight and 01:59 at the location where the flight crew
    member is acclimatized; ([service de fin de
    journée]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[local night's rest]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[local night's rest]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a rest period of at
    least nine hours that takes place between 22:30 and 09:30 at the
    location where the flight crew member is acclimatized; ([nuit de
    repos locale]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[main base]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[main base]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a location at which an air
    operator has personnel, aircraft and facilities for the conducting
    of aerial work or the operation of an air transport service and that
    is established as the principal place of business of the air
    operator; ([base principale]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[net take-off flight path]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[net take-off flight path]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the
    one-engine-inoperative flight path that starts at a height of 35
    feet at the end of the take-off distance required and extends to a
    height of at least 1,500 feet AGL, reduced at each point by a
    gradient of climb equal to 0.8 per cent for two-engined aeroplanes,
    0.9 per cent for three-engined aeroplanes and 1.0 per cent for
    four-engined aeroplanes; ([trajectoire nette de
    décollage]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[night duty]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[night duty]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means hours of work that begin
    between 13:00 and 01:59 and that end after 01:59 at a location where
    the flight crew member is acclimatized; ([service de
    nuit]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[operations between points abroad]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[operations between points abroad]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means air
    service operations that are conducted wholly outside Canada for any
    length of time; ([exploitation entre points à
    l'étranger]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[reserve availability period]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[reserve availability period]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the period
    in any period of 24 consecutive hours during which a flight crew
    member on reserve is available to report for flight duty; ([période
    de disponibilité en réserve]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[reserve duty period]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[reserve duty period]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the period that
    begins at the time that a flight crew member on reserve is available
    to report for flight duty and ends at the time that the flight duty
    period ends; ([période de service en réserve]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[single day free from duty]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[single day free from duty]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means time free
    from duty from the beginning of the first local night's rest until
    the end of the following local night's rest; ([journée isolée sans
    service]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[sub-base]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[sub-base]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a location at which an air
    operator positions aircraft and personnel and from which operational
    control is exercised in accordance with the air operator's
    operational control system; ([base secondaire]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[types of operation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[types of operation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means VFR, VFR at night
    and IFR operations; ([types de vols]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[types of service]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[types of service]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a domestic service, a
    scheduled international service, a non-scheduled international
    service and a sightseeing operation; ([types de
    service]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[visual approach]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[visual approach]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an approach in which
    the pilot-in-command of an IFR aircraft operating in VMC proceeds to
    the destination aerodrome by using visual reference to the surface
    and, as applicable, by maintaining visual separation from, and
    avoiding the wake turbulence of, a preceding aircraft; ([approche
    visuelle]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[window of circadian low]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[window of circadian low]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the period
    that begins at 02:00 and ends at 05:59 at the location where the
    flight crew member is acclimatized. ([phase de dépression
    circadienne]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

#### [Requirements for Air Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997085 .Subheading}

- **[[700.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.02
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an air
  transport service unless the person holds and complies with the
  provisions of an air operator certificate that authorizes the person
  to operate that service.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (3) and (4), no person shall,
  unless the person holds and complies with the provisions of an air
  operator certificate that authorizes the person to do so, operate an
  aeroplane or helicopter to conduct aerial work involving

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the carriage on board of persons other than flight
    crew members;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the carriage of helicopter Class B, C or D external
    loads;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the towing of objects; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the dispersal of products.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A person who does not hold an air operator
  certificate may conduct aerial work involving the dispersal of
  products if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person is a farmer;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person owns the aircraft that is used to
    disperse the products;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the products are dispersed for agricultural
    purposes; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the dispersal of the products takes place within 25
    miles of the centre of the person's farm.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} A person who holds a flight training unit operator
  certificate may conduct aerial work involving the carriage of persons
  other than flight crew members on board a single-engined aircraft if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command is the holder of a valid
    flight instructor rating in the appropriate category of aircraft;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is operated in day VFR flight;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} there are no more than nine passengers on board;
    and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the flight is conducted for the purpose of
    sightseeing operations.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsections (1) and (2), a person who does
  not hold an air operator certificate may operate an air transport
  service, or operate an aeroplane or helicopter to conduct aerial work
  involving the transport of passengers or goods, if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person holds a private operator registration
    document;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person operates the air transport service or
    conducts the aerial work under a management agreement with another
    person who has transferred to that person legal custody and control
    of the aircraft used to operate the service or to conduct the work;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the management agreement provides that the air
    transport service is operated or the aerial work is conducted
    exclusively in support of the activities of the person who has
    transferred legal custody and control of the aircraft; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} no payment is made in relation to the air transport
    service or the aerial work to a party to the management agreement by
    or on behalf of a passenger or the owner of a transported good
    unless the passenger or the owner is the person who has transferred
    legal custody and control of the aircraft.

#### [Authorization to Operate Specialty Air Service Under CUSMA]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997111 .Subheading}

- SOR/2020-150, s. 3

- **[[700.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.03
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A person who is a citizen, permanent
  resident or corporation of the United States of America or Mexico and
  who is eligible to operate a specialty air service in Canada in
  accordance with Chapter 15 and Annex I --- Schedule of Canada of CUSMA
  shall, prior to operating the service, obtain from the Minister an
  authorization to operate the service. The request for the
  authorization shall be in the form and shall contain the information
  specified in the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may, on receipt of a request referred to
  in subsection (1) and where the requirements of the Commercial Air
  Service Standards are met, issue an authorization containing the
  conditions under which the specialty air service may be operated.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An authorization referred to in subsection (1) is
  required in addition to an air operator certificate for those persons
  who are required to hold an air operator certificate pursuant to
  Subpart 2.

#### [Eligibility for Air Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997116 .Subheading}

- **[[700.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.04
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A Canadian is eligible to hold an
  air operator certificate.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who is a citizen, permanent resident or
  corporation of a foreign state is eligible to hold an air operator
  certificate that authorizes the person to operate an air transport
  service in Canada if the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} holds a similar document of entitlement issued by
    the foreign state; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements of Subpart 1.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A person who is a citizen, permanent resident or
  corporation of the United States of America or Mexico is eligible to
  hold an air operator certificate that authorizes the person to conduct
  aerial work in Canada if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aerial work is a specialty air service for
    which the person may obtain an operating certificate in accordance
    with Chapter 15 and Annex I --- Schedule of Canada of CUSMA; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person meets the requirements of Subpart 2.

#### [Aircraft Requirements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997125 .Subheading}

- **[[700.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.05
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), no
  Canadian air operator shall operate an aircraft in a commercial air
  service unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a certificate of airworthiness that meets the
    requirements of Article 31 of the Convention has been issued for the
    aircraft; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aircraft registered in another
    contracting state, the Minister has authorized its operation under
    Part II and, where a Canadian type certificate has not been issued
    for the aircraft type, the aircraft has been approved for operation
    under Part V.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No air operator that is a citizen, permanent resident
  or corporation of a foreign state shall operate an aircraft in a
  commercial air service in Canada unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is registered in Canada under Part II
    or in the foreign state; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where a Canadian type certificate has not been
    issued for the aircraft type, the aircraft has been approved for
    operation under Part V.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may authorize the operation of an
  aircraft in aerial work under Subpart 2 if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a special certificate of airworthiness in the
    restricted or limited classification has been issued in respect of
    the aircraft; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a foreign flight authority that is the equivalent
    of a special certificate of airworthiness in the restricted or
    limited classification has been issued in respect of the aircraft
    and validated by the Minister under section 507.05.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-112, s. 15
:::

#### [Extended Charter]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997138 .Subheading}

**[[700.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.06 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an aircraft on an extended charter unless the air operator

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in its air operator
  certificate; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

#### [Management Agreement]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997142 .Subheading}

**[[700.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.07 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall manage another air operator's operation unless the air operator
that manages the operation

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in its air operator
  certificate; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

#### [Operations between Points Abroad]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997146 .Subheading}

**[[700.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.08 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an air service between points abroad unless the air
operator

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in its air operator
  certificate; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

#### [Duties of Certificate Holder]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997150 .Subheading}

- **[[700.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.09
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The holder of an air operator
  certificate issued under section 702.07, 703.07, 704.07 or 705.07
  shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} appoint an operations manager and, where the holder
    does not hold an approved maintenance organization (AMO)
    certificate, a maintenance manager; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the operations manager meets the
    requirements of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} section 722.07 of Standard 722 --- Aerial Work of
      the Commercial Air Service Standards,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} section 723.07 of Standard 723 --- Air Taxi ---
      Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service Standards,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} section 723.07 of Standard 723 --- Air Taxi ---
      Helicopters of the Commercial Air Service Standards,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} section 724.07 of Standard 724 --- Commuter
      Operations --- Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service Standards,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} section 724.07 of Standard 724 --- Commuter
      Operations --- Helicopters of the Commercial Air Service
      Standards, or

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} section 725.07 of Standard 725 --- Airline
      Operations --- Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service Standards;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the maintenance manager meets the
    requirements of section 726.03 of Standard 726 --- Air Operator
    Maintenance of the Commercial Air Service Standards;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of the holder of an air operator
    certificate issued under section 705.07, ensure that the operations
    manager performs the duties set out in subsection 705.03(2);

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} in the case of the holder of an air operator
    certificate issued under section 705.07 who is also the holder of an
    approved maintenance organization (AMO) certificate issued under
    section 573.02, ensure that the person responsible for maintenance
    performs the duties set out in section 705.04;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} provide the operations manager and the maintenance
    manager with the financial and human resources necessary to ensure
    that the holder of the air operator certificate meets the
    requirements of these Regulations;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2022-246, s. 16\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} ensure that corrective actions are taken in respect
    of any findings resulting from a quality assurance program
    established under section 706.07 or a safety management system
    referred to in section 705.151; and

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} conduct reviews of the safety management system to
    determine its effectiveness.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The maintenance manager appointed under paragraph
  (1)(a) shall be the person responsible for the maintenance control
  system of the air operator appointed under paragraph 706.03(1)(a).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The maintenance manager appointed under paragraph
  (1)(a) shall remove aircraft from operation if the removal is
  justified because of non-compliance with the requirements of these
  Regulations or because of a risk to aviation safety or the safety of
  the public.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The holder of an air operator certificate issued
  under section 705.07 shall ensure that the person managing the safety
  management system referred to in section 705.153 performs the duties
  set out in that section.

### [Division II --- Approach Bans]{.HTitleText2} {#h-997172 .Subheading}

#### [Approach Bans --- Non Precision, APV and CAT I Precision]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997173 .Subheading}

- **[[700.10]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.10
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (3),
  the visibility with respect to an aeroplane is less than the minimum
  visibility required for a non-precision approach, an APV or a CAT I
  precision approach if, in respect of the advisory visibility specified
  in the Canada Air Pilot and set out in column I of an item in the
  table to this section,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where the RVR is measured by RVR "A" and RVR "B",
    the RVR measured by RVR "A" for the runway of intended approach is
    less than the visibility set out in column II of the item for the
    approach conducted;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the RVR is measured by only one of RVR "A"
    and RVR "B", the RVR for the runway of intended approach is less
    than the visibility set out in column II of the item for the
    approach conducted;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} where no RVR for the runway of intended approach is
    available, the runway visibility is less than the visibility set out
    in column II of the item for the approach conducted; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} where the aerodrome is located south of the 60th
    parallel of north latitude and no RVR or runway visibility for the
    runway of intended approach is available, the ground visibility at
    the aerodrome where the runway is located is less than the
    visibility set out in column II of the item for the approach
    conducted.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (3), the visibility
  with respect to a helicopter is less than the minimum visibility
  required for a non-precision approach, an APV or a CAT I precision
  approach if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where the RVR is measured by RVR "A" and RVR "B",
    the RVR measured by RVR "A" for the surface of intended approach is
    less than 1,200 feet; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the RVR is measured by only one of RVR "A"
    and RVR "B", the RVR for the surface of intended approach is less
    than 1,200 feet.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where the visibility is less than the minimum
  visibility set out in subsection (1) or (2), as applicable, no person
  shall continue a non-precision approach, an APV or a CAT I precision
  approach in an IFR aircraft unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at the time a visibility report is received, the
    aircraft has passed the FAF inbound or, where there is no FAF, the
    point where the final approach course is intercepted;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is on a training flight where a
    landing is not intended and the appropriate air traffic control unit
    is informed that a missed approach procedure will be initiated at or
    above the decision height or minimum descent altitude, as
    appropriate;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the RVR is varying between distances less than and
    greater than the minimum RVR;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} where the aerodrome is located south of the 60th
    parallel of north latitude and no RVR or runway visibility for the
    runway of intended approach is available, the ground visibility at
    the aerodrome where the runway is located is reported to vary
    between distances less than and greater than the minimum visibility;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a localized meteorological phenomenon is affecting
    the ground visibility to the extent that the visibility on the
    approach to the runway of intended approach and along that runway,
    as observed by the pilot-in-command in flight and reported
    immediately to ATS, if available, is equal to or greater than the
    advisory visibility specified in the Canada Air Pilot in respect of
    the runway of intended approach for the instrument approach
    procedure conducted; or

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the approach is conducted in accordance with
    section 703.41, 704.37 or 705.48.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} No pilot-in-command of an IFR aircraft operated under
  this Part shall commence a non-precision approach, an APV or a CAT I
  precision approach to an airport where low-visibility procedures are
  in effect.

#### [Approach Bans --- CAT II and CAT III Precision]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997200 .Subheading}

**[[700.11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.11 .sectionLabel}** No
pilot-in-command of an IFR aircraft operated under this Part who is
conducting a CAT II or CAT III precision approach shall continue the
approach beyond the FAF inbound or, where there is no FAF, the point
where the final approach course is intercepted, unless the RVR is equal
to or greater than the minimum RVR specified in the Canada Air Pilot in
respect of the runway or surface of intended approach for the instrument
approach procedure conducted.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-199, s. 15
:::

### [Division II.1 --- Portable Electronic Devices]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1195822 .Subheading}

**[[700.12]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.12 .sectionLabel}** Despite
subsection 602.08(1), an air operator that operates an aircraft under
Subpart 3, 4 or 5 of Part VII may permit the use of a PED on board an
aircraft if the air operator has validated that the use of the PED will
not adversely affect the operation of the aircraft or the functioning of
the aircraft's systems or equipment during any phase of the flight.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-296, s. 7](#1194432-1195825){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1194432-1195825.html"}
:::

**[[700.12.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.12.1 .sectionLabel}** An air
operator that permits the use of a PED shall keep an up-to-date record
of the following and provide a copy to the Minister on request:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the type, series and model of aircraft on which the
  air operator permits the use of a PED; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} for each aircraft referred to in paragraph (a),
  documents demonstrating that the use of a PED will not adversely
  affect the operation of the aircraft or the functioning of the
  aircraft's systems or equipment during any phase of the flight.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-296, s. 7](#1194432-1195830){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1194432-1195830.html"}
:::

**[[700.12.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.12.2 .sectionLabel}** If an air
operator suspects that a PED whose use it has permitted may adversely
affect, or is adversely affecting, the operation of an aircraft or the
functioning of an aircraft's systems or equipment, the air operator
shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} immediately prohibit the use of the PED; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} as soon as practicable, submit to the Minister a
  report of the adverse effects on the operation of the aircraft or the
  functioning of the aircraft's systems or equipment that are caused, or
  possibly caused, by the use of the PED.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-296, s. 7](#1194432-1195835){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1194432-1195835.html"}
:::

### [Division III --- Flight Crew Member Fatigue Management]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1279372 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2006-199, s. 15
- SOR/2018-269, s. 18

\]
:::

#### [Non-application and Interpretation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997252 .Subheading}

- **[[700.19]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.19
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This Division does not apply

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} to an air operator who operates an aircraft under
    Subpart 2 of this Part or to a flight crew member who operates an
    aircraft under that Subpart; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} to an air operator who conducts a medical
    evacuation flight or to a flight crew member who operates an
    aircraft to conduct such a flight.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Division, references to a
  time of day are

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if a flight crew member is acclimatized, references
    to the local time at their location; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if a flight crew member is not acclimatized,
    references to the local time at the last location where the member
    was acclimatized.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279384){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279384.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-700.19-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 700.19"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Monitoring System and Records]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997262 .Subheading}

- **[[700.20]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.20
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall have a system
  that monitors the flight times, flight duty periods, hours of work and
  rest periods of each of its flight crew members and shall include in
  its company operations manual the details of that system.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall, for each flight crew member,
  keep a record of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} all flight times;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the start and end times as well as the duration of
    each flight duty period;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the start and end times as well as the duration of
    each duty period;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the start and end times as well as the duration of
    each rest period; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} all time free from duty.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall keep a record of all
  notifications provided to it by a pilot-in-command under subsection
  700.63(4).

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall keep the records referred to in
  this section for a period of 24 months after the day on which they are
  made.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279397){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279397.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-700.20-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 700.20"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Air Operator Obligations --- Scheduling]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997264 .Subheading}

- **[[700.21]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.21
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall provide a
  flight crew member with their schedule sufficiently in advance for
  them to plan for adequate rest.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall, on a monthly basis, determine
  if a flight crew member's maximum flight duty period with respect to a
  flight is exceeded more than 10% of the time in a period of 90
  consecutive days.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If an air operator determines that more than 10% of a
  flight crew member's maximum flight duty periods are exceeded as a
  result of an unforeseen operational circumstance, the air operator
  shall change the schedule or the flight crew member pairing for the
  flight not later than 28 days after the day on which the determination
  is made.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the air operator sets schedules on a seasonal
  basis, the changes referred to in subsection (3) may be delayed until
  the beginning of the same season in the following year.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/99-158, s. 3
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279366){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279366.html"}
:::

#### [Fitness for Duty]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279405 .Subheading}

- **[[700.26]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.26
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall not allow a
  flight crew member to begin a flight duty period if, before the
  beginning of the period, the member advises the air operator that they
  are fatigued to the extent that they are not fit for duty.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A flight crew member shall advise every other flight
  crew member and the air operator as soon as the member becomes aware
  that they have become fatigued during a flight duty period to the
  extent that they are not fit for duty.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If there is only one flight crew member on board the
  aircraft, and the member becomes aware during a flight duty period
  that they have become fatigued to the extent that they are not fit for
  duty, they shall advise the air operator immediately or, if the
  aircraft is in flight, as soon as possible after the aircraft has
  landed.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a person who is assigned by an air operator to act
  as a flight crew member, or any other person, becomes aware that the
  assignment would result in the maximum flight time, maximum flight
  duty period or maximum number of hours of work being exceeded, the
  member or other person shall advise the air operator as soon as
  possible.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} If a flight crew member or any other person becomes
  aware that the member was not granted their rest period or time free
  from duty, the member or other person shall advise the air operator as
  soon as possible.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279413){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279413.html"}
:::

#### [Maximum Flight Time]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279414 .Subheading}

- **[[700.27]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.27
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall not assign
  flight time to a flight crew member, and a flight crew member shall
  not accept such an assignment, if the member's total flight time will,
  as a result, exceed

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 112 hours in any 28 consecutive days;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 300 hours in any 90 consecutive days;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} 1,000 hours in any 365 consecutive days; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a single-pilot operation, 8 hours in
    any 24 consecutive hours.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of subsection (1), a flight crew
  member's flight time includes

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the flight time accumulated from other flight
    operations; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the total flight time of a flight with an augmented
    flight crew.

#### [Maximum Flight Duty Period]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279437 .Subheading}

- **[[700.28]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.28
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall not assign a
  flight duty period to a flight crew member, and a flight crew member
  shall not accept such an assignment, if the flight duty period exceeds
  the maximum flight duty period set out in this section.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the average duration of all scheduled flights is
  less than 30 minutes, the maximum period of a flight duty period that
  begins during a period set out in column 1 of the table to this
  subsection is the number of hours set out in column 2, 3 or 4,
  according to the number of flights scheduled during the flight duty
  period.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsections (2) to (4), a flight
  crew member is considered to be acclimatized if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a time zone difference of less than
    four hours between local time and the time at the last location
    where the member was acclimatized, any rest periods required under
    these Regulations have been provided and the member has spent 72
    hours in the same time zone;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a time zone difference of four hours
    or more between local time and the time at the last location where
    the member was acclimatized, any rest periods required under these
    Regulations have been provided and the member has spent 96 hours in
    the same time zone; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the member has spent 24 hours in the same time zone
    for each hour of difference between local time and the time at the
    last location where the member was acclimatized.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsections (2) to (4),
  positioning is not to be considered a flight.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (5), the Canadian time
  zones are Pacific, Mountain, Central, Eastern, and the Atlantic time
  zone, which includes Newfoundland and Labrador.

- [(8)]{.lawlabel} The flight duty period for a flight crew member on
  standby begins at the time at which they report for duty at the
  location designated by the air operator.

- [(9)]{.lawlabel} When all flights are conducted under day VFR, the
  maximum period of a flight duty period that begins during a period set
  out in column 1 of the table to this subsection shall not exceed the
  number of hours set out in column 2.

#### [Maximum Number of Hours of Work]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279481 .Subheading}

- **[[700.29]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.29
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall not assign a
  flight duty period to a flight crew member, and a flight crew member
  shall not accept such an assignment, if, as a result, the member's
  number of hours of work will exceed

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 2,200 hours in any 365 consecutive days;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 192 hours in any 28 consecutive days;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} 60 hours in any 7 consecutive days if the air
    operator has provided the member with the following time free from
    duty:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} 1 single day free from duty in any 168
      consecutive hours, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} 4 single days free from duty in any 672
      consecutive hours; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} 70 hours in any 7 consecutive days if the air
    operator has provided 120 consecutive hours free from duty,
    including 5 consecutive local nights' rest, in any 504 consecutive
    hours and if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the member is not assigned early duty, late duty
      or night duty,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the member is not assigned a flight duty period
      greater than 12 hours, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the member's maximum number of hours of work is
      24 hours in any consecutive 48 hours.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator who has assigned to a flight crew
  member a flight duty period that will result in the member's number of
  hours of work exceeding those referred to in paragraph (1)(c) shall
  ensure that the member has 120 consecutive hours free from duty,
  including 5 consecutive local nights' rest, before assigning a flight
  duty period that will result in the member's number of hours of work
  exceeding those referred to in that paragraph.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A flight crew member's hours of work are to include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a flight crew member on reserve, 33%
    of the time that they are in a reserve availability period; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a flight crew member on standby,
    100% of the time that they are on standby.

::: HistoricalNote

**\[700.30 to 700.35 reserved\]**

#### [Home Base]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279500 .Subheading}

**[[700.36]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.36 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
shall assign a home base for each of its flight crew members.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279503){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279503.html"}
:::

#### [Nutrition Break]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279504 .Subheading}

**[[700.37]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.37 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
shall provide a flight crew member with not less than 15 minutes every 6
hours within a flight duty period to eat and drink.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279507){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279507.html"}
:::

**\[700.38 and 700.39 reserved\]**

#### [Rest Periods --- General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279509 .Subheading}

- **[[700.40]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.40
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall provide a
  flight crew member with the following rest periods at the end of a
  flight duty period:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the flight duty period ends at home base,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} either 12 hours, or 11 hours plus the travel time
      to and from the place where the rest period is taken, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if the air operator provides suitable
      accommodation, 10 hours in that suitable accommodation; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the flight duty period ends away from home base,
    10 hours in suitable accommodation.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If an air operator assigns a duty to a flight crew
  member for a period --- excluding the time required for positioning
  --- that exceeds by one hour or more the maximum flight duty period
  referred to in section 700.28, the rest period shall be the longer of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the maximum flight duty period plus the amount of
    time worked beyond the maximum flight duty period, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the rest period referred to in subsection (1).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall have a means to determine the
  travel time referred to in subparagraph (1)(a)(i).

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall provide a flight crew member
  with advance notice of the member's rest period and its duration.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279522){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279522.html"}
:::

#### [Disruptive Schedules]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279523 .Subheading}

- **[[700.41]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.41
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In addition to the rest periods
  required under section 700.40, an air operator shall provide a flight
  crew member with one local night's rest between

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the time at which late duty or night duty ends and
    the time at which the following early duty begins; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the time at which early duty ends and the time at
    which the following late duty or night duty begins.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply when a flight crew
  member is at a location where local time differs by more than four
  hours from the local time at the last location where the member was
  acclimatized.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279530){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279530.html"}
:::

#### [Rest Periods --- Time Zone Differences]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279531 .Subheading}

- **[[700.42]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.42
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite section 700.40, an air
  operator shall provide a flight crew member with the following rest
  periods when their flight duty period ends away from home base:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 11 consecutive hours in suitable accommodation, if
    the local time at the location where the flight duty period began
    differs by four hours from the local time at the location where the
    flight duty period ends; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 14 consecutive hours in suitable accommodation, if
    the local time at the location where the flight duty period began
    differs by more than four hours from the local time at the location
    where the flight duty period ends.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite section 700.40, an air operator shall provide
  a flight crew member with the following rest periods when their flight
  duty period begins at a location that is in a time zone other than the
  time zone in which home base is located and ends at home base:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 13 consecutive hours, if the local time at the
    location where the flight duty period began differs by four hours
    from the local time at home base and the member has been away from
    home base for more than 36 consecutive hours;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the local time at the location where the flight
    duty period began differs by more than 4 but not more than 10 hours
    from the local time at home base, and

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the member has been away from home base for 60
      consecutive hours or less and no part of the flight duty period
      occurs during any part of the member's window of circadian low,
      one local night's rest before the beginning of the next flight
      duty period, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the member has been away from home base for more
      than 60 consecutive hours, or any part of the flight duty period
      occurs within any part of the member's window of circadian low,
      two local nights' rest before the beginning of the next flight
      duty period; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the local time at the location where the flight
    duty period began differs by more than 10 hours from the local time
    at home base and

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the member has been away from home base for 60
      consecutive hours or less, two local nights' rest before the
      beginning of the next flight duty period, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the member has been away from home base for more
      than 60 consecutive hours, three local nights' rest before the
      beginning of the next flight duty period.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279545){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279545.html"}
:::

#### [Rest Period --- Positioning]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279546 .Subheading}

- **[[700.43]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.43
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a flight crew member is required
  by the air operator to travel for the purpose of positioning
  immediately after the completion of a flight duty period and the
  flight duty period plus the travel time required for positioning
  exceed the maximum flight duty period set out in section 700.28, the
  air operator shall provide the member with a rest period before the
  beginning of the next flight duty period that is equal to the duration
  of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the number of hours of work, if the maximum flight
    duty period is exceeded by three hours or less; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number of hours of work plus the amount of time
    by which the maximum flight duty period is exceeded, if the maximum
    flight duty period is exceeded by more than three hours.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), the rest period provided to
  the member by the air operator before the beginning of the next flight
  duty period shall not be shorter than the rest period required under
  subsection 700.40(1).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall not require the positioning of
  a flight crew member if it would result in the member's maximum flight
  duty period being exceeded by more than three hours unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the member agrees to the positioning; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the member's flight duty period is not exceeded by
    more than seven hours.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall consider the time required for
  the positioning of a flight crew member, that is not immediately
  followed by the assignment of a flight duty period, as a flight duty
  period for the purpose of determining the duration of the rest periods
  in accordance with section 700.40.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279557){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279557.html"}
:::

**\[700.44 to 700.49 reserved\]**

#### [Split Flight Duty]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279559 .Subheading}

- **[[700.50]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.50
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A flight crew member's flight duty
  period may exceed the maximum flight duty period set out in section
  700.28 by the following amount of time, if the air operator provides
  the member with a break, in suitable accommodation, of at least 60
  consecutive minutes during the flight duty period:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 100% of the duration of the break that is provided
    to the member during the period beginning at 24:00 and ending at
    05:59;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 50% of the duration of the break that is provided
    to the member during the period beginning at 06:00 and ending at
    23:59; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an unforeseen operational
    circumstance, 50% of the duration of the break that is provided to
    the member in the case of the replanning of a flight duty period
    after it has begun.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), the duration of
  the break provided to the flight crew member is reduced by 45 minutes
  before the calculation is made.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a flight crew member is assigned to night duty,
  their flight duty period may only be extended under subsection (1) for
  three consecutive nights.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The time referred to in paragraphs (1)(a) and (b) is
  the time at the location where the flight crew member is acclimatized.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} If a flight crew member on reserve is assigned to
  flight duty that includes split duty, the air operator may extend the
  reserve duty period by two hours if a break in accordance with this
  section is provided. There shall not be more than two flights during
  the flight duty period following the break.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279570){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279570.html"}
:::

#### [Consecutive Flight Duty Periods]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279571 .Subheading}

- **[[700.51]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.51
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall not assign to
  a flight crew member more than three consecutive flight duty periods
  if any part of those periods falls between 02:00 and 05:59, unless the
  air operator provides the member with one local night's rest at the
  end of the third flight duty period.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} However, an air operator may assign to a flight crew
  member up to five consecutive flight duty periods even if any part of
  those periods falls between 02:00 and 05:59 if the member is provided
  with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a rest period of three hours in suitable
    accommodation during each flight duty period; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 56 consecutive hours free from duty at the end of
    the last consecutive flight duty period.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279578){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279578.html"}
:::

#### [Delayed Reporting Time]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279579 .Subheading}

- **[[700.52]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.52
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If an air operator advises a flight
  crew member of a delay in the member's reporting time before the
  member leaves their suitable accommodation to report for duty, the
  duration of the flight duty period shall, for the purposes of
  determining the maximum flight duty period in accordance with section
  700.28, be calculated starting from either the initial reporting time
  or the delayed reporting time, whichever results in the shorter
  period.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), the flight duty period shall
  begin, if the delay in the reporting time

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is less than four hours, at the delayed reporting
    time; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is four hours or more but less than 10 hours, four
    hours after the initial reporting time.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the delay in the reporting time is 10 hours or
  more, the duration of the delay is considered to be a rest period if
  the air operator advises the flight crew member of the delay before
  they leave the suitable accommodation, and does not disturb their rest
  period before an agreed time.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Unless the air operator and flight crew member agree
  on a time when the air operator may disturb the member's rest period
  referred to in subsection (3), the air operator shall not interrupt
  the member's rest period other than

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} during the 30-minute period before the time the
    member was initially scheduled to leave the suitable accommodation;
    or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} during the 60-minute period before the initial
    reporting time.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279602){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279602.html"}
:::

**\[700.53 to 700.59 reserved\]**

#### [Maximum Flight Duty Period --- Augmented Flight Crew and Rest Facilities]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279604 .Subheading}

- **[[700.60]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.60
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite section 700.28, if the air
  operator assigns for a flight the number of additional flight crew
  members set out in column 2 of the table to this subsection and
  provides, for each additional member, the corresponding rest facility
  set out in column 3, the maximum flight duty period is the period set
  out in column 1.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The maximum flight duty period set out in
  subsection (1) applies only to a flight duty period during which there
  are three or fewer flights if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} for a flight duty period during which there is one
    flight, all flight crew members are provided with in-flight rest in
    a rest facility; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} for a flight duty period during which there are two
    or three flights,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the flight crew member who will be at the
      controls for the final landing is provided with two consecutive
      hours of in-flight rest in a rest facility; and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} all other flight crew members are provided with
      90 consecutive minutes of in-flight rest in a rest facility.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A flight crew member's flight duty period shall
  include all of the time spent in the rest facility.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The flight duty period for all flight crew members
  shall begin and end at the same location. However, for a period during
  which there is more than one flight and the first flight is scheduled
  to be less than 105 minutes long, an air operator may assign
  additional flight crew members to join a flight after the first
  flight, but all flight crew members shall end their flight duty period
  at the same location.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} At least one additional flight crew member shall be
  on the flight deck during all take-offs and landings, other than for
  the first flight, if additional flight crew members join the flight
  after the first flight in the case referred to in subsection (4).

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} In-flight rest shall occur between the time at which
  the aircraft reaches 3 048 m (10,000 feet) above aerodrome elevation
  and 15 minutes before the scheduled beginning of the descent.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} If a flight duty period has been extended, an air
  operator shall provide each flight crew member with a rest period that
  is the longer of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the duration of the duty period just completed, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 14 hours in suitable accommodation, or 16 hours
    when the member's duty period ends at home base.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279627){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279627.html"}
:::

#### [Long-range Flights]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279628 .Subheading}

**[[700.61]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.61 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
shall not assign a flight duty period to a flight crew member, and a
flight crew member shall not accept such an assignment, if the flight
duty period occurs within the member's window of circadian low and
includes a flight that follows a scheduled flight of more than seven
hours.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279634){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279634.html"}
:::

#### [Ultra Long-range Flights]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279635 .Subheading}

- **[[700.62]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.62
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall not assign a
  flight duty period of more than 18 hours to a flight crew member and a
  member shall not accept such an assignment.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall not assign a flight crew member
  to a flight with a scheduled flight time of more than 16 hours, and a
  member shall not accept such an assignment.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279640){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279640.html"}
:::

#### [Unforeseen Operational Circumstances --- Flight Duty Period and Rest Period]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279641 .Subheading}

- **[[700.63]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.63
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If the pilot-in-command is of the
  opinion that an unforeseen operational circumstance that occurs within
  60 minutes of the beginning of the flight duty period could lead to a
  level of fatigue that may adversely affect the safety of the flight,
  the pilot-in-command may, after consulting with all crew members on
  their level of fatigue,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} reduce a flight crew member's flight duty period;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} extend a flight crew member's flight duty period by
    the following number of hours in excess of the maximum flight duty
    period set out in section 700.28 or subsection 700.60(1) by

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} one hour for a single-pilot operation,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} two hours, if the flight crew is not augmented,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} three hours, if the flight crew is augmented
      and there is one flight during the scheduled flight duty period,
      and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} two hours, if the flight crew is augmented and
      there are two or three flights during the scheduled flight duty
      period; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} extend a flight crew member's rest period.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a further unforeseen operational circumstance
  arises after take-off on the final flight for which the maximum flight
  duty period was extended under subsection (1), the pilot-in-command
  may, despite that subsection, continue the flight to the destination
  aerodrome or to an alternate aerodrome.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall extend the rest period after a
  flight duty period is extended under this section by an amount of time
  that is at least equal to the extension of the flight duty period.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} At the end of a flight duty period, the
  pilot-in-command shall notify the air operator of any change to a
  flight duty period made under this section.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279655){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279655.html"}
:::

#### [Unforeseen Operational Circumstances --- Split Flight Duty]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279656 .Subheading}

- **[[700.64]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.64
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In the event of an unforeseen
  operational circumstance that occurs after the beginning of the flight
  duty period, an air operator may change a flight crew member's flight
  duty period to include a split flight duty in accordance with section
  700.50 if the pilot-in-command agrees and the change is made before
  the scheduled break on the ground.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command shall not agree to the change if
  they are of the opinion, after consulting with all other crew members,
  that a split flight duty period could lead to a level of fatigue that
  may adversely affect the safety of the flight.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279661){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279661.html"}
:::

**\[700.65 to 700.69 reserved\]**

#### [Flight Crew Member on Reserve]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279663 .Subheading}

- **[[700.70]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.70
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall notify a
  flight crew member on reserve of the start and end times of the
  reserve availability period and the location where it will take place
  no later than

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 12 hours before the start time of the reserve
    availability period, if no part of that period falls during the
    member's window of circadian low; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 32 hours before the start time of the reserve
    availability period, if any part of that period falls during the
    member's window of circadian low.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall not change the start time of a
  reserve availability period of a flight crew member by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} more than two hours before, or four hours after,
    the start time that was communicated to the flight crew member under
    subsection (1); or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} more than eight hours before or after the start
    time that was communicated to the member under subsection (1) in any
    period of 168 consecutive hours, unless the member is provided with
    two consecutive days free from duty within that period.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the start time of a reserve availability period is
  changed to a time after 02:00, the air operator shall not assign
  another reserve availability period to the flight crew member unless
  the member is provided with two consecutive days free from duty before
  the start time of that period.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall not change the start time of a
  reserve availability period so that it falls in a flight crew member's
  window of circadian low unless the air operator notifies the member of
  the change at least 24 hours before the revised start time.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall not assign to a flight crew
  member a reserve availability period that exceeds 14 consecutive
  hours.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall provide a flight crew member
  with a rest period of at least 10 consecutive hours between reserve
  availability periods.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall not assign to a flight crew
  member a reserve duty period that exceeds

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 18 consecutive hours, if the period begins between
    02:00 and 17:59;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 17 consecutive hours, if the period begins between
    18:00 and 18:59;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} 16 consecutive hours, if the period begins between
    19:00 and 20:59;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} 15 consecutive hours, if the period begins between
    21:00 and 22:59; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} 14 consecutive hours, if the period begins between
    23:00 and 01:59.

- [(8)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (7), an air operator may assign to
  a flight crew member a reserve duty period of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} no more than 20 hours, if the flight crew is
    augmented by one additional flight crew member and a class 1 rest
    facility or a class 2 rest facility is provided for the member;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} no more than 22 hours, when the reserve
    availability period begins between 21:00 and 03:00 at the location
    where the flight crew member is acclimatized, if the flight crew is
    augmented by two additional flight crew members and a class 1 rest
    facility or a class 2 rest facility is provided for each of the
    members; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} no more than 26 hours, when the reserve
    availability period begins before 21:00 or after 03:00 at the
    location where the flight crew member is acclimatized, if the flight
    crew is augmented by two additional flight crew members and a class
    1 rest facility is provided for each of the members.

- [(9)]{.lawlabel} If the reserve availability period begins between
  02:00 and 05:59 at the location where the flight crew member is
  acclimatized and the member is not contacted by the air operator
  during that period, the air operator may extend the reserve duty
  period by two hours or 50% of the reserve availability period that
  falls between 02:00 and 05:59, whichever is shorter.

- [(10)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall not assign to a flight crew
  member a flight duty period that exceeds the maximum reserve duty
  period set out in subsection (7) or (8) or the maximum flight duty
  period set out in section 700.28, whichever is shorter, unless the air
  operator

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} provides the member with at least 24 hours' notice
    of the assignment before the beginning of the flight duty period;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} does not provide the notice during the period that
    begins at 22:30 and ends at 7:30; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} assigns no duties to the member between the time
    the notice is provided and the beginning of the flight duty period.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279691){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279691.html"}
- [SOR/2022-246, s. 18(E)](#1380152-1380782){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1380152-1380782.html"}
:::
