#### [Flight Crew Member on Standby]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279692 .Subheading}

- **[[700.71]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.71
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The air operator shall provide a
  flight crew member on standby with a place that provides adequate
  protection from the elements, where it is possible to sit and to
  access food and drink and, if possible, that is not accessible to the
  public.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the flight crew member on standby is not assigned
  to flight duty, the air operator shall provide them with the following
  rest periods:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the member is at home base,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} 12 hours, or 11 hours plus the travel time to or
      from the member's lodging, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if the air operator provides suitable
      accommodation, 10 hours in that suitable accommodation; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the member is away from home base, 10 hours.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279701){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279701.html"}
:::

#### [Controlled Rest on Flight Deck]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279702 .Subheading}

- **[[700.72]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.72
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A flight crew member shall not take
  a controlled rest on the flight deck of an aircraft that is operated
  by an air operator unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the rest is 45 minutes or less, is taken during the
    cruise portion of the flight and is completed at least 30 minutes
    before the scheduled beginning of the descent;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} no other flight crew member is taking a rest at
    that time; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} at least two flight crew members remain on the
    flight deck.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Before taking a controlled rest on the flight deck, a
  flight crew member shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} transfer their duties to a flight crew member who
    is not taking a rest;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} review the status of the flight, including any
    specific duties to be performed during the rest;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} review the wake-up criteria; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} advise the flight attendants of the start and end
    times of the rest.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A flight crew member who takes a controlled rest on
  the flight deck shall not assume any duties, and no other flight crew
  member shall transfer any duties to them, until 15 minutes after the
  end of the rest.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} When a flight crew member returns to duty, another
  flight crew member shall provide them with an operational briefing.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279716){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279716.html"}
:::

**\[700.73 to 700.99 reserved\]**

### [Division IV --- Flight Crew Member Fatigue Management --- Medical Evacuation Flights]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1279718 .Subheading}

#### [Application and Interpretation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279719 .Subheading}

- **[[700.100]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.100
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This Division applies to an air
  operator who conducts a medical evacuation flight and to a flight crew
  member who operates an aircraft to conduct such a flight.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} This Division does not apply to an air operator who
  operates an aircraft under Subpart 2 of this Part or to a flight crew
  member who operates an aircraft under that Subpart.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Division, a flight to
  position an aircraft before or after a medical evacuation flight is
  considered to be a medical evacuation flight.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279725){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279725.html"}
:::

#### [Monitoring System and Records]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279726 .Subheading}

- **[[700.101]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.101
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall have a system
  that monitors the flight times, flight duty periods and rest periods
  of each of its flight crew members and shall include in its company
  operations manual the details of that system.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a person who is assigned by an air operator to act
  as a flight crew member, or any other person, becomes aware that the
  assignment would result in the maximum flight time referred to in
  section 700.103 or the maximum flight duty period referred to in
  section 700.104 being exceeded, the person shall advise the air
  operator as soon as possible.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279736){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279736.html"}
:::

#### [Fitness for Duty]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279737 .Subheading}

- **[[700.102]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.102
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall not allow a
  flight crew member to begin a flight duty period if, before the
  beginning of the period, the member advises the air operator that they
  are fatigued to the extent that they are not fit for duty.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A flight crew member shall advise every other flight
  crew member and the air operator as soon as the member becomes aware
  that they have become fatigued during a flight duty period to the
  extent that they are not fit for duty.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If there is only one flight crew member on board the
  aircraft, and the member becomes aware during a flight duty period
  that they have become fatigued to the extent that they are not fit for
  duty, they shall advise the air operator immediately or, if the
  aircraft is in flight, as soon as possible after the aircraft has
  landed.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a person who is assigned by an air operator to act
  as a flight crew member, or any other person, becomes aware that the
  assignment would result in the maximum flight time or maximum flight
  duty period being exceeded, the member or other person shall advise
  the air operator as soon as possible.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} If a flight crew member or any other person becomes
  aware that the member was not granted their rest period or time free
  from duty, the member or other person shall advise the air operator as
  soon as possible.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279745){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279745.html"}
:::

#### [Maximum Flight Time]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279746 .Subheading}

- **[[700.103]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.103
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall not assign a
  flight crew member for flight time, and a flight crew member shall not
  accept such an assignment, if the member's total flight time will, as
  a result, exceed

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the flight is conducted under Subpart 4 or 5
    using an aircraft other than a helicopter, 40 hours in any 7
    consecutive days;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the flight is conducted under Subpart 3, or is
    conducted using a helicopter, 60 hours in any 7 consecutive days;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} 120 hours in any 30 consecutive days or, in the
    case of a flight crew member on call, 100 hours in any 30
    consecutive days;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} 300 hours in any 90 consecutive days;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} 1,200 hours in any 365 consecutive days; or

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a single-pilot operation, 8 hours in
    any 24 consecutive hours.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of subsection (1), a flight crew
  member's flight time includes

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the flight time accumulated from other flight
    operations; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the total flight time of a flight with an augmented
    flight crew.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279759){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279759.html"}
:::

#### [Maximum Flight Duty Period]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279760 .Subheading}

**[[700.104]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.104 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
shall not assign a flight duty period to a flight crew member, and a
flight crew member shall not accept such an assignment, if the flight
duty period exceeds 14 hours.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279763){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279763.html"}
:::

**\[700.105 to 700.115 reserved\]**

#### [Rest Period --- General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279765 .Subheading}

- **[[700.116]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.116
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall provide a
  flight crew member, at the end of a flight duty period, with a rest
  period of 10 hours plus the travel time to and from the place where
  the rest period is taken.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall provide a flight crew member
  with advance notice of the member's rest period and its duration.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279770){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279770.html"}
:::

#### [Rest Period --- Positioning]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279771 .Subheading}

**[[700.117]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.117 .sectionLabel}** If a flight
crew member is required by the air operator to travel for the purpose of
positioning after the completion of a flight duty period, the air
operator shall provide the flight crew member with an additional rest
period at least equal to one-half the time spent travelling that is in
excess of the flight crew member's maximum flight duty period.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279786){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279786.html"}
:::

#### [Split Flight Duty]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279787 .Subheading}

- **[[700.118]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.118
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a flight duty period includes a
  rest period, an air operator may assign to a flight crew member a
  flight duty period that exceeds the maximum flight duty period
  referred to in section 700.104, by one-half the length of the rest
  period referred to in paragraph (b), to a maximum of three hours, if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator provides the member with notice,
    before the beginning of the flight duty period, of the extension of
    flight duty period;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator provides the member with a rest
    period of at least four consecutive hours in suitable accommodation;
    and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the member's rest period is not interrupted by the
    air operator.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall extend the rest period after a
  flight duty period referred to in subsection (1) by an amount that is
  at least equal to the length of the extension to the flight duty
  period.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279795){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279795.html"}
:::

#### [Time Free from Duty]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279796 .Subheading}

- **[[700.119]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.119
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall provide each
  flight crew member with one of the following periods of time free from
  duty:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at least 36 consecutive hours within each
    consecutive 7-day period;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} at least 3 consecutive days within each consecutive
    17-day period;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} at least 4 consecutive days within each consecutive
    19-day period.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall provide a flight crew member
  with advance notice of the member's time free from duty and its
  duration.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279803){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279803.html"}
- [SOR/2022-246, s. 19](#1380154-1380787){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1380154-1380787.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-700.119-20201212.html "Link to previous version of section 700.119"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Consecutive Flight Duty Periods]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279804 .Subheading}

**[[700.120]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.120 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
shall provide a flight crew member with at least 24 consecutive hours
free from flight duty following three consecutive flight duty period
assignments that exceed 12 consecutive hours unless the member has
received a rest period of at least 24 consecutive hours free from flight
duty between each flight duty period assignment.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279810){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279810.html"}
:::

#### [Delayed Reporting Time]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279811 .Subheading}

**[[700.121]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.121 .sectionLabel}** If an air
operator advises a flight crew member, before the member leaves a rest
facility, of a delay in excess of three hours in the member's reporting
time, the member's flight duty period is considered to have started
three hours after the original reporting time.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279814){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279814.html"}
:::

**\[700.122 to 700.130 reserved\]**

#### [Maximum Flight Duty Period --- Augmented Flight Crew and Rest Facility]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279816 .Subheading}

- **[[700.131]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.131
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Despite section 700.104, if the air
  operator assigns an additional flight crew member to a flight and
  provides for the member the rest facility set out in column 2 of the
  table to this subsection, the maximum flight duty period is the period
  set out in column 1.

  <figure id="1279819">

  class="table table-hover table-striped tablePointsize8 topdouble topbot">

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The maximum flight duty period set out in
  subsection (1) applies only to a flight duty period during which there
  are three or fewer flights.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A flight crew member's flight duty period shall
  include all time spent in the rest facility.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a flight duty period has been extended, an air
  operator shall provide each flight crew member with a rest period that
  is equal to the duration of the duty period just completed.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279830){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279830.html"}
:::

#### [Long-range Flights]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279831 .Subheading}

- **[[700.132]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.132
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A flight duty period during which
  there is one flight or a series of flights that ends more than four
  one-hour time zones from the point of departure, other than flights
  conducted entirely within Northern Domestic Airspace, shall be limited
  to three flights, in the case of a series of fights, and shall be
  followed by a rest period that is at least equal to the length of the
  flight duty period.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a flight referred to in subsection (1) is a
  transoceanic flight, the maximum number of flights that may be
  conducted after the transoceanic flight is one, excluding one
  unscheduled technical stop that occurs during the flight.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279841){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279841.html"}
:::

#### [Unforeseen Operational Circumstances]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279842 .Subheading}

- **[[700.133]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.133
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A pilot-in-command may, as a result
  of unforeseen operational circumstances, and after consulting with all
  crew members on their level of fatigue, extend a flight crew member's
  flight time and flight duty period in excess of the maximum flight
  time referred to in section 700.103 and the maximum flight duty period
  referred to in section 700.104.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command may extend the maximum flight
  time and maximum flight duty period by three hours if the
  pilot-in-command notifies the air operator of the length of and the
  reason for the extension. In the case of a flight duty period that is
  extended, the subsequent rest period shall be increased by an amount
  at least equal to the length of the extension of the flight duty
  period.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall keep a record of all
  notifications provided to it under subsection (2) for a period of 24
  months after the day on which they are provided.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279854){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279854.html"}
:::

#### [Flight Crew Member on Reserve]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279855 .Subheading}

- **[[700.134]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.134
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall provide each
  flight crew member on reserve with a rest period of at least 10
  consecutive hours in any 24 consecutive hours if the air operator

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} provides the member with 24 hours' notice of the
    start time and duration of the rest period;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} provides the member with a minimum of 10 hours'
    notice of the start time and duration of the rest period and the air
    operator does not assign any duty to the member during those 10
    hours; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} does not assign a flight duty period to the member
    and does not interrupt the member's rest period between 22:00 and
    06:00 local time.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Following a rest period provided under subsection
  (1), the start of a subsequent rest period cannot vary by more than
  three hours from the time of day that the preceding rest period
  started, or by more than a total of eight hours in any seven
  consecutive days.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If an air operator is unable to provide a flight crew
  member with the rest period referred to in subsection (1) and the
  member is notified to report for flight duty or the reporting time
  occurs between 22:00 and 06:00 local time

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the maximum flight duty period shall be 10 hours;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the rest period following the flight duty period
    shall be increased by at least one-half the length of the preceding
    flight duty period.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279866){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279866.html"}
:::

#### [Controlled Rest on Flight Deck]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279867 .Subheading}

- **[[700.135]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.135
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A flight crew member shall not take
  a controlled rest on the flight deck of an aircraft that is operated
  by an air operator unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the rest is 45 minutes or less, is taken during the
    cruise portion of the flight and is completed at least 30 minutes
    before the scheduled beginning of the descent;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} no other flight crew member is taking a rest at
    that time; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} at least two flight crew members remain on the
    flight deck.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Before taking a controlled rest on the flight deck, a
  flight crew member shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} transfer their duties to a flight crew member who
    is not taking a rest;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} review the status of the flight, including any
    specific duties to be performed during the rest;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} review the wake-up criteria; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} advise the other crew members of the start and end
    times of the rest.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A flight crew member who takes a controlled rest on
  the flight deck shall not assume any duties, and no other flight crew
  member shall transfer any duties to them, until 15 minutes after the
  end of the rest.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} When a flight crew member returns to duty, another
  flight crew member shall provide him or her with an operational
  briefing.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279881){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279881.html"}
:::

**\[700.136 to 700.199 reserved\]**

### [Division V --- Exemptions --- Fatigue Risk Management System]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1279883 .Subheading}

#### [Initial Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279884 .Subheading}

- **[[700.200]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.200
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (3) and (4),
  an air operator and flight crew members to whom sections 700.20 to
  700.72 or 700.101 to 700.135 apply are exempt, in respect of a flight,
  from the application of the provisions set out in the notice of intent
  referred to in section 700.206, if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator has sent to the Minister a notice
    of intent that complies with the requirements of section 700.206;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator has established and implemented
    the following components of the fatigue risk management system,
    referred to in subsection 700.214(1):

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the fatigue risk management plan, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the fatigue risk management process; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} starting on the date on which the flight is first
    conducted under the exemption in this subsection and ending when the
    exemption no longer applies, the air operator notifies the Minister
    that the analysis required by paragraph 700.225(2)(g) is available
    to the Minister for review

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} every 90 days, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if the period during which the flight is
      conducted is shorter than 90 days, at the end of the period.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (3) and (5), an air operator
  and flight crew members to whom sections 702.91 to 702.98 apply are
  exempt, in respect of a flight, from the application of the provisions
  set out in the notice of intent referred to in section 700.206, if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator has sent to the Minister a notice
    of intent that complies with the requirements of section 700.206;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator has established and implemented
    the following components of the fatigue risk management system,
    referred to in subsection 700.214(1):

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the fatigue risk management plan, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the fatigue risk management process; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} starting on the date on which the flight is first
    conducted under the exemption in this subsection and ending when the
    exemption no longer applies, the air operator notifies the Minister
    that the analysis required by paragraph 700.225(2)(g) is available
    to the Minister for review

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} every 90 days, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if the period during which the flight is
      conducted is shorter than 90 days, at the end of the period.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The exemptions referred to in subsections (1) and (2)
  continue to apply in respect of a flight as long as the air operator
  demonstrates compliance with the requirements of sections 700.213 to
  700.225 but cease to apply, in respect of that flight, on the earlier
  of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the date on which the exemption referred to in
    section 700.234 comes into effect with respect to the same
    provisions and for the same flight, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} three years after the date on which the notice of
    intent was sent.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The exemption referred to in subsection (1) may be in
  respect of any of the requirements set out in sections 700.27 to
  700.72 except for the requirements set out in the following
  provisions:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 700.27(1)(c);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 700.29(1)(a);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} section 700.36;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} section 700.37; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} paragraph 700.103(1)(e).

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The exemption referred to in subsection (2) may be in
  respect of any of the requirements set out in sections 702.92 to
  702.98 except for the requirements set out in paragraph 702.92(1)(a).

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279913){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279913.html"}
:::

#### [Series of Flights]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279914 .Subheading}

**[[700.201]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.201 .sectionLabel}** In this
Division, a reference to a flight is also a reference to a series of
flights if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the flights in the series of flights are consecutive
  and are conducted by the same flight crew members; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the flight crew members operate the flights during a
  single flight duty period or consecutive flight duty periods.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279919){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279919.html"}
:::

**\[700.202 to 700.205 reserved\]**

#### [Notice of Intent]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279921 .Subheading}

- **[[700.206]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.206
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall send a notice
  of intent to the Minister that includes

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a statement that the air operator has established
    and implemented a fatigue risk management plan and a fatigue risk
    management process --- and maintains the fatigue risk management
    plan and the fatigue risk management process --- and intends to
    establish, implement and maintain a program for fatigue risk
    management promotion and a quality assurance program for the fatigue
    risk management system in accordance with this Division;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a description of the flight that will be subject to
    an exemption referred to in section 700.200;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the provisions of these Regulations from which the
    air operator and flight crew members will be exempt;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a description of the manner in which the flight
    will be conducted results in a variance from the requirements of the
    provisions referred to in paragraph (c);

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the scientific studies used to demonstrate that the
    variance referred to in paragraph (d) is not likely to have an
    adverse effect on the levels of fatigue and alertness of flight crew
    members;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the expected day on which the exemption referred to
    in section 700.200 will first apply to the flight and, in the case
    of a flight that is not conducted year-round, the expected period
    during which the exemption referred to in that section will apply to
    the flight;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a description of the safety case that will be
    developed for the flight;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} a statement that the air operator intends to
    validate a safety case in accordance with subsection 700.225(3) and
    to ensure that an initial audit is conducted under subsection
    700.231(1); and

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the name and contact information of the person who
    will be responsible for implementing the fatigue risk management
    system.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The air operator may include in the notice of intent
  more than one flight if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the duration of the flight duty period is the same
    for all flights;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} all flights have the same number of consecutive
    flight duty periods;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the flight duty periods for the flights start
    within 60 minutes of each other;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the duration of any part of a flight duty period
    that occurs within the flight crew members' window of circadian low
    is the same for all flights;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} all flights have the same number of consecutive
    flight duty periods that occur during any part of the flight crew
    members' window of circadian low;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the duration of the rest period before and after
    each flight duty period is the same for all flights;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the time of day during which each rest period is
    taken is similar for all flights;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the flights are conducted in the same time zone or
    across the same number of time zones in the same direction by flight
    crew members who are all acclimatized to the same time zone;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the flights are conducted with the same aircraft
    type;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} the flights are conducted with the same number of
    flight crew members;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} the operating environments are similar for all
    flights; and

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} the hazards and risks are similar for all flights.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279947){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279947.html"}
:::

**[[700.207]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.207 .sectionLabel}** Despite
subsection 700.200(3), the initial exemption ceases to apply in respect
of a flight if the analysis referred to in paragraph 700.200(1)(c) or
(2)(c) does not show any progress in the development of the operator's
safety case.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279950){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279950.html"}
:::

**\[700.208 to 700.212 reserved\]**

#### [Fatigue Risk Management System --- Establishment and Implementation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279952 .Subheading}

- **[[700.213]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.213
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall establish and
  implement a fatigue risk management system.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operations manager appointed under paragraph
  700.09(1)(a) shall ensure that the fatigue risk management system
  complies with the requirements of this Division.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operations manager shall, when a finding
  resulting from the quality assurance program for the fatigue risk
  management system referred to in section 700.219 is reported to them,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} determine what, if any, corrective actions are
    required and take those actions; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} notify the accountable executive of any systemic
    deficiency and of the corrective action taken.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The operations manager may assign the management
  functions for the fatigue risk management system to another person.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The responsibility of the operations manager is not
  affected by the assignment of management functions to another person
  under subsection (4).

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} If the operations manager assigns the management
  functions for the fatigue risk management system to another person
  under subsection (4), that other person shall report to the operations
  manager the fatigue-related hazards, risks and incidents identified
  under the fatigue risk management system.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279963){.wb-lbx
