#### [Fatigue Risk Management System --- Components]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279964 .Subheading}

- **[[700.214]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.214
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall have a fatigue
  risk management system that includes

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a fatigue risk management plan;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a fatigue risk management process;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a program for fatigue risk management promotion;
    and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a quality assurance program for the fatigue risk
    management system.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The air operator shall take into account, when
  establishing the fatigue risk management system, all of the duties
  performed in the operations of the air operator by flight crew members
  who are assigned duties on a flight that is the subject of an
  exemption under this Division.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The air operator shall update its fatigue risk
  management system if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} there is a change in the size and scope of its
    operations;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any action is taken as a result of an audit of the
    fatigue risk management system conducted under subsection 700.231(1)
    or section 700.247;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the air operator's validation of the safety case in
    accordance with subsection 700.225(3) establishes that there is an
    increase in the level of fatigue or a decrease in the level of
    alertness of flight crew members; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a data analysis conducted in accordance with the
    process referred to in subsection 700.216(2) indicates that flight
    crew members are subject to an increase in their level of fatigue or
    a decrease in their level of alertness.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279978){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279978.html"}
:::

#### [Fatigue Risk Management Plan]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279979 .Subheading}

**[[700.215]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.215 .sectionLabel}** The air
operator's fatigue risk management plan shall include

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a fatigue risk management policy --- signed by the
  accountable executive --- that establishes the shared responsibility
  of the air operator and flight crew members in managing fatigue;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} safety objectives, including the identification and
  reduction of fatigue-related hazards and the effective management of
  fatigue in flight operations;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} safety performance indicators to measure the
  attainment of the safety objectives;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} defined responsibilities in relation to fatigue
  management for

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the air operator's managers,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the persons managing the fatigue risk management
    system, and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} other employees;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} a training plan that identifies the content of the
  initial and annual training;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} a plan for communicating the information referred to
  in paragraphs 700.218(4)(a) to (f) to flight crew members; and

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} a policy for the internal reporting of fatigue by
  flight crew members, without fear of reprisal.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1279992){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1279992.html"}
:::

#### [Fatigue Risk Management Process]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1279993 .Subheading}

- **[[700.216]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.216
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The air operator's fatigue risk
  management process shall include procedures for

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the internal reporting of fatigue by flight crew
    members;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} acknowledging in writing, to flight crew members,
    receipt of each fatigue report and advising of any follow-up action;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} collecting information to identify fatigue-related
    hazards, including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} flight crew member performance data,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} accident and incident information,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} data from work schedules,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} data from comparisons of planned schedules in
      relation to time worked, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} data from a review of operational or
      administrative duties;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} developing a list of the safety data and scientific
    studies used in support of the processes that form part of the
    fatigue risk management system;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} managing the data and information referred to in
    this subsection;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} identifying and assessing the levels of fatigue and
    alertness through modelling with respect to flight crew members'
    schedules; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} analyzing planned schedules in relation to time
    worked in order to assess whether fatigue is being managed.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The air operator's fatigue risk assessment process
  shall be based on the information referred to in subsection (1) and
  shall include procedures for

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} identifying the cause of fatigue-related hazards;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} assessing the likelihood that a fatigue-related
    event will occur and the severity of its consequences;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} identifying and prioritizing the risks that need to
    be managed;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} creating and updating a record of the risks that
    are identified;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} determining the actions to be taken to manage the
    risks referred to in paragraph (c), including the preventive
    measures or corrective actions; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} developing safety performance indicators to measure
    the effectiveness of the measures and actions taken under paragraph
    (e).

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1280016){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1280016.html"}
:::

#### [Collaboration with Employees]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1280017 .Subheading}

**[[700.217]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.217 .sectionLabel}** The air
operator shall have a process to collaborate with employees in the
development of the policy and procedure for the internal reporting of
fatigue.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1280020){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1280020.html"}
:::

#### [Fatigue Risk Management Promotion]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1280021 .Subheading}

- **[[700.218]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.218
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In the case of an air operator to
  whom sections 700.20 to 700.72 or 700.101 to 700.135 apply, its
  program for fatigue risk management promotion shall include training
  for its employees on the following subjects:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the components and functioning of the fatigue risk
    management system and the employees' responsibilities with respect
    to the system;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken with respect to
    fatigue-related risks; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the requirements of these Regulations with respect
    to fatigue management.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} In the case of an air operator to whom sections
  702.91 to 702.98 apply, its program for fatigue risk management
  promotion shall include training for its employees on the following
  subjects:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the components and functioning of the fatigue risk
    management system and the employees' responsibilities with respect
    to the system;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the actions to be taken with respect to
    fatigue-related risks;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the requirements of these Regulations with respect
    to fatigue management;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} personal fatigue management strategies relating to

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} sleep hygiene,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} lifestyle, exercise and diet, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the consumption of alcohol and drugs;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the impact of fatigue on aviation safety;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} sleep requirements and the science relating to
    fatigue;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the causes and consequences of fatigue;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} how to recognize fatigue in themselves and in
    others;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} sleep disorders, their impact on aviation safety
    and treatment options; and

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} human and organizational factors that may cause
    fatigue, including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} sleep quality and duration,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the effect of shift work and overtime,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the circadian rhythm, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the effects of changes of time zones.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The programs set out in subsections (1) and (2) shall
  include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} competency-based training for persons who have been
    assigned duties in respect of the fatigue risk management system;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} means of measuring the level of competency attained
    by each person who receives the training.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of promoting fatigue risk
  management, an air operator shall have a procedure for communicating
  the following information to its employees:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} industry reports on fatigue;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} industry best practices in respect of fatigue risk
    management;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} advancements in the science relating to fatigue;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the results of the data analysis conducted in
    accordance with the process referred to in subsection 700.216(2);

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} updates to the fatigue risk management system; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the results of the review of the fatigue risk
    management system.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1280056){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1280056.html"}
:::

#### [Quality Assurance Program for the Fatigue Risk Management System]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1280057 .Subheading}

- **[[700.219]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.219
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The air operator's quality assurance
  program for the fatigue risk management system shall include a process
  for the audit of the fatigue risk management system that includes
  procedures for

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} auditing the extent to which the air operator has
    implemented its fatigue risk management system, including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a checklist setting out all of the components of
      the air operator's fatigue risk management system that are to be
      audited, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a plan establishing the frequency of the audits
      and the manner in which they will be conducted;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} auditing the fatigue risk management system in the
    event of an accident or incident;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} analyzing the findings of the audit and determining
    the contributing factors of those findings;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} developing, implementing and monitoring preventive
    measures and corrective actions to address the findings of the
    audit; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} keeping and updating records, including the
    findings of the audit, the preventive measures and corrective
    actions to address those findings and any follow-up taken in respect
    of those measures and actions.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The air operator's process for the periodic review of
  the effectiveness of its fatigue risk management system shall include
  procedures for the assessment of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the fatigue risk management process;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the reliability of the safety performance
    indicators; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the attainment of the safety objectives.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall have procedures for the ongoing
  monitoring of the effect of the variance described in the notice of
  intent on the flight crew members' levels of fatigue and alertness.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1280073){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1280073.html"}
:::

**\[700.220 to 700.224 reserved\]**

#### [Safety Case]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1280075 .Subheading}

- **[[700.225]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.225
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The air operator shall ensure that a
  safety case is established in respect of a flight subject to an
  exemption referred to in section 700.200 to demonstrate that the
  variance described in the notice of intent does not increase the level
  of fatigue or decrease the level of alertness of the flight crew
  members.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The safety case shall consist of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a description of the flight in respect of which an
    exemption set out in section 700.200 applies;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the provisions of these Regulations from which the
    air operator and flight crew members are exempt;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a description of the manner in which the flight is
    conducted results in a variance from the requirements of the
    provisions referred to in paragraph (b);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the data collection methodology and data used
    initially to establish, in respect of the flight, the baseline
    levels of fatigue and alertness of the flight crew members and to
    identify fatigue-related hazards and risks;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the data collection methods used to evaluate the
    safety case on an ongoing basis;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the scientific studies used to demonstrate that the
    variance referred to in paragraph (c) is not likely to have an
    adverse effect on the flight crew members' levels of fatigue and
    alertness;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} an analysis of the effect of the variance on the
    levels of fatigue and alertness of flight crew members that takes
    into account the flight crew members' schedule before and after the
    flight in respect of which the exemption applies and the findings of
    the fatigue risk assessment;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the fatigue risk controls that are implemented to
    address the findings of the risk assessment;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} procedures to measure the effect of the variance on
    the levels of fatigue and alertness of the flight crew members;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} the preventive measures or corrective actions that
    are taken to remedy any adverse effect of the variance on the levels
    of fatigue and alertness of the flight crew members; and

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} the means that will be used to monitor the
    effectiveness of the fatigue risk management system in managing the
    safety case.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A safety case is validated when the following
  conditions are met:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} fatigue and alertness data have been collected
    during a period of not less than one year and not more than two
    years starting on the day on which the flight is first conducted
    under an exemption referred to in section 700.200, for not less than
    20 consecutive flights identified in the notice of intent, and the
    data shows that not more than 5% of those flights have an adverse
    effect of more than 5% on the baseline levels of fatigue and
    alertness of the flight crew members determined by means of the
    methodology described in paragraph (2)(d);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the fatigue risk assessment has been conducted and
    the findings of the assessment have been analyzed;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} mitigation measures have been implemented to manage
    the hazards and risks related to the variance to remedy increases in
    the level of fatigue and decreases in the level of alertness of
    flight crew members;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the mitigation measures have been monitored to
    determine their effect on the flight crew members' levels of fatigue
    and alertness;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} corrective actions have been taken if the
    mitigation measures monitored under paragraph (d) do not achieve the
    desired effect on the flight crew members' levels of fatigue and
    alertness; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the effectiveness of the mitigation measures and,
    if applicable, the corrective actions in maintaining the established
    levels of fatigue and alertness of the flight crew members is shown.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1280098){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1280098.html"}
:::

**\[700.226 to 700.230 reserved\]**

#### [Fatigue Risk Management System --- Initial Audit]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1280100 .Subheading}

- **[[700.231]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.231
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall ensure that an
  initial audit of its fatigue risk management system is conducted after
  validation of the safety case in accordance with the process
  established under subsection 700.219(1).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The air operator shall analyze the findings of the
  audit and shall, if deficiencies are identified,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} investigate and analyze their cause and
    contributing factors; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} develop and implement preventive measures and
    corrective actions to address the findings.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The air operator shall assess the preventive measures
  and corrective actions to ensure that they are effective and are used
  on an ongoing basis to improve the fatigue risk management system.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply if the air operator has
  already implemented a fatigue risk management system and validates a
  safety case for a subsequent variance for the purposes of an exemption
  referred to in subsection 700.234(1) or uses an approved safety case
  in respect of another flight for the purposes of an exemption referred
  to in subsection 700.240(1) if an audit has already been conducted.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1280109){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1280109.html"}
:::

#### [Submission of Safety Case for Approval]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1280110 .Subheading}

**[[700.232]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.232 .sectionLabel}** The air
operator shall submit the validated safety case to the Minister for
approval along with a statement that the initial audit has been
conducted in accordance with section 700.231 and that the fatigue risk
management system meets the requirements of this Division.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1280113){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1280113.html"}
:::

#### [Approval of the Safety Case]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1280114 .Subheading}

**[[700.233]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.233 .sectionLabel}** The Minister
shall approve the safety case of an air operator if the Minister
determines, on the basis of the information provided by the operator,
that the conditions of subsection 700.225(3) are met and that the
initial audit has been conducted.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1280117){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1280117.html"}
:::

#### [Continuing Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1280118 .Subheading}

- **[[700.234]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.234
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator and a flight crew
  member who are exempt under section 700.200 from the application of
  certain provisions in respect of a flight continue, on receipt of the
  approval of the safety case by the air operator, to be exempt from the
  application of the same provisions for that flight and, if applicable,
  for any other flight described in the notice of intent under section
  700.206.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The exemption referred to in subsection (1) continues
  to have effect as long as

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator maintains the fatigue risk
    management system in accordance with the applicable conditions of
    this Division;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator monitors the effectiveness of the
    safety case in managing the fatigue and alertness of the flight crew
    members in accordance with section 700.248; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the air operator remedies any adverse effects of
    the variance on the flight crew members' levels of fatigue and
    alertness no later than 60 days after the date on which the adverse
    effect is identified in the course of monitoring.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1280126){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1280126.html"}
:::

**\[700.235 to 700.239 reserved\]**

#### [Exemption for Other Flights]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1280128 .Subheading}

- **[[700.240]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.240
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator and flight crew
  members who are exempt under section 700.234 from the application of
  certain provisions in respect of a flight on the basis of an approved
  safety case are exempt from the application of the same provisions, on
  the basis of the same approved safety case, in respect of another
  flight if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator has provided the Minister a letter
    of confirmation in accordance with subsection (2);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the duration of the flight duty period for the
    other flight is not longer than the duration of the flight duty
    period of the flight;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the number of consecutive flight duty periods for
    the other flight does not exceed the number of consecutive flight
    duty periods for the flight;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} each flight duty period for the other flight starts
    within 60 minutes of each corresponding flight duty period for the
    flight;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the other flight is conducted in the same time zone
    or across the same number of time zones in the same direction as the
    flight and is conducted by flight crew members who are all
    acclimatized to the same time zone;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} any part of the flight duty period for the other
    flight that occurs within the flight crew members' window of
    circadian low does not exceed the duration of the flight duty period
    for the flight that occurs within the flight crew members' window of
    circadian low;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the other flight is conducted using aircraft of the
    same type as that used to conduct the flight;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the other flight is conducted with the same number
    of flight crew members on board as the flight;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the operating environment of the other flight is
    similar to the operating environment of the flight;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} the hazards and risks associated with the other
    flight are similar to those of the flight;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} the duration of each rest period before and after
    each flight duty period associated with the other flight is not
    shorter than each rest period associated with the flight;

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} the time of day of each rest period of the other
    flight is similar to the time of day of each rest period of the
    flight; and

  - [(m)]{.lawlabel} the number of consecutive flight duty periods
    occurring during any part of each flight crew member's window of
    circadian low for the other flight does not exceed the number of
    such consecutive flight duty periods for the flight.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The air operator shall provide the Minister a letter
  of confirmation for the other flight that will be conducted under an
  exemption referred to in subsection (1) that sets out

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a description of the other flight that will be
    subject to the exemption on the basis of the approved safety case;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the provisions of these Regulations from which the
    air operator and flight crew members will be exempt in respect of
    the other flight;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a description of the manner in which the other
    flight will be conducted results in a variance from the requirements
    of the provisions referred to in paragraph (b) in respect of the
    other flight;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a statement that the conditions in paragraphs
    (1)(a) to (m) are met; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the date on which the exemption will apply to the
    other flight for the first time.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An approved safety case in respect of a flight shall
  not be used for another flight unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the provisions of these Regulations from which the
    air operator is exempted are the same for all the flights; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the manner in which the flights are conducted
    results in a variance from the requirements of the provisions
    referred to in paragraph (a) is the same for all the flights.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The exemption referred to in subsection (1) continues
  to have effect as long as

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator maintains the fatigue risk
    management system in accordance with the applicable conditions of
    this Division;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator monitors the effectiveness of the
    safety case in managing the fatigue and alertness of the flight crew
    members in accordance with section 700.248; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the air operator remedies any adverse effects of
    the variance on the flight crew members' levels of fatigue and
    alertness no later than 60 days after the date on which the adverse
    effect is identified in the course of monitoring.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1280158){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1280158.html"}
:::

**\[700.241 to 700.245 reserved\]**

#### [Non-availability of Exemption]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1280160 .Subheading}

**[[700.246]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.246 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
who was exempt from the application of provisions in respect of a flight
under section 700.200 and who has not validated a safety case in the
period set out in paragraph 700.200(3)(b) shall not be exempted from the
application of the same provisions and in respect of the same flight for
a period of two years after the expiry of that period.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1280163){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1280163.html"}
:::

#### [Fatigue Risk Management System --- Audit]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1280164 .Subheading}

**[[700.247]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.247 .sectionLabel}** The air
operator who has implemented a fatigue risk management system in
accordance with this Division shall ensure that an audit of its system
is conducted, in accordance with the process referred to in subsection
700.219(1),

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} within 12 months after the day on which the initial
  audit is completed under subsection 700.231(1);

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} within 12 months after the day on which the previous
  audit was completed;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} after an incident or accident; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} after a major change in the air operator's activities
  that could affect the levels of fatigue or alertness of the flight
  crew members.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1280171){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1280171.html"}
:::

#### [Variance --- Monitoring of Effects]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1280172 .Subheading}

- **[[700.248]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.248
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The air operator shall monitor, in
  accordance with the procedures referred to in subsection 700.219(3),
  the effects of the variance described in the approved safety case on
  the flight crew members' levels of fatigue and alertness for each
  period of six months during which the flight that is subject to the
  exemption referred to in section 700.234 is conducted.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The air operator shall collect data in respect of a
  representative number of flights conducted over each period of six
  months in accordance with the methodology set out in the approved
  safety case.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the monitoring shows that the variance described
  in the approved safety case has an adverse effect on the flight crew
  members' levels of fatigue or alertness, the air operator shall
  develop and take corrective actions to remedy the adverse effect of
  the variance.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} If corrective actions are taken, the air operator
  shall assess their effectiveness.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} If the corrective actions remedy the adverse effect
  of the variance, the air operator shall modify the safety case to take
  into account the corrective actions and inform the Minister of the
  modification within 60 days after it is made.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1280180){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1280180.html"}
:::

#### [Fatigue Risk Management System --- Review]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1280181 .Subheading}

- **[[700.249]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.249
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The air operator shall conduct a
  review of its fatigue risk management system, in accordance with the
  procedures referred to in subsection 700.219(2), at least once every
  12 months after the initial audit required by subsection 700.231(1) is
  conducted.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The review of the fatigue risk management system
  shall assess

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the fatigue risk management process;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the reliability of the safety performance
    indicators; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the attainment of the safety objectives.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The air operator shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} determine what corrective actions are necessary to
    remedy any deficiency identified by the review and take those
    actions;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} keep a record of any determination made under
    paragraph (a) and the reason for it; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the air operator has assigned management
    functions to another person, provide that person with a copy of the
    determination.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall not assign a duty relating to
  the quality assurance program for the fatigue risk management system
  to a person who is responsible for carrying out a task or an activity
  evaluated by that program unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} owing to the size, nature and complexity of the air
    operator's operations and activities, it is impractical to assign
    the duty to a person who is not responsible for carrying out the
    task or activity;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} based on a risk analysis, assigning the duty to a
    person who is responsible for carrying out the task or activity will
    not result in an increased risk to aviation safety; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the audit of the fatigue risk management system
    will not be compromised.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1280197){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1280197.html"}
:::

**\[700.250 to 700.254 reserved\]**

#### [Training]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1280199 .Subheading}

- **[[700.255]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.255
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The air operator shall ensure that
  training is provided to its employees every 12 months and covers the
  subjects set out in section 700.218.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The air operator shall ensure that there is a
  training record that includes

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a description of all the training that each
    employee has received in accordance with this section; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} evaluation results for each employee who has
    received training in accordance with this section.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1280213){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1280213.html"}
:::

#### [Documentation --- Keeping up to Date]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1280214 .Subheading}

- **[[700.256]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.256
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The air operator shall ensure that
  the fatigue risk management system documentation reflects the
  procedures and processes that have been established and implemented.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The air operator shall notify the Minister of any
  changes to the fatigue risk management system within 60 days after the
  change is made.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1280219){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1280219.html"}
:::

#### [Data and Documentation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1280220 .Subheading}

- **[[700.257]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.257
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The air operator shall collect data
  in respect of flight crew members on the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the fatigue model used to assess the levels of
    fatigue and alertness of the flight crew members;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} records of testing for fatigue and alertness;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the evaluation of the level of fatigue against the
    baseline level established for comparative analysis.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The air operator shall keep the following
  documentation:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} records and documents created in the course of
    conducting an audit or a review under this Division; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any other material created under the fatigue risk
    management system.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1280230){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1280230.html"}
:::

#### [Preservation of Information]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1280231 .Subheading}

**[[700.258]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.258 .sectionLabel}** The air
operator shall keep the information collected and created under this
Division for five years after the day on which the information was
collected or created.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1280234){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1280234.html"}
:::

#### [Access to Documentation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1280235 .Subheading}

**[[700.259]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-700.259 .sectionLabel}** The air
operator shall make available to the Minister on request any
documentation that it is required to collect or create under this
Division.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2018-269, s. 13](#1045265-1280238){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045265-1280238.html"}
:::

### [Subpart 1 --- Foreign Air Operations]{.HTitleText2} {#h-997278 .Subheading}

#### [Division I --- General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997279 .Subheading}

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997280 .Subheading}

**[[701.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.01 .sectionLabel}** This Subpart
applies in respect of the operation in Canada of a foreign state
aircraft or an aircraft operated by a foreign operator in an air
transport service.

##### [Requirement for Canadian Foreign Air Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997282 .Subheading}

- **[[701.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.02
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) and (3),
  no person shall operate an aircraft in Canada unless the person
  complies with the conditions in a Canadian foreign air operator
  certificate issued to that person by the Minister pursuant to section
  701.07.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person is not required to hold a Canadian foreign
  air operator certificate in order to conduct an overflight of Canada
  or to perform a technical landing in Canada unless the person operates
  the aircraft under section 701.19, 701.20 or 701.21.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A person is not required to hold a Canadian foreign
  air operator certificate in order to operate a foreign state aircraft
  in Canada.

##### [Requirements for Flight Authorization]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997287 .Subheading}

- **[[701.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.03
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person, other than the holder of
  a Canadian foreign air operator certificate, shall conduct an
  overflight of Canada or perform a technical landing in Canada unless
  the person is authorized to do so in a flight authorization issued by
  the Minister pursuant to section 701.10.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate a foreign state aircraft in
  Canada unless the person is authorized to do so in a flight
  authorization issued by the Minister pursuant to section 701.10.

**\[701.04 to 701.06 reserved\]**

#### [Division II --- Certification and Authorization]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997292 .Subheading}

##### [Issuance or Amendment of Canadian Foreign Air Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997293 .Subheading}

**[[701.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.07 .sectionLabel}** Subject to
section 6.71 of the Act, the Minister shall, on receipt of an
application submitted in the form and manner required by the Commercial
Air Service Standards, issue or amend a Canadian foreign air operator
certificate.

##### [Contents of Canadian Foreign Air Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997295 .Subheading}

**[[701.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.08 .sectionLabel}** A Canadian
foreign air operator certificate shall contain

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the legal name, trade name and address of the foreign
  air operator;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number of the foreign air operator certificate;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the effective date of certification;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the date of issue of the certificate;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the general conditions identified in section 701.09;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} specific conditions with respect to

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the areas of operation authorized,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the types of service authorized,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the types of aircraft authorized, the conditions
    of operation and, if applicable, their registration, and

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the base of operations; and

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} where the foreign air operator complies with the
  Commercial Air Service Standards, operations specifications with
  respect to

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} instrument approach procedures,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} special weather minima authorizations,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} navigation system authorizations,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} authorizations concerning flight crew member
    complement,

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} special helicopter procedures, and

  - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} any other condition pertaining to the operation
    that the Minister deems necessary for aviation safety.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2022-246, s. 20(F)](#1380156-1380789){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1380156-1380789.html"}
- [SOR/2025-26, s. 27](#1511725-1516273){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1511725-1516273.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-701.08-20221207.html "Link to previous version of section 701.08"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [General Conditions of Canadian Foreign Air Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997314 .Subheading}

**[[701.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.09 .sectionLabel}** A Canadian
foreign air operator certificate shall contain the following general
conditions:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the foreign air operator shall have a valid air
  operator certificate or equivalent document issued by the state of the
  foreign air operator;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the foreign air operator shall make no change in its
  air transport service in Canada, except in the case of an emergency,
  without notifying the Minister;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the foreign air operator shall notify the Minister
  within 10 working days after any change in its legal name or trade
  name;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the foreign air operator shall conduct flight
  operations in accordance with the ICAO standards;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the foreign air operator shall maintain its aircraft
  in accordance with the ICAO standards;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the foreign air operator shall comply with the
  applicable provisions of these Regulations; and

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the foreign air operator shall conduct a safe
  operation.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2022-246, s. 21(F)](#1380158-1380791){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1380158-1380791.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-701.09-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 701.09"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Issuance of Flight Authorization]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997323 .Subheading}

**[[701.10]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.10 .sectionLabel}** Subject to
section 6.71 of the Act, the Minister shall, on receipt of an
application submitted in the form and manner required by the Commercial
Air Service Standards, issue a flight authorization

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} to conduct an overflight of Canada or to perform a
  technical landing in Canada; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} to operate a foreign state aircraft in Canada.

##### [Contents of Flight Authorization]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997327 .Subheading}

**[[701.11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.11 .sectionLabel}** A flight
authorization shall contain

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name of the holder of the flight authorization or
  of the person responsible for the flight;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the type of aircraft, the registration mark and, if
  applicable, the serial number;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the routing;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the date and time of arrival at, and departure from,
  the airports concerned;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the places of embarkation or disembarkation of
  passengers or freight;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} an authorization for the transportation of dangerous
  goods or agricultural products, if applicable;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a foreign state aircraft, an
  authorization to conduct flight operations referred to in section
  701.19, 701.20 or 701.21;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} a requirement to conduct all operations in accordance
  with the applicable provisions of these Regulations; and

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} any condition pertaining to the operation that the
  Minister deems necessary for aviation safety.

**\[701.12 to 701.15 reserved\]**

#### [Division III --- Flight Operations]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997339 .Subheading}

##### [Extended Range Twin-engined Operations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997340 .Subheading}

- **[[701.16]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.16
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no
  foreign air operator shall commence a flight in Canada in a
  twin-engined aeroplane certified for more than 20 passenger seats that
  is intended to be operated on a route containing a point that is
  farther from an adequate aerodrome than the distance that can be flown
  in 60 minutes at the one-engine-inoperative cruise speed, unless the
  flight is conducted wholly within Canadian Domestic Airspace.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A foreign air operator may commence a flight referred
  to in subsection (1) where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane is turbine-powered;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the foreign air operator holds a valid
    authorization or equivalent document issued by the state of the
    foreign air operator for extended range twin-engined operations; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the foreign air operator is authorized to do so in
    its Canadian foreign air operator certificate.

##### [Canadian Minimum Navigation Performance Specifications (CMNPS) or North Atlantic Minimum Navigation Performance Specifications (NAT-MNPS) Airspace]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997347 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2006-77, s. 25(F)

\]
:::

- **[[701.17]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.17
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no
  foreign air operator shall commence a flight in Canada in an aircraft
  that is intended to be operated in airspace designated as CMNPS or
  NAT-MNPS unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft has been certified by the state of
    registry as meeting the minimum navigation performance
    specifications contained in the North Atlantic MNPS Airspace
    Operations Manual;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the foreign air operator holds a valid
    authorization or equivalent document issued by the state of the
    foreign air operator or the state of registry for flight operations
    in airspace designated as CMNPS or NAT-MNPS; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the foreign air operator is authorized to do so in
    its Canadian foreign air operator certificate.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A foreign air operator may, in airspace designated as
  CMNPS, commence a flight in Canada in an aircraft that has not been
  certified in accordance with paragraph (1)(a) where the appropriate
  ATC unit indicates that the aircraft can be accommodated without
  penalizing CMNPS-certified aircraft.

##### [Routes in Uncontrolled Airspace]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997356 .Subheading}

**[[701.18]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.18 .sectionLabel}** No foreign air
operator commencing a flight in Canada shall, in uncontrolled airspace,
conduct an IFR flight or a night VFR flight on a route other than an air
route unless the foreign air operator

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in its Canadian foreign air
  operator certificate; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [No Alternate Aerodrome --- IFR Flight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997360 .Subheading}

**[[701.19]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.19 .sectionLabel}** For the purposes
of section 602.122, a person may conduct an IFR flight where an
alternate aerodrome has not been designated in the IFR flight plan or in
the IFR flight itinerary if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a foreign air operator, the foreign
  air operator is authorized to do so in its Canadian foreign air
  operator certificate and complies with the Commercial Air Service
  Standards; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a person who operates a foreign state
  aircraft, the person is authorized to do so in a flight authorization
  and complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [Take-off Minima]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997364 .Subheading}

**[[701.20]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.20 .sectionLabel}** For the purposes
of section 602.126, a person may conduct a take-off in an aircraft where
weather conditions are below the take-off minima specified in the Canada
Air Pilot if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a foreign air operator, the foreign
  air operator is authorized to do so in its Canadian foreign air
  operator certificate and complies with the Commercial Air Service
  Standards; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a person who operates a foreign state
  aircraft, the person is authorized to do so in a flight authorization
  and complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [Landing Minima]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997368 .Subheading}

**[[701.21]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.21 .sectionLabel}** For the purposes
of subsection 602.128(4), a person may conduct a CAT II or CAT III
precision approach in an IFR aircraft if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a foreign air operator, the foreign
  air operator is authorized to do so in its Canadian foreign air
  operator certificate and holds a valid authorization or equivalent
  document issued by the state of the foreign air operator to conduct a
  CAT II or CAT III precision approach in Canada; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a person who operates a foreign state
  aircraft, the person is authorized to do so in a flight authorization
  and complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [Transport of Passengers in Single-engined Aircraft]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997372 .Subheading}

- **[[701.22]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.22
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no
  foreign air operator commencing a flight in Canada shall operate a
  single-engined aircraft with passengers on board in IFR flight or in
  night VFR flight.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A foreign air operator may operate a single-engined
  aircraft with passengers on board in IFR flight or in night VFR flight
  if the foreign air operator

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so by the state of the foreign
    air operator;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in its Canadian foreign air
    operator certificate; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [Admission to Flight Deck]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997379 .Subheading}

- **[[701.23]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.23
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where a Department of Transport air
  carrier inspector presents an official identity card to the
  pilot-in-command of an aircraft operated by a foreign air operator in
  Canada, the pilot-in-command shall give the inspector free and
  uninterrupted access to the flight deck of the aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A foreign air operator and the pilot-in-command shall
  make available for the use of the air carrier inspector the observer
  seat most suitable to perform the inspector's duties, as determined by
  the inspector.

##### [Seats for Cabin Safety Inspectors]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997383 .Subheading}

**[[701.24]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.24 .sectionLabel}** A foreign air
operator shall provide a cabin safety inspector who is performing an
in-flight cabin inspection in Canada with a confirmed passenger seat in
the passenger compartment.

##### [Aircraft Icing Operations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997385 .Subheading}

- **[[701.25]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.25
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In this section, [[critical
  surfaces]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the wings, control surfaces,
  rotors, propellers, horizontal stabilizers, vertical stabilizers or
  any other stabilizing surfaces of an aircraft, as well as any other
  surfaces identified as critical surfaces in the aircraft flight
  manual.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct or attempt to conduct a
  take-off in an aircraft that has frost, ice or snow adhering to any of
  its critical surfaces.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (2), a person may conduct a
  take-off in an aircraft that has frost caused by cold-soaked fuel
  adhering to the underside or upper side, or both, of its wings if the
  take-off is conducted in accordance with the aircraft manufacturer's
  instructions for take-off under those conditions.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where conditions are such that frost, ice or snow may
  reasonably be expected to adhere to an aircraft, no person shall
  conduct or attempt to conduct a take-off in the aircraft unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft has been inspected immediately prior
    to take-off to determine whether any frost, ice or snow is adhering
    to any of its critical surfaces; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the foreign air operator or the holder of the
    flight authorization has

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} established, in accordance with ICAO Document No.
      9640 entitled Manual of Aircraft Ground De/Anti-icing Operations,
      an aircraft ground icing operations program that has been approved
      by the state of the foreign air operator or of the holder of the
      flight authorization, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} submitted to the Minister an aircraft ground
      icing operations program that meets the Commercial Air Service
      Standards.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The inspection referred to in paragraph (4)(a) shall
  be performed from outside the aircraft.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} The inspection referred to in paragraph (4)(a) shall
  be performed by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a flight crew member of the aircraft who is
    designated by the pilot-in-command; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a person, other than a person referred to in
    paragraph (a) or (b), who is designated by the foreign air operator
    or the holder of the flight authorization.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} No person shall perform the inspection referred to in
  paragraph (4)(a) unless the person has received annual training
  concerning aircraft surface contamination in accordance with the
  Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(8)]{.lawlabel} Where, before commencing a take-off, a crew member of
  an aircraft observes that there is frost, ice or snow adhering to the
  wings of the aircraft, the crew member shall immediately report that
  observation to the pilot-in-command, and the pilot-in-command or a
  flight crew member designated by the pilot-in-command shall inspect
  the wings of the aircraft before take-off.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-253, s. 10](#1274661-1276864){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1274661-1276864.html"}
:::
