[Previous
Version](section-701.25-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 701.25"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Division IV --- Flight Deck Security]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997402 .Subheading}

##### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997403 .Subheading}

**[[701.26]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.26 .sectionLabel}** In this Division,
[[payload capacity]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the maximum zero fuel
weight of an aeroplane set out in the type certificate issued in respect
of the aeroplane less

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the empty weight of the aeroplane;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the equipment necessary for the operation of the
  aeroplane; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the operating load of the aeroplane, which includes
  the minimum flight crew.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2003-121, s. 2
:::

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997410 .Subheading}

- **[[701.27]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.27
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} All the provisions of this Division
  apply in respect of the operation by a foreign air operator, in
  Canadian airspace, of a transport category aircraft that is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a passenger-carrying aeroplane in respect of which
    a type certificate has been issued authorizing the transport of 20
    or more passengers; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an all-cargo aeroplane with a payload capacity of
    more than 3 405 kg (7,500 pounds) that was equipped with a flight
    deck door on June 21, 2002.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Section 701.28 also applies in respect of the
  operation by a foreign air operator, in Canadian airspace, of a
  transport category aircraft that is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a passenger-carrying aeroplane in respect of which
    a type certificate has been issued authorizing the transport of
    fewer than 20 passengers; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an all-cargo aeroplane with a payload capacity of 3
    405 kg (7,500 pounds) or less that was equipped with a flight deck
    door on June 21, 2002.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2003-121, s. 2
:::

##### [Admission to Flight Deck]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997420 .Subheading}

**[[701.28]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.28 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
be admitted to the flight deck of an aeroplane other than

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a flight crew member;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a crew member performing their duties;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} an inspector of the civil aviation authority of the
  state where the aeroplane is registered; or

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a person who has expertise related to the aeroplane,
  its equipment or its crew members and who is required to be in the
  flight deck to provide a service to the air operator.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2003-121, s. 2
:::

##### [Closing and Locking of Flight Deck Door]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997428 .Subheading}

- **[[701.29]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.29
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), the
  pilot-in-command of an aeroplane that is equipped with a lockable
  flight deck door and that is carrying passengers shall ensure that at
  all times from the moment the passenger entry doors are closed in
  preparation for departure until they are opened on arrival the flight
  deck door is closed and locked.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply when crew members or
  persons authorized in accordance with subsection 701.28 are required
  to enter or leave the flight deck

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} for the performance of their duties;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} for physiological needs; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} for an overriding concern related to the safety of
    the flight.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2003-121, s. 2
:::

##### [Doors and Locks]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997437 .Subheading}

- **[[701.30]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-701.30
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (3) and (4),
  no foreign air operator shall operate a transport category aircraft,
  except for a newly manufactured aeroplane on a non-revenue flight and
  any aeroplane on an overflight, unless the transport category aircraft
  is equipped with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a passenger-carrying aeroplane,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a door between the flight deck and the passenger
      compartment, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if the aeroplane is equipped with a crew rest
      facility having an entry from the flight deck and a separate entry
      from the passenger compartment, a door between the crew rest
      facility and the passenger compartment; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an all-cargo aeroplane that was
    equipped with a flight deck door on June 21, 2002,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a door between the flight deck and a compartment
      occupied by a person, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if the aeroplane is equipped with a crew rest
      facility having an entry from the flight deck and a separate entry
      from a compartment occupied by a person, a door between the crew
      rest facility and the compartment.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The doors required by subsection (1) shall be
  equipped with a locking device that can be unlocked only from inside
  the flight deck or the crew rest facility, as the case may be.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A key shall be readily available to each crew member
  for each door that separates a passenger compartment or a compartment
  occupied by a person from an emergency exit, with the exception of a
  door required by subsection (1).

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} No crew member, except a flight crew member, shall
  have a key to a door required by subsection (1) at any time from the
  moment the passenger entry doors are closed in preparation for
  departure until they are opened on arrival unless the locking device
  required by subsection (2) is installed and locked.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} No foreign air operator shall operate an aeroplane
  that is required by subsection (1) to be equipped with a door unless
  each door meets the design requirements of section 525.795 of the
  Airworthiness Manual in effect on May 1, 2002.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2003-121, s. 2
:::

**\[701.31 to 701.36 reserved\]**

### [Subpart 2 --- Aerial Work]{.HTitleText2} {#h-997453 .Subheading}

#### [Division I --- General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997454 .Subheading}

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997455 .Subheading}

- **[[702.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.01
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), this
  Subpart applies in respect of the operation of an aeroplane or
  helicopter in aerial work involving

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the carriage on board of persons other than flight
    crew members;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the carriage of helicopter Class B, C or D external
    loads;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the towing of objects; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the dispersal of products.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} This Subpart does not apply in respect of the
  operation of an ultra-light aeroplane, or in respect of the operation
  of an aircraft in aerial work involving sightseeing operations.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/99-158, s. 4
:::

##### [Aircraft Operation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997465 .Subheading}

**[[702.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.02 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an aircraft under this Subpart unless the air operator
complies with the conditions and operations specifications in an air
operator certificate issued to that operator by the Minister pursuant to
section 702.07.

**\[702.03 to 702.06 reserved\]**

#### [Division II --- Certification]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997468 .Subheading}

##### [Issuance or Amendment of Air Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997469 .Subheading}

- **[[702.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.07
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 6.71 of the Act,
  the Minister shall, on receipt of an application submitted in the form
  and manner required by the Commercial Air Service Standards, issue or
  amend an air operator certificate where the applicant demonstrates to
  the Minister the ability to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} maintain an adequate organizational structure;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} maintain an operational control system;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} meet training program requirements;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} comply with maintenance requirements;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} meet the Commercial Air Service Standards for the
    operation; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} conduct the operation safely.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), an applicant
  shall have

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a management organization capable of exercising
    operational control;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} managerial personnel who meet the Commercial Air
    Service Standards, are employed on a full-time basis and perform the
    functions related to the following positions, namely,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} operations manager,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} chief pilot, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} where the applicant does not hold an approved
      maintenance organization (AMO) certificate, maintenance manager;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the ground handling services and equipment
    necessary to ensure the safe handling of its flights;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} aircraft that are properly equipped for and flight
    crew members who are qualified for the area of operation and the
    type of operation;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} an operational control system that meets the
    requirements of section 702.12;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a training program that meets the requirements of
    this Subpart;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} legal custody and control of at least one aircraft
    of each category of aircraft that is to be operated;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} a company operations manual that meets the
    requirements of sections 702.81 and 702.82; and

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a maintenance control system approved pursuant to
    Subpart 6.

##### [Contents of Air Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997491 .Subheading}

**[[702.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.08 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
certificate shall contain

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the legal name, trade name and address of the air
  operator;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number of the air operator certificate;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the effective date of certification;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the date of issue of the certificate;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the general conditions identified in section 702.09;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} specific conditions with respect to

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the areas of operation authorized,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the types of service authorized,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the types of aircraft authorized and, if
    applicable, their registration, and any operational restrictions,
    and

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the main base and, if applicable, sub-bases; and

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} where the air operator complies with the Commercial
  Air Service Standards, operations specifications with respect to

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} aircraft performance, equipment and emergency
    equipment requirements,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} instrument approach procedures,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} operations over a built-up area or in an aerial
    work zone,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the carriage of persons other than flight crew
    members and persons whose presence on board an aircraft is essential
    during flight,

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} special weather minima authorizations,

  - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} authorizations concerning flight crew member
    complement,

  - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} navigation system authorizations,

  - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} pilot training and pilot proficiency checks,

  - [(ix)]{.lawlabel} special helicopter procedures,

  - [(x)]{.lawlabel} the air operator maintenance control system
    approved pursuant to Subpart 6,

  - [(xi)]{.lawlabel} leasing arrangements, and

  - [(xii)]{.lawlabel} any other condition pertaining to the operation
    that the Minister deems necessary for aviation safety.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2022-246, s. 22(F)](#1380160-1380793){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1380160-1380793.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-702.08-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 702.08"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [General Conditions of Air Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997516 .Subheading}

**[[702.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.09 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
certificate shall contain the following general conditions:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall conduct flight operations in
  accordance with its company operations manual;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall maintain an adequate
  organizational structure;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall employ managerial personnel
  who meet the Commercial Air Service Standards;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall conduct training in accordance
  with its training program approved pursuant to this Subpart;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall maintain aircraft that are
  properly equipped for the area of operation and the type of operation;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall employ crew members who are
  qualified for the area of operation and the type of operation;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall maintain its aircraft in
  accordance with the requirements of Subpart 6;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall maintain operational support
  services and equipment that meet the Commercial Air Service Standards;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall notify the Minister within 10
  working days after

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} changing its legal name, its trade name, its main
    base, a sub-base or its managerial personnel, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} ceasing to operate a type of aircraft authorized
    under this Subpart; and

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall conduct a safe operation.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-152, s. 3
- [SOR/2022-246, s. 23(F)](#1380162-1380794){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1380162-1380794.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-702.09-20090528.html "Link to previous version of section 702.09"){.PITLink}
:::

**\[702.10 reserved\]**

#### [Division III --- Flight Operations]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997533 .Subheading}

##### [Operating Instructions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997534 .Subheading}

- **[[702.11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.11
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall ensure that
  all operations personnel are properly instructed about their duties
  and about the relationship of their duties to the operation as a
  whole.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operations personnel of an air operator shall
  follow the procedures specified in the air operator's company
  operations manual in the performance of their duties.

##### [Operational Control System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997538 .Subheading}

**[[702.12]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.12 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an aircraft unless the air operator has an operational
control system that meets the Commercial Air Service Standards and is
under the control of its operations manager.

##### [Flight Authorization]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997540 .Subheading}

**[[702.13]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.13 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
commence a flight unless the flight has been authorized in accordance
with the procedures specified in the air operator's company operations
manual.

##### [Operational Flight Plan]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997542 .Subheading}

**[[702.14]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.14 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall permit a person to commence a flight unless an operational flight
plan that meets the Commercial Air Service Standards has been prepared
in accordance with the procedures specified in the air operator's
company operations manual.

##### [Maintenance of Aircraft]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997544 .Subheading}

**[[702.15]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.15 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall permit a person to conduct a take-off in an aircraft that has not
been maintained in accordance with the air operator's maintenance
control system.

##### [Carriage of Persons]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997546 .Subheading}

**[[702.16]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.16 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall allow a person who is not a flight crew member to be carried on
board an aircraft unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person's presence on board is essential during
  the flight;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator is authorized in its air operator
  certificate to permit parachute descents and the person is a
  parachutist; or

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the air operator

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} is authorized in its air operator certificate to
    carry a person, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service
    Standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/99-158, s. 5
:::

##### [VFR Flight Minimum Flight Visibility --- Uncontrolled Airspace]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997555 .Subheading}

- **[[702.17]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.17
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where an aeroplane is operated in
  day VFR flight within uncontrolled airspace at less than 1,000 feet
  AGL, a person may, for the purposes of subparagraph 602.115(c)(i),
  operate the aeroplane when flight visibility is less than two miles if
  the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in an air operator
    certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a helicopter is operated in day VFR flight
  within uncontrolled airspace at less than 1,000 feet AGL, a person
  may, for the purposes of subparagraph 602.115(d)(i), operate the
  helicopter when flight visibility is less than one mile if the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in an air operator
    certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [Night, VFR OTT and IFR Operations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997563 .Subheading}

- **[[702.18]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.18
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no air
  operator shall operate an aircraft at night, in VFR OTT flight or in
  IFR flight

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} while towing;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} while carrying a helicopter Class B, C or D
    external load;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} while dispersing products; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is a single-engined aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may operate an aircraft at night, in
  VFR OTT flight or in IFR flight in any of the cases referred to in
  subsection (1), if the air operator

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in its air operator
    certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall operate an aircraft at night
  with persons other than flight crew members on board unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command has an instrument rating;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator is authorized in its air operator
    certificate to permit parachute descents and night VFR flight and

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the persons are parachutists,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the flight takes place within 10 nautical miles
      of the aerodrome of departure, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the flight takes place at night; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the air operator is authorized in its air operator
    certificate to carry persons, other than parachutists, and the air
    operator complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/99-158, s. 6
:::

##### [Entering or Leaving a Helicopter in Flight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997582 .Subheading}

**[[702.19]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.19 .sectionLabel}** For the purposes
of paragraph 602.25(2)(b), the pilot-in-command of a helicopter may
permit a person to enter or leave the helicopter in flight

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} where

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the helicopter is operated at a low hover,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the person is able to enter directly from or
    alight directly onto the supporting surface,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the air operator is authorized to do so in its
    air operator certificate, and

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the air operator complies with the Commercial Air
    Service Standards; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} where

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the helicopter is operated to enable hoisting or
    rappelling, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the air operator complies with section 702.21.

##### [Aircraft Operating over Water]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997592 .Subheading}

**[[702.20]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.20 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall, except when conducting a take-off or landing, operate a land
aircraft over water, beyond a point where the land aircraft could reach
shore in the event of an engine failure, unless the air operator

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in its air operator
  certificate; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [Helicopter Class D External Loads]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997596 .Subheading}

- **[[702.21]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.21
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no air
  operator shall operate a helicopter to carry a helicopter Class D
  external load unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the helicopter is a multi-engined helicopter that
    meets the transport category engine-isolation requirements of
    Chapter 529 of the Airworthiness Manual and that is capable of
    hovering with one engine inoperative at the existing weight and
    altitude;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator is authorized to do so in its air
    operator certificate; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the air operator complies with the Commercial Air
    Service Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may operate a helicopter other than a
  helicopter described in paragraph (1)(a) to carry a helicopter Class D
  external load if the air operator

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in its air operator
    certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [Built-up Area and Aerial Work Zone]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997605 .Subheading}

- **[[702.22]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.22
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection
  602.13(1), a person may conduct a take-off, approach or landing in an
  aircraft within a built-up area of a city or town at a place other
  than an airport, heliport or a military aerodrome, if the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} has an authorization from the Minister or is
    authorized to do so in an air operator certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of paragraph 602.15(2)(a), a person
  may operate an aircraft over a built-up area at altitudes and
  distances less than those specified in paragraph 602.14(2)(a), if the
  person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} has an authorization from the Minister or is
    authorized to do so in an air operator certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection 602.16(2), a person
  may operate a helicopter that is carrying a helicopter Class B, C or D
  external load over a built-up area or in an aerial work zone, if the
  person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} has an authorization from the Minister or is
    authorized to do so in an air operator certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 13
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-702.22-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 702.22"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Briefing of Persons Other Than Flight Crew Members]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997618 .Subheading}

**[[702.23]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.23 .sectionLabel}** The
pilot-in-command shall ensure that persons, other than flight crew
members, who are on board the aircraft are given a safety briefing that
meets the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [Operation of Aircraft in Icing Conditions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997620 .Subheading}

**[[702.24]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.24 .sectionLabel}** When icing
conditions are reported to exist or are forecast to be encountered along
the route of flight, no person shall authorize a flight or its
continuation or conduct a take-off or continue a flight in an aircraft,
even if the pilot-in-command determines that the aircraft is adequately
equipped to operate in icing conditions in accordance with paragraph
605.30(a), if, in the opinion of the pilot-in-command, the safety of the
flight might be adversely affected.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-152, s. 4
:::

**\[702.25 to 702.31 reserved\]**

#### [Division IV --- Aircraft Performance Operating Limitations]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997625 .Subheading}

**\[702.32 to 702.41 reserved\]**

#### [Division V --- Aircraft Equipment Requirements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997627 .Subheading}

##### [Night and IMC Flights]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997628 .Subheading}

- **[[702.42]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.42
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aircraft
  at night unless the aircraft is equipped with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at least one landing light; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the aircraft is operated in icing conditions, a
    means of illumination or other means to detect the formation of ice.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate a multi-engined aircraft in
  IMC unless the aircraft is equipped with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} two generators or two alternators, each of which is
    driven by a separate engine or by a rotor drive train; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} two independent sources of energy, at least one of
    which is not a battery, and each of which is able to drive all
    flight instruments requiring a source of energy and is installed so
    that the failure of one instrument or one source of energy will
    affect neither the energy supply to the remaining instruments nor
    the other source of energy.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-152, s. 5
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-702.42-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 702.42"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Additional Equipment for Single-pilot Operations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997638 .Subheading}

**[[702.43]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.43 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an aircraft on a single-pilot operation in IFR flight
unless the aircraft is equipped with

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} an auto-pilot that is capable of operating the
  aircraft controls to maintain flight and manoeuvre the aircraft about
  the lateral and longitudinal axes;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a headset with a boom microphone or equivalent and a
  transmit button on the control column; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a chart holder that is equipped with a light and that
  is placed in an easily readable position.

##### [Shoulder Harnesses]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997643 .Subheading}

**[[702.44]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.44 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an aircraft unless the pilot seat and any seat beside the
pilot seat are equipped with a safety belt that includes a shoulder
harness.

##### [External Load Equipment]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997645 .Subheading}

**[[702.45]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.45 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an aircraft carrying an external load unless the
attachment device is authorized in a supplemental type certificate or in
an airworthiness approval relating to the operational configuration of
the aircraft.

##### [ACAS]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997647 .Subheading}

- **[[702.46]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.46
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), no air
  operator shall operate a turbine-powered aeroplane having an MCTOW
  greater than 15 000 kg (33,069 pounds) in RVSM airspace unless the
  aeroplane is equipped with an operative ACAS that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements of CAN-TSO-C119b or a more
    recent version of it or other requirements that the Minister has
    accepted as providing a level of safety that is at least equivalent
    to the level that that CAN-TSO provides; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is equipped with a Mode S transponder that meets
    the requirements of CAN-TSO-C112 or a more recent version of it.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), no air operator shall
  operate a turbine-powered aeroplane having an MCTOW greater than 15
  000 kg (33,069 pounds) in airspace outside RVSM airspace unless the
  aeroplane is equipped with an operative ACAS that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements of CAN-TSO-C119a or a more
    recent version of it or other requirements that the Minister has
    accepted as providing a level of safety that is at least equivalent
    to the level that that CAN-TSO provides; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is equipped with a Mode S transponder that meets
    the requirements of CAN-TSO-C112 or a more recent version of it.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The air operator may operate the aeroplane without
  its being equipped with an operative ACAS if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where a minimum equipment list has not been
    approved by the Minister and subject to subsection 605.08(1), the
    operation takes place within the three days after the date of
    failure of the ACAS;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} it is necessary for the pilot-in-command to
    deactivate, in the interests of aviation safety, the ACAS or any of
    its modes and the pilot-in-command does so in accordance with the
    aircraft flight manual, aircraft operating manual, flight manual
    supplement or minimum equipment list; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane is engaged in or configured for use
    in fire fighting, aerial spraying services or aerial surveying and
    operates only in low level airspace.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} This section does not apply in respect of aeroplanes
  manufactured on or before the day on which this section comes into
  force until two years after that day.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-133, s. 6
- SOR/2009-280, ss. 37, 39, 41, 42
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-702.46-20070701.html "Link to previous version of section 702.46"){.PITLink}
:::

**\[702.47 to 702.53 reserved\]**

#### [Division VI --- Emergency Equipment]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997663 .Subheading}

**\[702.54 to 702.63 reserved\]**

#### [Division VII --- Personnel Requirements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997665 .Subheading}

##### [Designation of Pilot-in-command and Second-in-command]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997666 .Subheading}

- **[[702.64]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.64
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator must designate, for
  each flight, a pilot-in-command or, if the crew includes two pilots, a
  pilot-in-command and a second-in-command.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator must record the name of the
  pilot-in-command and, if applicable, the name of the second-in-command
  who were designated under subsection (1) and must retain the record
  for at least 180 days after the day on which the flight is completed.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-26, s. 28](#1511727-1516279){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1511727-1516279.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-702.64-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 702.64"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Flight Crew Member Qualifications]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997668 .Subheading}

**[[702.65]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.65 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall permit a person to act and no person shall act as a flight crew
member in an aircraft unless the person

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} holds the licence and ratings required by Part IV or,
  where the air operator is the holder of an air operator certificate
  issued in accordance with Chapter 15 and Annex I --- Schedule of
  Canada of CUSMA, the equivalent foreign licence and ratings;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is operated in IFR flight and
  persons other than flight crew members are on board, has successfully
  completed a pilot proficiency check, the validity period of which has
  not expired, for that type of aircraft, in accordance with the
  Commercial Air Service Standards;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the person is not the chief pilot, has
  successfully completed a competency check or a pilot proficiency
  check, the validity period of which has not expired, for that type of
  aircraft in accordance with the Commercial Air Service Standards; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} has fulfilled the requirements of the air operator's
  ground and flight training program.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/99-158, s. 7
- [SOR/2020-150, s. 4](#1252330-1253965){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1252330-1253965.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-702.65-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 702.65"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Check Authority]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997676 .Subheading}

- **[[702.66]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.66
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A pilot proficiency check shall be
  conducted by the Minister.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Any other check required under this Subpart may be
  conducted by the Minister.

##### [Validity Period]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997680 .Subheading}

- **[[702.67]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.67
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (3) and (5),
  the validity period of a pilot proficiency check expires on the first
  day of the twenty-fifth month following the month in which the
  proficiency check was completed.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (4) and (5), the validity
  period of a competency check and the annual training referred to in
  section 702.76 expires on the first day of the thirteenth month
  following the month in which the competency check or training was
  completed.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where a pilot proficiency check is renewed within the
  last 90 days of its validity period, its validity period is extended
  by 24 months.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where a competency check or annual training is
  renewed within the last 90 days of its validity period, its validity
  period is extended by 12 months.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may extend the validity period of a
  pilot proficiency check, a competency check or annual training by up
  to 60 days where the Minister is of the opinion that aviation safety
  is not likely to be affected.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} Where the validity period of a pilot proficiency
  check, a competency check or annual training has been expired for 24
  months or more, the person shall requalify by meeting the training
  requirements specified in the Commercial Air Service Standards.

**\[702.68 to 702.75 reserved\]**

#### [Division VIII --- Training]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997689 .Subheading}

##### [Training Program]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997690 .Subheading}

- **[[702.76]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.76
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every air operator shall establish
  and maintain a ground and flight training program that is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} designed to ensure that each person who receives
    training acquires the competence to perform the person's assigned
    duties; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} approved by the Minister in accordance with the
    Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator's ground and flight training program
  shall include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} company indoctrination training;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} upgrading training;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} training in the aerial work to be conducted; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} initial and annual training, including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} aircraft type training,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} aircraft servicing and ground handling training,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} emergency procedures training,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} aircraft surface contamination training for
      pilots and other operations personnel,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} training for personnel who are assigned to
      perform duties on board an aircraft or who are carried externally
      by an aircraft, and

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} any other training required to ensure a safe
      operation under this Subpart.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} include a detailed syllabus of its ground and
    flight training program in its company operations manual;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} ensure that adequate facilities and qualified
    personnel are provided for its ground and flight training program,
    in accordance with the Commercial Air Service Standards; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} establish and maintain a safety awareness program
    concerning the adverse effects of aircraft surface contamination and
    provide the program to all flight operations personnel who are not
    required to receive the training described in subparagraph
    (2)(d)(iv).

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-26, s. 29(F)](#1511729-1516281){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1511729-1516281.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-702.76-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 702.76"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Training and Qualification Records]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997710 .Subheading}

- **[[702.77]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.77
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every air operator shall, for each
  person who is required to receive training under this Subpart,
  establish and maintain a record of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person's name and, where applicable, personnel
    licence number, type and ratings;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, the person's medical category and
    the expiry date of that category;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the dates on which the person, while in the air
    operator's employ, successfully completed any training, pilot
    proficiency check, competency check or examination required under
    this Subpart or obtained any qualification required under this
    Subpart;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} information relating to any failure of the person,
    while in the air operator's employ, to successfully complete any
    training, pilot proficiency check, competency check or examination
    required under this Subpart or to obtain any qualification required
    under this Subpart; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the type of aircraft or flight training equipment
    used for any training, pilot proficiency check, competency check or
    qualification required under this Subpart.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall retain the records referred to
  in paragraphs (1)(c) and (d) and a record of each pilot proficiency
  check for at least three years.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall retain a copy of the most
  recent written examination completed by each pilot for each type of
  aircraft for which the pilot has a qualification.

##### [Amendments to Training Program]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1339522 .Subheading}

- **[[702.78]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.78
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister determines that an
  air operator's training program required under section 702.76 does not
  include the competencies required for each person who receives
  training to perform their assigned duties, the Minister shall notify
  the air operator of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the corrective actions that the air operator is
    required to implement to its training program; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the date by which the air operator is required to
    submit its amended training program to the Minister for approval
    under paragraph 702.76(1)(b).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The air operator referred to in subsection (1) shall
  submit its amended training program to the Minister on or before the
  date specified by the Minister under paragraph (1)(b).

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2022-17, s. 3](#1339257-1339529){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1339257-1339529.html"}
:::

**\[702.79 and 702.80 reserved\]**

#### [Division IX --- Manuals]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997721 .Subheading}

##### [Requirements relating to Company Operations Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997722 .Subheading}

- **[[702.81]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.81
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every air operator shall establish
  and maintain a company operations manual that meets the requirements
  of section 702.82.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall submit its company operations
  manual, and any amendments to that manual, to the Minister.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where there is a change in any aspect of an air
  operator's operation or where the company operations manual no longer
  meets the Commercial Air Service Standards, the air operator shall
  amend its company operations manual.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall, where the Commercial Air Service
  Standards are met, approve those parts of a company operations manual,
  and any amendments to those parts, that relate to the information
  required by section 702.82.

##### [Contents of Company Operations Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997728 .Subheading}

- **[[702.82]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.82
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A company operations manual, which
  may be issued in separate parts corresponding to specific aspects of
  an operation, shall include the instructions and information necessary
  to enable the personnel concerned to perform their duties safely and
  shall contain the information required by the Commercial Air Service
  Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A company operations manual shall be such that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} all parts of the manual are consistent and
    compatible in form and content;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the manual can be readily amended;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the manual contains an amendment control page and a
    list of the pages that are in effect; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the manual has the date of the last amendment to
    each page specified on that page.

##### [Distribution of Company Operations Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997736 .Subheading}

- **[[702.83]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.83
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), an air
  operator shall provide a copy of the appropriate parts of its company
  operations manual, including any amendments to those parts, to each of
  its crew members and to its ground operations and maintenance
  personnel.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If an air operator has established procedures in its
  company operations manual for amending the manual, the air operator
  may, instead of providing a copy of the appropriate parts of that
  manual to each crew member, place a copy of those parts

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in each aircraft that it operates; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in an appropriate place other than an aircraft that
    it operates for the purpose of conducting a parachute descent within
    25 nautical miles of the aerodrome of departure.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Every person who has been provided with a copy of the
  appropriate parts of a company operations manual pursuant to
  subsection (1) shall keep it up to date with the amendments provided
  and shall ensure that the appropriate parts are accessible when the
  person is performing assigned duties.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-152, s. 6
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-702.83-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 702.83"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Standard Operating Procedures]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997745 .Subheading}

- **[[702.84]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.84
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every air operator shall, for each
  of its aircraft that is required to be operated by two or more pilots,
  establish and maintain standard operating procedures that enable the
  crew members to operate the aircraft within the limitations specified
  in the aircraft flight manual and that meet the Commercial Air Service
  Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator that has established standard
  operating procedures for an aircraft shall ensure that a copy of the
  standard operating procedures is carried on board the aircraft.

**\[702.85 to 702.90 reserved\]**

#### [Division X --- Flight Time, Flight Duty Period Limitations and Rest Periods]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997750 .Subheading}

##### [Monitoring System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997751 .Subheading}

- **[[702.91]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.91
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall have a system
  that monitors the flight time, flight duty periods and rest periods of
  each of its flight crew members and shall include in its company
  operations manual the details of that system.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a person who is assigned by an air operator to act
  as a flight crew member, or any other person, becomes aware that the
  assignment would result in the maximum flight time referred to in
  section 702.92 or the maximum flight duty period referred to in
  section 702.93 being exceeded, the person shall advise the air
  operator as soon as possible.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-269, s. 14
:::

##### [Maximum Flight Time]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997757 .Subheading}

- **[[702.92]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.92
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), an air
  operator shall not assign flight time to a flight crew member, and a
  flight crew member shall not accept such an assignment, if the
  member's total flight time will, as a result, exceed

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 1,200 hours in any 365 consecutive days;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 300 hours in any 90 consecutive days;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} 120 hours in any 30 consecutive days or, in the
    case of a flight crew member on call, 100 hours in any 30
    consecutive days;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} 60 hours in any 7 consecutive days; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} if the member conducts single-pilot IFR flights,
    eight hours in any 24 consecutive hours.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} However, an air operator may assign flight time to a
  flight crew member, and a member may accept such an assignment, even
  if the member's flight time will, as a result, exceed the flight time
  referred to in subsection (1) if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the extension of flight time is authorized in the
    air operator certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator and the member comply with the
    Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 702.94, a flight crew member who
  reaches a flight time limitation established by this section shall not
  remain on flight duty or be reassigned to flight duty until the member
  has been provided with the rest period required by section 702.93 or
  the time free from duty required by section 702.96.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-269, s. 14
:::

##### [Maximum Flight Duty Period and Rest Periods]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997771 .Subheading}

- **[[702.93]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.93
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (3) and (5),
  an air operator shall not assign a flight duty period to a flight crew
  member, and a flight crew member shall not accept such an assignment,
  if the member's flight duty period will, as a result, exceed 14
  consecutive hours in any 24 consecutive hours.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Following a flight duty period, an air operator shall
  provide a flight crew member with the minimum rest period and any
  additional rest period required by this Subpart.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} When a flight duty period includes a rest period, the
  flight duty period may be extended beyond the maximum flight duty
  period referred to in subsection (1) by one-half the length of the
  rest period referred to in paragraph (b), to a maximum of three hours,
  if the air operator

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} provides the flight crew member with advance notice
    of the extension of the flight duty period;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} provides the member with a rest period of at least
    four consecutive hours in suitable accommodation; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} does not interrupt the member's rest period.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall extend the rest period that
  follows the flight duty period referred to in subsection (3) and that
  is provided before the next flight duty period by an amount of time
  that is at least equal to the length of the extension of the flight
  duty period.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may assign a flight duty period to a
  flight crew member, and a flight crew member may accept such an
  assignment, even if the flight duty period will, as a result, exceed
  the maximum flight duty period referred to in subsection (1) if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the extension of the flight duty period is
    authorized in the air operator certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator and the member comply with the
    Commercial Air Service Standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-269, s. 14
:::

##### [Unforeseen Operational Circumstances]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997785 .Subheading}

**[[702.94]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.94 .sectionLabel}** The total flight
time referred to in subsection 702.92(1) and the maximum flight duty
period referred to in subsection 702.93(1) may be exceeded if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the flight is extended as a result of an unforeseen
  operational circumstance that occurs after the beginning of the flight
  duty period;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command, after consulting with the other
  flight crew members, considers it safe to exceed the total flight time
  and maximum flight duty period; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the air operator and the pilot-in-command comply with
  the Commercial Air Service Standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-269, s. 14
:::

##### [Delayed Reporting Time]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997792 .Subheading}

**[[702.95]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.95 .sectionLabel}** If a flight crew
member is notified of a delay in reporting time before leaving a rest
facility and the delay is in excess of three hours, the member's flight
duty period is considered to have begun three hours after the original
reporting time.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-269, s. 14
:::

##### [Time Free from Duty]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997796 .Subheading}

- **[[702.96]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.96
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall provide each
  flight crew member with the following time free from duty:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at least 24 consecutive hours 13 times within any
    90 consecutive days and 3 times within any 30 consecutive days; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} when the member is a flight crew member on call, at
    least 36 consecutive hours within any 7 consecutive days or at least
    3 consecutive days within any 17 consecutive days.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} However, an air operator may provide a flight crew
  member with time free from duty other than as required by paragraph
  (1)(a) if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the time free from duty is authorized in the air
    operator certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator and the member comply with the
    Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall notify a flight crew member on
  call of the start and duration of the member's time free from duty.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-269, s. 14
:::

##### [Flight Crew Member Positioning]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997807 .Subheading}

**[[702.97]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.97 .sectionLabel}** If a flight crew
member is required by an air operator to travel for the purpose of
positioning after the completion of a flight duty period, the air
operator shall provide the member with an additional rest period that is
at least equal to one-half the time spent travelling that is in excess
of the member's maximum flight duty period.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-269, s. 14
:::

##### [Long-range Flights]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997811 .Subheading}

- **[[702.98]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-702.98
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A flight duty period during which
  there is one flight or a series of flights and that ends more than
  four one-hour time zones from the point of departure, other than a
  series of flights that is conducted entirely within Northern Domestic
  Airspace, shall be limited to three flights, in the case of a series
  of fights, and shall be followed by a rest period that is at least
  equal to the length of the flight duty period.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If a flight referred to in subsection (1) is a
  transoceanic flight, the maximum number of flights that may be
  conducted after the transoceanic flight is one, excluding one
  unscheduled technical stop that occurs during the flight.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-269, s. 14
:::

### [Subpart 3 --- Air Taxi Operations]{.HTitleText2} {#h-997817 .Subheading}

#### [Division I --- General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997818 .Subheading}

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997819 .Subheading}

**[[703.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.01 .sectionLabel}** This Subpart
applies in respect of the operation by a Canadian air operator, in an
air transport service or in aerial work involving sightseeing
operations, of any of the following aircraft:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a single-engined aircraft;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a multi-engined aircraft, other than a
  turbo-jet-powered aeroplane, that has a MCTOW of 8 618 kg (19,000
  pounds) or less and a seating configuration, excluding pilot seats, of
  nine or less;

- [(b.1)]{.lawlabel} a multi-engined helicopter certified for operation
  by one pilot and operated under VFR; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} any aircraft that is authorized by the Minister to be
  operated under this Subpart.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-193, s. 1
:::

##### [Aircraft Operation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997827 .Subheading}

**[[703.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.02 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an aircraft under this Subpart unless the air operator
complies with the conditions and operations specifications in an air
operator certificate issued to that operator by the Minister pursuant to
section 703.07.

**\[703.03 to 703.06 reserved\]**

#### [Division II --- Certification]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997830 .Subheading}

##### [Issuance or Amendment of Air Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997831 .Subheading}

- **[[703.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.07
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 6.71 of the Act,
  the Minister shall, on receipt of an application submitted in the form
  and manner required by the Commercial Air Service Standards, issue or
  amend an air operator certificate where the applicant demonstrates to
  the Minister the ability to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} maintain an adequate organizational structure;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} maintain an operational control system;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} meet training program requirements;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} comply with maintenance requirements;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} meet the Commercial Air Service Standards for the
    operation; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} conduct the operation safely.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), an applicant
  shall have

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a management organization capable of exercising
    operational control;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} managerial personnel who have been approved by the
    Minister in accordance with the Commercial Air Service Standards,
    are employed on a full-time basis and perform the functions related
    to the following positions, namely,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} operations manager,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} chief pilot, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} where the applicant does not hold an approved
      maintenance organization (AMO) certificate, maintenance manager;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} operational support services and equipment that
    meet the Commercial Air Service Standards;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} aircraft that are properly equipped for and flight
    crew members who are qualified for the area of operation and the
    type of operation;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} an operational control system that meets the
    requirements of section 703.16;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a training program that meets the requirements of
    this Subpart;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} legal custody and control of at least one aircraft
    of each category of aircraft that is to be operated;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} a company operations manual that meets the
    requirements of sections 703.104 and 703.105; and

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a maintenance control system approved pursuant to
    Subpart 6.

##### [Contents of Air Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997853 .Subheading}

**[[703.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.08 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
certificate shall contain

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the legal name, trade name and address of the air
  operator;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number of the air operator certificate;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the effective date of certification;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the date of issue of the certificate;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the general conditions identified in section 703.09;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} specific conditions with respect to

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the areas of operation authorized,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the types of service authorized,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the types of aircraft authorized and, if
    applicable, their registration, and any operational restrictions,
    and

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the main base, scheduled points and, if
    applicable, sub-bases; and

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} where the air operator complies with the Commercial
  Air Service Standards, operations specifications with respect to

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} aircraft performance, equipment and emergency
    equipment requirements,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} instrument approach procedures,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} enroute aerodrome authorizations and limitations,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} special weather minima authorizations,

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} authorizations concerning flight crew member
    complement,

  - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} pilot training and pilot proficiency checks,

  - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} special helicopter procedures,

  - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} the air operator maintenance control system
    approved pursuant to Subpart 6,

  - [(ix)]{.lawlabel} leasing arrangements,

  - [(ix.1)]{.lawlabel} navigation system authorizations, and

  - [(x)]{.lawlabel} any other condition pertaining to the operation
    that the Minister deems necessary for aviation safety.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-152, s. 7
- [SOR/2019-119, s. 38](#1126780-1144251){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126780-1144251.html"}
- [SOR/2021-152, s. 9(F)](#1302014-1308390){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1302014-1308390.html"}
- [SOR/2022-246, s. 24(F)](#1380164-1380795){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1380164-1380795.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-703.08-20210707.html "Link to previous version of section 703.08"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [General Conditions of Air Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997878 .Subheading}

**[[703.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.09 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
certificate shall contain the following general conditions:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall conduct flight operations in
  accordance with its company operations manual;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall maintain an adequate
  organizational structure;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall employ managerial personnel
  who meet the Commercial Air Service Standards;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall conduct training in accordance
  with its training program approved pursuant to this Subpart;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall maintain aircraft that are
  properly equipped for the area of operation and the type of operation;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall employ crew members who are
  qualified for the area of operation and the type of operation;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall maintain its aircraft in
  accordance with the requirements of Subpart 6;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall maintain operational support
  services and equipment that meet the Commercial Air Service Standards;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall notify the Minister within 10
  working days after

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} changing its legal name, its trade name, its main
    base, a sub-base, a scheduled point, or its managerial personnel, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} ceasing to operate a type of aircraft authorized
    under this Subpart; and

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall conduct a safe operation.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-152, s. 8
- [SOR/2022-246, s. 25(F)](#1380166-1380796){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1380166-1380796.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-703.09-20090528.html "Link to previous version of section 703.09"){.PITLink}
:::

**\[703.10 to 703.13 reserved\]**

#### [Division III --- Flight Operations]{.HTitleText3} {#h-997895 .Subheading}

##### [Operating Instructions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997896 .Subheading}

- **[[703.14]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.14
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall ensure that
  all operations personnel are properly instructed about their duties
  and about the relationship of their duties to the operation as a
  whole.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operations personnel of an air operator shall
  follow the procedures specified in the air operator's company
  operations manual in the performance of their duties.

##### [Scheduled Air Service Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997900 .Subheading}

- **[[703.15]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.15
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), every air
  operator that operates a scheduled air service for the purpose of
  transporting persons shall operate the service between airports or
  heliports or between an airport or heliport and a military aerodrome.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may operate a scheduled air service
  for the purpose of transporting persons between an airport and an
  aerodrome other than a military aerodrome or between two aerodromes if
  the air operator is authorized to do so in its air operator
  certificate.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 14
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-703.15-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 703.15"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Operational Control System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997906 .Subheading}

**[[703.16]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.16 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an aircraft unless the air operator has an operational
control system that meets the Commercial Air Service Standards and is
under the control of its operations manager.

##### [Flight Authorization]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997908 .Subheading}

**[[703.17]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.17 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
commence a flight unless the flight has been authorized in accordance
with the procedures specified in the air operator's company operations
manual.

##### [Operational Flight Plan]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997910 .Subheading}

- **[[703.18]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.18
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall permit a
  person to commence a flight unless an operational flight plan that
  meets the Commercial Air Service Standards has been prepared in
  accordance with the procedures specified in the air operator's company
  operations manual.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft shall ensure that
  a copy of the operational flight plan is left at a point of departure,
  in accordance with the procedures specified in the company operations
  manual.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall retain a copy of the
  operational flight plan, including any amendments to that plan, for at
  least 180 days after the day on which the flight is completed.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-26, s. 30](#1511731-1516283){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1511731-1516283.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-703.18-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 703.18"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Maintenance of Aircraft]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997915 .Subheading}

**[[703.19]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.19 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall permit a person to conduct a take-off in an aircraft that has not
been maintained in accordance with the air operator's maintenance
control system.

##### [Fuel Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997917 .Subheading}

**[[703.20]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.20 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall authorize a flight and no person shall commence a flight unless
the aircraft carries sufficient fuel to meet the fuel requirements of
Part VI and to allow the aircraft

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aeroplane operated in IFR flight,

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} to descend at any point along the route to the
    lower of

    - [(A)]{.lawlabel} the single-engined service ceiling, or

    - [(B)]{.lawlabel} 10,000 feet,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} to cruise at the altitude referred to in
    subparagraph (i) to a suitable aerodrome,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} to conduct an approach and a missed approach, and

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} to hold for 30 minutes at an altitude of 1,500
    feet above the elevation of the aerodrome selected in accordance
    with subparagraph (ii); and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a helicopter operated in night VFR
  flight, to fly to the destination aerodrome and then to fly for 30
  minutes at normal cruising speed.

##### [Admission to Pilot's Compartment]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997927 .Subheading}

- **[[703.21]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.21
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where a Department of Transport air
  carrier inspector presents an official identity card to the
  pilot-in-command of an aircraft, the pilot-in-command shall give the
  inspector free and uninterrupted access to the pilot's compartment of
  the aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator and the pilot-in-command shall make
  available for the use of the air carrier inspector the seat most
  suitable to perform the inspector's duties, as determined by the
  inspector.

##### [Transport of Passengers in Single-engined Aircraft]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997931 .Subheading}

- **[[703.22]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.22
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no air
  operator shall operate a single-engined aircraft with passengers on
  board in IFR flight or in night VFR flight.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may operate a single-engined aircraft
  with passengers on board in IFR flight or in night VFR flight if the
  air operator

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in its air operator
    certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [Aircraft Operating over Water]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997937 .Subheading}

**[[703.23]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.23 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall, except when conducting a take-off or landing, operate a land
aircraft over water, beyond a point where the land aircraft could reach
shore in the event of an engine failure, unless the air operator

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in its air operator
  certificate; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [Number of Passengers in Single-engined Aircraft]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997941 .Subheading}

**[[703.24]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.24 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate a single-engined aircraft with more than nine passengers
on board unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is a transport category helicopter;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator is authorized to do so in its air
  operator certificate; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the air operator complies with the Commercial Air
  Service Standards.

##### [Carriage of External Loads]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997946 .Subheading}

**[[703.25]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.25 .sectionLabel}** Except where
carriage of an external load has been authorized in a type certificate
or supplemental type certificate, no air operator shall operate an
aircraft to carry an external load with passengers on board.

##### [Simulation of Emergency Situations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997948 .Subheading}

**[[703.26]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.26 .sectionLabel}** No person shall,
if passengers or cargo are on board an aircraft, simulate emergency
situations that could affect the flight characteristics of the aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-151, s. 16](#1252607-1257185){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1252607-1257185.html"}
:::

Version](section-703.26-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 703.26"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [VFR Flight Obstacle Clearance Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997950 .Subheading}

**[[703.27]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.27 .sectionLabel}** Except when
conducting a take-off or landing, no person shall operate an aircraft in
VFR flight

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} at night, at less than 1,000 feet above the highest
  obstacle located within a horizontal distance of three miles from the
  route to be flown; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is an aeroplane, during the day,
  at less than 300 feet AGL or at a horizontal distance of less than 300
  feet from any obstacle.

##### [VFR Flight Minimum Flight Visibility --- Uncontrolled Airspace]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997954 .Subheading}

- **[[703.28]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.28
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where an aeroplane is operated in
  day VFR flight within uncontrolled airspace at less than 1,000 feet
  AGL, a person may, for the purposes of subparagraph 602.115(c)(i),
  operate the aeroplane when flight visibility is less than two miles if
  the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in an air operator
    certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a helicopter is operated in day VFR flight
  within uncontrolled airspace at less than 1,000 feet AGL, a person
  may, for the purposes of subparagraph 602.115(d)(i), operate the
  helicopter when flight visibility is less than one mile if the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in an air operator
    certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [VFR Flight Weather Conditions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997962 .Subheading}

**[[703.29]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.29 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
commence a VFR flight unless current weather reports and forecasts, if
obtainable, indicate that the weather conditions along the route to be
flown and at the destination aerodrome will be such that the flight can
be conducted in compliance with VFR.

##### [Take-off Minima]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997964 .Subheading}

- **[[703.30]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.30
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no person
  shall conduct a take-off in an aircraft in IMC where weather
  conditions are at or above the take-off minima, but below the landing
  minima, for the runway to be used unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the take-off is authorized in an air operator
    certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person complies with the Commercial Air Service
    Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person may conduct a take-off in an aircraft in IMC
  where weather conditions are at or above the take-off minima, but
  below the landing minima, for the runway to be used, if the weather
  conditions are at or above the landing minima for another suitable
  runway at that aerodrome.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of section 602.126, a person may
  conduct a take-off in an aircraft in IMC where weather conditions are
  below the take-off minima specified in the instrument approach
  procedure, if the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in an air operator
    certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section, the landing minima
  are the decision height or the minimum descent altitude and the
  visibility published for an approach.

##### [No Alternate Aerodrome --- IFR Flight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997974 .Subheading}

**[[703.31]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.31 .sectionLabel}** For the purposes
of section 602.122, a person may conduct an IFR flight where an
alternate aerodrome has not been designated in the IFR flight plan or in
the IFR flight itinerary, if the person

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in an air operator
  certificate; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [Enroute Limitations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997978 .Subheading}

**[[703.32]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.32 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate a multi-engined aircraft with passengers on board in IFR flight
or in night VFR flight if the weight of the aircraft is greater than the
weight that will allow the aircraft to maintain, with any engine
inoperative, the MOCA of the route to be flown.

##### [VFR OTT Flight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997980 .Subheading}

**[[703.33]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.33 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft in VFR OTT flight unless the person

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in an air operator
  certificate; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [Routes in Uncontrolled Airspace]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997984 .Subheading}

**[[703.34]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.34 .sectionLabel}** No person shall,
in uncontrolled airspace, conduct an IFR flight or a night VFR flight on
a route other than an air route unless the air operator establishes the
route in accordance with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

**[[703.35]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.35 .sectionLabel}** \[Reserved\]

##### [Minimum Altitudes and Distances]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997987 .Subheading}

**[[703.36]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.36 .sectionLabel}** For the purposes
of sections 602.13 and 602.15, a person may conduct a take-off, approach
or landing in a helicopter within a built-up area of a city or town, or
operate a helicopter at altitudes and distances less than those
specified in subsection 602.14(2), if the person

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} has an authorization from the Minister or is
  authorized to do so in an air operator certificate; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [Weight and Balance Control]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997991 .Subheading}

- **[[703.37]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.37
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aircraft
  unless, during every phase of the flight, the load restrictions,
  weight and centre of gravity of the aircraft conform to the
  limitations specified in the aircraft flight manual.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall have a weight and balance
  system that meets the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall specify in its company
  operations manual its weight and balance system and instructions to
  employees regarding the preparation and accuracy of weight and balance
  forms.

##### [Passenger and Cabin Safety Procedures]{.HTitleText4} {#h-997996 .Subheading}

- **[[703.38]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.38
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall establish
  procedures to ensure that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} passengers move to and from the aircraft and embark
    and disembark safely, in accordance with procedures that meet the
    requirements of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} section 723.38 of Standard 723 --- Air Taxi ---
      Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service Standards, in the case of
      an aeroplane, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} section 723.38 of Standard 723 --- Air Taxi ---
      Helicopters of the Commercial Air Service Standards, in the case
      of a helicopter;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} all passengers are seated and secured in accordance
    with subsection 605.26(1); and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} seats located at emergency exits are not occupied
    by passengers whose presence in those seats could adversely affect
    the safety of passengers or crew members during an emergency
    evacuation.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall permit an aircraft with
  passengers on board to be fuelled unless the fuelling is carried out
  in accordance with procedures that meet the requirements of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} section 723.38 of Standard 723 --- Air Taxi ---
    Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service Standards, in the case of
    an aeroplane; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} section 723.38 of Standard 723 --- Air Taxi ---
    Helicopters of the Commercial Air Service Standards, in the case of
    a helicopter.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2019-296, s. 8\]]{.Repealed}

##### [Briefing of Passengers]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998006 .Subheading}

- **[[703.39]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.39
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command shall ensure
  that passengers are given a safety briefing in accordance with the
  Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the safety briefing referred to in subsection (1)
  is insufficient for a passenger because of that passenger's physical,
  sensory or comprehension limitations, seat orientation or
  responsibility for another person on board the aircraft, the
  pilot-in-command shall ensure that the passenger is given an
  individual safety briefing that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is appropriate to the passenger's needs; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} meets the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall ensure that each passenger is
  provided, at the passenger's seat or by means of clearly visible
  placards, with the safety information required by the Commercial Air
  Service Standards.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command shall ensure that, in the event
  of an emergency and where time and circumstances permit, all
  passengers are given an emergency briefing in accordance with the
  Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command shall ensure that each passenger
  who is seated next to an emergency exit is made aware of how to
  operate that exit.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-152, s. 9
:::
