[Previous
Version](section-703.39-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 703.39"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Instrument Approach Procedures]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998017 .Subheading}

**[[703.40]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.40 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
terminate an instrument approach with a landing unless, immediately
before landing, the pilot-in-command ascertains, by means of
radiocommunication or visual inspection,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the condition of the runway or surface of intended
  landing; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the wind direction and speed.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-199, s. 17
:::

##### [Approach Bans --- Non-precision Approach, APV and CAT I Precision]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998023 .Subheading}

- **[[703.41]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.41
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsections (2)
  to (4), the visibility with respect to an aeroplane is less than the
  minimum visibility required for a non-precision approach, an APV or a
  CAT I precision approach if, in respect of the advisory visibility
  specified in the Canada Air Pilot and set out in column I of an item
  in the table to this section,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where the RVR is measured by RVR "A" and RVR "B",
    the RVR measured by RVR "A" for the runway of intended approach is
    less than the visibility set out in column II of the item for the
    approach conducted;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the RVR is measured by only one of RVR "A"
    and RVR "B", the RVR for the runway of intended approach is less
    than the visibility set out in column II of the item for the
    approach conducted;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} where no RVR for the runway of intended approach is
    available, the runway visibility is less than the visibility set out
    in column II of the item for the approach conducted; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} where the aerodrome is located south of the 60th
    parallel of north latitude and no RVR or runway visibility for the
    runway of intended approach is available, the ground visibility at
    the aerodrome where the runway is located is less than the
    visibility set out in column II of the item for the approach
    conducted.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall continue a non-precision approach or
  an APV unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator is authorized to do so in its air
    operator certificate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane has a minimum flight crew composed of
    a pilot-in-command and a second-in-command;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the flight crew does not use
    pilot-monitored-approach procedures, the aeroplane is equipped with
    an autopilot capable of conducting a non-precision approach or an
    APV to 400 feet AGL or lower;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the instrument approach procedure is conducted to
    straight-in minima; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a visibility report indicates that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the visibility is equal to or greater than that
      set out in subsection (1),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the RVR is varying between distances less than
      and greater than the minimum RVR set out in subsection (1), or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the visibility is less than the minimum
      visibility set out in subsection (1) and, at the time the
      visibility report is received, the aeroplane has passed the FAF
      inbound or, where there is no FAF, the point where the final
      approach course is intercepted.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No person shall continue an SCDA non-precision
  approach unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator is authorized to do so in its air
    operator certificate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane has a minimum flight crew composed of
    a pilot-in-command and a second-in-command;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the flight crew does not use
    pilot-monitored-approach procedures, the aeroplane is equipped with
    an autopilot capable of conducting a non-precision approach to 400
    feet AGL or lower;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the instrument approach procedure is conducted to
    straight-in minima with a final approach course that meets the
    requirements of section 723.41 of Standard 723 --- Air Taxi ---
    Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service Standards;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the final approach segment is conducted using a
    stabilized descent with a planned constant descent angle specified
    in section 723.41 of Standard 723 --- Air Taxi --- Aeroplanes of the
    Commercial Air Service Standards; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a visibility report indicates that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the visibility is equal to or greater than that
      set out in subsection (1),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the RVR is varying between distances less than
      and greater than the minimum RVR set out in subsection (1), or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the visibility is less than the minimum
      visibility set out in subsection (1) and, at the time the
      visibility report is received, the aeroplane has passed the FAF
      inbound or, where there is no FAF, the point where the final
      approach course is intercepted.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} No person shall continue a CAT I precision approach
  to a runway with centreline lighting unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator is authorized to do so in its air
    operator certificate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane has a minimum flight crew composed of
    a pilot-in-command and a second-in-command;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane is equipped with

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a flight director and autopilot capable of
      conducting a coupled precision approach to 200 feet AGL or lower,
      or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if the flight crew uses pilot-monitored-approach
      procedures, a flight director capable of conducting a precision
      approach to 200 feet AGL or lower;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the runway is equipped with serviceable
    high-intensity approach lighting, high-intensity runway centreline
    lighting and high-intensity runway edge lighting; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a visibility report indicates that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the visibility is equal to or greater than that
      set out in subsection (1),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the RVR is varying between distances less than
      and greater than the minimum RVR set out in subsection (1), or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the visibility is less than the minimum
      visibility set out in subsection (1) and, at the time the
      visibility report is received, the aeroplane has passed the FAF
      inbound or, where there is no FAF, the point where the final
      approach course is intercepted.

##### [Operation of Aircraft in Icing Conditions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998069 .Subheading}

**[[703.42]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.42 .sectionLabel}** When icing
conditions are reported to exist or are forecast to be encountered along
the route of flight, no person shall authorize a flight or its
continuation or conduct a take-off or continue a flight in an aircraft,
even if the pilot-in-command determines that the aircraft is adequately
equipped to operate in icing conditions in accordance with paragraph
605.30(a), if, in the opinion of the pilot-in-command, the safety of the
flight might be adversely affected.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-152, s. 10
:::

**\[703.43 to 703.51 reserved\]**

#### [Division IV --- Aircraft Performance Operating Limitations]{.HTitleText3} {#h-998074 .Subheading}

**\[703.52 to 703.63 reserved\]**

#### [Division V --- Aircraft Equipment Requirements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-998076 .Subheading}

##### [Night and IMC Flight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998077 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2009-152, s. 11

\]
:::

- **[[703.64]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.64
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate a
  multi-engined aircraft with passengers on board in IMC unless the
  aircraft is equipped with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a power failure warning device or vacuum indicator
    to show the power available for gyroscopic instruments from each
    power source;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an alternate source of static pressure for the
    altimeter and the airspeed and vertical speed indicators;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} two generators, each of which is driven by a
    separate engine or by a rotor drive train; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} two independent sources of energy, at least one of
    which is an engine-driven pump or generator, and each of which is
    able to drive all gyroscopic instruments and is installed so that
    the failure of one instrument or one source of energy will affect
    neither the energy supply to the remaining instruments nor the other
    source of energy.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aircraft at night unless
  the aircraft is equipped with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at least one landing light; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the aircraft is operated in icing conditions, a
    means of illumination or other means to detect the formation of ice.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-152, s. 12
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-703.64-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 703.64"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Airborne Thunderstorm Detection and Weather Radar Equipment]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998091 .Subheading}

**[[703.65]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.65 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft with passengers on board in IMC when current weather
reports or forecasts indicate that thunderstorms may reasonably be
expected along the route to be flown, unless the aircraft is equipped
with thunderstorm detection equipment or weather radar equipment.

##### [Additional Equipment for Single-pilot Operations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998093 .Subheading}

**[[703.66]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.66 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft on a single-pilot operation in IMC unless the
aircraft is equipped with

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} an auto-pilot that is capable of operating the
  aircraft controls to maintain flight and manoeuvre the aircraft about
  the lateral and longitudinal axes;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a headset with a boom microphone or equivalent and a
  transmit button on the control column; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a chart holder that is placed in an easily readable
  position and a means of illumination for the chart holder.

##### [Protective Breathing Equipment]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998098 .Subheading}

- **[[703.67]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.67
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall operate a
  pressurized aircraft unless protective breathing equipment with a
  15-minute supply of breathing gas at a pressure-altitude of 8,000 feet
  is readily available at each flight crew member position.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The protective breathing equipment referred to in
  subsection (1) may be used to meet the crew member oxygen requirements
  specified in section 605.31.

##### [First Aid Oxygen]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998102 .Subheading}

**[[703.68]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.68 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an aircraft with passengers on board above FL 250 unless
the aircraft is equipped with oxygen dispensing units and an undiluted
supply of first aid oxygen sufficient to provide at least one passenger
with oxygen for at least one hour or the entire duration of the flight
at a cabin pressure-altitude above 8,000 feet, after an emergency
descent following cabin depressurization, whichever period is longer.

##### [Shoulder Harnesses]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998104 .Subheading}

**[[703.69]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.69 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft unless the pilot seat and any seat beside the pilot
seat are equipped with a safety belt that includes a shoulder harness.

##### [ACAS]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998106 .Subheading}

- **[[703.70]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.70
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), no air
  operator shall operate an aeroplane having an MCTOW greater than 5
  700 kg (12,566 pounds) in RVSM airspace unless the aeroplane is
  equipped with an operative ACAS that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements of CAN-TSO-C119b or a more
    recent version of it or other requirements that the Minister has
    accepted as providing a level of safety that is at least equivalent
    to the level that that CAN-TSO provides; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is equipped with a Mode S transponder that meets
    the requirements of CAN-TSO-C112 or a more recent version of it.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), no air operator shall
  operate an aeroplane having an MCTOW greater than 5 700 kg (12,566
  pounds) in airspace outside RVSM airspace unless the aeroplane is
  equipped with an operative ACAS that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements of CAN-TSO-C118 or a more
    recent version of it or other requirements that the Minister has
    accepted as providing a level of safety that is at least equivalent
    to the level that that CAN-TSO provides; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements of CAN-TSO-C119a or a more
    recent version of it or other requirements that the Minister has
    accepted as providing a level of safety that is at least equivalent
    to the level that that CAN-TSO provides and is equipped with a Mode
    S transponder that meets the requirements of CAN-TSO-C112 or a more
    recent version of it.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The air operator may operate the aeroplane without
  its being equipped with an operative ACAS if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where a minimum equipment list has not been
    approved by the Minister and subject to subsection 605.08(1), the
    operation takes place within the three days after the date of
    failure of the ACAS; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} it is necessary for the pilot-in-command to
    deactivate, in the interests of aviation safety, the ACAS or any of
    its modes and the pilot-in-command does so in accordance with the
    aircraft flight manual, aircraft operating manual, flight manual
    supplement or minimum equipment list.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} This section does not apply in respect of aeroplanes
  manufactured on or before the day on which this section comes into
  force until two years after that day.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-133, s. 7
- SOR/2009-280, ss. 37, 39 to 42
:::

##### [TAWS]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998120 .Subheading}

- **[[703.71]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.71
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no air
  operator shall operate an aeroplane that has a seating configuration,
  excluding pilot seats, of six or more, unless the aeroplane is
  equipped with an operative TAWS that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements for Class A or Class B
    equipment set out in CAN-TSO-C151a or a more recent version of it;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} meets the altitude accuracy requirements set out in
    section 551.102 of Chapter 551 of the Airworthiness Manual; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} has a terrain and airport database compatible with
    the area of operation.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The air operator may operate the aeroplane without
  its being equipped with an operative TAWS if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane is operated in day VFR only;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the event that a minimum equipment list has not
    been approved by the Minister and subject to subsection 605.08(1),
    the operation takes place within the three days after the day on
    which the failure of the TAWS occurs; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} it is necessary for the pilot-in-command to
    deactivate, in the interests of aviation safety, the TAWS or any of
    its modes and the pilot-in-command does so in accordance with the
    aircraft flight manual, aircraft operating manual, flight manual
    supplement or minimum equipment list.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} This section does not apply in respect of aeroplanes
  manufactured on or before the day on which this section comes into
  force until the day that is two years after that day.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2012-136, s. 11
- [SOR/2020-253, s. 11](#1274666-1276867){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1274666-1276867.html"}
:::

#### [Division VI --- Emergency Equipment]{.HTitleText3} {#h-998134 .Subheading}

##### [Inspection Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998135 .Subheading}

**[[703.82]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.82 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an aircraft unless the emergency equipment carried on
board under Division II of Subpart 2 of Part VI and this Division is
inspected at the intervals recommended by the equipment manufacturer.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-253, s. 12](#1274668-1276870){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1274668-1276870.html"}
:::

##### [Flotation Devices]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1297756 .Subheading}

- **[[703.83]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.83
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), the air
  operator of a seaplane shall have, in its company operations manual,
  procedures to ensure that each crew member and passenger wears an
  inflatable life preserver, an inflatable individual flotation device
  or an inflatable personal flotation device when the seaplane is
  operated on or above water.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), the pilot-in-command of a
  seaplane shall give an instruction to each crew member and passenger
  to wear an inflatable life preserver, an inflatable individual
  flotation device or an inflatable personal flotation device when the
  seaplane is operated on or above water.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section, a person is wearing
  an inflatable life preserver, an inflatable individual flotation
  device or an inflatable personal flotation device if it

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is in a pouch that is attached to the person's
    waist;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} has been placed over the person's head and is
    secured at his or her waist; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} is attached to the person in accordance with the
    manufacturer's instructions.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} This section does not apply in respect of a person
  who is carried on a stretcher or in an incubator or other similar
  device.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-49, s. 4](#1113029-1297766){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1113029-1297766.html"}
:::

**\[703.84 and 703.85 reserved\]**

##### [First Aid Kits]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1276872 .Subheading}

**[[703.85.1]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.85.1 .sectionLabel}** No person
shall conduct a take-off in an aircraft operated by an air operator
unless the first aid kit carried on board in accordance with paragraph
602.60(1)(h) contains the supplies and equipment set out in the
[Aviation Occupational Health and Safety
Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-2011-87).

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-253, s. 13](#1274670-1276878){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1274670-1276878.html"}
:::

##### [Survival Equipment]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1276879 .Subheading}

- **[[703.85.2]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.85.2
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall operate an
  aircraft, other than an aircraft referred to in subsection 602.61(2),
  unless a survival manual is carried on board that contains information
  about how to use the survival equipment that is carried on board to
  meet the requirements of subsection 602.61(1).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall operate an aircraft on board of
  which life rafts are required to be carried in accordance with section
  602.63 unless the survival kit referred to in paragraph 602.63(6)(c)
  contains

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a life raft repair kit;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a bailing bucket and a sponge;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a whistle;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a waterproof flashlight;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a supply of potable water --- based on 500 mL per
    person and calculated using the rated capacity of the life raft ---
    or a means of desalting or distilling salt water that can provide
    500 mL of potable water per person;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a waterproof survival manual that contains
    information about how to use the survival equipment;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a first aid kit that contains antiseptic swabs,
    burn dressing compresses, bandages and motion sickness pills; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} a pyrotechnic signalling device, or an aviation
    visual distress signal that has a marking applied by the
    manufacturer indicating that the signal meets the requirements of
    CAN-TSO-C168, a signalling mirror and a dye marker for visually
    signalling distress.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (2), if there is insufficient
  space in the attached survival kit, a supplemental survival kit shall
  be stowed adjacent to each required life raft and contain

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a supply of potable water --- based on 500 mL per
    person and calculated using the rated capacity of the life raft ---
    or a means of desalting or distilling salt water that can provide
    500 mL of potable water per person; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} motion sickness pills.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-253, s. 13](#1274670-1276895){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1274670-1276895.html"}
:::

#### [Division VII --- Personnel Requirements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-998138 .Subheading}

##### [Minimum Crew]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998139 .Subheading}

**[[703.86]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.86 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an aircraft with passengers on board in IFR flight with
fewer than two pilots unless the air operator

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in its air operator
  certificate; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [Designation of Pilot-in-command and Second-in-command]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998143 .Subheading}

- **[[703.87]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.87
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator must designate, for
  each flight, a pilot-in-command or, if the crew includes two pilots, a
  pilot-in-command and a second-in-command.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator must record the name of the
  pilot-in-command and, if applicable, the name of the second-in-command
  who were designated under subsection (1) and must retain the record
  for at least 180 days after the day on which the flight is completed.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-119, s. 39](#1126782-1144257){.wb-lbx

- [SOR/2025-26, s. 32](#1511738-1516292){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1511738-1516292.html"}
:::

##### [Flight Crew Member Qualifications]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998145 .Subheading}

- **[[703.88]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.88
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (6) and (7),
  no air operator shall permit a person to act and no person shall act
  as a flight crew member in an aircraft unless the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} holds the licence and ratings required by Part IV;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} within the previous 90 days, has completed at least
    three take-offs and three landings

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} where a type rating for that aircraft is
      required, in an aircraft of that type, or in a flight simulator
      representing that type of aircraft that has been approved by the
      Minister under Subpart 6 of Part VI for take-off and landing
      qualifications, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where a type rating for that aircraft is not
      required, in an aircraft of that category and class, or in a
      flight simulator representing that category and class of aircraft
      that has been approved by the Minister under Subpart 6 of Part VI
      for take-off and landing qualifications;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} has successfully completed a pilot proficiency
    check or competency check for that type of aircraft, the validity
    period of which has not expired, in accordance with the Commercial
    Air Service Standards as follows:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in the case of the pilot-in-command of a
      multi-engined aircraft or of a single-engined aeroplane that is
      operated in accordance with subsection 703.22(2), a pilot
      proficiency check for that type of aircraft,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of the pilot-in-command of a
      single-engined helicopter, a pilot proficiency check on one of the
      types of single-engined helicopters operated by the air operator,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of the second-in-command of a
      multi-engined aircraft, a pilot proficiency check or a competency
      check for that type of aircraft, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} in the case of the pilot-in-command of a
      single-engined aeroplane that is not operated in accordance with
      subsection 703.22(2), a competency check for that type of
      aircraft; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} has fulfilled the requirements of the air
    operator's ground and flight training program.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may group similar aeroplanes as a
  single type for purposes of the pilot proficiency check referred to in
  paragraph (1)(c) if the air operator

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in its air operator
    certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No person shall act as the pilot-in-command of an
  aircraft with a person other than a flight crew member on board in
  night VFR flight unless the person acting as the pilot-in-command
  holds an instrument rating for that class of aircraft.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall permit a person to act and no
  person shall act as the pilot-in-command of an aircraft with
  passengers on board unless the person has acquired, prior to
  designation as pilot-in-command, the following flight time on that
  type and basic model of aircraft and in the pilot-in-command position:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a single-engined aeroplane or a
    helicopter, five hours; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a multi-engined aeroplane, 15 hours.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The flight time required by subsection (4) may be
  reduced by one hour for each take-off and landing completed, up to a
  maximum of 50 per cent.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may permit a person to act and a
  person may act as a flight crew member in an aircraft if the person
  does not meet the requirements set out in paragraphs (1)(b) to (d) if
  the air operator

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in its air operator
    certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} Subparagraph (1)(c)(iv) does not apply in the case of
  a chief pilot who acts as pilot-in-command of a single-engined
  aeroplane that is not operated in accordance with subsection
  703.22(2).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/99-158, s. 8
- SOR/2000-45, s. 1
:::

##### [Qualifications of Operational Control Personnel]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998172 .Subheading}

- **[[703.89]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.89
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall permit a
  person to act and no person shall act in an operational control
  position unless that person has fulfilled the training requirements
  set out in this Subpart and has demonstrated to the air operator the
  knowledge and abilities required by the Commercial Air Service
  Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who has not acted in an operational control
  position within the previous three months shall, prior to acting in an
  operational control position, satisfy the air operator that the person
  still has the knowledge and abilities referred to in subsection (1).

##### [Check Authority]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998176 .Subheading}

- **[[703.90]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.90
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A pilot proficiency check shall be
  conducted by the Minister.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Any other check required under this Subpart may be
  conducted by the Minister.

##### [Validity Period]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998180 .Subheading}

- **[[703.91]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.91
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) and (3),
  the validity period of a pilot proficiency check, a competency check
  and the annual training referred to in section 703.98 expires on the
  first day of the thirteenth month following the month in which the
  pilot proficiency check, competency check or training was completed.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a pilot proficiency check, a competency check
  or annual training is renewed within the last 90 days of its validity
  period, its validity period is extended by 12 months.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may extend the validity period of a
  pilot proficiency check, a competency check or annual training by up
  to 60 days where the Minister is of the opinion that aviation safety
  is not likely to be affected.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where the validity period of a pilot proficiency
  check, a competency check or annual training has been expired for 24
  months or more, the person shall requalify by meeting the training
  requirements specified in the Commercial Air Service Standards.

**\[703.92 to 703.97 reserved\]**

#### [Division VIII --- Training]{.HTitleText3} {#h-998187 .Subheading}

##### [Training Program]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998188 .Subheading}

- **[[703.98]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.98
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every air operator shall establish
  and maintain a ground and flight training program that is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} designed to ensure that each person who receives
    training acquires the competence to perform the person's assigned
    duties; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} approved by the Minister in accordance with the
    Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator's ground and flight training program
  shall include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} company indoctrination training;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} upgrading training;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} initial and annual training, including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} aircraft type training,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} aircraft servicing and ground handling training,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} emergency procedures training,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} training for operational control personnel, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} aircraft surface contamination training for
      pilots and other operations personnel;

  - [(c.1)]{.lawlabel} initial training followed by training every three
    years on underwater egress for seaplane pilots; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} any other training required to ensure a safe
    operation under this Subpart.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} include a detailed syllabus of its ground and
    flight training program in its company operations manual;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} ensure that qualified personnel are provided for
    its ground and flight training program, in accordance with the
    Commercial Air Service Standards; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} establish and maintain a safety awareness program
    concerning the adverse effects of aircraft surface contamination and
    provide the program to all flight operations personnel who are not
    required to receive the training described in subparagraph
    (2)(c)(v).

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall have a fatigue management
  training program for its flight crew members that contains

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} personal fatigue management strategies relating to

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} sleep hygiene,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} lifestyle, exercise and diet, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the consumption of alcohol and drugs;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the impact of fatigue on aviation safety;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} sleep requirements and the science relating to
    fatigue;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the causes and consequences of fatigue;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} how to recognize fatigue in themselves and in
    others;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} sleep disorders, their impact on aviation safety
    and treatment options; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} human and organizational factors that may cause
    fatigue, including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} sleep quality and duration,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the impact of shift work and overtime,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the circadian rhythm, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the effects of changes of time zones.

##### [Training and Qualification Records]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998224 .Subheading}

- **[[703.99]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.99
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every air operator shall, for each
  person who is required to receive training under this Subpart,
  establish and maintain a record of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person's name and, where applicable, personnel
    licence number, type and ratings;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, the person's medical category and
    the expiry date of that category;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the dates on which the person, while in the air
    operator's employ, successfully completed any training, pilot
    proficiency check, competency check or examination required under
    this Subpart or obtained any qualification required under this
    Subpart;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} information relating to any failure of the person,
    while in the air operator's employ, to successfully complete any
    training, pilot proficiency check, competency check or examination
    required under this Subpart or to obtain any qualification required
    under this Subpart; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the type of aircraft or flight training equipment
    used for any training, pilot proficiency check, competency check or
    qualification required under this Subpart.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall retain the records referred to
  in paragraphs (1)(c) and (d) and a record of each pilot proficiency
  check for at least three years.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall retain a copy of the most
  recent written examination completed by each pilot for each type of
  aircraft for which the pilot has a qualification.

##### [Amendments to Training Program]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1339531 .Subheading}

- **[[703.100]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.100
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister determines that an
  air operator's training program required under section 703.98 does not
  include the competencies required for each person who receives
  training to perform their assigned duties, the Minister shall notify
  the air operator of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the corrective actions that the air operator is
    required to implement to its training program; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the date by which the air operator is required to
    submit its amended training program to the Minister for approval
    under paragraph 703.98(1)(b).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The air operator referred to in subsection (1) shall
  submit its amended training program to the Minister on or before the
  date specified by the Minister under paragraph (1)(b).

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2022-17, s. 4](#1339259-1339538){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1339259-1339538.html"}
:::

**\[703.101 to 703.103 reserved\]**

#### [Division IX --- Manuals]{.HTitleText3} {#h-998235 .Subheading}

##### [Requirements Relating to Company Operations Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998236 .Subheading}

- **[[703.104]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.104
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every air operator shall establish
  and maintain a company operations manual that meets the requirements
  of section 703.105.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall submit its company operations
  manual, and any amendments to that manual, to the Minister.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where there is a change in any aspect of an air
  operator's operation or where the company operations manual no longer
  meets the Commercial Air Service Standards, the air operator shall
  amend its company operations manual.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall, where the Commercial Air Service
  Standards are met, approve those parts of a company operations manual,
  and any amendments to those parts, that relate to the information
  required by section 703.105.

##### [Contents of Company Operations Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998242 .Subheading}

- **[[703.105]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.105
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A company operations manual, which
  may be issued in separate parts corresponding to specific aspects of
  an operation, shall include the instructions and information necessary
  to enable the personnel concerned to perform their duties safely and
  shall contain the information required by the Commercial Air Service
  Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A company operations manual shall be such that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} all parts of the manual are consistent and
    compatible in form and content;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the manual can be readily amended;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the manual contains an amendment control page and a
    list of the pages that are in effect; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the manual has the date of the last amendment to
    each page specified on that page.

##### [Distribution of Company Operations Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998250 .Subheading}

- **[[703.106]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.106
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), an air
  operator shall provide a copy of the appropriate parts of its company
  operations manual, including any amendments to those parts, to each of
  its crew members and to its ground operations and maintenance
  personnel.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may place a copy of the appropriate
  parts of its company operations manual in each aircraft that it
  operates, instead of providing a copy to each crew member, if the air
  operator has established in its company operations manual procedures
  for amending that manual.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Every person who has been provided with a copy of the
  appropriate parts of a company operations manual pursuant to
  subsection (1) shall keep it up to date with the amendments provided
  and shall ensure that the appropriate parts are accessible when the
  person is performing assigned duties.

##### [Standard Operating Procedures]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998255 .Subheading}

- **[[703.107]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-703.107
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every air operator shall, for each
  of its aircraft that is required to be operated by two or more pilots,
  establish and maintain standard operating procedures that enable the
  crew members to operate the aircraft within the limitations specified
  in the aircraft flight manual and that meet the Commercial Air Service
  Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator that has established standard
  operating procedures for an aircraft shall ensure that a copy of the
  standard operating procedures is carried on board the aircraft.

**\[703.108 and 703.109 reserved\]**

### [Subpart 4 --- Commuter Operations]{.HTitleText2} {#h-998260 .Subheading}

#### [Division I --- General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-998261 .Subheading}

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998262 .Subheading}

**[[704.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.01 .sectionLabel}** This Subpart
applies in respect of the operation by a Canadian air operator, in an
air transport service or in aerial work involving sightseeing
operations, of any of the following aircraft:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a multi-engined aeroplane that has a MCTOW of 8
  618 kg (19,000 pounds) or less and a seating configuration, excluding
  pilot seats, of 10 to 19 inclusive;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a turbo-jet-powered aeroplane that has a maximum zero
  fuel weight of 22 680 kg (50,000 pounds) or less and for which a
  Canadian type certificate has been issued authorizing the transport of
  not more than 19 passengers;

- [(b.1)]{.lawlabel} a multi-engined helicopter with a seating
  configuration, excluding pilot seats, of 10 to 19 inclusive, unless it
  is certified for operation with one pilot and operated under VFR; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} any aircraft that is authorized by the Minister to be
  operated under this Subpart.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-193, s. 2
:::

##### [Aircraft Operation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998270 .Subheading}

**[[704.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.02 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an aircraft under this Subpart unless the air operator
complies with the conditions and operations specifications in an air
operator certificate issued to that operator by the Minister pursuant to
section 704.07.

**\[704.03 to 704.06 reserved\]**

#### [Division II --- Certification]{.HTitleText3} {#h-998273 .Subheading}

##### [Issuance or Amendment of Air Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998274 .Subheading}

- **[[704.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.07
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 6.71 of the Act,
  the Minister shall, on receipt of an application submitted in the form
  and manner required by the Commercial Air Service Standards, issue or
  amend an air operator certificate where the applicant demonstrates to
  the Minister the ability to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} maintain an adequate organizational structure;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} maintain an operational control system;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} meet training program requirements;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} comply with maintenance requirements;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} meet the Commercial Air Service Standards for the
    operation; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} conduct the operation safely.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), an applicant
  shall have

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a management organization capable of exercising
    operational control;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} managerial personnel who have been approved by the
    Minister in accordance with the Commercial Air Service Standards,
    are employed on a full-time basis and perform the functions related
    to the following positions, namely,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} operations manager,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} chief pilot, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} where the applicant does not hold an approved
      maintenance organization (AMO) certificate, maintenance manager;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} operational support services and equipment that
    meet the Commercial Air Service Standards;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} after January 1, 1997, where a master minimum
    equipment list has been established for a type of aircraft, a
    minimum equipment list for each aircraft of that type, approved by
    the Minister in accordance with the procedures specified in the
    MMEL/MEL Policy and Procedures Manual;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} aircraft that are properly equipped for and flight
    crew members who are qualified for the area of operation and the
    type of operation;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} an operational control system that meets the
    requirements of section 704.15;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a training program that meets the requirements of
    this Subpart;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} legal custody and control of at least one aircraft
    of each category of aircraft that is to be operated;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a company operations manual that meets the
    requirements of sections 704.120 and 704.121; and

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} a maintenance control system approved pursuant to
    Subpart 6.

##### [Contents of Air Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998297 .Subheading}

**[[704.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.08 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
certificate shall contain

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the legal name, trade name and address of the air
  operator;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number of the air operator certificate;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the effective date of certification;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the date of issue of the certificate;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the general conditions identified in section 704.09;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} specific conditions with respect to

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the areas of operation authorized,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the types of service authorized,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the types of aircraft authorized and, if
    applicable, their registration, and any operational restrictions,
    and

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the main base, scheduled points and, if
    applicable, sub-bases; and

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} where the air operator complies with the Commercial
  Air Service Standards, operations specifications with respect to

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} aircraft performance, equipment and emergency
    equipment requirements,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} instrument approach procedures,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} enroute aerodrome authorizations and limitations,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} special weather minima authorizations,

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} authorizations concerning flight crew member
    qualifications and flight crew member complement,

  - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} navigation system authorizations,

  - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} pilot training and pilot proficiency checks,

  - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} special helicopter procedures,

  - [(ix)]{.lawlabel} the air operator maintenance control system
    approved pursuant to Subpart 6,

  - [(x)]{.lawlabel} leasing arrangements, and

  - [(xi)]{.lawlabel} any other condition pertaining to the operation
    that the Minister deems necessary for aviation safety.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-152, s. 13
- [SOR/2022-246, s. 26(F)](#1380168-1380797){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1380168-1380797.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-704.08-20090528.html "Link to previous version of section 704.08"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [General Conditions of Air Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998323 .Subheading}

**[[704.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.09 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
certificate shall contain the following general conditions:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall conduct flight operations in
  accordance with its company operations manual;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall maintain an adequate
  organizational structure;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall employ managerial personnel
  who meet the Commercial Air Service Standards;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall conduct training in accordance
  with its training program approved pursuant to this Subpart;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall maintain aircraft that are
  properly equipped for the area of operation and the type of operation;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall employ crew members who are
  qualified for the area of operation and the type of operation;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall maintain its aircraft in
  accordance with the requirements of Subpart 6;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall maintain operational support
  services and equipment that meet the Commercial Air Service Standards;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall notify the Minister within 10
  working days after

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} changing its legal name, its trade name, its main
    base, a sub-base, a scheduled point or its managerial personnel, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} ceasing to operate a type of aircraft authorized
    under this Subpart; and

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall conduct a safe operation.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-152, s. 14
- [SOR/2022-246, s. 27(F)](#1380170-1380798){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1380170-1380798.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-704.09-20090528.html "Link to previous version of section 704.09"){.PITLink}
:::

**\[704.10 and 704.11 reserved\]**

#### [Division III --- Flight Operations]{.HTitleText3} {#h-998340 .Subheading}

##### [Operating Instructions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998341 .Subheading}

- **[[704.12]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.12
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall ensure that
  all operations personnel are properly instructed about their duties
  and about the relationship of their duties to the operation as a
  whole.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operations personnel of an air operator shall
  follow the procedures specified in the air operator's company
  operations manual in the performance of their duties.

##### [General Operational Information]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998345 .Subheading}

**[[704.13]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.13 .sectionLabel}** Every air
operator shall establish a system for the timely dissemination of
general operational information that includes a means for each crew
member to acknowledge receipt of such information.

##### [Scheduled Air Service Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998347 .Subheading}

- **[[704.14]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.14
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), every air
  operator that operates a scheduled air service for the purpose of
  transporting persons shall operate the service between airports or
  heliports or between an airport or heliport and a military aerodrome.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may operate a scheduled air service
  for the purpose of transporting persons between an airport and an
  aerodrome other than a military aerodrome or between two aerodromes if
  the air operator is authorized to do so in its air operator
  certificate.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 15
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-704.14-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 704.14"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Operational Control System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998353 .Subheading}

**[[704.15]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.15 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an aircraft unless the air operator has an operational
control system that meets the Commercial Air Service Standards and is
under the control of its operations manager.

##### [Flight Authorization]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998355 .Subheading}

**[[704.16]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.16 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
commence a flight unless the flight has been authorized in accordance
with the procedures specified in the air operator's company operations
manual.

##### [Operational Flight Plan]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998357 .Subheading}

- **[[704.17]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.17
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall permit a
  person to commence a flight unless an operational flight plan that
  meets the Commercial Air Service Standards has been prepared.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft shall ensure that
  one copy of the operational flight plan is left at a point of
  departure, in accordance with the procedures specified in the company
  operations manual, and that another copy is carried on board the
  aircraft until the aircraft reaches the final destination of the
  flight.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall retain a copy of the
  operational flight plan, including any amendments to that plan, for at
  least 180 days after the day on which the flight is completed.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-26, s. 34](#1511742-1516311){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1511742-1516311.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-704.17-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 704.17"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Maintenance of Aircraft]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998362 .Subheading}

**[[704.18]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.18 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall permit a person to conduct a take-off in an aircraft that has not
been maintained in accordance with the air operator's maintenance
control system.

##### [Checklist]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998364 .Subheading}

- **[[704.19]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.19
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every air operator shall establish
  the checklist referred to in paragraph 602.60(1)(a) for each aircraft
  type that it operates and shall make the appropriate parts of the
  checklist readily available to the crew members.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Every crew member shall follow the checklist referred
  to in subsection (1) in the performance of the crew member's assigned
  duties.

##### [Fuel Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998368 .Subheading}

**[[704.20]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.20 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall authorize a flight and no person shall commence a flight unless
the aircraft carries sufficient fuel to meet the fuel requirements of
Part VI and to allow the aircraft

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aeroplane operated in IFR flight,

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} to descend at any point along the route to the
    lower of

    - [(A)]{.lawlabel} the single-engined service ceiling, or

    - [(B)]{.lawlabel} 10,000 feet,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} to cruise at the altitude referred to in
    subparagraph (i) to a suitable aerodrome,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} to conduct an approach and a missed approach, and

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} to hold for 30 minutes at an altitude of 1,500
    feet above the elevation of the aerodrome selected in accordance
    with subparagraph (ii); and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a helicopter operated in night VFR
  flight, to fly to the destination aerodrome and then to fly for 30
  minutes at normal cruising speed.

##### [Admission to Flight Deck]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998378 .Subheading}

- **[[704.21]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.21
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where a Department of Transport air
  carrier inspector presents an official identity card to the
  pilot-in-command of an aircraft, the pilot-in-command shall give the
  inspector free and uninterrupted access to the flight deck of the
  aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator and the pilot-in-command shall make
  available for the use of the air carrier inspector the seat most
  suitable to perform the inspector's duties, as determined by the
  inspector.

##### [Simulation of Emergency Situations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998382 .Subheading}

**[[704.22]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.22 .sectionLabel}** No person shall,
if passengers or cargo are on board an aircraft, simulate emergency
situations that could affect the flight characteristics of the aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-151, s. 17](#1252609-1257188){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1252609-1257188.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-704.22-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 704.22"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [VFR Flight Obstacle Clearance Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998384 .Subheading}

**[[704.23]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.23 .sectionLabel}** Except when
conducting a take-off or landing, no person shall operate an aircraft in
VFR flight

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} at night, at less than 1,000 feet above the highest
  obstacle located within a horizontal distance of three miles from the
  route to be flown; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft is an aeroplane, during the day,
  at less than 500 feet AGL or at a horizontal distance of less than 500
  feet from any obstacle.

##### [VFR Flight Minimum Flight Visibility --- Uncontrolled Airspace]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998388 .Subheading}

**[[704.24]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.24 .sectionLabel}** Where a
helicopter is operated in day VFR flight within uncontrolled airspace at
less than 1,000 feet AGL, a person may, for the purposes of subparagraph
602.115(d)(i), operate the helicopter when flight visibility is less
than one mile if the person

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in an air operator
  certificate; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [VFR Flight Weather Conditions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998392 .Subheading}

**[[704.25]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.25 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
commence a VFR flight unless current weather reports and forecasts, if
obtainable, indicate that the weather conditions along the route to be
flown and at the destination aerodrome will be such that the flight can
be conducted in compliance with VFR.

##### [Take-off Minima]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998394 .Subheading}

- **[[704.26]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.26
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no person
  shall conduct a take-off in an aircraft in IMC where weather
  conditions are at or above the take-off minima, but below the landing
  minima, for the runway to be used unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the take-off is authorized in an air operator
    certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person complies with the Commercial Air Service
    Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person may conduct a take-off in an aircraft in IMC
  where weather conditions are at or above the take-off minima, but
  below the landing minima, for the runway to be used, if the weather
  conditions are at or above the landing minima for another suitable
  runway at that aerodrome, taking into account the aircraft performance
  operating limitations specified in Division IV.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of section 602.126, a person may
  conduct a take-off in an aircraft in IMC where weather conditions are
  below the take-off minima specified in the instrument approach
  procedure, if the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in an air operator
    certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section, the landing minima
  are the decision height or the minimum descent altitude and the
  visibility published for an approach.

##### [No Alternate Aerodrome --- IFR Flight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998404 .Subheading}

**[[704.27]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.27 .sectionLabel}** For the purposes
of section 602.122, a person may conduct an IFR flight where an
alternate aerodrome has not been designated in the IFR flight plan or in
the IFR flight itinerary, if the person

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in an air operator
  certificate; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [VFR OTT Flight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998408 .Subheading}

**[[704.28]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.28 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft in VFR OTT flight unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2007-78, s. 1\]]{.Repealed}

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person is authorized to do so in an air operator
  certificate; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the person complies with the Commercial Air Service
  Standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-78, s. 1
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-704.28-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 704.28"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Routes in Uncontrolled Airspace]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998415 .Subheading}

**[[704.29]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.29 .sectionLabel}** No person shall,
in uncontrolled airspace, conduct an IFR flight or a night VFR flight on
a route other than an air route unless the air operator establishes the
route in accordance with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

**[[704.30]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.30 .sectionLabel}** \[Reserved\]

##### [Minimum Altitudes and Distances]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998418 .Subheading}

**[[704.31]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.31 .sectionLabel}** For the purposes
of sections 602.13 and 602.15, a person may conduct a take-off, approach
or landing in a helicopter within a built-up area of a city or town, or
operate a helicopter at altitudes and distances less than those
specified in subsection 602.14(2), if the person

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} has an authorization from the Minister or is
  authorized to do so in an air operator certificate; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [Weight and Balance Control]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998422 .Subheading}

- **[[704.32]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.32
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aircraft
  unless, during every phase of the flight, the load restrictions,
  weight and centre of gravity of the aircraft conform to the
  limitations specified in the aircraft flight manual.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall have a weight and balance
  system that meets the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall specify in its company
  operations manual its weight and balance system and instructions to
  employees regarding the preparation and accuracy of weight and balance
  forms.

##### [Passenger and Cabin Safety Procedures]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998427 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2019-119, s. 40

\]
:::

- **[[704.33]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.33
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall establish
  procedures to ensure that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} passengers move to and from the aircraft and embark
    and disembark safely, in accordance with procedures that meet the
    requirements of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} section 724.33 of Standard 724 --- Commuter
      Operations --- Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service Standards,
      in the case of an aeroplane, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} section 724.33 of Standard 724 --- Commuter
      Operations --- Helicopters of the Commercial Air Service
      Standards, in the case of a helicopter.

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} all passengers are seated and secured in accordance
    with subsection 605.26(1);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsection (2), the back of each seat is
    in the upright position and all chair tables are stowed during
    movement on the surface, take-off and landing and at such other
    times as the pilot-in-command considers necessary for the safety of
    the persons on board the aircraft;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} seats located at emergency exits are not occupied
    by passengers whose presence in those seats could adversely affect
    the safety of passengers or crew members during an emergency
    evacuation; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the flight crew can exercise supervisory control
    over passengers by visual and aural means.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may, for the transportation of any
  passenger who has been certified by a physician as unable to sit
  upright, allow the back of the seat occupied by such a passenger to
  remain in the reclining position during movement on the surface,
  take-off and landing if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the passenger is seated in a location that will not
    restrict the evacuation of other passengers from the aircraft;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the passenger is not seated in a row that is next
    to or immediately in front of an emergency exit; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the seat immediately behind the passenger's seat is
    vacant.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall assign a person to perform
  duties on board an aircraft unless that person has received the
  training referred to in paragraph 704.115(2)(d).

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall not permit an aircraft with
  passengers on board to be fuelled unless the fuelling is carried out
  in accordance with procedures that meet the requirements set out in

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} subsection 724.33(2) of Standard 724 --- Commuter
    Operations --- Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service Standards,
    in the case of an aeroplane; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} subsection 724.33(2) of Standard 724 --- Commuter
    Operations --- Helicopters of the Commercial Air Service Standards,
    in the case of a helicopter.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2019-296, s. 9\]]{.Repealed}

##### [Briefing of Passengers]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998444 .Subheading}

- **[[704.34]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.34
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command shall ensure
  that passengers are given a safety briefing in accordance with the
  Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the safety briefing referred to in subsection (1)
  is insufficient for a passenger because of that passenger's physical,
  sensory or comprehension limitations, seat orientation or
  responsibility for another person on board the aircraft, the
  pilot-in-command shall ensure that the passenger is given an
  individual safety briefing that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is appropriate to the passenger's needs; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} meets the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command shall ensure that, in the event
  of an emergency and where time and circumstances permit, all
  passengers are given an emergency briefing in accordance with the
  Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command shall ensure that each passenger
  who is seated next to an emergency exit is made aware of how to
  operate that exit.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-152, s. 15
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-704.34-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 704.34"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Safety Features Card]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998454 .Subheading}

**[[704.35]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.35 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
shall provide each passenger, at the passenger's seat, with a safety
features card containing, in pictographic form, the information required
by the Commercial Air Service Standards, and any wording shall be in
English and French.

##### [Instrument Approach Procedures]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998456 .Subheading}

- **[[704.36]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.36
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a CAT II or
  CAT III precision approach unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator is authorized to do so in its air
    operator certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the approach is conducted in accordance with the
    Manual of All Weather Operations (Categories II and III).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall terminate an instrument approach with
  a landing unless, immediately prior to landing, the pilot-in-command
  ascertains, by means of radiocommunication or visual inspection,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the condition of the runway or surface of intended
    landing; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the wind direction and speed.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-199, s. 19
:::

##### [Approach Bans --- Non-precision, APV, and CAT I Precision]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998466 .Subheading}

- **[[704.37]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.37
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsections (2)
  to (4), the visibility with respect to an aeroplane is less than the
  minimum visibility required for a non-precision approach, an APV or a
  CAT I precision approach if, in respect of the advisory visibility
  specified in the Canada Air Pilot and set out in column I of an item
  in the table to this section,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where the RVR is measured by RVR "A" and RVR "B",
    the RVR measured by RVR "A" for the runway of intended approach is
    less than the visibility set out in column II of the item for the
    approach conducted;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the RVR is measured by only one of RVR "A"
    and RVR "B", the RVR for the runway of intended approach is less
    than the visibility set out in column II of the item for the
    approach conducted;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} where no RVR for the runway of intended approach is
    available, the runway visibility is less than the visibility set out
    in column II of the item for the approach conducted; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} where the aerodrome is located south of the 60th
    parallel of north latitude and no RVR or runway visibility for the
    runway of intended approach is available, the ground visibility at
    the aerodrome where the runway is located is less than the
    visibility set out in column II of the item for the approach
    conducted.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall continue a non-precision approach or
  an APV unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator is authorized to do so in its air
    operator certificate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane is equipped with

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} if the flight crew does not use
      pilot-monitored-approach procedures, an autopilot capable of
      conducting a non-precision approach or an APV to 400 feet AGL or
      lower, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a HUD capable of conducting a non-precision
      approach or an APV to 400 feet AGL or lower;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the instrument approach procedure is conducted to
    straight-in minima; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a visibility report indicates that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the visibility is equal to or greater than that
      set out in subsection (1),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the RVR is varying between distances less than
      and greater than the minimum RVR set out in subsection (1), or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the visibility is less than the minimum
      visibility set out in subsection (1) and, at the time the
      visibility report is received, the aeroplane has passed the FAF
      inbound or, where there is no FAF, the point where the final
      approach course is intercepted.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No person shall continue an SCDA non-precision
  approach unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator is authorized to do so in its air
    operator certificate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane is equipped with

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} if the flight crew does not use
      pilot-monitored-approach procedures, an autopilot capable of
      conducting a non-precision approach to 400 feet AGL or lower, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a HUD capable of conducting a non-precision
      approach to 400 feet AGL or lower;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the instrument approach procedure is conducted to
    straight-in minima with a final approach course that meets the
    requirements of section 724.37 of Standard 724 --- Commuter
    Operations --- Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service Standards;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the final approach segment is conducted using a
    stabilized descent with a planned constant descent angle specified
    in section 724.37 of Standard 724 --- Commuter Operations ---
    Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service Standards; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a visibility report indicates that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the visibility is equal to or greater than that
      set out in subsection (1),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the RVR is varying between distances less than
      and greater than the minimum RVR set out in subsection (1), or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the visibility is less than the minimum
      visibility set out in subsection (1) and, at the time the
      visibility report is received, the aeroplane has passed the FAF
      inbound or, where there is no FAF, the point where the final
      approach course is intercepted.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} No person shall continue a CAT I precision approach
  to a runway with centreline lighting or a CAT I precision approach in
  an aeroplane equipped with a HUD unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator is authorized to do so in its air
    operator certificate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aeroplane not equipped with a
    HUD,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} if the flight crew does not use
      pilot-monitored-approach procedures, the pilot-in-command and the
      second-in-command are qualified to conduct a CAT II precision
      approach,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane is equipped with

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} a flight director and autopilot capable of
        conducting a coupled precision approach to 200 feet AGL or
        lower, or

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} if the flight crew uses
        pilot-monitored-approach procedures, a flight director capable
        of conducting a precision approach to 200 feet AGL or lower, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the runway is equipped with serviceable
      high-intensity approach lighting, high-intensity runway centreline
      lighting and high-intensity runway edge lighting;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aeroplane equipped with a HUD
    capable of conducting a precision approach to 200 feet AGL or lower,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command and the second-in-command
      are qualified to conduct a CAT II precision approach,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane is equipped with a flight director
      and autopilot capable of conducting a coupled precision approach
      to 200 feet AGL or lower, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the runway is equipped with serviceable
      high-intensity approach lighting and high-intensity runway edge
      lighting; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a visibility report indicates that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the visibility is equal to or greater than that
      set out in subsection (1),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the RVR is varying between distances less than
      and greater than the minimum RVR set out in subsection (1), or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the visibility is less than the minimum
      visibility set out in subsection (1) and, at the time the
      visibility report is received, the aeroplane has passed the FAF
      inbound or, where there is no FAF, the point where the final
      approach course is intercepted.

#### [Division IV --- Aeroplane Performance Operating Limitations]{.HTitleText3} {#h-998520 .Subheading}

##### [Non-application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1189401 .Subheading}

**[[704.43]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.43 .sectionLabel}** This Division
does not apply to a seaplane when it takes off from or lands on water.

##### [Calculations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998521 .Subheading}

**[[704.44]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.44 .sectionLabel}** Any determination
made for the purposes of sections 704.45 to 704.51 shall be based on the
approved performance information specified in the aircraft flight
manual.

##### [Type Certification Performance Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998525 .Subheading}

- **[[704.45]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.45
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall authorize a
  flight unless the aeroplane has been certified on the basis of the
  type certification performance requirements set out in

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Subchapter B Flight --- General of Chapter 523 ---
    Normal, Utility, Aerobatic and Commuter Category Aeroplanes or
    Subchapter B Flight --- General of Chapter 525 --- Transport
    Category Aeroplanes of the Airworthiness Manual;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} Part 23 --- at amendment 23-34 and later --- or
    Part 25, Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations of the United
    States; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} Special Federal Aviation Regulation 41C, published
    by the Government of the United States, which includes the
    performance requirements set out in Annex 8 to the Convention.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), an air operator may authorize
  the take-off of an aeroplane if the aeroplane has fewer than 10
  passengers on board or is operated in a non-scheduled air service.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-135, s. 4](#1129596-1189420){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1129596-1189420.html"}
:::

:::

##### [Take-off and Landing Weight Limitations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998527 .Subheading}

- **[[704.46]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.46
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 704.51, no air
  operator shall authorize a flight --- and no person shall conduct a
  take-off --- in an aeroplane unless the following conditions are met:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the weight of the aeroplane does not exceed the
    maximum take-off weight specified in the aircraft flight manual for
    the pressure-altitude and the ambient temperature at the departure
    aerodrome; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} after allowing for planned fuel consumption during
    the flight to the destination aerodrome or alternate aerodrome, the
    weight of the aeroplane does not exceed the maximum landing weight
    specified in the aircraft flight manual for the pressure-altitude
    and the ambient temperature at the destination aerodrome or
    alternate aerodrome.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} In the determination of the maximum take-off weight
  referred to in paragraph (1)(a) for a propeller-driven aeroplane
  having an MCTOW of not more than 5 700 kg (12,566 pounds),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the required accelerate-stop distance specified in
    the aircraft flight manual shall not exceed the accelerate-stop
    distance available (ASDA) unless

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the maximum take-off weight is not limited by the
      accelerate-stop distance requirements set out in the aircraft
      flight manual, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane has fewer than 10 passengers on
      board or is operated in a non-scheduled air service; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the all-engines-operating take-off distance
    specified in the aircraft flight manual shall not exceed the
    take-off distance available (TODA).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} In the determination of the maximum take-off weight
  referred to in paragraph (1)(a) for a turbo-jet-powered aeroplane or a
  large aeroplane that is propeller-driven,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the required accelerate-stop distance specified in
    the aircraft flight manual shall not exceed the accelerate-stop
    distance available (ASDA) unless, in the case of a large aeroplane
    that is propeller-driven,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the maximum take-off weight is not limited by the
      required accelerate-stop distance requirements set out in the
      aircraft flight manual, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane has fewer than 10 passengers on
      board;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the required take-off run specified in the aircraft
    flight manual shall not exceed the take-off run available (TORA);
    and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the required take-off distance specified in the
    aircraft flight manual shall not exceed the take-off distance
    available (TODA) unless, in the case of a large aeroplane that is
    propeller-driven,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the maximum take-off weight is not limited by the
      take-off distance requirements set out in the aircraft flight
      manual, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane has fewer than 10 passengers on
      board.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} In the determination of the maximum take-off weights
  referred to in subsections (2) and (3), the following factors shall be
  taken into account:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the pressure-altitude at the aerodrome;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the ambient temperature at the aerodrome;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the runway slope in the direction of take-off; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a wind component that is not more than 50% of the
    reported headwind or not less than 150% of the reported tailwind.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a take-off or landing on a gravel
  runway, the maximum weights referred to in paragraphs (1)(a) and (b)
  shall be determined in accordance with the gravel runway information
  specified in the aircraft flight manual.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} In the absence of the information referred to in
  subsection (5) for a propeller-driven aeroplane, the maximum weights
  referred to in paragraphs (1)(a) and (b) shall be determined on the
  basis of the information specified in the aircraft flight manual for a
  dry, paved hard-surface runway that does not exceed 1 524 m (5,000
  feet) in length, except that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} no credit shall be allowed for reverse thrust;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in determining the maximum take-off weight, no
    credit shall be allowed for any clearway; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the corresponding length of dry, paved hard-surface
    runway used to determine the take-off distance required, the
    accelerate-stop distance required and the landing distance required
    shall be obtained by dividing the length of the gravel runway by a
    factor of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} 1.10, in the case of an aeroplane with an MCTOW
      of not more than 5 700 kg (12,566 pounds), or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} 1.15, in the case of a large aeroplane.

:::
