##### [Net Take-off Flight Path]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998547 .Subheading}

- **[[704.47]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.47
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), no air
  operator shall authorize a flight --- and no person shall conduct a
  take-off --- in a turbo-jet-powered aeroplane, a large aeroplane that
  is propeller-driven or a propeller-driven aeroplane that has a
  passenger seating configuration of 10 or more, if the weight of the
  aeroplane exceeds the weight specified in the aircraft flight manual
  as allowing a net take-off flight path that clears all obstacles by at
  least 10.7 m (35 feet) vertically or at least 60 m (200 feet)
  horizontally within the aerodrome boundaries, and by at least 91.5 m
  (300 feet) horizontally outside those boundaries.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} In the determination of the maximum weight, minimum
  distances and flight path referred to in subsection (1),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} corrections shall be made for

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the runway to be used,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the runway slope in the direction of take-off,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the pressure-altitude at the aerodrome,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the ambient temperature at the aerodrome, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the wind component at the time of take-off, that
      is not more than 50% of the reported headwind or not less than
      150% of the reported tailwind;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} calculations shall be based on the pilot

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} not banking the aeroplane before reaching an
      altitude of 15 m (50 feet),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} subject to paragraph (c), using no more than 15
      degrees of bank at altitudes between 15 m (50 feet) and 122 m (400
      feet), and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} using no more than 25 degrees of bank at
      altitudes above 122 m (400 feet), aeroplane speed and
      configuration permitting; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a bank angle greater than the angle referred to in
    subparagraph (b)(ii) may be used if it is authorized in an air
    operator certificate.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may authorize a flight --- and a
  pilot-in-command may conduct a take-off --- in an aeroplane referred
  to in subsection (1) that does not meet the requirements of that
  subsection if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a large aeroplane that is
    propeller-driven and for which visual obstacle clearance procedures
    are used during take-off and climb,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane has fewer than 10 passengers on
      board,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the air operator has conducted an obstacle
      assessment to identify fixed and transient obstacles along the
      take-off flight path,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the air operator has set out, in the company
      operations manual, a one-engine-inoperative departure plan that
      allows the pilot-in-command to rely on visual guidance to
      manoeuvre the aeroplane in a manner that will allow the net
      take-off flight path to be clear of all obstacles by at least
      10.7 m (35 feet) vertically or at least 60 m (200 feet)
      horizontally within the aerodrome boundaries, and by at least
      91.5 m (300 feet) horizontally outside those boundaries, until the
      aeroplane has reached the end of the take-off flight path,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the one-engine-inoperative departure plan
      includes

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} an obstacle assessment to identify fixed and
        transient obstacles along the take-off flight path,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane's approved performance
        information specified in the aircraft flight manual, and

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} the visual reference points to be used along
        the take-off flight path, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} existing meteorological conditions allow the
      clearance, through visual guidance, of all obstacles and terrain
      by the margins specified in subparagraph (iii); or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aeroplane operated in a
    non-scheduled air service,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the take-off weight of the aeroplane is not
      limited by any take-off weight limitations specified in the
      aircraft flight manual,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the aerodrome elevation is at or below 1 220 m
      (4,000 feet) ASL, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the ceiling and visibility are at or above the
      landing and approach minima for the departure aerodrome.

##### [Enroute Limitations with One Engine Inoperative]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998564 .Subheading}

**[[704.48]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.48 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate a multi-engined aircraft with passengers on board if the weight
of the aircraft is greater than the weight that will allow the aircraft
to maintain, with any engine inoperative, the following altitudes:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} when operating in IMC or in IFR flight on airways or
  air routes, the MOCA of the route to be flown;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} when operating in IMC or in night VFR flight on
  routes established by an air operator, the MOCA of the route to be
  flown; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} when operating in VFR flight, at least 500 feet above
  the surface.

##### [Dispatch Limitations: Landing at Destination and Alternate Aerodromes]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998569 .Subheading}

- **[[704.49]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.49
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), no person
  shall dispatch or conduct a take-off in an aeroplane unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a turbo-jet-powered aeroplane, the
    weight of the aeroplane on landing at the destination aerodrome and
    at the alternate aerodrome will allow a full-stop landing within 60%
    of the landing distance available (LDA);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a large aeroplane that is
    propeller-driven, the weight of the aeroplane on landing at the
    destination aerodrome and at the alternate aerodrome will allow a
    full-stop landing within 70% of the landing distance available
    (LDA); or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a large aeroplane that is
    propeller-driven and equipped with reverse thrust, the weight of the
    aeroplane on landing at the destination aerodrome and at the
    alternate aerodrome will allow a full-stop landing within 80% of the
    landing distance available (LDA) if

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the approach speed does not exceed an indicated
      airspeed of 100 knots, taking into account the estimated weight of
      the aeroplane, the flap setting and the ambient conditions
      expected on arrival,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the reverse thrust is operative and the runway
      surface conditions permit the use of full-rated reverse thrust,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane is operated on a paved,
      hard-surface runway,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the runway surface is forecast to be bare and
      dry at the estimated time of arrival,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} each flight crew member has completed specific
      training on short-field landing techniques on that type of
      aeroplane within the 12 months preceding the flight, and

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} the glide-path angle specified in the Canada Air
      Pilot or the Restricted Canada Air Pilot is not greater than 3
      degrees and the runway threshold crossing height is not greater
      than 15 m (50 feet).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} In determining whether an aeroplane may be dispatched
  or a take-off may be conducted under subsection (1), the following
  shall be taken into account:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the pressure-altitude at the destination aerodrome
    and at the alternate aerodrome;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a wind component that is not more than 50% of the
    reported headwind or not less than 150% of the reported tailwind at
    the destination aerodrome and at the alternate aerodrome; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the suitability of the runway with respect to the
    wind speed and direction, the ground handling characteristics of the
    aeroplane, the landing aids and the terrain.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If conditions at the destination aerodrome at the
  time of take-off do not permit compliance with the requirement set out
  in paragraph (2)(c), an aeroplane may be dispatched and a take-off may
  be conducted if conditions at the alternate aerodrome designated in
  the operational flight plan permit, at the time of take-off,
  compliance with the requirements set out in paragraph (1)(a) or (b)
  and subsection (2).

##### [Dispatch Limitations: Wet Runway --- Turbo-jet-powered Aeroplanes]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998583 .Subheading}

- **[[704.50]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.50
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), when
  weather reports or forecasts indicate that the runway may be wet at
  the estimated time of arrival, no person shall dispatch or conduct a
  take-off in a turbo-jet-powered aeroplane unless the landing distance
  available (LDA) at the destination airport is at least 115 per cent of
  the landing distance required pursuant to paragraph 704.49(1)(a).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The landing distance available on a wet runway may be
  shorter than that required by subsection (1), but not shorter than
  that required by section 704.49, if the aircraft flight manual
  includes specific information about landing distances on wet runways.

##### [Take-off and Landing on Gravel Runways]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1189501 .Subheading}

- **[[704.51]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.51
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall authorize a
  flight from or to a gravel runway in an aeroplane unless the company
  operations manual sets out procedures for take-offs and landings on
  gravel runways.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off or landing in an
  aeroplane on a gravel runway unless the person has

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} received ground training that includes the
    characteristics of take-off and landing surfaces, the conduct of
    obstacle assessments, and the air operator's procedures for
    take-offs and landings on gravel runways;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} conducted, within the previous two years, at least
    one take-off and one landing on a gravel runway in an aeroplane of
    the same type as the one to be operated; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} been certified by the chief pilot as being
    competent to conduct take-offs and landings on gravel runways.

::: HistoricalNote

  ajax-after="1129600-1189509.html"}
:::

##### [Take-off and Landing on Unprepared Surfaces]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1189510 .Subheading}

**[[704.52]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.52 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
conduct a take-off or a landing on an unprepared surface in an aeroplane
for which the aircraft flight manual does not set out any information
relating to unprepared surface operations, unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane is propeller-driven;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator has set out, in the company
  operations manual, procedures for take-offs and landings on unprepared
  surfaces, including

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} procedures for obtaining the air operator's
    approval for unprepared surface operations, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} procedures for assessing unprepared surfaces and
    unfamiliar approach and departure paths; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} before acting as pilot-in-command during a take-off
  or a landing on an unprepared surface, the person has

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} acquired at least 100 hours of flight time in an
    aeroplane of the same type as the one to be operated,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} received ground and flight training that includes
    the characteristics of take-off and landing surfaces, the conduct of
    obstacle assessments and the interpretation of the applicable
    aeroplane performance information specified in the aircraft flight
    manual,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} acquired at least 25 hours of line indoctrination
    training that includes unprepared surface operations, and

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} been certified by the chief pilot or his or her
    delegate as being competent to conduct take-offs and landings on
    unprepared surfaces.

#### [Division V --- Aircraft Equipment Requirements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-998588 .Subheading}

##### [General Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998589 .Subheading}

- **[[704.62]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.62
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aircraft
  in IMC unless the aircraft is equipped with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} at least two generators, each of which, subject to
    subsection (2), is driven by a separate engine, and at least half of
    which have a sufficient rating to supply the electrical loads of all
    instruments and equipment necessary for the safe emergency operation
    of the aircraft; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} two independent sources of energy and a means of
    selecting either source, at least one source of energy being an
    engine-driven pump or generator, and each source of energy being
    able to drive all gyroscopic instruments and being installed so that
    the failure of one instrument or one source of energy will affect
    neither the energy supply to the remaining instruments nor the other
    source of energy.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a multi-engined helicopter, the
  generators required by paragraph (1)(a) may be driven by the main
  rotor drive train.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aircraft at night unless
  the aircraft is equipped with at least one landing light.

##### [Operation of Aircraft in Icing Conditions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998596 .Subheading}

- **[[704.63]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.63
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} When icing conditions are reported
  to exist or are forecast to be encountered along the route of flight,
  no person shall authorize a flight or its continuation or conduct a
  take-off or continue a flight in an aircraft, even if the
  pilot-in-command determines that the aircraft is adequately equipped
  to operate in icing conditions in accordance with paragraph 605.30(a),
  if, in the opinion of the pilot-in-command, the safety of the flight
  might be adversely affected.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aeroplane in icing
  conditions at night unless the aeroplane is equipped with a means to
  illuminate or otherwise detect the formation of ice.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-152, s. 16
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-704.63-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 704.63"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Airborne Thunderstorm Detection and Weather Radar Equipment]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998602 .Subheading}

**[[704.64]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.64 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft with passengers on board in IMC when current weather
reports or forecasts indicate that thunderstorms may reasonably be
expected along the route to be flown, unless the aircraft is equipped
with thunderstorm detection equipment or weather radar equipment.

##### [Additional Equipment for Single-pilot Operations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998604 .Subheading}

**[[704.65]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.65 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft on a single-pilot operation in IMC unless the
aircraft is equipped with

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} an auto-pilot that is capable of operating the
  aircraft controls to maintain flight and manoeuvre the aircraft about
  the lateral and longitudinal axes;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a headset with a boom microphone or equivalent and a
  transmit button on the control column; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a chart holder that is equipped with a light and that
  is placed in an easily readable position.

##### [Protective Breathing Equipment]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998609 .Subheading}

- **[[704.66]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.66
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall operate a
  pressurized aircraft unless protective breathing equipment with a
  15-minute supply of breathing gas at a pressure-altitude of 8,000 feet
  is readily available at each flight crew member position.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The protective breathing equipment referred to in
  subsection (1) may be used to meet the crew member oxygen requirements
  specified in section 605.31.

##### [First Aid Oxygen]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998613 .Subheading}

**[[704.67]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.67 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an aircraft with passengers on board above FL 250 unless
the aircraft is equipped with oxygen dispensing units and an undiluted
supply of first aid oxygen sufficient to provide at least one passenger
with oxygen for at least one hour or the entire duration of the flight
at a cabin pressure-altitude above 8,000 feet, after an emergency
descent following cabin depressurization, whichever period is longer.

##### [Shoulder Harnesses]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998615 .Subheading}

**[[704.68]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.68 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft unless the pilot seat and any seat beside the pilot
seat are equipped with a safety belt that includes a shoulder harness.

##### [Pitot Heat Indication System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998617 .Subheading}

**[[704.69]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.69 .sectionLabel}** After June 30,
2008, no person shall conduct a takeoff in a transport category
aeroplane, or in a non-transport category aeroplane in respect of which
a type certificate was issued after December 31, 1964, that is equipped
with a flight instrument Pitot heating system unless the aeroplane is
also equipped with a Pitot heat indication system that meets the
requirements of section 525.1326 of Chapter 525 --- Transport Category
Aeroplanes of the Airworthiness Manual.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-78, s. 2
:::

##### [ACAS]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998621 .Subheading}

- **[[704.70]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.70
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), no air
  operator shall operate, in airspace outside RVSM airspace, a
  turbine-powered aeroplane having an MCTOW greater than 5 700 kg
  (12,566 pounds) but less than or equal to 15 000 kg (33,069 pounds) or
  an aeroplane that is not a turbine-powered aeroplane having an MCTOW
  greater than 5 700 kg (12,566 pounds), unless the aeroplane is
  equipped with an operative ACAS that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements of CAN-TSO-C118 or a more
    recent version of it or other requirements that the Minister has
    accepted as providing a level of safety that is at least equivalent
    to the level that that CAN-TSO provides; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements of CAN-TSO-C119a or a more
    recent version of it or other requirements that the Minister has
    accepted as providing a level of safety that is at least equivalent
    to the level that that CAN-TSO provides and is equipped with a Mode
    S transponder that meets the requirements of CAN-TSO-C112 or a more
    recent version of it.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), no air operator shall
  operate a turbine-powered aeroplane having an MCTOW greater than 15
  000 kg (33,069 pounds) in airspace outside RVSM airspace unless the
  aeroplane is equipped with an operative ACAS that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements of CAN-TSO-C119a or a more
    recent version of it or other requirements that the Minister has
    accepted as providing a level of safety that is at least equivalent
    to the level that that CAN-TSO provides; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is equipped with a Mode S transponder that meets
    the requirements of CAN-TSO-C112 or a more recent version of it.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), no air operator shall
  operate an aeroplane referred to in subsection (1) or (2) in RVSM
  airspace unless the aeroplane is equipped with an operative ACAS that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements of CAN-TSO-C119b or a more
    recent version of it or other requirements that the Minister has
    accepted as providing a level of safety that is at least equivalent
    to the level that that CAN-TSO provides; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is equipped with a Mode S transponder that meets
    the requirements of CAN-TSO-C112 or a more recent version of it.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The air operator may operate the aeroplane without
  its being equipped with an operative ACAS if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where a minimum equipment list has not been
    approved by the Minister and subject to subsection 605.08(1), the
    operation takes place within the three days after the date of
    failure of the ACAS; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} it is necessary for the pilot-in-command to
    deactivate, in the interests of aviation safety, the ACAS or any of
    its modes and the pilot-in-command does so in accordance with the
    aircraft flight manual, aircraft operating manual, flight manual
    supplement or minimum equipment list.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} This section does not apply in respect of aeroplanes
  manufactured on or before the day on which this section comes into
  force until two years after that day.

##### [TAWS]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998638 .Subheading}

- **[[704.71]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.71
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), no air
  operator shall operate an aeroplane that has a seating configuration,
  excluding pilot seats, of six to nine inclusive, unless the aeroplane
  is equipped with an operative TAWS that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements for Class A or Class B
    equipment set out in CAN-TSO-C151a or a more recent version of it;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} meets the altitude accuracy requirements set out in
    section 551.102 of Chapter 551 of the Airworthiness Manual; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} has a terrain and airport database compatible with
    the area of operation.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), no air operator shall
  operate an aeroplane that has a seating configuration, excluding pilot
  seats, of ten or more, unless the aeroplane is equipped with an
  operative TAWS that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements for Class A equipment set
    out in CAN-TSO-C151a or a more recent version of it;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} meets the altitude accuracy requirements set out in
    section 551.102 of Chapter 551 of the Airworthiness Manual; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} has a terrain and airport database compatible with
    the area of operation and a terrain awareness and situational
    display.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The air operator may operate the aeroplane without
  its being equipped with an operative TAWS if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane is operated in day VFR only;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the event that a minimum equipment list has not
    been approved by the Minister and subject to subsection 605.08(1),
    the operation takes place within the three days after the day on
    which the failure of the TAWS occurs; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} it is necessary for the pilot-in-command to
    deactivate, in the interests of aviation safety, the TAWS or any of
    its modes and the pilot-in-command does so in accordance with the
    aircraft flight manual, aircraft operating manual, flight manual
    supplement or minimum equipment list.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} This section does not apply in respect of aeroplanes
  manufactured on or before the day on which this section comes into
  force until the day that is two years after that day.

#### [Division VI --- Emergency Equipment]{.HTitleText3} {#h-998656 .Subheading}

##### [Hand-held Fire Extinguisher]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998657 .Subheading}

**[[704.83]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.83 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an aircraft with passengers on board unless at least one
hand-held fire extinguisher is readily accessible for immediate use and
is located in the passenger compartment.

##### [Inspection Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998659 .Subheading}

**[[704.84]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.84 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an aircraft unless the emergency equipment carried on
board under Division II of Subpart 2 of Part VI and this Division is
inspected at the intervals recommended by the equipment manufacturer.

##### [First Aid Kits]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1276906 .Subheading}

**[[704.85]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.85 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
conduct a take-off in an aircraft operated by an air operator unless the
first aid kit carried on board in accordance with paragraph 602.60(1)(h)
contains the supplies and equipment set out in the [Aviation
Occupational Health and Safety
Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-2011-87).

::: HistoricalNote

:::

##### [Survival Equipment]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1276910 .Subheading}

- **[[704.86]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.86
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall operate an
  aircraft, other than an aircraft referred to in subsection 602.61(2),
  unless a survival manual is carried on board that contains information
  about how to use the survival equipment that is carried on board to
  meet the requirements of subsection 602.61(1).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall operate an aircraft on board of
  which life rafts are required to be carried in accordance with section
  602.63 unless the survival kit referred to in paragraph 602.63(6)(c)
  contains

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a life raft repair kit;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a bailing bucket and a sponge;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a whistle;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a waterproof flashlight;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a supply of potable water --- based on 500 mL per
    person and calculated using the rated capacity of the life raft ---
    or a means of desalting or distilling salt water that can provide
    500 mL of potable water per person;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a waterproof survival manual that contains
    information about how to use the survival equipment;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a first aid kit that contains antiseptic swabs,
    burn dressing compresses, bandages and motion sickness pills; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} a pyrotechnic signalling device, or an aviation
    visual distress signal that has a marking applied by the
    manufacturer indicating that the signal meets the requirements of
    CAN-TSO-C168, a signalling mirror and a dye marker for visually
    signalling distress.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (2), if there is insufficient
  space in the attached survival kit, a supplemental survival kit shall
  be stowed adjacent to each required life raft and contain

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a supply of potable water --- based on 500 mL per
    person and calculated using the rated capacity of the life raft ---
    or a means of desalting or distilling salt water that can provide
    500 mL of potable water per person; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} motion sickness pills.

**\[704.87 to 704.105 reserved\]**

#### [Division VII --- Personnel Requirements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-998662 .Subheading}

##### [Minimum Crew]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998663 .Subheading}

**[[704.106]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.106 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an aircraft with fewer than two pilots, where the aircraft

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} is an aeroplane carrying 10 or more passengers; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} is carrying passengers and is being operated in IFR
  flight.

##### [Designation of Pilot-in-command and Second-in-command]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998667 .Subheading}

- **[[704.107]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.107
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator must designate, for
  each flight, a pilot-in-command or, if the crew includes two pilots, a
  pilot-in-command and a second-in-command.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator must record the name of the
  pilot-in-command and, if applicable, the name of the second-in-command
  who were designated under subsection (1) and must retain the record
  for at least 180 days after the day on which the flight is completed.

##### [Flight Crew Member Qualifications]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998669 .Subheading}

- **[[704.108]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.108
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (6), no air
  operator shall permit a person to act and no person shall act as a
  flight crew member in an aircraft unless the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} holds the licence and ratings required by Part IV;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} within the previous 90 days, has completed at least
    three take-offs and three landings

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} where a type rating for that aircraft is
      required, in an aircraft of that type, or in a flight simulator
      representing that type of aircraft that has been approved by the
      Minister under Subpart 6 of Part VI for take-off and landing
      qualifications, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where a type rating for that aircraft is not
      required, in an aircraft of that category and class, or in a
      flight simulator representing that category and class of aircraft
      that has been approved by the Minister under Subpart 6 of Part VI
      for take-off and landing qualifications;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} has successfully completed a pilot proficiency
    check, the validity period of which has not expired, for that type
    of aircraft, in accordance with the Commercial Air Service
    Standards; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} has fulfilled the requirements of the air
    operator's ground training program and, except where undergoing line
    indoctrination training, the air operator's flight training program.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may group similar aircraft as a
  single type for the purposes of the pilot proficiency check referred
  to in paragraph (1)(c) if the air operator

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in its air operator
    certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No person shall act as the pilot-in-command of an
  aircraft with passengers on board in IFR flight unless the person has
  acquired at least 1,200 hours of flight time as a pilot.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} No person shall act as the pilot-in-command of an
  aircraft in VFR flight unless the person has acquired at least 500
  hours of flight time as a pilot.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} No person shall act as the pilot-in-command of an
  aircraft with a person other than a flight crew member on board in
  night VFR flight unless the person acting as the pilot-in-command
  holds an instrument rating for that class of aircraft.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may permit a person to act and a
  person may act as a flight crew member in an aircraft where the person
  does not meet the requirements of paragraphs (1)(b) to (d), if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is operated on a training, ferry or
    positioning flight; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in its air operator
      certificate, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service
      Standards.

##### [Qualifications of Operational Control Personnel]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998689 .Subheading}

- **[[704.109]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.109
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall permit a
  person to act and no person shall act in an operational control
  position unless that person has fulfilled the training requirements
  set out in this Subpart and has demonstrated to the air operator the
  knowledge and abilities required by the Commercial Air Service
  Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who has not acted in an operational control
  position within the previous three months shall, prior to acting in an
  operational control position, demonstrate to the air operator that the
  person still has the knowledge and abilities referred to in subsection
  (1).

##### [Check Authority]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998693 .Subheading}

- **[[704.110]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.110
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A pilot proficiency check shall be
  conducted by the Minister.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Any other check required under this Subpart may be
  conducted by the Minister.

##### [Validity Period]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998697 .Subheading}

- **[[704.111]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.111
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) and (3),
  the validity period of a pilot proficiency check and of the annual
  training referred to in section 704.115 expires on the first day of
  the thirteenth month following the month in which the proficiency
  check or training was completed.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where a pilot proficiency check or annual training is
  renewed within the last 90 days of its validity period, its validity
  period is extended by 12 months.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may extend the validity period of a
  pilot proficiency check or annual training by up to 60 days where the
  Minister is of the opinion that aviation safety is not likely to be
  affected.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where the validity period of a pilot proficiency
  check or annual training has been expired for 24 months or more, the
  person shall requalify by meeting the training requirements specified
  in the Commercial Air Service Standards.

**\[704.112 to 704.114 reserved\]**

#### [Division VIII --- Training]{.HTitleText3} {#h-998704 .Subheading}

##### [Training Program]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998705 .Subheading}

- **[[704.115]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.115
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every air operator shall establish
  and maintain a ground and flight training program that is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} designed to ensure that each person who receives
    training acquires the competence to perform the person's assigned
    duties; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} approved by the Minister in accordance with the
    Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator's ground and flight training program
  shall include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} for flight crew members:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} company indoctrination training,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} line indoctrination training,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} high-altitude training, where applicable,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} upgrading training, where applicable, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} initial and annual training, including

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} aircraft type training,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} aircraft servicing and ground handling
        training,

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} emergency procedures training, and

      - [(D)]{.lawlabel} aircraft surface contamination training;

  - [(a.1)]{.lawlabel} initial training followed by training every three
    years on underwater egress for seaplane pilots;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} initial and annual training for operational control
    personnel;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} initial and annual aircraft surface contamination
    training for those operations personnel designated in the Commercial
    Air Service Standards;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} initial and annual training for personnel who are
    assigned to perform duties on board an aircraft; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} any other training required to ensure a safe
    operation under this Subpart.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} include a detailed syllabus of its ground and
    flight training program in its company operations manual;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} ensure that adequate facilities and qualified
    personnel are provided for its ground and flight training program,
    in accordance with the Commercial Air Service Standards; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} establish and maintain a safety awareness program
    concerning the adverse effects of aircraft surface contamination and
    provide the program to all flight operations personnel who are not
    required to receive the training described in paragraph (2)(c).

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall have a fatigue management
  training program for its flight crew members that contains

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} personal fatigue management strategies relating to

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} sleep hygiene,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} lifestyle, exercise and diet, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the consumption of alcohol and drugs;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the impact of fatigue on aviation safety;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} sleep requirements and the science relating to
    fatigue;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the causes and consequences of fatigue;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} how to recognize fatigue in themselves and in
    others;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} sleep disorders, their impact on aviation safety
    and treatment options; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} human and organizational factors that may cause
    fatigue, including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} sleep quality and duration,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the impact of shift work and overtime,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the circadian rhythm, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the effects of changes of time zones.

##### [Conditional Approval of Training Program]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998746 .Subheading}

- **[[704.116]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.116
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may give conditional
  approval to a training program where an air operator submits to the
  Minister a copy of a syllabus of its training program that provides
  enough information for a preliminary evaluation of the training
  program in light of the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may conduct training under a training
  program that has received conditional approval until the Minister has
  evaluated the effectiveness of the training program and has informed
  the air operator of any deficiencies that must be corrected.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall give final approval to a
  conditionally approved training program when the air operator
  demonstrates that the training conducted under that program is
  adequate to permit the persons who receive it to safely perform their
  assigned duties.

##### [Training and Qualification Records]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998751 .Subheading}

- **[[704.117]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.117
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every air operator shall, for each
  person who is required to receive training under this Subpart,
  establish and maintain a record of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person's name and, where applicable, personnel
    licence number, type and ratings;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, the person's medical category and
    the expiry date of that category;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the dates on which the person, while in the air
    operator's employ, successfully completed any training, pilot
    proficiency check or examination required under this Subpart or
    obtained any qualification required under this Subpart;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} information relating to any failure of the person,
    while in the air operator's employ, to successfully complete any
    training, pilot proficiency check or examination required under this
    Subpart or to obtain any qualification required under this Subpart;
    and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the type of aircraft or flight training equipment
    used for any training, pilot proficiency check or qualification
    required under this Subpart.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall retain the records referred to
  in paragraphs (1)(c) and (d) and a record of each pilot proficiency
  check for at least three years.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall retain a copy of the most
  recent written examination completed by each pilot for each type of
  aircraft for which the pilot has a qualification.

##### [Amendments to Training Program]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1339540 .Subheading}

- **[[704.118]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.118
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister determines that an
  air operator's training program required under 704.115 does not
  include the competencies required for each person who receives
  training to perform their assigned duties, the Minister shall notify
  the air operator of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the corrective actions that the air operator is
    required to implement to its training program; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the date by which the air operator is required to
    submit its amended training program to the Minister for approval
    under paragraph 704.115(1)(b).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The air operator referred to in subsection (1) shall
  submit its amended training program to the Minister on or before the
  date specified by the Minister under paragraph (1)(b).

**\[704.119 reserved\]**

#### [Division IX --- Manuals]{.HTitleText3} {#h-998762 .Subheading}

##### [Requirements relating to Company Operations Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998763 .Subheading}

- **[[704.120]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.120
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every air operator shall establish
  and maintain a company operations manual that meets the requirements
  of section 704.121.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall submit its company operations
  manual, and any amendments to that manual, to the Minister.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where there is a change in any aspect of an air
  operator's operation or where the company operations manual no longer
  meets the Commercial Air Service Standards, the air operator shall
  amend its company operations manual.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall, where the Commercial Air Service
  Standards are met, approve those parts of a company operations manual,
  and any amendments to those parts, that relate to the information
  required by section 704.121.

##### [Contents of Company Operations Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998769 .Subheading}

- **[[704.121]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.121
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A company operations manual, which
  may be issued in separate parts corresponding to specific aspects of
  an operation, shall include the instructions and information necessary
  to enable the personnel concerned to perform their duties safely and
  shall contain the information required by the Commercial Air Service
  Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A company operations manual shall be such that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} all parts of the manual are consistent and
    compatible in form and content;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the manual can be readily amended;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the manual contains an amendment control page and a
    list of the pages that are in effect; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the manual has the date of the last amendment to
    each page specified on that page.

##### [Distribution of Company Operations Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998777 .Subheading}

- **[[704.122]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.122
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), an air
  operator shall provide a copy of the appropriate parts of its company
  operations manual, including any amendments to those parts, to each of
  its crew members and to its ground operations and maintenance
  personnel.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may place a copy of the appropriate
  parts of its company operations manual in each aircraft that it
  operates, instead of providing a copy to each crew member, if all
  amendments to the manual are included in the system for the
  dissemination of general operational information referred to in
  section 704.13.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Every person who has been provided with a copy of the
  appropriate parts of a company operations manual pursuant to
  subsection (1) shall keep it up to date with the amendments provided
  and shall ensure that the appropriate parts are accessible when the
  person is performing assigned duties.

##### [Aircraft Operating Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998782 .Subheading}

- **[[704.123]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.123
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may establish and
  maintain an aircraft operating manual for the use and guidance of crew
  members in the operation of its aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An aircraft operating manual shall contain the
  information required by

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} section 724.123 of Standard 724 --- Commuter
    Operations --- Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service Standards,
    in the case of an aeroplane, or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} section 724.123 of Standard 724 --- Commuter
    Operations --- Helicopters of the Commercial Air Service Standards,
    in the case of a helicopter.

- [(2.1)]{.lawlabel} Where the aircraft flight manual is not carried on
  board the aircraft, an aircraft operating manual shall contain the
  aircraft performance data and limitations specified in the aircraft
  flight manual, which shall be clearly identified as aircraft flight
  manual requirements.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator that has established an aircraft
  operating manual shall ensure that a copy of the manual is carried on
  board each aircraft to which it relates.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-26, s. 40](#1511757-1516305){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1511757-1516305.html"}
:::

[Previous

:::

##### [Standard Operating Procedures]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998789 .Subheading}

- **[[704.124]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-704.124
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every air operator shall, for each
  of its aircraft that is required to be operated by two or more pilots,
  establish and maintain standard operating procedures that enable the
  crew members to operate the aircraft within the limitations specified
  in the aircraft flight manual and that meet the Commercial Air Service
  Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator that has established standard
  operating procedures for an aircraft shall ensure that a copy of the
  standard operating procedures is carried on board the aircraft.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where an air operator has established an aircraft
  operating manual, the standard operating procedures for the aircraft
  shall form part of that manual.

**\[704.125 to 704.127 reserved\]**

### [Subpart 5 --- Airline Operations]{.HTitleText2} {#h-998795 .Subheading}

#### [Division I --- General]{.HTitleText3} {#h-998796 .Subheading}

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998797 .Subheading}

**[[705.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.01 .sectionLabel}** This Subpart
applies in respect of the operation by a Canadian air operator, in an
air transport service or in aerial work involving sightseeing
operations, of any of the following aircraft:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} an aeroplane, other than an aeroplane authorized to
  operate under Subpart 4, that has a MCTOW of more than 8 618 kg
  (19,000 pounds) or for which a Canadian type certificate has been
  issued authorizing the transport of 20 or more passengers;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a helicopter that has a seating configuration,
  excluding pilot seats, of 20 or more; or

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} any aircraft that is authorized by the Minister to be
  operated under this Subpart.

##### [Aircraft Operation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998802 .Subheading}

**[[705.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.02 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an aircraft under this Subpart unless the air operator
complies with the conditions and operations specifications in an air
operator certificate issued to that operator by the Minister pursuant to
section 705.07.

##### [Operations Manager]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998804 .Subheading}

- **[[705.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.03
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2019-295, s.
  15\]]{.Repealed}

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operations manager appointed under paragraph
  700.09(1)(a) shall, where a finding resulting from a quality assurance
  program established under section 706.07 or a safety management system
  referred to in section 705.151 is reported to them,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} determine what, if any, corrective actions are
    required and carry out those actions;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} keep a record of any determination made under
    paragraph (a) and the reason for it;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if management functions have been assigned to
    another person under subsection (3) or (4), communicate any
    determination regarding a corrective action to that person; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} notify the accountable executive of any systemic
    deficiency and of the corrective action taken.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The operations manager may assign the management
  functions for the entire safety management system referred to in
  section 705.151 to another person if the assignment and its scope are
  described in the air operator's company operations manual.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The operations manager may assign the management
  functions for specific duties to another person if the assignment and
  its scope are described in the air operator's company operations
  manual.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The responsibility of the operations manager is not
  affected by the assignment of management functions to another person
  under subsection (3) or (4).

- SOR/2005-173, s. 22
- [SOR/2019-295, s. 15](#1194402-1195615){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1194402-1195615.html"}

##### [Holder of More Than One Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998817 .Subheading}

**[[705.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.04 .sectionLabel}** If the holder of
an air operator certificate issued under section 705.07 is also the
holder of an approved maintenance organization (AMO) certificate issued
under section 573.02, the person responsible for maintenance appointed
under paragraph 573.03(1)(a) shall, where a finding resulting from a
quality assurance program established under section 706.07 is reported
to them,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} determine what, if any, corrective actions are
  required and carry out those actions;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} keep a record of any determination made under
  paragraph (a) and the reason for it;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} if management functions have been assigned to another
  person under subsection 573.04(4) or (5), communicate any
  determination regarding a corrective action to that person; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} notify the accountable executive of any systemic
  deficiency and of the corrective action taken.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-173, s. 22
:::

**\[705.05 and 705.06 reserved\]**

#### [Division II --- Certification]{.HTitleText3} {#h-998826 .Subheading}

##### [Issuance or Amendment of Air Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998827 .Subheading}

- **[[705.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.07
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to section 6.71 of the Act,
  the Minister shall, on receipt of an application submitted in the form
  and manner required by the Commercial Air Service Standards, issue or
  amend an air operator certificate where the applicant demonstrates to
  the Minister the ability to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} maintain an adequate organizational structure;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} maintain an operational control system;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} meet training program requirements;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} comply with maintenance requirements;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} meet the Commercial Air Service Standards for the
    operation; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} conduct the operation safely.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), an applicant
  shall have

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a management organization capable of exercising
    operational control;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} managerial personnel who have been approved by the
    Minister in accordance with the Commercial Air Service Standards,
    are employed on a full-time basis and perform the functions related
    to the following positions, namely,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} operations manager,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} chief pilots,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} where the applicant does not hold an approved
      maintenance organization (AMO) certificate, maintenance manager,
      and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} where flight attendants are required for the
      operation, flight attendant manager;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a safety management system that meets the
    requirements of Subpart 7 of Part I and section 705.152;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} operational support services and equipment that
    meet the Commercial Air Service Standards;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} after January 1, 1997, where a master minimum
    equipment list has been established for a type of aircraft, a
    minimum equipment list for each aircraft of that type, approved by
    the Minister in accordance with the procedures specified in the
    MMEL/MEL Policy and Procedures Manual;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} aircraft that are properly equipped for and crew
    members who are qualified for the area of operation and the type of
    operation;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} an operational control system that meets the
    requirements of section 705.20;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} a training program that meets the requirements of
    section 705.124;

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} legal custody and control of at least one aircraft
    of each category of aircraft that is to be operated;

  - [(j)]{.lawlabel} a company operations manual that meets the
    requirements of sections 705.134 and 705.135;

  - [(k)]{.lawlabel} a maintenance control system approved pursuant to
    Subpart 6; and

  - [(l)]{.lawlabel} an air operator emergency response plan that has
    the components set out in subsection 725.07(3) of Standard 725 ---
    Airline Operations --- Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service
    Standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-173, s. 23
- SOR/2005-357, s. 7
:::

##### [Contents of Air Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998855 .Subheading}

**[[705.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.08 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
certificate shall contain

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the legal name, trade name and address of the air
  operator;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number of the air operator certificate;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the effective date of certification;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the date of issue of the certificate;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the general conditions identified in section 705.09;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} specific conditions with respect to

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the areas of operation authorized,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the types of service authorized,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the types of aircraft authorized and, if
    applicable, their registration, and any operational restrictions,
    and

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the main base, scheduled points and, if
    applicable, sub-bases; and

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} where the air operator complies with the Commercial
  Air Service Standards, operations specifications with respect to

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} aircraft performance, equipment and emergency
    equipment requirements,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} instrument approach procedures,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} enroute aerodrome authorizations and limitations,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} special weather minima authorizations,

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} authorizations concerning flight crew member
    qualifications and crew member complement,

  - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} navigation system authorizations,

  - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} pilot training and pilot proficiency checks,

  - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} the air operator maintenance control system
    approved pursuant to Subpart 6,

  - [(ix)]{.lawlabel} leasing arrangements,

  - [(x)]{.lawlabel} the use of synthetic flight training devices, and

  - [(xi)]{.lawlabel} any other condition pertaining to the operation
    that the Minister deems necessary for aviation safety.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-152, s. 17

##### [General Conditions of Air Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998881 .Subheading}

**[[705.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.09 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
certificate shall contain the following general conditions:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall conduct flight operations in
  accordance with its company operations manual;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall maintain an adequate
  organizational structure;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall employ managerial personnel
  who meet the Commercial Air Service Standards;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall conduct training in accordance
  with its training program approved pursuant to this Subpart;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall maintain aircraft that are
  properly equipped for the area of operation and the type of operation;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall employ crew members who are
  qualified for the area of operation and the type of operation;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall maintain its aircraft in
  accordance with the requirements of Subpart 6;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall maintain operational support
  services and equipment that meet the Commercial Air Service Standards;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall notify the Minister within 10
  working days after

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} changing its legal name, its trade name, its main
    base, a sub-base, a scheduled point or its managerial personnel, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} ceasing to operate a type of aircraft authorized
    under this Subpart; and

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} the air operator shall conduct a safe operation.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-152, s. 18
- [SOR/2022-246, s. 29(F)](#1380174-1380800){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1380174-1380800.html"}
:::

**\[705.10 to 705.15 reserved\]**

#### [Division III --- Flight Operations]{.HTitleText3} {#h-998898 .Subheading}

##### [Exceptions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998899 .Subheading}

- **[[705.16]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.16
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Sections 705.40, 705.43, 705.75,
  705.77 to 705.79, 705.139 and 705.201 do not apply if nine or fewer
  persons are on board an aircraft and each person is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an employee of the air operator;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a person whose presence on board the aircraft is
    necessary for

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the safety of the flight,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the safe handling of animals,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the safe handling of dangerous goods,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the security of valuable or confidential cargo,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the preservation of fragile or perishable cargo,
      or

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} the handling of cargo;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a person described in paragraph (b) who is
    travelling to or from an assignment;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} an owner or shipper of animals; or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a dependant of an employee of the air operator.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Any person referred to in subsection (1) may be
  carried on board an aircraft for which the type certificate does not
  authorize the transport of passengers.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall operate an aircraft with a
  person referred to in subsection (1) on board unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator has established procedures for the
    transport of that person;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person has unobstructed access from the
    person's seat to the flight deck, to an exit or to an emergency
    exit;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the person is provided with a means of two-way
    communication with the flight crew members;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command has a means of notifying the
    person when safety belts must be fastened; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the air operator ensures that, before every
    take-off, the person is given a briefing by a crew member in
    accordance with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 15
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-705.16-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 705.16"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Operating Instructions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998922 .Subheading}

- **[[705.17]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.17
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall ensure that
  all operations personnel are properly instructed about their duties
  and about the relationship of their duties to the operation as a
  whole.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The operations personnel of an air operator shall
  follow the procedures specified in the air operator's company
  operations manual in the performance of their duties.

##### [General Operational Information]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998926 .Subheading}

**[[705.18]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.18 .sectionLabel}** Every air
operator shall establish a system for the timely dissemination of
general operational information that includes a means for each crew
member and each flight dispatcher to acknowledge receipt of that
information.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-152, s. 19
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-705.18-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 705.18"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Scheduled Air Service Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998930 .Subheading}

- **[[705.19]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.19
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), every air
  operator that operates a scheduled air service for the purpose of
  transporting persons shall operate the service between airports or
  heliports or between an airport or heliport and a military aerodrome.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may operate a scheduled air service
  for the purpose of transporting persons between an airport and an
  aerodrome or between two aerodromes if the air operator is authorized
  to do so in its air operator certificate.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-87, s. 16
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-705.19-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 705.19"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Operational Control System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998936 .Subheading}

**[[705.20]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.20 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an aircraft unless the air operator has an operational
control system that meets the Commercial Air Service Standards and is
under the control of its operations manager.

##### [Flight Authorization]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998938 .Subheading}

**[[705.21]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.21 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
commence a flight unless the flight has been authorized in accordance
with the procedures specified in the air operator's company operations
manual.

##### [Operational Flight Plan]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998940 .Subheading}

- **[[705.22]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.22
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall permit a
  person to commence a flight unless an operational flight plan that
  meets the Commercial Air Service Standards has been prepared.

- [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall specify in its company
  operations manual

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the period for which the operational flight plan
    referred to in subsection (3) shall be kept;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the method of recording the formal approval of the
    plan by the flight dispatcher; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the method of recording the formal approval of the
    plan by the pilot-in-command.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command of an aircraft shall ensure that
  one copy of the operational flight plan is left at a point of
  departure, in accordance with the procedures specified in the company
  operations manual, and that another copy is carried on board the
  aircraft until the aircraft reaches the final destination of the
  flight.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall keep a copy of the operational
  flight plan, including any amendments to the plan, for not less than
  90 days.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/99-158, s. 9
- [SOR/2025-26, s. 41](#1511759-1516332){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1511759-1516332.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-705.22-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 705.22"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Maintenance of Aircraft]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998951 .Subheading}

**[[705.23]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.23 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall permit a person to conduct a take-off in an aircraft that has not
been maintained in accordance with the air operator's maintenance
control system.

##### [Checklist]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998953 .Subheading}

- **[[705.24]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.24
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every air operator shall establish
  the checklist referred to in paragraph 602.60(1)(a) for each aircraft
  type that it operates and shall make the appropriate parts of the
  checklist readily available to the crew members.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Every crew member shall follow the checklist referred
  to in subsection (1) in the performance of the crew member's assigned
  duties.

##### [Fuel Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998957 .Subheading}

- **[[705.25]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.25
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no air
  operator shall authorize a flight and no person shall commence a
  flight unless the aircraft

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} when operating in VFR flight, carries sufficient
    fuel to fly to the destination aerodrome and thereafter to fly for
    45 minutes at normal cruising speed;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} when operating in IFR flight on designated routes
    or over designated areas as defined in the Commercial Air Service
    Standards, carries an enroute fuel reserve of five per cent of the
    fuel required to fly to the destination aerodrome; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} when operating in IFR flight, except when complying
    with the Safety Criteria for Approval of Extended Range Twin-engine
    Operations (ETOPS) Manual, carries sufficient fuel to allow the
    aircraft

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} to descend at any point along the route to the
      lower of

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} the one-engine-inoperative service ceiling, or

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} 10,000 feet ASL,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} to cruise at the altitude referred to in
      subparagraph (i) to a suitable aerodrome,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} to conduct an approach and a missed approach,
      and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} to hold for 30 minutes at an altitude of 1,500
      feet above the elevation of the aerodrome selected in accordance
      with subparagraph (ii).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may be authorized in an air operator
  certificate to reduce the enroute fuel reserve required by paragraph
  (1)(b) where the air operator complies with the Commercial Air Service
  Standards.

##### [Extended Range Twin-engined Operations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998970 .Subheading}

- **[[705.26]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.26
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no air
  operator shall operate a twin-engined aeroplane on a route containing
  a point that is farther from an adequate aerodrome than the distance
  that can be flown in 60 minutes at the one-engine-inoperative cruise
  speed, unless the flight is conducted wholly within Canadian Domestic
  Airspace.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may operate an aeroplane on a route
  referred to in subsection (1) where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane is turbine-powered;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator is authorized to do so in its air
    operator certificate; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the air operator complies with the Safety Criteria
    for Approval of Extended Range Twin-engine Operations (ETOPS)
    Manual.

##### [Admission to Flight Deck]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998977 .Subheading}

- **[[705.27]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.27
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Where a Department of Transport air
  carrier inspector presents an official identity card to the
  pilot-in-command of an aircraft, the pilot-in-command shall give the
  inspector free and uninterrupted access to the flight deck of the
  aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator and the pilot-in-command shall make
  available for the use of the air carrier inspector the observer seat
  most suitable to perform the inspector's duties, as determined by the
  inspector.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall ensure that only the following
  persons are admitted to the flight deck of an aircraft:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a crew member;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an inspector referred to in subsection (1); and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a person authorized by the air operator under
    subsection (4).

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall not authorize a person referred
  to in column I of the table to this section to access the flight deck
  of an aircraft operating in domestic service unless the access would
  not have an adverse effect on aviation safety and the air operator has
  verified

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} that the person is a person referred to in column I
    of the table and is employed by an employer referred to in column II
    of the table; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the identity of the person by examining the
    document referred to in column III of the table and one of the
    documents referred to in column IV of the table.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} An air operator that authorizes access to the flight
  deck of an aircraft shall keep a record of the following information
  for two years after the day on which access is authorized:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name of the authorized person;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name of their employer; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the date of the flight and flight number.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} Before each flight, an air operator shall notify the
  pilot-in-command of the identity of the persons who the operator has
  authorized to access the flight deck of an aircraft.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} Before admitting a person authorized under
  subsection (4) to the flight deck of an aircraft, the pilot-in-command
  shall verify the identity of the person by means of the documents
  referred to in paragraph 4(b).

- [(8)]{.lawlabel} A person authorized under subsection (4) who is
  admitted to the flight deck of an aircraft may only occupy an observer
  seat.

- [(9)]{.lawlabel} The pilot-in-command may refuse access to the flight
  deck of an aircraft if they are of the opinion that there would be an
  adverse effect on aviation safety.

- [(10)]{.lawlabel} The air operator shall set out, in its company
  operations manual, procedures respecting

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the granting of authorization to access the flight
    deck;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the verification required under subsection (4); and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the notice to be provided to the pilot-in-command
    under subsection (6).

##### [Seats for Cabin Safety Inspectors]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998997 .Subheading}

**[[705.28]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.28 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
shall provide a cabin safety inspector who is performing an in-flight
cabin inspection with a confirmed passenger seat in the passenger
compartment.

##### [Flight Crew Members at Controls]{.HTitleText4} {#h-998999 .Subheading}

- **[[705.29]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.29
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), flight
  crew members who are on flight deck duty shall remain at their duty
  stations with their safety belts fastened and, where the aircraft is
  below 10,000 feet ASL, with their safety belts, including their
  shoulder harnesses, fastened.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Flight crew members may leave their duty stations
  where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} their absence is necessary for the performance of
    duties in connection with the operation of the aircraft;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} their absence is in connection with physiological
    needs; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} they are taking a rest period and are relieved by
    other flight crew members who meet the qualifications set out in the
    Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [Simulation of Emergency Situations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999006 .Subheading}

**[[705.30]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.30 .sectionLabel}** No person shall,
if passengers or cargo are on board an aircraft, simulate emergency
situations that could affect the flight characteristics of the aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-151, s. 19](#1252613-1257191){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1252613-1257191.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-705.30-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 705.30"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Crew Member Briefing]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999008 .Subheading}

**[[705.31]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.31 .sectionLabel}** The
pilot-in-command of an aircraft shall ensure that, prior to each flight
or series of flight segments, the crew members of the aircraft are given
a pre-flight briefing that meets the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [VFR Flight Obstacle Clearance Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999010 .Subheading}

**[[705.32]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.32 .sectionLabel}** Except when
conducting a take-off or landing, no person shall operate an aeroplane
in VFR flight

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} during the day, at less than 1,000 feet AGL or at a
  horizontal distance of less than 1,000 feet from any obstacle; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} at night, at less than 1,000 feet above the highest
  obstacle located within a horizontal distance of five miles from the
  route to be flown or, in designated mountainous regions, at less than
  2,000 feet above the highest obstacle located within a horizontal
  distance of five miles from the route to be flown.

##### [VFR Flight Weather Conditions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999014 .Subheading}

**[[705.33]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.33 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
commence a VFR flight unless current weather reports and forecasts, if
obtainable, indicate that the weather conditions along the route to be
flown and at the destination aerodrome will be such that the flight can
be conducted in compliance with VFR.

##### [Take-off Minima]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999016 .Subheading}

- **[[705.34]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.34
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no person
  shall conduct a take-off in an aircraft in IMC where weather
  conditions are at or above the take-off minima, but below the landing
  minima, for the runway to be used unless an alternate aerodrome is
  specified in the operational flight plan and that aerodrome is located

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a twin-engined aircraft, within the
    distance that can be flown in 60 minutes at the
    one-engine-inoperative cruise speed; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a three- or four-engined aircraft or
    where an air operator is authorized in its air operator certificate
    to conduct ETOPS with the type of aircraft operated, within the
    distance that can be flown in 120 minutes at the
    one-engine-inoperative cruise speed.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person may conduct a take-off in an aircraft in IMC
  where weather conditions are at or above the take-off minima, but
  below the landing minima, for the runway to be used, if the weather
  conditions are at or above the landing minima for another suitable
  runway at that aerodrome, taking into account the aircraft performance
  operating limitations specified in Division IV.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of section 602.126, a person may
  conduct a take-off in an aircraft in IMC where weather conditions are
  below the take-off minima specified in the instrument approach
  procedure, if the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in an air operator
    certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this section, the landing minima
  are the decision height or the minimum descent altitude and the
  visibility published for an approach.

##### [No Alternate Aerodrome --- IFR Flight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999026 .Subheading}

**[[705.35]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.35 .sectionLabel}** For the purposes
of section 602.122, a person may conduct an IFR flight where an
alternate aerodrome has not been designated in the IFR flight plan or in
the IFR flight itinerary, if the person

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in an air operator
  certificate; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [VFR OTT Flight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999030 .Subheading}

**[[705.36]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.36 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft in VFR OTT flight unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is a helicopter;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person is authorized to do so in an air operator
  certificate; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the person complies with the Commercial Air Service
  Standards.

##### [Routes in Uncontrolled Airspace]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999035 .Subheading}

**[[705.37]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.37 .sectionLabel}** No person shall,
in uncontrolled airspace, conduct an IFR flight or a night VFR flight on
a route other than an air route unless the air operator establishes the
route in accordance with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

**[[705.38]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.38 .sectionLabel}** \[Reserved\]

##### [Weight and Balance Control]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999038 .Subheading}

- **[[705.39]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.39
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aircraft
  unless, during every phase of the flight, the load restrictions,
  weight and centre of gravity of the aircraft conform to the
  limitations specified in the aircraft flight manual.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall have a weight and balance
  system that meets the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall keep a copy of the weight and
  balance forms, including any amendments to the forms, for not less
  than 90 days.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall specify in its company
  operation manual

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} its weight and balance system;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} its instructions to employees regarding the
    preparation and accuracy of weight and balance forms; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the period for which the forms shall be kept.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/99-158, s. 11
:::

##### [Passenger and Cabin Safety Procedures]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999049 .Subheading}

- **[[705.40]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.40
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall establish
  procedures to ensure that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} passengers move to and from the aircraft and embark
    and disembark safely, in accordance with procedures that meet the
    requirements of section 725.40 of Standard 725 --- Airline
    Operations --- Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service Standards;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} all passengers are seated and secured in accordance
    with subsection 605.26(1);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsection (2), the back of each seat is
    in the upright position and all chair tables and carry-on baggage
    are stowed during movement on the surface, take-off and landing and
    at such other times as the pilot-in-command considers necessary for
    the safety of the persons on board the aircraft; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} seats located at emergency exits and seats that are
    not located on the main deck of an aircraft are not occupied by
    passengers whose presence in those seats could adversely affect the
    safety of passengers or crew members during an emergency evacuation.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may, for the transportation of any
  passenger who has been certified by a physician as unable to sit
  upright, allow the back of the seat occupied by such a passenger to
  remain in the reclining position during movement on the surface,
  take-off and landing if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the passenger is seated in a location that will not
    restrict the evacuation of other passengers from the aircraft;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the passenger is not seated in a row that is next
    to or immediately in front of an emergency exit; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the seat immediately behind the passenger's seat is
    vacant.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall not permit an aircraft with
  passengers on board to be fuelled unless the fuelling is carried out
  in accordance with procedures that meet the requirements set out in
  subsection 725.40(2) of Standard 725 --- Airline Operations -
  Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2019-296, s. 10\]]{.Repealed}

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-295, s. 16](#1194403-1195618){.wb-lbx

- [SOR/2019-296, s. 10](#1194436-1195848){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1194436-1195848.html"}
