##### [Flight Attendant Stations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999064 .Subheading}

- **[[705.41]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.41
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Each flight attendant shall, for
  take-off and landing, occupy a seat in the passenger cabin that meets
  the requirements of subsection (2).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Each flight attendant station shall be approved by
  the Minister in accordance with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall permit a flight attendant seat
  to be occupied by a person other than a flight attendant unless the
  air operator

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in its air operator
    certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [Carry-on Baggage]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999071 .Subheading}

- **[[705.42]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.42
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every air operator shall establish a
  carry-on baggage control program that is approved by the Minister in
  accordance with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall permit a person to carry on
  board an aircraft any carry-on baggage unless that baggage has been
  accepted in accordance with a carry-on baggage control program and can
  be

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} stowed in a compartment or overhead rack that has
    been approved by the Minister in accordance with Chapter 551 of the
    Airworthiness Manual for the stowage of carry-on baggage;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} stowed under a passenger seat; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} restrained by a means that has been approved by the
    Minister in accordance with Chapter 551 of the Airworthiness Manual.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No person shall carry on board an aircraft any
  carry-on baggage unless that baggage has been accepted in accordance
  with a carry-on baggage control program.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} All carry-on baggage that is stowed under a passenger
  seat shall be restrained in a manner that has been approved by the
  Minister in accordance with Chapter 551 of the Airworthiness Manual.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} All carry-on baggage shall be stowed so that it does
  not obstruct access to safety equipment, exits or the aisles of the
  aircraft.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall allow the passenger entry doors
  of an aircraft to be closed for departure until a crew member has
  verified that all carry-on baggage is stowed in a location that has
  been approved by the Minister in accordance with Chapter 551 of the
  Airworthiness Manual or is restrained by a means that has been
  approved by the Minister in accordance with Chapter 551 of the
  Airworthiness Manual.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} All carry-on baggage shall be safely stowed prior to
  movement of the aircraft on the surface and during take-off, periods
  of in-flight turbulence and landing.

- [(8)]{.lawlabel} No carry-on baggage that may cause injury to
  passengers in the event of turbulence or an emergency shall be stowed
  in an overhead rack unless the rack is equipped with restraining
  devices or doors that have been approved by the Minister in accordance
  with Chapter 551 of the Airworthiness Manual.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/99-158, s. 12
:::

##### [Briefing of Passengers]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999086 .Subheading}

- **[[705.43]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.43
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall ensure that
  passengers are given a safety briefing in accordance with the
  Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall ensure that the safety briefing
  referred to in subsection (1) is given in English and French.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If the safety briefing referred to in subsection (1)
  is insufficient for a passenger because of that passenger's physical,
  sensory or comprehension limitations, seat orientation or
  responsibility for another person on board the aircraft, the air
  operator shall ensure that the passenger is given an individual safety
  briefing that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is appropriate to the passenger's needs; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} meets the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall ensure that, in the event of an
  emergency and where time and circumstances permit, all passengers are
  given an emergency briefing in accordance with the Commercial Air
  Service Standards.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall ensure that each passenger who
  is seated next to a window emergency exit is informed by a crew member
  that the window is an emergency exit and is made aware of how to
  operate that exit.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-152, s. 20
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-705.43-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 705.43"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Safety Features Card and Supplemental Briefing Card]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999097 .Subheading}

- **[[705.44]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.44
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall provide each
  passenger, at the passenger's seat, with a safety features card
  containing, in pictographic form, the information required for a
  safety features card by section 725.44 of Standard 725 --- Airline
  Operations --- Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service Standards, and
  any wording shall be in English and French.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall ensure that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the information required for a supplemental
    briefing card by section 725.44 of Standard 725 --- Airline
    Operations --- Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service Standards is
    available to passengers in the following four formats:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} English text in 14-point or larger sans-serif
      type with dark characters on a light background,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} French text in 14-point or larger sans-serif
      type with dark characters on a light background,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} English braille as defined and set out in the
      publication entitled English Braille, American Edition, 1994,
      published in 1994 or later by the Braille Authority of North
      America, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} French braille as set out in the Code braille
      français uniformisé pour la transcription des textes imprimés
      (CBFU), Quebec Edition (2008); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} two copies in each format are on board every
    aircraft.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The four formats may be displayed on one or more
  supplemental briefing cards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-152, s. 21
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-705.44-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 705.44"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Closing and Locking of Flight Deck Door]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999110 .Subheading}

- **[[705.45]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.45
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), after May
  1, 2002, the pilot-in-command of an aeroplane that is equipped with a
  flight deck door shall ensure that at all times from the moment the
  passenger entry doors are closed in preparation for departure until
  they are opened on arrival,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aeroplane referred to in
    subsection 705.80(1), the flight deck door is closed and locked
    using the locking device required by subsection 705.80(2); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of any other aeroplane,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the flight deck door is closed, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if the door is equipped with a locking device,
      it is locked.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply if a Department of
  Transport air carrier inspector, a crew member or a person authorized
  under subsection 705.27(4) to access the flight deck is required to
  enter or leave the flight deck

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} for the performance of their duties;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} for physiological needs; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} for an overriding concern related to the safety of
    the flight.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} In all cases, persons entering or leaving the flight
  deck must comply with the procedures for opening, closing and locking
  flight deck doors set out in the company operations manual.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-135, s. 2
- SOR/2003-121, s. 3

  ajax-after="1252615-1257219.html"}
:::

Version](section-705.45-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 705.45"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Night VFR Flight --- Aeroplane]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999124 .Subheading}

**[[705.46]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.46 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aeroplane in night VFR flight unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the flight is conducted within 25 nautical miles of
  the departure aerodrome; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an IFR flight, the pilot-in-command
  establishes visual contact with the intended aerodrome of landing and
  receives an authorization from the appropriate ATC unit to conduct a
  visual approach or such an authorization is relayed to the pilot by an
  FS unit.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2003-348, s. 1
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 16](#1522550-1525218){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522550-1525218.html"}
:::

##### [Instrument Approach Procedures]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999130 .Subheading}

- **[[705.47]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.47
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a CAT II or
  CAT III precision approach unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator is authorized to do so in its air
    operator certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the approach is conducted in accordance with the
    Manual of All Weather Operations (Categories II and III).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall terminate an instrument approach with
  a landing unless, immediately prior to landing, the pilot-in-command
  ascertains, by means of radiocommunication or visual inspection,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the condition of the runway or surface of intended
    landing; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the wind direction and speed.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-199, s. 21
:::

##### [Approach Bans --- Non-precision, APV and CAT I Precision]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999140 .Subheading}

- **[[705.48]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.48
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsections (2)
  to (4), the visibility with respect to an aeroplane is less than the
  minimum visibility required for a non-precision approach, an APV or a
  CAT I precision approach if, in respect of the advisory visibility
  specified in the Canada Air Pilot and set out in column I of an item
  in the table to this section,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where the RVR is measured by RVR "A" and RVR "B",
    the RVR measured by RVR "A" for the runway of intended approach is
    less than the visibility set out in column II of the item for the
    approach conducted;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the RVR is measured by only one of RVR "A"
    and RVR "B", the RVR for the runway of intended approach is less
    than the visibility set out in column II of the item for the
    approach conducted;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} where no RVR for the runway of intended approach is
    available, the runway visibility is less than the visibility set out
    in column II of the item for the approach conducted; or

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} where the aerodrome is located south of the 60th
    parallel of north latitude and no RVR or runway visibility for the
    runway of intended approach is available, the ground visibility at
    the aerodrome where the runway is located is less than the
    visibility set out in column II of the item for the approach
    conducted.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall continue a non-precision approach or
  an APV unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator is authorized to do so in its air
    operator certificate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane is equipped with

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} if the flight crew does not use
      pilot-monitored-approach procedures, an autopilot capable of
      conducting a non-precision approach or an APV to 400 feet AGL or
      lower, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a HUD capable of conducting a non-precision
      approach or an APV to 400 feet AGL or lower;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the instrument approach procedure is conducted to
    straight-in minima; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a visibility report indicates that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the visibility is equal to or greater than that
      set out in subsection (1),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the RVR is varying between distances less than
      and greater than the minimum RVR set out in subsection (1), or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the visibility is less than the minimum
      visibility set out in subsection (1) and, at the time the
      visibility report is received, the aeroplane has passed the FAF
      inbound or, where there is no FAF, the point where the final
      approach course is intercepted.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} No person shall continue an SCDA non-precision
  approach unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator is authorized to do so in its air
    operator certificate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane is equipped with

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} if the flight crew does not use
      pilot-monitored-approach procedures, an autopilot capable of
      conducting a non-precision approach to 400 feet AGL or lower, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a HUD capable of conducting a non-precision
      approach to 400 feet AGL or lower;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the instrument approach procedure is conducted to
    straight-in minima with a final approach course that meets the
    requirements of section 725.48 of Standard 725 --- Airline
    Operations --- Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service Standards;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the final approach segment is conducted using a
    stabilized descent with a planned constant descent angle specified
    in section 725.48 of Standard 725 --- Airline Operations ---
    Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service Standards; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a visibility report indicates that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the visibility is equal to or greater than that
      set out in subsection (1),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the RVR is varying between distances less than
      and greater than the minimum RVR set out in subsection (1), or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the visibility is less than the minimum
      visibility set out in subsection (1) and, at the time the
      visibility report is received, the aeroplane has passed the FAF
      inbound or, where there is no FAF, the point where the final
      approach course is intercepted.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} No person shall continue a CAT I precision approach
  to a runway with centreline lighting or a CAT I precision approach in
  an aeroplane equipped with a HUD unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator is authorized to do so in its air
    operator certificate;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aeroplane not equipped with a
    HUD,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} if the flight crew does not use
      pilot-monitored-approach procedures, the pilot-in-command and the
      second-in-command are qualified to conduct a CAT II precision
      approach,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane is equipped with

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} a flight director and autopilot capable of
        conducting a coupled precision approach to 200 feet AGL or
        lower, or

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} if the flight crew uses
        pilot-monitored-approach procedures, a flight director capable
        of conducting a precision approach to 200 feet AGL or lower, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the runway is equipped with serviceable
      high-intensity approach lighting, high-intensity runway centreline
      lighting and high-intensity runway edge lighting;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aeroplane equipped with a HUD
    capable of conducting a precision approach to 200 feet AGL or lower,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command and the second-in-command
      are qualified to conduct a CAT II precision approach,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane is equipped with a flight director
      and autopilot capable of conducting a coupled precision approach
      to 200 feet AGL or lower, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the runway is equipped with serviceable
      high-intensity approach lighting and high-intensity runway edge
      lighting; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a visibility report indicates that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the visibility is equal to or greater than that
      set out in subsection (1),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the RVR is varying between distances less than
      and greater than the minimum RVR set out in subsection (1), or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the visibility is less than the minimum
      visibility set out in subsection (1) and, at the time the
      visibility report is received, the aeroplane has passed the FAF
      inbound or, where there is no FAF, the point where the final
      approach course is intercepted.

**\[705.49 to 705.53 reserved\]**

#### [Division IV --- Aircraft Performance Operating Limitations]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999194 .Subheading}

##### [Exceptions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999195 .Subheading}

**[[705.54]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.54 .sectionLabel}** A person may
operate an aircraft without complying with the requirements of this
Division if the person

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in an air operator
  certificate; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [General Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999199 .Subheading}

**[[705.55]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.55 .sectionLabel}** Any determination
made for the purposes of sections 705.56 to 705.61 shall be based on
approved performance data set out in the aircraft flight manual.

##### [Take-off Weight Limitations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999201 .Subheading}

- **[[705.56]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.56
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off
  in an aircraft if the weight of the aircraft

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} exceeds the maximum take-off weight specified in
    the aircraft flight manual for the pressure-altitude and the ambient
    temperature at the aerodrome where the take-off is to be made; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} after allowing for planned fuel consumption during
    the flight to the destination aerodrome or alternate aerodrome,
    exceeds the landing weight specified in the aircraft flight manual
    for the pressure-altitude and the ambient temperature at the
    destination aerodrome or alternate aerodrome.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} In the determination of the maximum take-off weight
  referred to in subsection (1) for an aeroplane,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the required accelerate-stop distance shall not
    exceed the accelerate-stop distance available (ASDA);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the required take-off run shall not exceed the
    take-off run available (TORA); and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the required take-off distance shall not exceed the
    take-off distance available (TODA).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (2), the following
  factors shall be taken into account:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the pressure-altitude at the aerodrome;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the ambient temperature;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the runway slope in the direction of take-off; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} not more than 50 per cent of the reported headwind
    component or not less than 150 per cent of the reported tailwind
    component.

##### [Net Take-off Flight Path]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999215 .Subheading}

- **[[705.57]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.57
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off
  in an aeroplane if the weight of the aeroplane is greater than the
  weight specified in the aircraft flight manual as allowing a net
  take-off flight path that clears all obstacles by at least 35 feet
  vertically or at least 200 feet horizontally within the aerodrome
  boundaries, and by at least 300 feet horizontally outside those
  boundaries.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} In the determination of the maximum weight, minimum
  distances and flight path referred to in subsection (1),

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} corrections shall be made for

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the runway to be used,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the runway slope in the direction of take-off,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the pressure-altitude at the aerodrome,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the ambient temperature, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the wind component at the time of take-off, where
      not more than 50 per cent of the reported headwind component or
      not less than 150 per cent of the reported tailwind component is
      considered; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} calculations shall be based on the pilot

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} not banking the aeroplane before reaching an
      altitude of 50 feet,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsection (3), using 15 degrees or
      less of bank at or below 400 feet, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} using no more than 25 degrees of bank
      thereafter, aircraft speed and configuration permitting.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A bank angle greater than the 15 degrees referred to
  in subparagraph (2)(b)(ii) may be used if it is authorized in an air
  operator certificate.

##### [Enroute Limitations with One Engine Inoperative]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999230 .Subheading}

- **[[705.58]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.58
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off
  in an aeroplane if the weight of the aeroplane is greater than the
  weight that will allow the aeroplane to attain, with any engine
  inoperative, a net flight path that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} has a positive slope at 1,000 feet above all
    terrain and obstructions within five nautical miles on either side
    of the intended track, at all points along the route or planned
    diversion therefrom; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} will permit flight from the cruising altitude to an
    aerodrome where the requirements of section 705.60 can be complied
    with, and clears vertically, by at least 2,000 feet, all terrain and
    obstructions within five nautical miles on either side of the
    intended track.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), the following
  factors shall be taken into account after an engine failure:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the effects of wind and temperature on the net
    flight path; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the effects of fuel jettisoning, where the
    jettisoning is conducted in accordance with procedures set out in
    the company operations manual and sufficient fuel remains to
    complete a landing with the required fuel reserves.

- [SOR/2025-98, s. 17(F)](#1522552-1525220){.wb-lbx

:::

##### [Enroute Limitations with Two Engines Inoperative]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999238 .Subheading}

- **[[705.59]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.59
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aeroplane
  having three or more engines unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} all points along the intended track are located at
    a distance that can be flown in 90 minutes or less, with all engines
    operating at cruise power, from an aerodrome where the requirements
    of section 705.60 can be complied with; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the weight of the aeroplane is not greater than the
    weight that, according to the two-engines-inoperative enroute net
    flight path data shown in the aircraft flight manual, will allow the
    aeroplane to clear vertically, by at least 2,000 feet, all terrain
    and obstructions within five nautical miles on either side of the
    intended track, and thereafter to continue flight to an aerodrome
    where the requirements of section 705.60 can be complied with.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of paragraph (1)(b), the following
  factors shall be taken into account after the failure of two engines:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the effects of wind and temperature on the net
    flight path; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the effects of fuel jettisoning, where the
    jettisoning is conducted in accordance with procedures set out in
    the company operations manual and sufficient fuel remains to arrive
    at the destination aerodrome at 1,500 feet AGL with a fuel reserve
    sufficient to fly for 15 minutes thereafter at cruise power.

  ajax-after="1522554-1525222.html"}
:::

##### [Dispatch Limitations: Landing at Destination and Alternate Aerodromes]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999246 .Subheading}

- **[[705.60]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.60
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), no person
  shall dispatch or conduct a take-off in an aeroplane unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the weight of the aeroplane on landing at the
    destination aerodrome will allow a full-stop landing

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a turbo-jet-powered aeroplane,
      within 60 per cent of the landing distance available (LDA), or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a propeller-driven aeroplane,
      within 70 per cent of the landing distance available (LDA); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the weight of the aeroplane on landing at the
    alternate aerodrome will allow a full-stop landing

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a turbo-jet-powered aeroplane,
      within 60 per cent of the landing distance available (LDA), and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a propeller-driven aeroplane,
      within 70 per cent of the landing distance available (LDA).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} In determining whether an aeroplane can be dispatched
  or a take-off can be conducted in accordance with subsection (1), the
  following shall be taken into account:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the pressure-altitude at the destination aerodrome
    and at the alternate aerodrome;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} not more than 50 per cent of the reported headwind
    component or not less than 150 per cent of the reported tailwind
    component; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} that the aeroplane must be landed on a suitable
    runway, considering the wind speed and direction, the ground
    handling characteristics of the aeroplane, and other conditions such
    as landing aids and terrain.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where conditions at the destination aerodrome at the
  time of take-off do not permit compliance with paragraph (2)(c), an
  aeroplane may be dispatched and a take-off conducted if the alternate
  aerodrome designated in the operational flight plan permits, at the
  time of take-off, compliance with paragraph (1)(b) and subsection (2).

##### [Dispatch Limitations: Wet Runway --- Turbo-jet-powered Aeroplanes]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999260 .Subheading}

- **[[705.61]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.61
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), when
  weather reports or forecasts indicate that the runway may be wet at
  the estimated time of arrival, no air operator shall dispatch or
  conduct a take-off in a turbo-jet-powered aeroplane unless the landing
  distance available (LDA) at the destination aerodrome is at least 115
  per cent of the landing distance required pursuant to paragraph
  705.60(1)(a).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The landing distance available on a wet runway may be
  shorter than that required by subsection (1), but not shorter than
  that required by section 705.60, if the aircraft flight manual
  includes specific information about landing distances on wet runways.

**\[705.62 to 705.66 reserved\]**

#### [Division V --- Aircraft Equipment Requirements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999265 .Subheading}

##### [General Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999266 .Subheading}

**[[705.67]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.67 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft unless the aircraft is equipped with

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} two independent static pressure systems;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a windshield wiper or rain removal system for each
  pilot station;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} heating or de-icing equipment for each carburetor or
  an alternate air source for each pressure carburetor or fuel injection
  system;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a placard on each door that provides passenger access
  to a passenger emergency exit, stating that the door must be secured
  or locked open during take-off and landing; and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} a means for the crew, in an emergency, to unlock each
  door that leads to a compartment that is normally accessible to
  passengers and that can be locked by passengers.

##### [Landing Lights]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999273 .Subheading}

**[[705.68]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.68 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft at night unless the aircraft is equipped with at
least two landing lights.

##### [Operation of Aircraft in Icing Conditions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999275 .Subheading}

- **[[705.69]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.69
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} When icing conditions are reported
  to exist or are forecast to be encountered along the route of flight,
  no person shall authorize a flight or its continuation or conduct a
  take-off or continue a flight in an aircraft, even if the
  pilot-in-command determines that the aircraft is adequately equipped
  to operate in icing conditions in accordance with paragraph 605.30(a),
  if, in the opinion of the pilot-in-command, the safety of the flight
  might be adversely affected.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aeroplane in icing
  conditions at night unless the aeroplane is equipped with a means to
  illuminate or otherwise detect the formation of ice.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-152, s. 22
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-705.69-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 705.69"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Weather Radar Equipment]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999281 .Subheading}

**[[705.70]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.70 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft with passengers on board in IMC when current weather
reports or forecasts indicate that thunderstorms may reasonably be
expected along the route to be flown, unless the aircraft is equipped
with weather radar equipment.

##### [Protective Breathing Equipment]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999283 .Subheading}

- **[[705.71]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.71
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall operate a
  pressurized aircraft unless, at each station listed in paragraph
  (3)(b), protective breathing equipment with a 15-minute supply of
  breathing gas at a pressure-altitude of 8,000 feet is provided in
  accordance with this section.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The protective breathing equipment referred to in
  subsection (1) may be used to meet the crew member oxygen requirements
  specified in section 605.31.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Protective breathing equipment shall be conveniently
  located and readily available

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} with a fixed or portable breathing gas supply for
    use by each flight crew member on the flight deck; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} with a portable breathing gas supply for use by
    crew members in combatting fires, as follows:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} one unit for use in each Class A, B and E cargo
      compartment that is accessible to crew members in the cabin during
      flight,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} one unit for each hand-held fire extinguisher
      located in each isolated galley,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} one unit on the flight deck,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} one unit located within one metre of each
      hand-held fire extinguisher required in the passenger compartment
      by section 705.93, except if the Minister has authorized the
      location of protective breathing equipment more than one metre
      from each hand-held fire extinguisher where special circumstances
      exist that make compliance with this subparagraph impractical and
      that location provides an equivalent level of safety, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the number of units of protective breathing
      equipment used to satisfy the requirements of this paragraph shall
      not be less than the number of flight attendants required for the
      flight.

##### [First Aid Oxygen]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999295 .Subheading}

**[[705.72]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.72 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate a pressurized aircraft with passengers on board unless the
aircraft is equipped with oxygen dispensing units and an undiluted
supply of first aid oxygen sufficient to provide two per cent of the
occupants, and in any case at least one person, with oxygen for one hour
or the entire duration of the flight at a cabin pressure-altitude above
8,000 feet, after an emergency descent following cabin depressurization,
whichever period is longer.

##### [Interphone System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999297 .Subheading}

**[[705.73]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.73 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft unless the aircraft is equipped with an interphone
system that can be operated independently of the public address system
required by section 705.74, except for handsets, headsets, microphones,
selector switches and signalling devices.

##### [Public Address System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999299 .Subheading}

**[[705.74]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.74 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft with passengers on board unless the aircraft is
equipped with a public address system that can be operated independently
of the interphone system required by section 705.73, except for
handsets, headsets, microphones, selector switches and signalling
devices.

##### [Crew Member Shoulder Harnesses]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999301 .Subheading}

**[[705.75]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.75 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft unless each pilot seat and the seat for each flight
attendant required under section 705.201 is equipped with a safety belt
that includes dual upper torso straps with a single-point release.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 16
:::

[Previous
Version](section-705.75-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 705.75"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Lavatory Fire Protection]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999305 .Subheading}

**[[705.76]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.76 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} each lavatory in the aircraft is equipped with a
  smoke detector system or equivalent that provides

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a warning light in the cockpit, or

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a warning light or audible warning in the
    passenger compartment that can be readily detected by a flight
    attendant, taking into consideration the positioning of flight
    attendants throughout the passenger compartment during the flight;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} each lavatory in the aircraft is equipped with a
  built-in fire extinguisher for each waste disposal receptacle that is
  installed in the lavatory, and each extinguisher is designed to
  discharge automatically into the disposal receptacle on the occurrence
  of a fire in that receptacle;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a readily visible sign that clearly displays a symbol
  indicating that smoking is prohibited or the words "No Smoking" and
  "Défense de fumer" is installed above the door handle on both sides of
  the door to each lavatory in the aircraft;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a readily visible sign that clearly displays a symbol
  indicating that cigarette disposal is prohibited or the words "No
  Cigarette Disposal" and "Défense de jeter des cigarettes" is installed
  adjacent to the opening of each waste disposal receptacle that is
  located in a lavatory in the aircraft; and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} a self-contained, removable ashtray is installed on
  or near the outside of the door to each lavatory in the aircraft or in
  some other location or locations where it is readily visible to the
  users of each lavatory from outside the lavatory.

##### [Flammability Requirements for Aeroplane Seat Cushions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999314 .Subheading}

**[[705.77]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.77 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aeroplane for which an initial type certificate was issued
after January 1, 1958 unless all passenger compartment seat cushions
meet the standards respecting the fire protection of seat cushions set
out in Chapter 525 of the Airworthiness Manual.

##### [Floor Proximity Emergency Escape Path Markings]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999316 .Subheading}

**[[705.78]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.78 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate, with passengers on board, an aeroplane for which an initial
type certificate was issued after January 1, 1958 unless the aeroplane
is provided with floor proximity emergency escape path markings that
meet the standards set out in Chapter 525 of the Airworthiness Manual.

##### [Flashlight Stowage]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999318 .Subheading}

**[[705.79]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.79 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft unless it is equipped with flashlight stowage
provisions that are accessible from each required flight attendant seat.

##### [Doors and Locks]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999320 .Subheading}

- **[[705.80]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.80
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (3) and (4),
  no person shall operate an aeroplane in respect of which an initial
  type certificate was issued after January 1, 1958 unless the aeroplane
  is equipped with

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a passenger-carrying aeroplane,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a door between the flight deck and the passenger
      compartment, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if the aeroplane is equipped with a crew rest
      facility having an entry from the flight deck and a separate entry
      from the passenger compartment, a door between the crew rest
      facility and the passenger compartment; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an all-cargo aeroplane that was
    equipped with a flight deck door on January 15, 2002,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a door between the flight deck and a compartment
      occupied by a person, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} if the aeroplane is equipped with a crew rest
      facility having an entry from the flight deck and a separate entry
      from a compartment occupied by a person, a door between the crew
      rest facility and the compartment.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The doors required by subsection (1) shall be
  equipped with a locking device that can be unlocked only from inside
  the flight deck or the crew rest facility, as the case may be.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A key shall be readily available to each crew member
  for each door that separates a passenger compartment or a compartment
  occupied by a person from an emergency exit, with the exception of a
  door required by subsection (1).

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} No crew member, except a flight crew member, shall
  have a key to a door required by subsection (1) at any time from the
  moment the passenger entry doors are closed in preparation for
  departure until they are opened on arrival unless the locking device
  required by subsection (2) is installed and locked.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aeroplane that is required
  by subsection (1) to be equipped with a door unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} each door meets the design requirements of section
    525.795 of the Airworthiness Manual in effect on May 1, 2002; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the locking device required by subsection (2) and
    any other system used to control access to the flight deck can be
    operated from each flight crew member position.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-135, s. 3
- SOR/2003-121, s. 4
:::

##### [Cargo and Baggage Compartment Fire Protection]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999337 .Subheading}

**[[705.81]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.81 .sectionLabel}** After June 1,
2004, no person shall operate a transport category aeroplane in respect
of which an initial type certificate was issued after January 1, 1958
unless each cargo or baggage compartment of the aeroplane meets the
requirements set out in section 725.81 of Standard 725 --- Airline
Operations --- Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service Standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2003-361, s. 1
:::

##### [Pitot Heat Indication System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999341 .Subheading}

**[[705.82]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.82 .sectionLabel}** After June 30,
2008, no person shall conduct a take-off in a transport category
aeroplane, or in a non-transport category aeroplane in respect of which
a type certificate was issued after December 31, 1964, that is equipped
with a flight instrument Pitot heating system unless the aeroplane is
also equipped with a Pitot heat indication system that meets the
requirements of section 525.1326 of Chapter 525 --- Transport Category
Aeroplanes of the Airworthiness Manual.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-78, s. 3
:::

##### [ACAS]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999345 .Subheading}

- **[[705.83]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.83
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), no air
  operator shall operate a turbine-powered aeroplane in airspace outside
  RVSM airspace unless the aeroplane is equipped with an operative ACAS
  that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements of CAN-TSO-C119a or a more
    recent version of it or other requirements that the Minister has
    accepted as providing a level of safety that is at least equivalent
    to the level that that CAN-TSO provides; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is equipped with a Mode S transponder that meets
    the requirements of CAN-TSO-C112 or a more recent version of it.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), no air operator shall
  operate an aeroplane that is not a turbine-powered aeroplane in
  airspace outside RVSM airspace unless the aeroplane is equipped with
  an operative ACAS that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements of CAN-TSO-C118 or a more
    recent version of it or other requirements that the Minister has
    accepted as providing a level of safety that is at least equivalent
    to the level that that CAN-TSO provides; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements of CAN-TSO-C119a or a more
    recent version of it or other requirements that the Minister has
    accepted as providing a level of safety that is at least equivalent
    to the level that that CAN-TSO provides and is equipped with a Mode
    S transponder that meets the requirements of CAN-TSO-C112 or a more
    recent version of it.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (4), no air operator shall
  operate an aeroplane referred to in subsection (1) or (2) in RVSM
  airspace unless the aeroplane is equipped with an operative ACAS that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements of CAN-TSO-C119b or a more
    recent version of it or other requirements that the Minister has
    accepted as providing a level of safety that is at least equivalent
    to the level that that CAN-TSO provides; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is equipped with a Mode S transponder that meets
    the requirements of CAN-TSO-C112 or a more recent version of it.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The air operator may operate the aeroplane without
  its being equipped with an operative ACAS if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} where a minimum equipment list has not been
    approved by the Minister and subject to subsection 605.08(1), the
    operation takes place within the three days after the date of
    failure of the ACAS; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} it is necessary for the pilot-in-command to
    deactivate, in the interests of aviation safety, the ACAS or any of
    its modes and the pilot-in-command does so in accordance with the
    aircraft flight manual, aircraft operating manual, flight manual
    supplement or minimum equipment list.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} This section does not apply in respect of aeroplanes
  manufactured on or before the day on which this section comes into
  force until two years after that day.

##### [TAWS]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999362 .Subheading}

- **[[705.84]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.84
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no air
  operator shall operate an aeroplane unless the aeroplane is equipped
  with an operative TAWS that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements for Class A equipment set
    out in CAN-TSO-C151a or a more recent version of it;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} meets the altitude accuracy requirements set out in
    section 551.102 of Chapter 551 of the Airworthiness Manual; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} has a terrain and airport database compatible with
    the area of operation and a terrain awareness and situational
    display.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The air operator may operate the aeroplane without
  its being equipped with an operative TAWS if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the event that a minimum equipment list has not
    been approved by the Minister and subject to subsection 605.08(1),
    the operation takes place within the three days after the day on
    which the failure of the TAWS occurs; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} it is necessary for the pilot-in-command to
    deactivate, in the interests of aviation safety, the TAWS or any of
    its modes and the pilot-in-command does so in accordance with the
    aircraft flight manual, aircraft operating manual, flight manual
    supplement or minimum equipment list.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} This section does not apply in respect of aeroplanes
  manufactured on or before the day on which this section comes into
  force until the day that is two years after that day.

- SOR/2012-136, s. 13

#### [Division VI --- Emergency Equipment]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999375 .Subheading}

##### [Megaphones]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999376 .Subheading}

**[[705.89]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.89 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate, with passengers on board, an aeroplane for which a type
certificate has been issued authorizing the transport of 60 or more
passengers, unless the following number of portable battery-powered
megaphones are carried on board the aeroplane and are conveniently
located and readily available for use by the flight attendants:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} for each passenger deck, at least one megaphone;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} 61 to 99 passenger seats, one megaphone; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} 100 or more passenger seats, two megaphones.

##### [First Aid Kits]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999381 .Subheading}

- **[[705.90]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.90
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off
  in an aircraft operated by an air operator that is configured as
  follows unless, for the purposes of paragraph 602.60(1)(h), the
  corresponding number of first aid kits is carried on board and each
  kit contains the supplies and equipment set out in the [Aviation
  Occupational Health and Safety
  Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-2011-87):

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} configured for 0 to 50 passenger seats, one kit;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} configured for 51 to 150 passenger seats, two kits;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} configured for 151 to 250 passenger seats, three
    kits; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} configured for 251 or more passenger seats, four
    kits.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall conduct a take-off in an aircraft
  operated by an air operator unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the first aid kits referred to in subsection (1)
    are distributed throughout the cabin and are readily available to
    crew members and passengers;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} each first aid kit is clearly identified; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if a first aid kit is stowed in a bin or
    compartment, the bin or compartment is clearly marked as containing
    a first aid kit.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-253, s. 18](#1274680-1276961){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1274680-1276961.html"}
:::

##### [Emergency Medical Kit]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999395 .Subheading}

**[[705.91]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.91 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft that has a seating configuration, excluding crew
seats, of more than 100 unless an emergency medical kit that meets the
Commercial Air Service Standards is carried on board the aircraft.

##### [Crash Axe]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999397 .Subheading}

**[[705.92]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.92 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft unless a crash axe is carried on board the aircraft.

##### [Hand-held Fire Extinguishers]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999399 .Subheading}

- **[[705.93]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.93
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate an aircraft
  unless hand-held fire extinguishers for use in the flight deck,
  passenger compartment and cargo compartment are carried on board the
  aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The type and quantity of extinguishing agent shall be
  suitable for extinguishing fires that are likely to occur in the
  flight deck, passenger compartment or cargo compartment where the
  extinguisher is intended to be used and, in the case of the
  extinguishing agent for extinguishers intended to be used in the
  passenger compartment, shall be designed to minimize the hazard of
  toxic gas concentrations.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} At least one hand-held fire extinguisher shall be
  conveniently located and readily available for immediate use in each
  class E cargo compartment that is accessible to crew members during
  flight, and at least one hand-held fire extinguisher shall be located
  in each isolated galley.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} At least one hand-held fire extinguisher shall be
  conveniently located on the flight deck and readily available for
  immediate use by the flight crew members.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The following number of hand-held fire extinguishers
  shall be conveniently located, readily available for immediate use and
  uniformly distributed throughout the passenger compartment on each
  deck:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 60 or fewer passenger seats, two extinguishers;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 61 to 200 passenger seats, three extinguishers;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} 201 or more passenger seats, one extra extinguisher
    for each additional unit of 100 passenger seats.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} At least two hand-held fire extinguishers shall
  contain Halon 1211 (bromochlorodifluoromethane) or its equivalent.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} A stowage compartment or stowage container that
  contains a hand-held fire extinguisher shall be clearly marked as to
  its contents.

##### [Portable Oxygen]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999411 .Subheading}

**[[705.94]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.94 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate a pressurized aircraft above FL 250 unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} there is readily available to each flight attendant
  on board portable oxygen equipment with a 15-minute supply of oxygen;
  or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} sufficient portable oxygen units with masks, or spare
  outlets and masks, to ensure an immediate supply of oxygen to each
  flight attendant are distributed throughout the cabin.

##### [Survival Equipment]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999415 .Subheading}

- **[[705.95]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.95
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall operate an
  aircraft, other than an aircraft referred to in subsection 602.61(2),
  unless a survival manual is carried on board that contains information
  about how to use the survival equipment that is carried on board to
  meet the requirements of subsection 602.61(1).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall operate an aircraft on board of
  which life rafts are required to be carried in accordance with section
  602.63 unless the survival kit referred to in paragraph 602.63(6)(c)
  contains

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a life raft repair kit;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a bailing bucket and a sponge;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a whistle;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a waterproof flashlight;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a supply of potable water --- based on 500 mL per
    person and calculated using the rated capacity of the life raft ---
    or a means of desalting or distilling salt water that can provide
    500 mL of potable water per person;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a waterproof survival manual that contains
    information about how to use the survival equipment;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a first aid kit that contains antiseptic swabs,
    burn dressing compresses, bandages and motion sickness pills; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} a pyrotechnic signalling device, or an aviation
    visual distress signal that has a marking applied by the
    manufacturer indicating that the signal meets the requirements of
    CAN-TSO-C168, a signalling mirror and a dye marker for visually
    signalling distress.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (2), if there is insufficient
  space in the attached survival kit, a supplemental survival kit shall
  be stowed adjacent to each required life raft and contain

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a supply of potable water --- based on 500 mL per
    person and calculated using the rated capacity of the life raft ---
    or a means of desalting or distilling salt water that can provide
    500 mL of potable water per person; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} motion sickness pills.

##### [Inspection Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999417 .Subheading}

**[[705.96]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.96 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an aircraft unless the emergency equipment carried on
board under Division II of Subpart 2 of Part VI and this Division is
inspected at the intervals recommended by the equipment manufacturer.

**[[705.97]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.97 .sectionLabel}** Each flight
attendant required under section 705.201 shall have a flashlight readily
available for use.

#### [Division VII --- Personnel Requirements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999424 .Subheading}

##### [Designation of Pilot-in-command and Second-in-command]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999425 .Subheading}

- **[[705.103]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.103
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator must designate, for
  each flight, a pilot-in-command and a second-in-command.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator must record the name of the
  pilot-in-command and, if applicable, the name of the second-in-command
  who were designated under subsection (1) and must retain the record
  for at least 180 days after the day on which the flight is completed.

**[[705.105]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.105 .sectionLabel}** \[Reserved,
SOR/2015-127, s. 18\]

##### [Pilot Qualifications]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999429 .Subheading}

- **[[705.106]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.106
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), no air
  operator shall permit a person to act and no person shall act as the
  pilot-in-command, second-in-command or cruise relief pilot of an
  aircraft unless the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} holds the licence, ratings and endorsements
    required by Part IV;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} within the previous 90 days,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} has completed at least three take-offs and three
      landings as the pilot at the controls and one sector assigned to
      duty as a flight crew member in an aircraft of that type,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} has completed five sectors assigned to duty as a
      flight crew member in an aircraft of that type, or

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} has fulfilled the training requirements set out
      in the Commercial Air Service Standards;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} has successfully completed a pilot proficiency
    check, the validity period of which has not expired, for that type
    of aircraft, in accordance with the Commercial Air Service
    Standards;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} has successfully completed or is undergoing a line
    check or line indoctrination training, the validity period of which
    has not expired, for that type of aircraft, in accordance with the
    Commercial Air Service Standards; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} has fulfilled the requirements of the air
    operator's training program.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A pilot who does not meet the requirements of
  subparagraph (1)(b)(i) or (ii) shall regain competency in accordance
  with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may permit a person to act and a
  person may act as the pilot-in-command or second-in-command of an
  aircraft where the person does not meet the requirements of subsection
  (1), if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is operated on a training, ferry or
    positioning flight; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} is authorized to do so in its air operator
      certificate, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} complies with the Commercial Air Service
      Standards.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} A pilot shall, on successful completion of a pilot
  proficiency check, meet the requirements of the consolidation period
  in accordance with the Commercial Air Service Standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-26, s. 44(F)](#1511765-1516325){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1511765-1516325.html"}
:::

##### [Flight Engineer and Second Officer Qualifications]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999447 .Subheading}

- **[[705.107]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.107
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no air
  operator shall permit a person to act and no person shall act as a
  flight engineer or a second officer on board an aircraft unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person holds the licence and endorsements
    required by Part IV;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator has determined, by means of a
    check in flight or in a flight simulator that has been approved by
    the Minister under Subpart 6 of Part VI, that the person meets the
    Commercial Air Service Standards for that type of aircraft, or the
    person has, within the previous six months, completed at least 50
    hours of flight time as a flight engineer on an aircraft of that
    type;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the person has successfully completed or is
    undergoing line indoctrination training for that type of aircraft,
    in accordance with the Commercial Air Service Standards; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the person has fulfilled the requirements of the
    air operator's training program.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who is qualified to act as a
  pilot-in-command or a second-in-command in accordance with section
  705.106 may act as a second officer on board an aircraft during the
  cruise portion of a flight, if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person has received initial and annual
    recurrent training in normal and emergency procedures pertaining to
    the cruise portion of the flight, in accordance with the Commercial
    Air Service Standards; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air operator has determined, by means of a
    check, that the person meets the Commercial Air Service Standards
    for that type of aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-26, s. 45(F)](#1511767-1516327){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1511767-1516327.html"}
:::

##### [Crew Pairing]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999457 .Subheading}

**[[705.108]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.108 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall assign a pilot-in-command and a second-in-command to an aircraft
unless their combined experience on that type of aircraft meets the
Commercial Air Service Standards.

##### [Flight Attendant Qualifications]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999459 .Subheading}

- **[[705.109]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.109
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall permit a
  person to act and no person shall act as a flight attendant on board
  an aircraft unless the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} has successfully completed the air operator's
    training program, except that a person may act as a flight attendant
    while undergoing line indoctrination training if the person is
    carried in addition to the number of flight attendants required
    under section 705.201 and is under the supervision of a flight
    attendant;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} has successfully completed line indoctrination
    training within 90 days after completing the air operator's training
    program or has regained competency in accordance with the Flight
    Attendant Training Standard; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} holds a certificate or certification in first aid
    in accordance with the [Aviation Occupational Health and Safety
    Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-2011-87).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who has not completed line indoctrination
  training within the period specified in paragraph (1)(b) shall
  requalify in accordance with the Flight Attendant Training Standard.

##### [Flight Dispatcher Qualifications]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999467 .Subheading}

- **[[705.110]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.110
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall permit a
  person to act and no person shall act as a flight dispatcher unless
  the person has fulfilled the requirements of the air operator's
  training program and, after June 1, 1998, holds a flight dispatcher
  certificate.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall notify the Minister whenever a
  flight dispatcher certificate is issued or becomes invalid.

##### [Route and Aerodrome Qualifications]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999471 .Subheading}

**[[705.111]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.111 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall permit a person to act and no person shall act as the
pilot-in-command of an aircraft on a flight along a route or into an
aerodrome unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} within the previous 12 months, the person has acted
  as a flight crew member or has been on the flight deck as an observer
  on a flight along that route and into that aerodrome; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person has received training and demonstrated
  adequate knowledge, in accordance with the Commercial Air Service
  Standards.

##### [Check Authority]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999475 .Subheading}

- **[[705.112]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.112
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A pilot proficiency check shall be
  conducted by the Minister.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Any other check required under this Subpart may be
  conducted by the Minister.

##### [Validity Period]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999479 .Subheading}

- **[[705.113]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.113
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (4) and (5),
  the validity period of a line check and of the training referred to in
  section 705.124 expires on the first day of the thirteenth month
  following the month in which the check or training was completed.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (4) and (5), the validity
  period of a pilot proficiency check expires

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} on the first day of the seventh month following the
    month in which the check was completed;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} on the first day of the thirteenth month following
    the month in which the check was completed, where the pilot
    successfully completes the six-month recurrency training that has
    been approved by the Minister, in accordance with the Commercial Air
    Service Standards, as a substitute for the pilot proficiency check
    and that is identified in the company operations manual; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} at the end of the validation period, where the air
    operator has an operations specification authorizing an advanced
    qualification program in accordance with the Commercial Air Service
    Standards and the pilot completes a proficiency evaluation within
    the evaluation period authorized for the air operator in the
    operations specification.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The validity period of a flight dispatcher competency
  check expires on the first day of the thirteenth month following the
  month in which the check was completed.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where a pilot proficiency check, a flight dispatcher
  competency check, a line check or training is renewed within the last
  90 days of its validity period, its validity period is extended by six
  or 12 months, as appropriate.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may extend the validity period of a
  pilot proficiency check, a flight dispatcher competency check, a line
  check or any training by up to 60 days where the Minister is of the
  opinion that aviation safety is not likely to be affected.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (7), where the validity period
  of a pilot proficiency check, a line check, or annual or semi-annual
  training has been expired for 24 months or more, the person shall
  requalify by meeting the training requirements specified in the
  Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} Where the validity period of a flight dispatcher
  competency check or annual training has been expired for 12 months or
  more, the person shall requalify by meeting the training requirements
  specified in the Commercial Air Service Standards.

**\[705.114 to 705.123 reserved\]**

#### [Division VIII --- Training]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999492 .Subheading}

##### [Training Program]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999493 .Subheading}

- **[[705.124]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.124
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every air operator shall establish
  and maintain a training program that is

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} designed to ensure that each person who receives
    training acquires the competence to perform the person's assigned
    duties; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} approved by the Minister in accordance with the
    Commercial Air Service Standards and, in respect of flight
    attendants, in accordance with the Commercial Air Service Standards
    and the Flight Attendant Training Standard.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator's training program shall include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} for flight crew members:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} company indoctrination training,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} line indoctrination training,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} upgrading training, where applicable, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} initial and annual training, including

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} aircraft type training,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} aircraft servicing and ground handling
        training,

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} emergency procedures training, and

      - [(D)]{.lawlabel} aircraft surface contamination training;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} for flight attendants:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} aviation indoctrination,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} line indoctrination training,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} in-charge training, where applicable, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} initial and annual training, including

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} safety procedures training,

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} aircraft type training,

      - [(C)]{.lawlabel} emergency procedures training, and

      - [(D)]{.lawlabel} aircraft surface contamination training;

      - [(E)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2020-253, s. 21\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} for flight dispatchers:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} initial and annual aircraft type training,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} on-the-job training, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} aircraft cockpit familiarization training;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} initial and annual aircraft surface contamination
    training for those operations personnel designated in the Commercial
    Air Service Standards; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} any other training required to ensure a safe
    operation under this Subpart.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} include a detailed syllabus of its training program
    in its company operations manual;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} ensure that adequate facilities and qualified
    personnel are provided for its training program, in accordance with
    the Commercial Air Service Standards; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} establish and maintain a safety awareness program
    concerning the adverse effects of aircraft surface contamination and
    provide the program to all flight operations personnel who are not
    required to undergo the training described in paragraph (2)(d).

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall have a fatigue management
  training program for its flight crew members that contains

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} personal fatigue management strategies relating to

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} sleep hygiene,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} lifestyle, exercise and diet, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the consumption of alcohol and drugs;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the impact of fatigue on aviation safety;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} sleep requirements and the science relating to
    fatigue;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the causes and consequences of fatigue;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} how to recognize fatigue in themselves and in
    others;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} sleep disorders, their impact on aviation safety
    and treatment options; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} human and organizational factors that may cause
    fatigue, including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} sleep quality and duration,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the impact of shift work and overtime,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the circadian rhythm, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the effects of changes of time zones.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-269, s. 17
- [SOR/2020-253, s. 21](#1274686-1276935){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1274686-1276935.html"}

##### [Conditional Approval of Training Program]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999545 .Subheading}

- **[[705.125]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.125
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may give conditional
  approval to a training program where an air operator submits to the
  Minister a copy of a syllabus of its training program that provides
  enough information for a preliminary evaluation of the training
  program in light of the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may conduct training under a training
  program that has received conditional approval until the Minister has
  evaluated the effectiveness of the training program and has informed
  the air operator of any deficiencies that must be corrected.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall give final approval to a
  conditionally approved training program when the air operator
  demonstrates that the training conducted under that program is
  adequate to permit the persons who receive it to safely perform their
  assigned duties and when any identified deficiencies have been
  corrected.

##### [Cabin Emergency Evacuation Trainer]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999550 .Subheading}

**[[705.126]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.126 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
may conduct emergency training and testing on a cabin emergency
evacuation trainer, rather than on an aircraft, if the trainer has been
approved by the Minister in accordance with the Commercial Air Service
Standards.

##### [Training and Qualification Records]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999552 .Subheading}

- **[[705.127]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.127
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every air operator shall, for each
  person who is required to receive training under this Subpart,
  establish and maintain a record of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person's name and, where applicable, personnel
    licence number, type and ratings;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, the person's medical category and
    the expiry date of that category;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the dates on which the person, while in the air
    operator's employ, successfully completed any training, pilot
    proficiency check or examination required under this Subpart or
    obtained any qualification required under this Subpart;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} information relating to any failure of the person,
    while in the air operator's employ, to successfully complete any
    training, pilot proficiency check or examination required under this
    Subpart or to obtain any qualification required under this Subpart;
    and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the type of aircraft or flight training equipment
    used for any training, pilot proficiency check, line check or
    qualification required under this Subpart.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall retain the records referred to
  in paragraphs (1)(c) and (d) and a record of each pilot proficiency
  check for at least three years.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall keep a master copy of each
  examination on file and make it available for review by the Minister
  for a period of not less than three years.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-152, s. 23
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-705.127-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 705.127"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Amendments to Training Program]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1339549 .Subheading}

- **[[705.128]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.128
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If the Minister determines that an
  air operator's training program required under 705.124 does not
  include the competencies required for each person who receives
  training to perform their assigned duties, the Minister shall notify
  the air operator of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the corrective actions that the air operator is
    required to implement to its training program; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the date by which the air operator is required to
    submit its amended training program to the Minister for approval
    under paragraph 705.124(1)(b).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The air operator referred to in subsection (1) shall
  submit its amended training program to the Minister on or before the
  date specified by the Minister under paragraph (1)(b).

- [SOR/2022-17, s. 6](#1339263-1339556){.wb-lbx
