**\[705.129 to 705.133 reserved\]**

#### [Division IX --- Manuals]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999565 .Subheading}

##### [Requirements relating to Company Operations Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999566 .Subheading}

- **[[705.134]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.134
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every air operator shall establish
  and maintain a company operations manual that meets the requirements
  of section 705.135.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall submit its company operations
  manual, and any amendments to that manual, to the Minister.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where there is a change in any aspect of an air
  operator's operation or where the company operations manual no longer
  meets the Commercial Air Service Standards, the air operator shall
  amend its company operations manual.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall, where the Commercial Air Service
  Standards are met, approve those parts of a company operations manual,
  and any amendments to those parts, that relate to the information
  required by section 705.135.

##### [Contents of Company Operations Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999572 .Subheading}

- **[[705.135]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.135
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A company operations manual, which
  may be issued in separate parts corresponding to specific aspects of
  an operation, shall include the instructions and information necessary
  to enable the personnel concerned to perform their duties safely and
  shall contain the information required by the Commercial Air Service
  Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A company operations manual shall be such that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} all parts of the manual are consistent and
    compatible in form and content;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the manual can be readily amended;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the manual contains an amendment control page and a
    list of the pages that are in effect; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the manual has the date of the last amendment to
    each page specified on that page.

##### [Distribution of Company Operations Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999580 .Subheading}

- **[[705.136]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.136
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), an air
  operator shall provide a copy of the appropriate parts of its company
  operations manual, including any amendments to those parts, to each of
  its crew members and to its ground operations and maintenance
  personnel.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may place a copy of the appropriate
  parts of its company operations manual in each aircraft that it
  operates, instead of providing a copy to each crew member, if all
  amendments to the manual are included in the system for the
  dissemination of general operational information referred to in
  section 705.18.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Every person who has been provided with a copy of the
  appropriate parts of a company operations manual pursuant to
  subsection (1) shall keep it up to date with the amendments provided
  and shall ensure that the appropriate parts are accessible when the
  person is performing assigned duties.

##### [Aircraft Operating Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999585 .Subheading}

- **[[705.137]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.137
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator may establish and
  maintain an aircraft operating manual for the use and guidance of crew
  members in the operation of its aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An aircraft operating manual shall contain

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft operating procedures; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the aircraft flight manual is not carried on
    board the aircraft, the aircraft performance data and limitations
    specified in the aircraft flight manual, which shall be clearly
    identified as aircraft flight manual requirements.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator that has established an aircraft
  operating manual shall submit a copy of the manual, and any amendments
  to that manual, to the Minister for approval.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall approve an aircraft operating
  manual, and any amendments to that manual, where the Commercial Air
  Service Standards are met.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} An air operator that has established an aircraft
  operating manual shall ensure that a copy of the manual is carried on
  board each aircraft to which it relates.

##### [Standard Operating Procedures]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999594 .Subheading}

- **[[705.138]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.138
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every air operator shall, for each
  of its aircraft, establish and maintain standard operating procedures
  that enable the crew members to operate the aircraft within the
  limitations specified in the aircraft flight manual, and that meet the
  Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall submit a copy of its aircraft
  standard operating procedures, and any amendments to those procedures,
  to the Minister.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall ensure that a copy of the
  standard operating procedures for an aircraft is carried on board the
  aircraft.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where an air operator has established an aircraft
  operating manual, the standard operating procedures for the aircraft
  shall form part of that manual.

##### [Flight Attendant Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999600 .Subheading}

- **[[705.139]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.139
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every air operator, other than an
  air operator that is authorized solely for the transport of cargo in
  its air operator certificate, shall establish and maintain, as part of
  its company operations manual, a flight attendant manual for the use
  and guidance of flight attendants in the operation of its aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A flight attendant manual shall contain the
  instructions and information necessary to enable flight attendants to
  perform their duties safely and shall contain the information required
  by the Flight Attendant Manual Standard.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall, where the Flight Attendant Manual
  Standard is met, approve those parts of a flight attendant manual, and
  any amendments to those parts, that relate to the safety and emergency
  information contained in Part A of the Flight Attendant Manual
  Standard.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall provide a copy of its flight
  attendant manual, including any amendments to that manual, to each of
  its flight attendants.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} Every flight attendant who has been provided with a
  copy of a flight attendant manual pursuant to subsection (4) shall
  keep it up to date with the amendments provided and shall ensure that
  the appropriate parts are accessible when the flight attendant is
  performing assigned duties on board an aircraft.

**\[705.140 to 705.150 reserved\]**

#### [Division X --- Safety Management System]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999608 .Subheading}

##### [Requirements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999609 .Subheading}

**[[705.151]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.151 .sectionLabel}** The safety
management system required under section 107.02 in respect of an
applicant for, or a holder of, an air operator certificate shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} meet the requirements of Subpart 7 of Part I and
  section 705.152;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} be under the control of the operations manager
  appointed under paragraph 700.09(1)(a); and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} cover the maintenance control activities undertaken
  under Subpart 6.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-173, s. 24
:::

##### [Components of the Safety Management System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999616 .Subheading}

- **[[705.152]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.152
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The safety management system shall
  include, among others, the following components:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a safety management plan that includes

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a safety policy that the accountable executive
      has approved and communicated to all employees,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the roles and responsibilities of personnel
      assigned duties under the quality assurance program established
      under section 706.07 or the safety management system,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} performance goals and a means of measuring the
      attainment of those goals,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a policy for the internal reporting of a hazard,
      an incident or an accident, including the conditions under which
      immunity from disciplinary action will be granted, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} a review of the safety management system to
      determine its effectiveness;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} procedures for reporting a hazard, an incident or
    an accident to the appropriate manager;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} procedures for the collection of data relating to
    hazards, incidents and accidents;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} procedures for analysing data obtained under
    paragraph (c) and during an audit conducted under subsection
    706.07(3) and for taking corrective actions;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} an audit system referred to in subsection
    706.07(3);

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} training requirements for the operations manager,
    the maintenance manager and personnel assigned duties under the
    safety management system; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} procedures for making progress reports to the
    accountable executive at intervals determined by the accountable
    executive and other reports as needed in urgent cases.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The components specified in subsection (1) and the
  components of the safety management system that are required under
  section 107.03 shall be set out in

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the company operations manual of the applicant for,
    or the holder of, an air operator certificate; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the maintenance control manual (MCM) of the holder
    of an air operator certificate.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-173, s. 24
- [SOR/2019-295, s. 17](#1194405-1195639){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1194405-1195639.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-705.152-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 705.152"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Person Managing the Safety Management System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999634 .Subheading}

**[[705.153]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.153 .sectionLabel}** The person
managing the safety management system shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} establish and maintain a reporting system to ensure
  the timely collection of information related to hazards, incidents and
  accidents that may adversely affect safety;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} identify hazards and carry out risk management
  analyses of those hazards;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} investigate, analyze and identify the cause or
  probable cause of all hazards, incidents and accidents identified
  under the safety management system;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} establish and maintain a safety data system, either
  by electronic or by other means, to monitor and analyze trends in
  hazards, incidents and accidents;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} monitor and evaluate the results of corrective
  actions with respect to hazards, incidents and accidents;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} monitor the concerns of the civil aviation industry
  in respect of safety and their perceived effect on the air operator;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} determine the adequacy of the training required by
  paragraph 705.152(1)(f); and

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} where the operations manager has assigned the
  management functions for the safety management system under subsection
  705.03(3) to another person, report to the operations manager the
  hazards, incidents and accidents identified under the safety
  management system or as a result of an audit required under subsection
  706.07(3).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-173, s. 24
:::

##### [Holder of More Than One Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999646 .Subheading}

**[[705.154]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.154 .sectionLabel}** The holder of
an air operator certificate issued under section 705.07 who is also the
holder of an approved maintenance organization (AMO) certificate issued
under section 573.02 must comply with the requirements referred to in
section 573.30 with respect to a safety management system when
undertaking maintenance control activities under Subpart 6.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-173, s. 24
- [SOR/2025-26, s. 48(E)](#1511779-1516330){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1511779-1516330.html"}
:::

#### [Division XI --- Interference With a Crew Member]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999651 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote

##### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999654 .Subheading}

**[[705.171]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.171 .sectionLabel}** In this
Division,

[[interference with a crew member]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[interference with a crew member]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means any
    action or statement set out in the levels listed in section 705.175
    by a person on board or about to board an aircraft that distracts a
    crew member from their assigned safety responsibilities or prevents
    the crew member from carrying out those responsibilities; ([entrave
    au travail d'un membre d'équipage]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[operational personnel]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[operational personnel]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an air
    operator's employees whose duties require that they interact
    directly with persons on board or about to board an aircraft, and
    includes crew members, gate and check-in staff and their immediate
    supervisors. ([personnel d'exploitation]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-90, s. 4
- SOR/2015-160, s. 32
:::

:::

##### [Preventing and Managing Incidents of Interference with a Crew Member]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999660 .Subheading}

**[[705.172]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.172 .sectionLabel}** An applicant
for an air operator certificate shall set out in the company operations
manual and in their flight attendant manual the procedures established
to prevent and manage incidents of interference with a crew member
covering the topics set out in section 725.172 of Standard 725 ---
Airline Operations --- Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service
Standards.

::: HistoricalNote

- SOR/2015-160, s. 33(F)

:::

##### [Training]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999666 .Subheading}

**[[705.173]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.173 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
shall provide initial and annual training to all operational personnel
that covers the topics set out in subsection 725.124(56) of Standard 725
--- Airline Operations --- Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service
Standards for the purpose of enabling

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the recognition, prevention and management of
  behaviour that could reasonably be expected to lead to an incident of
  interference with a crew member;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the recognition, prevention and management of
  incidents of interference with a crew member; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the knowledge of post-flight procedures related to
  incidents of interference with a crew member.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-90, s. 4
- SOR/2015-160, s. 34
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-705.173-20100610.html "Link to previous version of section 705.173"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Reporting Incidents of Interference with a Crew Member]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999673 .Subheading}

- **[[705.174]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.174
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An applicant for an air operator
  certificate shall set out in the company operations manual and in
  their flight attendant manual the procedures established to ensure
  that level 2, level 3 and level 4 incidents of interference with a
  crew member are reported to them and to allow for the reporting of a
  level 1 incident.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2019-295, s. 19\]]{.Repealed}

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A report of an incident of interference with a crew
  member shall contain the information set out in section 725.174 of
  Standard 725 --- Airline Operations --- Aeroplanes of the Commercial
  Air Service Standards.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall ensure that reports are
  retained for a period of three years after the date of the incident
  and are made available to the Minister on request.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall submit to the Minister
  statistics relating to incidents of interference with a crew member,
  the content of which is set out in section 725.174 of Standard 725 ---
  Airline Operations --- Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service
  Standards, every six months.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-90, s. 4
- SOR/2015-160, s. 35(F)

##### [Levels of Interference with a Crew Member]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999682 .Subheading}

**[[705.175]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.175 .sectionLabel}** The levels of
interference with a crew member are as follows:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a level 1 incident, which is an incident of a minor
  nature that either requires no action of the crew member beyond
  heightened awareness or is quickly resolved by a crew member, and
  which includes but is not limited to

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the use of insulting or obscene language towards a
    crew member,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the causing of a disturbance, including verbal
    abuse or obscene gestures towards a crew member, and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a display of suspicious behaviour;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a level 2 incident, which is an incident of a
  moderate nature that is resolved by a crew member only after some
  difficulty and which includes but is not limited to

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the repetition of a level 1 incident,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the continuation of a level 1 incident that was
    unresolved,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the repeated failure of a passenger to comply
    with a crew member's safety instructions, and

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} belligerent, obscene or lewd behaviour towards a
    crew member;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a level 3 incident, which is an incident where the
  safety of passengers or crew members is seriously threatened and which
  includes but is not limited to

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} threatening a person on board or about to board the
    aircraft or making threats in an attempt to board the aircraft,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the continuation of a level 2 incident that was
    unresolved,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} tampering with any emergency or safety equipment
    on board the aircraft,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} deliberate damage of any part of the aircraft or
    any property on board the aircraft,

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} injuring a person on board the aircraft, and

  - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} violent, argumentative, threatening, intimidating
    or disorderly behaviour, including harassment and assault; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} a level 4 incident, which is an incident that
  constitutes a security threat and which includes but is not limited to

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} an attempted or unauthorized intrusion into the
    flight deck,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a credible threat of death or serious bodily
    injury in an attempt to gain control over the aircraft,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the display or use of a weapon,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the sabotage of, or the attempt to sabotage, an
    aircraft that renders it incapable of flight or that is likely to
    endanger its safety in flight,

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} any attempt to unlawfully seize control of the
    aircraft, and

  - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} an incident that is required to be reported under
    section 543 of the [Canadian Aviation Security Regulations,
    2012](/eng/regulations/SOR-2011-318).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-90, s. 4

#### [Division XII --- Flight Attendants and Emergency Evacuation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999710 .Subheading}

##### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999711 .Subheading}

- **[[705.200]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.200
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Division
  and subject to subsection (2), [[model]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means
  [[aircraft master series]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} as described in section
  3.7 of version 1.3 of the document entitled International Standard for
  Aircraft Make, Model, and Series Groupings, dated October 2012 and
  published by the Common Taxonomy Team of the International Civil
  Aviation Organization (ICAO) and the Commercial Aviation Safety Team
  (CAST).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If no aircraft master series is assigned to an
  aeroplane, [[model]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} in respect of that aeroplane
  means [[aircraft model]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} as described in section
  3.6 of version 1.3 of the document entitled International Standard for
  Aircraft Make, Model, and Series Groupings, dated October 2012 and
  published by the Common Taxonomy Team of the International Civil
  Aviation Organization (ICAO) and the Commercial Aviation Safety Team
  (CAST).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 20
:::

##### [Minimum Number of Flight Attendants]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999717 .Subheading}

- **[[705.201]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.201
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall operate an
  aeroplane to carry passengers unless the air operator does so with the
  minimum number of flight attendants required on each deck.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (4) to (7), the minimum number
  of flight attendants required on each deck of an aeroplane is
  determined in accordance with one of the following ratios that is
  selected by the air operator in respect of the model of that
  aeroplane:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} one flight attendant for each unit of 40 passengers
    or for each portion of such a unit; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} one flight attendant for each unit of 50 passenger
    seats or for each portion of such a unit.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A Department of Transport air carrier inspector or a
  person authorized under subsection 705.27(4) to access the flight deck
  is not counted as a passenger for the purposes of paragraph (2)(a).

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An air operator who has selected, in respect of a
  model of aeroplane, the ratio set out in paragraph (2)(b) shall not
  operate an aeroplane of that model with only one flight attendant
  unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane has a single deck and is configured
    for 50 or fewer passenger seats;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane was certified under

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} part 25, title 14, of the Code of Federal
      Regulations of the United States, in the version in effect on
      March 6, 1980 or after that date,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the European Joint Aviation Requirements ---
      Large Aeroplanes (JAR-25), published by the Joint Aviation
      Authorities, in the version in effect on November 30, 1981 or
      after that date,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the Certification Specifications, Including
      Airworthiness Code and Acceptable Means of Compliance, for Large
      Aeroplanes (CS-25), published by the European Aviation Safety
      Agency, in the version in effect on October 17, 2003 or after that
      date, or

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} Chapter 525 --- Transport Category Aeroplanes of
      the Airworthiness Manual, in the version in effect on July 1, 1986
      or after that date;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} only one flight attendant was used for the
    emergency evacuation demonstration required for the certification of
    that model of aeroplane;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the air operator's flight attendant manual
    indicates how normal and emergency procedures differ depending on
    whether the aeroplane is operated with one flight attendant or with
    more than one flight attendant;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the flight attendant occupies a flight attendant
    station that is located near a floor-level exit; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the public address system and the crew member
    interphone system are operative and are capable of being used at the
    flight attendant station.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} If an air operator has selected, in respect of a
  model of aeroplane, the ratio set out in paragraph (2)(a), but has
  carried out a successful demonstration of its emergency evacuation
  procedures for that model using more flight attendants than would have
  been required in accordance with that ratio, the minimum number of
  flight attendants required on each deck of an aeroplane of that model
  that is operated by the air operator is the number of flight
  attendants used in the demonstration.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} If an air operator has selected, in respect of a
  model of aeroplane, the ratio set out in paragraph (2)(b), but has
  carried out a successful demonstration of its emergency evacuation
  procedures for that model using more flight attendants than would have
  been required in accordance with that ratio, the minimum number of
  flight attendants required on each deck of an aeroplane of that model
  that is operated by the air operator is the number of flight
  attendants used in the demonstration.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} If the emergency evacuation demonstration required
  for the certification of a model of aeroplane was carried out using
  more flight attendants than would have been required in accordance
  with the ratio set out in paragraph (2)(b) and, after the
  demonstration, an aeroplane of that model is reconfigured for fewer
  passenger seats, the minimum number of flight attendants required on
  each deck of the reconfigured aeroplane is the number of flight
  attendants required in accordance with the ratio set out in paragraph
  (2)(b) plus an additional number of flight attendants that is equal to
  the difference between

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the number of flight attendants used in the
    demonstration, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number of flight attendants that would have
    been required in accordance with the ratio set out in paragraph
    (2)(b) at the time of the demonstration.

##### [Notice]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999742 .Subheading}

- **[[705.202]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.202
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator who decides, in
  respect of a model of aeroplane, to change the ratio that it has
  selected for the purposes of subsection 705.201(2) shall not implement
  this change unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the air operator has provided the Minister with a
    notice in writing of the decision at least 60 days before
    implementing the change; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the Minister has acknowledged receipt of the
    notice.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall acknowledge receipt of the notice
  not later than one working day after receiving it.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 20
:::

##### [Emergency Features]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999750 .Subheading}

**[[705.203]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.203 .sectionLabel}** If an air
operator has selected, in respect of a model of aeroplane, the ratio set
out in paragraph 705.201(2)(b), the air operator shall not operate an
aeroplane of that model unless

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the features that facilitate emergency evacuations
  meet the requirements set out in paragraphs 725.203(a) to (n) of
  Standard 725 --- Airline Operations --- Aeroplanes of the Commercial
  Air Service Standards;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the passenger seats and flight attendant seats meet
  the requirements set out in paragraph 725.203(o) of Standard 725 ---
  Airline Operations --- Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service
  Standards;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} compartments occupied by passengers and crew members
  meet the requirements respecting flammability set out in paragraph
  725.203(p), (q) or (r) of Standard 725 --- Airline Operations ---
  Aeroplanes of the Commercial Air Service Standards; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the thermal insulation and acoustic insulation meet
  the requirements respecting flammability set out in paragraph
  725.203(s) of Standard 725 --- Airline Operations --- Aeroplanes of
  the Commercial Air Service Standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 20

  ajax-after="1126790-1144274.html"}

##### [Demonstration of Emergency Evacuation Procedures]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999758 .Subheading}

- **[[705.204]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.204
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator who decides to
  introduce a model of aeroplane into its fleet for the purpose of
  carrying passengers shall carry out a successful demonstration of its
  emergency evacuation procedures for that model of aeroplane before
  operating an aeroplane of that model to carry passengers.

- [(1.1)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsection (1), the demonstration of
  emergency evacuation procedures is not required if the air operator
  has

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} carried out a successful demonstration of its
    emergency evacuation procedures for another model of aeroplane in
    its fleet;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} conducted a comparative analysis to ensure that
    there is no difference in any of the following items between the
    model of aeroplane for which a successful demonstration has been
    carried out and the model of aeroplane being introduced:

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the location of the flight attendants and their
      emergency evacuation duties and procedures,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the number, location and type of emergency
      exits, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the number, location and type of opening
      mechanisms for the emergency exits;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} verified that no changes have been made to any of
    the items listed in subparagraphs (b)(i) to (iii), in respect of the
    model of aeroplane for which a successful demonstration has been
    carried out, between the time of the successful demonstration and
    the time the comparative analysis is conducted; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} before operating an aeroplane of the model being
    introduced to carry passengers, informed the Minister of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} its decision to use the results of a successful
      demonstration of its emergency evacuation procedures for another
      model of aeroplane instead of carrying out a demonstration for the
      model of aeroplane it has decided to introduce, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the model of aeroplane for which a successful
      demonstration has been carried out and the model of aeroplane it
      has decided to introduce.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If an air operator decides to introduce an aeroplane
  into its fleet and there is a difference in any of the following items
  between that aeroplane and other aeroplanes of the same model that are
  already in the fleet, the air operator shall treat the aeroplane as if
  it were a different model of aeroplane and carry out a successful
  demonstration of its emergency evacuation procedures for that model
  before operating the aeroplane to carry passengers:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the location of the flight attendants or their
    emergency evacuation duties or procedures;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number, location or type of emergency exits; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the number, location or type of opening mechanisms
    for the emergency exits.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator who decides to change any of the
  following items in respect of an aeroplane shall carry out a
  successful demonstration of its emergency evacuation procedures for
  the model of that aeroplane, as changed, before operating the
  aeroplane to carry passengers:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the location of the flight attendants or their
    emergency evacuation duties or procedures;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number, location or type of emergency exits; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the number, location or type of opening mechanisms
    for the emergency exits.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} If an air operator who has selected the ratio set out
  in paragraph 705.201(2)(b) in respect of a model of aeroplane decides
  to reconfigure an aeroplane of that model by adding or removing
  passenger seats, and if the reconfiguration will result in a change in
  the minimum number of flight attendants required on each deck, the air
  operator shall carry out a successful demonstration of its emergency
  evacuation procedures for the reconfigured model of that aeroplane
  before operating the reconfigured aeroplane to carry passengers.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} Subsections (1) to (4) do not apply in respect of a
  model of aeroplane that is configured to carry fewer than 44
  passengers.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 20

  ajax-after="1274687-1276936.html"}
:::

##### [Carrying Out a Demonstration of Emergency Evacuation Procedures]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999773 .Subheading}

- **[[705.205]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.205
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator who carries out a
  demonstration of its emergency evacuation procedures for a model of
  aeroplane shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} do so in the presence of the Minister;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} do so without passengers;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} do so with flight attendants who have completed the
    air operator's training program for that model of aeroplane; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} begin the demonstration using the air operator's
    normal procedures, then transition to its emergency procedures.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The demonstration is successful if the flight
  attendants can, within 15 seconds after the transition from the air
  operator's normal procedures to its emergency procedures,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} open 50% of the floor-level emergency exits that
    are required by the certification basis established in respect of
    the model of aeroplane;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} open 50% of the non-floor-level emergency exits the
    opening of which is set out as an emergency evacuation duty in the
    air operator's operations manual; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} deploy 50% of the escape slides.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 20
:::

##### [Extended Over-water Operations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999786 .Subheading}

**[[705.206]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.206 .sectionLabel}** If an air
operator decides to operate an aeroplane to carry passengers in extended
over-water operations and the aeroplane is required to have survival
equipment under section 602.63, the air operator shall carry out a
demonstration of its ditching emergency evacuation procedures for the
model of that aeroplane before starting the extended over-water
operations.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 21
:::

##### [Carrying Out a Demonstration of Emergency Evacuation Procedures --- Ditching]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999790 .Subheading}

- **[[705.207]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.207
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator who carries out a
  demonstration of its ditching emergency evacuation procedures for a
  model of aeroplane shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} do so in the presence of the Minister;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} use an aeroplane of that model, a life-sized
    mock-up of that model of aeroplane or a floating device;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} assume that the ditching occurs during daylight
    hours and that all required crew members are available;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} ensure that passengers are on board and participate
    in the demonstration if the air operator's operations manual
    requires passengers to assist in the launching of life rafts;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} ensure that, after the ditching signal has been
    received, each evacuee dons a life preserver;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} ensure that each life raft is removed from its
    stowage compartment;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} ensure that, as applicable, one life raft or one
    slide raft is inflated; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} ensure that each evacuee boards the life raft or
    slide raft and that a crew member assigned to the life raft or slide
    raft indicates the location of the required survival equipment and
    describes the use of that equipment.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A life-sized mock-up of a model of aeroplane or
  floating device must

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} be representative of the passenger cabin of the
    model of aeroplane;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} contain seats for all of the evacuees participating
    in the demonstration;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} be equipped with the same survival equipment that
    is installed on the model of aeroplane, including a life preserver
    for each evacuee participating in the demonstration;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} have emergency exits and doors that simulate those
    on the model of aeroplane; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} have enough wing area installed outside the window
    emergency exits to simulate the portions of the wings of the model
    of aeroplane that would be used in a ditching situation.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 21
:::

**\[705.208 to 705.219 reserved\]**

##### [In-charge Flight Attendant]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999810 .Subheading}

- **[[705.220]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.220
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator who operates an
  aeroplane with more than one flight attendant shall designate an
  in-charge flight attendant for each flight and keep a record of that
  designation for at least 90 days after the day on which the flight is
  completed.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (3), an air operator shall not
  allow an individual to act as an in-charge flight attendant and no
  individual shall act as an in-charge flight attendant unless the
  individual has successfully completed in-charge training as part of
  the air operator's training program.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall set out procedures in its
  company operations manual for the selection of an acting in-charge
  flight attendant if the designated in-charge flight attendant becomes
  incapacitated after take-off.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a flight with scheduled stops, an air
  operator shall replace an acting in-charge flight attendant with a new
  designated in-charge flight attendant at the first scheduled stop
  where the replacement can be made.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 20
:::

##### [Incapacitated Flight Attendant]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999818 .Subheading}

- **[[705.221]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.221
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator who has selected, in
  respect of a model of aeroplane, the ratio set out in paragraph
  705.201(2)(a) and who has assigned two or more flight attendants to a
  flight using an aeroplane of that model may operate the aeroplane for
  that flight without one of the flight attendants if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} one of the flight attendants is incapacitated;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} no other flight attendant who is qualified for the
    model of aeroplane is available at the point of departure;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command authorizes an employee of the
    air operator to occupy a flight attendant station until the
    aeroplane reaches the nearest airport at which the employee can be
    replaced by a flight attendant who is qualified for the model of
    aeroplane;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} before the movement of the aeroplane on the
    surface, the employee is briefed under the supervision of the
    pilot-in-command on the operation of the emergency exits and on
    emergency procedures, including those related to the flight
    attendant station to be occupied by the employee; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the pilot-in-command is of the opinion that the
    employee understood the briefing.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator who has assigned two or more flight
  attendants to a flight may operate the aeroplane for that flight
  without one of the flight attendants if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} one of the flight attendants is incapacitated;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} no other flight attendant who is qualified for the
    model of aeroplane is available at the point of departure;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} procedures are established and implemented by the
    air operator to

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} reduce the number of passengers,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} reseat passengers, taking into account the
      emergency exits and other factors related to the configuration of
      the aeroplane, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} relocate flight attendants, taking into account
      the emergency duties established in accordance with section
      705.224;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} at least one flight attendant, other than the
    incapacitated flight attendant, is on board for each unit of 50
    passengers or for each portion of such a unit; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} at least one flight attendant is assigned to each
    pair of floor-level exits.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The air operator must submit a report to the Minister
  after the completion of each flight referred to in subsection (1)
  or (2) that contains:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the date of the flight;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the flight number;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the aerodrome of departure; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a flight referred to in subsection
    (1), the name of the authorized employee occupying the flight
    attendant station.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 20
- [SOR/2025-26, s. 49](#1511781-1516334){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1511781-1516334.html"}
:::

##### [Embarking and Disembarking of Passengers]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999829 .Subheading}

- **[[705.222]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.222
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) and (3),
  an air operator who operates an aeroplane to carry passengers shall
  ensure that all flight attendants assigned to a flight using that
  aeroplane are on board during passenger embarkation and
  disembarkation.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a flight to which more than one flight
  attendant is assigned, the air operator may reduce the number of
  flight attendants by one during passenger embarkation if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the flight attendant who leaves the aeroplane
    remains within the immediate vicinity of the door through which
    passengers are embarking and carries out safety-related duties for
    the flight;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the engines used for the propulsion of the
    aeroplane are not running; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} at least one floor-level exit remains open to
    provide for passenger egress.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a flight to which more than one flight
  attendant is assigned, the air operator may reduce the number of
  flight attendants during passenger disembarkation if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the engines used for the propulsion of the
    aeroplane are not running;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} at least one floor-level exit remains open to
    provide for passenger egress; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} half of the required number of flight attendants
    --- rounded down to the next lower number in the case of fractions,
    but never less than one --- remain on board.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Paragraphs (2)(b) and (3)(a) do not apply in respect
  of an engine on a propeller-driven aeroplane if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the engine has a propeller brake;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the propeller brake is set; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane flight manual indicates that the
    engine may be used as an auxiliary power unit.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The air operator shall ensure that, during passenger
  embarkation and disembarkation,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if only one flight attendant is on board, he or she
    remains in the vicinity of the door through which passengers are
    embarking or disembarking; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if more than one flight attendant is on board, they
    are evenly distributed in the passenger cabin and are in the
    vicinity of the floor-level exits.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 20
:::

##### [Stops]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999849 .Subheading}

- **[[705.223]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.223
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall not permit
  passengers to remain on board an aeroplane during an intermediate stop
  unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the engines used for the propulsion of the
    aeroplane are not running;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} at least one floor-level exit remains open to
    provide for passenger egress;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aeroplane operated with only one
    flight attendant, the flight attendant remains on board;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an aeroplane operated with more than
    one flight attendant, at least half of the required number of flight
    attendants --- rounded down to the next lower number in the case of
    fractions, but never less than one --- remain on board; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} flight attendants are located in the vicinity of
    the floor-level exits and are ready to initiate and oversee an
    emergency evacuation.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Paragraph (1)(a) does not apply in respect of an
  engine on a propeller-driven aeroplane if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the engine has a propeller brake;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the propeller brake is set; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the aeroplane flight manual indicates that the
    engine may be used as an auxiliary power unit.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Paragraph (1)(b) does not apply if the exit is closed
  or latched for climatic reasons.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} A flight attendant on board an aeroplane referred to
  in paragraph (1)(c) or (d) may be replaced by an individual other than
  a flight attendant if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the individual has successfully completed the air
    operator's training on the emergency evacuation procedures for the
    model of that aeroplane in accordance with subsection 725.124(14)
    or (47) of Standard 725 --- Airline Operations --- Aeroplanes of the
    Commercial Air Services Standards;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the individual is identified to the passengers as
    an acting flight attendant; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the individual is located in the vicinity of a
    floor-level exit and is ready to initiate and oversee an emergency
    evacuation.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 20
:::

##### [Emergency Duties]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999868 .Subheading}

- **[[705.224]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.224
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall, for each
  model of aeroplane in its fleet that is operated to carry passengers,
  set out, in its flight attendant manual, the duties to be performed by
  the flight attendants in an emergency.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The air operator shall not operate an aeroplane to
  carry passengers unless those duties are assigned to flight attendants
  on board the aeroplane.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 20
:::

##### [Emergency Evacuation --- Before and During Surface Movements]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999874 .Subheading}

**[[705.225]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.225 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
shall, for each aeroplane in its fleet that is operated to carry
passengers, have procedures to ensure that

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} at least one floor-level exit provides for passenger
  egress before the movement of the aeroplane on the surface; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} every automatically deployable means of emergency
  passenger evacuation is ready for immediate use during the movement of
  the aeroplane on the surface.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 20
:::

##### [Single-aisle Aeroplane]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999880 .Subheading}

**[[705.226]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.226 .sectionLabel}** Despite section
605.09, no person shall conduct a take-off in a single-aisle aeroplane
that is carrying passengers unless all emergency exits and escape slides
are operative.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 20
:::

##### [Standardization]{.HTitleText4} {#h-999884 .Subheading}

**[[705.227]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-705.227 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall operate an aeroplane to carry passengers unless the emergency
equipment, the stowage locations for emergency equipment and the
emergency procedures are standardized for all aeroplanes in the air
operator's fleet that are operated under this Subpart to carry
passengers.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2015-127, s. 22
:::

### [Subpart 6 --- Aircraft Maintenance Requirements for Air Operators]{.HTitleText2} {#h-999888 .Subheading}

#### [Application]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999889 .Subheading}

**[[706.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-706.01 .sectionLabel}** This Subpart
applies to every person who operates an aircraft in a commercial air
service under this Part.

#### [Maintenance Control System]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999891 .Subheading}

**[[706.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-706.02 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an aircraft unless the aircraft is maintained in accordance with
a maintenance control system that

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements of this Subpart; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} is described in the air operator's maintenance
  control manual (MCM) required by section 706.08.

#### [Duties of Certificate Holder]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999895 .Subheading}

- **[[706.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-706.03
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The holder of an air operator
  certificate shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} appoint one of its employees to be a person
    responsible for the maintenance control system;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} subject to subsection (4), ensure that the person
    responsible for the maintenance control system has achieved a grade
    of 70% or more in an open-book examination that demonstrates
    knowledge of the provisions of the [Canadian Aviation
    Regulations](/eng/regulations/SOR-96-433);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2022-246, s. 31\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the person responsible for the
    maintenance control system performs the duties referred to in
    subsections 706.07(2) and (3);

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} provide the person responsible for the maintenance
    control system with the financial and human resources necessary to
    ensure that the holder of the air operator certificate meets the
    requirements of these Regulations; and

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2022-246, s. 31\]]{.Repealed}

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} ensure that corrective actions are taken in respect
    of any findings resulting from a quality assurance program
    established under section 706.07.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2022-246, s. 31\]]{.Repealed}

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2022-246, s. 31\]]{.Repealed}

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The knowledge requirement set out in paragraph (1)(b)
  does not apply in respect of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a person responsible for the maintenance control
    system who held that position on January 1, 1997; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the holder of an aircraft maintenance engineer
    (AME) licence.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The holder of an air operator certificate shall
  ensure that no person is appointed to be responsible for the
  maintenance control system or remains responsible for the system if,
  at the time of their appointment or during their tenure, they have a
  record of conviction for

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an offence under section 7.3 of the Act; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} two or more offences under any of sections 605.84
    to 605.86 not arising from a single occurrence.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} The person responsible for maintenance control system
  of the holder of an air operator certificate may assign the management
  functions for specific maintenance control activities, to another
  person if the assignment and its scope are described in the
  maintenance control manual (MCM) of the air operator.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} If the holder of an air operator certificate is also
  the holder of an approved maintenance organization (AMO) certificate
  issued under section 573.02, the person appointed under paragraph
  (1)(a) shall be the person responsible for maintenance of the AMO
  appointed under paragraph 573.03(1)(a).

- [(8)]{.lawlabel} The person responsible for the maintenance control
  system of the holder of an air operator certificate shall remove
  aircraft from operation if the removal is justified because of
  non-compliance with the requirements of these Regulations or because
  of a risk to aviation safety or the safety of the public.

#### [Maintenance Personnel and Facilities]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999917 .Subheading}

**[[706.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-706.04 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
shall provide the person who is responsible for its maintenance control
system with the staff, facilities, technical and regulatory data,
supplies and spare parts referred to in the Commercial Air Service
Standards that are necessary to ensure compliance with this Subpart.

#### [Defect Recording, Rectification and Control Procedures]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999919 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2020-151, s. 22

\]
:::

**[[706.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-706.05 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
shall include in its maintenance control system the procedures referred
to in the Commercial Air Service Standards for

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} recording aircraft defects;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} ensuring that defects are rectified in accordance
  with the requirements of these Regulations;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} detecting defects that recur and identifying those
  defects as recurring defects; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} subject to sections 605.09 and 605.10, scheduling the
  rectification of defects whose repair has been deferred.

#### [Technical Dispatch Procedures]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999925 .Subheading}

- **[[706.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-706.06
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall include in its
  maintenance control system technical dispatch procedures to ensure
  that aircraft are not operated unless they are

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} airworthy;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} appropriately equipped, configured and maintained
    for their intended use; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} maintained in accordance with the air operator's
    maintenance control manual (MCM).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Where an additional flight authority has been issued
  in respect of an aircraft pursuant to section 507.08, the technical
  dispatch procedures required by this section shall include procedures
  to control the use of that additional flight authority.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where an air operator has a fleet empty weight and
  balance control program approved in accordance with the Commercial Air
  Service Standards, the technical dispatch procedures required by this
  section shall include specific procedures that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} ensure the quality of the program by meeting the
    applicable requirements of the Commercial Air Service Standards; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} ensure that accurate empty weight and balance data
    for each aircraft to which the program applies is provided to the
    flight crew of the aircraft, or is input into the program, prior to
    each flight.

#### [Quality Assurance Program]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999935 .Subheading}

- **[[706.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-706.07
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall, in order to
  ensure that its maintenance control system and all of the included
  maintenance schedules continue to be effective and to comply with
  these Regulations, establish and maintain a quality assurance program
  that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} is under the sole control of the person responsible
    for the maintenance control system appointed under paragraph
    706.03(1)(a); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} meets the requirements of section 726.07 of
    Standard 726 --- Air Operator Maintenance of the Commercial Air
    Service Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The person responsible for the maintenance control
  system shall distribute the records relating to the findings resulting
  from the quality assurance program to the appropriate manager for
  corrective action and follow-up in accordance with the policies and
  procedures specified in the maintenance control manual (MCM).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The person responsible for the maintenance control
  system shall establish an audit system in respect of the quality
  assurance program that consists of the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an initial audit within 12 months after the date on
    which the air operator certificate is issued;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} subsequent audits conducted at intervals set out in
    the MCM;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a record of each occurrence of compliance or
    non-compliance with the MCM found during an audit referred to in
    paragraph (a) or (b);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} checklists of all activities controlled by the MCM
    and the maintenance schedules;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} procedures for ensuring that each finding of an
    audit is communicated to them and, if management functions have been
    assigned to another person under subsection 705.03(3) or (4), to
    that person;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} follow-up procedures for ensuring that corrective
    actions are effective; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a system for recording the findings of initial and
    periodic audits, corrective actions and follow-ups.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The records required under paragraph (3)(g) shall be
  retained for the greater of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} two audit cycles; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} two years.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The duties related to the quality assurance program
  that involve specific tasks or activities within an air operator's
  activities shall be fulfilled by persons who are not responsible for
  carrying out those tasks or activities.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2005-173, s. 26
:::

#### [Maintenance Control Manual (MCM)]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999955 .Subheading}

- **[[706.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-706.08
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall establish,
  maintain and authorize the use of a maintenance control manual (MCM)
  that contains information to ensure the efficiency of the maintenance
  control system, as set out in the Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister may authorize the incorporation by
  reference in an MCM of detailed procedures manuals prepared by the air
  operator, where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the policies affecting the detailed procedures
    remain in the MCM;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the incorporation is clearly indicated in the MCM;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the air operator ensures that the incorporated
    manuals meet the requirements of this section; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the person responsible for the air operator's
    maintenance control system, or the person to whom the management
    function has been assigned under subsection 706.03(6), has certified
    in writing that the incorporated manuals meet the requirements of
    this section.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Except where otherwise authorized by the Minister in
  writing where it is demonstrated that the granting of the
  authorization will not jeopardize the safety of the product or
  service, an air operator shall comply with the policies and procedures
  contained in its MCM.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall submit each page of its MCM to
  the Minister for approval, either individually or in accordance with
  an equivalent procedure that meets the applicable requirements of the
  Commercial Air Service Standards.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall amend its MCM when instructed
  to do so by the Minister where

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the MCM does not meet the requirements of this
    Subpart; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the MCM contains policies or procedures, or a lack
    thereof, such that the air operator's maintenance control system no
    longer meets the requirements of these Regulations.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall provide the means to ensure
  that a current copy of its MCM, or of the relevant portions of its
  MCM, is made available to each person who performs or certifies a
  function that is dealt with in the MCM or in any manual that is
  incorporated in the MCM in accordance with subsection (2).

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall amend each copy of its MCM
  within 30 days after the approval of an amendment under subsection
  (8).

- [(8)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall approve an air operator's MCM, and
  any amendments to that manual, if the requirements of the Commercial
  Air Service Standards are met.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2000-389, s. 2
- SOR/2009-152, s. 24

  ajax-after="1380184-1380812.html"}
:::

:::

#### [Maintenance Arrangements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999973 .Subheading}

- **[[706.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-706.09
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No air operator shall permit a
  person or organization to perform maintenance on the air operator's
  aircraft unless the person or organization has adequate facilities,
  equipment, spare parts and personnel available at the site where the
  maintenance is to be performed and

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person or organization holds an approved
    maintenance organization (AMO) certificate issued pursuant to
    section 573.02 with a rating in a category applicable to the
    maintenance to be performed;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} where the maintenance is to be performed outside
    Canada by a person or organization that does not hold an AMO
    certificate issued pursuant to section 573.02, the person or
    organization has been approved under the laws of a state that is
    party to an agreement with Canada that provides for recognition of
    the work performed; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in cases other than those described in
    paragraphs (a) and (b), the performance of the maintenance by the
    person or organization has been approved by the Minister as being in
    conformity with these Regulations.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall ensure that a maintenance
  arrangement made with a person or organization pursuant to subsection
  (1)

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} specifies the maintenance required and clearly
    defines the tasks to be performed; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is made in accordance with the procedures governing
    maintenance arrangements included in the MCM or is approved by the
    Minister as being in conformity with these Regulations.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where an air operator makes a maintenance arrangement
  to have maintenance performed outside Canada by a person or
  organization that does not hold an AMO certificate issued pursuant to
  section 573.02, the Minister shall, in the following cases, authorize
  the arrangement by issuing a maintenance specification to indicate
  that the maintenance control procedures set out in the arrangement
  conform to the Commercial Air Service Standards:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the maintenance is performed by a person or
    organization that has been approved in accordance with paragraph
    (1)(b) and the issuance of a maintenance specification is either
    required by the agreement or requested by the foreign state; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the maintenance is performed in a state that is not
    party to an agreement with Canada that provides for recognition of
    the work performed.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall ensure the completion of all of
  the tasks defined in a maintenance arrangement in accordance with
  subsection (2).

#### [Elementary Work]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999986 .Subheading}

**[[706.10]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-706.10 .sectionLabel}** No air operator
shall authorize a person to perform, without supervision, a task that is
elementary work set out in the Aircraft Equipment and Maintenance
Standards unless the person

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} has satisfactorily completed training for the task
  under a training program required by section 706.12; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} has previously performed that task under the direct
  supervision of the holder of an aircraft maintenance engineer (AME)
  licence or a training organization approved pursuant to Subpart 3 of
  Part IV.

#### [Servicing]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999990 .Subheading}

**[[706.11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-706.11 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
shall ensure that each person who performs or requests the performance
of servicing has satisfactorily completed training, under a training
program required by section 706.12, for the servicing to be performed.

#### [Training Program]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999992 .Subheading}

**[[706.12]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-706.12 .sectionLabel}** An air operator
shall implement a training program to ensure that persons who are
authorized to perform a function under this Subpart are trained in
respect of the regulations, standards and air operator procedures
applicable to that function, as specified in the Commercial Air Service
Standards.

#### [Personnel Records]{.HTitleText3} {#h-999994 .Subheading}

- **[[706.13]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-706.13
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air operator shall establish,
  maintain and retain for at least two years after an entry is made, for
  each affected person, a record of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} all personal qualifications in respect of any
    appointment made pursuant to section 706.03;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any authorization to perform elementary work given
    in accordance with section 706.10 and incorporated in the
    maintenance control manual (MCM) in accordance with the Commercial
    Air Service Standards; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} all training conducted pursuant to section 706.12.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The air operator shall provide a copy of each record
  required by subsection (1) to the person to whom the record refers on
  the completion of any training or the giving of an authorization
  referred to in paragraph (1)(b).

#### [Service Difficulty Reporting]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000001 .Subheading}

**[[706.14]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-706.14 .sectionLabel}** The holder of an
air operator certificate shall report to the Minister, in accordance
with Division IX of Subpart 21 of Part V, any reportable service
difficulty related to any aircraft that it operates.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2009-280, s. 36
:::

Version](section-706.14-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 706.14"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Safety Management System]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000005 .Subheading}

**[[706.15]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-706.15 .sectionLabel}** The holder of an
air operator certificate issued under section 705.07 must, for all
maintenance control activities performed under this Subpart, comply with
the requirements set out in section 705.151 or 705.154 with respect to a
safety management system.

:::

### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1000010 .Subheading}

- **[[800.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-800.01
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In this Part,

  [[air traffic control unit]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[air traffic control unit]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed,
      SOR/2002-352, s. 4\]]{.Repealed}

  [[air traffic services]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[air traffic services]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} or
      [[ATS]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed, SOR/2025-98, s.
      19\]]{.Repealed}

  [[altitude reservation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[altitude reservation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an airspace of
      defined dimensions within controlled airspace reserved for the use
      of a civil or military agency during a specified period and whose
      location is fixed or moves in relation to the aircraft that
      operate within it; ([réservation d'altitude]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[ATS operations certificate]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[ATS operations certificate]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed,
      SOR/2007-290, s. 11\]]{.Repealed}

  [[conflict resolution]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[conflict resolution]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an air traffic
      control service provided to avoid potential conflicts between
      identified aircraft that are in communication with an air traffic
      controller; ([résolution de conflit]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[CVFR aircraft]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[CVFR aircraft]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an aircraft operating
      in controlled VFR flight; ([aéronef CVFR]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[emergency assistance services]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[emergency assistance services]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means
      services provided for the purpose of

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} assisting aircraft in a state of emergency,
        including aircraft in the uncertainty, alert and distress
        phases,

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} assisting aircraft involved in a hijacking, or

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} alerting rescue coordination agencies of
        missing or overdue aircraft; ([services
        d'urgence]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[flight information services]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[flight information services]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed,
      SOR/2002-352, s. 4\]]{.Repealed}

  [[identified aircraft]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[identified aircraft]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an aircraft
      whose position as indicated on a situation display is confirmed by
      an air traffic controller; ([aéronef identifié]{.DefinedTermLink
      lang="fr"})

  [[operational location]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[operational location]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the physical
      location of an ATS unit; ([emplacement
      opérationnel]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

  [[visual approach]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

  :   [[visual approach]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an approach in which
      the pilot-in-command of an IFR aircraft operating in VMC proceeds
      to the destination aerodrome by using visual reference to the
      surface and, as applicable, by maintaining visual separation from,
      and avoiding the wake turbulence of, a preceding
      aircraft. ([approche visuelle]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Any reference in this Part to an annex to the
  Convention includes the differences notified to ICAO by the Government
  of Canada in respect of the standards specified in that annex.

### [Application]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1000025 .Subheading}

**[[800.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-800.02 .sectionLabel}** This Part does
not apply in respect of any air navigation services that are provided by
or under the authority of the Minister of National Defence.

**\[800.03 to 800.08 reserved\]**

### [Subpart 1 --- Air Traffic Services]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1000028 .Subheading}

#### [Division I --- Prohibitions]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000029 .Subheading}

##### [Alcohol or Drugs --- Air Traffic Controllers and Flight Service Specialists]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525423 .Subheading}

**[[801.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.01 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
act as an air traffic controller or a flight service specialist

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} within eight hours after consuming an alcoholic
  beverage;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} while under the influence of alcohol; or

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} while under the influence of any drug or other
  substance that impairs the person's faculties to the extent that
  aviation safety is affected.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-352, s. 5
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525429){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522562-1525429.html"}
:::

Version](section-801.01-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 801.01"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Air Traffic Control Clearances or Air Traffic Control Instructions]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1000040 .Subheading}

**[[801.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.02 .sectionLabel}** No air traffic
controller shall issue an air traffic control clearance or air traffic
control instruction except in accordance with

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the standards contained in Chapter 3 of Annex 11 to
  the Convention, in the case of airspace in respect of which Canada has
  accepted, by means of a regional air navigation agreement, the
  responsibility of providing air traffic services; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} Standard 821 --- Canadian Domestic Air Traffic
  Control Separation Standards, in the case of any other airspace.

#### [Division II --- ATS Operations Certificate]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1525456 .Subheading}

##### [Requirement for ATS Operations Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1000070 .Subheading}

**[[801.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.06 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate an ATS unit unless the person holds and complies with the
provisions of an ATS operations certificate that authorizes the person
to operate the ATS unit.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2022-246, s. 33(F)](#1380186-1380814){.wb-lbx

##### [Application for ATS Operations Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1000078 .Subheading}

**[[801.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.07 .sectionLabel}** An application
for an ATS operations certificate shall be submitted to the Minister
along with a copy of the proposed ATS site manual for each operational
location to be listed on the certificate.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525463){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522562-1525463.html"}
:::

Version](section-801.07-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 801.07"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Issuance of ATS Operations Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1000103 .Subheading}

- **[[801.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.08
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall issue an ATS
  operations certificate to an applicant, authorizing the applicant to
  operate an ATS unit, if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the Minister has approved an ATS site manual for
    the operational location; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the applicant demonstrates that

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} it has personnel who are qualified to provide an
      air traffic service at the operational location of the ATS unit,
      and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the ATS unit will be operated in a manner that
      provides for safe aircraft operations.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall approve the ATS site manual if it

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} accurately describes the operational location of
    the ATS unit; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} contains the information required under section
    801.10.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525475){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522562-1525475.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-801.08-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 801.08"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Contents of ATS Operations Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1000107 .Subheading}

**[[801.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.09 .sectionLabel}** An ATS operations
certificate shall contain

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the legal name, trade name and address of the holder
  of the certificate;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number of the certificate;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the date of issue of the certificate;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the effective date of certification;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the types of air traffic services that the holder of
  the certificate is authorized to provide; and

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} a list of the operational locations for which an ATS
  site manual has been approved by the Minister.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-352, s. 7
- SOR/2007-290, s. 12
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525484){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522562-1525484.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-801.09-20080101.html "Link to previous version of section 801.09"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Contents of ATS Site Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1000122 .Subheading}

- **[[801.10]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.10
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An ATS site manual shall set out the
  types of air traffic services that are provided by the holder of the
  ATS operations certificate at a specific operational location.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An ATS site manual shall contain

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a table of contents;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any information relating to the administration of
    the ATS unit, including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a record of any amendments to the manual,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a list of the holders of copies of the manual,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a description of the procedure for amending the
      manual,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a description of the organizational structure of
      the ATS unit management,

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} a statement, signed by the holder of the ATS
      operations certificate, certifying that the manual is complete and
      accurate, and

    - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} a statement, signed by the Minister, indicating
      that the Minister has approved the manual;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} any information relating to the operation of the
    ATS unit, including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a description of the airspace and its
      classification,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} where applicable, a description of the
      manoeuvring areas and movement areas of all aerodromes served, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a description of the system used to ensure that
      any operational information necessary for operational staff to
      perform their duties or functions is available on a daily basis;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} if air traffic advisory services or flight
    information services are provided, a description of the procedures
    for providing those services;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a description of the procedures for providing
    emergency assistance services;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a copy of any agreements or memoranda of
    understanding relating to the operation of the ATS unit; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an ATS unit that provides services
    to aerodrome traffic, all information pertaining to all aerodromes
    served in respect of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} emergency response measures,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} aerodrome safety measures,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} access to the movement areas and vehicle
      control procedures,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} apron management plans and apron safety plans,
      and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} information services in respect of runway surface
      friction characteristics.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-352, s. 8
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525510){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522562-1525510.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-801.10-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 801.10"){.PITLink}
:::
