#### [Division III --- Provision of Air Traffic Services]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1525515 .Subheading}

##### [Provision of Services in Class A, B, C, D and E Airspace]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525516 .Subheading}

- **[[801.21]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.21
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The air traffic services provided to
  aircraft operating in Class A or Class B airspace shall include air
  traffic control services.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The air traffic services provided to aircraft
  operating in Class C airspace shall include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} air traffic control services to IFR aircraft;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} conflict resolution between IFR aircraft and VFR
    aircraft;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} conflict resolution between VFR aircraft, on
    request;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} traffic information; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} air traffic control separation between all aircraft
    during runway operations.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The air traffic services provided to aircraft
  operating in Class D airspace shall include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} air traffic control services to IFR aircraft;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} conflict resolution between IFR aircraft and VFR
    aircraft, to the extent that providing the service does not
    interfere with the ability to provide air traffic control services
    or emergency assistance services;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} conflict resolution between VFR aircraft, on
    request, to the extent that providing the service does not interfere
    with the ability to provide air traffic control services or
    emergency assistance services;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} traffic information; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} air traffic control separation between all aircraft
    during runway operations.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The air traffic services provided to aircraft
  operating in Class E airspace shall include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} air traffic control services to IFR aircraft; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} traffic information, to the extent that providing
    the service does not interfere with the ability to provide air
    traffic control services or emergency assistance services.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525535){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522562-1525535.html"}
:::

##### [Provision of Air Traffic Services]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525536 .Subheading}

**[[801.22]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.22 .sectionLabel}** No holder of an
ATS operations certificate shall provide air traffic services at an
operational location unless the location is listed on the ATS operations
certificate and, in the case of air traffic control services, the
services are provided in accordance with

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the standards contained in Chapter 3 of Annex 11 to
  the Convention, in the case of airspace in respect of which Canada has
  accepted, by means of a regional air navigation agreement, the
  responsibility of providing air traffic services; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} Standard 821 --- Canadian Domestic Air Traffic
  Control Separation Standards, in the case of any other airspace.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525541){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522562-1525541.html"}
:::

##### [Provision of Air Traffic Services in Accordance with ESCAT Plan]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525542 .Subheading}

**[[801.23]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.23 .sectionLabel}** If the holder of
an ATS operations certificate is notified by the Minister of National
Defence of the implementation of the ESCAT plan, the certificate holder
shall ensure that air traffic services are provided to aircraft in
accordance with the plan.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525545){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522562-1525545.html"}
:::

##### [Units That Provide Air Traffic Services in English and French]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525546 .Subheading}

**[[801.24]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.24 .sectionLabel}** An ATS unit set
out in column 1 of the table to this section shall provide air traffic
advisory services, relay services of IFR traffic control messages and
air traffic control services in the languages set out in columns 2 to 4,
respectively.

##### [Units That Provide Aeronautical Radiocommunication Services in English]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525556 .Subheading}

**[[801.25]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.25 .sectionLabel}** All ATS units and
FS units shall provide aeronautical radiocommunication services in
English.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525559){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522562-1525559.html"}
:::

**\[801.26 to 801.29 reserved\]**

#### [Division IV --- Training and Competency of Flight Service Specialists]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1525561 .Subheading}

##### [Prohibition and Training]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525562 .Subheading}

- **[[801.30]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.30
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No holder of an ATS operations
  certificate shall permit a person to act as a flight service
  specialist at an ATS unit that the holder operates, and no person
  shall act as a flight service specialist, unless the person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} has successfully completed

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} training that has been accepted by the Minister
      in the performance of the functions of a flight service
      specialist, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a safety-related initial training course on
      human and organizational factors; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} has been certified by the holder of the certificate
    as being competent to perform those functions.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of a person
  who, under supervision, acts as a flight service specialist while
  undergoing

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} instruction, training or testing in respect of
    flight service specialist certification; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} FS unit familiarization in the course of the
    person's employment.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The holder of an ATS operations certificate shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} maintain, for each person who acts as a flight
    service specialist, a training record showing the place where and
    the date on which the person successfully completed the training
    referred to in paragraph (1)(a); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} at the request of the Minister, provide the
    Minister with a copy of the training record of any person acting as
    a flight service specialist at an ATS unit that the holder of the
    certificate operates.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525576){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522562-1525576.html"}
:::

**\[801.31 to 801.39 reserved\]**

#### [Division V --- Separation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1525578 .Subheading}

##### [Wake Turbulence Separation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525579 .Subheading}

**[[801.40]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.40 .sectionLabel}** An air traffic
controller shall establish and maintain wake turbulence separation
between aircraft, in accordance with the requirements of section 821.40
of Standard 821 --- Canadian Domestic Air Traffic Control Separation
Standards, if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} one aircraft takes off from the same airport as
  another aircraft or from an adjacent airport; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} one of the aircraft is flying at an altitude of less
  than 1,000 feet below a preceding aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525584){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522562-1525584.html"}
:::

##### [Airport Separation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525585 .Subheading}

**[[801.41]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.41 .sectionLabel}** An air traffic
controller shall establish and maintain air traffic control separation
between aircraft at a controlled aerodrome, in accordance with the
requirements of section 821.41 of Standard 821 --- Canadian Domestic Air
Traffic Control Separation Standards, if one of the aircraft is
operating on the manoeuvring area, taking off or landing.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525588){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522562-1525588.html"}
:::

##### [Initial IFR Separation on Departure]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525589 .Subheading}

**[[801.42]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.42 .sectionLabel}** Unless ATS
surveillance separation under section 821.06 of Standard 821 ---
Canadian Domestic Air Traffic Control Separation Standards is applied,
an air traffic controller shall, on departure, establish and maintain an
initial IFR air traffic control separation, in accordance with the
requirements of section 821.42 of that standard, between

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} IFR aircraft;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} CVFR aircraft; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} an IFR aircraft and a CVFR aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525595){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522562-1525595.html"}
:::

##### [CMNPS Separation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525596 .Subheading}

**[[801.43]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.43 .sectionLabel}** An air traffic
controller shall establish and maintain, within Canadian minimum
navigation performance specifications (CMNPS) airspace and the CMNPS
transition area, air traffic control separation, in accordance with the
requirements of section 821.43 of Standard 821 --- Canadian Domestic Air
Traffic Control Separation Standards, between aircraft that can be
operated in accordance with CMNPS.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525599){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522562-1525599.html"}
:::

##### [RNPC Separation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525600 .Subheading}

**[[801.44]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.44 .sectionLabel}** An air traffic
controller shall establish and maintain, within required navigation
performance capability (RNPC) airspace, air traffic control separation,
in accordance with the requirements of section 821.44 of Standard 821
--- Canadian Domestic Air Traffic Control Separation Standards, between
aircraft that can be operated in accordance with RNPC.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525603){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522562-1525603.html"}
:::

##### [Separation --- Class F Airspace and Restricted Airspace]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525604 .Subheading}

**[[801.45]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.45 .sectionLabel}** An air traffic
controller shall establish and maintain air traffic control separation,
in accordance with the requirements of section 821.45 of Standard 821
--- Canadian Domestic Air Traffic Control Separation Standards, between
Class F airspace or restricted airspace and an IFR aircraft or CVFR
aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525607){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522562-1525607.html"}
:::

##### [Separation --- Photographic Survey Flights]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525608 .Subheading}

**[[801.46]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.46 .sectionLabel}** An air traffic
controller shall establish and maintain air traffic control separation,
in accordance with the requirements of section 821.46 of Standard 821
--- Canadian Domestic Air Traffic Control Separation Standards, between
an aircraft used to conduct photographic survey flights and an IFR
aircraft or CVFR aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525611){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522562-1525611.html"}
:::

##### [Separation --- Altitude Reservations]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525612 .Subheading}

**[[801.47]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.47 .sectionLabel}** An air traffic
controller shall establish and maintain air traffic control separation,
in accordance with the requirements of section 821.47 of Standard 821
--- Canadian Domestic Air Traffic Control Separation Standards, between

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} altitude reservations; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} an altitude reservation and an IFR aircraft or CVFR
  aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525617){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522562-1525617.html"}
:::

##### [Military IFR Aircraft Separation --- Formation Flights]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525618 .Subheading}

**[[801.48]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.48 .sectionLabel}** An air traffic
controller shall establish and maintain air traffic control separation,
in accordance with the requirements of section 821.48 of Standard 821
--- Canadian Domestic Air Traffic Control Separation Standards, between
a formation flight conducted by military IFR aircraft and another IFR
aircraft or CVFR aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525621){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522562-1525621.html"}
:::

##### [Separation --- USAF Bomber Cell Formation Flights]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525622 .Subheading}

**[[801.49]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.49 .sectionLabel}** An air traffic
controller shall establish and maintain air traffic control separation,
in accordance with the requirements of section 821.49 of Standard 821
--- Canadian Domestic Air Traffic Control Separation Standards, between
a United States Air Force (USAF) bomber cell formation and an IFR
aircraft or CVFR aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525625){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522562-1525625.html"}
:::

##### [Separation --- Turbojet Aircraft Approach and Penetration Turns]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525626 .Subheading}

**[[801.50]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.50 .sectionLabel}** An air traffic
controller shall maintain air traffic control separation, in accordance
with the requirements of section 821.50 of Standard 821 --- Canadian
Domestic Air Traffic Control Separation Standards, between a turbojet
aircraft conducting a jet approach or penetration turn and an IFR
aircraft or CVFR aircraft and between turbojet aircraft conducting a jet
approach or penetration turn.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525629){.wb-lbx

##### [Separation --- Fuel Dumping]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1525630 .Subheading}

**[[801.51]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-801.51 .sectionLabel}** An air traffic
controller shall establish and maintain air traffic control separation,
in accordance with the requirements of section 821.51 of Standard 821
--- Canadian Domestic Air Traffic Control Separation Standards, between
an aircraft jettisoning fuel in flight and another aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 20](#1522562-1525633){.wb-lbx

:::

### [Subpart 2 --- Aeronautical Telecommunications]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1000127 .Subheading}

#### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000128 .Subheading}

**[[802.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-802.01 .sectionLabel}** In this Subpart,
[[aeronautical telecommunications system]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} includes
radio navigation aids and aeronautical communications systems.

#### [Aeronautical Telecommunications Systems]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000130 .Subheading}

- **[[802.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-802.02
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A person who operates any equipment
  that is part of an aeronautical telecommunications system referred to
  in Annex 10 to the Convention shall ensure that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the equipment is installed, maintained and operated
    in accordance with the standards specified in Annex 10 to the
    Convention; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} documentation is maintained that shows how
    compliance with the standards referred to in paragraph (a) is being
    achieved.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall perform a function related to the
  installation, maintenance or operation of any aeronautical
  telecommunications equipment unless the person has successfully
  completed training in the performance of that function and has been
  certified by the operator of the aeronautical telecommunications
  system as being competent to perform that function.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A person who operates any equipment that is part of
  an aeronautical telecommunications system referred to in Annex 10 to
  the Convention shall, at the request of the Minister, provide the
  Minister with a copy of the documentation referred to in paragraph
  (1)(b).

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} [\[Repealed, SOR/2020-151, s. 23\]]{.Repealed}

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-151, s. 23](#1252621-1257228){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1252621-1257228.html"}
:::

Version](section-802.02-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 802.02"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Subpart 3 --- Aeronautical Information Services]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1000141 .Subheading}

#### [Provision of Aeronautical Information Services]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000142 .Subheading}

- **[[803.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-803.01
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} In this Subpart, [[aeronautical
  information services]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the services
  necessary to meet the requirements of Annexes 4 and 15 to the
  Convention that relate to aeronautical information.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall provide aeronautical information
  services except in accordance with the standards set out in Annexes 4
  and 15 to the Convention.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2002-352, s. 9
:::

#### [Development and Publication of Instrument Procedures]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000148 .Subheading}

**[[803.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-803.02 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
publish or submit for publishing in the Canada Air Pilot an instrument
procedure unless the procedure has been developed

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} in accordance with the standards and criteria
  specified in the manual entitled Criteria for the Development of
  Instrument Procedures; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} by a person who has successfully completed training
  in the interpretation and application of the standards and criteria
  specified in the manual entitled Criteria for the Development of
  Instrument Procedures, which training has been accepted by the
  Minister.

**\[803.03 to 803.08 reserved\]**

### [Subpart 4 --- Aviation Weather Services and Assessment of Runway Visibility]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1000153 .Subheading}

#### [Division I --- Aviation Weather Services]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000154 .Subheading}

##### [Provision of Aviation Weather Services]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1000155 .Subheading}

- **[[804.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-804.01
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to Division III, a person
  who provides aviation weather services shall provide them in
  accordance with the standards specified in

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} Annex 3 to the Convention;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the Manual of Standards and Procedures for Aviation
    Weather Forecasts; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the Manual of Surface Weather Observations.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of paragraph (1)(a), the words
  [[aerodrome]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} and [[aircraft]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}
  used in Annex 3 to the Convention have the same meaning as in
  subsection 3(1) of the Act.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of paragraph (1)(a), the expressions
  [[alternate aerodrome]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, [[control
  area]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} and [[flight crew
  member]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} used in Annex 3 to the Convention have
  the same meaning as in subsection 101.01(1).

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of paragraph (1)(a),
  [[operator]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}, used in Annex 3 to the Convention,
  has the meaning assigned by the definition [[air
  operator]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} in subsection 101.01(1).

#### [Division III --- Runway Visibility]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000169 .Subheading}

##### [Application]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1000170 .Subheading}

**[[804.22]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-804.22 .sectionLabel}** This Division
applies in respect of the making and reporting of the assessment of
runway visibility at an aerodrome.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-199, s. 22
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 21](#1522564-1525635){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522564-1525635.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-804.22-20061201.html "Link to previous version of section 804.22"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Visibility Markers and Conversion Tables]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1000174 .Subheading}

- **[[804.23]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-804.23
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Before the operator of an aerodrome
  gives permission to a person to make or report an assessment of runway
  visibility at an aerodrome, the operator shall produce a visibility
  markers chart that meets the requirements of section 824.23 of
  Standard 824 --- Runway Visibility Assessment Standards.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If runway edge lights are used to assess the runway
  visibility, the operator shall produce a conversion table before
  giving their permission.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-199, s. 22
- [SOR/2025-98, s. 22](#1522566-1525640){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1522566-1525640.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-804.23-20061201.html "Link to previous version of section 804.23"){.PITLink}
:::

##### [Person Qualified to Assess and Report Runway Visibility]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1000180 .Subheading}

**[[804.24]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-804.24 .sectionLabel}** Except for a
pilot who meets the requirements of section 602.131, no person other
than a person qualified in accordance with section 804.26 shall assess
runway visibility and report the assessment.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-199, s. 22
:::

##### [Assessment and Reporting of Runway Visibility]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1000184 .Subheading}

- **[[804.25]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-804.25
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A person qualified to assess runway
  visibility shall obtain authorization to report an assessment of
  runway visibility from the operator of the aerodrome.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person qualified to assess runway visibility shall
  assess runway visibility and report the assessment in accordance with
  section 824.25 of Standard 824 --- Runway Visibility Assessment
  Standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-199, s. 22
:::

##### [Qualifications and Training]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1000190 .Subheading}

**[[804.26]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-804.26 .sectionLabel}** A person who
assesses runway visibility shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} have a distant visual acuity with or without
  correction of 6/12 (20/40) or better in each eye separately and
  binocular visual acuity of 6/9 (20/30) or better;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} be qualified to operate a vehicle equipped with a
  two-way radio communication system on the manoeuvring area of the
  aerodrome; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} have received the training set out in section 824.26
  of Standard 824 --- Runway Visibility Assessment Standards.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2006-199, s. 22
:::

### [Subpart 5 --- Safety Management System]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1000197 .Subheading}

#### [Requirements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000198 .Subheading}

**[[805.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-805.01 .sectionLabel}** The safety
management system required under section 107.02 in respect of an
applicant for, or a holder of, an ATS operations certificate shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} meet the requirements of Subpart 7 of Part I and
  section 805.02; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} be under the control of the accountable executive
  appointed under paragraph 106.02(1)(a).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-290, s. 13
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-805.01-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 805.01"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Components of the Safety Management System]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000204 .Subheading}

- **[[805.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-805.02
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The safety management system shall
  include, among others, the following components:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a safety management plan that includes

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a safety policy that the accountable executive
      has approved and communicated to all employees,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the roles and responsibilities of personnel
      assigned duties under the safety management system,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} performance goals and a means of measuring
      attainment of those goals,

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a policy for the internal reporting of hazards,
      incidents and accidents, including the conditions under which
      immunity from disciplinary action will be granted, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} a process for reviewing the safety management
      system to determine its effectiveness;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} procedures for reporting hazards, incidents and
    accidents to the appropriate manager;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} procedures for the collection of data relating to
    hazards, incidents and accidents;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} procedures for the exchange of information in
    respect of hazards, incidents and accidents among the operators of
    aircraft and the provider of air traffic services at an airport and
    the airport operator;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} procedures for analysing data obtained under
    paragraph (c) and during an audit conducted under subsection
    805.03(3) and for taking corrective actions;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} training requirements for the accountable executive
    and for personnel assigned duties under the safety management
    system;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} procedures for making progress reports to the
    accountable executive at intervals determined by the accountable
    executive and other reports as needed in urgent cases; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} procedures for involving employees in the
    implementation and ongoing development of the safety management
    system.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The components specified in subsection (1) shall be
  set out in a manual or another document established by the holder of
  the ATS operations certificate that includes

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a record of any amendments to the manual or
    document;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a description of the procedures for amending the
    manual or document; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a statement, signed by the accountable executive,
    certifying that the manual or document is complete and its content
    accurate.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall approve the manual or document if
  it contains the information and statement required under subsection
  (2).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-290, s. 13
:::

#### [Quality Assurance Program]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000227 .Subheading}

- **[[805.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-805.03
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The quality assurance program
  required under paragraph 107.03(g) in respect of an applicant for, or
  a holder of, an ATS operations certificate shall include a process for
  quality assurance that includes periodic reviews or audits of the
  activities authorized under a certificate and reviews or audits, for
  cause, of those activities.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The holder of an ATS operations certificate shall
  ensure that records relating to the findings resulting from the
  quality assurance program are distributed to the appropriate manager
  for corrective action.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The holder of an ATS operations certificate shall
  establish an audit system in respect of the quality assurance program
  that consists of the following:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} an initial audit conducted within 12 months after
    the day on which the ATS operations certificate is issued;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} an audit of the entire quality assurance program
    carried out every three years, calculated

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an ATS operations certificate
      issued before January 1, 2008, from that date, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an ATS operations certificate
      issued on or after January 1, 2008, from the date of the initial
      audit;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} checklists of all activities carried out under the
    certificate;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a record of each occurrence of compliance or
    non-compliance with the manual or any other document established
    under subsection 805.02(2) that is found during an audit referred to
    in paragraph (a) or (b);

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} procedures for ensuring that each finding of an
    audit is communicated to the accountable executive;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} follow-up procedures for ensuring that corrective
    actions are effective; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a system for recording the findings of an audit
    referred to in paragraph (a) or (b), corrective actions and
    follow-ups.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The audit referred to in paragraph (3)(b) shall be
  carried out in one of the following ways:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} as a complete audit, or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} as a series of audits conducted at intervals
    determined by the holder of the ATS operations certificate and set
    out in the manual or document established under subsection
    805.02(2).

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The records resulting from a system required under
  paragraph (3)(g) shall be retained for the greater of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} two audit cycles, and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} two years.

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} The duties related to the quality assurance program
  that involve specific tasks or activities among the activities of an
  ATS operations certificate holder shall be fulfilled by persons who
  are not responsible for carrying out those tasks or activities unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the size, nature and complexity of the operations
    and activities authorized under the ATS operations certificate
    justify the fulfilling of those duties by the person responsible for
    carrying out those tasks or activities;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the holder of the ATS operations certificate
    demonstrates to the Minister by means of a risk analysis, that the
    fulfilling of those duties by the person responsible for carrying
    out those tasks or activities will not result in an unacceptable
    risk to aviation safety; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the holder of the ATS operations certificate
    provides the Minister, in writing, with the information required
    under paragraphs (a) and (b).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-290, s. 13
- [SOR/2019-122, s. 19](#1126368-1131011){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126368-1131011.html"}
- [SOR/2019-295, s. 20](#1194411-1195766){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1194411-1195766.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-805.03-20190515.html "Link to previous version of section 805.03"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Duties of the Certificate Holder]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000253 .Subheading}

**[[805.04]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-805.04 .sectionLabel}** The holder of an
ATS operations certificate shall ensure that

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} corrective actions are taken in respect of any
  findings resulting from the safety management system referred to in
  section 805.01; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the accountable executive performs the duties
  prescribed in section 805.05.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-290, s. 13
:::

#### [Management of the Safety Management System]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000259 .Subheading}

- **[[805.05]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-805.05
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The accountable executive shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} implement a reporting system to ensure the timely
    collection of information related to hazards, incidents and
    accidents that may adversely affect safety;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} identify hazards and carry out risk management
    analyses of those hazards;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} investigate, analyze and identify the cause or
    probable cause of all hazards, incidents and accidents identified
    under the safety management system;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} implement a safety data system, by either
    electronic or other means, to monitor and analyze trends in hazards,
    incidents and accidents;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} monitor and evaluate the results of corrective
    actions with respect to hazards, incidents and accidents;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} monitor the concerns of the civil aviation industry
    in respect of safety and their perceived effect on the holder of the
    ATS operations certificate; and

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} determine the adequacy of the training required by
    paragraph 805.02(1)(f).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The accountable executive shall, if a finding
  resulting from a quality assurance program referred to in subsection
  805.03(1) or a safety management system referred to in section 805.01
  is reported to them,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} determine what, if any, corrective actions are
    required and carry out those actions;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} keep a record of any determination made under
    paragraph (a) and the reason for it;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if management functions have been assigned to
    another person under subsection (3), communicate any determination
    regarding a corrective action to that person; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} notify the certificate holder of any systemic
    deficiency and of the corrective action taken.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The accountable executive may assign the management
  functions of the safety management system referred to in section
  805.01 to another person if the assignment and its scope are described
  in the manual or document referred to in subsection 805.02(2).

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The person to whom management functions have been
  assigned under subsection (3) shall notify the accountable executive
  of any systemic deficiency and of the corrective action taken.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} The responsibility and accountability of the
  accountable executive are not affected by the assignment of management
  functions to another person under subsection (3).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2007-290, s. 13
- [SOR/2019-122, s. 20](#1126370-1131015){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126370-1131015.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-805.05-20080101.html "Link to previous version of section 805.05"){.PITLink}
:::

### [Subpart 6 --- Levels of Service]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1000279 .Subheading}

#### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000280 .Subheading}

**[[806.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-806.01 .sectionLabel}** In this Subpart,

[[aeronautical study]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[aeronautical study]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a study designed to
    identify the risks to aviation safety attendant upon a particular
    course of action and to determine how to eliminate or reduce those
    risks; ([étude aéronautique]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[level of service]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[level of service]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the type or nature of
    civil air navigation services provided to support safe and efficient
    aircraft operations, and includes the times at which the services
    are provided. ([niveau de service]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-119, s. 46](#1126796-1144332){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1126796-1144332.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-806.01-20060322.html "Link to previous version of section 806.01"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Maintenance of Level of Service]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000284 .Subheading}

- **[[806.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-806.02
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every person who provides a civil
  air navigation service shall, where the person proposes to terminate
  the service or to reduce the level of service that is provided, notify
  the Minister

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a proposal to terminate the service
    or to materially reduce the level of service, at least 60 days
    before the termination or reduction; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in all other cases, as far in advance of the
    reduction as reasonably practicable.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} On receipt of a notice referred to in subsection (1)
  from the ANS Corporation, the Minister may request the ANS Corporation
  to conduct an aeronautical study for the purpose of demonstrating that
  the risk to aviation safety would not be unacceptably increased by the
  proposed termination or reduction in the level of service.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Where the Minister requests the ANS Corporation to
  conduct an aeronautical study pursuant to subsection (2), the ANS
  Corporation shall not implement the proposed termination or reduction
  in the level of service until the Minister has been provided with a
  copy of the study and has had a reasonable opportunity to review it.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} Where, after reviewing an aeronautical study
  conducted pursuant to subsection (2), the Minister is of the opinion
  that an unacceptable risk to aviation safety would result from the
  proposed termination or reduction in the level of service, the
  Minister may, by order, direct the ANS Corporation to maintain its
  level of service in accordance with the terms and conditions specified
  in the order.

#### [Increase in Level of Service]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000292 .Subheading}

**[[806.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-806.03 .sectionLabel}** Where, after
conducting an aeronautical study or reviewing an aeronautical study
conducted by another person or organization, the Minister is of the
opinion that the level of service provided by the ANS Corporation should
be increased in the interests of aviation safety, the Minister may, by
order, direct the ANS Corporation to increase its level of service in
accordance with the terms and conditions specified in the order.

**\[806.04 to 806.08 reserved\]**

### [Subpart 7 --- Aviation Occurrences]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1000295 .Subheading}

#### [Reporting of Aviation Occurrences]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000296 .Subheading}

**[[807.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-807.01 .sectionLabel}** The holder of an
ATS operations certificate shall report to the Minister any aviation
occurrence information specified in the CADORS Manual in accordance with
the criteria and reporting procedures specified in that manual.

**\[807.02 to 807.06 reserved\]**

## [Part IX --- Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1000299 .Part}

### [Division I --- General Provisions]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1000300 .Subheading}

#### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1110493 .Subheading}

**[[900.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-900.01 .sectionLabel}** The following
definitions apply in this Part.

[[advertised event]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[advertised event]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an outdoor event that
    is advertised to the general public, including a concert, festival,
    market or sporting event. ([événement annoncé]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[autonomous]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[autonomous]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed, SOR/2025-70, s.
    43\]]{.Repealed}

[[BVLOS]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[BVLOS]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means beyond visual
    line-of-sight. ([BVLOS]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[BVLOS operation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[BVLOS operation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an operation of a
    remotely piloted aircraft that is not in visual line-of-sight, but
    does not include an extended VLOS operation or a sheltered
    operation. ([opération en BVLOS]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[command and control link]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[command and control link]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed,
    SOR/2025-70, s. 43\]]{.Repealed}

[[contingency procedures]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[contingency procedures]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the procedures
    to be followed to address conditions that could lead to an unsafe
    situation. ([procédure de contingence]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[contingency volume]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[contingency volume]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the area
    immediately surrounding the flight geography within which
    contingency procedures are intended to be used to return a remotely
    piloted aircraft to the flight geography or safely terminate the
    flight. ([volume de contingence]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[control station]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[control station]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed, SOR/2025-70, s.
    43\]]{.Repealed}

[[detect and avoid functions]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[detect and avoid functions]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed,
    SOR/2025-70, s. 43\]]{.Repealed}

[[extended VLOS operation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[extended VLOS operation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an operation
    of a remotely piloted aircraft that is not in visual line-of-sight
    but during which unaided visual contact is maintained with the
    airspace in which the aircraft is operating in a manner sufficient
    to detect conflicting air traffic and other hazards and take action
    to avoid them. ([opération en VLOS prolongée]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[first-person view device]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[first-person view device]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed,
    SOR/2025-70, s. 43\]]{.Repealed}

[[flight geography]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[flight geography]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the area within which
    a remotely piloted aircraft is intended to fly for a specific
    operation. ([géographie de vol]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[flight termination system]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[flight termination system]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}[\[Repealed,
    SOR/2025-70, s. 43\]]{.Repealed}

[[fly-away]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[fly-away]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means, in respect of a remotely
    piloted aircraft, an interruption or loss of the command and control
    link such that the pilot is no longer able to control the aircraft
    and the aircraft no longer follows its preprogrammed procedures or
    operates in a predictable or planned
    manner. ([dérive]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[ground risk buffer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[ground risk buffer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the area
    immediately surrounding the contingency volume that, when measured
    horizontally from the perimeter of the contingency volume, is at
    least equal to the planned maximum altitude of the remotely piloted
    aircraft for the flight. ([tampon de risque au sol]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[mandatory action]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[mandatory action]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the inspection,
    repair or modification of a remotely piloted aircraft system that is
    necessary to prevent an unsafe or potentially unsafe
    condition. ([mesure obligatoire]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[medium remotely piloted aircraft]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[medium remotely piloted aircraft]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a
    remotely piloted aircraft that has an operating weight of more than
    25 kg (55 pounds) but not more than 150 kg (331 pounds). ([aéronef
    télépiloté moyen]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[operating weight]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[operating weight]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the weight of a
    remotely piloted aircraft at any point during a flight, including
    any payload and any safety equipment that is on board or otherwise
    connected to the aircraft. ([masse opérationnelle]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[operational volume]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[operational volume]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the area that is
    composed of the flight geography, contingency volume and ground risk
    buffer. ([volume opérationnel]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[payload]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[payload]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a system, object or collection
    of objects, including a slung load, that is on board or is otherwise
    connected to a remotely piloted aircraft but that is not required
    for flight. ([charge utile]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[populated area]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[populated area]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an area with more than
    five people per square kilometre. ([zone peuplée]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[RPAS ground school instruction]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[RPAS ground school instruction]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means
    instructor-led training given to one or more persons, delivered
    in-person or virtually, and provided through an organized program of
    lectures, homework or self-paced study. ([instruction théorique au
    sol pour les SATP]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[RPAS operations manual]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[RPAS operations manual]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the manual
    established by an RPAS operator under section 901.217. ([manuel
    d'exploitation de SATP]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[RPAS operator]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[RPAS operator]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the holder of an RPAS
    operator certificate. ([exploitant de SATP]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[RPAS operator certificate]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[RPAS operator certificate]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a
    certificate issued under section 901.214. ([certificat
    d'exploitation de SATP]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[sheltered operation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[sheltered operation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an operation of a
    remotely piloted aircraft that is not in visual line-of-sight and
    during which the aircraft remains at a distance of less than 200
    feet (61 m), measured horizontally, from a building or structure and
    at an altitude no greater than 100 feet (30 m) above that building
    or structure. ([opération protégée]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[small remotely piloted aircraft]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[small remotely piloted aircraft]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a
    remotely piloted aircraft that has an operating weight of at least
    250 g (0.55 pounds) but not more than 25 kg (55 pounds). ([petit
    aéronef télépiloté]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[sparsely populated area]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[sparsely populated area]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an area with
    more than 5 but not more than 25 people per square kilometre. ([zone
    peu densément peuplée]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[Standard 922]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[Standard 922]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means Standard 922 --- RPAS
    Safety Assurance, published by the Department of Transport. ([norme
    922]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[visual line-of-sight]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[visual line-of-sight]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} or
    [[VLOS]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means unaided visual contact maintained
    with a remotely piloted aircraft in a manner sufficient to maintain
    control of the aircraft, know its location and scan the airspace in
    which it is operating in order to detect conflicting air traffic and
    other hazards and take action to avoid them. ([visibilité
    directe]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"} ou [VLOS]{.DefinedTermLink
    lang="fr"})

[[visual observer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[visual observer]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a crew member who is
    trained to assist the pilot in ensuring the safe conduct of a
    flight. ([observateur visuel]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[VLOS operation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[VLOS operation]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means an operation of a
    remotely piloted aircraft in visual line-of-sight. ([opération en
    VLOS]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[Water Aerodrome Supplement]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[Water Aerodrome Supplement]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} has the same
    meaning as in section 300.01. ([Supplément
    hydroaérodromes]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote

### [Division II --- General Operating and Flight Rules]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1111560 .Subheading}

::: HistoricalNote
\[

- SOR/2025-70, s. 46

\]
:::

#### [Reckless or Negligent Operation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1111561 .Subheading}

**[[900.06]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-900.06 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
operate a remotely piloted aircraft system in such a reckless or
negligent manner as to endanger or be likely to endanger aviation safety
or the safety of any person.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-11, s. 23](#1045417-1111564){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045417-1111564.html"}
:::

#### [Inadvertent Entry Into Restricted Airspace]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1528552 .Subheading}

**[[900.07]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-900.07 .sectionLabel}** A person who
operates a remotely piloted aircraft shall ensure that the appropriate
air traffic control unit, flight service station or user agency is
notified immediately any time the aircraft is no longer under the
person's control and inadvertently enters or is likely to enter into
Class F Special Use Restricted airspace, as specified in the Designated
Airspace Handbook.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 47](#1516917-1528555){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1516917-1528555.html"}
:::

#### [Prohibition --- Emergency Security Perimeter]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1528556 .Subheading}

- **[[900.08]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-900.08
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall operate a remotely
  piloted aircraft over or within the security perimeter established by
  a public authority in response to an emergency.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply to the operation of a
  remotely piloted aircraft for the purpose of an operation to save
  human life, a police operation, a fire-fighting operation or any other
  operation that is conducted in the service of a public authority.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 47](#1516917-1528566){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1516917-1528566.html"}
:::

#### [Prohibition --- Commercial Air Service]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1528567 .Subheading}

- **[[900.09]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-900.09
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (2) and (3),
  no person shall operate a remotely piloted aircraft having an
  operating weight of 250 g (0.55 pounds) or more to provide a
  commercial air service unless that person is Canadian or an employee,
  an agent or mandatary or a representative of an RPAS operator.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person who does not meet the criteria referred to
  in subsection (1) may operate a remotely piloted aircraft to provide a
  specialty air service if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} they are a citizen, permanent resident or
    corporation of a foreign state with which Canada has entered into a
    free trade agreement that Canada has implemented and under which the
    operation is authorized; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the operation is conducted in accordance with a
    special flight operations certificate --- RPAS issued under section
    903.03.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A person that does not meet the criteria referred to
  in subsection (1) may operate a remotely piloted aircraft to provide
  an air transport service if the person holds a licence issued under
  section 61 of the [Canada Transportation Act](/eng/acts/C-10.4).

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 47](#1516917-1528575){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1516917-1528575.html"}
:::

**\[900.10 to 900.12 reserved\]**

### [Division III --- Registration of Remotely Piloted Aircraft]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1528577 .Subheading}

#### [Registration]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1528578 .Subheading}

- **[[900.13]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-900.13
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no person
  shall operate a remotely piloted aircraft system that includes a
  remotely piloted aircraft having an operating weight of 250 g (0.55
  pounds) or more unless the remotely piloted aircraft is registered in
  accordance with this Division.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A person may operate a remotely piloted aircraft
  system that includes a remotely piloted aircraft that is not
  registered in accordance with this Division if the operation is
  conducted in accordance with a special flight operations certificate
  --- RPAS issued under section 903.03.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 47](#1516917-1528583){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1516917-1528583.html"}
:::

#### [Registration Number]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1528584 .Subheading}

**[[900.14]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-900.14 .sectionLabel}** No pilot shall
operate a remotely piloted aircraft system unless the registration
number referred to in paragraph 900.16(3)(a) is clearly visible on the
remotely piloted aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 47](#1516917-1528587){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1516917-1528587.html"}
:::

#### [Qualifications To Be Registered Owner of Remotely Piloted Aircraft]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1528588 .Subheading}

- **[[900.15]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-900.15
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), a person
  is qualified to be the registered owner of a remotely piloted aircraft
  if they are

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a Canadian citizen or permanent resident of Canada;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a corporation or entity that is incorporated or
    formed under the laws of Canada or a province; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a government in Canada or an agent or mandatary of
    such a government.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No individual is qualified to be the registered owner
  of a remotely piloted aircraft unless that individual is at least 14
  years of age.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 47](#1516917-1528596){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1516917-1528596.html"}
:::

#### [Registration Requirements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1528597 .Subheading}

- **[[900.16]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-900.16
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall, on receipt of an
  application, register a remotely piloted aircraft if the applicant is
  qualified to be the registered owner of the aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The application shall include the following
  information:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the applicant is an individual,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the applicant's name and address,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the applicant's date of birth, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} an indication as to whether the applicant is a
      Canadian citizen or permanent resident of Canada;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the applicant is a corporation or entity that is
    incorporated or formed under the laws of Canada or a province,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the corporation's or entity's legal name and
      address,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the name and title of the person making the
      application, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the business number assigned to the corporation
      or entity by the Minister of National Revenue, if any;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the applicant is His Majesty in right of Canada
    or a province,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the name of the government body, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the name and title of the person making the
      application;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} an indication as to whether the aircraft was
    purchased or built by the applicant;

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the date of purchase of the aircraft by the
    applicant, if applicable;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the manufacturer and model of the aircraft, if
    applicable;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} the serial number of the aircraft, if applicable;

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} the category of aircraft, such as a fixed-wing
    aircraft, rotary-wing aircraft, hybrid aircraft or lighter-than-air
    aircraft; and

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} any Canadian registration number previously issued
    in respect of the aircraft.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} On registering the remotely piloted aircraft, the
  Minister shall issue to the registered owner of the aircraft a
  certificate of registration that includes

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a registration number;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the registered owner; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the serial number of the aircraft, if applicable.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 47](#1516917-1528623){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1516917-1528623.html"}
:::

#### [Register of Remotely Piloted Aircraft]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1528624 .Subheading}

**[[900.17]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-900.17 .sectionLabel}** The Minister
shall establish and maintain a register of remotely piloted aircraft in
which there shall be entered, in respect of each aircraft for which a
certificate of registration has been issued under section 900.16,

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name and address of the registered owner;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the registration number referred to in paragraph
  900.16(3)(a); and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} any other particulars concerning the aircraft that
  the Minister determines necessary for the registration of the remotely
  piloted aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 47](#1516917-1528630){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1516917-1528630.html"}
:::

#### [Cancellation of Certificate of Registration]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1528631 .Subheading}

- **[[900.18]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-900.18
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A registered owner of a remotely
  piloted aircraft shall, within seven days after becoming aware that
  any of the following events has occurred, notify the Minister that

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is destroyed;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is permanently withdrawn from use;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft is missing and the search for the
    aircraft is terminated;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the aircraft has been missing for 60 days or more;
    or

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the registered owner has transferred legal custody
    and control of the aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} When an event referred to in subsection (1) has
  occurred, the certificate of registration in respect of the remotely
  piloted aircraft is cancelled.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The certificate of registration of a remotely piloted
  aircraft is cancelled when

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the registered owner of the aircraft dies;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the entity that is the registered owner of the
    aircraft is wound up, dissolved or amalgamated with another entity;
    or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the registered owner of the aircraft ceases to be
    qualified to be a registered owner under section 900.15.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Division, an owner has legal
  custody and control of a remotely piloted aircraft when the owner has
  complete responsibility for the operation and maintenance of the
  remotely piloted aircraft system of which the aircraft is an element.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 47](#1516917-1528646){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1516917-1528646.html"}
:::

#### [Change of Name or Address]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1528647 .Subheading}

**[[900.19]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-900.19 .sectionLabel}** The registered
owner of a remotely piloted aircraft shall notify the Minister of any
change in the name or address of the registered owner by not later than
seven days after the change.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 47](#1516917-1528650){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1516917-1528650.html"}
:::

#### [Access to Certificate of Registration]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1528651 .Subheading}

**[[900.20]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-900.20 .sectionLabel}** No pilot shall
operate a remotely piloted aircraft system unless the certificate of
registration issued in respect of the remotely piloted aircraft that is
an element of the system is easily accessible to the pilot for the
duration of the operation.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 47](#1516917-1528654){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1516917-1528654.html"}
:::

#### [Division III --- General Operating and Flight Rules]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1111649 .Subheading}

##### [Visual Line-of-sight]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1111650 .Subheading}

- **[[901.11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.11
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no pilot
  shall operate a remotely piloted aircraft system unless the pilot or a
  visual observer has the aircraft in visual line-of-sight.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A pilot may operate a remotely piloted aircraft
  system without the pilot or a visual observer having the aircraft in
  visual line-of-sight if the operation is conducted in accordance with
  a special flight operations certificate --- RPAS issued under section
  903.03.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-11, s. 23](#1045417-1111655){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045417-1111655.html"}
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 51](#1516925-1527690){.wb-lbx

:::

:::

**\[901.12 reserved\]**

**[[901.12]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.12 .sectionLabel}** [\[Reserved,
SOR/2025-70, s. 52\]]{.Repealed}

Version](section-901.12-20190109.html "Link to previous version of section 901.12"){.PITLink}

##### [Prohibition --- Canadian Domestic Airspace]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1111662 .Subheading}

- **[[901.13]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.13
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), no pilot
  operating a remotely piloted aircraft shall cause the aircraft to
  leave Canadian Domestic Airspace.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A pilot may operate a remotely piloted aircraft
  outside of Canadian Domestic Airspace if the operation is conducted in
  accordance with a special flight operations certificate --- RPAS
  issued under section 903.03.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-11, s. 23](#1045417-1111665){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045417-1111665.html"}
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 53](#1516932-1527697){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1516932-1527697.html"}
:::

[Previous
Version](section-901.13-20190109.html "Link to previous version of section 901.13"){.PITLink}
