#### [Division X --- Training and Flight Review]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1528013 .Subheading}

##### [Prohibition --- Flight Reviewer]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528014 .Subheading}

- **[[901.175]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.175
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No person shall perform the duties
  of a flight reviewer for a flight review referred to in paragraph
  901.64(c) unless that person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} holds a pilot certificate --- remotely piloted
    aircraft --- advanced operations endorsed with a flight reviewer
    rating under section 901.176 or a pilot certificate --- remotely
    piloted aircraft --- level 1 complex operations endorsed with such a
    rating; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is able to demonstrate that they are affiliated
    with a training provider that has made a declaration to the Minister
    in accordance with the requirements of section 921.05 or 921.08 of
    Standard 921 --- Remotely Piloted Aircraft.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} No person shall perform the duties of a flight
  reviewer for a flight review referred to in paragraph 901.90(e) unless
  that person

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} holds a pilot certificate --- remotely piloted
    aircraft --- level 1 complex operations endorsed with a flight
    reviewer rating under section 901.176; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} is able to demonstrate that they are affiliated
    with a training provider that has made a declaration to the Minister
    in accordance with the requirements of section 921.08 of Standard
    921 --- Remotely Piloted Aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528023){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528023.html"}
:::

##### [Flight Reviewer Rating]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528024 .Subheading}

**[[901.176]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.176 .sectionLabel}** The Minister
shall, on receipt of an application, endorse the applicant's pilot
certificate with a flight reviewer rating if the applicant demonstrates
to the Minister that the applicant

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} is at least 18 years of age;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} holds a pilot certificate --- remotely piloted
  aircraft --- advanced operations issued under section 901.64 or a
  pilot certificate --- remotely piloted aircraft --- level 1 complex
  operations issued under section 901.90 and meets the recency
  requirements set out in section 901.65 or 901.91, as the case may be;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} has held one of the certificates referred to in
  paragraph (b) for at least six months immediately before the date of
  application; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} has successfully completed the examination "Remotely
  Piloted Aircraft Systems --- Flight Reviewers" in accordance with the
  document entitled Knowledge Requirements for Pilots of Remotely
  Piloted Aircraft Systems, 250 g up to and including 150 kg, Basic and
  Advanced Operations, TP 15263, published by the Minister.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528031){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528031.html"}
:::

##### [Examination Rules]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528032 .Subheading}

**[[901.177]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.177 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
commit an act referred to in paragraphs 901.58(a) to (c) in respect of
an examination referred to in paragraph 901.176(d).

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528035){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528035.html"}
:::

##### [Retaking of Examination]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528036 .Subheading}

**[[901.178]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.178 .sectionLabel}** No person who
fails an examination referred to in paragraph 901.176(d) shall retake
the examination for a period of 24 hours after the examination.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528039){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528039.html"}
:::

##### [Eligibility to Make Declaration]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528040 .Subheading}

**[[901.179]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.179 .sectionLabel}** A training
provider is eligible to make a declaration to the Minister in accordance
with the requirements of section 921.05 or 921.08 of Standard 921 ---
Remotely Piloted Aircraft if the training provider is Canadian.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528043){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528043.html"}
:::

##### [Training Provider Requirements --- Flight Reviews]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528044 .Subheading}

**[[901.180]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.180 .sectionLabel}** A training
provider that has made a declaration referred to in paragraph
901.175(1)(b) or (2)(b) shall

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} submit to the Minister the name of any person who is
  affiliated with the provider and who intends to perform the duties of
  a flight reviewer;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the person referred to in paragraph (a)
  conducts flight reviews in accordance with section 901.181; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the person referred to in paragraph (a) ceases to
  be affiliated with the provider, notify the Minister of that fact
  within seven days after the day on which the affiliation ceases.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528050){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528050.html"}
:::

##### [Conduct of Flight Reviews]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528051 .Subheading}

**[[901.181]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.181 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
conduct a flight review referred to in paragraph 901.64(c) or 901.90(e)
unless the review is conducted in accordance with section 921.06 of
Standard 921 --- Remotely Piloted Aircraft.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528057){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528057.html"}
:::

##### [Training Provider Requirements --- RPAS Ground School Instruction]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528058 .Subheading}

- **[[901.182]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.182
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} No training provider shall deliver
  the RPAS ground school instruction referred to in paragraph 901.90(c)
  unless the training provider

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} has made a declaration to the Minister in
    accordance with the requirements of section 921.08 of Standard 921
    --- Remotely Piloted Aircraft; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} has appointed a chief ground instructor responsible
    for the delivery of the RPAS ground school instruction.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} A training provider shall inform the Minister within
  30 days after any change in the appointment of a chief ground
  instructor.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528065){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528065.html"}
:::

##### [Requirements for Chief Ground Instructor]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528066 .Subheading}

**[[901.183]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.183 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
act as chief ground instructor unless the person holds a pilot
certificate --- remotely piloted aircraft --- level 1 complex operations
issued under section 901.90 and endorsed with a flight reviewer rating
under section 901.176.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528069){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528069.html"}
:::

##### [Proof of Ground Instruction]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528070 .Subheading}

**[[901.184]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.184 .sectionLabel}** A training
provider shall provide written proof of completion to every person who
completes the RPAS ground school instruction referred to in paragraph
901.90(c).

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528073){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528073.html"}
:::

**\[901.185 to 901.193 reserved\]**

#### [Division XI --- RPAS Declaration]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1528075 .Subheading}

##### [Declaration]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528076 .Subheading}

- **[[901.194]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.194
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A person who makes a declaration to
  the Minister in respect of a model of remotely piloted aircraft system
  and in respect of any technical requirement set out in Standard 922
  shall do so in accordance with subsection (2).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The declaration shall

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} specify the legal name, trade name, if any, address
    and contact information of the person making the declaration and, in
    respect of the remotely piloted aircraft system,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the name of the model,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the configurable elements of the system,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the operations described in section 901.69 or
      901.87 that the model of system is intended to conduct, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the technical requirements set out in Standard
      922 that are the subject of the declaration; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} indicate that the person making the declaration has
    verified that the model of system meets the technical requirements
    specified under subparagraph (a)(iv) and, in the case of a model for
    which an acceptance letter has been issued under section 901.196,
    has completed that verification using the means set out in the
    person's application for an acceptance letter under subparagraph
    901.196(2)(c)(ii).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a model of remotely piloted aircraft
  system that is intended to conduct any of the operations described in
  paragraph 901.69(f) or (g) or 901.87(b), no person shall provide the
  Minister with a declaration referred to in subsection (1) unless an
  acceptance letter has been issued in respect of that model of system
  under section 901.196 in the two years before the making of the
  declaration.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The declaration is invalid if

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the Minister has determined that the model of
    remotely piloted aircraft system does not meet the technical
    requirements specified under subparagraph (2)(a)(iv);

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the person who has made the declaration has
    provided a notification to the Minister under section 901.195; or

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the person who has made the declaration has failed
    to submit their annual report in accordance with section 901.199.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} In the case referred to in paragraph (4)(b) in
  respect of a notification referred to in paragraph 901.195(1)(b), the
  declaration is only invalid with respect to the operations described
  in paragraphs 901.69(f) and (g) and 901.87(b).

- [(6)]{.lawlabel} In the case referred to in paragraph (4)(c), the
  declaration is only invalid with respect to the operations described
  in paragraphs 901.69(f) and (g) and 901.87(b) and only for the period
  during which the annual report is outstanding.

- [(7)]{.lawlabel} A person who has made a declaration shall notify the
  Minister within 30 days after any change to the names, address or
  contact information referred to in paragraph (2)(a).

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528095){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528095.html"}
:::

##### [Notice to the Minister]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528096 .Subheading}

- **[[901.195]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.195
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A person who has made a declaration
  referred to in section 901.194 shall notify the Minister of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any deficiency related to the model of remotely
    piloted aircraft system that causes the model to no longer meet the
    technical requirements specified under subparagraph
    901.194(2)(a)(iv); and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the fact that they are no longer maintaining a
    service difficulty reporting system, if they are required to
    establish and maintain such a system under section 901.197.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The person shall notify the Minister, in the case
  referred to in paragraph (1)(a), as soon as feasible after the
  deficiency is identified and, in the case referred to in paragraph
  (1)(b), on the day on which the person ceases to maintain the service
  difficulty reporting system.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528110){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528110.html"}
:::

##### [Issuance of Acceptance Letter]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528111 .Subheading}

- **[[901.196]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.196
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister shall, on receipt of an
  application containing the information set out in subsection (2),
  issue an acceptance letter to the applicant in respect of a model of
  remotely piloted aircraft system that is the subject of the
  application, if the applicant demonstrates the ability to

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} verify that the model of system meets the technical
    requirements set out in Standard 922 for which the applicant
    proposes to make a declaration referred to in section 901.194;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} establish and maintain a service difficulty
    reporting system that meets the requirements of section 901.197; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an applicant who manufactures an
    element of the remotely piloted aircraft system, ensure production
    consistency or, in the case of an applicant who provides a service
    that is an element of the system, ensure consistent activation and
    delivery of the service.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The applicant shall provide the following
  information:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the applicant's legal name, trade name, if any,
    address and contact information;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a concept of operations that includes

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a description of the principal design features
      and specifications of the remotely piloted aircraft system,
      including a technical description of

      - [(A)]{.lawlabel} the remotely piloted aircraft, including the
        category of aircraft, such as a fixed-wing aircraft, rotary-wing
        aircraft, hybrid aircraft or lighter-than-air aircraft, and

      - [(B)]{.lawlabel} all other elements of the system that are
        required for it to meet the technical requirements identified
        under subparagraph (c)(i),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} an indication of the operations described in
      section 901.69 or 901.87 that the model of system is intended to
      conduct,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a description of any operating limitations of
      the system, including personnel or environmental limitations, that
      must be adhered to in order for the system to meet the technical
      requirements identified under subparagraph (c)(i),

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} any procedures for operating the system,
      instructions for integrating and testing the elements of the
      system and instructions related to the servicing and maintenance
      of the system, and

    - [(v)]{.lawlabel} any mandatory actions that must be completed in
      order for the system to meet the technical requirements identified
      under subparagraph (c)(i);

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a declaration plan that identifies

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the technical requirements set out in Standard
      922 for which the applicant proposes to make a declaration
      referred to in section 901.194,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the means to be used to demonstrate that the
      model system meets the technical requirements referred to in
      subparagraph (i), including any industry standards that will be
      followed and any proposed deviations from those standards, and how
      those means will demonstrate that the system meets those technical
      requirements,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the resources necessary for carrying out the
      demonstration referred to in subparagraph (ii), and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the schedule for carrying out the demonstration
      referred to in subparagraph (ii);

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} copies in English or French, or both, of all
    standards the applicant intends to follow to demonstrate that the
    system meets the technical requirements identified under
    subparagraph (c)(i);

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} documentation that demonstrates that the applicant
    has, or has access to, the technical capability to

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} conduct the design analyses and tests required to
      demonstrate that the system meets the technical requirements
      identified under subparagraph (c)(i),

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} manufacture any elements of the remotely piloted
      aircraft system for which the applicant is the manufacturer, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} support the operation of the remotely piloted
      aircraft system in service;

  - [(f)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an applicant who manufactures an
    element of the system, a manufacturing plan that includes a
    description of the

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} manufacturing processes, including how the
      applicant will ensure production consistency,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} quality control procedures, including with
      respect to work performed by a supplier contracted by the
      applicant, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} configuration management processes for all
      aspects of production;

  - [(g)]{.lawlabel} in the case of an applicant who provides a service
    that is an element of the system, a commissioning plan that includes
    a description of the

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} procedures and tests for the service's
      activation, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} procedures for verifying that the service is
      functioning as intended; and

  - [(h)]{.lawlabel} a product support plan that describes how the
    applicant will support the operation of the system in service,
    including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a description of the service difficulty reporting
      system that the applicant will establish under section 901.197,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a description of the modifications that can be
      performed on the system by a person other than the applicant and
      any instructions with respect to those modifications,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a description of the required system
      maintenance and how the system, or elements of it, can be returned
      for maintenance, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a description of how any mandatory actions will
      be made available to each user of the model of system.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528150){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528150.html"}
:::

##### [Establishing a Service Difficulty Reporting System]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528151 .Subheading}

- **[[901.197]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.197
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If a declaration referred to in
  section 901.194 is made in respect of a model of remotely piloted
  aircraft system for which an acceptance letter has been issued under
  section 901.196, the person who has made the declaration shall
  establish and maintain a service difficulty reporting system for the
  purpose of receiving, recording, analyzing and investigating reports
  and information concerning any reportable service difficulty related
  to that model.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The service difficulty reporting system shall include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a means for receiving reports and information
    concerning any reportable service difficulty; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} instructions regarding what information must be
    submitted to the person who has made the declaration.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528158){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528158.html"}
:::

##### [Investigation of Service Difficulty Reports]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528159 .Subheading}

**[[901.198]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.198 .sectionLabel}** If a person
receives a service difficulty report in respect of a model of remotely
piloted aircraft system for which they have made a declaration referred
to in section 901.194 and for which an acceptance letter has been issued
under section 901.196, that person shall investigate the service
difficulty and, if it results from a deficiency in the model that causes
the system to no longer meet the technical requirements specified under
subparagraph 901.194(2)(a)(iv), develop a mandatory action to rectify
the deficiency.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528162){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528162.html"}
:::

##### [Annual Report]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528163 .Subheading}

- **[[901.199]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.199
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A person who has made a declaration
  referred to in section 901.194 in respect of a model of remotely
  piloted aircraft system for which an acceptance letter has been issued
  under section 901.196 shall submit to the Minister an annual report in
  respect of that model.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The annual report shall include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name of the person submitting the report;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name of the model of remotely piloted aircraft
    system;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the actual, if available, or estimated total number
    of hours of operation in Canada of systems of that model during the
    year to which the annual report relates; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the number of reportable service difficulty reports
    received during the year to which the annual report relates, a
    summary of the reports in respect of which mandatory actions were
    developed and a description of those mandatory actions.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The annual report shall be submitted to the Minister
  each year by not later than the anniversary of the day on which the
  declaration referred to in section 901.194 was made.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528173){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528173.html"}
:::

##### [Documentation]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528174 .Subheading}

**[[901.200]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.200 .sectionLabel}** A person who
has made a declaration referred to in section 901.194 in respect of a
model of remotely piloted aircraft system shall make available to each
user of that model of system

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} a maintenance program that includes

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} instructions related to the servicing and
    maintenance of the system, and

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} an inspection program to maintain system
    readiness;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} any mandatory actions the person develops in respect
  of the system; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} an operating manual that includes

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a description of the system,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the ranges of weights and centres of gravity
    within which the system may be safely operated under normal and
    emergency conditions and, if a weight and centre of gravity
    combination is considered safe only within certain loading limits,
    those limits and the corresponding weight and centre of gravity
    combinations,

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} with respect to each flight phase and mode of
    operation, the conditions required to maintain a stable command and
    control link and the minimum and maximum altitudes and velocities
    within which the remotely piloted aircraft can be operated safely
    under normal and emergency conditions,

  - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} a description of the effects of foreseeable
    weather conditions and other environmental conditions on the
    performance of the system,

  - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the characteristics of the system that could result
    in severe injury to crew members during operation,

  - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} the design features of the system, and their
    associated operations, that are intended to protect against injury
    to persons not involved in the operations,

  - [(vii)]{.lawlabel} the warning information provided to the pilot in
    the event of a degradation in system performance that may result in
    an unsafe operation condition,

  - [(viii)]{.lawlabel} procedures for operating the system in normal
    and emergency conditions,

  - [(ix)]{.lawlabel} assembly, adjustment and modification instructions
    for the system, and

  - [(x)]{.lawlabel} instructions for integrating the elements of the
    system.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528192){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528192.html"}
:::

##### [Record-keeping]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528193 .Subheading}

- **[[901.201]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.201
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A person who has made a declaration
  referred to in section 901.194 in respect of a model of remotely
  piloted aircraft system shall keep, and make available to the Minister
  on request, a record of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} any mandatory actions developed in respect of the
    system;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the results of, and the reports related to, the
    verifications that the person has undertaken to ensure that the
    model of system meets the technical requirements specified under
    subparagraph 901.194(2)(a)(iv); and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the results of any service difficulty
    investigations that the person has undertaken, if that person must
    establish and maintain a service difficulty reporting system under
    section 901.197.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The person shall keep the records referred to in
  subsection (1) for the later of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} two years after the day on which manufacturing of
    the model of remotely piloted aircraft system permanently ceases;
    and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} two years after the day on which the person
    provides a notification to the Minister under section 901.195.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528203){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528203.html"}
:::

**\[901.202 to 901.212 reserved\]**

#### [Division XII --- RPAS Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1528205 .Subheading}

##### [Eligibility to Hold an RPAS Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528206 .Subheading}

**[[901.213]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.213 .sectionLabel}** A person is
eligible to hold an RPAS operator certificate if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} with respect to a person who proposes to provide a
  commercial air service, the person is Canadian; or

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} in any other case, the person is

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a Canadian citizen or a permanent resident of
    Canada,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a government in Canada or an agent or mandatary of
    such a government, or

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a corporation or entity that is incorporated or
    formed under the laws of Canada or a province.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528214){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528214.html"}
:::

##### [Issuance]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528215 .Subheading}

**[[901.214]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.214 .sectionLabel}** The Minister
shall, on receipt of an application containing the following
information, issue an RPAS operator certificate:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the applicant's legal name, trade name, if any,
  address and contact information;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the name of the accountable executive;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} a declaration stating that the applicant has

  - [(i)]{.lawlabel} an RPAS operations manual that meets the
    requirements of section 901.217,

  - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the processes set out in section 901.218, and

  - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} a training program that meets the requirements of
    section 901.219; and

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} an indication of the type of operations the applicant
  intends to conduct and whether they intend to provide a commercial air
  service.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528225){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528225.html"}
:::

##### [Contents of RPAS Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528226 .Subheading}

**[[901.215]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.215 .sectionLabel}** An RPAS
operator certificate shall contain the following information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the legal name, trade name, if any, address and
  contact information of the RPAS operator;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the number of the certificate; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the date of issue of the certificate.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528232){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528232.html"}
:::

##### [General Conditions of RPAS Operator Certificate]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528233 .Subheading}

**[[901.216]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.216 .sectionLabel}** The general
conditions of an RPAS operator certificate are the following:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the RPAS operator shall maintain an adequate
  organizational structure;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the RPAS operator shall conduct training in
  accordance with section 901.219;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the RPAS operator shall have remotely piloted
  aircraft systems that are properly equipped for the type of operation
  to be conducted;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the RPAS operator shall conduct maintenance of
  remotely piloted aircraft systems in accordance with the
  manufacturer's instructions; and

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the RPAS operator shall notify the Minister of any
  change in its legal name, trade name, address and contact information
  of the RPAS operator within seven days of the change.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528241){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528241.html"}
:::

##### [RPAS Operations Manual]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528242 .Subheading}

- **[[901.217]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.217
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every RPAS operator shall establish
  and maintain an RPAS operations manual that consists of the following
  information:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a description of the roles and responsibilities of
    crew members before, during and after a flight;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a description of the roles and responsibilities of
    all operational and maintenance personnel and the hierarchy and
    chain of command within management;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the processes established under section 901.218;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the procedures established under section 901.23;
    and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a description of personnel training and
    qualifications, including a detailed syllabus of the RPAS operator's
    training program established under section 901.219.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If there is a change in any aspect of an RPAS
  operator's operations or the RPAS operations manual no longer meets
  the requirements of subsection (1), the RPAS operator shall amend its
  operations manual.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An RPAS operator shall provide a copy of its RPAS
  operations manual and a copy of every amendment to that manual to
  every person who is involved in the RPAS operator's operations.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} An RPAS operator shall provide a copy of its RPAS
  operations manual to the Minister on request.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528254){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528254.html"}
:::

##### [Processes]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528255 .Subheading}

- **[[901.218]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.218
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An RPAS operator shall establish and
  maintain processes for

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} setting goals for the improvement of aviation
    safety, measuring the attainment of those goals and addressing
    instances when those goals are not met;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} identifying and documenting hazards to aviation
    safety and evaluating, managing and documenting the associated
    risks;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} evaluating the effectiveness of measures taken to
    mitigate or remove the hazards and associated risks;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} internally reporting and analyzing hazards,
    incidents and accidents and taking corrective actions to prevent
    their recurrence; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} ensuring that maintenance is conducted in
    accordance with the RPAS operator's maintenance control manual.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The processes required under subsection (1) shall be
  under the control of the accountable executive appointed by the RPAS
  operator under paragraph 106.02(1)(a).

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528265){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528265.html"}
:::

##### [Training Program]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528266 .Subheading}

- **[[901.219]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.219
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every RPAS operator shall establish
  and maintain a training program that is designed to ensure that each
  person who receives training acquires the competence to perform their
  assigned duties.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} An RPAS operator's training program shall include

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} indoctrination training;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} initial and annual training, including training in
    respect of

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the models of remotely piloted aircraft operated
      by the RPAS operator,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} remotely piloted aircraft servicing and ground
      handling, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the procedures set out in the RPAS operations
      manual; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a process for assessing the competency of each
    person who receives training and for evaluating the effectiveness of
    the training program.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} An RPAS operator shall ensure that any training
  provided to meet the requirements of this section is based on the
  content of the RPAS operator's training program.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} No RPAS operator shall permit a person to act, and no
  person shall act, as an instructor unless

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the person has demonstrated to the RPAS operator
    knowledge of the content of the RPAS operations manual; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a flight training instructor, the
    person holds the pilot certificate required by this Part in respect
    of the operations to be conducted.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} No RPAS operator shall permit a person to act, and no
  person shall act, as an instructor unless the person has received,
  before the day on which the person begins to act as an instructor,
  training that includes the following elements:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the teaching and learning processes;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} instructional techniques; and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the student-instructor relationship.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528363){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528363.html"}
:::

##### [Person Responsible for RPAS Maintenance]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528364 .Subheading}

- **[[901.220]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.220
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An RPAS operator shall appoint a
  person responsible for RPAS maintenance.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The person responsible for RPAS maintenance shall
  plan and oversee the maintenance of the RPAS operator's remotely
  piloted aircraft systems, including coordinating maintenance
  arrangements with third-party maintenance providers.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528369){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528369.html"}
:::

##### [Maintenance Control Manual (MCM)]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528370 .Subheading}

- **[[901.221]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.221
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} An RPAS operator shall establish and
  maintain a maintenance control manual that includes

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the name of every person authorized by the RPAS
    operator to perform maintenance actions;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} any records referred to in paragraph 901.223(1)(e);
    and

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} procedures for servicing, maintenance and
    pre-flight and post-flight inspections of the RPAS operator's
    remotely piloted aircraft systems that are consistent with any
    instructions from the manufacturer.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The RPAS operator shall ensure that the maintenance
  control manual is made available to the Minister on request.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528386){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528386.html"}
:::

##### [Designation of Pilot-in-Command]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528387 .Subheading}

**[[901.222]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.222 .sectionLabel}** An RPAS
operator shall designate a pilot-in-command for each operation conducted
under Division VI.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528390){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528390.html"}
:::

##### [Records]{.HTitleText4} {#h-1528391 .Subheading}

- **[[901.223]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-901.223
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Every RPAS operator shall keep the
  following records:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a record containing the names of the pilots,
    pilots-in-command and other crew members who are involved in each
    flight and, in respect of a remotely piloted aircraft system, the
    time of each flight or series of flights;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a record containing the names of the employees, the
    agents or mandataries and the representatives of the operator;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a record containing the names of every person who
    has received training provided by the operator and the nature of
    that training;

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a record containing the registration numbers of all
    remotely piloted aircraft it operates; and

  - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a record containing the particulars of any
    mandatory action and any other maintenance action, modification or
    repair performed on a remotely piloted aircraft system, including

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the names of the persons who performed them,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the dates on which they were undertaken,

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a modification, the
      manufacturer, model and a description of the part or equipment
      installed to modify the system, and

    - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} if applicable, any instructions provided to
      complete the work.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Every RPAS operator shall ensure that the records are
  made available to the Minister on request and are retained for a
  period of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of the records referred to in
    paragraphs (1)(a), (b) and (c), 12 months after the day on which
    they are created; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of the records referred to in
    paragraphs (1)(d) and (e), 24 months after the day on which they are
    created.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 94](#1517042-1528423){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517042-1528423.html"}
:::

### [Subpart 2 --- \[Reserved\]]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1112131 .Subheading}

### [Subpart 3 --- Special Flight Operations --- Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1112132 .Subheading}

#### [Prohibition]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1112133 .Subheading}

**[[903.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-903.01 .sectionLabel}** No person shall
conduct any of the following operations using a remotely piloted
aircraft system unless the person complies with the provisions of a
special flight operations certificate --- RPAS issued by the Minister
under section 903.03:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the operation of a remotely piloted aircraft having
  an operating weight of more than 25 kg (55 pounds);

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the operation of a remotely piloted aircraft having
  an operating weight of less than 250 g (0.55 pounds) at an advertised
  event; and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} any other operation of a small remotely piloted
  aircraft for which the Minister determines that a special flight
  operations certificate --- RPAS is necessary to ensure aviation safety
  or the safety of any person.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-11, s. 23](#1045417-1112145){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045417-1112145.html"}
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 95](#1517044-1528428){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517044-1528428.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-903.01-20190109.html "Link to previous version of section 903.01"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Application for Special Flight Operations Certificate --- RPAS]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1112146 .Subheading}

**[[903.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-903.02 .sectionLabel}** An application
for a special flight operations certificate --- RPAS shall be submitted
to the Minister and include the following information:

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the legal name, trade name, address and contact
  information of the applicant;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the means by which the person responsible for the
  operation or the pilot may be contacted directly during operations;

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the operation for which the application is made;

- [(d)]{.lawlabel} the purpose of the operation;

- [(e)]{.lawlabel} the dates, alternate dates and times of the
  operation;

- [(f)]{.lawlabel} the manufacturer and model of the system, including
  three-view drawings or photographs of the aircraft and a complete
  description of the aircraft, including performance, operating
  limitations and equipment;

- [(g)]{.lawlabel} a description of the safety plan for the proposed
  area of operation;

- [(h)]{.lawlabel} a description of the emergency contingency plan for
  the operation;

- [(i)]{.lawlabel} a detailed plan describing how the operation is to be
  carried out;

- [(j)]{.lawlabel} the names, certificates, licences, permits and
  qualifications of the crew members, including the pilots and visual
  observers, and the remotely piloted aircraft system maintenance
  personnel;

- [(k)]{.lawlabel} the instructions regarding the maintenance of the
  system and a description of how that maintenance will be performed;

- [(l)]{.lawlabel} a description of weather minima for the operation;

- [(m)]{.lawlabel} a description of separation and collision avoidance
  capability and procedures;

- [(n)]{.lawlabel} a description of normal and emergency procedures for
  the operation;

- [(o)]{.lawlabel} a description of air traffic control services
  coordination, if applicable; and

- [(p)]{.lawlabel} any other information requested by the Minister
  pertinent to the safe conduct of the operation.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-11, s. 23](#1045417-1112165){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045417-1112165.html"}
- [SOR/2021-152, s. 17(F)](#1302030-1308400){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1302030-1308400.html"}
- [SOR/2022-246, s. 34(F)](#1380188-1380815){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1380188-1380815.html"}
- [SOR/2025-70, s. 96](#1517051-1528430){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1517051-1528430.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-903.02-20221207.html "Link to previous version of section 903.02"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Issuance of Special Flight Operations Certificate --- RPAS]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1112166 .Subheading}

**[[903.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-903.03 .sectionLabel}** The Minister
shall, on receipt of an application submitted in accordance with section
903.02, issue a special flight operations certificate --- RPAS if the
applicant demonstrates to the Minister the ability to perform the
operation without adversely affecting aviation safety or the safety of
any person.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2019-11, s. 23](#1045417-1112169){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1045417-1112169.html"}
:::

## [Part X --- Greenhouse Gas Emissions from International Aviation --- CORSIA]{.HTitleText1} {#h-1000313 .Part}

### [Division I --- General]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1000314 .Subheading}

#### [Interpretation]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000315 .Subheading}

**[[1000.01]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1000.01 .sectionLabel}** The following
definitions apply in this Part.

[[CO~2~]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[CO~2~]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means carbon
    dioxide. ([CO~2~]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[compliance period]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[compliance period]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means one of the
    three-year periods set out in subsection 1020.01(2) of the CORSIA
    Standard. ([période de conformité]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[CORSIA]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[CORSIA]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the International Civil
    Aviation Organization's (ICAO) Carbon Offsetting and Reduction
    Scheme for International Aviation set out in Volume IV of Annex 16
    to the Convention. ([CORSIA]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[CORSIA eligible emissions unit]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[CORSIA eligible emissions unit]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} has the same
    meaning as in subsection 1020.01(1) of the CORSIA Standard. ([unité
    d'émissions admissible du CORSIA]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[CORSIA eligible fuel]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[CORSIA eligible fuel]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} has the same meaning as
    in subsection 1020.01(1) of the CORSIA Standard. ([carburant
    admissible CORSIA]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[CORSIA Standard]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[CORSIA Standard]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means Standard 1020 ---
    CORSIA, published by the Department of Transport. ([Norme du
    CORSIA]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

[[new entrant]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

:   [[new entrant]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} has the same meaning as in
    CORSIA and, for the purposes of interpreting this definition,
    "aeroplane operator" is to be read as "private operator" or "air
    operator". ([nouveau venu]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-240, s. 2
- [SOR/2020-275, s. 2](#1278933-1282883){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1278933-1282883.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1000.01-20190101.html "Link to previous version of section 1000.01"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Application]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000328 .Subheading}

- **[[1000.02]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1000.02
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} This Part applies to Canadian
  private operators and Canadian air operators that produce --- from the
  use of one or more large aeroplanes --- more than 10 000 t of CO~2~
  emissions from flights between contracting states during a calendar
  year.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection (1), the emissions are
  calculated in accordance with section 1000.03.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of this Part, flights are attributed
  to a private operator or air operator in accordance with section
  1020.02 of the CORSIA Standard and the flight departure time (UTC)
  determines the calendar year to which a flight belongs.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} The following flights are exempt from the application
  of subsection (1):

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} humanitarian flights;

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} medical evacuation flights;

  - [(c)]{.lawlabel} fire-fighting flights; and

  - [(d)]{.lawlabel} positioning flights required in relation to the
    flights referred to in paragraphs (a) to (c).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-240, s. 2
- [SOR/2020-275, s. 2](#1278933-1282892){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1278933-1282892.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1000.02-20190101.html "Link to previous version of section 1000.02"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Calculation Method]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000342 .Subheading}

- **[[1000.03]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1000.03
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} CO~2~ emissions are to be determined
  using the following formula and expressed in tonnes:

  ::: {#1282905 .Subsection}
  $\underset{f}{\Sigma}{M_{f}x{FCF}_{f}}$

  where

  [M~*f*~]{.dfn}
  :   is the mass of fuel *f* used, expressed in tonnes and calculated
      according to
      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a method described in subsection 1020.03(1) of
        the CORSIA Standard, subject to subsection (2); or

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a method described in subsection 1020.03(2) of
        the CORSIA Standard; and

  [FCF~*f*~]{.dfn}
  :   is the fuel conversion factor of given fuel *f*, expressed in kg
      CO~2~/kg fuel, and is equal to
      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 3.16 for Jet-A and Jet-A1 fuels; or

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 3.10 for aviation gasoline (*AvGas*) and Jet-B
        fuel.
  :::

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of the methods described in
  paragraphs 1020.03(1)(a) and (b) of the CORSIA Standard, if a flight
  is operated on behalf of a private operator or air operator, that
  operator must ensure that the fuel measurement values calculated
  according to the method described in paragraph 1020.03(1)(c) of the
  CORSIA Standard are provided to it and taken into account in its
  calculations.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-240, s. 2
- [SOR/2020-275, s. 2](#1278933-1282902){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1278933-1282902.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1000.03-20190101.html "Link to previous version of section 1000.03"){.PITLink}
:::

**\[1000.04 to 1000.09 reserved\]**

### [Division II --- Monitoring]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1000357 .Subheading}

#### [Emissions Monitoring Plan]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000358 .Subheading}

- **[[1000.10]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1000.10
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Within 90 days after the day on
  which a private operator or air operator becomes subject to this Part,
  the operator must submit to the Minister for approval an emissions
  monitoring plan for its flights between contracting states --- other
  than flights referred to in subsection 1000.02(4) --- that are
  conducted using one or more large aeroplanes.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The plan must contain the information referred to in
  subsections 1020.10(1) to (3) of the CORSIA Standard.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The private operator or air operator must choose one
  of the following monitoring methods:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of flights between states referred to
    in subsection 1020.10(4) of the CORSIA Standard,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a method described in subsection 1020.03(1)
      or (2) of the CORSIA Standard, if the annual CO~2~ emissions from
      those flights are less than 50 000 t, or

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a method described in subsection 1020.03(1) of
      the CORSIA Standard, if the annual CO~2~ emissions from those
      flights are equal to or greater than 50 000 t; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in any other case, a method described in subsection
    1020.03(1) or (2) of the CORSIA Standard.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} A private operator or air operator whose emissions
  monitoring plan was approved by the Minister before January 1, 2021
  must submit to the Minister, no later than February 28, 2021,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the monitoring method identified in that plan
    meets the requirements of subsection (3), the information referred
    to in paragraphs 1020.10(2)(g), (i), (j) and (k) of the CORSIA
    Standard; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the monitoring method identified in that plan
    does not meet the requirements of subsection (3), an amended plan
    for approval that identifies a method chosen in accordance with
    subsection (3) and contains the information referred to in
    subsection (2).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-240, s. 2
- [SOR/2020-275, s. 2](#1278933-1282914){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1278933-1282914.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1000.10-20190101.html "Link to previous version of section 1000.10"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Approval]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000369 .Subheading}

**[[1000.11]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1000.11 .sectionLabel}** The Minister
must approve the emissions monitoring plan if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} the information referred to in subsection 1000.10(2)
  is provided;

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} a monitoring method is chosen in accordance with
  subsection 1000.10(3); and

- [(c)]{.lawlabel} the information referred to in subsections 1020.10(2)
  and (3) of the CORSIA Standard and submitted in accordance with
  section 1000.10 is consistent with the chosen monitoring method and
  the activities of the private operator or air operator, as applicable.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-240, s. 2
- [SOR/2020-275, s. 2](#1278933-1282926){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1278933-1282926.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1000.11-20190101.html "Link to previous version of section 1000.11"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Amendment]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000376 .Subheading}

- **[[1000.12]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1000.12
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (2), if any of
  the information referred to in subsection 1020.10(2) of the CORSIA
  Standard is amended, the private operator or air operator must submit
  an amended emissions monitoring plan to the Minister for approval
  before it is implemented.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the information referred to in paragraph
  1020.10(2)(i), (j) or (k) of the CORSIA Standard is amended, the
  private operator or air operator must submit an amended emissions
  monitoring plan to the Minister for approval no later than September
  30 of the year preceding the beginning of the next compliance period.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If there is a change to the information referred to
  in subsection 1020.10(1) of the CORSIA Standard, the private operator
  or air operator must submit the updated information to the Minister
  without delay.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} If the annual CO~2~ emissions from a private
  operator's or air operator's flights between states referred to in
  subsection 1020.10(4) of the CORSIA Standard increase to an amount
  equal to or greater than 50 000 t for two consecutive years, the
  operator must choose a monitoring method in accordance with
  subparagraph 1000.10(3)(a)(ii) and submit an amended emissions
  monitoring plan to the Minister for approval before it is implemented
  and no later than September 30 of the year following the two
  consecutive years of increased emissions.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} If the annual CO~2~ emissions from a private
  operator's or air operator's flights between states referred to in
  subsection 1020.10(4) of the CORSIA Standard decrease to an amount
  less than 50 000 t for two consecutive years, the operator may choose
  a different monitoring method in accordance with subparagraph
  1000.10(3)(a)(i) and, if a different monitoring method is chosen, must
  submit an amended emissions monitoring plan to the Minister for
  approval before it is implemented and no later than September 30 of
  the year following the two consecutive years of decreased emissions.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-240, s. 2
- [SOR/2020-275, s. 2](#1278933-1282931){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1278933-1282931.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1000.12-20190101.html "Link to previous version of section 1000.12"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Implementation of Monitoring Plan]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000384 .Subheading}

- **[[1000.13]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1000.13
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsection (5), a private
  operator or air operator must implement its emissions monitoring plan
  as soon as it is approved.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subject to subsections (3) to (5), the private
  operator or air operator must use the monitoring method identified in
  its approved emissions monitoring plan for at least an entire
  compliance period.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} If a private operator or air operator changes its
  monitoring method in accordance with subsection 1000.12(4) or (5), the
  operator must use the new method beginning on January 1 of the year
  after the year in which the amended emissions monitoring plan is
  approved.

- [(4)]{.lawlabel} If a private operator or air operator changes its
  monitoring method as a corrective measure taken under subparagraph
  1000.15(1)(a)(ii), the operator must use the new method as soon as its
  amended emissions monitoring plan is approved.

- [(5)]{.lawlabel} A new entrant must implement its approved emissions
  monitoring plan on January 1 of the year after the year during which
  the new entrant becomes subject to this Part.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-240, s. 2
- [SOR/2020-275, s. 2](#1278933-1282938){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1278933-1282938.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1000.13-20190101.html "Link to previous version of section 1000.13"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Data Gaps --- Threshold]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000390 .Subheading}

**[[1000.14]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1000.14 .sectionLabel}** A private
operator or air operator that uses a monitoring method described in
subsection 1020.03(1) of the CORSIA Standard must not have data gaps
related to fuel quantities in respect of more than 5% of its flights
between states referred to in subsection 1020.10(4) of the CORSIA
Standard.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-240, s. 2
- [SOR/2020-275, s. 2](#1278933-1282945){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1278933-1282945.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1000.14-20190101.html "Link to previous version of section 1000.14"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Data Gaps --- Requirements]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1282946 .Subheading}

- **[[1000.15]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1000.15
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} If there are data gaps in respect of
  a private operator's or air operator's flights between states referred
  to in subsection 1020.10(4) of the CORSIA Standard, the operator must,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if the gaps are in respect of more than 5% of those
    flights,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} notify the Minister of the reasons for the gaps
      within three months after the day on which it becomes aware of
      those gaps,

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} take corrective measures before submitting the
      verified emissions report referred to in section 1000.30, which
      may include changing the monitoring method if an amended emissions
      monitoring plan is submitted to the Minister in accordance with
      section 1000.12 and the Minister approves it, and

    - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} fill in the gaps before submitting the verified
      emissions report referred to in section 1000.30 using one of the
      monitoring methods described in subsection 1020.03(1) of the
      CORSIA Standard, which is to be pre-approved by the Minister if
      the requirements related to that method are met; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if the gaps are in respect of no more than 5% of
    those flights,

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} take corrective measures, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} fill in the gaps using one of the monitoring
      methods described in section 1020.15 of the CORSIA Standard before
      submitting the verified emissions report referred to in section
      1000.30.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If there are data gaps in respect of a private
  operator's or air operator's flights between contracting states other
  than the flights between states referred to in subsection 1020.10(4)
  of the CORSIA Standard, the operator must

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} take corrective measures; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} fill in the gaps using one of the monitoring
    methods described in section 1020.15 of the CORSIA Standard before
    submitting the verified emissions report referred to in section
    1000.30.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-275, s. 2](#1278933-1282961){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1278933-1282961.html"}
:::

**\[1000.16 to 1000.19 reserved\]**

### [Division III --- Offsetting]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1283017 .Subheading}

#### [Obligation to Offset]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000403 .Subheading}

- **[[1000.20]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1000.20
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} For each compliance period, a
  private operator or air operator must offset the final amount of CO~2~
  emissions calculated in accordance with subsection 1000.24(1) and
  indicated in a notice provided by the Minister by cancelling, within a
  registry referred to in section 1020.20 of the CORSIA Standard, an
  amount of CORSIA eligible emissions units equal to the amount
  indicated in the notice, by the later of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the last day of the 13th month after the end of the
    compliance period to which the notice relates; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the 60th day after the day on which the operator
    receives the notice.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of calculating offsetting
  obligations, the CO~2~ emissions to be taken into account are those
  from flights between states referred to in subsection 1020.10(4) of
  the CORSIA Standard --- other than flights referred to in subsection
  1000.02(4) --- that are conducted using one or more large aeroplanes.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} A private operator or air operator must ensure that
  the information referred to in subsection 1020.30(4) of the CORSIA
  Standard in respect of each of its cancelled CORSIA eligible emissions
  units for a given compliance period is published on the website of the
  registry referred to in subsection (1).

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-240, s. 2
- [SOR/2020-275, s. 2](#1278933-1282962){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1278933-1282962.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1000.20-20190101.html "Link to previous version of section 1000.20"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Prohibition]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000415 .Subheading}

**[[1000.21]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1000.21 .sectionLabel}** A private
operator or air operator must not operate an aircraft for a flight
between states referred to in subsection 1020.10(4) of the CORSIA
Standard unless that operator has offset its CO~2~ emissions in
accordance with subsection 1000.20(1) of these Regulations.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-240, s. 2
- [SOR/2020-275, s. 2](#1278933-1282969){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1278933-1282969.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1000.21-20190101.html "Link to previous version of section 1000.21"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Calculation of Annual Offsetting Obligations]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000423 .Subheading}

- **[[1000.22]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1000.22
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister must calculate the
  amount of CO~2~ emissions, expressed in tonnes, required to be offset
  by a private operator or air operator for a given calendar year,
  without consideration of any reduction resulting from the use of
  CORSIA eligible fuels, using the following formula:

  ::: {#1282974 .Subsection}
  ${\% S}_{y}x\left( {OE}_{y} \right.x\left. {SGF}_{y} \right) + {\% O}_{y}x\left( {OE}_{y} \right.x\left. {OGF}_{y} \right)$

  where
  :::

  [%S~*y*~]{.dfn}
  :   is the per cent sectoral for the given calendar year *y,* as
      indicated in subsection 1020.22(2) of the CORSIA Standard;

  [OE~*y*~]{.dfn}
  :   is the CO~2~ emissions from the operator's flights referred to in
      subsection 1000.20(2) for the given calendar year *y*;

  [SGF~*y*~]{.dfn}
  :   is the sector's growth factor for the given calendar year *y*
      referred to in subsection 1020.22(3) of the CORSIA Standard;

  [%O~*y*~]{.dfn}
  :   is the per cent individual for the given calendar year *y*, as
      indicated in subsection 1020.22(2) of the CORSIA Standard; and

  [OGF~*y*~]{.dfn}
  :   is the operator's growth factor for the given calendar year *y*,
      calculated in accordance with the formula set out in subsection
      (2).

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister must, taking into account the CO~2~
  emissions set out in the verified emissions report submitted by the
  private operator or air operator, calculate the operator's growth
  factor for a given calendar year using the following formula:

  ::: {#1282982 .Subsection}
  $\frac{\left( {OE}_{y}–{OE}_{B,y} \right)}{{OE}_{y}}$

  where

  [OE~*y*~]{.dfn}
  :   is the CO~2~ emissions from the operator's flights referred to in
      subsection 1000.20(2) for the given calendar year *y*; and

  [OE~*B,y*~]{.dfn}
  :   is the value set out in subsection 1020.22(4) of the CORSIA
      Standard.
  :::

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} In the case of a new entrant, the Minister must not
  take into account the CO~2~ emissions produced by the new entrant
  during the shorter of the following periods:

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the period beginning on the day on which the new
    entrant becomes subject to this Part and ending on January 1 of the
    third year after that day; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the period beginning on the day on which the new
    entrant becomes subject to this Part and ending on December 31 of
    the year preceding the year during which the CO~2~ emissions from
    its flights referred to in subsection 1000.20(2) exceed the
    threshold set out in subsection 1020.22(1) of the CORSIA Standard.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-240, s. 2
- [SOR/2020-275, s. 2](#1278933-1282971){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1278933-1282971.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1000.22-20190101.html "Link to previous version of section 1000.22"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Calculation of Reductions from Use of CORSIA Eligible Fuels]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000433 .Subheading}

- **[[1000.23]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1000.23
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A private operator or air operator
  may claim an emissions reduction resulting from the use of CORSIA
  eligible fuels in a given calendar year and, if a claim is made, the
  reduction is to be calculated for each CORSIA eligible fuel using the
  following formula and be expressed in tonnes:

  ::: {#1282992 .Subsection}
  [FCFx\[ΣfMSf,yx(1--LSfLC)\]]{.math
  xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"}

  where

  [FCF]{.dfn}
  :   is the fuel conversion factor, expressed in kg CO~2~/kg fuel, and
      is equal to
      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 3.16 for Jet-A and Jet-A1 fuels; or

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 3.10 for aviation gasoline (*AvGas*) and Jet-B
        fuel;

  [MS~*f*,*y*~]{.dfn}
  :   is the total mass, expressed in tonnes, of a given CORSIA eligible
      fuel *f* claimed for the given calendar year *y*, as calculated in
      accordance with subsection 1020.23(3) of the CORSIA Standard and
      as reported in accordance with section 1000.30 of these
      Regulations;

  [LS~*f*~]{.dfn}
  :   is the life-cycle emissions value for a given CORSIA eligible fuel
      *f*, calculated in accordance with subsection (2) and expressed in
      gCO~2~e/MJ; and

  [LC]{.dfn}
  :   is the life-cycle emissions value for fuel, expressed in
      gCO~2~e/MJ and equal to
      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} 89 for jet fuels; and

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} 95 for aviation gasoline (*AvGas*).
  :::

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of calculating the life-cycle
  emissions value for a CORSIA eligible fuel,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} if a default life-cycle emissions value is used,
    the private operator or air operator must use the value referred to
    in subsection 1020.23(1) of the CORSIA Standard; or

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} if an actual life-cycle emissions value is used,
    the private operator or air operator must

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} use the calculation methodology referred to in
      paragraph 1020.23(2)(a) of the CORSIA Standard, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} ensure that the application of the calculation
      methodology is verified in accordance with paragraph 1020.23(2)(b)
      of the CORSIA Standard.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} In order to claim an emissions reduction resulting
  from the use of CORSIA eligible fuels during a given compliance
  period, a private operator or air operator must submit the information
  required by subparagraph 1000.30(1)(a)(ii) no later than in its
  verified emissions report in respect of the final year of that
  compliance period.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-240, s. 2
- [SOR/2020-275, s. 2](#1278933-1282989){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1278933-1282989.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1000.23-20190101.html "Link to previous version of section 1000.23"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Calculation of Final Offsetting Obligations]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1283029 .Subheading}

- **[[1000.24]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1000.24
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} The Minister must calculate, for
  each private operator and air operator, the final amount of CO~2~
  emissions that that operator is required to offset for a given
  compliance period, rounded up to the nearest tonne, using the
  following formula:

  ::: {#1283032 .Subsection}
  $\left( {OR}_{1,c} \right. + {OR}_{2,c} + \left. {OR}_{3,c} \right)–\left( {ER}_{1,c} \right. + {ER}_{2,c} + \left. {ER}_{3,c} \right)$

  where

  [OR~*y*,*c*~]{.dfn}
  :   is the amount of CO~2~ emissions that the operator is required to
      offset for the given calendar year *y* (where *y* = *1*, *2* or
      *3*) of the compliance period *c*, calculated in accordance with
      section 1000.22; and

  [ER~*y*,*c*~]{.dfn}
  :   is the emissions reduction claimed resulting from the use of
      CORSIA eligible fuels in the given calendar year *y* (where *y* =
      *1*, *2* or *3*) of the compliance period *c*, calculated in
      accordance with section 1000.23.
  :::

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} If the amount of CO~2~ emissions calculated in
  accordance with subsection (1) is a negative amount for a given
  compliance period, that amount cannot be used to reduce the private
  operator's or air operator's emissions-offsetting obligations for a
  subsequent compliance period.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-275, s. 2](#1278933-1283038){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1278933-1283038.html"}
:::

**\[1000.25 to 1000.29 reserved\]**

### [Division IV --- Reporting, Verification and Record Keeping]{.HTitleText2} {#h-1283018 .Subheading}

#### [Verified Emissions Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1000440 .Subheading}

- **[[1000.30]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1000.30
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A private operator or air operator
  must submit to the Minister, no later than April 30 of the calendar
  year following the calendar year during which the monitoring of
  emissions was carried out,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a verified emissions report containing the
    information referred to in

    - [(i)]{.lawlabel} subsection 1020.30(1) of the CORSIA Standard, and

    - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} subsection 1020.30(2) of the CORSIA Standard, if
      an emissions reduction resulting from the use of CORSIA eligible
      fuel is being claimed; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the verification report associated with the report
    referred to in paragraph (a) containing the information referred to
    in paragraph 1020.32(3)(j) of the CORSIA Standard.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The private operator or air operator must ensure that
  the verification body submits to the Minister, with the operator's
  prior authorization, the reports referred to in subsection (1) no
  later than April 30 of the calendar year following the calendar year
  during which the monitoring of emissions was carried out.

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} Despite subsections (1) and (2), the verified
  emissions report and associated verification report for the year 2020
  must contain the information referred to in, and be submitted in
  accordance with, section 1000.20, as it read before January 1, 2021.

::: HistoricalNote
- SOR/2018-240, s. 2
- [SOR/2020-275, s. 2](#1278933-1283008){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1278933-1283008.html"}
:::

::: PITLink
[Previous
Version](section-1000.30-20190101.html "Link to previous version of section 1000.30"){.PITLink}
:::

#### [Verified Emissions Unit Cancellation Report]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1283039 .Subheading}

- **[[1000.31]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1000.31
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A private operator or air operator
  must submit to the Minister, for a given compliance period,

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a verified emissions unit cancellation report
    containing the information referred to in subsections 1020.30(3)
    to (5) of the CORSIA Standard; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the verification report associated with the report
    referred to in paragraph (a) containing the information referred to
    in paragraph 1020.32(3)(j) of the CORSIA Standard.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The private operator or air operator must submit to
  the Minister the reports referred to in subsection (1) by the later of

  - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the last day of the 16th month after the end of the
    given compliance period; and

  - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the last day of the 5th month after the day on
    which the operator receives the notice referred to in subsection
    1000.20(1).

- [(3)]{.lawlabel} The private operator or air operator must ensure that
  the verification body submits to the Minister, with the operator's
  prior authorization, the reports referred to in subsection (1) by the
  later of the dates set out in subsection (2).

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-275, s. 2](#1278933-1283049){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1278933-1283049.html"}
:::

#### [Verification Body]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1283050 .Subheading}

- **[[1000.32]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1000.32
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A private operator or air operator
  must select a verification body that is accredited as meeting the
  requirements set out in subsection 1020.32(2) of the CORSIA Standard
  by a national accreditation body that is a member of the International
  Accreditation Forum and that meets the requirements referred to in
  subsection 1020.32(1) of the CORSIA Standard.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The private operator or air operator must ensure that
  the verification of the emissions report and the emissions unit
  cancellation report is conducted in accordance with the requirements
  set out in subsection 1020.32(3) of the CORSIA Standard.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-275, s. 2](#1278933-1283055){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1278933-1283055.html"}
:::

#### [Parent Company and Subsidiaries]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1283056 .Subheading}

**[[1000.33]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1000.33 .sectionLabel}** A private
operator or air operator and one or more other private operators or air
operators may consolidate their emissions monitoring plans, verified
emissions reports, verified emissions unit cancellation reports and
associated verification reports if

- [(a)]{.lawlabel} they are in a parent-subsidiary relationship in which
  the subsidiary is wholly owned by the parent company or they are
  wholly owned subsidiaries of the same parent company; and

- [(b)]{.lawlabel} the consolidated emissions monitoring plan
  establishes that the subsidiary is wholly owned.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-275, s. 2](#1278933-1283061){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1278933-1283061.html"}
:::

#### [Publication]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1283062 .Subheading}

- **[[1000.34]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1000.34
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A private operator or air operator
  that uses a monitoring method described in subsection 1020.03(1) of
  the CORSIA Standard may make a request to the Minister that certain
  information be considered confidential, in the cases set out in
  section 1020.34 of the CORSIA Standard, and must indicate the reasons
  for the request.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The Minister must determine that information is
  confidential if it is established that publication would harm the
  commercial interests of the private operator or air operator and such
  information must be designated as confidential when provided to ICAO.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-275, s. 2](#1278933-1283067){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1278933-1283067.html"}
:::

#### [Records]{.HTitleText3} {#h-1283068 .Subheading}

- **[[1000.35]{.sectionLabel}]{#s-1000.35
  .sectionLabel}** [(1)]{.lawlabel} A private operator or air operator
  must retain a copy of the emissions monitoring plans, the verified
  emissions reports, the verified emissions unit cancellation reports,
  the authorizations referred to in subsections 1000.30(2) and
  1000.31(3) and the associated verification reports, together with the
  supporting documents, for at least 10 years after the day on which
  they are made.

- [(2)]{.lawlabel} The private operator or air operator must provide the
  Minister with a copy of the records referred to in subsection (1) on
  request.

::: HistoricalNote
- [SOR/2020-275, s. 2](#1278933-1283073){.wb-lbx
  ajax-after="1278933-1283073.html"}
:::

:::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::
::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::::

- --- SOR/2025-70, s. 60

  - [60]{.lawlabel} Section 901.27 of the Regulations is replaced by the
    following:

    :::: section
    ::: AmendedText
    - [901.27]{.lawlabel} No pilot shall operate a remotely piloted
      aircraft system unless, before commencing the operation, they
      determine that the operational volume is suitable by conducting a
      site survey that takes into account the following factors:

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} the type of airspace and any requirements
        applicable to the flight geography, including any specified in a
        NOTAM;

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the altitudes and routes to be used for
        approach, take-off, launch, landing or recovery;

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} the proximity of other aircraft operations;

      - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the proximity of airports, heliports and other
        aerodromes;

      - [(e)]{.lawlabel} the location and height of obstacles, including
        wires, masts, buildings, cell phone towers and wind turbines;

      - [(f)]{.lawlabel} the predominant weather and environmental
        conditions and the weather forecast for the duration of the
        flight;

      - [(g)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a VLOS operation, an extended
        VLOS operation or a sheltered operation, the horizontal distance
        from any person not involved in the operation; and

      - [(h)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a BVLOS operation, the distance
        from any populated area or sparsely populated area.
    :::
    ::::
